format: Handheld iOS ARKit mobile RGB-D captures with 3D oriented bounding box annotations for 17 indoor object categories

name: EPFL Electron Microscopy Dataset
format: 3D grayscale electron microscopy volume (FIB-SEM, 5x5x5 nm/voxel) of hippocampal CA1 neural tissue; synthetic anisotropy applied at x4/x8/x10
metric: PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS (isotropic reconstruction); IoU (mitochondria segmentation)
notes: EPFL CVLab hippocampal FIB-SEM dataset; 5x5x5 um^3 volume; widely used for VEM isotropic reconstruction benchmarking; anisotropic data synthetically generated by z-axis degradation

name: CREMI
num_samples: 3 volumes (samples A, B, C; 193 sections each)
storage: ~2-3GB total (HDF5 format, 4x4x40 nm/voxel serial section TEM)
format: Serial section Transmission Electron Microscopy (ssTEM) of adult Drosophila melanogaster brain; 3 volumes at 4x4x40nm/voxel; inherently anisotropic (z-resolution 10x coarser than lateral)
notes: CREMI challenge dataset (Funke & Saalfeld, 2016); 3 samples (A/B/C) of 193 sections at 1250x1250 lateral resolution; used for VEM super-resolution due to inherent anisotropy (40nm axial vs 4nm lateral)

name: MINDCUBE
storage: ~15GB (3268 multi-view indoor scenes, each with multiple images + 21K+ spatial QA pairs)
format: Multi-view indoor images + spatial question-answer pairs; 3 task types: rotation, among, around
notes: MINDCUBE probes 3D spatial reasoning under limited views; 3268 scenes, 3 camera motion types; MINDCUBE-1k is a 1050-question evaluation subset

name: MINDCUBE-1k
format: Multi-view indoor images + spatial question-answer pairs; 3 task types: rotation, among, around
notes: Subset of MINDCUBE with 1050 questions specifically designed for evaluation purposes

name: OMNI3D-BENCH
format: Single-view images with spatial reasoning questions; 4 subtasks: numeric-count, numeric-other, yes/no, multi-choice
metric: accuracy / mean relative accuracy (MRA) for numeric subtasks
notes: Single-view spatial reasoning benchmark from VADAR paper; evaluates MLLMs on spatial understanding from single images

name: MMSI-Bench
format: Multi-view images + spatial questions spanning 11 subtask categories (positional relationships, attributes, motion)
notes: Multi-modal spatial reasoning benchmark covering camera-camera, object-object, region, motion, measurement subtasks

name: MuS-Polar3D
num_samples: 726 scattering samples (multi-object, multi-turbidity) + clean-water references + ground-truth surface normal maps
storage: ~15-25GB (4-channel polarization images at multiple scattering levels, multiple objects)
eval_time: <1 hour (inference + MAE computation on test split)
format: 4-channel polarization images (0/45/90/135 degrees) from a DoFP polarization camera, with per-pixel surface normal ground truth and clean-water reference images; multiple turbidity levels (emulsion concentration)
metric: Mean Angular Error (MAE, degrees) for surface normal estimation; PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS for descattering evaluation
access: arXiv:2512.21513 (Wang et al., Fuzhou University / Tsinghua University, 2025)

name: Waste-Weight-10K
eval_time: minutes (inference on held-out test set of 1,500 samples)
format: Synchronized image-metadata pairs: high-resolution RGB images + physical measurements (3D object dimensions Lx/Ly/Lz, camera distance Dx, lens height Dy, object category label, ground-truth weight in kg); 11 C&I waste categories (Automotive Scrap, Ferrous Metal, Cardboard, Rigid Plastic, Wood, General Trash, Industrial Gas Cylinder, Rubber, Appliance, Foam, Battery); weight range 3.5-3450 kg; stratified 70/15/15 train/val/test split by category
license: research use (proprietary; collected by authors at logistics and recycling sites)
access: not publicly available as of 2026-03-16; contact the corresponding authors
notes: Introduced in Islam et al. (arXiv:2603.00931, 2026). Ground-truth weights measured with industrial load cells at precision ±0.05 kg. Data collected at various logistics centers and recycling facilities using multiple mobile imaging devices. Addresses scale ambiguity in C&I waste weight estimation.

name: Set12
format: 12 standard grayscale images commonly used for image denoising evaluation

name: BSD68
format: 68 grayscale images selected from BSDS500 for image denoising evaluation

name: Classic5
format: 5 standard images (Monarch, Parrots, Barbara, Starfish, Lena/Cameraman) commonly used for image deblocking evaluation with PSNR-B metric
access: widely available in JPEG artifact removal papers

name: LIVE1
format: 29 color images from the LIVE image quality assessment database used for image deblocking and quality assessment

name: JailNewsBench
num_samples: ~300k instances across 34 regions and 22 languages (7 attack conditions x seed instructions)
eval_time: days for full evaluation across all models
format: Seed instructions derived from real news articles, modified by 5 jailbreak attacks + 2 baselines, evaluated by LLM-as-a-Judge on 8 harmfulness sub-metrics
metric: attack success rate (ASR), infelicity rate (IFL), harmfulness score (1-5)
access: Restricted release; contact authors (MBZUAI). Introduced in Kaneko et al. 2026.

name: Multilingual News Headlines Dataset
format: Multi-lingual news headline and full-article pairs in local language and English, collected from world media via NewsAPI; covers multiple regions

name: BeaverTails
format: Human-preference pairs of question-answer sets labeled for safety/harmlessness across 14 harm categories, plus cost model annotations

name: JailBreakBench
format: 100 unique behaviors (10 per category across 10 harm categories) with 5 jailbreak attack strings each; open robustness benchmark for jailbreaking LLMs

name: Do-Not-Answer
format: Instructions that responsible language models should not comply with, covering 5 harm areas and 12 harm types; annotated with risk level and response category

name: collective-alignment
format: Public input on LLM default behaviors, covering sensitive topics and model behavior preferences collected via public consultation; includes topics across multiple harm categories

name: XCAV
num_samples: 111 complete X-ray coronary angiography video recordings from 59 patients (8:2 train/test split)
storage: ~10-15GB (512x512 XCA video sequences; each video has 1-2 annotated frames per video at maximal contrast agent prominence)
format: X-ray coronary angiography video sequences (varying frame lengths) with sparse binary vessel segmentation masks (1-2 annotated frames per video)
metric: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Normal Surface Distance (NSD), centreline Dice (clDice), Specificity (Spe), Sensitivity (Sen)
license: research use (released with Denver/Wu et al. CVPR 2025)
access: Released with Denver paper (Wu et al., CVPR 2025); contact authors at https://github.com/wu-cvgl/Denver

name: CADICA
num_samples: 662 complete coronary artery disease video recordings from 42 patients (no ground-truth segmentation masks; used for generalization evaluation only)
eval_time: <1 hour (inference only; no pixel-level labels for training)
format: X-ray coronary angiography video sequences without segmentation ground truth; used for cross-institutional generalization testing
access: https://github.com/amolina-uniovi/CADICA (Jiménez-Partinen et al., Expert Systems 41(12), 2024, doi:10.1111/exsy.13708)

name: CAVSA
num_samples: 1061 complete coronary XCA video sequences from 121 patients (8:2 train/test; 16 fully annotated + remainder with 1-2 annotated frames)
format: 512x512 X-ray coronary angiography video sequences with radiologist-annotated binary vessel masks; 16 fully annotated + partial annotation for remaining videos
metric: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Normal Surface Distance (NSD), centreline Dice (clDice), Specificity (Spe), Sensitivity (Sen)
license: private institutional dataset; not publicly available
access: Private — collected by authors (Yu Luo et al.) at institutional hospitals; not publicly available

name: AIBL (Australian Imaging Biomarker and Lifestyle)
num_samples: ~700+ participants longitudinal; subset of 20 T1w subjects used in tagged MRI paper
format: 3D T1-weighted brain MRI at 1mm isotropic resolution from Australian Alzheimer's biomarker study; includes healthy controls and MCI/AD subjects
license: AIBL data use agreement (non-commercial research, free registration)

name: R2R
num_samples: ~22k instruction-path pairs over 783 validation unseen paths (3 instructions each)
storage: ~100GB (Matterport3D panoramic images + instruction JSONs + connectivity graphs)
eval_time: hours (run navigation episodes on discrete graph)
format: Step-by-step natural language navigation instructions over Matterport3D indoor environments; discrete graph-based navigation with panoramic observations
metric: SR (Success Rate), OSR (Oracle SR), SPL, NE (Navigation Error)
license: Matterport3D academic license (free, requires registration) + R2R annotations CC BY

name: REVERIE
storage: ~100GB (shared Matterport3D panoramic images + REVERIE instruction JSONs)
eval_time: hours (run navigation episodes on discrete graph)
format: High-level natural language instructions requiring navigation to a target location + object grounding in Matterport3D environments
metric: OSR, SR, SPL (navigation); RGSPL, RGS (remote grounding)
license: Matterport3D academic license (free, requires registration) + REVERIE CC BY-NC

name: Matterport3D
storage: ~80-100GB (6K equirectangular RGBD panoramas + mesh reconstructions + semantic labels)
format: RGBD panoramic scans of real indoor spaces with semantic annotations, mesh reconstructions, and navigation graph connectivity
license: Matterport3D Academic Use License (free, requires online registration)

name: BDD-X
num_samples: ~77K driving video clips (~26K with textual explanations)
format: Dashcam driving video clips with natural language action descriptions, justifications, and control signals (speed, steering angle)
metric: BLEU, METEOR, CIDEr for captions; MSE/RMSE for control signals

name: DriveGPT4
format: Video clips from BDD-X augmented with LLM-generated Q&A pairs, control signals (speed m/s, steering angle degrees), action descriptions and justifications
metric: RMSE, accuracy thresholds (A0.1, A0.5, A1.0, A5.0) for speed and turning angle prediction

name: DriveGPT4-V2
format: Synthetic data from CARLA simulator with vehicle decision outputs: steering angle, waypoints, route point coordinates. Single front-view camera images with Q&A format
metric: Theta Error (degrees), Point Error (L2 m), Speed Error (m/s)

name: OpenBookQA
format: 4-choice open-book QA with associated core science fact

name: StoryCloze
format: 4-sentence story with 2 candidate endings, choose correct conclusion

name: CosmosQA
format: 4-choice reading comprehension requiring commonsense reasoning over narrative text

name: SocialIQA
format: 3-choice QA about social interactions and everyday situations

name: RealToxicityPrompts
format: web-text prompts with toxicity scores; split into challenging and standard subsets
metric: toxicity score (Perspective API), Expected Maximum Toxicity

name: ToxiGen
format: machine-generated implicit hate speech targeting 13 minority groups; binary toxic/benign labels

name: VITON-HD
format: 1024x768 frontal-view female person images paired with upper-body clothing images

name: DressCode
num_samples: ~53,792 image-garment pairs across upper-body, lower-body, and dresses; 15,366 upper-body pairs
format: 1024x768 person images paired with garment images across three clothing categories

name: Beyond8Bits
storage: ~1.5-3TB (44K 10-bit HDR video clips at 1080p-360p, multiple bitrate tiers 0.2-5Mbps)
format: HDR (PQ/BT.2020 10-bit HEVC) video clips up to 10 seconds with MOS from >1.5M crowd ratings (AMT); landscape and portrait orientations; diverse UGC scenes
metric: SRCC, PLCC, KRCC, RMSE vs MOS

name: LIVE-HDR
storage: ~20GB (professional HDR video clips with subjective MOS)
format: Annotated HDR video clips with human MOS from controlled lab study
metric: SRCC, PLCC, KRCC, RMSE vs MOS

name: SFV+HDR
format: HDR video clips derived from YouTube Structured Format Video dataset with MOS annotations
metric: SRCC, PLCC, KRCC, RMSE vs MOS

name: I2P (Inappropriate Image Prompts)
eval_time: hours (requires running T2I model + NudeNet detector on all prompts)
format: Text prompts covering 7 inappropriate concept categories (hate, harassment, violence, self-harm, sexual, shocking, illegal activity)
metric: NudeNet detection count per body-part category; lower is better for erasure evaluation
notes: Benchmark for evaluating concept erasure and safety of text-to-image models; introduced by Schramowski et al. 2023

name: Ring-A-Bell
eval_time: hours (requires running T2I/T2V inference + NudeNet detection)
format: Adversarial text prompts designed to bypass concept erasure methods via semantic similarity attacks; tests both individual and union attack variants
metric: Attack success rate (lower is better for erased model)
notes: Adversarial robustness benchmark for concept erasure methods; uses concept retrieval to find semantically equivalent prompts that bypass token-level filtering

name: UnlearnDiffAtk
format: Adversarial prompts generated via attack algorithm targeting concept-erased diffusion models
metric: Attack success rate (% of explicit content generated despite erasure)
notes: Evaluates robustness of concept erasure methods against gradient-based adversarial prompt attacks; introduced by Zhang et al. 2024

name: ReFlux
format: Adversarial prompts specifically designed for flow-matching transformer models (e.g., Flux.1) to test concept erasure robustness
access: Introduced in paper evaluating Flux safety; details in corresponding paper
notes: Robustness benchmark specifically targeting Flux-based concept erasure methods

name: 200-Artist Dataset
eval_time: hours (requires generating style images + CLIP evaluation)
format: Artist names split into erasure and preservation groups; evaluation via CLIP score alignment between generated images and artist style descriptions
metric: ACC_e (CLIP score for erased styles, lower is better), ACC_ir (CLIP score for preserved styles, higher is better), H_a = ACC_ir - ACC_e (overall balance)
access: Introduced by MACE (Mass Concept Erasure); https://github.com/Shilin-LU/MACE
notes: Used to evaluate artistic style erasure in concept erasure papers; part of MACE benchmark suite

name: Pick-a-Pic
format: Crowdsourced human preference pairs for text-to-image generation; users pick preferred image from two candidates given a text prompt; used to train PickScore reward model

name: DrawBench
format: 200 challenging text prompts across 11 categories (colors, counting, conflicting, DALL-E, descriptions, Gary Marcus, misspellings, positional, rare words, Reddit, text) for evaluating text-to-image generation
metric: human preference win rate, CLIPScore, FID

name: PartiPrompts
format: 1632 English text prompts spanning 12 categories (abstract, world knowledge, arts, illustrations, artifacts, people, animals, food & beverage, transportation, plants, outdoor, indoor) for comprehensive T2I evaluation
metric: human preference win rate, CLIPScore, FID
access: https://github.com/google-research/parti (Yu et al., TMLR 2022 / Parti paper)

name: HPSv2
format: Human Preference Score v2: reward model + benchmark for evaluating T2I generation quality from human preference perspective; covers anime, photo, concept-art, and paintings styles; test benchmark with human preference annotations
metric: HPSv2 score (0-1), Pearson correlation with human preferences

name: ImageReward
format: Reward model trained on expert human preference annotations for text-to-image generation; outputs scalar reward signal; used as external reward in RL post-training of diffusion models
metric: ImageReward score, Pearson correlation with human preferences, Normalized Reward

name: PickScore
format: CLIP-based reward model trained on Pick-a-Pic preference dataset; outputs scalar preference score for (prompt, image) pairs; used as external reward signal in RL fine-tuning of T2I diffusion models
metric: win rate on Pick-a-Pic test set, human preference correlation

name: UnifiedReward
format: Unified reward model for both multimodal understanding and generation; supports image and video reward scoring; trained with a think-then-score paradigm; used as external reward in RL post-training of generative models
metric: correlation with human preferences, GenAI-Bench score

name: D-NeRF Dataset
format: monocular synthetic dynamic scenes rendered from known deformation fields; separate train/test viewpoints

name: Objaverse
format: 3D objects with multi-view rendered RGB images and camera poses

name: Google Scanned Objects (GSO)
storage: ~50GB (3D scanned household items with multi-view renders)
format: High-quality 3D scanned household objects with multi-view images and poses

name: Fashion-MNIST
format: 28x28 grayscale images of 10 fashion categories (60k train / 10k test)

name: BTCV
format: 3D abdominal CT volumes with 13-organ labels from the Multi-Atlas Labeling Beyond the Cranial Vault challenge (MICCAI 2015)

name: Medical Segmentation Decathlon (MSD)
format: 3D NIfTI medical volumes (CT and MRI) across 10 segmentation tasks including liver, brain, heart, lung, prostate, etc.

name: TotalSegmentator
num_samples: 1228 CT scans with 104 anatomical structure labels
eval_time: n/a (used for shape bank extraction or model training)
format: 3D CT volumes with dense per-voxel labels for 104 anatomical structures across the whole body

name: MSD (Medical Segmentation Decathlon)
num_samples: 10 tasks; Task02 (Heart): 30 MRI; Task06 (Lung): 96 CT; Task09 (Spleen): 61 CT (80/20 splits per task)
eval_time: 1-4 hours per task depending on architecture
format: 3D volumetric medical images (CT/MRI) with segmentation masks across 10 diverse anatomical targets; standardized NIfTI format with train/test splits; Antonelli et al. Nature Communications 2022

name: RadGenome-ChestCT
num_samples: ~5000 chest CT volumes with grounded vision-language annotations
eval_time: n/a (used as pre-training data for SSL baselines)
format: 3D chest CT scans with radiology report-grounded region annotations; used for self-supervised pre-training of 3D medical ViTs (SwinMM, SwinUNETR-SSL)

name: Occ3D-nuScenes
num_samples: 850 annotated scenes (700 train / 150 val), ~34k annotated frames with 6-camera surround-view inputs; 150 test scenes excluded due to missing LiDAR
storage: ~50-100GB (occupancy annotations only; raw nuScenes data ~1.4TB required separately)
eval_time: hours (inference over full val set + mIoU/IoU computation)
format: 3D voxel-wise semantic occupancy annotations over 80m x 80m x 6.4m ego-centric range at 0.4m voxel resolution; 18 semantic classes (16 object + free-space + other); derived from nuScenes with LiDAR-based dense labeling and camera mask supervision
metric: mIoU (mean Intersection-over-Union over semantic classes), IoU (binary occupied/free)

name: Fishyscapes
num_samples: ~1,405 total (30 val + 1000 test Static; 100 val + 275 test Lost&Found)
format: Cityscapes-based driving images with overlaid anomalous objects; pixel-level OOD masks

name: NeRF Blender Synthetic Dataset
num_samples: 8 synthetic scenes (Chair, Drums, Ficus, Hotdog, Lego, Materials, Mic, Ship) × 100 train + 100 val + 200 test views
format: Rendered 800x800 RGBA images from Blender with camera poses; each scene has train/val/test splits

name: Stanford 3D Shapes
num_samples: 5 high-resolution 3D meshes (Thai Statue, Lucy, Armadillo, Dragon, Buddha)
format: High-resolution 3D triangle meshes suitable for signed distance field (SDF) learning; voxelized or point-sampled for INR tasks

name: VideoMME
num_samples: 2700 QA pairs across 900 videos (254 hours total)
eval_time: hours (40h on 1xA100 for full evaluation with EFS-style preprocessing)
format: Multi-choice video QA covering short/medium/long durations, 12 subtasks (perception, reasoning, OCR, etc.)

name: CelebA-Spoof
format: Face images with rich annotations: 10 spoof types (print/screen/mask/etc.), 43 attributes, bounding boxes
metric: HTER / AUC (for FAS models trained on it)

name: MSU-MFSD
format: Video clips of real/spoof faces (printed photo and video replay attacks), cropped face sequences
license: research only (request from MSU PRIP lab)

name: CASIA-MFSD
format: Video clips (printed photo, video replay, cut photo attacks) from CASIA Face Anti-Spoofing Database

name: CASIA-FASD
format: Same as CASIA-MFSD; printed photo, video replay, cut photo attacks on live subjects

name: REPLAY-ATTACK
format: Video clips of face presentation attacks (print and video replay) from Idiap Research Institute

name: OULU-NPU
format: Mobile face presentation attack database with 4 protocols testing generalization across devices/conditions

name: SIW
format: Spoof-in-the-Wild dataset with 165 subjects, 8 spoof types including print and replay variants

name: SIW-M-V2
format: SIW-Makeup V2: multi-type 3D mask and makeup attacks with 14 spoof subcategories

name: Rose-Youtu
format: Face liveness detection dataset with 5 types of attacks (print, replay, mask) and 5 mobile devices

name: HKBU-MARs-V1+
format: 3D mask face presentation attack database with 7 3D mask types, multiple environments and sensors

name: WMCA
format: Wide Multi-Channel Presentation Attack database with 14 attack types, multiple channels (color, depth, IR, thermal)

name: CASIA-SURF-3DMask
format: High-fidelity 3D mask attack dataset from CASIA-SURF challenge with multi-modal (RGB, depth, IR) captures

name: HiFiMask
format: High-Fidelity 3D Mask face presentation attack database with transparent/plaster/resin/paper/silicone masks

name: MMMU
format: Multi-discipline multimodal multiple-choice QA across 30 subjects and 6 disciplines requiring expert-level knowledge

name: SEED-Bench
format: Multimodal benchmark with multiple-choice questions for generative comprehension across 12 evaluation dimensions

name: ChartQA
format: Chart images with question-answer pairs requiring visual and logical reasoning over bar/line/pie charts

name: DocVQA
format: Document images with questions requiring understanding of text, layout, and structure in scanned documents

name: InfoVQA
format: Infographic images with QA pairs requiring understanding of complex data visualizations and information graphics

name: DPG-Bench
format: Dense prompt gallery for text-to-image evaluation; tests faithful rendering of long, information-dense prompts with complex entity relationships
metric: GPT-4V-based scoring across Global, Entity, Attribute, Relation, Other dimensions

name: AesEval-Bench
storage: ~5-10GB (1500 graphic design images with JSON metadata, QA pairs across 3 tasks x 12 indicators)
eval_time: hours (depends on model; API models may be rate-limited)
format: Graphic design images (from Crello) + JSON metadata + QA pairs; three tasks: aesthetic judgment (yes/no), region selection (4-choice), precise localization (bbox)
metric: accuracy (judgment and region selection), IoU (precise localization)

name: AesEval-Train
storage: ~15-30GB (30k QA pairs with design images, reasoning paths with bbox annotations, JSON metadata)
format: Graphic design images + JSON metadata + QA pairs with indicator-grounded reasoning paths (bbox coordinates + textual explanations)

name: Crello
storage: ~10-20GB (design images + element-level JSON metadata with layout, font, color info)
format: Graphic design images with element-level metadata in JSON (positions, fonts, colors, layers)

name: MCMR
num_samples: 3,997 queries and 104,981 product candidates across 5 domains (upper/bottom clothing, shoes, jewelry, furniture)
format: Natural-language multi-condition query paired with image+text product candidates; dual-evidence design requiring both visual and textual constraint satisfaction

name: ACDC
storage: ~1-2GB (compressed NIfTI 3D cine MRI + segmentation masks, 100 labeled subjects + 50 test)
format: 3D cardiac cine MRI volumes (ED/ES frames with LV/Myo/RV segmentation labels) resampled to 1.5x1.5x3.15mm, 128x128x32 crops; split: 90 train / 10 val / 50 test
metric: Dice score (LV/Myo/RV), Hausdorff distance, ejection fraction MAE

name: MM2
format: 3D cardiac cine MRI from multiple centres/diseases/views with LV/Myo/RV segmentation labels; split: 156 train / 38 val / 157 test; also known as M&Ms-2 (Multi-Disease, Multi-View & Multi-Center Right Ventricular Segmentation Challenge)
metric: Dice score (LV/Myo/RV), ejection fraction MAE, myocardial thickness MAE

name: USC-SIPI Image Database
num_samples: hundreds of natural and synthetic images
format: Grayscale and color images in various resolutions organized into categories (miscellaneous, textures, aerials, sequences); commonly used for image restoration benchmarking

name: CAVE Multispectral Dataset
format: 31-channel multispectral images at 512x512 pixels covering wavelengths 400-700nm; includes diverse real-world scenes

name: Hyperspectral Remote Sensing Scenes
num_samples: multiple scenes (Washington DC, Botswana, Salinas, etc.)
format: Hyperspectral image cubes with hundreds of spectral bands; includes airborne and satellite hyperspectral data for land-use classification and remote sensing research

name: SHOT Point Cloud Dataset
format: 3D point clouds of toy figures (Doll, Duck, Frog, Mario, PeterRabbit, Squirrel); used for point cloud recovery/completion benchmarking

name: YUV Video Sequences
num_samples: multiple sequences (News, Carphone, Container, Salesman, etc.)
format: Uncompressed YUV video sequences at various resolutions (QCIF, CIF); standard benchmark sequences for video coding and restoration research

name: Egolife
num_samples: ~240 hours of daily life first-person video with QA pairs
format: Long-form first-person daily life video captured by smart glasses with multi-choice QA requiring long-horizon temporal reasoning over hours of footage

name: EPIC-KITCHENS
num_samples: ~45K action segments across 700 hours of egocentric kitchen activity video (EPIC-KITCHENS-100)
format: First-person RGB video of kitchen activities with frame-level action annotations (verb + noun + action class); multiple tasks including action recognition, object detection, and action anticipation

name: ImageNet-V2
format: ImageNet validation images re-collected with stricter selection protocol to test robustness of ImageNet classifiers

name: ImageNet-Sketch
format: Sketch-style images of ImageNet-1K classes for OOD evaluation of visual recognition models
license: research use (derived from web scraping; see paper)

name: ImageNet-A
format: Naturally adversarial images that fool ImageNet classifiers; curated from real photographs across 200 ImageNet classes

name: ImageNet-R
format: ImageNet Renditions: art, cartoons, deviantart, graffiti, embroidery, graphics, origami, paintings, patterns, sculptures, sketches, tattoos, toys, and video game renditions of 200 ImageNet classes

name: SimpleVQA
format: Image + short natural language question pairs; static, verifiable reference answers; diverse topics

name: MMSearch
format: 171 image-based queries requiring cross-modal visual and textual retrieval to answer complex questions

name: LiveVQA
format: Visual question answering focused on up-to-date visual knowledge; sourced from recent news, video, and academic platforms

name: FVQA
format: Image-question-answer triplets with supporting facts from commonsense knowledge bases; requires external knowledge retrieval

name: InfoSeek
format: Information-seeking visual questions requiring fine-grained knowledge beyond typical VQA; human-annotated and auto-generated pairs
access: InfoSeek (Chen et al., arXiv 2023); evaluation subset of 2000 used by MMSearch-R1

name: BrowseComp-VL
format: Multimodal browsing benchmark extending BrowseComp; requires strategic planning, sequential evidence synthesis, and cross-modal retrieval across text, images, and web content

name: Oil Painting Brushstroke Dataset
storage: <200MB (520 scanned oil-painting strokes at 295x295 px, plus augmented copies)
format: Scanned oil-painting brushstrokes from a single professional artist drawn on a 20x26 grid canvas, cropped and standardized to 295x295 pixels, with background removal and color normalization
