name: Open Images Dataset v4
num_samples: ~9M training images (1.7M with bounding box annotations, ~41M labels across 600 categories)
storage: ~565GB (full training set compressed); subsets range from <1GB to hundreds of GB
eval_time: varies by task and subset size
format: Diverse internet photos with image-level labels, bounding boxes, segmentation masks, visual relationships, and localized narratives
metric: mAP, accuracy, FID (used as training subset for generative models)
license: CC BY 4.0 (annotations); images under original licenses

name: LLFF
eval_time: hours per experiment (per-scene optimization ~1-4 hours, evaluation minutes)
format: Posed RGB photos for forward-facing novel view synthesis; camera poses from COLMAP; standard train/test splits at 2/3/6 training views for sparse-view benchmarks

name: ISIC 2017
format: variable-resolution RGB dermoscopy images + binary lesion segmentation masks; skin lesion analysis challenge from the 2017 ISBI Symposium (ISIC archive)
license: ISIC data sharing agreement (research, CC BY-NC 4.0 equivalent)

name: TN3K
storage: ~6GB (thyroid ultrasound images with pixel-level nodule annotations)
format: variable-resolution grayscale thyroid ultrasound images from 2421 patients + binary thyroid nodule segmentation masks; TN3K = Thyroid Nodule 3K dataset

name: PadChest
format: Chest X-ray images with multi-label radiologist annotations (174 findings, 19 differential diagnoses); frontal views from Hospital San Juan, Spain

name: CheXpert
format: Chest X-ray images with 14 automated radiology report-extracted labels (uncertainty labels); Stanford Hospital data
license: Stanford University Dataset Research Use Agreement (free)

name: ChestX-ray14
format: Chest X-ray images with 14 disease labels mined from radiology reports; NIH Clinical Center data; also known as NIH ChestX-ray14 or ChestX-ray8

name: NAVSIM
num_samples: ~85k planning scenarios (curated to 24k for RL training)
storage: ~100-200GB (OpenScene sensor data subset with camera images, ego states, and map annotations)
format: Planning-oriented autonomous driving dataset built on OpenScene nuPlan data; front-camera images + ego state + navigation commands → 8-step future trajectory; includes NAVSIMv1 and NAVSIMv2 variants
metric: PDMS (Predictive Driver Model Score, v1) and EPDMS (Extended PDMS, v2) combining NC/DAC/TTC/EP/CF sub-scores

name: NAVSIMv1
format: NAVSIMv1 benchmark split for closed-loop trajectory evaluation; 5 sub-metrics: NC, DAC, TTC, CF, EP

name: NAVSIMv2
format: NAVSIMv2 benchmark split with expanded metrics over NAVSIMv1; 9 sub-metrics: NC, DAC, DDC, TLC, EP, TTC, LK, HC, EC

name: DriveLM
num_samples: ~360k graph-structured QA pairs from ~155k nuScenes keyframes
format: Graph visual question answering on nuScenes driving scenes; QA covers perception, prediction, planning with explicit causal and logical structure; driving with graph VQA paradigm

name: NuScenes-QA
format: Multi-modal VQA benchmark for autonomous driving scenarios; questions cover object existence, counts, status, and spatial relationships from nuScenes sensor data

name: NuInstruct
num_samples: ~91k multi-view instruction-following QA pairs from nuScenes
format: Multi-view, multi-type, chain-of-thought instruction-following dataset for autonomous driving; covers BEV understanding, localization, planning, causal reasoning with multi-view camera inputs

name: ImpromptuVLA
format: Open weights and open data driving VLA dataset; includes diverse instruction-following driving scenarios with CoT reasoning and trajectory outputs for end-to-end autonomous driving

name: GroundedSurg
storage: ~2-5GB (surgical images + segmentation masks + bounding boxes + center points + language annotations in JSON)
eval_time: hours per model (zero-shot VLM inference over 1,071 instances)
format: Surgical images paired with natural-language queries, pixel-level segmentation masks, bounding boxes, and center point annotations; spans 4 surgical procedure types (ophthalmic, laparoscopic, robotic, open surgery); derived from InSeg1, InSeg2, SISVE, EndoVis, CholecInstanceSeg
metric: Mask IoU, mIoU@0.1/0.3, BBox IoU, NDE (Normalized Distance Error), Dice
license: CC BY or research use (per source datasets); GroundedSurg annotations: research use
notes: First language-conditioned, instance-level surgical tool grounding benchmark (arXiv:2603.01108). Evaluates models in zero-shot mode. Queries generated by Qwen-2.5 VL-Instruct and clinician-verified. SAM2/SAM3 used as frozen segmentation backend.

name: xBD
num_samples: ~11K paired 1024x1024 RGB satellite images (9168 train, 933 val, 933 test)
format: Paired pre/post-disaster RGB satellite images with building localization and 4-level damage classification pixel masks (JSON polygon annotations)

name: Pakistan Flooding (EBD)
num_samples: 3540 paired 512x512 RGB images (2478 train, 531 val, 531 test)
format: Paired pre/post-disaster RGB satellite images with 4-level building damage masks; part of EBD collection covering July 2022 Pakistan floods
access: EBD dataset collection (Wang et al., 2025 arXiv)

name: Turkey Earthquake (EBD)
num_samples: 944 paired 512x512 RGB images (566 train, 189 val, 189 test)
format: Paired pre/post-disaster RGB satellite images with 4-level building damage masks; covers Kahramanmaras earthquakes Feb 2023
access: EBD dataset collection (Wang et al., 2025 arXiv)

name: Hurricane Ida (EBD)
format: Paired pre/post-disaster RGB satellite images with 4-level building damage masks; covers Hurricane Ida 2021 Louisiana
access: EBD dataset collection (Wang et al., 2025 arXiv)

name: ColoRadar
num_samples: ~43000 synchronized radar frames (single-chip and cascade radar + LiDAR)
format: Millimeter-wave radar ADC data (single-chip and cascade configurations) synchronized with LiDAR point clouds across indoor and outdoor scenes; frustum-based voxelization used to derive occupancy ground truth from LiDAR
metric: Chamfer Distance (CD), F-score, Clutter Point Ratio (CPR)

name: RaDelft
num_samples: ~21000 frames (~35 min at 10Hz) across 7 large-scale urban scenes
format: Long-range cascade millimeter-wave radar ADC data synchronized with LiDAR in large-scale urban driving environments; used for radar point cloud enhancement and uncertainty field evaluation

name: SemanticKITTI
format: LiDAR point cloud sequences (22 sequences, 64-beam Velodyne HDL-64E) with per-point semantic labels, 19-class taxonomy
metric: mIoU per class and mean IoU

name: SynLiDAR
format: Synthetic LiDAR point cloud scans (19 billion points) generated in Unreal Engine 4, 32-class labels mapped to 19-class taxonomy

name: SemanticSTF
format: Real LiDAR scans from STF dataset under adverse weather conditions (snow, dense fog, light fog, rain); 1326 train/250 val/500 test; 19-class labels
metric: mIoU per weather condition and overall

name: SemanticKITTI-C
format: Corrupted versions of SemanticKITTI point clouds via physics-based simulation of adverse weather; 19-class labels

name: SlideBench(TCGA)
num_samples: TCGA cohort whole-slide images with multiple-choice VQA pairs (Microscopy and Diagnosis subsets)
format: Gigapixel WSIs with multiple-choice VQA questions covering microscopy and diagnosis tasks
metric: Overall accuracy, Microscopy accuracy, Diagnosis accuracy
access: https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov/ (TCGA slides); benchmark from SlideChat (Chen et al. CVPR 2025)

name: SlideBench(BCNB)
num_samples: Breast Cancer Needle Biopsy WSIs with VQA pairs
format: Gigapixel WSIs with multiple-choice VQA questions (zero-shot transfer benchmark)
access: https://github.com/bupt-ai-cz/BCNB; benchmark from SlideChat (Chen et al. CVPR 2025)

name: WSI-VQA
format: Whole-slide images with VQA pairs for slide-level reasoning evaluation
access: SlideChat benchmark suite (Chen et al. CVPR 2025)

name: TCGA-BRCA
format: TCGA breast cancer H&E whole-slide images with IDC/ILC subtype labels for MIL binary classification

name: TCGA-NSCLC
num_samples: ~1,000 non-small cell lung cancer WSIs (LUAD + LUSC)
format: TCGA lung cancer H&E whole-slide images with LUAD/LUSC subtype labels for MIL binary classification

name: PANDA (Prostate cANcer graDe Assessment)
format: Prostate biopsy H&E whole-slide images with Gleason grade group labels (0-5) for MIL classification

name: SVRT
num_samples: 23 tasks x (10,000 train + 500 val + 1,000 test) per task; reformulated as 4-choice problem
format: 4-choice abstract visual reasoning: identify outlier among 4 images; 23 tasks defined by 2 rules each, constructed from 7 attributes (shape, position, size, rotation, flip, inside, contact)
access: Fleuret et al., PNAS 2011; reformulated for CVR setting by Zerroug et al. NeurIPS 2022

name: CVR
num_samples: 103 tasks x (10,000 train + 500 val + 1,000 test) per task
format: 4-choice abstract visual reasoning: identify outlier among 4 images; 103 compositional rules from 9 attributes (shape, position, size, color, rotation, flip, count, inside, contact); 20 single-rule, 65 two-rule, 9 three-plus-rule tasks

name: MC2R
num_samples: 103 tasks x (10,000 train + 500 val + 1,000 test) per task
format: 5-image abstract visual reasoning: 3 conforming + 2 outlier images; rules hierarchically composed using logical (and/or/not), relational and arithmetic operators from 9 attribute types; harder than CVR due to multi-answer format

name: CBSD68
format: 68 color natural images from the Berkeley Segmentation Dataset (BSDS500), used for color Gaussian denoising evaluation

name: Kodak24
format: 24 lossless true-color images from Kodak photo suite for denoising and SR evaluation

name: McMaster
format: 18 color images from the McMaster dataset for color demosaicking and denoising evaluation

name: SIDD
num_samples: ~30000 noisy/clean image pairs (training); 1280 validation patches; 1280 test patches
format: Real-world noisy/clean smartphone camera image pairs from 5 smartphone cameras in 10 scenes under various lighting conditions (SIDD and SIDD+)

name: DND
num_samples: 50 real noisy images (no public clean GT, online evaluation)
format: 50 real-world high-resolution noisy image patches from 4 consumer cameras; test by submitting denoised results to online server

name: FFHQR
num_samples: ~70000 high-resolution face images with retouching labels
eval_time: minutes (inference on test split of ~1000 images)
format: High-resolution portrait images (from FFHQ base) with retouched reference images; used for evaluating face retouching methods via no-reference perceptual metrics
metric: NIQE, NIMA, MUSIQ, MANIQA, NRQM, TOPIQ, FID, ArcFace similarity

name: FRPref-10K
format: Face retouching preference triplets (input, candidate A, candidate B) with multi-dimensional fine-grained annotations across 5 aesthetic dimensions (skin smoothing, blemish removal, texture quality, clarity, identity preservation); annotated by ensemble of VLMs (GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-VL-72B, Gemini 2.5 Pro) + human verification
access: Not publicly released; constructed for BeautyGRPO (arXiv:2603.01163)

name: I2V-Edit-Bench
num_samples: 60 videos with corresponding edited first frames
eval_time: ~2-3 hours per method (1-3 min per video on A100)
format: Video clips from DAVIS dataset and internet sources with edited first frames created via Photoshop and MagicBrush; 6 editing types: object replacement, style transfer, adding/removing objects, attribute change, background editing
metric: CLIP score (edit fidelity), Warp Error (temporal consistency), CLIP score+ / Warp Error+ / SSIM+ / PSNR+ / LPIPS+ (non-editing area preservation)
license: research (not publicly released as of March 2026)
notes: Custom benchmark introduced in FREE-Edit (Li et al. arXiv:2603.01164). Edited frames from DAVIS + internet videos. Not released publicly.

name: GameVerse
num_sessions: 458 human gameplay sessions + VLM eval sessions
storage: ~300-500GB (game installations for 15 games including commercial titles like Forza Horizon 5, RDR2, Genshin Impact; free/indie games are <1GB each; expert walkthrough videos ~5-10GB)
eval_time: days for full evaluation across all 15 games and 7 VLMs
format: Interactive video game environments with dual action spaces (semantic and GUI), video-based reflection pipeline, and VLM-based milestone scoring; 15 games spanning 5 cognitive categories (Markov Grid, Non-Real-time Linear, Non-Real-time Non-linear, Real-time Linear, Real-time Non-linear) at 3 difficulty tiers
metric: Normalized score (0-100) per game; game-specific metrics (intrinsic scores for 8 games, VLM-based milestone scores for 7 games)
license: Custom benchmark license (website release); individual game licenses vary; some commercial titles required
notes: Introduced by Zhang et al. 2025 (arXiv:2603.06656). Key features: cognitive hierarchical taxonomy, reflect-and-retry paradigm with failure/tutorial video reflection, dual semantic+GUI action space, VLM milestone scoring using Gemini-3-pro for games without intrinsic scores.

name: SumMe
format: YouTube user videos with per-frame importance scores from multiple annotators; 5-fold cross-validation; evaluated with Kendall tau and Spearman rho rank correlation

name: TVSum
format: YouTube videos with per-frame importance scores from 20 annotators; 5-fold cross-validation; evaluated with Kendall tau and Spearman rho

name: Mr. HiSum
format: YouTube videos with Most Replayed statistics as frame-level importance proxy; evaluated with Kendall tau, Spearman rho, mAP50, mAP15
metric: Kendall tau, Spearman rho, mAP50, mAP15

name: MoSu
format: YouTube in-the-wild videos with visual, text (transcript), and audio modalities; Most Replayed statistics as frame-level importance ground truth; 10 thematic clusters from YouTube-8M
metric: Kendall tau, Spearman rho, mAP50, mAP15

name: CAMELYON-16
format: Whole Slide Images (WSI) + pixel-level tumor annotations; 270 training + 129 test slides from lymph nodes

name: CAMELYON-17
format: Whole Slide Images (WSI) + slide-level labels; 500 public slides from 5 medical centers

name: BRACS
format: Whole Slide Images (WSI) + slide-level labels (benign/atypical/malignant breast tumors); 395 train / 65 val / 87 test

name: 3Dcompat200
format: 3D shapes with fine- and coarse-grained semantic part annotations across 200 everyday object categories; used for promptable 3D part segmentation. Train/test splits with ~2K test shapes annotated at coarse and fine granularity.
metric: mIoU (mean Intersection-over-Union per part, averaged across instances)

name: ShapeNet-Part
format: 3D point clouds from 16 ShapeNet object categories annotated with 50 semantic part labels total; standard benchmark for 3D part segmentation (Yi et al., TOG 2016)

name: PartNet-E
num_samples: ~45 object categories with fine-grained hierarchical part annotations
format: 3D shapes with fine-grained hierarchical part annotations focusing on object materials and structural details; used to evaluate open-world promptable 3D segmentation with 45 categories

name: Doosan A0509 3D Object Position Dataset
num_samples: ~100,000 images across ~750 objects, 5 sequences per object
format: Monocular RGB images from wrist-mounted Logitech Brio webcam on Doosan A0509 robot arm; synchronized with TCP position/orientation metadata; 2-6 fps sequences of robot approaching objects; single and multi-object settings; varying lighting conditions
metric: Mean Absolute Error (MAE mm), Euclidean distance error (mm), CDF of error
access: not publicly available (contact Fraunhofer HHI authors)
notes: Introduced by Wahl et al. arXiv:2603.01224. Training/val/test split: 90/10 with group-based split to prevent object height leakage. The dataset is specific to the Doosan A0509 robot arm workspace and cannot be reproduced without the physical hardware.

name: LEVIR-CD
num_samples: 10192 image pairs (7120 train, 1024 val, 2048 test) at 256x256 pixels
format: Bitemporal high-resolution satellite image pairs (0.5m/pixel) with binary change masks focusing on building construction/demolition

name: DSIFN-CD
num_samples: 15952 image pairs (14400 train, 1360 val, 192 test) at 256x256 pixels
format: Bitemporal high-resolution Google Earth image pairs from 6 Chinese cities with binary land-cover change masks

name: CDD (Change Detection Dataset)
num_samples: 16000 image pairs (10000 train, 3000 val, 3000 test) at 256x256 pixels
format: Bitemporal Google Earth image pairs (0.03-1m/pixel) capturing seasonal changes and disaster-related transformations with binary change masks

name: WHU-CD
num_samples: 7434 image pairs (5947 train, 744 val, 743 test) at 256x256 pixels
format: Bitemporal aerial image pairs (0.3m/pixel) from Christchurch, NZ (2012-2016) with binary building change masks

name: LLaVA-Wild
format: 60 challenging open-ended questions over diverse real-world images; evaluated by GPT-4 judge comparing to reference answers
metric: GPT-4 judge score (relative to reference model)

name: Vision-Flan-186K
format: Diverse multimodal instruction-following dataset spanning 191 distinct tasks (classification, QA, captioning, OCR, reasoning, etc.); designed for broad task coverage with fewer samples per task than LLaVA-665K

name: MAMA-MIA Dataset
format: 3D fat-suppressed DCE-MRI NIfTI volumes with voxel-wise tumor segmentation masks, bounding boxes, and clinical metadata (age, menopausal status, tumor subtype, pCR label)
access: https://www.ub.edu/mama-mia / https://github.com/BCN-AIM/MamaMIA (aggregates ISPY-1, ISPY-2, NACT, DUKE from TCIA)

name: ISPY-1 (ACRIN 6657) Breast DCE-MRI
format: 3D T1-weighted DCE breast MRI sagittal volumes with tumor segmentation and pCR labels

name: ISPY-2 Breast DCE-MRI
format: 3D T1-weighted DCE breast MRI axial volumes with pCR labels and clinical metadata

name: DUKE Breast Cancer DCE-MRI
format: 3D T1-weighted DCE breast MRI axial volumes with tumor location annotations

name: CHAIR
format: Image captioning hallucination evaluation using COCO object annotations; computes Ci (instance-level) and Cs (sentence-level) hallucination rates plus recall and caption length
metric: Ci (hallucinated objects / all mentioned objects), Cs (captions with hallucinated objects / all captions), Recall, Len

name: MMBench-CN
format: Chinese translation of MMBench; human-curated vision-language questions grouped by skill with Chinese instructions

name: PyCMG Concrete Microstructure Volumetric Dataset
num_samples: 13 unique 256x256x256 3D volumes (10 train, 3 test) of simulated concrete microstructures
format: 3D volumetric arrays (256x256x256 voxels) with paired simulated neutron CT and X-ray CT projections under various acquisition settings

name: SLAM PGO Benchmark Suite (MIT/CSAIL/Intel/KITTI/Manhattan/City/Ais2klinik/Grid/Garage/Sphere/Torus/Cubicle/Rim/SmallGrid)
num_samples: 15 pose graph datasets ranging from 125 to 15115 poses and up to 22236 measurements
eval_time: seconds to 350s per dataset on laptop CPU
format: SLAM pose graph files (.g2o format) with 2D/3D relative pose measurements
metric: objective value (QCQP/SDP), runtime, global optimality certificate
access: Various sources: MIT/CSAIL/Intel from https://lucacarlone.mit.edu/datasets/, KITTI from https://www.cvlibs.net/datasets/kitti/, synthetic datasets from https://github.com/david-m-rosen/SE-Sync

name: Victoria Park Landmark SLAM Dataset
format: 2D landmark SLAM dataset with pose and landmark observations

name: Trees Landmark SLAM Dataset
format: 2D outdoor landmark SLAM dataset

name: UTIAS Range-Aided SLAM Datasets (Goats/Plaza/SingleDrone)
num_samples: 5 datasets: Goats16 (201 poses), Goats15 (472 poses), Plaza1 (9658 poses), Plaza2 (4091 poses), SingleDrone (1754 poses, 3D)
eval_time: seconds to 200s per dataset on CPU
format: Range-aided SLAM datasets with pose and range measurements (2D and 3D)
metric: SDP value, refined objective value, global optimality certificate

name: WHU-Hi-LongKou
format: hyperspectral image cube (550x400 pixels, 270 bands, 400-1000nm wavelength range) captured by airborne hyperspectral sensor over LongKou, China

name: WHU-Hi-HongHu
format: hyperspectral image cube (940x475 pixels, 270 bands, 400-1000nm wavelength range) captured by airborne hyperspectral sensor over HongHu, China

name: Salinas Valley (AVIRIS)
format: hyperspectral image cube (512x217 pixels, 224 spectral bands) captured by AVIRIS sensor over Salinas Valley, California; widely used benchmark for HSI classification

name: QUH-Qingyun
num_samples: labeled pixels across multiple land-use classes
format: hyperspectral image cube captured over Qingyun region; part of the Qingyun University Hyperspectral dataset collection

name: UnsafeBench
format: Binary safe/unsafe image classification benchmark covering 9 harmful content categories (Hate, Violence, Self-Harm, Sexual, Shocking, Illegal, Deception, Political, Spam); includes both real and AI-generated images
metric: F1-score per category and overall accuracy
notes: arXiv:2405.03486. Introduced to evaluate image safety classifiers on real-world and AI-generated images.

name: LlavaGuardBench
format: Visual content safety evaluation benchmark covering 9 visual harm categories (O1-O9): Violence, Discriminatory, Sexual, Illegal, Disturbing, Personal info, Financial, Medical/Health, Legal/Ethical; each image labeled with detailed policy-conditioned verdicts
notes: arXiv:2406.05113. Benchmark and training dataset released by Helff et al. (TU Darmstadt / Armasuisse). Used as training data for QwenGuard and SafeGuard-VL.

name: SafeEditBench
num_samples: 128 images (62 safe-unsafe pairs with 5 policy levels = 620 evaluation instances)
format: Cross-policy image safety evaluation benchmark; 62 paired safe/unsafe images generated via Nano Banana image editing from LlavaGuard test images; evaluated under 5 distinct safety policies (L1 most permissive to L5 most restrictive); human-annotated labels
metric: F1-score per policy level and macro-averaged F1 across 5 policies; accuracy for all-safe L1 policy
access: not yet publicly released (as of arXiv:2603.01228)
notes: New benchmark introduced in arXiv:2603.01228 (SafeGuard-VL). Designed to test cross-policy generalization of safety guardrails. Unsafe images from LlavaGuard test set, safe counterparts generated by minimal image editing via Nano Banana.

name: MMT-Bench
format: Comprehensive multimodal benchmark for evaluating large VLMs towards multitask AGI; covers visual recognition, OCR, knowledge retrieval, commonsense reasoning, relation reasoning, attribute recognition, and more across 162 subtasks
notes: arXiv:2404.16006. Used as a general multimodal capability benchmark in SafeGuard-VL (arXiv:2603.01228).

name: RealWorldQA
format: Real-world visual QA benchmark with images from diverse real-world settings requiring practical spatial understanding and reasoning; multiple-choice format
notes: Released by xAI (Grok team) to evaluate models on practical real-world visual reasoning. Used as general capability benchmark in SafeGuard-VL (arXiv:2603.01228).

name: LlavaGuard training set
format: VLM safety training dataset with images labeled according to 9 visual harm taxonomy categories (O1-O9) with detailed policy-grounded rationales; JSON-structured annotations
notes: arXiv:2406.05113. Used as RL training data in SafeGuard-VL (arXiv:2603.01228) for policy-conditioned binary safe/unsafe discrimination.

name: Argoverse 1
format: Vehicle trajectory sequences with 2s observation → 3s prediction; HD map context (lane centerlines, crosswalks); multi-agent scenarios from Pittsburgh and Miami

name: Argoverse 2
format: Vehicle trajectory sequences with 5s observation → 6s prediction; richer HD map context; more complex multi-agent scenarios from 6 US cities; successor to Argoverse 1

name: MedMNIST-v2
num_samples: ~708K images across 12 2D tasks spanning radiology, microscopy, and visible light photography
format: Standardized 2D biomedical image classification suite with 12 tasks: PathMNIST, ChestMNIST, DermaMNIST, OCTMNIST, PneumoniaMNIST, RetinaMNIST, BreastMNIST, BloodMNIST, TissueMNIST, OrganAMNIST, OrganCMNIST, OrganSMNIST; all at 28x28, 64x64, 128x128, or 224x224 resolution

name: MedXpertQA
format: Expert-level medical reasoning benchmark requiring deep multi-step clinical logic across multiple medical imaging modalities and clinical knowledge domains; subset used as MedX-M in evaluation

name: BUSI-WHU
num_samples: 927 ultrasound images (561 benign, 387 malignant) with lesion masks
format: Grayscale breast ultrasound frames + binary lesion segmentation masks, two-class (benign/malignant)

name: NeRSemble
num_samples: 220 subjects, 16 synchronized viewpoints, dynamic expression videos (~3000+ multi-view frame sets used in NVB-Face)
format: Multi-view synchronized RGB video captures of human heads with 16 calibrated cameras, covering dynamic expressions
metric: SSIM / LPIPS / DISTS / FID / ID similarity / POSE error

name: LFW (Labeled Faces in the Wild)
format: Aligned face images of 5749 subjects collected from the web; used for face recognition and blind face restoration evaluation (LFW-Test subset)
metric: face verification accuracy / perceptual quality (SSIM, LPIPS, FID)

name: MVTec-AD
num_samples: 5354 images (3629 normal train + 1725 test with anomaly masks) across 15 object/texture categories
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on method
format: High-resolution industrial surface images with pixel-level anomaly masks; 15 categories including wood, metal, fabric and objects

name: KSDD2
num_samples: 2335 images (246 defective + 2089 non-defective surface images of steel)
format: RGB images of steel kos surfaces with binary pixel-level defect masks; mixed supervision for defect detection

name: RSDD
num_samples: ~195 rail surface images with defect annotations across 2 types (in-field and tank rail)
format: Grayscale/RGB rail surface images with binary anomaly masks; two subsets: in-field rail defects and tank surface defects

name: ColonDB
format: Colonoscopy frames with binary polyp segmentation masks; challenging low-resolution frames

name: RealIAD
num_samples: ~150K images across 30 industrial product categories with multi-view captures
format: Multi-view industrial anomaly images with pixel-level defect masks; 30 product types; diverse anomaly types per category

name: PKU-GoodsAD
num_samples: ~6124 images across 6 supermarket goods categories with normal/abnormal splits
format: RGB images of packaged supermarket goods with binary pixel-level defect masks; fine-grained anomaly types including surface defects, shape defects, contamination

name: DTD-Synthetic
num_samples: ~12 texture categories with synthetic anomaly generation
format: Synthetic anomaly dataset built on top of DTD textures with programmatically-generated defects; used for zero-shot anomaly detection training/evaluation

name: Anomaly-Instruct20K
storage: ~5GB (images from RealIAD, GoodsAD, DTD-Synthetic + structured text annotations)
format: Instruction-tuning dataset with structured 5-field annotations (Expectation, Observation, Diagnosis, Summary, Explanation) generated by InternS1-241B; covers diverse instruction types: Direct Segmentation, Describe-then-Segment, Segment-then-Explain

name: FloodNet+
storage: ~8GB (high-resolution UAV aerial images + pixel-wise semantic labels)
format: High-resolution UAV aerial imagery from post-flood scenes with 9-class semantic segmentation masks (water, road-flooded, road-non-flooded, building-flooded, building-non-flooded, vehicle, pool, grass, tree)
access: https://github.com/sahilkhose/FloodNet (Rahnemoonfar et al., IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing 2024)

name: RescueNet
storage: ~18GB (high-resolution UAV imagery with semantic segmentation labels)
format: UAV aerial imagery from post-earthquake disaster scenarios with 10-class semantic segmentation masks (background, water, building-no-damage, building-minor-damage, building-major-damage, building-total-destruction, vehicle, road-clear, road-blocked, tree)

name: D-Fire
format: UAV and ground-view RGB images of fire and smoke with 2-class object detection bounding boxes (fire, smoke) in YOLO format
access: https://github.com/gaiasd/DFireDataset (de Venancio et al., Neural Computing and Applications 2022)

name: LADD
storage: ~2GB (aerial drone imagery + YOLO-format bounding box annotations)
format: Aerial drone imagery for Search and Rescue with 1-class object detection (pedestrian) bounding boxes; captured from UAVs for small aerial target detection
access: Shuranov et al., Lacmus Drone Dataset 2023

name: ESOL
format: SMILES strings with aqueous solubility values (log mol/L) for drug-like small molecules

name: FreeSolv
format: SMILES strings with experimental and calculated hydration free energies (kcal/mol) for neutral molecules

name: MoleculeNet Lipophilicity
format: SMILES strings with experimental octanol/water distribution coefficients (logD at pH 7.4) for drug-like molecules from ChEMBL

name: AqSolDB
format: SMILES strings with curated aqueous solubility (log mol/L) and 2D molecular descriptors for diverse compounds; aggregated from 9 sources

name: OPERA 2.9
format: SMILES strings with computed/validated physicochemical properties (logP, melting point, boiling point, vapor pressure, water solubility) predicted by QSAR models from EPA

name: NIST ThermoML
num_samples: 100K+ thermophysical property measurements across thousands of compounds
format: XML-based thermophysical and thermochemical property data for pure compounds and mixtures; properties include boiling point, vapor pressure, viscosity, heat capacity, etc.

name: ECHA REACH
format: Registered chemical substance data including physicochemical and toxicological properties from EU registration dossiers; accessed by SMILES/InChI

name: Bradley Open Melting Point Dataset
num_samples: ~28000+ melting point values (original); ~3041 after curation in MultiPUFFIN
format: Open-access melting point data (°C) for organic compounds compiled by Jean-Claude Bradley from various sources

name: Sun et al. Flash Point Dataset
format: SMILES strings with flash point values (K) for fuel mixtures and pure compounds; curated for deep learning-based molecular property prediction
access: Supplementary material of Sun et al. Fuel, 239:109-116, 2019

name: Chew et al. Viscosity Dataset
format: SMILES strings with temperature-dependent dynamic viscosity measurements (mPa·s) for diverse organic compounds; compiled for deep learning molecular property prediction
access: Supplementary material of Chew et al. Journal of Cheminformatics, 16:82, 2024

name: RTE
format: Sentence pairs with entailment/not-entailment labels; part of GLUE and SuperGLUE benchmarks

name: BioProBench
num_samples: 4 subsets: Subset A (Protocol Drafting), Subset B (Code Generation), Subset C (9 long-horizon protocols with 547 atomic steps), Subset D (Error Correction with injected faults)
storage: <100MB (protocol texts + hardware registry for 22 instruments; provided as supplementary material)
eval_time: 1-3 hours for full evaluation with API-based LLMs
format: Biological protocol generation tasks requiring scientific validity and hardware compliance; inputs are intent + hardware registry; outputs are protocol drafts and executable API code
metric: Scientific Score Cs (LLM-as-judge), ROUGE-L, Semantic Score Ssem, Code Score Scode, Physical Compliance Cp, AccSeq, AccParam, Success Rate, Loop Rate, Token count
license: Research use (provided in supplementary of arXiv:2603.00876)
access: arXiv:2603.00876 supplementary material; see also Liu et al. 2025b arXiv:2505.07889

name: MC-SEARCH
storage: ~500GB (3,333 QA examples + knowledge base: ~390K images + ~784K Wikipedia text documents)
eval_time: hours-days (requires agentic MM-RAG pipeline with iterative retrieval over large KB)
format: Multi-hop multimodal QA benchmark with 5 reasoning topologies (Image-Initiated Chain, Text-Initiated Chain, Parallel Image-Text Fork, Multi-Images Fork, Text-Only Chain); each example has step-wise annotations with sub-questions, retrieval modalities, supporting facts, and intermediate answers; avg 3.79 hops per chain
metric: F1, DeltaF1, Golden F1, LLM-as-Judge (LJ), Hit-per-Step (HPS), Rollout Deviation (RD)
notes: First benchmark for agentic MM-RAG with long step-wise annotated reasoning chains. Data verified via HAVE (Hop-wise Attribution and Verification of Evidence) procedure. arXiv:2603.00873.

name: OK-VQA
format: Visual QA benchmark requiring external knowledge (outside of what is immediately visible in the image); 14K open-ended QA pairs over COCO images annotated to require external knowledge retrieval; single-hop

name: WebQA
format: Multi-hop multimodal QA dataset; each question requires retrieving and reasoning over 1-2 web sources (images and text); up to 2 retrieval hops; distractor sources included

name: CSE-CIC-IDS2018
num_samples: ~3.5M flow records across 7 classes (Benign, Botnet, Brute-force, DDoS, DoS, Infiltration, Web Attack); 50k train / 5k val / 5k+ test used in AMDS paper
format: Network flow CSV with 77 flow-level features (CICFlowMeter-derived) labeled across 7 traffic classes; collected on AWS infrastructure simulating realistic attack scenarios

name: UNSW-NB15
num_samples: ~2.5M records across 9 attack categories plus normal traffic; used for cross-dataset evaluation in NIDS research
format: Network traffic CSV with 49 features (190 in extended version) and 9 attack types (Fuzzers, Analysis, Backdoors, DoS, Exploits, Generic, Reconnaissance, Shellcode, Worms) plus normal class; generated via IXIA PerfectStorm tool

name: XBOW Benchmark
format: Isolated Docker containers, each embedding a hidden flag accessible only through successful exploitation
metric: solve rate (flag capture), time-to-solve, token usage, API cost

name: DVWA
num_samples: 5 vulnerability classes x configurable difficulty levels
eval_time: minutes per test run (n=10 trials per vulnerability type)
format: Containerized vulnerable web application with configurable security levels (low/medium/high)

name: ADNI Clinical Morphometric Features
num_samples: ~800 subjects; 116 variable groups (46 single-covariate subcortical volumes SV; 70 four-covariate cortical groups: TA, TS, SA, CV)
format: Tabular clinical neuroimaging features grouped by brain region; groups defined by structural categories or prior domain knowledge for grouped variable selection studies
metric: MSE, gk-FWER, gFDP (as used in Stepdown SLOPE paper)
license: ADNI Data Use Agreement (free academic registration required)
access: http://adni.loni.usc.edu (requires registration and approval at https://ida.loni.usc.edu/)

name: UnlearnCanvas
num_samples: 20 object categories + 50 artistic styles; evaluation images generated from diffusion models
eval_time: varies (hours to evaluate unlearning across all concepts)
format: Stylized image dataset for evaluating machine unlearning in diffusion models. Evaluation metrics: Unlearning Accuracy (UA), In-Domain Retain Accuracy (IRA), Cross-Domain Retain Accuracy (CRA).
notes: arXiv:2402.11846 / NeurIPS 2024 Datasets & Benchmarks Track. Introduced by Zhang et al. for evaluating concept unlearning methods in text-to-image diffusion models.

name: Holistic Unlearning Benchmark
format: Multi-faceted evaluation benchmark for text-to-image diffusion model unlearning. Evaluates over-erasure (related concept preservation) and other robustness aspects when unlearning specific concepts.
notes: arXiv:2410.05664 by Moon et al. (2024). Tests whether unlearned models still generate related concepts after unlearning (e.g., unlearning 'English Springer' while preserving 'Beagle').

name: EraseBench
num_samples: multiple concept hierarchies (erased, paraphrased, similar, unrelated)
format: Benchmark for evaluating hierarchical effects of concept erasure in diffusion models. Tests unlearning accuracy across erased targets, paraphrased variants, semantically similar concepts, and unrelated concepts.
metric: Unlearning accuracy at each hierarchy level (erased↓, paraphrased↓, similar↑, unrelated↑)
notes: arXiv:2501.09833 by Amara et al. (2025). Understanding the ripple effects of concept erasure techniques.

name: SummEval
format: 1600 machine-generated summaries from 100 news articles (16 models × 100 articles), each annotated by 8 expert human annotators on 4 dimensions: coherence, consistency, fluency, relevance (scored 1-5)
metric: Correlation with human judgment (Spearman, Pearson); accuracy of LLM-assigned scores vs human labels
notes: Fabbri et al. 2021 (Transactions of ACL). Used for criteria-based LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation in CollabEval (arXiv:2603.00993).

name: chatbot_arena_conversations
format: Pairwise conversation comparisons from LMSYS Chatbot Arena; each example has (id, query, response_a, response_b, winner) for pairwise LLM evaluation
metric: Accuracy of predicted winner vs human preference
notes: Released by LMSYSOrg in 2023. Used for pairwise comparison evaluation in CollabEval (arXiv:2603.00993).

name: lmsys_arena_human_preference_55k
format: Human preference comparisons from Chatbot Arena; each example has (id, query, response_a, response_b, winner) with human preference annotations from crowd-sourced evaluation
metric: Accuracy of predicted winner vs human preference
notes: Chiang et al. 2024 (Chatbot Arena). Used for pairwise preference evaluation in CollabEval (arXiv:2603.00993).

name: ALFWorld
num_samples: 6 task types (Pick, Look, Clean, Heat, Cool, Pick2), ~3.5k test episodes total
eval_time: minutes per episode, hours for full eval
format: Text-based embodied household task environment requiring multi-step sequential decision-making
metric: success rate per task type and overall

name: Sokoban (gym-sokoban)
format: Visually-grounded 2D grid puzzle where an agent must push boxes onto target positions without getting stuck

name: AudioSet
format: audio (MP3/WAV) + multi-label event annotations, 527 audio event classes
license: CC BY 4.0 (annotations); audio via YouTube terms
access: https://research.google.com/audioset/ (audio requires YouTube download via yt-dlp)

name: SWE-QA
format: 576 human-validated QA pairs from 12 widely-used open-source Python repositories (astropy, sphinx, matplotlib, pylint, flask, pytest, django, xarray, scikit-learn, requests, sympy, sqlfluff); targets cross-file, multi-hop repository reasoning (intent inference, dependency tracing, feature localization)
metric: LLM-as-judge rubric scoring on 5 dimensions: Correctness, Completeness, Clarity, Relevance, Reasoning (each 0-10, max total 50)
license: GitHub OSS licenses (benchmark annotations CC BY)
notes: Introduced by Peng et al. (2025); evaluates repository-level question answering ability of LLMs; used in FastCode (arXiv:2603.01012) as primary QA evaluation benchmark

name: LongCodeQA
format: Multiple-choice questions (1 of 4 options) derived from real GitHub issue discussions, spanning input token lengths from 32K to 1M tokens; subset of LongCodeBench
notes: Introduced by Rando et al. (2025) as part of LongCodeBench; emphasizes long-context repository comprehension; used in FastCode (arXiv:2603.01012) to evaluate performance at extreme context lengths (up to 1M tokens)

name: LOC-BENCH
format: 274 issue-patch pairs from popular Python projects (SWE-Bench-Lite subset); measures ability to localize relevant files and code regions for resolving real-world issues (bug fixes, feature updates)
metric: Acc@k (k in {1,3,5}): fraction of instances where all ground-truth files appear in top-k candidates
notes: Introduced by Chen et al. (2025) as part of the LocAgent work; used in FastCode (arXiv:2603.01012) where Gemini-3-Flash achieves 86.13% Acc@1, surpassing prior SOTA LocAgent (77.74%)

name: GitTaskBench
eval_time: hours to 1 day (execution-based evaluation requiring environment setup)
format: 54 human-curated end-to-end repository maintenance tasks across multiple modalities/domains; tasks require setting up environments, navigating GitHub codebases, and producing runnable outputs; evaluated via automated harness
metric: Execution Completion Rate (ECR): whether valid non-empty outputs are produced; Task Pass Rate (TPR): whether outputs satisfy quality thresholds and functional requirements
notes: Introduced by Ni et al. (2025); evaluates agentic performance on practical repository workflows; includes cost-aware metrics; used in FastCode (arXiv:2603.01012) where Gemini-3-Flash achieves 53.70% TPR at ~2365x lower cost than OpenHands+Claude 3.7

name: MetaMathQA
format: Question-answer pairs augmented from GSM8K and MATH benchmarks via bootstrapping techniques (rephrasing, backward reasoning, FOBAR); each sample has a query and chain-of-thought response
notes: Yu et al., ICLR 2024. Used as training data for MetaMath-LLaMA-7B and MetaMath-Mistral-7B models. Also used in OTV (arXiv:2603.01025) as the standard mathematical reasoning training set for fine-tuning OTV on Qwen3-4B/8B and LLaMA/Mistral backbones.

name: DAPO17K
format: Hard math competition problems with final numeric answers (no human-written reasoning traces); sourced from competition mathematics for RLVR (RL Verifiable Reward) training
access: BytedanceDouyinContent/DAPO-Math-17k on HuggingFace (Yu et al., arXiv:2503.14476)
notes: Introduced in DAPO paper (Yu et al., 2025). Used in OTV (arXiv:2603.01025) as the advanced mathematical reasoning training set (provides only final answers, no reasoning traces, requiring the model to self-generate traces for OTV pseudo-labeling).

name: CINIC-10
format: 32x32 RGB images (10 classes); union of CIFAR-10 images and ImageNet-derived samples; 90k train, 90k val, 90k test

name: CIFAR-100-Ext
format: 100x100 RGB images re-sampled from CIFAR-100 classes (10 selected classes); used as auxiliary dataset for membership inference attacks against CIFAR-100 distilled models

name: ATOMIC2020
format: commonsense knowledge triples (head, relation, tail) spanning 23 relation types covering social, physical, and eventive commonsense

name: Flickr30k
format: Flickr images with 5 crowdsourced natural language captions each

name: LAION-5B
storage: ~240TB (full dataset); typically accessed via streaming or small subsets
format: Image-text pairs with CLIP embeddings, watermark scores, and aesthetic scores; partitioned into English (~2.3B), multilingual (~2.3B), and other subsets

name: CelebA-HQ
format: High-quality celebrity face images at 1024x1024 resolution, derived from CelebA with progressive GAN upsampling
metric: FID, PSNR, SSIM (for generative model evaluation)

name: SWE-bench Lite
format: 300 representative instances from SWE-bench full dataset; each instance is a GitHub issue with failing tests requiring a code patch; selected to be more tractable while preserving diversity
notes: Subset of SWE-bench selected by Princeton NLP for faster evaluation cycles. Used in arXiv:2603.00991 (tacit framework) and many agent benchmarking papers. Distinct from SWE-bench Verified (500 human-verified instances).

name: AgentDojo
num_samples: ~97 tasks across 5 environments (banking, slack, travel, workspace, filesystem); extensible
format: Dynamic environment simulating realistic multi-tool agent workflows; tasks paired with prompt-injection attacks injected into tool outputs; measures utility (task completion) and security (absence of data exfiltration or unintended actions)
metric: utility rate (task success), attack success rate (ASR), security rate
notes: NeurIPS 2024 (Debenedetti et al.). Primary benchmark for evaluating prompt injection defenses in LLM agents. Used as the evaluation framework in arXiv:2603.00991 (tacit) to construct the safety benchmark with Classified type protection.

name: τ²-bench
num_samples: ~200 tasks per domain (airline + retail); 10 independent runs per task
format: Dual-control conversational agent benchmark; LLM agent assists simulated users in airline (flight changes, cancellations) and retail (order management, returns) customer service scenarios; measures task completion under conversation constraints
metric: pass@1 (fraction of tasks solved correctly, averaged over 10 independent runs)
notes: arXiv:2506.07982 (Barres et al., 2025). Used in arXiv:2603.00991 (tacit) to evaluate whether capability-safe Scala code generation degrades agent performance vs. standard JSON tool calling.

name: SILO-BENCH
eval_time: days (500+ GPU-hours at full scale; hours for small N subset)
format: 30 algorithmically-grounded tasks across 3 communication complexity levels (Aggregation O(N), Mesh O(N), Global Shuffle O(N log N to N^2)); tasks procedurally generated; evaluated across 54 configurations (6 agent scales x 3 protocols x 3 models)
metric: Success Rate (SR), Partial Correctness Score (PCS), Token Consumption, Communication Density
access: arXiv:2603.01045 (code not yet released as of 2026-03)

name: AgentBench
eval_time: hours-days per model (multi-environment LLM agent evaluation)
format: 8 distinct agent environments: OS, DB, KG, digital card game, lateral thinking puzzles, house-holding, web shopping, web browsing; each with task descriptions and evaluation scripts
metric: Overall score (weighted avg across environments), per-environment success rate

name: Slakh2100
format: multi-track audio (WAV), MIDI annotations, 4-track stems (bass, drums, guitar, piano)
metric: FAD (Frechet Audio Distance), IRS (Inner-track Rhythmic Stability), CBS (Cross-track Beat Synchronization), CBD (Cross-track Beat Dispersion)

name: MUSDB18
storage: ~7GB (150 full-length stereo tracks with 4 stems: drums, bass, other, vocals)
format: multi-track audio (WAV/MP4), 4-stem separation tracks from real studio recordings
metric: SDR (Signal-to-Distortion Ratio), FAD, IRS, CBS, CBD

name: SWE-bench Multimodal
storage: ~10GB (JavaScript/TypeScript GitHub repository snapshots + issues with screenshots/GIFs; Docker images ~50-100GB)
format: 517 real-world GitHub issues from 12 JS/TypeScript repositories incorporating multimodal information (text + screenshots + GIFs/videos); test suites validate patch correctness; frequently involves multi-file changes

name: NeurIPS/ICLR/ICML LLM Papers Corpus (2020-2025)
format: Research papers (PDF/text) on large language models accepted at NeurIPS, ICLR, and ICML from 2020 to 2025; collected via OpenReview API; each paper is distilled into a ~2-page blog-post summary and decomposed into conceptual units / idea atoms
metric: reconstruction quality (LLM-as-judge 5-point scale), diversity (Coverage/Gini/Mean Rep), coherence (Max Intersection/Jaccard), novelty (cosine distance)
license: papers are copyright of their respective authors; OpenReview API public access
access: OpenReview API (https://openreview.net/); venues: NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML; years: 2020-2025; domain filter: large language models
notes: Corpus used in Alien Science (arXiv:2603.01092) to extract 39,028 conceptual units clustered into 2,457 idea atoms for training coherence and availability models.

name: WeatherBench2 (ERA5)
storage: ~100GB for a typical subset (full ERA5 >5PB on ECMWF)
format: NetCDF/Zarr global atmospheric reanalysis (ERA5) with 100+ variables at multiple pressure levels; accessible via WeatherBench2 Google Cloud bucket
metric: n/a (used as data source for meteorological index computation and forecasting evaluation)
license: ECMWF open data (Copernicus C3S); free registration required
access: https://weatherbench2.readthedocs.io/ and gs://weatherbench2/ on GCS; full ERA5 at https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/

name: HVR-Met Extreme Weather Diagnosis Benchmark
num_samples: 350 total: 100 end-to-end extreme weather cases + 150 index computation QA + 100 figure generation tasks
storage: ~50-500GB (ERA5 reanalysis data via WeatherBench2 API; benchmark QA pairs <100MB)
eval_time: hours-days (100 end-to-end cases with multi-agent workflows; atomic tasks ~5-10hr)
format: Three-component benchmark: (1) 100 real extreme weather events (gale/rainstorm/snowstorm/cold wave/heat wave, 20 each) for end-to-end agentic diagnosis; (2) 150 situational QA tasks covering 30 meteorological index types (Easy/Medium/Hard tiers); (3) 100 figure generation tasks across 20 figure categories with VLM-based semantic verification
metric: 5-dimension scoring (Hypothesis/Data/Index/Figure/Final Report, 0-5 scale, pass>4); index computation pass rate (relative error <5%); figure semantic accuracy (%)
access: Not publicly available; introduced in HVR-Met (arXiv:2603.01121 by Tang et al.)

name: Framingham Heart Study
format: Longitudinal tabular epidemiological data: demographics, clinical measurements, disease outcomes (coronary heart disease, stroke, etc.)
license: restricted access via NHLBI Biologic Specimen and Data Repository

name: WeMath
format: Multimodal math problems organized by knowledge concepts and difficulty levels; includes images and text; 67 knowledge concepts across K-12 math
notes: Qiao et al., 2024. We-Math: Does Your Large Multimodal Model Achieve Human-Like Mathematical Reasoning? Tests concept-level and multi-step mathematical reasoning in MLLMs.

name: MMK12
format: Multimodal STEM problems from K-12 curriculum (math, physics, chemistry, biology) with images; split into train/test
notes: Meng et al., 2025. Introduced in MM-Eureka paper. Covers 4 disciplines (mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology) at K-12 level. Train split used for RL training (e.g., DIVA-GRPO uses 52K samples from R1-ShareVL-52K and 5K subsets from MMK12 for ablations).

name: R1-ShareVL-52K
format: Multimodal math problems with images and text; collected from multiple sources for RL-based MLLM training
notes: Yao et al., 2025 (R1-ShareVL paper). Main training dataset used in DIVA-GRPO and R1-ShareVL. A 52K sample collection of multimodal math problems suitable for GRPO-based RL training of VLMs.

name: HBN (Healthy Brain Network)
storage: ~10-20GB (processed FCN matrices); raw fMRI much larger
format: rs-fMRI data with demographics (Gender, Age, Handedness) and phenotypes for pediatric mental health
metric: classification/regression ACC, MCC, F1, MAE, PCC

name: HCP (Human Connectome Project)
storage: ~15-30GB (processed FCN matrices + phenotypes); raw MRI several TB
format: High-quality multimodal MRI data with extensive phenotypic and cognitive measures (Gender, Age, Handedness, 12 phenotype metrics)

name: ABIDE (Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange)
format: Multi-site rs-fMRI for autism (ASD vs HC), with demographics, cognition (FIQ/VIQ/PIQ), and diagnosis labels

name: ABIDE II
format: Extended multi-site rs-fMRI for autism (ASD vs HC), used for zero-shot evaluation; includes cognitive and diagnosis labels

name: SRPBS Multi-disorder fMRI
format: Multi-site rs-fMRI for multiple psychiatric disorders (schizophrenia, OCD, MDD, bipolar, etc.) from Tanaka et al. (2021)

name: CNP (UCLA Neuropsychiatric Phenomics)
format: rs-fMRI for ADHD/schizophrenia/bipolar from UCLA, with demographic and diagnosis labels; used for zero-shot evaluation

name: GSP (Brain Genomics Superstruct Project)
format: rs-fMRI with structural MRI from Holmes et al. (2015), with demographic measures

name: QTIM (Queensland Twin Imaging)
format: rs-fMRI twin study with demographic measures (Gender, Age, Handedness) from Strike et al. (2023)

name: MDD rs-fMRI (Yan et al. 2019)
format: Multi-site rs-fMRI for Major Depressive Disorder (MDD vs HC) from Yan et al. (2019)

name: GDSC (Genomics of Drug Sensitivity in Cancer)
num_samples: ~1000 cancer cell lines x ~500 drugs; colorectal subset N=83
eval_time: minutes (ML model training on tabular data)
format: Pharmacogenomics dataset: cancer cell line RNA-seq (TPM), binary mutation vectors, drug IC50 values; accessed via Sanger GDSC1/GDSC2 portals; unique cell lines identified by COSMIC IDs

name: TCGA-COAD
num_samples: ~450 colon adenocarcinoma patients (full cohort); 200-patient synthetic proxy used in CIWM paper
format: Colorectal cancer patient genomic profiles (RNA-seq, somatic mutations) with overall survival data from The Cancer Genome Atlas colon adenocarcinoma cohort; used for Kaplan-Meier survival stratification
access: https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov/ (TCGA-COAD project); also via cBioPortal https://www.cbioportal.org/

name: WildChat-1M
format: JSON conversation logs of real ChatGPT interactions (multilingual, multi-turn, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4)

name: StuLife
num_samples: hundreds of self-evolving agent interaction episodes
format: Long-horizon multi-turn interaction environments for evaluating self-evolving LLM agents
metric: task success rate, capability accumulation over time

name: DeepResearch-9K
storage: ~5GB (questions, search trajectories with reasoning chains, and answers)
eval_time: hours-days (requires multi-turn web search via Serper API)
format: 9,000 multi-hop QA instances across 3 difficulty levels (L1-L3) with progressive entity obfuscation; each instance includes question, search trajectory from Tongyi-DeepResearch-30B-A3B, and verifiable answer; difficulty tied to number of tool calls (L1: mean 4.3, L2: mean 10.7, L3: mean 20.2)
notes: Introduced in DeepResearch-9K (arXiv:2603.01152). Also includes DeepResearch-Hard subset (3,974 instances where teacher model Tongyi-DeepResearch-30B-A3B fails). Built from HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, and MuSiQue source datasets via LLM-based data synthesis pipeline costing ~$200 in Serper API fees + ~8,064 A100 GPU hours.

name: BrowseComp-Plus
format: 830 complex tasks requiring strategic multi-step information seeking and comparative analysis across web sources; designed as a fairer and more transparent version of BrowseComp
notes: Extension of BrowseComp (Wei et al. arXiv:2504.12516) with improved fairness and transparency. Tongyi-DeepResearch-30B-A3B achieves 24.94% accuracy; L3 of DeepResearch-9K matches this difficulty level (23.73%).

name: 2WikiMultihopQA
format: Multi-hop QA built from two Wikipedia articles with explicit reasoning chains and Wikipedia-grounded verifiability; supports bridge, comparison, inference, and compositional question types
notes: Also known as 2WikiMultiHopQA. Introduced by Ho et al. (arXiv:2011.01060). Used as a source dataset in DeepResearch-9K (arXiv:2603.01152) for seed entity extraction.

name: ClinicalBench
format: Real-world patient cases from internet hospital consultations with chief complaints, longitudinal medical history, and examination findings. Requires triage (department routing) and multi-disease diagnosis prediction. From ClinicalLab (Yan et al. arXiv:2406.13890).
metric: ACC (diagnostic accuracy), CDR (comprehensive diagnostic rate), DCA (department classification accuracy), Entity-F1 (hallucination suppression), C_dept (department consistency)
access: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13890 (ClinicalLab paper; dataset release via project page)

name: HACK@DAC'18
num_samples: 20 hardware bugs across 8 modules in OpenTitan RISC-V SoC
eval_time: hours (LLM-assisted property generation + JasperGold formal verification)
format: Buggy SystemVerilog RTL for OpenTitan SoC modules with known CWE-labeled security bugs; requires JasperGold for formal verification
metric: CWE detection rate, assertion property success rate, formal verification (FV) pass rate
license: Competition benchmark; OpenTitan RTL under Apache 2.0

name: HACK@DAC'19
num_samples: 11 hardware bugs across 5 modules in OpenTitan RISC-V SoC
eval_time: hours (LLM-assisted property generation + JasperGold formal verification)
format: Buggy SystemVerilog RTL for OpenTitan SoC modules with known CWE-labeled security bugs; requires JasperGold for formal verification
metric: CWE detection rate, assertion property success rate, formal verification (FV) pass rate
license: Competition benchmark; OpenTitan RTL under Apache 2.0

name: HACK@DAC'21
num_samples: 17 hardware bugs across 9 modules in OpenTitan RISC-V SoC
eval_time: hours (LLM-assisted property generation + JasperGold formal verification)
format: Buggy SystemVerilog RTL for OpenTitan SoC modules with known CWE-labeled security bugs (DMA, JTAG, CSR, AES, RSA, SHA256 modules); requires JasperGold for formal verification
metric: CWE detection rate, assertion property success rate, formal verification (FV) pass rate
license: Competition benchmark; OpenTitan RTL under Apache 2.0

name: Flensburg District Heating Dataset
format: Hourly district heating production time-series with ERA5 weather covariates for Flensburg, Germany

name: Aalborg Residential Smart Meter Dataset
num_samples: ~26280 hourly aggregated records (3 years, 3021 smart meters)
format: Hourly aggregated residential heat consumption from 3021 Danish smart meters with DMI weather covariates

name: WordNet
format: Lexical database of English organized into synsets (groups of synonyms) connected by semantic relations (hypernymy/hyponymy, meronymy, antonymy). Used via NLTK wordnet corpus.
metric: Precision/Recall/F1 over concept subsumption relations, MRR for meet/join retrieval
notes: Used in arXiv:2603.01227 (Lattice Representation Hypothesis) to construct five WordNet-derived evaluation datasets (WN-Animal, WN-Plant, WN-Food, WN-Event, WN-Cognition) with ~1000-8000 concepts each and GPT-4o-generated binary attribute annotations.

name: SNARE
format: Longitudinal social network graph with node features (24-dim) and multi-class labels; represents offline peer network with temporal snapshots
access: McGlohon et al. KDD 2009 (SNARE: a link analytic system for graph labeling and risk detection); contact authors or ACM Digital Library

name: PHEME
format: Twitter conversation trees with node features (300-dim) and rumor veracity labels; online discourse hypergraph with temporal dynamics
access: Sharma & Sharma IJCNN 2021 (identifying possible rumor spreaders on Twitter); original PHEME dataset from Zubiaga et al., https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/PHEME_dataset_for_Rumour_Detection_and_Veracity_Classification/6392078

name: AMIGOS
num_samples: 40 nodes, 120 hyperedges, 4 classes, 4 time points; originally 40 participants
format: Multimodal group affect dataset with physiological signals (EEG, GSR, ECG), facial expressions; node features are 128-dim per agent; labeled for emotion/affect classification at group and individual levels
access: Miranda-Correa et al. IEEE TAC 2018; https://github.com/juanmoo/amigos or IEEE DataPort

name: OPAQUE KNAPSACK
num_samples: 1000 train + 100 easy eval + 100 hard eval (procedurally generated)
eval_time: minutes-hours (depends on LLM inference speed per episode)
format: Partially observable combinatorial optimization task; agent interacts via three-tool API (list_items, inspect, take_item, finish) to maximize knapsack value subject to capacity and class constraints; item attributes are hidden behind a budgeted inspect tool; two difficulty levels (Easy: 25-40 items, Hard: 80-120 items)
metric: Normalized optimality (achieved value / optimal value), exact solve rate, token efficiency (Score/1k tokens), interaction footprint (steps, tokens, wall-clock time)
license: Introduced in arXiv:2603.01209 (no separate license; procedural generator code not publicly released)
access: arXiv:2603.01209 — Agents Learn Their Runtime: Interpreter Persistence as Training-Time Semantics
notes: Designed to be non-collapsible for tool-augmented agents: attributes are tool-gated, feasibility depends on hidden class constraints, and inspection is budget-limited. Used in a controlled 2x2 study crossing train semantics (persistent vs. stateless) x runtime semantics. Two matched trajectory datasets generated by Gemini 3 Flash teacher.

name: RMBench
eval_time: hours (100 rollouts per task per policy, 9 tasks)
format: Dual-arm robotic manipulation tasks in SAPIEN simulation with memory complexity annotations (M(1) and M(n) tasks), language instructions, and auto-generated demonstrations

name: MultiHopQA
format: Multi-hop QA requiring cross-document evidence and step-wise verification over Wikipedia passages

name: MuJoCo HalfCheetah-v4
eval_time: ~1-2 hours per agent training run (~1.5-2M env steps)
format: Continuous-control locomotion task; 17-dim observations, 6-dim torque actions; maximize forward velocity

name: MiniGrid
format: 2D grid-world RL environments; discrete action space; symbolic/image observations

name: BabyAI
format: 2D grid-world with language instructions; discrete action space; text + grid observations

name: BALROG
format: Grid-world and roguelike game environments for LLM/VLM agent evaluation; text-based and multimodal observations
metric: episode reward, game score, win rate

name: Jumanji
format: JAX-based RL environments; hardware-accelerated; diverse game suite

name: MOSAIC MultiGrid
format: Multi-agent grid-world environments (soccer, etc.) supporting RL, LLM, VLM, and human agents; discrete action space
metric: episode reward, win rate, team score

name: Griddly
format: Flexible grid-world engine for custom game design; supports multi-agent; C++ backend with Python interface

name: Melting Pot
format: Multi-agent social dilemma environments; diverse substrates; 3D-like grid rendering; tests generalization to novel social partners
metric: episode return, focal agent performance vs. background population

name: NCCDC Blue Team Dataset
format: 2,390 single-turn conversations from student blue-team defenders during NCCDC competitions, annotated for task category, offensive terminology, authorization signals, and model refusal outcomes across 8 defensive task categories
metric: refusal rate, relative risk ratio, chi-square statistics
license: Restricted (collected by Scale AI during NCCDC; not publicly released)
access: Not publicly available; contact Scale AI Security and Policy Research Lab

name: OR-Bench
format: Over-refusal benchmark with prompts across 10 sensitivity levels designed to test false-positive refusal rates in LLMs

name: FORTRESS
format: Frontier risk evaluation benchmark for national security and public safety, measuring both over-refusal and successful jailbreaks

name: CyberSecEval 2
format: Synthetic CTF (capture-the-flag) style challenges measuring cybersecurity risks in LLMs, including False Refusal Rate metric for defensive tasks
metric: False Refusal Rate, cyber-attack assistance rate

name: SANDBOXESCAPEBENCH
storage: ~1GB (VM images, Docker container configs, exploit scripts per scenario)
eval_time: minutes to hours per model-scenario run; days for full multi-model evaluation (760 samples at 2.5M token budget each)
format: 18 Capture-the-Flag container escape scenarios spanning 3 attack layers (L1 Orchestration: 4, L3 Engine/Runtime: 8, L4 Host/Kernel: 6); nested VM-in-sandbox architecture; binary success criterion (flag retrieval from host /flag.txt); difficulty ratings 1-5
metric: success rate (binary flag retrieval), inference-time compute scaling (success vs token budget)
notes: Introduced by Marchand et al. (2026), arXiv:2603.02277. Built on Inspect AI framework with Vagrant/EC2 VM providers. Covers CVEs including CVE-2024-21626 (runc), CVE-2019-5736, CVE-2022-0492, CVE-2022-0847 (Dirty Pipe), CVE-2016-5195 (Dirty COW), and common misconfigurations (privileged containers, docker.sock exposure, RBAC over-permissioning). Private test set maintained separately.

name: TDC ADME+Toxicity Benchmarks
num_samples: varies per task: BBB ~1975, Bioavailability ~640, HIA ~578, Pgp ~1212, CYP2C9 Inhib ~12092, CYP2D6 Inhib ~13130, CYP3A4 Inhib ~12328, CYP2C9 Subs ~666, CYP2D6 Subs ~836, CYP3A4 Subs ~667, DILI ~475, hERG ~655, AMES ~7255
storage: ~50MB total (all TDC ADME+Tox datasets; SMILES tabular format)
format: SMILES strings with binary classification labels for ADME properties (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion) and toxicity endpoints; scaffold split 80/10/10 standard for molecular ML generalization evaluation
access: pip install PyTDC; from tdc.single_pred import ADME, Tox; Huang et al. 2021, Therapeutics Data Commons, https://tdcommons.ai/
notes: Part of Therapeutics Data Commons (TDC) platform (Huang et al., arXiv:2102.09548). Used in GlassMol (arXiv:2603.01274) to evaluate interpretable molecular property prediction via Concept Bottleneck Models across 13 benchmark tasks.

name: FastF1 2026 Formula 1 Race Telemetry
num_samples: ~3,480 sector observations per rival per race (58 laps x 3 sectors)
format: Per-car 10Hz speed, throttle, braking, sector times via FOM timing feed; access via Python FastF1 library

name: EEDI
