format: Student responses to 4-choice multiple-choice math questions (binary correct/incorrect). Includes demographic info (gender, age, socio-economic status).
metric: Coverage probability of confidence intervals (UQ evaluation)

name: MicroVQA
num_samples: 1,042 MCQs across 255 unique image sets (423 multi-image questions)
eval_time: minutes to hours per model depending on size
format: Multiple-choice VQA with images (microscopy) and text questions across 3 task types: expert visual understanding, hypothesis generation, experiment proposal
license: research (images sourced from contributors' own experiments, image databases, and recent papers with redistribution-permitting licenses)
notes: Research-level scientific VQA benchmark for microscopy. Peak MLLM performance ~53% (o1); human expert baseline ~50.3%. 31 organisms, 33 research areas, 3 microscopy modalities (light, fluorescence, electron). Bloom's taxonomy levels 3-4 (apply/analyze).

name: AudioCaps
format: Audio files with captions

name: Freesound
format: Audio files with metadata

name: FDopenl3
format: Frechet Distance using OpenL3 embeddings

name: CLAP
format: Audio-text alignment score using CLAP embeddings

name: KLpasst
format: KL divergence of PASST embeddings

name: PASST
format: Audio tagging embeddings for diversity metrics

name: Places365
num_samples: ~8M train / ~36k val images across 365 scene categories
format: Scene photographs (256x256), 365 categories

name: EpicKitchens
format: egocentric video with action annotations, object bounding boxes, hand tracking

name: RoboCasa
format: Mujoco simulation environment with kitchen tasks

name: GraspNet-1B (GraspNet-1Billion)
num_samples: 97K RGB-D images, 1.2B grasp annotations, 0.1K 3D models, 30-35 categories
format: RGB-D images with 6-DOF grasp pose annotations. Grasps represented as view direction, angle, width, depth, quality, graspness.
metric: AP (Average Precision) at various friction coefficients (0.2-1.2)

name: ReOcS (Reconstruction under Occlusion Dataset)
num_samples: 1,125 RGB-D images with ground-truth instance masks, 6D poses, and 3D shapes; 22 3D models across 3 splits (Easy/Normal/Hard)
format: RGB-D images with instance masks, 6D object poses, and 3D shape ground-truth. Three difficulty splits based on occlusion level.
metric: Chamfer Distance (CD), F1-Score (10mm threshold), Normal Consistency (NC)

name: FBIS-22M
format: Multi-resolution satellite image patches (0.25m-10m) with agricultural field instance masks. Sources: Sentinel-2, Planet, Maxar, Pleiades, orthophotos.

name: AI4Boundaries
format: Satellite imagery with field boundary annotations. 1m and 10m resolution.

name: OLMES
num_samples: ~10 benchmarks (MMLU: 14079, HellaSwag: 70042, ARC-Easy: 7787, ARC-Challenge: 2590, PIQA: 16113, CommonsenseQA: 12102, SocialIQA: 33583, OpenBookQA: 5957, BoolQ: 15942+3270, Wino-Grande: 44007)
format: 4-choice or 2-choice multiple-choice QA with cloze formulation and per-task length normalization
license: Varies per component benchmark (AI2, MIT, CC BY-SA 3.0)

name: ETTh1
format: Hourly electricity transformer temperature data; 7 channels (oil temperature + 6 feature loads)

name: ETTh2
format: Hourly electricity transformer temperature data; 7 channels (oil temperature + 6 feature loads)

name: ETTm1
format: 15-min interval electricity transformer temperature data; 7 channels

name: ETTm2
format: 15-min interval electricity transformer temperature data; 7 channels

name: Weather
format: 10-min interval weather data with 21 meteorological features

name: Electricity (ECL)
format: Hourly electricity consumption data for 321 customers

name: Traffic
format: Hourly road traffic data from 862 sensors in the Bay Area

name: Exchange
format: Daily exchange rates for 8 currencies (2000-2016)

name: Solar-Energy
format: 10-min interval solar power generation data from 137 stations in Alabama

name: PEMS03
format: 5-min interval California traffic flow data from 358 sensors (PEMS03 subset)

name: PEMS04
format: 5-min interval California traffic flow data from 307 sensors (PEMS04 subset)

name: PEMS07
format: 5-min interval California traffic flow data from 883 sensors (PEMS07 subset)

name: PEMS08
format: 5-min interval California traffic flow data from 170 sensors (PEMS08 subset)

name: GIFT-Eval
num_samples: 8 diverse datasets (Loop Seattle, BizITObs-L2C, Electricity, ETT1, Hierarchical Sales, Jena Weather, Solar, US Births)
format: Multi-domain time series forecasting benchmark spanning finance, energy, transportation, healthcare. Various sampling frequencies and prediction horizons.

name: FaceScrub
format: Face images with identity labels, used for face recognition evaluation

name: Stanford Dogs
format: Dog images with breed-level annotations, subset of ImageNet

name: VLGuard
format: MLLM safety benchmark with safe/unsafe image-text pairs; includes risk detection and safe response generation tasks
metric: ASR (Attack Success Rate), Win Rate (safe-safe subset)
notes: Zong et al., 2024. Used as training data source and evaluation benchmark in DREAM paper (arXiv:2504.18053). Provides 9 risk categories from OpenAI Usage Policies.

name: FigStep
format: Typographic jailbreak attacks: harmless text instructions paired with images containing malicious text (typography attack)
notes: Gong et al., 2023. Used in DREAM paper (arXiv:2504.18053) to evaluate model safety under structured jailbreak attacks. FigStep-Unsafe evaluates attack success; FigStep-Benign evaluates oversafety.

name: FigStep-Benign
format: Benign version of FigStep: misleading typography images with benign text prompts to test model oversafety
access: Created for DREAM paper (arXiv:2504.18053); generated from FigStep subset using GPT-4o benign phrase conversion
notes: Introduced in DREAM paper to test oversensitivity. Converts 50 jailbreak queries to benign queries to evaluate whether models wrongly refuse safe instructions due to typographic patterns.

name: SIUO
format: Safe & Unsafe Outputs benchmark: 167 human-crafted queries covering 9 safety areas with complex multimodal risk scenarios
metric: Safe Rate, Effective Rate, Safe&Effective Rate
notes: Wang et al., 2024. Used in DREAM paper (arXiv:2504.18053) as primary evaluation metric. Safe Rate measures refusal of unsafe queries; Effective Rate measures helpful response quality; Safe&Effective requires both.

name: MOSSBench
num_samples: Not specified (3 types: Exaggerated Risk, Negated Harm, Counterintuitive Interpretation)
format: Oversensitivity benchmark for MLLMs: benign queries that may trigger incorrect refusal due to exaggerated risk, negated harm, or counterintuitive interpretation
metric: RR (Refusal Rate) averaged across 3 data types
notes: Li et al., 2024. Used in DREAM paper (arXiv:2504.18053) to evaluate oversafety. Lower RR indicates better balance between safety and helpfulness.

name: SPA-VL
format: Large-scale MLLM safety training dataset: prompts multiple MLLMs to collect malicious queries and responses, uses GPT-4 as judge to construct chosen-reject pairs
notes: Zhang et al., 2024. Used in DREAM paper (arXiv:2504.18053) for scalability experiments with 30K subset.

name: CCDS (CLAP Conditional Diversity Score)
format: Average CLAP cosine distance between pairs of generations with same prompt, averaged across batches

name: PRM12K
format: Math problems with step-level process reward labels from OpenAI's 'Let's Verify Step by Step' (Lightman et al. 2023); each step rated as correct/incorrect

name: Breakpoint
num_samples: 930 code repair tasks across 30 Python GitHub repositories
eval_time: hours to days (full evaluation depends on model and number of tasks)
format: Adversarially corrupted functions within real Python repositories; agents must restore functionality using test feedback
metric: Test pass rate (binary: all tests pass or fail)
notes: Hariharan et al., 2025 (arXiv:2506.00172). Uses inverse problem methodology: corrupts well-tested functions in real repos to generate scalable, difficulty-tunable code repair tasks. Difficulty controlled by cyclomatic complexity (local reasoning) and harmonic centrality (system-level reasoning). Two modes: REMOVE (target known) and DISCOVERY (target unknown).

name: CATH 4.2
format: Protein backbone structures with CATH hierarchical classification
notes: Standard benchmark for protein inverse folding. Proteins categorized by CATH (Class, Architecture, Topology, Homologous superfamily).

name: CATH 4.3
format: Protein backbone structures with CATH hierarchical classification
notes: Updated version of CATH benchmark for protein inverse folding.

name: TS45
format: De novo protein structures from CASP15 competition
notes: CASP15 target domains (TS45) used for evaluating de novo protein design. Represents realistic unseen protein structures.

name: SlimPajama
num_samples: ~1T tokens (various subset sizes used in practice, e.g., 200B)
format: Cleaned web text corpus from CommonCrawl, C4, Wikipedia, etc., deduplicated and quality filtered; derived from RedPajama
license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (for processed data; source licenses vary)

name: Winogrande
format: Fill-in-the-blank commonsense reasoning problems (Winograd schema style) with binary choices

name: EuRoC MAV
eval_time: minutes to hours for full SLAM evaluation
format: Stereo grayscale images (20 Hz), synchronized IMU data (200 Hz), and ground truth camera poses from motion capture system. Indoor environments (Vicon room and factory floor).
metric: ATE RMSE (camera tracking), PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS (novel view synthesis / reconstruction quality)

name: Penn Treebank (PTB)
format: Word-level Penn Treebank corpus for language modeling evaluation
notes: Standard language modeling benchmark. Used in BAQ paper for perplexity evaluation.

name: Last.fm
format: User-artist listening counts from Last.fm API; used in conversational bandits for artist recommendation. Key terms are tag IDs. User feedback is binary (1 if user assigns tag to artist, 0 otherwise).

name: HealthVer
format: Claim, Evidence1, Evidence2, Label (SUPPORTS/REFUTES/NEUTRAL)
metric: N/A (used for fact-checking uncertainty explanation evaluation)

name: DRUID
format: Claim, Evidence1, Evidence2, Label (SUPPORTS/REFUTES/NEUTRAL)
metric: N/A (used for fact-checking uncertainty explanation evaluation)

name: OmniMedVQA
num_samples: 127,995 QA pairs from 118,010 medical images spanning 73 datasets
format: Large-scale medical VQA benchmark covering 12 imaging modalities (X-ray, CT, MRI, PET, ultrasound, pathology, etc.) and 20+ anatomical regions; includes multiple question types (open-ended, multiple-choice, yes/no)

name: Polyglot
num_samples: ~100-200 tasks across multiple languages (C++, Rust, Python, etc.)
format: Multi-language coding tasks with ground-truth tests; agent must implement solutions from scratch in single files
notes: Created by Paul Gauthier for evaluating Aider; more niche than SWE-bench, less likely in FM training data; tasks require understanding interplay between files across multiple programming languages.

name: REALSI
num_samples: not specified in paper; speech utterances with simultaneous translation references
format: Streaming speech-to-text translation (Zh↔En) with partial translation references; used for simultaneous machine translation evaluation
metric: COMET, BLEURT, GPT-4 score, AL, LAAL
license: not specified (from Cheng et al. 2024, Bytedance)
notes: Real-time simultaneous translation dataset. Paper: 'Towards achieving human parity on end-to-end simultaneous speech translation via LLM agent' (Cheng et al. 2024). Used in SeqPO-SiMT (2505.20622) as evaluation benchmark.

name: MuST-C (MUST-C)
format: TED Talks audio (16kHz) paired with English→target language translations at sentence level
notes: Multilingual United Speech Translation Corpus. Paper: Di Gangi et al. 2019. Used in SeqPO-SiMT (2505.20622) for En→Zh evaluation.

name: NEWSTEST2021
format: English-Chinese parallel news sentences from WMT2021 shared task
notes: WMT2021 news translation test set. Used in SeqPO-SiMT (2505.20622) for both En→Zh and Zh→En evaluation. Test sets from WMT are standard MT benchmarks.

name: MMLU-Pro
num_samples: ~12k (from Wang et al., 2024, published at NeurIPS 2024)
format: 4-choice MC (more robust and challenging than original MMLU)

name: Big-Bench-Hard
format: Multiple-choice and free-response tasks; paper uses subset with consistent MC format

name: Alpaca (Evaluation)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Instruction-response pairs for open-ended generation evaluation

name: EXP-Bench
num_samples: 461 research tasks (12,737 subtasks) from 51 NeurIPS/ICLR 2024 papers
eval_time: weeks (full evaluation: 461 tasks × 40min timeout × multiple agent configurations)
format: Structured research tasks with: (1) Research Question, (2) High-level Method description, (3) Starter code (masked repo), (4) Expected outcome (experimental design, implementation git diff, final conclusion). Graded on 4 metrics: D (design), I (implementation), E (execution), C (conclusion).
metric: Multi-metric: D (design correctness), I (implementation correctness), E (executability), C (conclusion correctness). Conjunctive metrics: I·E, All✓ (D∧I∧C), All✓·E.
notes: EXP-Bench evaluates AI agents on end-to-end AI research experimentation. Agents must design experiments, implement code, execute them, and derive conclusions from real papers. Top agent (OpenHands + o3-mini) achieves only 1.4% on All✓, 0.5% on All✓·E. Most common failures: missing essential implementation components (39.7%), environment/dependency misconfigs (29.4%), incomplete design variables (16.1%).

name: WikiTQ
format: Semi-structured tables (Wikipedia) with natural language questions; answers are text or numbers
notes: Wikipedia-based table QA dataset with relatively simple factoid questions over relational tables. From Pasupat & Liang (2015). Used in FORTUNE paper (arXiv:2505.23667) as in-distribution benchmark.

name: TabFact
format: Wikipedia tables with fact verification claims (true/false labels)
notes: Table-based fact verification dataset. Each claim is labeled as either true or false. From Chen et al. (2020). Used in FORTUNE paper (arXiv:2505.23667) as in-distribution benchmark.

name: FinQA
format: Financial tables (SEC filings) with reasoning questions requiring symbolic/numerical computation
notes: Financial domain table QA dataset requiring symbolic reasoning over semi-structured input. From Chen et al. (EMNLP 2021). Used in FORTUNE paper (arXiv:2505.23667) as in-distribution benchmark.

name: HiTab
format: Hierarchical tables from statistical reports with QA questions
notes: Hierarchical table dataset for QA and natural language generation. From Cheng et al. (2021). Used in FORTUNE paper (arXiv:2505.23667) as in-distribution benchmark.

name: MultiHiertt
format: Multi-table hierarchical and textual data with numerical reasoning questions
notes: Multi-hierarchical table and text dataset for numerical reasoning. From Zhao et al. (ACL 2022). Used in FORTUNE paper (arXiv:2505.23667) as in-distribution benchmark.

name: AIT-QA
format: Hierarchical tables from airline industry with QA questions
notes: Airline industry table QA dataset with hierarchical tables. From Katsis et al. (2021). Used in FORTUNE paper (arXiv:2505.23667) as out-of-distribution benchmark.

name: TableBench
format: Complex relational tables from various domains with multi-step reasoning questions
notes: Comprehensive and complex benchmark for table QA requiring multi-step symbolic reasoning. From Wu et al. (2025). Most challenging benchmark in FORTUNE paper (arXiv:2505.23667) evaluation; used as out-of-distribution benchmark.

name: ACS (Acceptability in Code-Switching) benchmark
num_samples: 9,000+ minimal pairs across 11 language pairs (de-en, da-en, es-en, fr-en, it-en, id-en, nl-en, sv-en, tr-en, tr-de, zh-en)
eval_time: minutes per model for full evaluation
format: Minimal pairs of code-switching sentences: one naturally observed CS sentence vs. one synthetically manipulated counterpart with a single word language change. Bilingual human judgments included for validation. Universal Dependencies annotations on monolingual translations.
metric: Accuracy (% correct predictions of more acceptable CS sentence)
license: Research use (likely MIT/CC BY — released with Sterner & Teufel 2025)
notes: Minimal pair-based evaluation benchmark for code-switching (Sterner & Teufel, ACL 2025). Each pair contains a naturally-observed CS sentence and a synthetically manipulated version. Task: predict which is more acceptable. Languages: German-English (training), 10 other language pairs for zero-shot generalization testing. Includes spoken (transcribed) and written CS data.

name: StaticHikes
num_samples: Multiple outdoor hiking sequences (~500-1500 imgs each, avg ~972)
format: Ordered wide-baseline RGB photo sequences for novel view synthesis

name: SARCOS Robot Arm Dataset
format: Multi-output regression: 21 input features, 7 output targets

name: LCBench
num_samples: 35 datasets × 2000 learning curves × 52 steps = up to 3.64M observations
format: Learning curves: 7 hyperparameters → training loss/accuracy over 52 epochs

name: Nordic Gridded Climate Dataset
num_samples: Up to 5M (5000 spatial locations × 1000 time steps)
format: Gridded spatiotemporal data: latitude, longitude, day → temperature/precipitation

name: MegaScenes
storage: ~3.2TB original images (512x512 would be much smaller)
format: Internet photo collections with SfM camera poses, depth maps, appearance variations (lighting, weather, transient occlusions)
notes: Large-scale scene-level view synthesis dataset from photo tourism. Used in WildCAT3D (arXiv:2506.13030) as primary training data. Permissively licensed enabling web-scale NVS training.

name: Re10K
format: Multi-view stereo dataset with consistent camera poses and lighting
notes: Curated multi-view dataset used in WildCAT3D and CAT3D for training. Limited diversity and camera movement compared to MegaScenes.

name: Middlebury v3
num_samples: 33 training scenes, 15 test scenes with subpixel-accurate ground truth
format: High-resolution stereo RGB image pairs with precise disparity maps

name: SceneFlow
format: Synthetic stereo sequences with dense ground truth disparity and optical flow

name: IMDB
format: Text reviews with binary sentiment labels (positive/negative)

name: ActorsHQ
storage: ~50GB high-resolution actor images with multi-view captures and SMPL-X annotations
format: High-resolution actor images with calibrated camera poses and SMPL-X body model parameters for 3D human reconstruction

name: 4D-Dress
storage: ~30GB multi-view video sequences of dressed humans with SMPL-X and clothing annotations
format: 4D captured human clothing sequences with semantic annotations, multi-view RGB, SMPL-X parameters

name: CustomHumans
storage: ~20GB high-quality 3D human scans with multi-view renderings
format: High-quality 3D human scans rendered from multiple viewpoints with camera calibration

name: SHHQ
storage: ~100GB in-the-wild human images with SMPL-X annotations
format: In-the-wild human images with estimated SMPL-X parameters for human avatar reconstruction

name: VBench-2.0
num_samples: Evaluation prompts for intrinsic video quality dimensions
format: Evaluates video generation across multiple quality dimensions: aesthetic, quality, temporal consistency, dynamic, semantic alignment. Extension of VBench with improved metrics.
notes: Used in Captain Cinema (arXiv:2507.18634) for long-form video generation evaluation

name: LLaVA-Bench
format: Multi-turn image-based conversations with questions covering detail description, spatial reasoning, and conversation. Evaluated via GPT-4 judge scoring.
notes: Benchmark from Liu et al. (LLaVA paper). Used to evaluate LVLMs on general visual conversation and reasoning. Used in RED paper (arXiv:2507.07685) as one of the evaluation benchmarks.

name: JetClass
format: Jet constituents (particle features) + jet-level observables, 10 jet classes
metric: Classification accuracy, AUC for jet flavour tagging
notes: Large-scale jet classification dataset for deep learning in HEP (Qu, Li & Qian 2022). 10 classes: H→bb, H→cc, H→gg, H→4q, t→bℓν, t→bqql, W→qq, Z→qq, q/g, plus a top decay class. Jets from LHC Monte Carlo simulations (Pythia + DELPHES). Used in this paper for training transformer-based jet classifier and for source/target dataset generation.

name: HOT3D
num_samples: ~833 minutes of video with 33 rigid objects
storage: Large (precise 3D hand and camera pose annotations)
format: Egocentric RGB video with precise 3D hand and camera pose annotations for object interaction

name: TACO
format: Egocentric video sequences of tool-use interactions with action annotations

name: Ego Humanoid Manipulation Benchmark
eval_time: Hours per model (27-66 rollouts per task)
format: NVIDIA Isaac Lab simulation with Unitree H1 humanoid + Inspire dexterous hands; RGB-D egocentric observations, 36-DoF actions at 30Hz

name: Algonauts 2025
format: fMRI responses to video stimuli across multiple subjects
metric: Pearson correlation between predicted and actual BOLD signals

name: Courtois NeuroMod
num_samples: 80+ hours fMRI per subject, 4 subjects used
format: fMRI recordings of subjects watching TV shows and movies (Friends, Bourne Supremacy, Hidden Figures, Wolf of Wall Street, Life)

name: BrightKite
eval_time: seconds to minutes for trace simulation
format: Page request traces derived from check-in data; cache misses evaluated against Belady's optimal algorithm
notes: Location-based social network dataset used for caching evaluation. Paper uses BrightKite with cache size k=10 following Lykouris & Vassilvtiskii setup.

name: CitiBike
eval_time: seconds to minutes for trace simulation
format: Bike trip request sequences; each trip is a page request for a station. Cache size k=100 following Lykouris & Vassilvtiskii.
notes: NYC bike sharing trip data used for caching evaluation. Paper uses CitiBike with cache size k=100.

name: SPEC CPU2006 Memory Traces
num_samples: 13 memory trace datasets from SPEC CPU2006 benchmark
format: Memory address traces (16-way 2MB cache configuration). Each trace is a sequence of memory addresses used to derive page request sequences.
notes: Standard CPU benchmark traces used for cache replacement evaluation. Paper uses 16-way 2MB cache configuration following Liu et al. and Chledowski et al.

name: CMMLU
format: Multiple-choice questions across 70+ Chinese subjects

name: C-Eval
format: Multiple-choice questions across 52 Chinese subjects

name: MMLU-STEM
format: STEM subset of MMLU

name: BIG-Bench
format: Diverse set of challenging tasks designed to probe LLMs

name: DROP
format: Reading comprehension requiring discrete reasoning over paragraphs

name: Algonauts 2025 brain encoding competition
storage: Competition data ~5-10TB for full fMRI + stimuli
format: fMRI time series (Schaefer 1000 parcellation) + video/audio/text stimuli
metric: Pearson correlation between predicted and actual BOLD responses

name: Courtois NeuroMod dataset
num_samples: 6 subjects, ~80 hours of fMRI per subject watching naturalistic videos (Friends TV series + movies)
storage: ~5-10TB for full dataset (4 subjects used in Algonauts 2025)
format: fMRI BOLD signals (MNI152NLin2009cAsym space, Schaefer 1000 parcellation)

name: GEN-Bench
format: Dynamic Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling problem instances with stochastic events (new job arrivals, machine breakdowns, job cancellations, emergency jobs)
notes: General-purpose DFJSP benchmark introduced in ReflecSched paper (arXiv:2508.01724). Control for rule-balance bias to properly evaluate greedy behavior.

name: MK-Bench
format: Derived from Brandimarte MK01-MK10 Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling instances, adapted to dynamic environment with stochastic events
notes: Cross-benchmark evaluation in ReflecSched paper. Standardized FJSP instances converted to dynamic scenario.

name: JMS-Bench
format: Semiconductor cluster tool manufacturing scenario with 5 heterogeneous process modules (PM1-PM5), re-entrant flows, residency time constraints
notes: Industrial semiconductor manufacturing benchmark in ReflecSched paper. Models wafer fabrication with robot transport synchronization.

name: PDR-Bench
format: Diagnostic benchmark where each instance has a known optimal heuristic by design
notes: Diagnostic benchmark to evaluate LLM's ability to apply provided heuristics. Designed to isolate heuristic utilization capability.

name: CUB-200-2011 (Caltech-UCSD Birds-200)
format: 200 bird species images with bounding boxes and part annotations
notes: Fine-grained bird classification dataset used in OCD (On-the-fly Category Discovery) paper. Categories split into seen (100) and unseen (100) for OCD evaluation.

name: iNaturalist 2017 - Arachnida subset
format: Spider species images from iNaturalist
notes: Subset of iNaturalist 2017 used in OCD paper. Split into 28 known and 56 total categories (50% seen/50% unseen split).

name: iNaturalist 2017 - Animalia subset
format: Animal kingdom images from iNaturalist
notes: Subset of iNaturalist 2017 used in OCD paper. Split into 39 known and 77 total categories (50% seen/50% unseen split).

name: iNaturalist 2017 - Mollusca subset
format: Mollusk species images from iNaturalist
notes: Subset of iNaturalist 2017 used in OCD paper. Split into 47 known and 93 total categories (50% seen/50% unseen split).

name: FLORES-200
format: Multilingual machine translation - parallel sentences across 200 languages from wikinews

name: XQuAD
format: Extractive question answering - context paragraph with question and answer span

name: Belebele
num_samples: ~900 examples per language across 122 language variants
format: Multiple-choice reading comprehension in 122 language variants

name: CulturaX
format: Parquet - multilingual text corpus from mC4 and OSCAR, cleaned and deduplicated
license: Varies by source (mC4 CC BY SA 3.0, OSCAR CC BY 4.0)

name: Winoground
format: Two images and two captions with subtle semantic differences - model must match correct caption to each image
metric: Text Score, Image Score, Group Score

name: VisMin-Bench
format: Image-text pairs with minimal semantic differences - focuses on fine-grained visual understanding across multiple images
metric: Text Score, Image Score, Group Score

name: Mantis-Eval
format: Multi-image understanding tasks requiring deep cross-image reasoning - includes multiple-choice and short-answer formats

name: MuirBench
format: Comprehensive multi-image reasoning benchmark covering 12 skills including geographic understanding, diagram interpretation, visual retrieval

name: SSCBench-KITTI-360
format: Camera-based 3D semantic scene completion benchmark derived from KITTI-360 dataset. 18 semantic classes + 1 free class. Voxel grid 256x256x32 at 0.2m resolution covering 51.2m x 51.2m x 6.4m.
access: https://www.cvlibs.net/datasets/kitti-360/ (original); SSCBench from Li et al., IROS 2024

name: ClothoAQA
format: Audio files with crowdsourced questions and answers

name: MELD
format: Multimodal multi-party dialogues (audio, text, video) with emotion labels

name: VocalSound
format: Audio files of non-verbal human vocalizations

name: MCR-BENCH
format: Audio-text pairs with faithful, adversarial, and irrelevant text conditions for 3 audio tasks (AQA, SER, VSC)

name: ParaToMi
format: Question-answer pairs about false belief scenarios with linguistically diverse rewording

name: FANToM
format: Multi-party conversation QA with theory of mind questions about belief inference

name: HiToM
format: Higher-order theory of mind reasoning with recursive belief inference

name: SOTOPIA-hard
format: Interactive social reasoning with goal-driven multi-agent dialogue scenarios

name: Text-to-Image-2M
format: text-image pairs, preprocessed to 512x512 resolution
notes: Used in OminiControl (Tan et al. 2024, arXiv:2411.15098) and NanoControl (arXiv:2508.10424) for training controllable diffusion transformer models. OminiControl uses the last 300K images; NanoControl uses the full dataset.

name: MJHQ-30K
format: Aesthetic-quality-oriented text-to-image generation benchmark; 30K prompts evaluated by IM-3 (aesthetic scorer)
notes: Introduced in Playground v2.5 (arXiv:2402.17245). Standard T2I perceptual quality benchmark. Lower FID is better.

name: ShareGPT-4o-Image
num_samples: 46000 image editing pairs (46K text-and-image-to-image samples from 91K total; 45K are T2I)
format: Image editing pairs synthesized using GPT-4o image generation; includes source image, instruction, and target edited image
notes: From ShareGPT-4o-Image (arXiv:2506.18095). Used in DIM-Edit (233K) as one of three data sources (46K semantically rich samples).

name: Dimba
format: Image-text pairs with long prompts (avg 78.29 words); Transformer-Mamba diffusion model for image generation
notes: Dimba (arXiv:2406.01159). Used as one of the auxiliary T2I datasets in DIM-4.6B-T2I training (0.3M samples).

name: DIM-T2I
format: 14M web-crawled images (512x512+) with long-context annotations (avg 146.76 words) across 21 dimensions, covering scene, object, attribute, relationship, etc.
notes: Draw-In-Mind T2I dataset (arXiv:2509.01986). Curated for complex CoT-guided image editing; forms foundation for DIM-4.6B-T2I training. Built by crawling web images and annotating with 21-dimensional in-house model annotations.

name: DIM-Edit
format: 233K image editing pairs with 4-step chain-of-thought blueprints (Global Layout Perception, Local Object Perception, Edit Area Localization, Edited Image Imagination); includes source image, optimized instruction, and target image with CoT annotations
notes: Draw-In-Mind Edit dataset (arXiv:2509.01986). Constructed from UltraEdit-160K-CoT (160K), ShareGPT-4o-Image-CoT (46K), and HumanEdit-CoT (27K). GPT-4o generates 4-step CoT editing blueprints. Central contribution of the paper.

name: MMHal-Bench
format: Multimodal hallucination evaluation benchmark using GPT-4 to assess model responses across 9 categories (object existence, attribute, spatial relation, counting, comparative reasoning, and more); responses scored by GPT-4 on hallucination severity
notes: Introduced in 'Aligning Large Multimodal Models with Factually Augmented RLHF' (Sun et al., 2023). arXiv:2309.14525. Used in D-LEAF paper (2509.07864) for GPT-4 assisted hallucination evaluation in comprehensive general scenarios.

name: Enwik9
num_samples: 1 billion bytes (1GB) of Wikipedia XML dump
format: Raw text from Wikipedia XML dump - standard Large Text Compression Benchmark entry

name: Silesia Corpus
format: Diverse file types including text, executables, images, databases - standard compression benchmark

name: ITC-99
format: RTL (Verilog) circuit graphs; nodes represent operators/variables, edges represent data flow
metric: MAE, R2, Recall@k for circuit functional modeling tasks

name: OpenCores
num_samples: ~1000+ RTL circuit designs from OpenCores repository
format: RTL (Verilog/VHDL) circuit graphs; open-source processor and peripheral designs
metric: MAE, R2, Recall@k for circuit functional modeling tasks

name: ISCAS-89
format: Sequential circuit benchmarks in bench format; nodes are flip-flops and gates, edges are wire connections
metric: MAE, R2 for sequential circuit modeling (transition probability, logic-1 probability)

name: ForgeEDA
num_samples: ~67K AIG and PM netlist circuits (comb. AIG: 9,800; PM netlist: 83,042)
format: And-Inverter Graphs (AIG) and Post-Mapping (PM) netlists from EDA tool flows; used for circuit representation learning

name: DeepCircuitX
num_samples: ~1000 RTL designs with multiple views (source code, graph, layout)
format: RTL designs with code, graph, and PPA (power/performance/area) annotations for multimodal circuit understanding
metric: PPA prediction accuracy, recall@k for circuit retrieval

name: DRAMP
format: Protein sequences with antimicrobial activity annotations and MIC values

name: AMPSphere
format: Protein sequences from microbial genomes and metagenomes with AMP predictions

name: DBAASP
format: Peptide sequences with MIC values and biological activity annotations

name: CUB-200-2011
format: 11788 images across 200 bird species with class labels and part annotations (head, body)

name: TIIF-Bench
eval_time: ~2-4 GPU hours for full evaluation on 1xA100
format: Compositional text-to-image prompts evaluating basic, advanced, and designer-level instruction following
metric: task-specific success rate across Basic, Advanced, and Designer subsets
license: Research (likely Apache-2.0 or similar - introduced in Wei et al. 2025)

name: MD-Cath
format: Molecular dynamics trajectories of protein domains (up to 500 residues) at 5 temperatures with 5 replicas each, frames saved at 1ns intervals

name: Tetrapeptides MD
format: Explicit solvent MD trajectories of tetrapeptides, 100ns each at 10ps resolution (10,000 frames per trajectory)

name: OGBench
num_samples: 85 goal-conditioned RL datasets + 410 standard offline RL tasks; some datasets reach 100M transitions
storage: Variable; pixel-based datasets require ~120GB RAM during training; total benchmark size tens of GBs
format: Offline RL trajectories with goals; state-based and pixel-based observations; 5 tasks per dataset

name: Natural Scenes Dataset (NSD)
num_samples: 8 participants, up to ~9000 unique images + ~1000 shared COCO images each; 7T fMRI beta volumes
storage: ~500GB-1TB (whole-brain 7T fMRI data for 8 participants in fsaverage space)
format: 7T fMRI beta volumes (1.8-mm resolution, fsaverage space), stimulus images (COCO), human captions (5 per image), and question-answer pairs (LVIS-Instruct4V)
metric: N/A (neural decoding dataset; evaluations use CLIPScore, Qwen3-Embedding cosine similarity)
license: NSD data access agreement required (free for researchers)

name: HiPhO
num_samples: ~300-400 problems from 7 latest physics Olympiads (IPhO, APhO, EuPhO, NBPhO, PanPhO, PanMechanics, F=MA)
format: Multimodal physics Olympiad problems with diagrams, plots, and free-response questions; evaluated using official marking schemes with step-level and answer-level scoring
metric: exam score (out of full mark), Pass@k, medal thresholds (gold/silver/bronze)

name: The Pile
format: Large-scale diverse text corpus for language modeling; 22 subsets including academic text, web text, code, etc.
license: Varies by subset (CC BY-SA 3.0 for many)

name: Wikitext-103
format: Word-level language modeling benchmark from Wikipedia articles; train/valid/test splits with long-term dependencies

name: Tetrapeptides MD Dataset
num_samples: 3309 tetrapeptides (3109 train / 100 val / 100 test), each with 100ns trajectories at 10ps resolution = ~10^4 frames per trajectory
format: MD trajectories of tetrapeptides (4-residue peptides) in explicit solvent at 100ns per trajectory, frames saved at 10ps intervals (~10,000 frames per trajectory); used for generative model evaluation via torsion angles, TICA projections, and MSM-based metrics
metric: JSD (torsion angles, TICA projections, MSM states), Macrostate MAE
notes: From Jing et al. (2024b), ICML'24 Workshop. Small-peptide MD benchmark for MD Emulator evaluation. Used in MARS-FM (arXiv:2509.24779) as preliminary evaluation before MD-Cath.

name: REDS
format: High-resolution video clips (720p-1080p) with multiple degradation tracks for video deblurring and super-resolution; Nah et al. NTIRE 2019 challenge

name: UDM10
format: 10 video sequences (100 frames each) with known degradation for video super-resolution evaluation; Tao et al. ICCV 2017

name: SPMCS
format: 30 video sequences for video super-resolution with progressive fusion; Yi et al. ICCV 2019. ~100 frames each.

name: VideoLQ
format: 10 real-world low-quality video sequences for video restoration; Chan et al. CVPR 2022b. Variable length (30-100 frames).

name: MovieLQ
format: 1000-frame-long single-shot real-world degraded videos from Vimeo and Pixabay (CC license); proposed in InfVSR paper (Zhang et al. arXiv:2510.00948) for long-form VSR evaluation
metric: MUSIQ, CLIP-IQA, DOVER, E*warp, BC, SC, MS (VBench semantic metrics)

name: MVSR4x
format: Real-world video super-resolution benchmark at 4x upscaling; Wang et al. CVPRW 2023b

name: OMOMO
num_samples: ~2.78 hours of retargeted trajectories (original motion capture not specified)
format: SMPL-format human motion with object interactions; retargeted to humanoid robots as joint angle trajectories at 30fps
license: Research use (from Li et al. TOG 2023)

name: LAFAN1
num_samples: ~4.6 hours of retargeted trajectories from 5 LAFAN1 subjects
format: BVH skeleton hierarchy format; retargeted to humanoid robots as joint angle trajectories at 30fps

name: DAPO-14k-MATH
format: 14k English math competition problems (derived from DAPO-Math-17k, excluding Chinese-language prompts). Used for label-free RL training in RESTRAIN experiments.

name: Synthetic S1k (CoT-Self-Instruct)
format: 5k synthetic reasoning problems with verifiable target answers, generated by prompting LLMs to reason step-by-step from the s1k seed set. From CoT-Self-Instruct (Yu et al., 2025a).

name: ExoRL
num_samples: Multiple domains (walker, cheetah, quadruped, pointmass) with millions of transitions
format: Offline RL trajectories from diverse reward-free policies; state-based and pixel-based observations; multiple tasks per domain

name: Nemotron-CC
format: Refined English web text from Common Crawl using classifier ensembling and synthetic rephrasing

name: τ-Bench
num_samples: retail: 500 train + 115 test tasks; airline: 50 train + 25 test tasks
format: Tool-use agent trajectories (observation-action pairs) with task descriptions and reward signals
metric: Task Success Rate (TSR), Attack Success Rate (ASR)

name: WebArena-Lite
format: Multi-step web navigation trajectories with accessibility tree observations
metric: Task Success Rate (TSR), Attack Success Rate (ASR)

name: NNetNav-WA
num_samples: ~45k observation-action pairs from web agent exploration
format: Browser interaction trajectories from NNetNav unsupervised collection with Llama-3.1-70B teacher

name: Glaive Tool-Calling Dataset
format: Tool-calling trajectories with function definitions and user queries

name: Go-Browse
num_samples: ~10k web browsing traces collected in WebArena environment
format: Browser interaction traces with goal annotations

name: DoomArena
num_samples: Framework for injecting triggers into WebArena environments
format: Framework that injects hidden HTML elements (triggers) into web pages for agent red-teaming

name: MQuAKE-3K
num_samples: ~3000 multi-hop edit instances (filtered subset of MQuAKE)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model size
format: Multi-hop factual question-answering pairs with knowledge editing prompts; tests cascade effects of single-hop edits on multi-hop reasoning chains

name: ChartBench
format: Chart images (9 major categories, 42 subcategories) with QA pairs; 75%+ unannotated charts requiring visual reasoning; numeric QA and relationship QA

name: ChartX
format: Chart images (18 categories including complex types) with QA pairs; 60%+ unannotated; numeric QA, value comparison, and global perception QA

name: MIMIR
num_samples: ~varies by model size (based on The Pile)
format: Membership inference benchmark for LLMs based on The Pile dataset with deduped train/test splits; evaluates attacks like LOSS, Zlib, Min-K%, Min-K%++, DC-PDD, Ref

name: ELSA-RAMD
num_samples: 75K train (2017-2019), 5K test goodware (2020-2022), 1.25K test malware (2020-2022), Track 3: 4 temporal test sets 25K each
eval_time: hours per full benchmark evaluation (genetic algorithm attacks)
format: DREBIN binary feature vectors (1,461,078 features per APK) extracted from AndroidManifest.xml and disassembled Dalvik bytecode
metric: TPR under feature-space attack (Track 1), TPR under problem-space attack (Track 2), AUT F1 (Track 3)

name: TinyImageNet
format: 64x64 RGB images (200 classes, 500 train/50 val/50 test per class)

name: FEVER
format: Claim + label (SUPPORTS/REFUTES/NOT_ENOUGH_INFO) with evidence sentences

name: SciFact
format: Claim + label (SUPPORTS/REFUTES) with abstract sentences

name: Climate-FEVER
format: Claim + label (SUPPORTS/REFUTES/NOT_ENOUGH_INFO) related to climate

name: LNCO2
storage: ~500GB+ (WSIs at 40x magnification, multiple scanners: Leica Aperio and Hamamatsu)
format: Whole-slide images of colon adenocarcinoma lymph node metastasis from Sweden; scanned at different magnifications (20x/40x); AIDA Data Hub access requires application and approval
metric: Accuracy, Precision, Recall (lymph node metastasis detection)
notes: External validation dataset for Pathology-CoT paper (arXiv:2510.04587). 321 WSIs from Sweden. Domain shift from training data (Stanford, Leica Aperio at 40x). Used to validate generalization of behavior-guided pathology agent.

name: Pathology-CoT
num_samples: 5,222 conversational rounds from 10.6 hours of recorded interactions (921 sessions, 137 slides, 25 cases, 8 pathologists)
storage: ~50-100GB (cropped ROIs, thumbnails, behavior bounding boxes, reasoning labels)
format: Expert pathologist viewing behavior data: <inspect>/<peek> commands with ROI bounding boxes, pathologist-verified reasoning rationales (avg 152 words for inspect, 82 words for peek), task-conditioned behavior+reasoning pairs
notes: First large-scale expert pathologist behavior dataset for computational pathology agent training. Records tacit diagnostic knowledge from pathologists at Stanford Medicine (attendings, fellows, residents). Enables training of behavior-guided pathology agents like Pathology-o3.

name: NUMINAMATH-LEAN-PF
format: NL (natural language) theorem-proof pairs paired with Lean 4 theorem-proof pairs. 30% human-written proofs, 70% KiminaProver-generated. Type-checked and paired. From NuminaMath-LEAN source.
notes: Curated by PROOFBRIDGE paper (arXiv:2510.15681) for proof autoformalization. Each pair has NL theorem+proof and Lean 4 theorem+proof (type-checked). Used to train PROOFBRIDGE's joint embedding and SFT model.

name: MINIF2F-TEST-PF
format: Lean v4.15.0 version of miniF2F-Test with NL theorem-proof pairs. Olympiad-level problems from AIME, AMC, IMO, and undergraduate courses in algebra, number theory, and inequalities.
notes: Curated by PROOFBRIDGE paper (arXiv:2510.15681). Lean v4.15.0-aligned version of miniF2F for proof autoformalization evaluation. Metrics: Type Correctness (TC) via Lean type-checker, Semantic Correctness (SC) via bi-directional equivalence proving with Gemini 2.5 Pro.

name: WebVoyager
eval_time: hours to days (long-horizon web navigation, up to 50 steps/task)
format: Multi-step web navigation trajectories via screenshots; tasks require visual grounding, information retrieval, form completion, multi-site coordination

name: WebArena
num_samples: 812 tasks across 6 self-hosted websites (GitLab, Reddit, OneStopShop, CMS, OpenStreetMap, Wikipedia)
eval_time: days (highly sequential, stateful, difficult to parallelize)
format: Multi-step web agent tasks with URL match, HTML artifact check, and LLM-judge evaluation; includes form filling, cross-site navigation, content management

name: OSWorld
storage: ~100GB (AWS Ubuntu VM images with desktop apps: LibreOffice, GIMP, Chrome, Thunderbird, VS Code, VLC)
format: Real Ubuntu VM screenshots (1920x1080, VNC) with keyboard/mouse actions; programmatic evaluation of file/app state

name: AndroidWorld
eval_time: hours (multi-step mobile tasks, up to 150 steps)
format: Android emulator screenshots with touch/keyboard gestures; ADB-based state verification; tasks across 20+ apps (Markor, VLC, OpenTracks, SMS, etc.)

name: FashionMNIST
format: 28x28 grayscale images of fashion items (10 classes)

name: Ditto-1M
num_samples: ~1M video triplets (source video, instruction, edited video)
format: video triplets with editing instructions

name: Gift-Eval
num_samples: 23 diverse real-world datasets across domains and horizons
format: Univariate time series forecasting tasks with various horizons; evaluates CRPS and MASE metrics
metric: CRPS (Continuous Ranked Probability Score), MASE (Mean Absolute Scaled Error)

name: Chronos-ZS
num_samples: 27 diverse datasets from GluonTS and Monash repositories
format: Zero-shot time series forecasting benchmark spanning multiple domains (energy, transport, healthcare) and frequencies

name: fev-bench
format: Standardized zero-shot forecasting benchmark with rigorous data leakage tracking and failure rate monitoring; evaluates Win Rate and Skill Score
metric: Win Rate (%), Skill Score (%), MASE, SQL (Scaled Quantile Loss)

name: RAID
num_samples: ~millions of human-written/machine-generated text pairs across 8 domains (Wikipedia, News, Abstracts, Recipes, Reddit, Poetry, Books, Reviews)
eval_time: hours per model (15 methods × 8 domains × multiple generators)
format: Large-scale machine-generated text detection benchmark. Human-written texts from diverse domains; machine-generated texts from multiple generators (GPT-2-XL, MPT-30B-Chat, LLaMA-2-70B-Chat, ChatGPT, GPT-4). Tests zero-shot detection methods.
access: https://github.com/ryuryukke/mint (see RAID paper: Dugan et al., ACL 2024)

name: U-Shaped Multi-Terminal HVDC System (Bertozzi et al.)
num_samples: 4-terminal HVDC with 4 AC areas, bipolar links, 4851 generation-mix combos × 11 windows (~50k samples)
eval_time: seconds per simulation, hours for full dataset generation
format: Time-domain simulation snapshots from DIgSILENT PowerFactory: voltage, frequency, active/reactive power measurements at all terminals and buses
metric: Stability classification (small-signal and transient), accuracy, precision, recall, F1, AUROC
license: Research use (custom system from Bertozzi et al. 2024/2025)
access: Reconstruct from paper description (Section III-B2, Fig 2) or contact authors

name: Arxiv
format: ArXiv papers for scientific language modeling

name: MADLAD-400
format: Web-crawled multilingual text corpus with document-level audits; used for pretraining and evaluation of multilingual language models

name: Flores-101
format: Language-parallel translation benchmark for low-resource and multilingual machine translation; human-translated sentences in 101 languages

name: PIE
eval_time: ~1-2 GPU hours for full evaluation on PIE-bench
format: Image editing instruction-image pairs covering object addition/removal, style transfer, pose modification; evaluated with LPIPS, SSIM, and EditScore
metric: LPIPS (lower is better), SSIM (higher is better), EditScore (higher is better)
license: Research (from PNP inversion, Ju et al., ICLR 2024)

name: ImageNette
format: 224x224 RGB images (10 easily classified ImageNet classes: tench, English springer, cassette player, chain saw, church, French horn, garbage truck, gas pump, golf ball, parachute)

name: LAION-400M
format: CLIP-filtered image-text pairs from Common Crawl
notes: Used for training Stable Diffusion models. Large-scale dataset that makes full-scale experiments expensive.

name: DiffusionDB
storage: ~ hundreds of GB to TB scale
format: Images generated by Stable Diffusion with user-provided prompts
notes: Used as source of attribution queries for Stable Diffusion experiments in FastGDA paper.

name: ChemO
eval_time: hours (API-based evaluation across multiple model configurations)
format: IChO 2025 theoretical chemistry problems reformulated via AER (Assessment-Equivalent Reformulation): visual-output problems converted to SMILES/numerical/textual outputs. Includes structured visual enhancement (SVE) as optional component.

name: Ambiguous-MNIST
format: 28x28 grayscale images with ambiguous/noisy labels for studying aleatoric uncertainty; same 10 digit classes as MNIST but with label ambiguity introduced to capture epistemic vs aleatoric uncertainty distinction
metric: AUROC (OOD/uncertainty detection), classification accuracy, softmax entropy
access: Available from Mukhoti et al. 2023 (Deep Deterministic Uncertainty) authors or similar
notes: Used in DDU benchmark to introduce aleatoric uncertainty during prediction. Paper trains exclusively on MNIST and uses Ambiguous-MNIST only at inference to test uncertainty disentanglement.

name: Deep Deterministic Uncertainty (DDU) Benchmark
num_samples: Varies by sub-task (MNIST: 70k, Fashion-MNIST: 70k, variants vary)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model architecture
format: Benchmark framework for evaluating uncertainty quantification in neural networks. In-distribution: MNIST. Out-of-distribution: Fashion-MNIST (epistemic uncertainty) and Ambiguous-MNIST (aleatoric uncertainty). Tests ability to distinguish between known classes, unknown classes, and ambiguous inputs.
metric: AUROC (OOD detection), ECE (Expected Calibration Error), NLL, classification accuracy
access: https://github.com/AMLab-Amsterdam/DDU or see Mukhoti et al. CVPR 2023
notes: Introduced by Mukhoti et al. 2023. Key insight: training only on MNIST without exposure to uncertainty samples, then evaluating on Fashion-MNIST (epistemic OOD) and Ambiguous-MNIST (aleatoric). Paper under analysis (2512.02217) uses this benchmark to demonstrate photonic BNN's ability to reason about uncertainty types.

name: D4RL
num_samples: varies by task (~1M transitions total across MuJoCo tasks)
eval_time: hours per full benchmark evaluation (training + evaluation of offline RL algorithms)
format: Offline RL transitions: (state, action, reward, next_state, done) tuples as numpy arrays. MuJoCo locomotion tasks: Walker2d, Hopper, HalfCheetah. Adroit manipulation tasks. Evaluation via normalized score (0-100 where 100=expert).
notes: D4RL (Datasets for Deep Data-Driven Reinforcement Learning) is the standard offline RL benchmark. Paper: Fu et al., arXiv:2004.07219. Used extensively in offline RL research including CQL, BCQ, BEAR, IQL papers.

name: RewardBench
format: Preference pairs across Chat, Chat-Hard, Safety, Code, Math categories; evaluates reward models and LLM-as-Judge methods
notes: RewardBench benchmark from Lambert et al. 2025. Used in arXiv:2512.02807 (SR-GRPO) to evaluate stable rank as a zero-shot reward proxy.

name: WildBench
format: Open-ended conversation prompts with GPT-4o-mini as judge; scores reported as Elo ratings
notes: WildBench from Lin et al. 2025. Used in arXiv:2512.02807 (SR-GRPO) to evaluate general chat quality with GPT-4o-mini as judge.

name: SmolTalk2
format: Diverse conversation prompts for LLM fine-tuning, from SmolLM2 paper (Allal et al. 2025)
notes: SmolTalk2 training dataset. Used in arXiv:2512.02807 (SR-GRPO) as the training prompt dataset for alignment fine-tuning.

name: BEHAVE
format: Multi-view RGB-D videos of human-object interactions with 3D annotations (SMPL + object pose)
notes: BEHAVE: Dataset and Method for Tracking Human Object Interactions (CVPR 2022). Full-body human-object interaction with object category and instance annotations, SMPL-H body parameters, 6DoF object poses. Used in CARI4D for training and evaluation.

name: HODome
format: Multi-view capture of human-object interactions in domestic environments with 3D annotations
notes: NeuralDome: A Neural Modeling Pipeline on Multi-View Human-Object Interactions (CVPR 2023). Captures diverse domestic interactions with multiple camera views and detailed 3D annotations. Used in CARI4D for training CoCoNet.

name: InterCap
format: Multi-view RGB videos of human-object interaction with joint markerless 3D annotations
notes: InterCap: Joint Markerless 3D Tracking of Humans and Objects in Interaction (GCPR 2022). Used in CARI4D as an unseen dataset for zero-shot generalization testing.

name: OPV2V
num_samples: 11,464 LiDAR frames from 2-5 agents across 70 scenes in 8 CARLA towns
format: LiDAR point clouds with 3D bounding box annotations for cooperative perception; includes V2X communication simulation
notes: OPV2V is a large-scale simulated cooperative perception dataset. Used in JigsawComm (arXiv:2511.17843) and other CP papers like Where2comm, ERMVP, CoST.

name: DAIR-V2X
format: Real-world vehicle-infrastructure cooperative perception dataset with LiDAR point clouds and 3D annotations
notes: DAIR-V2X is the first large-scale real-world cooperative perception dataset. Used in JigsawComm (arXiv:2511.17843) for evaluating vehicle-infrastructure cooperation.

name: IoT-23
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on replay setup
format: PCAP network captures of IoT traffic: real malware (Mirai, Torii, Hajime, Kenjiro) and benign traffic captured in a real IoT network environment at Stratosphere Labs (Czech Technical University). Each capture contains full packet payloads with labeled attack/benign labels.
metric: attack detection rate, mitigation rate, FPR
notes: IoT-23 dataset from Garcia et al. (2020). Used in paper 2512.23849 (EDS) for real malware validation of the Economic Denial Security framework against Mirai, Torii, Hajime, and Kenjiro botnet families.

name: FineWeb
format: Web text filtered for quality, tokenized for LLM training

name: CoCoGlide
format: Image pairs (original + edited) with pixel-level masks for diffusion-based editing localization. Generated using GLIDE model (mask-required).
notes: CoCoGlide benchmark from Wang et al. (CVPR 2023). First major DIML benchmark using GLIDE-generated images. Used in DEAL-300K paper for cross-dataset evaluation.

name: AutoSplice
format: Image pairs with pixel-level masks for diffusion-based manipulation localization. Generated using DALL-E2 (mask-required).
notes: AutoSplice dataset from Huang et al. (ICCV 2023). Diffusion-based image manipulation dataset with DALL-E2 edits. Used in DEAL-300K paper for cross-dataset evaluation.

name: Repaint-P2/CelebA-HQ
format: Face image pairs with pixel-level masks for diffusion-based inpainting localization. Generated using Repaint method.
notes: Repaint-P2 dataset from Carcagni et al. (CVPR 2024). Face-specific diffusion manipulation localization benchmark using Repaint inpainting. Used in DEAL-300K paper for cross-dataset evaluation.

name: DEAL-300K
format: Large-scale dataset for Diffusion-based Image Manipulation Localization (DIML). Contains original/edited image pairs with pixel-level masks. Generated using InstructPix2Pix (mask-free). Includes DEAL-A (authentic-only), DEAL-E (edited-only), DEAL-Full (mixed), and DEAL-MB (multi-step) test subsets.
notes: DEAL-300K: Diffusion-based Editing Area Localization with a 300K-Scale Dataset (arXiv:2511.23377). Largest-scale DIML dataset to date. Uses MLLM-driven instruction generation and active learning-based annotation pipeline.

name: PPE (Preference Proxy Evaluation)
num_samples: ~22900 samples total (PPE Preference: 10200 pairs, PPE Correctness: 12700 pairs)
format: PPE Preference: real-world prompts from LM Arena with human preference pairs from 20 LLMs across 121 languages. PPE Correctness: response pairs from four models on five benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, MATH, GPQA, MBPP-Plus, IFEval) spanning knowledge, mathematics, STEM, coding, and instruction following.
metric: Kuiper statistic, ECE (Expected Calibration Error), accuracy
notes: PPE dataset from Frick et al. 2024. Addresses two key LLM judge tasks: preference alignment and correctness. Used in arXiv:2512.22245 (Calibrating LLM Judges) to train linear probes for uncertainty estimation.

name: JudgeBench
format: Correct-incorrect response pairs across knowledge, reasoning, math, and coding tasks. Tests out-of-distribution generalization of LLM judge methods.
notes: JudgeBench from Tan et al. 2024. Used in arXiv:2512.22245 (Calibrating LLM Judges) for out-of-distribution evaluation of calibration methods.

name: MVSEC (Multi Vehicle Stereo Event Camera)
num_samples: Multiple sequences (outdoor_day2 for training, outdoor_night1-3 for testing)
format: Synchronized RGB frames (APS), asynchronous event streams (DVS), and LiDAR-derived depth ground truth from Velodyne Puck LITE
metric: Abs Rel, RMSE log, delta < 1.25 (depth); ATE, RPE trans, RPE rot (pose)
notes: Event camera dataset for 3D perception. Contains outdoor day/night sequences with stereo event cameras. Used in EAG3R paper for zero-shot low-light depth estimation and pose tracking.

name: Waymo Open E2E Dataset
num_samples: 4021 driving scenes, 20 seconds each sampled at 4Hz (~321k frames); 8 cameras providing 360-degree FOV (5 used in paper: front, front-left, front-right, side-left, side-right)
format: Multi-view camera images (448x448), past state sequence (16 timesteps = 4 seconds), driving intent (go left/straight/right)
license: Waymo Research License (free for research, requires agreement)
notes: Curated to capture long-tail scenarios (<0.003% frequency in daily driving). Used in 2025 Waymo End-to-End Driving Challenge. Task: predict future waypoints for next 5 seconds (H=20 at 4Hz) from current sensor inputs and past state.

name: VERITAS
num_samples: 24K claims (1K per quarterly split) with 8,377 images and 4,785 videos across 54 languages
format: Real-world multimodal claims (text + images/videos) annotated with fine-grained integrity scores (-1 to 1), media authenticity, contextualization, veracity, and context coverage properties, with textual justifications

name: SynCamVideo
format: Synthetic multi-camera dynamic RGB sequences of human motion captured under dynamic and static camera trajectories across 40 synthetic 3D environments
notes: SyncCamMaster: Synchronizing Multi-Camera Video Generation from Diverse Viewpoints (Bai et al., ICLR 2025). Used alongside MultiCamVideo for training PlenopticDreamer on Basic benchmark.

name: Agibot World Colosseo
num_samples: ~1M episodes total; 145,820 sampled for PlenopticDreamer training
format: Synchronized multi-view videos (head-view + 2 gripper-views) with precise camera pose annotations for robotic manipulation tasks
notes: Agibot World Colosseo: A Large-Scale Manipulation Platform for Scalable and Intelligent Embodied Systems (Bu et al., IROS 2025). Used for training PlenopticDreamer-Agibot on head-view to gripper-view transformations.

name: VNN-COMP (Verification of Neural Networks Competition)
num_samples: Multiple benchmark sets (ACASXu, CIFAR-ResNet, CIFAR-CNN, etc.)
format: Pre-trained neural networks with specified safety/robustness properties to verify
metric: Verified accuracy, verification time, number of branch-and-bound subproblems
notes: Annual competition for neural network verification. Uses branch-and-bound based verifiers to certify robustness and safety properties.

name: ACASXu
num_samples: 97 neural networks (acasxu_nn_n with n=1-5, 6 variants each)
format: Pre-trained neural networks for aircraft collision avoidance, with property specifications
notes: Standard benchmark for neural network verification from aerospace control. Networks have 5 hidden layers with 50-100 neurons each.

name: AMC
format: American Mathematics Competitions (AMC 10/12) multiple-choice math problems

name: Jericho
eval_time: hours (text-based game playing with multiple episodes)
format: Text-based adventure games where agents interact purely via textual commands; sparse reward signals
notes: Jericho benchmark from Hausknecht et al. AAAI 2020. Tests agents on long-horizon text-based games with sparse rewards.

name: UCI German Credit
format: credit attributes with good/bad credit risk labels

name: UCI Bank Marketing
format: bank client attributes with binary subscription labels

name: UltraVideo
format: High-quality 4K videos with detailed captions
notes: High-quality UHD video dataset with comprehensive captions for 4K video generation. Used in T3-Video paper (arXiv:2512.13492) for fine-tuning.

name: 4K-VBench
format: 4K video prompts for evaluation
metric: VQA (Video Quality Assessment), VTC (Video-Text Consistency), DoG, BM, RA, TDS, TEP
notes: 4K video generation benchmark introduced in T3-Video paper (arXiv:2512.13492). Uses FineVQ for VQA at 1080P and 4K, and Qwen3-VL-32B for VTC.

name: SynthShape
format: Synthetic geometric primitives (circle, square, triangle, cross, star) with unique segmentation masks. Ground truth assigns class label per shape type.
notes: Introduced in arXiv:2601.19884 (SONIC). Designed to evaluate robustness to geometric transformations including rescaling, rotation, translation, distortion, and Gaussian noise.

name: HalliGalli-SRT
format: 64x64 images with a central patch and four corner patches. Task: classify central patch based on whether exactly two matching shapes appear in the corners. The center carries no class signal; only long-range spatial dependencies encode the label.
metric: accuracy (and accuracy under Gaussian noise sigma=0.1)
notes: Introduced in arXiv:2601.19884 (SONIC). Tests effective long-range dependency modeling. Purely local models fail. Architectures with untargeted global filters either fail due to missing orientation or degrade under Gaussian noise. SONIC solves it with its globally-oriented structured receptive field.

name: Textualized Gridworld
format: Text-based grid navigation task where agent navigates using cardinal directions (up/down/left/right) while avoiding obstacles; states are grid coordinates, actions are single moves; evaluates exact path matching
notes: From Kim et al., 2024 ('How language models extrapolate outside the training data'). Used in TSLM paper (arXiv:2601.22688) for structured planning evaluation with in-distribution (10x10) and out-of-distribution (20x20) grid sizes.

name: ProntoQA
format: Logical reasoning dataset where models verify statement truth given premises using deductive reasoning steps; actions are logical deduction steps, states are accumulated facts; evaluates exact matching of deduction chains
notes: From Saparov & He, 2023 ('Language models are greedy reasoners'). Used in TSLM paper (arXiv:2601.22688) for open-ended reasoning evaluation.

name: Text2World
format: Natural language descriptions paired with PDDL domain definitions
metric: Executability, Structural Similarity, Component-wise F1 (predicates, parameters, preconditions, effects)
notes: Benchmark for text-to-PDDL world model generation. Evaluates whether generated PDDL domains are syntactically valid and semantically similar to ground truth.

name: Code World Models Benchmark (CWMB)
format: Python code implementing MuJoCo-style physics environments
metric: Accuracy (predictive correctness), Normalized Return R (discrete/continuous control utility)
notes: Benchmark for generating executable code world models. Tests both predictive accuracy and downstream control performance.

name: ByteSized32
format: Python text games requiring reasoning and executable environments
metric: Technical validity, Specification compliance, Winnability, Physical reality alignment
notes: Suite of reasoning-heavy text games requiring executable Python environments. Tests generation of interactive text-based game simulators.

name: Camelyon17-WILDS
format: Breast cancer metastasis detection in淋巴结whole-slide images. Domain shift: training from 3 hospitals, test on 4th hospital.

name: FMoW-WILDS
format: Functional land-use classification from satellite imagery. Domain shift: training on past years (2002-2014), test on future years (2016-2018). Also has geographic subpopulation shift.

name: CivilComments-WILDS
format: Toxic comment classification with demographic subgroup annotations. Subpopulation shift: toxicity rates vary across demographic identities.

name: BREEDS-Living-17
format: BREEDS benchmark: subpopulation shift on ImageNet-17 classes. Tests robustness to spurious correlations in object classification.

name: BREEDS-Entity-30
format: BREEDS benchmark: subpopulation shift on ImageNet-30 entity classes. More diverse than Living-17.

name: RouterBench
storage: <100MB (pre-computed per-query model performance scores for 11 models)
eval_time: minutes (router inference only; no LLM inference needed)
format: Query-level routing decisions with pre-computed accuracy/cost for each candidate model. Aggregates HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-Challenge, MMLU, MT-Bench, GSM8K, MBPP, and RAG subsets.
metric: nAUC, QNC, Peak Score, RCI (Routing Collapse Index)
notes: Primary benchmark for LLM routing. Introduced in arXiv:2403.12031 (Hu et al., 2024). Pre-computed model outputs enable offline router evaluation without API calls.

name: MMR-Bench
storage: <200MB (pre-computed per-query model performance scores for multimodal LLMs)
eval_time: minutes (router inference only; no LLM inference needed)
format: Multimodal LLM routing benchmark covering OCRBench, SEED-Bench-v2-Plus, MM-Star, RealWorldQA, MathVerse, MathVista, MathVision with pre-computed per-query model accuracy/cost.
metric: nAUC, QNC, Peak Score, RCI (Routing Collapse Index)
notes: Multimodal extension of RouterBench. Introduced in arXiv:2601.17814 (Ma et al., 2026). Pre-computed model outputs enable offline evaluation.

name: BiGGen Bench
format: Free-form generation benchmark with instance-specific criteria evaluating what a good answer should contain for each prompt
metric: Per-axis rubric scores (Instruction Following, Reasoning, Safety, etc.)
notes: BiGGen Bench from Kim et al. 2024. LLM-based evaluation benchmark for fine-grained assessment of language models across diverse capabilities including instruction following, reasoning, planning, theory of mind, tool use, and safety.

name: SimBench
format: Multiple-choice questions on social and behavioral topics (AfroBarometer, ESS, ISSP, LatinoBarometro, OpinionQA, etc.)
metric: Majority-vote accuracy (whether persona selects most frequent human response for demographic group)
notes: Composite benchmark for evaluating LLM ability to simulate human behavioral responses. Aggregates 20 large-scale social and behavioral datasets.

name: ZsRE
format: Zero-shot relation extraction QA pairs derived from relation extraction data; used for evaluating knowledge editing generalization across paraphrased queries

name: WikiBigEdit
format: Large-scale lifelong knowledge editing benchmark constructed from real-world Wikidata snapshot diffs; chronological stream of factual changes with question-answer pairs, paraphrases, and locality probes
metric: edit success (ES), generalization success (GS), locality success (LS)

name: SPIDER (Supervised Pathology Image Dataset for Event Recognition)
num_samples: ~10,000+ H&E patches across 4 cancer progressions (SCC, CRC-Conventional, CRC-Serrated, BDC)
format: H&E-stained histopathology patches at 20x magnification from HI-STAI collection; provides patch-level class labels for disease progression trajectories
license: Research use (institutional sources, scanner mappings not publicly disclosed)
access: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.02876 (Nechaev et al., 2025b); associated HI-STAI collection at https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.12120
notes: Used in 'Do Pathology Foundation Models Encode Disease Progression' paper (2601.21334) to evaluate trajectory fidelity of pathology foundation models. Four disease progressions: Skin SCC (epidermis→actinic keratosis→SCC in situ→invasive SCC), CRC-Conventional (adenoma low→adenoma high→adenocarcinoma low→adenocarcinoma high), CRC-Serrated (hyperplastic polyp→SSL→adenocarcinoma high grade), BDC (DCIS low→DCIS high→invasive carcinoma).

name: G4SAT
storage: ~1-2GB (CNF files, easy ~26 vars to hard++ ~5000 vars, selected near satisfiability threshold)
eval_time: minutes per instance (WL test + SAT solver check)
format: CNF files in DIMACS format, grouped by family (3-sat, k-clique, k-vercov, CA) and difficulty
metric: WL distinguishability (r_crit vs r_converged), satisfiability of augmented formulas

name: International SAT Competition
num_samples: hundreds of instances per year across multiple families
storage: ~50GB+ (full competition archives); paper uses subset <10MB per instance
eval_time: minutes to hours per instance (WL convergence + SAT solving)
format: CNF/DIMACS format with instance metadata (family, year, source application)
metric: WL distinguishability (r_crit vs r_converged), satisfiability of augmented formulas

name: IOI (Indirect Object Identification)
format: Synthetic sentences testing model's ability to identify indirect object (e.g., 'Then, [Name A] and [Name B] went to the [place]. [Name B] gave a [item] to [Name A]'); model must predict which name receives the item
notes: Canonical interpretability benchmark testing induction heads and causal reasoning in language models. Used to assess whether post-trained MDMs preserve autoregressive circuitry for local causal dependencies.

name: Countdown
format: Given a set of integers and a target value, generate a valid arithmetic expression that equals the target (e.g., inputs: [3, 5, 7, 10], target: 36; output: 10*3+7-5=36)
notes: Numerical reasoning task requiring inverse planning - early decisions must be conditioned on final goal. Challenges left-to-right causality of ARMs while favoring bidirectional context and iterative refinement of MDMs.

name: TikTok Human Video Dataset
format: Social media dance videos from TikTok with diverse human motions, used for human video generation/animation evaluation

name: FRAMES
format: multi-hop QA requiring retrieval, reasoning, and multi-constraint satisfaction over Wikipedia

name: GAIA
format: real-world open-ended questions requiring multi-step research and tool use

name: BIG-Bench Extra Hard (BBEH)
format: Multiple-choice questions requiring multi-step reasoning across diverse domains

name: ZebraLogicBench
format: Zebra puzzles (logic grid puzzles) requiring multi-step deductive reasoning

name: MuSR
format: Multi-step soft reasoning puzzles requiring logical deduction from narrative text

name: FOLIO
format: First-order logic deduction problems (True/Uncertain/False)

name: MCP-Bench
storage: <1GB (task definitions + MCP server configs; actual tool data fetched at runtime)
eval_time: hours for full evaluation (28 servers × multiple task types × multiple models)
format: Multi-server tool-use tasks requiring planning, tool selection, and parameter accuracy across diverse MCP servers (weather, academic search, scientific computing, etc.)
metric: Task fulfillment (LLM-judged), planning effectiveness, tool selection correctness, parameter accuracy; efficiency metrics (token usage, execution time, turns)
notes: Primary MCP evaluation benchmark from Wang et al. (2025). Used in arXiv:2602.15945 for comparing traditional MCP vs CE-MCP architectures.

name: CWQ (ComplexWebQuestions)
format: Complex question answering over knowledge graphs; requires multi-hop reasoning

name: WebQSP
format: WebQuestion SPARQL dataset; requires single-hop or multi-hop reasoning over Freebase

name: GrailQA
format: Graph-based question answering requiring multi-hop reasoning over knowledge graphs; includes different difficulty levels

name: OneIG-Bench
format: Text-to-image evaluation with English (OneIG-EN) and Chinese (OneIG-ZH) prompts; tests alignment, text rendering, reasoning, style, and diversity
metric: GPT-4V-based scoring across Alignment, Text, Reasoning, Style, Diversity dimensions

name: OTDD (Optimal Transport Dataset Distance)
format: Measures distance between labeled datasets using entropic OT with feature-label cost matrix

name: RGB-Stacking
format: Synthetic robotic manipulation videos with large texture-less regions for evaluating point tracking

name: RoboTAP
format: Real-world robotic manipulation videos for tracking any point evaluation

name: The Common Pile
format: Curated 880GB English text corpus derived from The Pile, focusing on high-quality sources; designed for training language models with improved quality and reduced compute requirements
license: Varies by subset (CC BY-SA 3.0 for many)
notes: v0.1 used in DLM-Scope paper for SAE training

name: Epic-Kitchens100
format: Egocentric videos of daily kitchen activities with verb+noun action labels, captured from head-mounted cameras; subsampled to 10fps in ARM4R paper

name: OpenX-Embodiment
num_samples: millions of robot demonstrations across 22 robot embodiments
format: Multi-robot, multi-task manipulation dataset with diverse sensor modalities, tasks, and action spaces; includes data from 22 different robots

name: VisA
num_samples: 10,821 images (8,659 normal train + 962 normal + 1,200 anomalous test) across 12 object categories
format: High-resolution industrial images with pixel-level anomaly masks; 12 object categories (candle, capsules, cashew, chewinggum, fryum, pipe fryum, macaroni, margarita, me骯ta, Lesdog, rectifiedsprite, and screws)

name: LeetCode-2K
format: Code problems with Python solutions, derived from LeetCode platform. Each problem includes description, function signature, and reference solutions. Used for RL training and evaluation of code reasoning models.
notes: Introduced in Xia et al., 2025 (arXiv:2504.14655). Used in this paper for RL training experiments with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to study CoT length evolution during reinforcement learning.

name: Clipart1K
format: 1,000 clipart images with bounding box annotations for cross-domain object detection; used in this paper for vectorization evaluation on non-photorealistic images

name: DanbooRegion
format: High-quality anime/cartoon illustration images with region-level annotations for structure-aware vectorization; used in this paper for vectorization evaluation on cartoon images
access: Zhang et al., ECCV 2020; https://github.com/lvmin zhang/DanbooRegion

name: MiniF2F
eval_time: hours to days depending on sample budget
format: Formal Lean 4 theorem proving problems from AIME, AMC, IMO, MATH competitions

name: PutnamBench
eval_time: hours to days depending on sample budget
format: Formal Lean 4 problems from Putnam Mathematical Competition (1962-2023)
metric: number of problems solved (proof verification by Lean)

name: ProofNet
eval_time: hours to days depending on sample budget
format: Formal Lean 3/4 problems from undergraduate textbooks (real/complex analysis, linear algebra, abstract algebra, topology)

name: CombiBench
format: Formal Lean 4 combinatorial competition problems with natural language statements

name: FormalMATH
format: Formal Lean 4 problems ranging from high school Olympiad to undergraduate-level mathematics

name: ProverBench
format: Formal Lean 4 problems; 15 from AIME competitions (number theory, algebra), 310 from textbooks covering diverse math domains

name: QReCC
format: Conversational QA with query-response pairs and reference passages

name: TopiOCQA
format: Conversational QA with topic switching and reference passages

name: SciConvQA
format: Conversational QA in scientific domain with reference passages

name: Bench2Drive
num_samples: Base set: 1000 clips (950 train, 50 val); Closed-loop eval: 220 short routes across 44 interactive scenarios
eval_time: hours for closed-loop evaluation per run (CARLA simulator)
format: Multi-view camera clips (~150m continuous driving) with VQA annotations; CARLA V2 simulator for closed-loop evaluation
metric: Driving Score (DS), Success Rate (SR), Efficiency, Comfortness, Multi-Ability

name: MM-MT-Bench
format: Multi-turn multimodal benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on complex visual dialogue tasks

name: MSEarth
format: Multimodal scientific comprehension benchmark for earth science requiring expert-level knowledge

name: QuALITY
num_samples: ~1000 questions across 50 articles (15-20 questions per 5-8k token article)
format: multiple-choice QA with long documents

name: LongHealth
num_samples: 4 contexts, 100 questions per context (60k tokens per context)
format: clinical patient records QA

name: Ref-AVSBench
num_samples: 2,908 audio-equipped video clips (training), test set size not specified

format: Reasoning Video Object Segmentation; text instructions require temporal reasoning and world knowledge to identify target objects across video sequences

name: MeVIS
num_samples: ~2,600 videos in training set (used in Omni-R1 paper)
format: Large-scale video object segmentation dataset with temporal annotations; videos typically <30 seconds

name: AVHBench
num_samples: 5,302 samples in JUDGE subset (audio-visual hallucination evaluation)
format: Audio-visual hallucination benchmark evaluating perception and comprehension of audio-visual LLMs; tests audio-related hallucination issues

format: Full-modality leaderboard benchmark for omni-modal models covering text, audio, image, and video understanding

format: Harmful instructions for evaluating LLM safety refusal behaviors

format: Tabular dataset with reaction conditions (reactants, products, catalysts, solvents, temperature) and yield outcomes

name: Arylation

format: Tabular dataset with C-H functionalization reaction conditions and yield outcomes
metric: Best found yield (%), convergence speed (iterations to 95% of optimum)
