num_samples: ~2500 original entries (15 aryl halides × 4 ligands × 3 bases × 23 additives); paper uses sub-sets Buchwald-sub1 (629 entries) and Buchwald-sub2 (765 entries)
format: Tabular dataset with C-N coupling reaction conditions (aryl halides, ligands, bases, additives) and yield outcomes
metric: Best found yield (%), convergence speed (iterations to 95% of optimum)

name: Pistachio
num_samples: ~19.17M total reactions in full dataset; ~50k used for pre-training in ChemBOMAS paper
storage: ~50GB for full dataset (SMILES strings); ~50MB for 50k subset used in paper
format: Chemical reaction SMILES strings extracted from USPTO and EPO patents, with reaction conditions

name: VERITE
eval_time: minutes to hours per contract depending on method
format: EVM smart contract source code + deployment bytecode + constructor arguments + block numbers for 27 real-world DeFi exploits on Ethereum and Binance Smart Chain (April 2021 – 2025)
metric: exploit success rate, revenue extracted (USD), exploit complexity (SLOC, external calls)
notes: VERIFY: Kong et al., FSE 2025. 27 incidents covering access control, logic/invariant bugs, tokenomics/pool accounting, arithmetic, oracle mispricing, predictable randomness, and signature vulnerabilities. A1 paper (arXiv:2507.05558) uses 27 VERITE incidents plus 9 additional real-world exploits for total of 36 DeFi incidents.

name: ProofWriter
format: Synthetic natural language reasoning problems with rule-based microworlds; evaluates logical deduction with implications, proofs, and abductive statements
notes: From Tafjord et al., 2020 ('ProofWriter: Generating implications, proofs, and abductive statements over natural language'). Used in LogicAgent paper (arXiv:2509.24765) for logical reasoning evaluation.

name: ProverQA
format: Natural language reasoning with first-order logic; generated via ProverGen pipeline combining LLM generation with theorem proving
notes: From Qi et al., 2025 ('Large language models meet symbolic provers for logical reasoning evaluation'). Used in LogicAgent paper (arXiv:2509.24765) for hard logical reasoning evaluation.

name: RepublicQA
format: College-level semantic difficulty (FKGL=11.94) logical reasoning benchmark with abstract philosophical propositions; systematically constructed contrary and contradictory forms; True/False/Uncertain labels
notes: New benchmark from LogicAgent paper (arXiv:2509.24765). Derived from Plato's Republic with multi-stage cross-validated annotation. Designed to evaluate logical reasoning under semantic complexity and ambiguity.

name: ReasonVOS
num_samples: 91 videos with 253 long-form queries (averaging 105 frames each)
format: Videos with complex linguistic reasoning queries including causal reasoning and hypothetical scenarios; pixel-level mask sequences

name: MeViS
format: Videos with motion-centric referring expressions; pixel-level mask sequences for multi-object and motion-intensive expressions

name: TensoIR
num_samples: 4 objects x 6 lights x 200 views = 4800 renderings
format: Synthetic object renderings with known geometry, materials, and lighting for inverse rendering evaluation
access: https://github.com/ImnoIR/ Tensoir (paper: Jin et al., CVPR 2023)

name: Stanford-ORB
format: Real-world 3D object captures with multi-light imaging for inverse rendering
access: https://github.com/ Stanford-ORB (paper: Kuang et al., NeurIPS 2024)

name: Polyhaven
format: High dynamic range equirectangular environment maps for lighting/relighting

name: nuPlan
format: Large-scale autonomous driving planning benchmark with 15-second scenarios covering 10 dynamic scenario categories; includes sensor data (cameras, LiDAR, radar), map data, and agent annotations; supports closed-loop non-reactive (CL-NR) and reactive (CL-R) evaluation
metric: NR Score, R Score combining collision, TTC, drivable area, comfort, progress, speed metrics

name: DeepUrban
num_samples: Drone-recorded urban trajectory data for Munich scenarios
storage: ~100-200GB estimated (drone aerial imagery and trajectory data)
format: Drone-recorded trajectory data for urban driving scenarios in Munich; captures diverse challenging scenarios in densely populated areas; used for open-loop planning evaluation with collision rate, off-road percentage, and progress ratio metrics
metric: Collision Rate, Off-Road Percentage, Progress Ratio

name: MMAU
format: Multi-task audio understanding benchmark covering sound, music, and speech categories with reasoning tasks

name: MMAR
format: Benchmark for deep reasoning in speech, audio, music, and their mix

name: SongDescriber
format: Music audio captions dataset for evaluating text-to-audio generation; each audio has descriptive captions
metric: FDopenl3, KLpasst, CLAP, AES, OVL, REL

name: RULER
format: Synthetic long-context retrieval tasks including S-NIAH (needle-in-a-haystack) variants

name: BABILONG
format: Extended bAbI tasks with up to 1k distractor tokens for long-context reasoning evaluation

name: VGGSound
format: 10-second video clips with single audio label from YouTube; 309 classes
metric: mAP, FD, KL, IS, IB-score, DeSync

name: VGG-Impact
format: Curated subset of VGGSound focusing on object-object interaction events (collisions, impacts, bouncing); 10 sound classes; paired video-audio with object-level physics annotations
access: Not publicly released as of paper submission (contact authors)

name: NOCS-CAMERA25
format: Synthetic RGB-D images with 6 categories, 1085 object instances; used for category-level 6D pose estimation
metric: mAP (3D IoU @50%, 75%), rotation error (5°, 10°), translation error (2cm, 5cm)

name: NOCS-REAL275
format: Real-world RGB-D images from 13 scenes with 6 categories; each category has 3 unseen test instances; standard benchmark for category-level 6D pose estimation
metric: mAP (3D IoU @50%, 75%), rotation error (5°, 10°), translation error (2cm, 5cm)

name: METR-LA
format: Traffic speed measurements from 207 sensors in Los Angeles County (5-min intervals)

name: AQI
format: Hourly PM2.5 pollutant measurements from 437 air quality monitoring stations in China

name: GPVAR
format: Synthetic spatiotemporal data generated via graph diffusion process on 60-node community graph
access: Generated via code in Zambon & Alippi (2022)

name: HELLASWAG
format: 4-choice commonsense reasoning about event sequences

name: WINOGRANDE
format: Winograd-schema challenge for commonsense reasoning

name: OPENBOOKQA
format: 4-choice science question answering requiring world knowledge

name: D-PILE
format: Deduplicated Pile dataset for language model pretraining

name: HiRO ARVC Registry
num_samples: 1,344 ECGs from 645 patients (13 Canadian cardiac centers)
storage: ~100MB (8-lead x 2,500 samples at 32-bit float per ECG)
format: 12-lead ECG (8-lead used: I, II, V1-V6); 10-second duration at 250Hz; stored as 32-bit float tensors
metric: AUROC (macro for multi-class, per-class for binary)
license: Research use only (Canadian Hearts in Rhythm Organization)
access: not publicly released; data access through HiRO registry agreement with University of British Columbia et al.
notes: Canadian multi-center inherited arrhythmia registry containing ARVC (n=121 patients, 379 ECGs), LQTS (n=268 patients, 465 ECGs), and controls (n=256 patients, 500 ECGs). Used for training and evaluation in LASAN paper (arXiv:2601.07124). Preprocessed ECGs up-sampled to 500Hz, truncated to 5s (8 leads x 2,500 samples). Patient-level 70/15/15 train/val/test split.

name: R2R-CE
format: R2R task in continuous Habitat simulator environment with low-level robot control (forward/back/turn); not restricted to predefined navigation graph
metric: Success Rate (SR), Oracle Success Rate (OSR), Trajectory Length (TL), Navigation Error (NE), SPL, nDTW
notes: R2R in Continuous Environments (Krantz et al. 2020). VLN variant in Habitat 0.3.2 simulator with low-level control instead of discrete navigation graph. Paper uses random subset of 100 trajectories from val-unseen.

name: RxR-CE
format: Room-Across-Room multilingual VLN in continuous Habitat environment; instruction in English, Hindi, or Telugu
metric: Success Rate (SR), Oracle Success Rate (OSR), SPL, nDTW
notes: RxR-CE (Ku et al. 2020): RxR dataset variant in continuous Habitat environments. Multilingual VLN with instructions in English, Hindi, and Telugu. Paper uses random subset of 200 trajectories from val-unseen.

name: Habitat
format: Continuous environment simulator for embodied AI; supports low-level robot control, RGB-D sensing, collision checking; version 0.3.2 used
notes: Habitat simulator (Savva et al. 2019). Used for continuous VLN environments (R2R-CE, RxR-CE) in this paper. Version 0.3.2 specifically used as stated in the paper.

name: SYSU-CD
format: Bitemporal multi-spectral satellite image pairs from Google Earth with binary land-cover change masks; captures heterogeneous changes (urban, farmland, vegetation)
access: Paper: Shi et al., IEEE TGRS 2021

name: VL-CMU-CD
num_samples: ~260k image pairs (~250k train / 10k test) at 256x256 pixels
format: Urban street-view image pairs from Pittsburgh with large viewpoint shifts, dynamic objects, and illumination changes; bitemporal images with binary change masks

name: Event Camera Dataset (ECD)
num_samples: ~several sequences for motion estimation (boxes, dynamic, poster, shapes rotations and translations)
format: Event camera data (timestamped asynchronous events with polarity) for ego-motion, odometry, and SLAM
metric: RMS error (deg/s for rotation, m/s for translation), trajectory error
notes: From Mueggler et al. 2017. Used for event-based motion estimation, optical flow, and SLAM benchmarks.

name: DSEC (Dense Events Stereo Camera)

metric: EPE (End Point Error), Angular Error, 3PE (outlier percentage)

name: DNA-Rendering

name: OE62
format: Molecular structures with 3D coordinates, atomic numbers, DFT-computed energies (PBE functional)
access: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.12538 (original publication), similar structures available in computational chemistry databases

name: AQM
format: Gas-phase molecular conformations with DFTB3+MBD reference calculations for energy and forces

name: HDTF
format: High-resolution face video dataset for talking head / portrait animation evaluation
metric: FVD, Sync-C, Sync-D, CSIM, LPIPS, PSNR, L1, MAE

name: TalkingHead-1KH
format: Talking head dataset for one-shot face animation; used as source image dataset in cross-reenactment

name: CMU-Mosei
format: Multimodal sentiment analysis dataset with audio, video, and text; used as driving video source for portrait animation evaluation

name: FairFace
format: Face images with balanced demographic annotations (race, gender, age); 7 race categories, 2 gender categories, 9 age categories
metric: attribute accuracy, subgroup gap, KL divergence, MaxSkew

name: SPEC-CPU2017
num_samples: ~50 billion instructions per benchmark (10 ref inputs)
format: CPU benchmark programs (integer: 505.mcf_r, 523.xalancbmk_r, 531.deepsjeng_r, 541.leela_r, 548.exchange2_r, 557.xz_r, 500.perlbench_r, 502.gcc_r; floating-point: 503.bwaves_r, 507.cactuBSSN_r, 508.namd_r, 510.parest_r, 511.povray_r, 519.lbm_r, 521.wrf_r, 526.blender_r, 527.cam4_r, 538.imagick_r, 544.nab_r, 549.fotonik3d_r, 554.roms_r, 520.omnetpp_r, 525.x264_r, 527.mixerr_r)
notes: Standard CPU benchmark suite used for performance evaluation. Used extensively in Concorde paper (arXiv:2503.23076) for training and evaluation. Programs include integer (CINT2017) and floating-point (CFP2017) benchmarks.

name: LIT-PCBA
num_samples: 15 protein targets (LIT: Likely Therapeutic Targets - PubChem PCBA)
format: 15 virtual screening targets for structure-based drug design; evaluation via Vina docking score
metric: Vina docking score (lower is better), ligand efficiency, synthesizability (AiZynth)

name: CrossDocked2020
num_samples: ~22M protein-ligand poses (original); ~100 test pockets for SBDD evaluation
format: Protein-ligand docking dataset with pocket-specific evaluation; used for training pose prediction and testing SBDD methods
metric: Vina docking score, AiZynth success rate, diversity, validity

name: Vina Dock
format: AutoDock Vina docking score as evaluation metric for binding affinity prediction

name: AiZynth
format: AiZynthFinder for synthesis accessibility prediction
metric: Success rate (percentage of molecules with valid synthesis pathway)

name: PoseCheck
format: Evaluates protein-ligand interactions: H-bond acceptors/donors, van der Waals contacts, hydrophobic effects
metric: H-bond counts, hydrophobic contact counts, vdW interaction scores

name: LeanWorkbook
num_samples: 89,221 de-duplicated Lean 4 statements (from 140K original natural language to formal pairs)
format: Formal Lean 4 statements translated from natural language math problems; contains statement-proof pairs for some and statements without proofs for others; used as training data for theorem proving
notes: From Ying et al., 2024 (arXiv:2406.03847). De-duplicated version used in STP paper (2502.00212) has ~89K statements without proofs.

name: Google Analogies
format: Word analogy pairs (e.g., man:woman::king:queen)

name: MEN test set
format: Word pairs with human-rated similarity scores

name: WordSim353
format: Word pairs with human-rated similarity scores

name: Books3
format: text files (books)
access: known to be included in training data of several LLMs (LLaMA, Pythia)
notes: Notorious dataset used in copyright litigation; a 'shadow library' of books

name: W4-17
format: Total atomization energies of 200 diverse molecules computed at CCSDTQ5/CBS level

name: Alexandria Database
format: Crystal structures with DFT-computed energies, forces, stresses, and convex hull distances

name: sAlex25 (Subsampled Alexandria 2025)
format: DFT relaxation trajectories with energies, forces, and stresses along relaxation paths
metric: Used for training universal ML interatomic potentials

name: Matbench Discovery
eval_time: Hours to days depending on model
format: Evaluates MLIP performance on crystal stability prediction and relaxation tasks
metric: MAE, energy accuracy, forces accuracy, Matbench Discovery ranking

name: WBM (Wang-Botti-Marques) Benchmark
num_samples: Chemical substitution dataset from stable/near-stable compounds
format: Crystal structures generated via chemical substitution, evaluated for DFT convex hull distance
metric: MAE (meV/atom) for energy predictions, Ehull accuracy
access: Referenced in paper as Wang-Botti-Marques dataset from Chem. Mater. 29, 5090 (2017)

name: CoIR
format: Code retrieval tasks: text-to-code, code-to-code, code-to-text, hybrid
notes: Comprehensive benchmark for code information retrieval. Includes Apps, CosQA, ST2SQL, CodeSearchNet, StackOverflowQA, CodeFeedback, CodeTransOcean tasks.

name: BRIGHT
format: Reasoning-intensive retrieval across diverse domains requiring minimal lexical overlap
notes: Benchmark for reasoning-intensive retrieval. Includes StackExchange (Bio, Earth, Econ, Psy, Rob, Stack, Sus), LeetCode, Pony, AoPS, TheoremQA tasks.

name: BEIR
format: Heterogeneous benchmark covering multiple domains for general information retrieval
notes: Zero-shot evaluation benchmark for information retrieval. Includes TREC-COVID, NFCorpus, NQ, HotpotQA, FiQA, ArguAna, Webis-Touche2020, DBpedia-entity, MSMARCO, BigBird, Natural Questions, Vintagefindo, Quora.

name: ACID
format: Aerial drone-captured nature scenes for novel view synthesis, camera poses obtained via SfM
access: Referenced in Infinite Nature paper (Liu et al., ICCV 2021)
notes: Used in 3D Gaussian splatting papers for outdoor/nature scene reconstruction. Contains diverse camera motions from aerial drone footage.

name: Cervantes Coronary Angiography
format: Contrast-enhanced X-ray coronary angiograms, 128x128 pixels, with vessel segmentation masks; used for vascular segmentation in OCiC telesurgery paper
metric: Dice similarity coefficient, F1 score, ASD, HD
license: Research use (Cervantes-Sanchez et al., Applied Sciences 2019)

name: COUNTERFACT
format: Counterfactual question-answer pairs with rephrased prompts; target answers initially assigned low probabilities by models
metric: edit success rate, generalization success rate

name: MedEditBench
format: Medical knowledge editing QA pairs covering various medical domains

name: WildJailbreak
format: Dataset of jailbreak attack prompts covering both vanilla (direct harmful queries) and adversarial (deceptive/manipulative) variants. Used for safety alignment training and evaluation.

name: PROOF-BENCH
num_samples: 145 problems (APMO, EGMO, IMO, Putnam, USA TST, USAMO 2022-2025) with 435 LLM-generated solutions (o3, Gemini-2.5-Pro, DeepSeek-R1-0528)
format: Math competition proof problems with reference solutions, problem-specific marking schemes (0-7 point allocations + deductions), LLM-generated proofs, and expert scores on 0-7 scale
metric: MAE vs expert scores, RMSE, Bias, WTA≤1 (within-1-point accuracy), Kendall-τ ranking correlation

name: STAR-200K
num_samples: ~170K traffic-logic pairs (150K training, 20K test) from top-200K Tranco list
storage: ~100-200GB estimated (encrypted traffic packet traces + browser developer logs for logic modality)
format: Dual-modality: encrypted HTTPS traffic traces (packet-level features: direction, HTTP version, flow index) + semantic website logic profiles (resource URI lengths, sizes, protocol versions, MIME types). Each site accessed once via Selenium-controlled Chrome on AWS EC2.
notes: Collected by authors across 10 AWS EC2 instances in North America, Europe, Asia. Used for training STAR dual-encoder cross-modal alignment.

name: H&W-1600
num_samples: 64,000 traffic samples (40 samples x 1,600 websites); popular subset from original H&W dataset covering popular, random, and censorship website groups
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Encrypted HTTPS traffic traces captured from Chrome browser access to 1,600 popular websites. Each sample contains full packet-level traces suitable for website fingerprinting evaluation.
access: Referenced in Cheng et al. 2025 (Holmes & Watson paper, ACM Web Conference 2025)
notes: Public dataset from prior website fingerprinting work (Cheng et al. 2025). Disjoint from STAR-200K training set. Used as evaluation benchmark for closed-world (1,600 classes) and open-world (monitored vs. unmonitored) WF tasks.

name: PhysicsIQ
format: Text/image/video prompts for physics consistency evaluation across I2V, V2V, T2V settings

name: AGIEval
format: Human-centric benchmark with diverse tasks including LSAT, LogiQA, math, English proficiency; multiple-choice and free-response

name: LibriTTS
format: Multi-speaker English speech corpus derived from LibriVox audiobooks; includes speaker IDs, text transcripts, and audio waveforms at 16kHz
notes: Used for training voice conversion models. train-clean-100 (~100h) and train-clean-360 (~360h) subsets used in AdaptVC paper.

name: VCTK
eval_time: minutes to hours for zero-shot VC evaluation
format: Multi-speaker English speech corpus with diverse accents (Oxford University); used for zero-shot voice conversion evaluation with unseen source and target speakers
metric: MOS-N, MOS-S, WER, CER, SECS (when paired with ASR/speaker verification models)
notes: VCTK corpus used in AdaptVC for zero-shot VC evaluation with 20 source and 20 target unseen speakers.

name: KAIST Hyperspectral Dataset
storage: ~5-8GB (30 HSI scenes at 2704x3376 pixels, 31 spectral bands)
format: 31-band hyperspectral images at 2704x3376 spatial resolution covering visible wavelengths; used for spectral compressive imaging evaluation

name: ICVL Hyperspectral Dataset
format: Hyperspectral image cubes captured withSpecim PS Kappa DX4 102f; 31 spectral bands over 400-700nm; used for generalization testing in HSI reconstruction

name: Real CASSI Dataset
format: Real snapshot compressive imaging measurements from coded aperture spectral imaging system; dimensions 660x714x28 (spatial x spatial x spectral), wavelength range 450-650nm, dispersion 54 pixels; from Meng et al. 2020
access: Referenced in Meng, Ma, and Yuan 2020

name: Defects4J
num_samples: 147 bugs across 5 Java projects (Commons-CLI, Commons-CSV, Gson, JFreeChart, Commons-Lang)
eval_time: minutes to hours (per bug, depending on test suite size and coverage measurement)
format: Defective Java projects with known bugs; each bug has a focal class and focal method for test generation, evaluated by line coverage and branch coverage of generated test suites

name: FeTaQA
format: Free-form Table QA dataset with natural language questions over Wikipedia tables; answers are complete sentences requiring table reasoning

name: fastMRI
num_samples: ~1000 subjects (brain MRI), split into 800 train/100 val/100 test; middle 7-9 transverse slices per subject
format: Fully-sampled multi-coil k-space MRI data (T2-weighted brain); coil sensitivity maps estimated via ESPIRiT; supports Cartesian undersampling for CS-MRI evaluation
license: NYU Langon Health fastMRI data use agreement (free for research)

name: EC-40
num_samples: ~120M parallel sentences, 1640 translation directions (41 languages, 80 supervised + 1560 zero-shot)
format: English-centric multilingual parallel corpus with 41 languages across 5 families; 4 resource tiers (High: 5M, Medium: 1M, Low: 100K, Extra Low: 50K sentence pairs per language)
access: Tan and Monz (2023) - introduced in 'Towards a better understanding of variations in zero-shot neural machine translation performance' (EMNLP 2023)
notes: Large-scale zero-shot translation benchmark. Evaluation uses FLORES dev (997 sentences) and devtest (1012 sentences) per language.

name: Wikidata5M
format: Wikidata knowledge graph with language-agnostic entity IDs and multilingual textual information (names, aliases, descriptions) for 10 languages. Transductive split for KGC evaluation.

name: WikiKGE-10++
num_samples: ~25,000 entities across 10 languages (AR, DE, EN, ES, FR, IT, JA, KO, TH, ZH)
format: Manually-curated KGE benchmark with entity names, aliases, and descriptions. Includes head/torso/tail entity popularity tiers. Evaluation via Coverage, Precision (F1), and COMET scores.

name: SynthASpoof
format: Synthetic face PAD dataset generated with StyleGAN2-ADA, filtered through CR-FIQA. Contains print attacks (3.8K subjects printed and recaptured) and replay attacks (75K images from 3 devices)

name: CAMO
format: Camouflaged object images with pixel-level masks; includes animal camouflage and body painting

name: COD10K
format: Camouflaged object images with pixel-level masks covering diverse species and scenes

name: CHAMELEON
format: Camouflaged object test images with pixel-level masks

name: NC4K
format: Large-scale camouflaged object test set with pixel-level masks

name: ISTD
format: Shadow images with shadow/non-shadow mask annotations for shadow detection

name: CASIA-2.0
format: Image tampering detection dataset with manipulated/non-manipulated labels and pixel-level masks

name: CASIA-1.0
format: Image forgery detection test set with tampered/authentic labels and mask annotations

name: Multi30k
num_samples: 31K images (30K train / 1K test), each with 5 German captions
format: Flickr30k images with human-written German captions by native speakers; parallel non-translated data for German image captioning

name: Crossmodal-3600 (XM3600)
format: Flickr30k-derived images with cross-lingual captions for multilingual VL evaluation

name: FlickrStyle
num_samples: 7000 images (6000 train / 1000 test) with humorous and romantic style captions
format: Flickr30k images with stylistically edited captions (humorous and romantic); annotators generated captions based on existing Flickr30k captions

name: DiverseVul
eval_time: hours for full LLM evaluation on test set
format: Source code from 809 projects with CPG (Code Property Graph) representations, CWE labels (150 types), 70-15-15 train-val-test split
notes: Latest vulnerability detection dataset (as of 2024). Used in CGP-Tuning paper (arXiv:2501.04510) for evaluating graph-enhanced soft prompt tuning on code vulnerability detection. Code property graphs generated using Joern v2.0.44.

name: PANORAMA
format: 3D abdominal CT scans with pancreatic tumor (PDAC) annotations for tumor detection and segmentation benchmark
metric: Sensitivity, Specificity, F1-score, Dice Similarity Coefficient

name: PanTS-XL
format: Large-scale abdominal CT dataset with per-voxel annotations for pancreatic tumors (benign/malignant) and 88 anatomical structures. Sourced from 112 hospitals across 13 countries, includes structured and narrative radiology reports
metric: Dice Similarity Coefficient (for segmentation models trained on it)

name: AbdomenAtlas 1.0
format: Abdominal CT dataset with multi-organ annotations created using AI-assisted labeling

name: WORD
format: Whole abdominal organ dataset with 16 organ annotations from MICCAI 2022

name: DIS5K
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model and image resolution
format: High-resolution images with foreground/background segmentation masks for dichotomous image segmentation
metric: Max F-measure (Fβ_max), Weighted F-measure (Fβ_ω), E-measure (E_φ_m), Structural Similarity (S_m), MAE, Dice, IoU, BER, Accuracy
license: Research use (referenced in Qin et al. ECCV 2022)

name: TableVQA
format: Visual question answering on table images; includes VWTQ, VWTQ_syn, and VTabFact subsets

name: CharXiv
format: Expert-annotated VQA on charts from arXiv papers with reasoning questions

name: NExT-QA
format: Multiple-choice video QA for causal and temporal reasoning; questions require understanding temporal actions and causal relationships in videos

name: Env-QA
num_samples: ego-centric videos from virtual environments with QA pairs
format: Video QA benchmark for comprehensive understanding of dynamic environments; ego-centric virtual environment videos with multiple-choice questions about state, event, and order reasoning

name: PG19
format: Book corpus for language modeling evaluation

name: OpenWebText2
eval_time: hours to days for full evaluation
format: Large web text corpus for language modeling

name: Longbench
format: Multi-task benchmark for long context understanding: QA, summarization, few-shot learning, code completion

name: POPQA
format: Open-domain questions with entity-centric answers from Wikipedia

name: MVTecAD
format: High-resolution industrial images with pixel-annotated defects; categories include bottle, cable, carpet, grid, leather, pill, screw, toothbrush, transistor, etc.

name: BTAD
format: Industrial product images with pixel-level defect annotations for unsupervised anomaly detection

name: MTSD
format: Magnetic tile surface defect dataset; images with pixel-annotated defects for surface inspection

name: OpenbookQA
format: 4-choice science fact questions requiring external knowledge from OpenBook QA

name: CALVIN
num_samples: ~100 manipulation tasks with scripted demonstrations (~10k base trajectories, up to +30k extended)
eval_time: varies by task count; 500 random episodes for success rate
format: simulated Franka Panda robot manipulation with multi-view RGB observations, text instructions, openable drawer/chairs/LED tasks
metric: task success rate per task type (Push, Open/Close, Turn on/off)

name: Video-GoBench
num_samples: 10M 9x9 Go game records (3.2M KataGo self-play + 6.8M OGS human games), ~400M unique board states; 1K test matches (56K unique states after removing opening moves)
eval_time: hours (11.2K tournament games for Elo calculation)
format: 9x9 Go game records converted to video frames of board states; evaluation via online gameplay against KataGo
metric: Legal rate (%), Action-value (% vs KataGo-9d oracle), Best action accuracy (%), Tournament Elo rating
license: research use (OGS data CC BY 4.0 for human games)

name: SHIFT
format: Synthetic driving dataset with discrete and continuous splits; provides depth, optical flow, and scene flow annotations

name: MOVi-F
format: Kubric-style synthetic dynamic scenes with forward motion; provides scene flow annotations in relative scale

name: Natural Plan
num_samples: ~2300 (320 val + 1280 test Trip Planning; 500 val + 500 test Meeting Planning)
format: natural language planning queries (trip planning, meeting planning) with constraint satisfaction evaluation

name: StegPoet
format: encode hidden number sequence into poem/essay using cipher; validated by programmatic detector

name: WinoBias
num_samples: Not specified (from Zhao et al. 2018 paper)
format: Coreference resolution templates with gendered pronouns for profession stereotypes; measures Delta-G (gender) and Delta-S (stereotype) bias metrics

name: WinoMT
num_samples: Not specified (from Stanovsky et al. 2019 paper)
format: Winograd-style gender bias evaluation for machine translation; evaluates gender inflection accuracy in translation from gender-neutral English to grammatically gendered languages (German, Czech, Russian, etc.)

name: BUG
format: Naturally occurring gender bias dataset for coreference resolution and machine translation; contains real-world sentences with gender stereotypes

name: ChartCraft
num_samples: hundreds of chart images with edit instructions (exact count not specified in PlotEdit paper)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Chart images paired with natural language editing instructions across 4 categories: style, layout, format, data-centric. Evaluated using SSIM, VAES, and RMS metrics.
access: Introduced in Yan et al. (2024) ChartReformer paper; used as evaluation benchmark in PlotEdit paper (2501.11233)

name: NuScenes
num_samples: 1,000 sequences; 1.4M images, 390k LiDAR scans, 1.4M annotated boxes; 28,310 train / 6,019 val / 6,008 test
eval_time: minutes per model on val set
format: Multi-modal autonomous driving dataset with LiDAR, cameras, radar; 10Hz sensor suite; 3D bounding boxes for 10 classes; evaluated with mAP and NDS (nuScenes Detection Score)
metric: mAP (mean Average Precision) and NDS (nuScenes Detection Score = mAP weighted with translation/scale/rotation/attribute errors)

name: ARC (Aphasia Recovery Cohort)
format: Multi-site 3D T1w, T2w, and FLAIR MRI with stroke lesion segmentations

name: BDD100K
num_samples: ~100k videos (40s each at 30fps), 10 tasks with multi-annotator labels
format: Driving videos with annotations for detection, tracking, segmentation, lane marking, drivable area, road objects, etc.

name: UVG
format: RGB video sequences at 3840x2160 resolution with 50fps and 120fps variants; used for video interpolation, super-resolution, and compression benchmarks

name: Vid4
format: Low-resolution video sequences for video super-resolution evaluation; typically cropped and downsampled for testing

name: Adobe240
format: High-resolution videos (1280x720) captured at 240fps or 120fps with hand-held cameras; used for video frame interpolation and super-resolution

name: CrossTask
format: Instructional videos with step annotations derived from WikiHow; tasks include cooking, car maintenance, crafting, home repairs

name: CPTAC-BRCA
format: Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium breast cancer H&E whole-slide images with matched RNA-Seq gene expression; used as independent validation set for gene expression prediction from WSIs
metric: Pearson correlation between predicted and ground truth gene expression

name: MsigDB CGN (Cancer Gene Neighborhood)
format: Gene-gene co-expression network: undirected unweighted graph where edges connect genes with Pearson correlation > 0.85 in the CGN subcollection of Computational Gene Sets
metric: n/a (used as prior knowledge for training)

name: LeQua T1B (CLEF 2022)
num_samples: 20k individual examples + 1k bags (700 train + 300 val) + 5k test bags
storage: ~100MB (pre-extracted 300-d tabular features from Amazon product reviews, 28 classes)
format: Pre-extracted tabular features (300 numeric features per review) from Amazon product reviews; bags labeled by 28-class prevalence vectors. Task: predict class prevalence in test bags under prior probability shift.
notes: LeQua@CLEF 2022 multiclass quantification task (T1B). Used in arXiv:2501.13638 (GMNet) as primary benchmark.

name: LeQua T2 (CLEF 2024)
num_samples: 20k individual examples + 1k bags (700 train + 300 val) + 5k test bags
storage: ~100MB (pre-extracted 256-d tabular features from Amazon product reviews, 28 classes)
format: Pre-extracted tabular features (256 numeric features per review) from Amazon product reviews; bags labeled by 28-class prevalence vectors. Task: predict class prevalence in test bags under prior probability shift.
notes: LeQua@CLEF 2024 multiclass quantification task (T2). Same as T1B but with 256 features (vs T1B's 300). Used in arXiv:2501.13638 (GMNet) as primary benchmark.

name: LeQua T3 (CLEF)
num_samples: 20k individual examples + 1k bags (700 train + 300 val) + 5k test bags
storage: ~100MB (pre-extracted features from Amazon product reviews, 5 ordinal sentiment classes)
format: Pre-extracted tabular features from Amazon product reviews; bags labeled by 5-class ordinal sentiment (star ratings 1-5) prevalence vectors. Task: ordinal quantification predicting class prevalence with ordered classes under prior probability shift.
notes: LeQua ordinal quantification task (T3). Ordinal structure: 5 star ratings with implicit ordering; mistakes weighted by class distance. Used in arXiv:2501.13638 (GMNet) for ordinal quantification evaluation.

name: ogbg-molpcba
format: Molecular graph classification. Nodes=atoms, edges=chemical bonds. 128 binary activity classification tasks (inactive/active). Scaffold-based split.
notes: Large-scale molecular property prediction benchmark from OGB. Multi-task binary classification on 128 bioactivity targets.

name: ogbg-molmuv
format: Molecular graph classification. Nodes=atoms, edges=chemical bonds. 17 binary classification tasks from PubChem BioAssay (virtual screening). Scaffold-based split.
notes: Molecular property prediction benchmark subset of PubChem BioAssay for virtual screening evaluation.

name: ogbg-molhiv
format: Molecular graph classification. Nodes=atoms, edges=chemical bonds. Binary classification: predict whether molecule inhibits HIV. Scaffold-based split.
notes: Single-task molecular property prediction: HIV infection inhibition.

name: ogbg-moltoxcast
format: Molecular graph classification. Nodes=atoms, edges=chemical bonds. 617 binary toxicity classification tasks. Scaffold-based split.
notes: Large-scale toxicity prediction benchmark with 617 qualitative toxicity measurement tasks.

name: ogbg-moltox21
format: Molecular graph classification. Nodes=atoms, edges=chemical bonds. 12 binary toxicity classification tasks on nuclear receptor and stress response pathways. Scaffold-based split.
notes: Toxicity prediction benchmark on 12 biological targets.

name: ogbg-molbace
format: Molecular graph classification. Nodes=atoms, edges=chemical bonds. Binary classification: predict BACE-1 (beta-secretase 1) inhibition. Scaffold-based split.
notes: Small-scale molecular property prediction: BACE-1 inhibition for Alzheimer's drug discovery.

name: EgoSchema
format: Long-form egocentric video with multiple-choice QA; requires understanding of complex human activities

name: Long Range Arena (LRA)
num_samples: Varies by task (ListOps ~96k, Text ~250k, Retrieval ~50k, Image ~50k, Pathfinder ~40k samples)
format: Multi-task benchmark for long-range sequence modeling: ListOps (mathematical reasoning), Text (sentiment), Retrieval (byte-level), Image (32x32), Pathfinder (maze patterns)

name: Multi-Query Associative Recall (MQAR)
format: Synthetic associative recall task requiring models to memorize key-value pairs and recall values upon seeing keys; tests long-range dependency handling in sequence models
access: Generated per Arora et al. (2024) specification

name: V2X-Seq
format: Vehicle trajectory sequences from infrastructure sensors at signalized intersections; 10s duration sampled at 10Hz (5s history → 5s prediction); includes traffic signal states, V2X communication data
metric: minADE, minFDE, MR, minJointADE, minJointFDE, minJointMR

name: SinD
num_samples: ~7 hours of trajectory data, 13k+ traffic participants
format: Drone-captured trajectory data at signalized intersection in Tianjin, China; 10Hz sampling; includes traffic signal states and semantic annotations; 1.2s observation → 1.2s/1.8s prediction tasks

name: Crafter
eval_time: minutes-hours per experiment (1M step budget typical)
format: 2D pixel-based survival game environment (64x64x3); discrete action space; 22 achievements; sparse reward (+1 per new achievement)
metric: achievement unlock rate, geometric mean score

name: MiniWorld
format: 3D first-person partial-observable environments; procedurally generated mazes/rooms; discrete action space (forward, turn left/right); sparse reward (goal reach)

name: Bongard-OpenWorld
format: Few-shot visual reasoning: 6 positive images, 6 negative images, 1 query image. Each case requires discovering an abstract visual rule from positive/negative examples and applying it to query. Natural images from COCO/Visual Genome.

name: Bongard-HOI
num_samples: ~100 per split (4 standard splits: sosa, soua, uosa, uoua)
format: Few-shot visual reasoning focused on human-object interactions (HOI). Uses natural images withHOI concepts. Same structure as Bongard-OpenWorld but specific to interaction-based rules.

name: Bongard-Logo
format: Few-shot visual reasoning with logo images. Tests concept learning and reasoning with synthetic/structured visual stimuli.

name: Sketchy
num_samples: 12,500 photos from 125 classes, each with at least 5 fine-grained paired sketches
format: Sketch-photo pairs with fine-grained instance-level association. Photos are from 125 classes with multiple instances per class, each paired with sketches depicting specific object instances.

name: Sketchy-Extended
format: Sketchy dataset extended with ImageNet photos. Category-level sketch-photo association where every sketch of a category is associated with all photos of the same category.

name: SketchySegment
num_samples: Test set of Sketchy dataset with manually annotated pixel-level segmentation masks
format: Pixel-level segmentation annotations for Sketchy test images, created by the SketchYourSeg authors for evaluation purposes.

name: CRSP
eval_time: seconds to minutes for panel operations
format: Monthly stock returns, trading volume, shares outstanding, exchange codes for NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ stocks
license: proprietary (CRSP via Wharton Research Data Services)

name: Compustat
eval_time: seconds to minutes for characteristic computation
format: Quarterly/annual firm fundamentals: book value, earnings, sales, assets, liabilities, cash flow, profitability, investment, and 57 other firm characteristics

name: Hybrid-QA
eval_time: minutes per model for 500 dev samples
format: Multi-hop QA over Wikipedia tables + linked text passages. Answers can be In-Table, In-Passage, or Computed.

name: OTT-QA
eval_time: minutes per model for 500 dev samples
format: Open-domain Table-Text QA requiring table and passage retrieval before answering. Mixes in-domain Hybrid-QA questions with out-of-domain questions.

name: BraTS 2023
format: T1/T2/FLAIR/T1Gd brain tumour MRI volumes with segmentation masks
metric: 3D Dice (enhancing tumour, tumour core, whole tumour)

name: Instruct-NeRF2NeRF
num_samples: 3 edited scenes with ~100 input images each
format: Posed RGB images with text editing instructions for 3D scene editing
notes: Dataset for editing 3D scenes with instructions. Used in DYG (Drag Your Gaussian) paper arXiv:2501.18672 for evaluation.

name: SAEBench
num_samples: Varies by metric (SCR, TPP, Sparse Probing, AutoInterp, Absorption)
format: Multi-metric benchmark for SAE evaluation: SCR (spurious correlation removal), TPP (targeted probe perturbation), Sparse Probing, AutoInterp (automated interpretability), Absorption (feature absorption)
metric: Various (SCR score, TPP score, probing accuracy, interpretability score, absorption score)

name: BEIR-SCIDOCS
format: Scientific document similarity task from BEIR benchmark. Given a scientific paper, retrieve other semantically related papers from the corpus.
notes: Used in Riddle Me This (CCS 2025) for evaluating membership inference attacks on RAG systems.

name: Cora
format: Citation network: nodes are papers, edges are citation links. Node features (1433-dim bag-of-words), 7 classes (paper topics). Homophilic graph (homophily ratio H=0.825).

name: Citeseer
format: Citation network: nodes are papers, edges are citation links. Node features (3703-dim bag-of-words), 6 classes (paper topics). Homophilic graph (homophily ratio H=0.718).

name: PubMed
format: Citation network: nodes are papers, edges are citation links. Node features (500-dim TF-IDF), 5 classes (diabetes types). Homophilic graph (homophily ratio H=0.792).

name: Actor
format: Actor co-occurrence network: nodes are actors, edges indicate co-occurrence on Wikipedia pages. Node features (932-dim), 5 classes (actor categories). Highly heterophilic (homophily ratio H=0.215).

name: Texas/Cornell
format: WebKB webpage graphs: nodes are webpages, edges are hyperlinks. Node features (1703-dim), 5 classes (webpage types). Highly heterophilic (Texas H=0.057, Cornell H=0.301).

name: Spider 2.0
storage: Databases accessed via warehouse APIs (Snowflake, BigQuery) - not stored locally
format: Enterprise-scale Text-to-SQL benchmark: large cross-domain databases (150+, up to 800+ columns), multiple SQL dialects (BigQuery, Snowflake, SQLite), complex nested data types, ambiguous queries. Spider 2.0-Snow uses Snowflake dialect; Spider 2.0-Lite uses BigQuery, Snowflake, and SQLite.
access: https://github.com/spider benchmark/Spider (original Spider); Spider 2.0 at arXiv:2411.07763

name: KuaiRec
format: Viewer-video interaction data with watch ratio (play duration / video duration); grouped into K=L=20 subgroups via clustering for experiments in arXiv:2502.01792

name: BBOB (Black-Box Optimization Benchmark)
num_samples: 24 functions (BBOB 2010), plus additional functions in BBOB 2009 and noisy variants
eval_time: seconds to minutes per function per run
format: Synthetic mathematical optimization functions (Sphere, Ellipsoidal, Rastrigin, Rosenbrock, Schwefel, Gallagher peaks, Ackley, Levy, Dixon-Price, Salomon, etc.) with configurable dimensionality and noise

name: Brax Physics Simulator
eval_time: Varies by task (robot locomotion typically seconds per episode)
format: Differentiable physics engine for rigid body simulation. Includes environments: Hopper, Walker2d, Half Cheetah, Ant, Arm reaching. Supports various fitness functions and behavioral descriptors.
metric: Task-specific (forward velocity for locomotion, position accuracy for reaching)

name: Split-CIFAR100 (20 Tasks)
num_samples: 60k images across 100 classes, split into 20 tasks of 5 classes each
format: CIFAR-100 partitioned into 20 sequential class-incremental tasks (5 classes per task) for continual learning
metric: average accuracy (Acc), average anytime accuracy (AAA), worst-case accuracy (WC-Acc), probed accuracy

name: Split-TinyImageNet (20 Tasks)
num_samples: 100k images across 200 classes, split into 20 tasks of 10 classes each
format: Tiny ImageNet partitioned into 20 sequential class-incremental tasks (10 classes per task) for continual learning
metric: average accuracy (Acc), average anytime accuracy (AAA), worst-case accuracy (WC-Acc), probed accuracy

name: Online CLEAR
num_samples: Not specified; real-world ImageNet images with temporal distribution shift across 10 tasks
format: Domain-incremental continual learning benchmark on ImageNet-derived data with 10 tasks; each task introduces temporal distribution shift rather than new classes
metric: average accuracy (Acc), average anytime accuracy (AAA), worst-case accuracy (WC-Acc)

name: MotionFix
num_samples: ~6,730 source-target motion pairs with text descriptions
format: 3D human motion pairs (source and target) in HumanML3D skeleton format, with text editing instructions. Used for text-based and trajectory-based motion editing evaluation.
metric: R-precision (R@1, R@2, R@3), AvgR, Average Error, AITS
notes: First dataset for text-based human motion editing. Introduced in MotionFix (2024). MotionLab (2502.02358) extends it to trajectory-based editing evaluation.

name: lcbench
num_samples: 34 image classification datasets, 2000 configurations each (pre-computed learning curves)
format: Surrogate-based HPO benchmark via YAHPO-Gym. Provides pre-computed validation performance for hyperparameter configurations on image classification tasks (tabular datasets converted via Auto-PyTorch).
notes: Used in HyperSHAP (2502.01276) for explaining hyperparameter importance and interactions.

name: rbv2_ranger
format: Surrogate-based HPO benchmark via YAHPO-Gym for tuning random forest (ranger) hyperparameters.
notes: Used in HyperSHAP (2502.01276) as a random forest benchmark case study.

name: PD1
num_samples: 4 HPO tasks (transformer models, image classification), multiple configurations
format: Surrogate-based HPO benchmark via YAHPO-Gym. Derived from Bayesian optimization runs on realistic deep learning HPO tasks including lm1b transformer scenario.
notes: Used in HyperSHAP (2502.01276) for ablation and tunability analysis.

name: JAHS-Bench-201
num_samples: Surrogate model for NAS + HPO on ImageNet16-120
format: Surrogate-based benchmark for joint architecture and hyperparameter search (NAS + HPO) on NAS-Bench-201 search space with 10 hyperparameters including categorical architecture choices.
notes: Used in HyperSHAP (2502.01276) for demonstrating scalability to 10 hyperparameters.

name: 20NewsGroups
format: Text documents from Usenet newsgroups, organized into 20 categories (top 2 categories used for binary classification in some FL papers)

name: DCLM-baseline
num_samples: ~30B tokens (the subset used in this paper; full dataset is larger)
storage: ~800GB for 30B token subset at 8192 seq len
format: Cleaned web text corpus for autoregressive language model pretraining

name: LIMA
format: High-quality instruction-response pairs for supervised fine-tuning; Less-is-More for Alignment

name: TheoremQA
format: Theorem-driven question answering dataset covering 350+ theorems across Math, EE&CS, Physics, and Finance. Each question requires multi-step reasoning with verifiable answers.
notes: From Chen et al. 2023 (EMNLP). Used as OOD benchmark in long CoT reasoning studies.

name: WebInstruct
format: Web-extracted QA pairs from mathematical web content, deduplicated via MinHash. Used as noisy silver supervision signal for scaling verifiable reward in RL training.
notes: From Yue et al. 2024b (MAmmoTH2). WebInstruct-462k is the deduplicated subset used in demystify-long-cot paper for scaling RL with noisy data.

name: CSQA
num_samples: ~12,100 (train + val + test); paper uses val split with 1,221 questions
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model size
format: Multiple-choice commonsense questions (5 options per question); tests physical and social commonsense knowledge

name: MACO (Multi-Agent Coordination)
num_samples: 4 environments (Gather, Disperse, Pursuit, Hallway); 5-12 agents per environment
eval_time: hours per environment (9-30 hours for DMCG training)
format: Cooperative multi-agent RL environments in Python; episodic tasks requiring coordination
metric: win rate (Gather, Hallway), return (Disperse), prey caught (Pursuit)

name: SMACv2 (StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge v2)
format: StarCraft II multi-agent RL environments with stochasticity and partial observability

name: S3DIS
format: Indoor 3D point clouds with per-point semantic labels (13 classes: ceiling, floor, wall, beam, column, window, door, table, chair, sofa, bookshelf, board, clutter); Area 5 is standard test split, Areas 1-5 for training

name: Gaze360
format: Unconstrained gaze estimation dataset with 3D gaze labels in camera coordinate system; captured in the wild with head-mounted cameras

name: MPIIGaze
format: Person-independent gaze estimation dataset with 2D and 3D gaze labels; collected in daily laptop usage scenarios

name: EVE
format: Video-based eye tracking dataset with 2D screen gaze labels; collected during video watching on desktop computers

name: GazeCapture
format: Mobile device gaze estimation dataset with 2D screen gaze labels; collected using smartphones and tablets

name: OpenLane-V2
num_samples: ~700 scenes (sensor split) with associated 7-view images, HD maps, and topology annotations
format: Lane topology reasoning benchmark with lane centerlines, traffic elements (traffic lights, signs), and topology relationships. Extends Argoverse 2 sensor set with ground-truth annotations for DET_l (lane geometry), DET_t (traffic element detection), TOP_ll (lane-to-lane topology), TOP_lt (lane-to-traffic-element topology). Evaluated via OpenLane-V2 Score (OLS).

name: TL-DR
num_samples: ~90k preference pairs from Stiennon et al. 2020a ( Reddit TL;DR posts with human-written summaries and preference annotations)
format: Reddit posts (prompt) with human-written summaries and pairwise preference labels. Used for summarization alignment via RLHF/DPO/RGTG.
metric: reward score (full-sequence reward model), ROUGE-L, GPT-4 win-rate

name: FanOutQA
format: Complex information-seeking questions requiring aggregating information about multiple entities from several sources; includes human-written decompositions
access: Referenced in paper; dataset not yet widely indexed in registry

name: StrategyQA
format: Open-domain questions requiring implicit reasoning steps; each question includes strategy decomposition and evidence paragraphs

name: OmniBlender
num_samples: 3 synthetic scenes (~25 training + 25 test views per scene)
format: Multi-view 360-degree equirectangular images rendered from Blender synthetic indoor scenes (Classroom CC0, Barbershop CC-BY 4.0, Flat CC-BY 4.0) with ground-truth camera poses and depth maps
notes: Used in SC-OMNIGS (arXiv:2502.04734) for synthetic omnidirectional radiance field evaluation

name: 360Roam
num_samples: 8 real-world multi-room scenes (~110 training + ~37 test views per scene)
eval_time: 30 min per scene for SC-OMNIGS optimization
format: Real-world 360-degree indoor images captured with omnidirectional cameras; SfM camera poses as ground truth; sparse point clouds for initialization
notes: Used in SC-OMNIGS (arXiv:2502.04734) for real-world omnidirectional radiance field evaluation

name: HEHS (Human-crafted Evil Harmful prompts)
format: 40 manually designed toxic prompts that violate VLLM safety policies
access: Released in Qi et al. 2023 (arXiv:2306.13213); used in Multi-Faceted Attack paper (arXiv:2502.05772)
notes: Dataset of 40 harmful prompts used to evaluate jailbreaking attacks on VLLMs. An attack is successful if the model provides a non-refused, harmful response aligned with the toxic prompt. Human evaluators assess harmfulness.

name: StrongREJECT
num_samples: not specified (test set of jailbreak prompts)
format: Toxic prompts for evaluating LLM content moderators
notes: Evaluation benchmark for LLM-based content moderators. Used in Multi-Faceted Attack paper (arXiv:2502.05772) to evaluate adversarial signature attacks on content moderators. More rigorous than HEHS for testing moderator robustness.

name: SKEMPI v2.0
num_samples: 348 protein complexes, 7085 mutation combinations with ΔΔG labels
eval_time: minutes for evaluation of ΔΔG prediction
format: PDB complex structures + mutation lists + experimental binding free energy changes (ΔΔG in kcal/mol)
notes: Standard benchmark for ΔΔG prediction. Core benchmark for this paper. Mutations include single and multi-point; structures are wild-type only (mutant structures must be predicted).

name: SKEMPI-Aug
format: Augmented mutation data generated by Prompt-DDG annotations on SKEMPI v2.0 structures using K-fold cross-augmentation to prevent data leakage
access: Referenced in paper as available on Github: wulirong/Light-DDG
notes: Authors' released augmented dataset for supervised pre-training. Two orders of magnitude larger than original SKEMPI v2.0. Generated via K-fold cross-augmentation to prevent leakage between training and annotation.

name: SAbDab
format: Structural Antibody Database: PDB structures of antibody-antigen complexes with annotations
notes: Used in this paper for antibody optimization evaluation (500 CDR-H3 optimization cases). The paper uses SAbDab structures to evaluate Uni-Anti on diverse antibody-antigen complexes.

name: TRACE
num_samples: 8 domains, multiple datasets per domain (C-STANCE, FOMC, MeetingBank, Py150, ScienceQA, NumGLUE-cm, NumGLUE-ds, 20Minuten)
format: Continual instruction tuning benchmark for LLMs across 8 sequential domains: classification (C-STANCE, FOMC, 20Minuten), summarization (MeetingBank), code generation (Py150), VQA (ScienceQA), numerical reasoning (NumGLUE-cm, NumGLUE-ds)
license: Varies by constituent dataset (CC BY-NC 4.0, MIT, etc.)
notes: Continual instruction tuning benchmark from arXiv:2310.06762. Used in arXiv:2502.07274 (Forget Remembering) for evaluating LLM continual learning across 8 sequential domains with varying exemplar memory sizes (20%-80%).

name: TOFU
num_samples: 200 fictitious author profiles, 20 QAs each = ~4000 QA pairs
format: Question-answer pairs about fictitious authors; used for instance-level unlearning evaluation. Metrics: ROUGE1, MRR, Deviation Score.
metric: ROUGE1 (forget lower, retain higher), Deviation Score, Control Score
notes: Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs. Synthetic dataset with fictitious author profiles generated by GPT-4. Standard unlearning benchmark for evaluating knowledge removal at instance level.

name: PISTOL
num_samples: 20 contractual relationships, 20 QA pairs each = ~400 QA pairs
format: Synthetic contractual QA pairs with fictitious entity names/addresses generated from random knowledge graphs. Concise ground truth answers. Metrics: ROUGE1, MRR, Deviation Score.
metric: ROUGE1 (forget lower, retain higher), Deviation Score, Control Score
notes: Pipeline for Instance-level Structural T5 unlearning. Synthetic dataset derived from random knowledge graphs for studying fine-grained, instance-level LLM unlearning. Unlike TOFU, PISTOL has concise ground truth making evaluation more consistent.

name: QVHighlights
format: Online videos (vlogs, news) with sentence queries, moment annotations, and saliency scores for highlight detection

name: Dollar Street
format: Household item images from diverse countries; used for geo-localization and cultural diversity evaluation of vision-language models

name: GeoDE
num_samples: ~62K manually annotated images from diverse geographic locations
format: Manually annotated images from diverse geographic locations; used for zero-shot geographic localization evaluation

name: Google Landmarks Dataset v2 (GLDv2)
format: Large-scale landmark recognition dataset; images with landmark and geographic annotations

name: Fairface
format: Face images with gender, race, and age annotations for fairness evaluation

name: PCQM4Mv2
num_samples: 3.4M organic molecules with one equilibrium conformation each
format: 3D molecular structures with HOMO-LUMO gap labels
notes: PubChemQC project: large-scale first-principles electronic structure database. Widely used for molecular property prediction pre-training. Used in EMPP paper for self-supervised pre-training before fine-tuning on QM9/MD17.

name: GEOM-Drug
num_samples: ~200k training molecules + 10k validation (diverse conformations per molecule)
format: 3D molecular conformations with energy labels (equilibrium and non-equilibrium)
notes: GEOM dataset of energy-annotated molecular conformations for drug-like molecules. Contains both equilibrium and non-equilibrium conformations. Used in EMPP paper to validate effectiveness on diverse molecular data beyond QM9/MD17.

name: VAERS (Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System)
num_samples: Thousands of vaccine adverse event reports (paper filters for COVID-19 vaccine myocarditis reports)
eval_time: seconds to minutes for sequential test processing
format: Tabular data: report ID, date, demographic info (age, sex), vaccine type, adverse event keywords, outcome
metric: n/a (data source for sequential hypothesis test)

name: HMDA (Home Mortgage Disclosure Act) 2019
num_samples: ~183k loan applicants (after filtering for conventional loans, positive income)
eval_time: seconds to minutes for sequential test processing
format: Tabular data: applicant demographics (race, sex, age), loan amount, income, debt-to-income ratio, loan outcome (approved/denied)
metric: n/a (data source for sequential hypothesis test)

name: VaxView (CDC Vaccination Coverage)
num_samples: Vaccination rates by demographic (age, sex, ethnicity) at population level
format: Tabular data: vaccination rates disaggregated by age bucket, sex, and ethnicity. Used to compute base rates mu_G^0 for subgroups.
metric: n/a (reference data for base rate computation)

name: Market1501
format: Person re-identification images from 6 cameras with ID labels

name: DukeMTMC-reID
format: Person re-identification images from 8 cameras with ID labels

name: MSMT17
format: Person re-identification images from 15 cameras with ID labels (most challenging dataset)

name: CUHK03-NP
format: Person re-identification images from 2 cameras with ID labels

name: derm7pt
num_samples: 1,011 skin lesion images (clinical + dermoscopic views) with 7-point checklist annotations and lesion classification
format: Dermatology benchmark with skin lesion images (clinical and dermoscopic), clinical metadata, 7 visual attributes (pigment network, blue-whitish veil, vascular structures, pigmentation, streaks, dots/globules, regression structures), and 5-class lesion diagnosis (nevus, seborrheic keratosis, melanoma, basal cell carcinoma, miscellaneous)
access: https://derm7pt.herokuapp.com (referenced in Kawahara et al., JBHI 2019)

name: ADReSSo 2021 Challenge
num_samples: 237 patients total (166 training: 79 CN + 87 AD; 71 independent test)
format: Audio recordings of picture-description task (Cookie Theft picture); speech samples analyzed for acoustic and linguistic biomarkers of Alzheimer's Disease

name: NPLIB1 (CANOPUS)
format: LC-MS/MS spectra with molecular formulas and structures
access: https://gnps-external.ucsd.edu/ or original NPLIB1 publication (Dührkop et al., 2021)

name: MassSpecGym
format: LC-MS/MS spectra from various sources with ground truth molecules

name: DSSTox
format: Molecular structures with CAS registry numbers and toxicity data

name: HMDB
format: Human metabolites with structures, biofluid locations, disease associations

name: COCONUT
format: Natural product molecules with structures and taxonomy

name: GOOD
format: graph structured data (molecular, synthetic)
notes: Graph Out-of-Distribution benchmark. Sub-datasets: GOOD-HIV (molecular, HIV inhibition), GOOD-CMNIST (digit graphs from MNIST), GOOD-Motif (synthetic motif classification), GOOD-PCBA (128 bioassays). Distribution splits: scaffold size, basis size, color.

name: DrugOOD
format: molecular graphs
notes: Drug OOD benchmark for AI-aided drug discovery. Sub-datasets: IC50 and EC50 measurements with distribution shifts from assay, scaffold, and size splits.

name: KernelBench
num_samples: 250 tasks (100 Level-1 single operations, 100 Level-2 operator sequences, 50 Level-3 full architectures)
storage: <1GB (task definitions are self-contained PyTorch model code with random input generators)
eval_time: 1-4 hours per model on 1x NVIDIA L40S (250 tasks × iterative refinement multiplies this)
format: PyTorch nn.Module subclasses with forward() methods; LM outputs ModelNew with custom CUDA kernels via torch.utils.cpp_extension.load_inline; evaluated on correctness (5 random inputs) and performance (100 timing trials)
metric: fast_p: percentage of kernels that are functionally correct AND p-times faster than PyTorch Eager baseline; also correctness rate, speedup distribution
access: https://github.com/kernelbench (inferred from kernelbench.github.io mentioned in paper)
notes: Benchmark for evaluating LLMs' ability to write efficient GPU kernels for PyTorch ML workloads. Tasks range from single operations (matmul, conv) to full architectures (AlexNet, MiniGPT). Evaluated models: GPT-4o, OpenAI o1, DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-R1, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Llama 3.1. Key finding: frontier models match PyTorch baseline in <20% of cases. Paper: arXiv:2502.10517, Stanford University.

name: ZINC (Benchmarking GNNs subset)
num_samples: 12,000 molecular graphs (10k train / 1k val / 1k test splits)
format: Molecular graphs with atoms as nodes and bonds as edges. 9 atom types, 3 bond types. Predicting constrained solubility (MAE metric).
notes: Subset of ZINC database used in Benchmarking GNNs paper (Dwivedi et al., 2023). Standard graph regression benchmark. Used in SPSE paper (arXiv:2502.09365) to evaluate molecular property prediction.

name: Peptides-functional (LRGB)
format: Peptide graphs where nodes are atoms and edges are bonds. Task: predict 18 functional properties simultaneously (multi-label classification). Average 150.9 nodes, 307.3 edges per graph.
notes: Long-Range Graph Benchmark (Dwivedi et al., 2022). Evaluates models on long-range dependencies in molecular graphs. Used in SPSE paper (arXiv:2502.09365) to test structural encoding improvements.

name: Peptides-structural (LRGB)
format: Peptide graphs where nodes are atoms and edges are bonds. Task: predict 10 structural properties (multi-label regression). Average 150.9 nodes, 307.3 edges per graph.
notes: Long-Range Graph Benchmark (Dwivedi et al., 2022). Structural property prediction task on peptide graphs. Used in SPSE paper (arXiv:2502.09365).

name: PATTERN (SBM benchmark)
num_samples: 14,000 stochastic block model graphs (1.2M nodes total)
format: Dense graphs generated from stochastic block models. Node features from spectral embeddings. Task: node clustering/classification. Average 118.9 nodes, 3039.3 edges per graph.
notes: From Benchmarking GNNs paper (Dwivedi et al., 2023). Tests ability to capture long-range patterns in dense graphs. Used in SPSE paper (arXiv:2502.09365).

name: CLUSTER (SBM benchmark)
format: Dense graphs generated from stochastic block models with community structure. Node features from spectral embeddings. Task: community detection. Average 117.2 nodes, 2150.9 edges per graph.
notes: From Benchmarking GNNs paper (Dwivedi et al., 2023). Tests structural pattern recognition in dense graphs. Used in SPSE paper (arXiv:2502.09365). SPSE shows limited improvement on this dataset due to high graph density.

name: MNIST-superpixel (Benchmarking GNNs)
num_samples: 60,000 digit images converted to superpixel graphs
format: MNIST images segmented into superpixels (SLIC). Each superpixel is a node with spatial coordinates and color features. Edges between adjacent superpixels. Task: 10-class digit classification.
notes: MNIST images converted to graph format using superpixel segmentation for graph neural network benchmarking. From Benchmarking GNNs paper (Dwivedi et al., 2023). Used in SPSE paper (arXiv:2502.09365).

name: CIFAR10-superpixel (Benchmarking GNNs)
format: CIFAR10 images segmented into superpixels (SLIC). Each superpixel is a node with spatial coordinates and RGB features. Edges between adjacent superpixels. Task: 10-class image classification.
notes: CIFAR10 images converted to graph format using superpixel segmentation for graph neural network benchmarking. From Benchmarking GNNs paper (Dwivedi et al., 2023). Used in SPSE paper (arXiv:2502.09365).

name: PrOntoQA
num_samples: ~7,000 QA pairs across 80 question types (from paper: 80 types)
format: Synthetic QA dataset with chain-of-thought reasoning chains; questions require multi-step logical deduction over structured knowledge bases (ontologies)

name: PandaLM Test Set
num_samples: 170 instructions from human evaluation dataset of self-instruct
format: Pairwise comparison prompts evaluated by LLM evaluators

name: Olympic 2024
num_samples: 220 instances (50 instructions across 5 categories: writing, math, extraction, reasoning, roleplay)
format: Pairwise comparison with response confidence as auxiliary input, human annotated by 3 PhD-level evaluators

name: M4 (Multi-generator, Multi-domain, Multi-lingual Machine-Generated Text Detection)
num_samples: ~12,000 English text pairs (3,000 pairs per domain x 4 domains x 3 generators), split 2,000/500/500 per combination
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on detector complexity
format: Pairs of human-written and LLM-generated texts from Wikipedia, Reddit, WikiHow, arXiv; generated by ChatGPT, GPT-4, Dolly-v2

name: AIGCDetect
num_samples: ~151,500 images generated by 17 different generative models
format: AI-generated images from diverse generative models (GANs, diffusion models, text-to-image systems) plus real images. Includes outputs from commercial APIs like Midjourney, covering varied resolutions and source datasets (LSUN, ImageNet, COCO).

name: HM3D
num_samples: 800 training + 61 MP3D training + 11 MP3D validation scenes (used in NavRAG paper)
format: Indoor 3D environment scans from Habitat-Matterport 3D dataset; panoramic RGB-D observations; navigation graphs with connectivity

name: NavRAG
num_samples: 861 scenes, 2,115,019 navigation instructions (from paper: NavRAG: Generating User Demand Instructions for Embodied Navigation through Retrieval-Augmented LLM, arXiv:2502.11142)
format: Synthetic user-style navigation instructions generated via GPT-4o-mini RAG pipeline; paired with navigation trajectories in HM3D/MP3D environments; hierarchical scene description trees

name: BigCodeBench
format: Python function completions (Complete) and NL instructions (Instruct) with unit tests
notes: BigCodeBench-Complete: code completion from structured docstrings. BigCodeBench-Instruct: code generation from NL instructions. BigCodeBench-Hard is a harder subset requiring complex API composition. From arxiv:2406.15877.

name: APPS+
format: Sanitized version of APPS with removed wrong descriptions or test cases. Programming problems with IO examples, solutions, and tests.
notes: APPS+ introduced in StepCoder paper (arXiv:2402.01391). Used in GiFT paper (2502.11466) with Introductory and Interview difficulty splits.

name: MBPP+
num_samples: 974 (MBPP-sanitized for train, MBPP+ for test with more test cases)
format: Extended version of MBPP with more comprehensive test cases for each problem. Natural language prompt with reference Python solution and unit tests.
notes: MBPP+ introduced in Liu et al. 2024. More comprehensive test cases than original MBPP. Used in GiFT paper (2502.11466) for evaluation.

name: CodeInsight
format: Curated dataset of practical coding solutions from StackOverflow focusing on standard library usage. Natural language descriptions with Python code solutions and test cases.
notes: CodeInsight introduced in Beau and Crabbé 2024. Used in GiFT paper (2502.11466) as one of the evaluation benchmarks.

name: Vibe-Eval
format: Visual question answering benchmark with human expert reference answers; evaluates multimodal LMs on image-based prompts requiring visual commonsense reasoning
metric: Spearman correlation with human ratings (1-5 scale pairwise comparisons)
notes: Vibe-Eval from Padlewski et al. 2024. Used in arXiv:2502.10961 (Privileged Information for LLM grading) to evaluate grader performance with multimodal annotations as privileged information.

name: MathOdyssey
format: Olympiad-level math competition problems (open-ended and multiple-choice) with human expert reference solutions; particularly challenging for frontier models (GPT-4 Turbo achieves ~10% accuracy)
notes: MathOdyssey from Fang et al. 2024. MathOdyssey-Olympiad subset used in arXiv:2502.10961 to evaluate LLM grading correlation with expert human raters on frontier-level math reasoning.

name: PALM Dataset (Pathologic Myopia Recognition)
num_samples: 1200 fundus images with binary labels for pathologic myopia
format: Color fundus photographs with binary labels for pathologic myopia and anatomical structure annotations
notes: Used in Fundus2Globe (arXiv:2502.13182) for external validation of 3D eye globe generation from fundus images.

name: VATEX
format: Short videos (~10s) with multilingual human captions; 8 English captions per video

name: CoDa
format: Human-annotated color distributions for commonly recognized objects. Each object has 11 candidate color attributes with human preference scores. Used for attribute value ranking tasks in commonsense plausibility estimation.
metric: Spearman rank correlation, Binary comparison accuracy
notes: Color Dataset (CoDa) from Paik et al. 2021 (EMNLP). Used in ComPaSS paper (arXiv:2502.13464) for attribute value ranking. CoDa tests whether models can rank object colors by plausibility (e.g., penguin → black > green).

name: ViComTe
storage: Depends on Visual Genome image access (~1GB+)
format: Visual commonsense tests derived from Visual Genome dataset. Covers attribute value ranking across three property types: color (12 candidates), shape (12 candidates), material (18 candidates). Tests alignment with human visual common sense.
metric: Spearman rank correlation, Binary comparison accuracy
notes: Visual Commonsense Tests (ViComTe) from Zhang et al. 2022 (NAACL). Used in ComPaSS paper (arXiv:2502.13464) for attribute value ranking across color, shape, and material properties. Derived from Visual Genome (Krishna et al. 2017).

name: Commonsense Frame Completion (CFC)
num_samples: 55 questions (validation set used for zero-shot evaluation)
format: Free-form question-answer pairs with multiple plausible answers and human-annotated preference scores. Tests implicit commonsense reasoning and probabilistic alignment with human preferences.
notes: Commonsense Frame Completion from Cheng et al. 2024 (ACL). Used in ComPaSS paper (arXiv:2502.13464). Test set is not public; validation set (55 questions) is used for zero-shot evaluation. Tests whether models can rank plausible completions for open-ended prompts.

name: MM-SafetyBench
format: Multimodal safety evaluation with SD image, TYPO, and SD+TYPO attacks; 13 scenarios including illegal activity, hate speech, malware, physical harm, fraud, sexual violence, privacy violations
notes: Liu et al. 2024c. Foundation for VA-SafetyBench video/audio extensions.

name: VA-SafetyBench
num_samples: ~8,000 video-text and audio-text pairs across 8 harm categories
format: Video (DM, TYPO, DM+TYPO) and audio (Audio-only, KPT, KPT+noise) safety benchmark; 8 scenarios from MM-SafetyBench
notes: SEA arXiv:2502.12562. Extends MM-SafetyBench to video/audio MLLMs.

name: SafeRLHF
format: Safety-aligned preference dataset with chosen/rejected responses and harmlessness/helpfulness scores
notes: Ji et al. 2024a. Training dataset for SEA (sampled 3k: 2k harmful + 1k harmless).

name: US Weather
format: Hourly weather data for US cities with 12 meteorological features

name: BabyLM 10M
num_samples: ~10M words (child-directed speech from Kiddie Tales, Charlotte utterson, Child-directed speech corpora)
format: Plain text, developmentally plausible small corpus for language model training

name: BLiMP
num_samples: ~67 minimal pairs per phenomenon, 12 phenomena (agreement, binding, control, determiner, ellipsis, focus, island, licensing, mood, negation, quantification, scalar implicature)
format: Minimal pairs (grammatical vs ungrammatical sentence pairs)

name: Wuggy
format: Multilingual pseudoword generator creating minimal pairs with real words

name: OpenSubtitles
format: Movie and TV subtitles in multiple languages with timestamps

name: CELEX
num_samples: ~50k words with phonological, morphological, frequency information
format: Lexical database with word frequency scores, phonological codes, morphology

name: MetaQA
format: Multi-hop question answering over movie knowledge graph; requires 1-hop, 2-hop, or 3-hop reasoning

name: FactKG
format: Fact verification via reasoning on knowledge graphs (DBpedia); includes one-hop, conjunction, existence, multi-hop, and negation reasoning types

name: CRONQUESTIONS
format: Temporal question answering over Wikidata knowledge graph with quintuple format [head, relation, tail, start_time, end_time]; includes simple time, simple entity, before/after, first/last, and time join reasoning

name: HH-RLHF
format: Helpful and harmless RLHF dataset with pairwise preference annotations; includes Helpfulness and Red-Team subsets

name: ToxicChat
num_samples: 2853 real user queries from LMSys platform
format: User queries with binary toxicity annotations (7.33% toxic); toxic intention categories include racism, self-harm, etc.

name: Dxy
num_samples: 529 real patient-doctor conversations from DingXiangYuan platform
format: Patient-doctor dialogues with disease diagnosis labels; targeted diseases include Pneumonia and Upper Respiratory Tract Infection (sharing similar symptoms)

name: ∞Bench
num_samples: ~4K test samples with context length beyond 100K tokens
format: Long-context benchmark with tasks including summarization (En.Sum), long-book QA (En.QA), multi-choice QA (En.MC)
notes: From Zhang et al. ACL 2024. Used in LongPO paper (2502.13922) as main long-context evaluation benchmark.

name: Long-Data-Collection
num_samples: Book and ArXiv subsets with long documents
format: Long document corpus from books and arXiv papers used for long-context training
notes: Used in LongPO paper (2502.13922) to construct short-to-long preference data by sampling documents and creating instruction-response pairs.

name: Amazon Beauty Reviews (5-core, Sequential Rec)
format: User-item interaction sequences; 5-core filtering ensures >=5 interactions per user/item

name: Amazon Sports and Outdoors Reviews (5-core, Sequential Rec)
format: User-item interaction sequences; 5-core filtering ensures >=5 interactions per user/item

name: Amazon Musical Instruments Reviews (5-core, Sequential Rec)
format: User-item interaction sequences; 5-core filtering ensures >=5 interactions per user/item

name: SNLI (Stanford Natural Language Inference)
format: Premise-hypothesis pairs labeled entailment, contradiction, or neutral

name: InfographicVQA
format: Infographic images with question-answer pairs requiring reasoning over text, layout, and visual elements

name: ScreenQA
format: Screenshot images from mobile, desktop, and web UIs with text-rich QA pairs

name: NutritionQA
format: Photos of nutrition labels with questions about serving size, daily value percentages, and ingredient analysis; includes multi-hop reasoning questions
access: Introduced in CoSyn paper (arXiv:2502.14846); not independently released

name: DocPointQA
format: Document images with pointing questions requiring coordinate prediction for specific elements; derived from DocVQA validation set
metric: F1 score, precision, recall, L2 distance
access: Introduced in CoSyn paper (arXiv:2502.14846); not independently released

name: CoSyn-400K
format: Synthetic text-rich image dataset across 9 categories (charts, documents, math, tables, diagrams, vector graphics, music sheets, electrical circuits, chemical structures); generated via code-guided LLM pipeline

name: WikiText2
format: Text generation; perplexity evaluation on Wikipedia articles

name: MMIR (Multimodal Inconsistency Reasoning)
eval_time: hours (8 models x 534 samples x 2 settings)
format: Artifacts (webpages, slides, posters) with synthetically injected semantic inconsistencies; evaluated in open-ended and multiple-choice settings
metric: accuracy (regex match for MCQ; o1-mini judge for open-ended)
license: Not released (no official code/data release found)
notes: First benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on detecting semantic mismatches across modalities. 5 error categories: Factual Contradiction, Identity Misattribution, Contextual Mismatch, Quantitative Discrepancy, Temporal/Spatial Incoherence. Source artifacts from VisualWebArena (349 webpages) and Zenodo (172 presentations).

name: City Facts
num_samples: Country-capital pairs translated into multiple languages (English, German, Dutch, French)
format: Structured facts: 'The capital of [Country] is [City]' in multiple languages. Used for cross-lingual fact localization experiments.
notes: Used in arXiv:2502.15603 to study how facts are encoded across languages in multilingual LLMs.

name: LLM-Insight
num_samples: 72 target words × 10 prompts × 10 sentences × 5 languages (English, Dutch, French, German, Mandarin) = 72,000 samples
format: Custom dataset with: (1) 72 target words with word forms across 5 languages, (2) 10 open-ended prompts per word that can be completed with multiple semantically distinct words, (3) 10 sentences per word in each language. Designed for steering vector computation and logit lens evaluation.
notes: Created by the authors of arXiv:2502.15603 for studying English-centric routing in multilingual LLMs. Promised for release alongside the paper.

name: InductionBench
eval_time: minutes to hours (depending on model and infrastructure)
format: Synthetic string-to-string transformation tasks from subregular function classes (ISL, L-OSL, R-OSL); model receives input-output examples and must infer minimal rule set
notes: From Hua et al., 2025 (arXiv:2502.15823). Evaluates inductive reasoning: inferring underlying rules from observed input-output pairs. Grounded in subregular hierarchy from formal language theory. Tasks are synthetically generated from controlled parameters (k, alphabet size, rule count). Even o3-mini achieves only ~10% compatibility on hard settings.

name: MetalNet2
num_samples: 4,449 protein chains (training: ~18,230 binding residues; test: 1,981 binding residues)
format: Protein chains with CHED residue labels, co-evolved residue graphs, MSA files
metric: F1 score, Precision, Recall (for metal-binding prediction and metal-type classification across 11 metal types)
access: https://github.com/ZhangFangyi/MetalNet2 (original); code+data also released in MBGNN repo (2502.16189)
notes: Benchmark dataset for metal-binding residue prediction and metal-type classification. Contains 11 metal types (Zn, Ca, Mg, Mn, Fe, SF4, Ni, Cu, Co, FeS, Fe3S). Used as primary benchmark in MBGNN (2502.16189) and prior work MetalNet2.

name: MIonSite
format: Protein sequences with CHED residue ground-truth annotations for Zn, Mg, Ca, Mn
metric: F1 score, Precision, Recall (for metal-binding prediction across 4 metal types)
access: Available from original MIonSite publication; filtered to remove overlap with MetalNet2 in MBGNN evaluation
notes: Independent benchmark dataset for metal-binding site prediction. Used in MBGNN (2502.16189) to evaluate generalization performance of MBGNN and baseline methods. Contains ground-truth annotations for 4 metal types (Zn, Mg, Ca, Mn).

name: Machiavelli
format: Text-based adventure games with annotated harm categories; evaluates trade-offs between rewards and ethical behavior
metric: Harm rate across multiple harm categories
notes: Benchmark for measuring trade-offs between rewards and ethical behavior in LLMs. Used in emergent-misalignment paper (arXiv:2502.17424) to evaluate misalignment of models fine-tuned on insecure code. Measures harm-related behaviors in annotated text-based adventure games.

name: LR2Bench
format: Text-formatted Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSPs): Crossword, Acrostic, Logic Puzzle, Cryptogram, Sudoku, Drop Quote
metric: Exact Match (EM), Subtask Accuracy (S-Acc), Completion Ratio (CR), Partial Match (PM-0.5)

name: Tweet Emotions (SemEval-2018 Task 1)
format: Tweets labeled with 8 emotions (anger, joy, sadness, fear, surprise, anticipation, trust, disgust)

name: Rotten Tomatoes
format: Movie reviews labeled with binary sentiment (positive/negative)
