name: Sentence Polarity
format: Movie review sentences labeled with binary sentiment (positive/negative)

name: HumanEval+
format: Python function completions with test cases
notes: Augmented version of HumanEval with re-generated test cases for more rigorous evaluation. Used in Liu et al. 2023 for evaluating LLM code generation.

name: HumanEvalPack
format: Code completion for Python, C++, and Java with test cases
notes: Multi-language benchmark extending HumanEval to C++ and Java. From Muennighoff et al. 2024 (Octopack).

name: V2XSet
num_samples: 11,447 LiDAR frames (2-5 connected agents) across 73 scenes; 6,694 train / 1,920 val / 2,833 test
format: LiDAR point clouds with 3D bounding box annotations for V2X cooperative perception; co-simulated by CARLA and OpenCDA
notes: V2XSet is a cooperative perception dataset for vehicle-to-everything communication. Used in CoopDETR (arXiv:2502.19313) for evaluating multi-agent 3D detection.

name: FICO Credit Risk
format: Credit risk attributes with binary default labels, used in Explainable ML Challenge

name: BBBC022
format: Multi-channel cell painting images (5 channels: DNA, ER, RNA, AGP, Mito) at 448x448 or similar resolution, with treatment labels and MoA annotations
metric: FoE (Folds of Enrichment), MAP (Mean Average Precision), Recall@K, IMAD

name: CDRP-BIO-BBBC036
format: Multi-channel cell painting images from compound treatments, with treatment labels
metric: FoE (Folds of Enrichment), MAP (Mean Average Precision), Recall@K

name: TAORF-BBBC037
format: Multi-channel cell painting images from gene overexpression perturbations, with pathway annotations
metric: FoE (Folds of Enrichment), MAP (Mean Average Precision), Recall@K

name: cpg0019
num_samples: ~8.42 million single-cell cropped images from cell painting assays
format: Segmented single-cell images from 5 cell painting datasets (BBBC022, CDRP-BIO-BBBC036, TAORF-BBBC037, LUAD-BBBC043, LINCS), with 450 treatments and CellProfiler morphology profiles
metric: Used as regression targets and for contrastive learning in phenotypic profiling

name: LUAD-BBBC043
num_samples: Multi-channel cell painting images from lung cancer cell lines
format: Multi-channel cell painting images for gene overexpression perturbations in LUAD cells
metric: Used as auxiliary data for non-end-to-end training in phenotypic profiling
access: Part of cellpainting-gallery on AWS S3

name: LINCS
num_samples: Multi-channel cell painting images from LINCS project
format: Multi-channel cell painting images for compound treatments across multiple cell lines
metric: Used as auxiliary data for non-end-to-end training in phenotypic profiling
access: Part of cellpainting-gallery on AWS S3

name: MIMIC-IV-ECG
format: 12-lead ECG waveforms (10s, 500Hz) paired with machine-generated ECG reports
notes: Pretraining dataset for SuPreME (arXiv:2502.19668). 800,035 samples from 161,352 patients. Each sample has 18 machine-generated reports and corresponding 12-lead ECG data.

name: PTB-XL
format: 12-lead ECG (10s, 500Hz) with SCP-ECG diagnostic labels at multiple levels (superclass, subclass, form, rhythm)
notes: Downstream evaluation dataset for SuPreME (arXiv:2502.19668). 71 different SCP-ECG compliant ECG reports covering diagnostic, form and rhythm annotations.

name: CPSC-2018
format: 12-lead ECG (6-60s, 500Hz) from 9 hospitals, 9 diagnostic labels
notes: China Physiological Signal Challenge 2018 dataset. Downstream evaluation dataset for SuPreME (arXiv:2502.19668). 1 normal + 8 abnormal types.

name: Chapman-Shaoxing-Ningbo
format: 12-lead ECG (10s, 500Hz) from Chapman University and Chinese hospitals, 38 diagnostic labels
notes: Downstream evaluation dataset for SuPreME (arXiv:2502.19668). Created with support from Chapman University, Shaoxing People's Hospital and Ningbo First Hospital.

name: H2O
format: RGB videos of first-person hand interactions with 3D hand poses, 6D object poses, object types, and interaction class labels
metric: Mean End-Point Error (MPJE) for pose, Top-1 accuracy for interaction recognition

name: FPHA
format: First-person RGB-D hand action videos with 3D hand pose annotations, 6D object poses, and action labels

name: CIFAR10-C
num_samples: 10000 images per corruption (15 corruptions, 5 severity levels = 750k total)
format: 32x32 corrupted RGB images derived from CIFAR-10 test set; 15 corruption types at 5 severity levels each
notes: Corruption robustness benchmark (Hendrycks & Dietterich, ICLR 2019). Corruption types: Gaussian/shot/impulse noise, defocus/glass/motion/zoom blur, snow/frost/fog/brightness/contrast/elastic transform, pixelate/JPEG compression. FoCTTA (arXiv:2502.20677) uses severity level 5 only.

name: CIFAR100-C
num_samples: 10000 images per corruption (15 corruptions, 5 severity levels = 750k total)
format: 32x32 corrupted RGB images derived from CIFAR-100 test set; 15 corruption types at 5 severity levels each
notes: Corruption robustness benchmark (Hendrycks & Dietterich, ICLR 2019). Same 15 corruption types as CIFAR10-C. FoCTTA (arXiv:2502.20677) uses severity level 5 only.

name: DexGraspNet
num_samples: ~1000+ robotic dexterous grasp configurations across diverse objects
format: 3D object meshes with annotated grasp poses for dexterous manipulation
metric: grasp success rate / grasp quality metrics

name: MusicCaps
format: 10-second music clips with text captions (genre, mood, tempo, instrumentation) from expert musicians
notes: Music generation benchmark from Google (Agostinelli et al. 2023). Each sample has a free-text caption and list of music aspects from expert musicians.

name: Song Describer
format: Permissively licensed music recordings with text captions for music-language evaluation
notes: Music captioning and text-to-music generation benchmark (Manco et al. 2023). Evaluates models on music captioning, text-to-music generation, and music-language retrieval tasks.

name: Yelp (GraphSAGE)
format: User-business graph from Yelp. Nodes: users and businesses. Edges: user reviews/ratings. Node features (300-dim), multi-label classification (business categories). Large-scale heterophilic graph.
access: GraphSAGE paper (Hamilton et al., NeurIPS 2017), torch-geometric.datasets.Yelp
notes: Standard large-scale inductive GNN benchmark. Train/test split by time. Used in AMPLE (arXiv:2502.21196) for evaluating large-graph GNN acceleration.

name: HART (Hierarchical AI Risk in Text)
num_samples: 32K test + 32K dev across 4 domains x 4 types x 5 languages
format: AI-generated text detection dataset with 4 types (human-only, human-polished, AI-content, AI-only) across Student Essays, ArXiv Intros, Creative Writing, CC News (EN/ZH/FR/ES/AR)
notes: From Bao et al. 2025 (arXiv:2503.00258). Hierarchical AI risk levels: Level-1 (any AI), Level-2 (AI content), Level-3 (pure AI). Used to evaluate 2D detection method (content+expression decoupling).

name: RAID (Robust AI-generated Text Detection)
format: AI-generated text detection benchmark across 8 domains: News, Books, Wiki, Abstracts, Reddit, Recipes, Poetry, Reviews
notes: From Dugan et al. 2024 (arXiv:2405.07940). Used in Bao et al. 2025 (arXiv:2503.00258) as external evaluation benchmark for 2D detection method.

name: RoleBench
format: Role-playing benchmark dataset with 100 total characters (95 English, 5 Chinese); detailed role profiles with personality and background; general instructions from multiple datasets; data generated via RoleGPT and Context-Instruct with rigorous cleaning; split into general-purpose and role-specific subsets
metric: Rouge-L (RAW: instruction response accuracy, SPE: role-specific knowledge/memory, CUS: speaking style mimicry)

name: ECLeKTic
format: Multilingual closed-book QA pairs targeting language-specific facts with source/target language metadata

name: Cholec80
format: Laparoscopic surgery videos (cholecystectomy) at 25fps, annotated at 1fps with surgical phase labels
notes: Surgical phase recognition benchmark from Twinanda et al. (IEEE TMI 2017). 80 videos, mean duration ~39 min. Phases: trocars placement, calibration, dissection, clipping/cutting, gallbladder extraction, cleaning, closing.

name: BernBypass70
format: Bypass surgery videos at 25fps, annotated at 1fps with surgical phase labels
notes: Challenging multi-centric surgical phase recognition benchmark. 70 Roux-en-Y gastric bypass videos, avg 72 min. Multi-centric generalization challenge. More challenging than Cholec80 due to procedural complexity and multi-center variation.

name: AutoLaparo
format: Laparoscopic hysterectomy videos at 25fps, annotated at 1fps with surgical phase labels
notes: Multi-task surgical dataset for laparoscopic hysterectomy. 21 videos, avg 66 min. Includes phase recognition and instrument segmentation annotations.

name: Nectar
num_samples: ~300K+ preference pairs (prompts with chosen/rejected response pairs)
format: Prompt with two candidate responses and binary preference label indicating which response is preferred. Used for DPO/RLHF training.
notes: Preference dataset used in arXiv:2503.01076 (Active Learning for DPO). Paper samples N=5000 prompts for experiments with Llama-3.2-3B and Phi-3.

name: Text-VQA
num_samples: 5000+ images with questions requiring reading text in images
format: Images + questions about text in images + answers; requires OCR and visual reasoning

name: VSR
num_samples: ~1200 image-caption pairs with spatial reasoning questions
format: Images with natural language spatial relationship captions; tests spatial reasoning between text and images

name: SNLI-VE
format: Image + hypothesis text + label (entailment/contradiction/neutral); evaluates visual entailment understanding

name: Vision-Flan
format: Multimodal instruction-following data with image-text pairs covering diverse tasks (VQA, captioning, reasoning, etc.)

name: StyleBench
num_samples: 73 distinct styles with 5+ reference images each
format: Style transfer reference images with text prompts; focuses on style personalization tasks
access: https://github.com/jylinlau/StyleShot (StyleBench derived from StyleShot paper, arXiv:2407.01414)

name: CASAS (Milan, Aruba, Cairo)
num_samples: ~2.9M total sensor readings across 3 homes (Milan: 433665, Aruba: 1716039, Cairo: 726534)
num_classes: 6-9 activity labels per home (Cook, Eat, Relax, Sleep, Work, Bathing, etc.)
format: Time-series sensor event streams (motion, door, temperature sensors) with activity annotations
license: Research use (CASAS project, Washington State University)
notes: CASAS (Center for Advanced Studies in Adaptive Systems) smart home datasets. Milan: 72 days, single resident, 30 sensors. Aruba: 220 days, single resident. Cairo: 58 days, two residents. Used in DISCOVER (arXiv:2503.01733) for self-supervised PDL discovery. 33-77% of data is unlabeled ('No Label'), which DISCOVER addresses.

name: ScanNet200
format: Indoor RGB-D video sequences with camera poses, 3D reconstructions, and instance-level semantic segmentation annotations for 200 object categories
notes: Extended version of ScanNet with 200 semantic categories for instance segmentation. Used in OnlineAnySeg (2503.01309) for evaluating online zero-shot 3D instance segmentation. The paper uses the validation set (312 scenes) for evaluation.

name: SceneNN
num_samples: 100+ indoor scenes with high-quality mesh reconstructions
format: Indoor RGB-D sequences with per-frame camera poses and instance-level segmentation annotations
notes: Indoor 3D scene dataset with high-quality mesh reconstructions. OnlineAnySeg (2503.01309) uses 12 high-quality scenes following the EmbodiedSAM split. Smaller than ScanNet200 but with higher quality reconstructions.

name: ConFiQA (Counterfactual QA)
format: RAG QA pairs with counterfactual passages that conflict with LLM parametric memory; designed to evaluate context faithfulness under knowledge conflicts
notes: Counterfactual QA dataset for RAG faithfulness evaluation. Introduced in Bi et al. 2024 (Context-DPO paper, arXiv:2412.15280). Used for out-of-domain evaluation in GenDiE paper. Contains knowledge conflict scenarios where provided context contradicts LLM's internal knowledge.

name: ICL-NUIM
num_samples: 4 photorealistic synthetic indoor scenes (living room, office) with multiple trajectory variants
format: Synthetic RGB-D sequences with accurate ground-truth camera poses and 3D models from ICL institute

name: OpenLORIS-Scene
num_samples: Multiple real-world indoor sequences (office, home, corridor scenes) for lifelong SLAM
format: Multi-sensor data (RGB-D, LiDAR, IMU) for lifelong visual SLAM benchmarking with scene variations and illumination changes
metric: ATE RMSE, tracking accuracy, localization rate

name: SMapper
num_samples: 6 sequences (~44 minutes, ~620m trajectories) of indoor multi-room environments
format: Custom multi-modal data (RGB-D video + LiDAR point clouds) collected with SMapper device, with LiDAR-derived ground truth poses from S-Graphs
access: SMapper platform described in Soares et al., JINT 2026

name: CMNIST-75sp
format: MNIST digit images converted to superpixel graphs. 10 classes. Average ~61 nodes, ~489 edges per graph. Bias degrees: 0.8, 0.9, 0.95 (causal/non-causal co-occurrence rates in training set). Testing sets are unbiased.
access: https://github.com_divelab/GOOD (GOOD-CMNIST variant); original from CAL/DisC papers
notes: Graph OOD benchmark for digit classification. Used in GPro paper (arXiv:2503.02988) and prior OOD graph methods (CAL, DisC, CIGA, GALA). Bias degree controls spurious correlations between non-causal features (e.g., background color) and labels.

name: CFashion-75sp
format: Fashion-MNIST images converted to superpixel graphs. 10 classes. Average ~61 nodes, ~488 edges per graph. Bias degrees: 0.8, 0.9, 0.95. Testing sets are unbiased.
notes: Graph OOD benchmark for fashion product classification. Used in GPro paper (arXiv:2503.02988). Higher difficulty than CMNIST-75sp due to more complex visual patterns.

name: CKuzushiji-75sp
format: Kuzushiji handwritten character images converted to superpixel graphs. 10 classes. Average ~53 nodes, ~422 edges per graph. Bias degrees: 0.8, 0.9, 0.95. Testing sets are unbiased.
access: Original source: CMU爬起来 Kuzushiji dataset; graph version from CAL/DisC papers
notes: Graph OOD benchmark for Japanese character classification. Hardest of the three 75sp benchmarks. Used in GPro paper (arXiv:2503.02988).

name: Spider
format: English questions paired with SQL queries across 200+ databases; evaluated by execution accuracy

name: SAMSum
format: English dialogues with human-written summaries; simulates digital communications

name: DART
format: RDF triples with corresponding text summaries; structured data to text generation

name: SpeechInstructBench
num_samples: ~13K (7,718 En closed-ended + 5,208 Cn closed-ended + 500 En open-ended + 500 Cn open-ended + 250 En adjustment + 250 Cn adjustment)
format: Speech-based instruction-following tasks with closed-ended (rule-based verification), open-ended (GPT-4o judged), and adjustment instruction types. Covers accents, background noise, disfluencies, paralinguistic variations.
metric: Prompt-level accuracy, Instruction-level accuracy (strict/loose), IAR (Instruction Adherence Rate), ECR (Error Correction Rate)
notes: From Wang et al. 2025 (InSerter paper). Bilingual (English/Chinese) benchmark for speech instruction-following. Incorporates 13 English + 8 Chinese accents, 80 background noises, 6 emotions, disfluencies.

name: VoiceBench
format: Multi-task speech benchmark covering AlpacaEval, CommonEval, SD-QA, MMSU, OpenBookQA, AdvBench in speech modality
notes: From Chen et al. 2024b. Benchmark for evaluating LLM-based voice assistants across diverse tasks including instruction following, commonsense QA, and safety.

name: SD-QA
format: Speech dialogue QA benchmark with context-dependent questions
notes: From VoiceBench (Chen et al. 2024b). Speech-based dialogue understanding benchmark.

name: MMSU
format: Multi-modal speech understanding benchmark
notes: From VoiceBench (Chen et al. 2024b). Multi-modal speech evaluation benchmark.

name: EchoNet-Dynamic
format: Echocardiogram videos (apical-4-chamber view) with frame-level left ventricular segmentation masks and LVEF labels
metric: MAE, RMSE, MAPE for LVEF regression; Dice for segmentation

name: EchoNet-Pediatric
num_samples: ~3284 apical-4-chamber echocardiogram videos across 3 pediatric age groups (831 Pre-School, 914 School-Age, 1539 Adolescence)
format: Echocardiogram videos (apical-4-chamber view) from pediatric patients with LVEF labels; stratified by age cohorts
metric: MAE, RMSE, MAPE for LVEF regression; mAUROC at clinical thresholds (35%, 40%, 45%, 50%)

name: BC5CDR
format: PubMed articles with entity annotations (chemical, disease) and chemical-disease relations

name: NCBI-Disease
format: PubMed abstracts with disease entity annotations

name: BioRED
format: PubMed articles with multiple entity types and relation annotations

name: LitCovid
format: COVID-19 literature with multi-label topic classifications

name: HoC (Hallmarks of Cancer)
format: Cancer literature with multi-label hallmarks classifications

name: MIL (Mathematics in Lean)
format: Formal Lean 4 theorems from Mathlib4 tutorial (group theory, topology, number theory, etc.)

name: Mathlib4
format: Lean 4 formal mathematical library (algebra, analysis, topology, number theory, etc.)

name: LeanNavigator dataset
format: Lean 4 theorems with tactic-based proofs, generated by state-graph exploration of Mathlib4 theorems

name: AgentHarm
num_samples: 110 unique + 330 augmented agent behaviors across 11 harm categories (fraud, cybercrime, harassment, etc.)
eval_time: hours for full evaluation across models
format: Harmful instruction prompts for LLM agents requiring multi-step tool use (2-8 tools per task). Augmented from 44 base prompts with detail level and first-tool hint variations.
metric: Attack Success Rate (ASR) — agent refusal rate + target tool execution rate
notes: From Andriushchenko et al. (2024b). UDora paper (arXiv:2503.01908) evaluates red-teaming attacks on this benchmark, achieving 97.7% ASR on Llama-3.1-8B and 100% ASR on Ministral-8B.

name: BRCA (Breast Cancer) - Patch Dataset
num_samples: 120 patches (80 train / 10 val / 30 test) from 113 patients
format: H&E histopathology image patches with point annotations (nucleus centroids) and categories (tumor, inflammatory, stromal)
metric: F1-score per nucleus type, Average F1-score
notes: From Abousamra et al. 2021. Nucleus detection benchmark for breast cancer WSIs. Three nucleus categories: tumor, inflammatory, stromal.

name: OCELOT (Overlapped Cell on Tissue)
num_samples: 664 patches (400 train / 137 val / 126 test) from 303 WSIs
format: H&E histopathology patches with point annotations for nucleus centroids; binary classification: tumor vs non-tumor
metric: F1-score per nucleus type, Average F1-score
notes: From Ryu et al., CVPR 2023. Overlapped cell dataset for histopathology. 113,026 nuclei total.

name: PUMA (Pathology UMA)
format: H&E histopathology patches from melanoma tissue with point annotations; three categories: tumor, TILs (tumor infiltrating lymphocytes), other
metric: F1-score per nucleus type, Average F1-score
notes: Melanoma nucleus detection benchmark. Three nucleus types: tumor, TILs, other.

name: NLVR2
format: Image-sentence pairs for visual reasoning — determine if a natural language statement describes an image correctly (true/false)

name: MIT-Adobe FiveK Dataset
num_samples: 5000 raw images (4500 train, 500 validation) captured with DSLR cameras
format: Raw images in DNG format with expert retouched outputs from 5 experts (A-E). Used for photo retouching and image processing pipeline tuning.
notes: From Bychkovsky et al., CVPR 2011. Widely used for photo finishing tuning. In this paper: 4500 training images with random parameter generation for targets, 500 validation images with expert-C targets.

name: mmGait10
num_samples: ~5 hours radar measurements from 10 subjects, 3 walking modalities, ~60k frames total
format: mmWave FMCW radar point cloud sequences (4D: x, y, z, velocity) and micro-Doppler spectrograms. Texas Instruments MMWCAS-RF-EVM radar operating at 77-81 GHz.
notes: From Mazzieri et al. (2025). First publicly available dataset for open-set gait recognition from sparse radar point clouds. Subjects walk freely in indoor environment (7.81m x 7.26m room) with 3 modalities: walking freely, walking while holding smartphone, walking with hands in pockets. Average 150-200 points per frame.

name: m-bigearthnet
format: 120x120 Sentinel-2 multispectral patches (12 bands) with 43 multi-label land cover classes

name: m-so2sat
format: 32x32 multispectral + SAR patches (Sentinel-2 + Sentinel-1) with 17 land cover classes

name: m-forestnet
format: 332x332 Landsat-8 patches (6 bands) with 12 forest/land cover classes

name: RSICD
format: Aerial/satellite RGB images paired with natural language descriptions for remote sensing image captioning
metric: Recall@K (R@1, R@5, R@10) for image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval

name: RSITMD
format: Aerial/satellite RGB images paired with natural language descriptions for remote sensing image captioning
metric: Recall@K (R@1, R@5, R@10) for image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval

name: UCM-caption
format: UCM land use dataset aerial images with natural language captions
metric: Recall@K (R@1, R@5, R@10) for image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval

name: MADOS (Marine Debris and Oil Spill)
format: High-resolution Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery for marine pollution detection (oil spill, marine debris)

name: m-nz-cattle
format: 500x500 aerial RGB images for cattle detection/segmentation in New Zealand pastoral scenes

name: m-NeonTree
format: 400x400 aerial/satellite images with RGB + hyperspectral + elevation data for tree detection/segmentation

name: SkyScript
num_samples: 7000 test images (70 classes), ~1.5M training image-text pairs from OSM
format: Aerial RGB images paired with OpenStreetMap semantic tags and natural language descriptions for zero-shot EO classification

name: BookMIA
num_samples: ~40,000 samples for fine-tuning (from 'unseen' split of copyrighted books)
format: 32-word text samples extracted from copyrighted books, labeled as 'seen' or 'unseen' based on whether books were published before or after model pretraining cutoff
metric: Rouge-L, BERT similarity, Edit Similarity, MAUVE, Membership Inference metrics
access: Shi et al. 2023, arXiv:2310.16789; https://github.com/xxx (original paper should have the dataset link)
notes: Used in PoisonedParrot (arXiv:2503.07697) for evaluating copyright infringement via data poisoning. 'Unseen' samples are from books published after LLM pretraining cutoff.

name: RefactorBench
num_samples: 100 multi-file refactoring tasks across 9 Python repositories (Flask, Django, FastAPI, Celery, Ansible, Requests, Scrapy, Tornado, Salt)
storage: ~1-2GB (9 Python repositories as benchmark substrates + task definitions + AST unit tests)
eval_time: hours (full agent evaluation across 100 tasks with cost cap)
format: Multi-file code refactoring tasks with AST-based unit tests for verification. Three instruction tiers: lazy (unspecific), base (succinct), descriptive (exhaustive).
metric: Task completion rate (pass all AST tests)
license: MIT (benchmark); GitHub OSS licenses for repository substrates
notes: Introduced in arXiv:2503.07832 (Gautam et al., 2025). Evaluates stateful reasoning in LM agents through multi-file refactoring. Baseline SWE-agent achieves 22% on base instructions vs 87% human success rate. State-aware interface modification improves performance by 43.9%.

name: MURA
eval_time: minutes per model on single GPU
format: Grayscale musculoskeletal X-ray images (hand, wrist, forearm, elbow, shoulder, humerus, finger) with binary labels (normal vs abnormal)

name: City-Networks
num_samples: 4 cities: Paris (114k nodes), Shanghai (184k), Los Angeles (241k), London (569k)
format: City road networks from OpenStreetMap. Node features: 37-dim (latitude, longitude, land use, aggregated edge features). Edge features: road length, speed limit, lanes, road type. Task: 10-class node classification based on local eccentricity (k=16 hops).
notes: Large-scale transductive benchmark for long-range dependency in GNNs. Features large diameters (100-400 hops). Proposed in arXiv:2503.09008 by Liang et al. (Oxford).

name: Speech Commands v2
format: 1-second 16kHz single-word speech commands across 35+ classes (e.g., 'yes', 'no', 'up', 'down', digits)
notes: Limited-vocabulary speech recognition dataset by Warden (2018). Used in AST paper for audio classification. Test set is pre-defined with fixed split.

name: ODinW-13 (Object Detection in the Wild)
format: Open-vocabulary object detection across 13 diverse domains (Aerial Maritime Drone, Aquarium, Cottontail Rabbit, EgoHands, Mushrooms, Packages, Pascal VOC, Pistols, Pothole, Raccoon, Shellfish, Thermal Dogs and People, Vehicles)
notes: Used in DitHub paper (arXiv:2503.09271) for incremental vision-language object detection evaluation. Derived from ODinW benchmark originally introduced in GLIP/Grounded VL paper (Li et al., 2022).

name: ODinW-O (Overlapped)
num_samples: 6 sub-datasets with class overlap across tasks
format: Subset of ODinW-35 with class overlap across tasks. Classes reappear across multiple domains: Aerial Maritime Drone (boat, car), Pascal VOC (boat, car, dog, person), Thermal Dogs and People (dog, person), Vehicles (car, truck), Hard Hat Workers (person), Self Driving Cars (car, truck).
access: Introduced in DitHub paper (arXiv:2503.09271), derived from ODinW-35 (Elevater benchmark)
notes: New benchmark introduced in DitHub paper (arXiv:2503.09271) to evaluate incremental learning under class reappearance across domains.

name: DynaMath
format: Dynamic visual math benchmark with 501 seed questions each generating 10 concrete variants; tests VLM robustness to visual variations in math problems
metric: worst-case accuracy (correct across all variants) and average-case accuracy

name: LogicVista
format: Multimodal LLM logical reasoning benchmark in visual contexts; 448 multiple-choice questions evaluating 5 logical reasoning tasks across 9 capabilities

name: VisualProcessBench
num_samples: 2866 samples with 26950 human-annotated step-wise correctness labels
format: Benchmark for evaluating PRMs and MLLMs on detecting erroneous steps in multimodal reasoning; requires identifying ALL erroneous steps (not just first); human-annotated step correctness labels
metric: macro F1 score for correct and incorrect steps

name: MMPR v1.1
format: Multimodal reasoning preference dataset constructed via automated preference data pipeline; used as source of image-question pairs for VisualPRM400K
access: Wang et al., 2024 (arXiv:2411.10442); used in MixPO paper

name: VisualPRM400K
num_samples: ~400K samples with ~2M step-level process supervision labels
format: Multimodal process supervision dataset with image-question pairs (from MMPR v1.1), step-by-step solutions (from InternVL2.5), and MC-based step correctness annotations (16 continuations per step, step correct if mc > 0)

name: OpenSRH
num_samples: ~285K patches (229K train + 56K val) from 303 patients, 7 classes
storage: ~50-100GB estimated (300x300 RGB patches from whole slide images)
format: Digital pathology patches (300x300) extracted from gigapixel whole slide images of brain tumor biopsies and resections
metric: kNN classification accuracy at patch, slide, and patient levels; adversarial robustness (white-box/black-box attack accuracy)

name: WorkArena
num_samples: 33 task types, up to 1000 instances each (~495 training + 165 evaluation tasks used in paper)
format: Multi-step web navigation trajectories with accessibility tree observations on enterprise websites

name: LasHeR
format: RGB-Thermal (RGBT) video pairs for object tracking. 12 challenge attributes including occlusion, low illumination, thermal crossover.
metric: PR (Precision Rate), SR (Success Rate), NPR (Normalized PR)

name: GTOT
format: RGB-Thermal video pairs for object tracking. One of the earliest RGBT tracking benchmarks.

name: RGBT210
format: RGB-Thermal video pairs for object tracking with bounding box annotations and 12 challenge attributes.

name: RGBT234
format: RGB-Thermal video pairs with improved alignment and precise bounding boxes, 12 challenge attributes. Refinement of RGBT210.

name: CAMUS (Corpus of Echocardiography for Multi-task Understanding)
description: 500 patients, 2 apical views each (A2C and A4C), systolic phase videos with sparse LV segmentations
format: 2D echocardiography videos with sparse left-ventricle contour annotations and mitral annulus landmark endpoints
metric: MAE for landmark detection, segmentation metrics for LV

name: ASMA-Bench
num_samples: 90 questions (30 assembly snippets x 3 question types: conversation, description, reasoning)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Assembly-language instruction-following evaluation. GPT-4-Turbo reference predictions establish upper bound. GPT-4-Turbo evaluates candidate model outputs on 5 dimensions (helpfulness, relevance, accuracy, detail, comprehensiveness) 1-10 scale.
metric: Average score across dimensions, per question type
access: Not yet released (from ASMA-Tune paper, arXiv:2503.11617)
notes: First benchmark for instruction-following in assembly language. Randomly selected 30 assembly snippets from BinaryCorp-3M Test (364 projects, 1908 binaries). Spans cryptography, malware, and protocol implementations.

name: BinaryCorp-3M
num_samples: 10,265 binaries, 3M functions from Arch Linux official repos and AUR
format: Binary functions with assembly code, extracted using Capstone disassembly. Covers gcc/clang compilers with O0-O4 optimization levels. Diverse categories: editors, messaging, HTTP servers, browsers, compilers, crypto libraries.
access: Not publicly released. Contact authors or reconstruct from Arch Linux packages.
notes: Largest binary dataset for BCSD tasks. Used in JTrans, CLAP, and ASMA-Tune papers. Requires recompilation and disassembly pipeline to reconstruct.

name: Juliet Test Suite
num_samples: 64,099 test cases with C/C++ source and compiled binaries
format: C/C++ vulnerability test cases with function pairs (GoodSource/BadSource, GoodSink/BadSink). Each test case has vulnerability type label and semantic annotations.
notes: Mature vulnerability analysis dataset. Used in ASMA-Tune paper for assembly function descriptions via Source-Sink combinations. Juliet Test Suite 1.1 contains C/C++ and Java test cases.

name: TGIF-QA
format: Animated GIFs from Tumblr with QA pairs covering count, action, transition, and object questions; evaluating spatial-temporal reasoning
notes: TGIF-QA: Toward Spatio-Temporal Reasoning in Visual Question Answering (Jang et al., CVPR 2017). Used in VideoMAP paper for VideoLLaVA evaluation.

name: Breakfast
format: First-person videos of daily breakfast preparation activities (pouring cereal, cutting fruit, etc.) with action segment annotations; 48 action classes
notes: The Language of Actions: Recovering the Syntax and Semantics of Goal-Directed Human Activities (Kuehne et al., CVPR 2014). Used in VideoMAP paper for long-term video understanding evaluation.

name: N3DV
format: Multi-view synchronized MP4 videos with camera poses (poses_bounds.npy)

name: MeetRoom
format: Multi-view video with camera poses

name: Basketball-Court
format: Multi-view video, large motion dataset

name: CPRD Aurum
num_samples: ~4 million patients (UK primary care, ~20% of UK population)
storage: ~100-500GB (linked primary/secondary care with HES and ONS mortality data)
format: structured EHR: diagnoses (SNOMED), medications, procedures, demographics, lifestyle factors, linked to hospital episodes and mortality records
license: CPRD research data agreement (institutional access required)

name: MPBench
format: Multimodal benchmark for evaluating process-level reward models (PRMs); 3 evaluation paradigms: Step Correctness (binary step evaluation), Answer Aggregation (best-of-N and majority voting), Reasoning Process Search (guided search); data from M3CoT across science, math, commonsense domains; multimodal image-question pairs with step-by-step reasoning solutions
metric: RMScore (F1_neg + F1 weighted), F1, MCC, accuracy

name: AVS-Semantic (AVSBench-semantic)
format: Audio-visual video segmentation with 10 frames and 10-second audio segment per pair; semantic annotations identifying sounding regions and specific audio types; 10 semantic categories

name: VPO (Visual Prompting for Objects)
format: Synthetic dataset combining COCO single-frame images with 3-second VGGSound audio clips; includes single-source (SS), multi-source (MS), and multi-source with matching spatial info (MSMI) subsets for audio-visual segmentation
access: Associated with CAVP paper (Chen et al., CVPR 2024)

name: Humaneval+
num_samples: 164 (same as HumanEval, but with 80x more test cases per problem)
format: Python code generation problems with extended test suites; evaluates functional correctness via execution
access: https://github.com/THUDM/CodeMATE (related); original HumanEval from Chen et al. 2021
notes: Introduced by Liu et al. (2023) to address HumanEval saturation. Used in RaSA paper for rigorous code generation evaluation.

name: Magicoder-Evol-Instruct-110k
format: Programming QA pairs generated via evolution pipeline from OSS-instruct; decontaminated version of WizardCoder data
notes: From Wei et al. (2024). Used as training data in RaSA paper for code generation fine-tuning.

name: Histo-VL
num_samples: 5,358,942 patches from 41,508 WSIs, 32 cancer types, 26 organs, 14 cohorts, 11 acquisition tools, 7 clinical tasks
eval_time: days (full evaluation of 7 VLMs on 5.3M patches)
format: Histopathology image patches with paired captions (single and ensemble templates). Images from multiple tissue preservation methods (FFPE, snap-freezing) and magnification levels (4X-400X).
metric: Balanced accuracy, F1-score, precision, MCC, ECE (Expected Calibration Error), reliability plots

name: MUSTARDSAUCE
eval_time: hours to days depending on sample budget
format: Each sample includes: informal mathematical statement, informal proof in natural language, and Lean-validated formal proof. Generated using GPT-4 from seed mathematical concepts.
notes: From Huang et al. (AAAI 2024). Used in KG-Prover (arXiv:2503.11657) as one of three evaluation benchmarks. Paper used 250 randomly selected problems.

name: Action Genome
num_samples: ~10K videos, 234,253 frames, 476,229 bounding boxes (35 object categories), 1,715,568 predicate instances (25 predicate classes across 3 types: attention, spatial, contacting)
format: Video scene graph dataset — frames annotated with bounding boxes, object classes, and predicate labels. Extended from Charades. Supports PredCLS, SGCLS, SGDET evaluation protocols.
metric: Recall@K (K=10,20,50), Mean-Recall@K, under w/ and w/o constraint settings
notes: Action Genome (Ji et al., CVPR 2020) is the standard benchmark for VSGG. Extends Charades with spatio-temporal scene graph annotations.

name: Strecha
format: Multi-view RGB images (3072x2048) with ground truth point clouds from laser scans
notes: Strecha et al. CVPR 2008 benchmark for high-resolution imagery and multi-view stereo. Fountain and HerzJesu scenes used for evaluation in SED-MVS paper.

name: HCSTVG-v1
format: Spatio-temporal video grounding: given a language query, localize the target object both temporally and spatially in the video (bounding box tube)

name: HCSTVG-v2
format: Extended version of HCSTVG-v1 with more diverse videos and complex queries for spatio-temporal video grounding

name: VidSTG
format: Video spatio-temporal grounding benchmark with both declarative and interrogative sentences; requires localizing objects both temporally and spatially

name: TempCompass
num_samples: ~1,000+ video pairs with temporal reasoning questions
format: Video temporal reasoning benchmark with multiple-choice QA testing whether video LLMs understand temporal ordering and causality in videos

name: Rope3D
format: Traffic camera images with 3D bounding box annotations for monocular 3D detection; multiple camera locations with varying FOVs
metric: AP_3D, AP_BEV at IoU 0.5/0.7 for car class

name: CDrone
format: Drone/aerial images with 3D bounding box annotations for monocular 3D detection; bird's-eye view perspective
metric: AP_3D at IoU 0.5 for car class

name: PreSIL (Precise Synthetic Image and Lidar)
format: Synthetic driving dataset from CARLA/GTA V simulator with paired RGB images, depth maps, and LiDAR point clouds; 3D bounding box annotations
license: Research use (GTA V EULA for synthetic data)

name: MT-PRMBench
num_samples: 1,200 examples (200 per translation direction across 6 directions)
format: Token-level and sequence-level preference pairs for evaluating Process Reward Models in machine translation; examples from WMT17-WMT20 test sets and Flores data for EN, DE, ZH, RU language pairs
metric: Accuracy (classification: given chosen/rejected pair, does PRM correctly identify the better one?)
notes: First MT-specific PRM benchmark, introduced in MT-RewardTree paper (arXiv:2503.12123). Two subsets: token-level (assessing preferences between immediate next-token candidates) and sequence-level (comparing entire generated sequence completions).

name: BEATv2 (BEAT2-Standard)
num_samples: ~27 hours of motion data (Speaker-2 subset), ~60 hours total
format: 3D full-body mesh (SMPLX) at 30fps, audio (22kHz), text transcripts, semantic and emotional labels
metric: FGD (Frechet Gesture Distance), BC (Beat Consistency), Diversity

name: SHOW Dataset
format: 3D full-body mesh (SMPLX) at 30fps, audio (22kHz) from in-the-wild talk show recordings
metric: FGD (Frechet Gesture Distance), BC (Beat Consistency), Diversity

name: ColBench
num_samples: 10k train + 1k test (Backend Programming); 10k train + 500 test (Frontend Design)
format: Multi-turn collaborative tasks: Backend Programming (Python function writing with unit tests) and Frontend Design (HTML web page creation); LLM-simulated human collaborator with reference artifact access; functional evaluators for success measurement
metric: Backend: % tests passed, success rate (all 10 tests pass); Frontend: cosine similarity of CLIP embeddings between generated and reference web page
notes: Introduced in SWEET-RL paper (arXiv:2503.15478). First benchmark designed for multi-turn RL algorithm research on reasoning-intensive collaborative tasks. Uses LLM as human simulator with ground-truth artifacts for faithful simulation. Supports offline RL training and evaluation with functional verifiers.

name: WebSight
num_samples: 10k+ HTML web page pairs (screenshot + HTML code)
format: Paired web page screenshots and corresponding HTML/HTML+CSS code; used for frontend design tasks in ColBench
notes: Original source: WebSight dataset from HuggingFace (uttihalab/websight). Used in ColBench Frontend Design task as the source of reference web pages for collaborative HTML design tasks.

name: DocLayNet
format: document images + OCR annotations (11 page object types)

name: Comp-HRDoc
format: document images + OCR + hierarchical structure annotations
metric: Segm. mAP (page object detection), REDS (reading order), Semantic-TEDS (TOC extraction, hierarchical reconstruction)

name: IconQA
num_samples: ~100k train, ~18k test (multiple sub-tasks: fill-in-the-blank, multiple-choice, free-form answer)
format: Visual question answering benchmark over abstract diagram images; tests abstract reasoning, diagram understanding, and visual literacy; includes icon recognition, diagram parsing, and reasoning over abstract visual symbols
notes: From Lu et al., NeurIPS 2021. Paper: 'IconQA: A New Benchmark for Abstract Diagram Understanding and Visual Language Reasoning'. The paper uses the fill-in-the-blank subset.

name: OCRVQA
storage: ~50GB (images of book covers, movie posters, CD covers, etc.)
format: Visual question answering benchmark requiring reading and reasoning about text in images; images contain text such as book titles, author names, movie titles, etc.; tests OCR capability combined with VQA
notes: From Mishra et al., ICDAR 2019. Paper: 'OCR-VQA: Visual Question Answering by Reading Text in Images'. Tests ability to read and reason over text in images.

name: MoCA-Mask
format: Video camouflage object detection dataset based on Moving Camouflaged Animals (MoCA); consecutive video frames with pixel-level binary segmentation masks for camouflaged animals
access: https://github.com/xb Jiu/SLT-Net (original MoCA from Lamdouar et al. 2020)

name: CAD (Camouflaged Animal Dataset)
format: Early video camouflage dataset with bounding box annotations for camouflaged animals; used for validation in VCOD papers
access: https://github.com/xb Jiu/SLT-Net (original CAD from Bideau & Learned-Miller 2016)

name: WikiBio GPT-3 Hallucination Dataset
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on method complexity
format: GPT-3 generated biographical passages with sentence-level hallucination annotations; multiple samples per passage for sampling-based detection
notes: From SelfCheckGPT paper (Manakul et al., 2023). Only existing dataset for evaluating sampling-based hallucination detection before FavaMultiSamples. Contains passages generated by GPT-3 from Wikipedia seed facts with human-annotated hallucination labels at sentence level.

name: FavaMultiSamples
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on method complexity
format: Diverse knowledge-intensive queries with multiple LLM response samples per prompt; sentence-level hallucination annotations; built upon FAVA dataset
notes: Contributed by FactSelfCheck paper (arXiv:2503.17229). Addresses the gap in evaluation datasets for sampling-based hallucination detection methods. Built upon FAVA dataset (Mishra et al., 2024). 20 samples generated per passage at temperature 1.0 using GPT-3.5-turbo-1106 and Llama2-Chat-70B.

name: HER2+ Spatial Transcriptomics (10x Visium)
num_samples: 36 tissue sections from 8 patients (13,620 spots total)
storage: ~20-50GB (WSI images + gene expression matrices, top 785 highly variable genes after filtering)
eval_time: minutes for model inference per fold
format: Paired H&E-stained whole slide images (WSIs) and spatial gene expression counts from 10x Visium; each spot has a 224x224 pixel image patch and gene expression vector; evaluated using PCC, CCC, MAE
metric: PCC (Pearson Correlation Coefficient), CCC (Concordance Correlation Coefficient), MAE (Mean Absolute Error)
license: Research use (data from Andersson et al., 2021 Nature Communications)
notes: Human HER2-positive breast cancer spatial transcriptomics dataset. Used in PH2ST (arXiv:2503.16816) and prior ST prediction works (ST-Net, HisToGene, Hist2ST, HGGEP, BLEEP, TRIPLEX).

name: cSCC Spatial Transcriptomics (10x Visium)
num_samples: 12 tissue sections from 4 patients (23,205 spots total)
storage: ~20-50GB (WSI images + gene expression matrices, top 171 highly variable genes after filtering)
eval_time: minutes for model inference per fold
format: Paired H&E-stained whole slide images (WSIs) and spatial gene expression counts from 10x Visium; each spot has a 224x224 pixel image patch and gene expression vector; evaluated using PCC, CCC, MAE
metric: PCC (Pearson Correlation Coefficient), CCC (Concordance Correlation Coefficient), MAE (Mean Absolute Error)
license: Research use (data from Ji et al., 2020 Cell)
notes: Human cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma spatial transcriptomics dataset. Used in PH2ST (arXiv:2503.16816) and prior ST prediction works (ST-Net, HisToGene, Hist2ST, HGGEP, BLEEP, TRIPLEX).

name: AuditoryBench
num_samples: 21,714 total (6,212 Animal Sound Recognition + 15,502 Sound Pitch Comparison across train/dev/test/wiki)
eval_time: minutes to fine-tune on encoder, hours for full evaluation with audio generation
format: Text sentences with audio-related spans; two task types: (1) Animal Sound Recognition: classify the animal from its sound description, (2) Sound Pitch Comparison: compare pitch between two instruments/objects
access: Reference: Ok et al., 2025 (AudioBERT, ICASSP 2025). No explicit access URL in Imagine to Hear paper (arXiv:2503.16853).
notes: Benchmark for evaluating auditory commonsense knowledge in language models. Introduced by AudioBERT (Ok et al., ICASSP 2025). Used in Imagine to Hear (ITH) paper (arXiv:2503.16853) as the primary evaluation benchmark. Animal Sound Recognition: 4,211 train / 593 dev / 1,211 test / 197 wiki. Sound Pitch Comparison: 8,312 train / 1,178 dev / 2,387 test / 3,625 wiki.

name: VIGOR
num_samples: ~90k ground-aerial image pairs across 4 US cities (same-area + cross-area splits)
format: Ground-level 360-degree panorama images paired with aerial orthoimages for cross-view localization; includes camera pose annotations (3 DoF: location + yaw)
metric: mean/median localization error (meters), orientation error (degrees), percentage within threshold

name: Google Immersive
format: Multi-view light field video with layered mesh representation

name: PhotoTourism
num_samples: ~5 scenes (Brandenburg Gate, Sacre Coeur, Trevi Fountain, Palace of Westminster, Pantheon Exterior), ~10-20 images per scene
eval_time: hours per scene for NVS training
format: Unconstrained internet photo collections of tourist landmarks with varying viewpoints, times, illumination, and transient occlusions; no camera calibration provided

name: BONN RGB-D Dynamic
num_samples: 6 dynamic indoor RGB-D sequences with ground truth depth and camera poses
format: RGB-D videos of dynamic indoor scenes with accurate depth maps and camera pose ground truth for evaluating depth estimation and SLAM in dynamic environments
metric: Abs Rel, delta<1.25 (depth); ATE, RPE (camera pose)
notes: BONN dynamic RGB-D dataset used in Refusion (IROS 2019) for 3D reconstruction in dynamic environments. Also used in AETHER paper (arXiv:2503.18945) for zero-shot depth estimation evaluation.

name: HIT (Human Implicit Tissues)
num_samples: 398 adults (157 male, 241 female) scanned in prone position using 1.5T MRI
storage: ~10-20GB estimated (MRI volumes with skin surface segmentations and SMPL registrations)
format: MRI scans with paired SMPL mesh registrations; skin surface point clouds extracted via marching cubes; used for in-silico validation of in-bed pose and shape estimation
notes: From Keller et al. CVPR 2024. Provides paired volumetric MRI data and full-body SMPL registrations. Used in VIM-PSE (arXiv:2503.19405) for large-scale simulation study (N=300 subjects).

name: SLP (Simultaneously-collected Multimodal Lying Pose)
num_samples: Not specified in paper (paper: Liu et al. 2022)
storage: ~GB range estimated (RGB-D, IR, pressure map, SMPL annotations)
format: Multi-modal lying pose dataset: RGB, depth, infrared, pressure maps with SMPL annotations; captures natural supine sleeping configurations
notes: From Liu et al. IEEE TPAMI 2022. Provides in-bed pose configurations used for re-posing HIT subjects in VIM-PSE (arXiv:2503.19405).

name: TREC Deep Learning Track
num_samples: 43 queries (DL19) / 54 queries (DL20) with multiple judgments per query
format: Ad hoc retrieval benchmark using MS MARCO passage corpus; TREC 2019 and 2020 tracks share the same document collection
notes: Deep Learning track uses MS MARCO v1 passage corpus (8.8M passages). Official metric is NDCG@10. Used in arXiv:2503.19092 (SIGIR 2025) for studying LLM judge biases.

name: WikiArt
format: Fine-art paintings with style labels (artist, genre, style). Used for style classification and stylized image generation evaluation.
metric: N/A (dataset); downstream metrics include FID, SSIM, PSNR for generation quality
notes: Large-scale fine-art painting dataset introduced in Saleh & Elgammal (arXiv:1505.00855). Widely used for artwork classification and style transfer/generation tasks.

name: ArtBench
format: Artwork images at 224x224 resolution with 10 style categories. Train/test split provided. Benchmark for generative models on artwork domain.
access: https://github.com/liaopeiyuan/ArtBench (unofficial) or original from paper arXiv:2206.11404
notes: ArtBench dataset introduced in Liao et al. (arXiv:2206.11404). Benchmarking generative models with artworks. Used in SITA paper (arXiv:2503.19791) for evaluating adversarial protection methods.

name: DENSE (Event-based Depth Dataset)
num_samples: Synthetic driving sequences with image-event-depth tuples
format: Synthetic RGB-event pairs with depth ground truth; depth range 3.34-1000m; official train/test splits
notes: From Hidalgo-Carrio et al., 'Learning Monocular Dense Depth from Events', 3DV 2020. Used in FUSE paper (2503.19739) for evaluating image-event depth estimation. Synthetically generated driving scenarios for event camera research.

name: EventScape
format: Synthetic image-event pairs without depth ground truth; used for self-supervised pretraining of event encoders
notes: From Gehrig et al., 'Combining Events and Frames Using Recurrent Asynchronous Multimodal Networks', RAL 2021. Used in FUSE paper (2503.19739) for Stage I PST training (Parameter-efficient Self-supervised Transfer) — the knowledge transfer from Depth Anything V2 to the event encoder via paired image-event data without requiring depth labels.

name: MultiVENT 2.0
num_samples: 218,000 videos, 3,906 manually curated queries (108,600 train / 109,800 test videos; 1,361 train / 2,545 test queries)
format: Multilingual event-centric video retrieval; 6 languages (Arabic, Chinese, English, Korean, Russian, Spanish); queries reflect real-world information-seeking behavior

name: TVR (TV show Retrieval)
format: Video-subtitle moment retrieval dataset from 6 TV shows; queries use subtitles, video, or both; requires moment localization within videos

name: AVUT
num_samples: 2,662 videos, 11,609 QA pairs (AV-Human: 698 videos / 1,734 QA; AV-Gemini: 1,964 videos / 9,875 QA)
eval_time: 4-6 hours per model for full evaluation
format: Audio-centric video understanding benchmark with 8 task types: 6 multiple-choice (AIE, ACC, AEL, AVCM, AVOM, AVTM) and 2 open-ended (AVSM, AVDiar). Questions require genuine audio understanding and audio-visual alignment, not just visual reasoning.
license: Research (YouTube TOS compliant — only links shared)

name: Observed Antibody Space (OAS)
num_samples: >10M antibody sequences (paired and unpaired VH/VL sequences)
format: Database of antibody sequences with IMGT numbering, CDR annotations, and paired/unpaired status. Contains both human and non-human antibodies with germline annotations.
notes: Used in IgCraft paper for training on 118M unpaired VH + 135M unpaired VL sequences and 1.5M paired VH/VL sequences. Also used in multiple other antibody design papers (AbLang2, p-IgGen, etc.) as the primary source of antibody sequence data.

name: OmniObject3D
format: Large-vocabulary 3D object dataset with real-scanned objects; multi-view RGB renders and camera poses; used for 3D reconstruction and generation benchmarks
metric: F-Score / CD / NC (Chamfer Distance / Normal Consistency)

name: EXPo (Event-based Cross-Platform Perception)
num_samples: ~89k frames (61k train, 26k val) from 21 sequences across vehicle, drone, and quadruped platforms
format: Event voxel grids (T=20, H=360, W=640) with 11-class and 19-class semantic segmentation labels
notes: From Kong et al. 2025 (arXiv:2503.19916). Built on M3ED dataset. Largest event camera perception benchmark for cross-platform adaptation.

name: DSEC-Semantic
format: Event camera data from driving scenarios with pixel-level semantic annotations; 11 semantic classes
notes: From Gehrig et al. 2021 and subsequent semantic segmentation annotations. Used in ESS (Semantic Segmentation for Event Cameras) and EventFly paper.

name: M3ED (Multi-Modal Event Dataset)
num_samples: ~Event data from vehicle, drone, and quadruped platforms
format: Event camera data (Prophesee Gen4 EVKv4, 720x1280) with RGB frames, IMU data, and semantic labels
notes: From Zhang et al. 2024. The foundation dataset for EXPo benchmark. Contains ~90k event frames across multiple robotic platforms.

name: VerilogEval
num_samples: 138 HDL code samples across 3 complexity levels
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on PPA tool flow
format: Verilog HDL code benchmark for evaluating LLM-based code generation and understanding. Levels 1-3 range from simple combinational circuits to complex FSMs and sequential circuits (up to 607 gates).
metric: Pass rate at relative error thresholds (5%, 10%, 20%) for PPA metrics; functional correctness
notes: From Liu et al. (ICCAD 2023). Used in RocketPPA paper (arXiv:2503.21971) for evaluating PPA estimation accuracy. Level 3 (72 modules) is the most challenging subset.

name: MG-Verilog
format: Large collection of Verilog HDL modules for hardware design training. Modules span from simple combinational circuits to complex FSMs.
notes: One of three training data sources in RocketPPA paper (arXiv:2503.21971). Used alongside verilog_github and VeriGen to create a 20,953-module training dataset for LLM-based PPA estimation.

name: verilog_github
format: Curated collection of Verilog HDL modules from GitHub repositories. Includes a broad spectrum of design complexities and styles.
notes: One of three training data sources in RocketPPA paper (arXiv:2503.21971). Combined with MG-Verilog (9,239) and VeriGen (3,923) for a total of 20,953 training modules.

name: VeriGen
format: Synthetic Verilog HDL generation dataset. Modules generated via code-to-code augmentation and self-reflection pipelines.
notes: From OriGen paper (arXiv:2407.16237). One of three training data sources in RocketPPA paper (arXiv:2503.21971). Used alongside MG-Verilog and verilog_github to create a 20,953-module training dataset.

name: ImageNet-Hard
format: Curated subset of ImageNet containing the hardest/most complex images, selected for difficulty and spatial reasoning challenges
notes: From Taesiri et al. 2024 (NeurIPS). Used in paper arXiv:2503.22079 for evaluating flexible object recognition on challenging images.

name: FDA (Flexible Object Dataset)
num_samples: 2474 images across 9 classes (clouds, smoke, fog, fire, light, water, etc.)
format: Flexible object images curated for recognition tasks
notes: From Yang et al. 2025 (TCSVT). Used in arXiv:2503.22079 as one of the main evaluation datasets for flexible object recognition.

name: FSCW (Flexible烟雾云水 Dataset)
num_samples: 5267 images across 6 classes (clouds, smoke-like clouds, smoke, fire, water, sea)
format: Flexible object images curated from CCSN, Firenet, CDD, and Kaggle sources
notes: Proposed dataset in arXiv:2503.22079. Larger-scale flexible dataset curated from existing sources. Used as main evaluation dataset alongside FDA.

name: DIR (Deformable Image Registration) Dataset
num_samples: 5 patients (4D CT with 10 respiratory phases each)
format: 4D CT scans from thoracic cancer patients (esophageal or lung cancer); each patient has 10 3D CT volumes at different respiratory phases; spatial resolution 0.97-1.16mm in xy, 2.5mm in z
notes: Castillo et al., Phys. Med. Biol., 2009. Used in X²-Gaussian paper for 4D CT reconstruction evaluation.

name: 4DLung Dataset
num_samples: 5 NSCLC patients (4D CT with 10 respiratory phases each)
format: 4D CT from non-small cell lung cancer patients; respiratory-synchronized into 10 breathing phases; transverse resolution 0.9766-1.053mm, axial resolution 3mm
notes: Hugo et al., 2016. Used in X²-Gaussian paper for 4D CT reconstruction evaluation.

name: SPARE Dataset
num_samples: 3 patients (4D CT with 10 respiratory phases each)
format: 4D cone-beam CT from sparse-view reconstruction challenge; isotropic 1mm resolution in all directions
notes: Shieh et al., Med. Phys., 2019. Used in X²-Gaussian paper for 4D CT reconstruction evaluation.

name: M3SVD
format: Temporally synchronized and spatially registered infrared-visible video pairs. Covers daytime, nighttime, low-light, over-exposure, disguise, and occlusion scenarios across 100 scenes.
metric: EN, MI, SD, SSIM, VIF (fusion quality); flowD (temporal consistency)

name: HDO (High-quality Dual-Optical Dataset)
format: Infrared-visible video dataset for fusion. Contains 24 multi-modal video sequences.
metric: EN, MI, SD, SSIM, VIF (fusion quality); flowD (temporal consistency)

name: TNO
format: Multi-band (infrared-visible) image dataset. Contains 3 multi-modal video sequences for fusion evaluation.
metric: EN, MI, SD, SSIM, VIF (fusion quality); flowD (temporal consistency)

name: INO
format: Infrared-visible video dataset for object tracking and fusion. Lower resolution dataset.

name: RoadScene
format: Infrared-visible image pairs for road scene fusion. Static image pairs (no temporal information).

name: MSRS
format: Multi-spectral street scene image pairs for fusion. Static image pairs (no temporal information).

name: M2FD
format: Multi-modal face dataset with infrared-visible image pairs. Includes disguise and occlusion scenarios.

name: LLVIP
format: Low-light visible-infrared pairs for fusion. Static images (no temporal information). Large-scale dataset.

name: FMB
format: Fusion Medical Benchmark dataset. Infrared-visible image pairs for medical/scientific fusion.
access: Released with FMB fusion benchmark paper

name: EchoNet-LVH
num_samples: ~10,000 PLAX (parasternal long axis) echocardiogram videos with left ventricular hypertrophy
format: Echocardiogram videos (PLAX view) with left ventricle tracings for ESV/EDV estimation and derived LVEF labels
notes: From the paper: used for PLAX view experiments in EchoFlow. EF estimated via Teichholz formula from left ventricle tracings.

name: TMED2
num_samples: Large collection of ultrasound images for semi-supervised classification (used in EchoFlow for A-VAE pretraining)
format: Ultrasound images from multiple vendors and modalities; used for A-VAE training in EchoFlow
notes: From Huang et al., DataPerf workshop at ICML 2022. EchoFlow uses TMED2 to increase A-VAE training data diversity, disregarding splits and labels.

name: BIRD
format: English questions paired with SQL queries across 70+ databases (train) and 37 databases (test); real-world SQL challenges with diverse schemas and noisy queries; evaluated by execution accuracy (exact row match)
metric: Execution Accuracy (EX) - exact row match between predicted and gold SQL execution results
notes: BIRD (Benchmarks for Interactive-driven Language-to-SQL). Introduced by Li et al. (NeurIPS 2023). Known for noisy/ambiguous queries requiring complex reasoning.

name: Spider-DK
format: Spider queries augmented with domain knowledge to reflect realistic paraphrasing; evaluated by execution accuracy
notes: Domain Knowledge augmented Spider. Tests robustness of Text-to-SQL models to realistic domain-specific paraphrasing.

name: Spider-Syn
format: Spider queries with schema-related synonyms replacing column/table names; evaluated by execution accuracy
notes: Synonym-altered Spider. Tests robustness of Text-to-SQL models to synonym substitution in schema elements.

name: 3DTeethSeg'22 (MICCAI Challenge)
format: 3D triangular meshes of upper and lower human jaws, segmented into 17 classes (16 teeth + gingiva/background)
metric: mIoU per tooth class, overall mIoU, boundary IoU

name: 3D-IOSSeg
num_samples: ~hundreds of intraoral scan models (exact number varies by split)
format: 3D intraoral scans of human teeth with fine-grained tooth segmentation labels

name: SEED-Bench-R1
storage: Training data from EpicKitchens; validation from EpicKitchens and Ego4D; not yet publicly released
format: Multiple-choice QA on egocentric videos requiring perception + reasoning; 16 frames at 252x252 per video

name: EgoPlan-Bench
format: Multiple-choice QA for multimodal LLM planning in egocentric scenarios; requires understanding task goals, tracking visual progress, and reasoning about next actions

name: EgoPlan-Bench2
format: Multiple-choice QA extending EgoPlan-Bench to broader domains (hobbies, recreation, work) using Ego4D videos; tests cross-environment and cross-task generalization

name: MMVP
num_samples: 150 CLIP blind-pairs testing fine-grained visual reasoning
format: Binary multiple-choice VQA pairs designed to expose visual shortcomings of CLIP-based VLMs; models must identify which of two images matches a text description

name: UniAttackData
format: Multi-modal face videos with physical attacks (Print, Replay) and digital attacks (6 editing + 6 adversarial methods); two protocols: Protocol 1 (all attacks seen) and Protocol 2 (leave-one-type-out for unseen attacks)
notes: Unified Physical-Digital Face Attack Detection dataset. Extends CASIA-SURF CeFA with digital forgery techniques. Protocol 2.1 tests generalization to unseen physical attacks, Protocol 2.2 to unseen digital attacks.

name: JFSFDB
format: Joint Face Spoofing and Forensic Detection Benchmark with 9 subsets; supports separate training (PA and DA independently) and joint training protocols for Presentation Attack (PA) and Deepfake Attack (DA)
access: Yu et al. 2024 - Benchmarking joint face spoofing and forgery detection with visual and physiological cues (IEEE TDSC 2024)
notes: Integrates multiple face spoofing and deepfake detection subsets. Joint protocol evaluates unified detection of both physical and digital attacks.

name: ISLES'22
storage: ~80GB (multi-modal 3D MRI DWI/ADC volumes for ischemic stroke lesion segmentation)
format: Multi-center MRI scans with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and ADC maps; expert-annotated ischemic stroke lesion masks
metric: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Hausdorff Distance 95th percentile (HD95)

name: GlaS
format: High-resolution H&E-stained histopathology images of colorectal cancer with expert-annotated gland segmentations; 2D images
metric: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Hausdorff Distance 95th percentile (HD95)

name: FIVES
storage: ~15GB (high-resolution fundus photographs with retinal vessel segmentation masks)
format: High-resolution fundus photographs with manual segmentation masks for retinal blood vessels; 2D color fundus images
metric: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Hausdorff Distance 95th percentile (HD95)

name: FB15k-237
format: Knowledge graph triples (head, relation, tail) with numeric literals for link prediction evaluation
access: Standard KGE benchmark repositories; literal-enriched version from LiteralE authors
notes: Subset of Freebase KB. Inverse relations removed. Enriched with numeric literals by LiteralE (2019). Used in ReaLitE paper (2504.00852).

name: YAGO15k
format: Knowledge graph triples (head, relation, tail) with numeric literals for link prediction evaluation
access: Standard KGE benchmark repositories; literal-enriched version from KGA authors
notes: Subset of YAGO KG. Higher quality numeric literals than FB15k-237. Used in ReaLitE paper (2504.00852).

name: kgbench
format: Multimodal KGs (dmgfull, dmg777k, mdgenre) with numeric and date literals for node classification
notes: Collection of multimodal KG datasets. Paper uses only numbers and dates converted to decimal format. Used in ReaLitE paper (2504.00852).

name: DDAD (Dense Depth for Autonomous Driving)
format: Urban driving videos with metric depth ground truth from LiDAR sensors; multiple camera views; more challenging than KITTI with greater depth range
notes: DDAD: Dense Depth for Autonomous Driving (Guizilini et al., CVPR 2020). Used in GeometryCrafter paper (2504.01016) for outdoor autonomous driving evaluation.

name: MONAKa (Flying Things)
format: Synthetic stereo RGB images with per-pixel disparity ground truth from rendered 3D scenes with flying objects; tests depth estimation in dynamic, colorful environments
notes: Part of the Flying Things 3D dataset (Mayer et al., CVPR 2016). Used in GeometryCrafter paper (2504.01016) for synthetic depth evaluation with challenging dynamic scenes.

name: GMU Kitchen
num_samples: RGB-D videos from 5 kitchen scenes with multiple object instances
format: Multi-view RGB-D dataset for object instance detection; contains annotated bounding boxes for objects in kitchen environments with depth from Kinect sensor
notes: GMU Kitchen (Georgakis et al., 3DV 2016). Used in GeometryCrafter paper (2504.01016) for indoor scene depth and point map evaluation.

name: CEBaB
format: Short restaurant reviews annotated with sentiment ratings at review level (positive/neutral/negative) and for four concept aspects: Good Food, Good Ambiance, Good Service, Good Noise

name: NaturalQuestions
format: Real user questions from Google search with answers from Wikipedia; requires both question answering and passage reading comprehension
notes: Used in DeepResearcher (2504.03160) as single-hop training and evaluation dataset.

name: PASCAL-5i
num_samples: 10,582 train + 1,449 val images (4 folds, 5 classes each)
eval_time: minutes to hours for full cross-validation
format: Derived from PASCAL VOC 2012 with SBD annotations. N-way K-shot few-shot segmentation with 20 semantic categories split into 4 folds.
access: Standard few-shot segmentation benchmark; PASCAL VOC 2012 available at http://host.robots.ox.ac.uk/pascal/VOC/, SBD at http://home.bharansk.com/
notes: Few-shot segmentation benchmark from Shaban et al. (2017). Used in CMaP-SAM paper (arXiv:2504.05049) achieving 71.1 mIoU (1-shot) and 76.3 mIoU (5-shot).

name: COCO-20i
num_samples: 82,081 train + 40,137 val images (4 folds, 20 classes each)
format: Derived from MS COCO with dense multi-instance annotations. N-way K-shot few-shot segmentation with 80 categories split into 4 folds.
notes: Few-shot segmentation benchmark from Nguyen & Todorovic (2019). More challenging than PASCAL-5i due to complex scenes, occlusions, and small objects. Used in CMaP-SAM paper (arXiv:2504.05049) achieving 56.1 mIoU (1-shot).

name: FSS-1000
format: Fine-grained few-shot segmentation dataset with 1000 classes, focusing on part-whole relationships. 1-way 1-shot and 5-shot protocols.
notes: Few-shot segmentation benchmark from Li et al. (CVPR 2020). High inter-class similarity and limited samples per category. Used in CMaP-SAM paper (arXiv:2504.05049).

name: ShanghaiTech Part_A
num_samples: 482 images (300 train, 182 test), 330165 annotated people total
format: Crowd images with head dot annotations; density map generation for training

name: ShanghaiTech Part_B
format: Crowd images captured at fixed camera angle with head dot annotations

name: UCF-QNRF
format: High-resolution crowd images with head dot/box annotations; density maps

name: NWPU-Crowd
num_samples: 5109 images (3109 train, 500 val, 1500 test), up to 20033 people per image
format: Crowd images with head dot annotations; negative samples included; 5 density level subsets (S0-S4)

name: SpaceR-151k
num_samples: ~151,000 QA pairs (91k spatial reasoning + 60k general multimodal understanding)
format: Video spatial reasoning QA dataset: 91k SR pairs derived from ScanNet v2 (6 task types: relative distance, relative direction, appearance order, object/room size, absolute distance, counting) with cognitive map annotations; 60k general multimodal samples for broader understanding. QA format with options, solutions, and spatial annotations.
notes: From SpaceR paper (arXiv:2504.01805). SR-91k subset excludes ScanNet scenes overlapping with VSI-Bench evaluation set.

name: NYU Comprehensive Mammography Dataset
num_samples: V1: ~496k exams (~938k breasts); V2: ~768k exams (~1.4M breasts)
storage: Estimated 50-100+ TB (high-res mammography with DBT slices)
format: Mammography images: FFDM, C-View synthetic 2D, DBT 3D volumes with pathology-confirmed cancer labels and bounding-box annotations
access: Not publicly available - contact authors for evaluation on test set
notes: Private dataset from NYU Langone Health. Used in Park et al. (2504.05636) for multi-modal mammography AI. Contains ~500k-768k screening/diagnostic exams with FFDM+C-View+DBT.

name: CMMD (Chinese Mammography Database)
format: FFDM mammography images with biopsy-confirmed breast-level labels (benign/malignant)
notes: CMMD (Cui et al., 2021). Used in Park et al. (2504.05636) for external validation of mammography AI.

name: OPTIMAM (OMI-DB)
format: FFDM mammography images (for-presentation) with clinical data from UK screening sites
notes: OPTIMAM mammography database (Halling-Brown et al., Radiology AI 2020). Restricted access. Used in Park et al. (2504.05636) for external validation.

name: CSAW-CC (Cohort of Screen-Aged Women)
num_samples: ~23,395 screening mammography studies (524 cancer, rest negative)
format: FFDM mammography images from Hologic scanners with cancer status labels
access: Contact Karolinska Institute for CSAW access
notes: CSAW-CC (Dembrower et al., 2020). Subset of larger CSAW dataset. Used in Park et al. (2504.05636) for external validation.

name: EMBED (Emory Breast Imaging Dataset)
num_samples: ~3.4M images from ~110k patients (paper used ~10k studies subset)
format: FFDM, C-View, DBT mammography images with BI-RADS labels
license: Restricted - requires access request; small subset on AWS Open Data
notes: EMBED dataset (Jeong et al., Radiology AI 2023). Used in Park et al. (2504.05636) for external validation with FFDM images.

name: CBIS-DDSM (Curated Breast Imaging Subset of DDSM)
format: Digitized film mammography images with bounding-box annotations for masses/calcifications
notes: CBIS-DDSM (Lee et al., 2017; Shen et al., 2019). Publicly available. Used in Park et al. (2504.05636) for external validation.

name: INbreast
num_samples: 115 exams (31 in test set used by paper)
format: Digital mammography images (FFDM) with biopsy-confirmed labels and bounding boxes
access: Contact Centro Hospitalar de S. João (Portugal) for access
notes: INbreast (Moreira et al., 2012). Digital mammography dataset. Used in Park et al. (2504.05636) for external validation.

name: BCS-DBT (Breast Cancer Screening-DBT)
format: DBT 3D volumes from Hologic Selenia Dimensions with bounding-box annotations for lesions
notes: BCS-DBT / DBTex challenge dataset (Buda et al., 2021; Konz et al., 2023). Publicly available on TCIA. Used in Park et al. (2504.05636) for external validation of DBT models.

name: SMDD (Synthetic Morphing Detection Dataset)
format: High-quality StyleGAN2-based synthetic face images with morphing attacks

name: FRGC-Morphs
format: Face morphing images (bona fide + morphs) with AMSL, FaceMorpher, OpenCV, StyleGAN2 variants

name: FERET-Morphs
format: Face morphing images from FERET dataset with multiple morphing methods

name: FRLL-Morphs
format: Face morphing images from Face Research Lab London dataset with AMSL, FaceMorpher, OpenCV, StyleGAN2, Webmorph

name: Morph-PIPE
format: Diffusion-based face morphing attacks using identity prior enhancement (Plug-in Identity Prior)

name: Greedy-DiM
format: Greedy algorithms for unreasonably effective face morphs using diffusion models

name: MorCode
format: GAN-based face morphing using generative codebooks with VQ-GAN and spherical interpolation

name: REFUGE (Retinal Fundus Glaucoma Challenge)
format: 2124x2056 retinal fundus images with optic disc and cup segmentation masks for glaucoma assessment
notes: Used in HER-Seg paper (2504.06205) for high-resolution retinal segmentation at 1024x1024.

name: PCXA (Chest X-ray Lung Segmentation)
num_samples: 704 chest X-ray images with lung masks
format: 4020x4892 chest X-rays with lung segmentation masks for tuberculosis screening
access: https://www.kaggle.com/c/rsna-pneumonia-detection-challenge/data or similar public chest X-ray repositories
notes: Used in HER-Seg paper (2504.06205) for high-resolution chest X-ray lung segmentation at 1024x1024.

name: UDIAT Breast Ultrasound
format: 760x570 breast ultrasound images with lesion segmentation masks
notes: Used in HER-Seg paper (2504.06205) for breast lesion segmentation evaluation.

name: DSB-2018 (Data Science Bowl 2018)
num_samples: 670 microscopic cell nuclei images (high resolution up to 1024x1024)
format: High-resolution microscopy images with nuclei instance segmentation masks; diverse staining protocols and imaging conditions
notes: 2018 Data Science Bowl nuclei segmentation challenge. Used in HER-Seg paper (2504.06205) for high-resolution cell nuclei segmentation at 1024x1024.

name: CVC-ColonDB
num_samples: 380 colonoscopy video frames with polyp masks
format: Colonoscopy frames with binary polyp segmentation masks; used for medical video segmentation evaluation
notes: Used in HER-Seg paper (2504.06205) for medical video segmentation evaluation alongside CVC-ClinicDB.

name: Natural Reasoning
format: Large-scale diverse reasoning questions from multiple domains (Physics, CS, Economics, Social Sciences, etc.) with reference answers. Used with filtering in EMPO (arXiv:2504.05812) for free-form natural reasoning training.
notes: Source: Yuan et al. arXiv:2502.13124. EMPO uses 18K filtered prompts after removing over-long/over-difficult samples.

name: Human3.6M
format: RGB video frames with 3D joint annotations (32 joints per frame); standard protocol uses subjects 1,5,6,7,8 for training and 9,11 for testing

name: MPI-INF-3DHP
num_samples: ~1.3M frames from multiple settings (green screen, non-green screen, outdoor)
format: RGB video frames with 3D joint annotations; multi-camera setup with varying environments

name: Omni3D
format: Large-scale 3D object detection benchmark aggregating KITTI, nuScenes, SUNRGBD, ARKitScenes, Objectron, Hypersim and more with unified 3D bounding box annotations
notes: Omni3D benchmark from Brazil et al. (CVPR 2023). Used as foundation for DA3D in DetAny3D (arXiv:2504.07958) which extends it with additional datasets.

name: Cityscapes3D
format: Urban street scenes with 3D bounding boxes for vehicles (9DoF: 3D center, dimensions, rotation). Subset of original Cityscapes with 3D annotations.
notes: Used as zero-shot dataset in DetAny3D (arXiv:2504.07958) for cross-dataset evaluation with novel camera configurations.

name: 3RScan
format: Indoor 3D scans with 3D bounding box annotations for multi-object detection and 3D visual grounding. Contains novel categories not in training sets.
notes: Used as zero-shot dataset in DetAny3D (arXiv:2504.07958) for cross-dataset evaluation with both novel camera configurations and novel object categories.

name: Digital Twin Catalog (DTC)
num_samples: 2,000 scanned 3D object models + 100 DSLR evaluation sequences + 200 egocentric Aria evaluation sequences
eval_time: hours per scene for inverse rendering baselines; minutes per scene for Gaussian splatting
format: 3D object digital twins with millimeter-level geometry accuracy, photorealistic PBR material maps, multiview HDR images, camera poses, environment maps, and egocentric Aria recordings with aligned 3D object poses
metric: PSNR-H, PSNR-L, SSIM, LPIPS, Depth, Normal, Shape Chamfer Distance
notes: From Meta Reality Labs Research & Stanford University (arXiv:2504.08541). Largest real-world 3D object digital twin dataset with PBR materials. Includes both DSLR and egocentric (Project Aria) evaluation data. Used for benchmarking inverse rendering, novel view synthesis, and robotic manipulation tasks.

name: Hellaswag
format: Multiple-choice commonsense reasoning (winograd-style) with 4 choices per question
notes: Used in SWAN-GPT paper (2504.08719) for standard LLM benchmark evaluation.

name: VISUALPUZZLES
eval_time: minutes to hours per model depending on size
format: Multiple-choice visual reasoning questions (image + text query) with image-based or text-based 4-option answers across 5 reasoning categories: algorithmic, analogical, deductive, inductive, spatial
notes: Multimodal reasoning benchmark from CMU NeuLab (arXiv:2504.10342). Designed to isolate reasoning from domain-specific knowledge. 82.1% of solution steps are logical reasoning steps (vs 71.5% on MMMU). Average knowledge concepts per question: 1.1 (vs 3.9 for MMMU).

name: SOTS-Outdoor
format: Synthetic hazy/clean outdoor image pairs (RESIDE benchmark, outdoor subset SOTS) for dehazing evaluation

name: Rain100L
format: Paired rainy/clean image dataset (100 pairs for training Rain100L, 100 for testing) for light rain removal

name: Snow100K
format: Large-scale snow removal dataset with 100K synthetic snow images (Snow100K-S small, Snow100K-L large snow streaks) for desnowing evaluation

name: WeatherBench
format: Real-world weather removal benchmark with 41,402 training and 600 test images covering rain, haze, snow, and combinations; captured under diverse real-world weather conditions

name: CDD-11
format: Composite Degradation Dataset with 11 types (single: l/h/r/s; composite: l+h, l+r, l+s, h+r, h+s, l+h+r, l+h+s) synthesized using physically-based rendering for evaluation on mixed degradations

name: AllWeather
format: Combined all-weather dataset from TransWeather paper (CVPR 2022) containing samples from Raindrop, Outdoor-Rain, and Snow100K for training all-weather removal models

name: GOT-10k
format: Video sequences with bounding box annotations for generic object tracking; one-shot tracking protocol

name: LaSOT
format: High-quality long-term tracking sequences with manual annotations; diverse object categories

name: TrackingNet
format: Large-scale tracking dataset with bounding box annotations; real-world videos

name: DTB70
format: UAV tracking sequences with occlusion and challenging maneuvers; manual bounding box annotations

name: UAVDT
format: UAV captured urban traffic scenes with bounding box annotations for car/pedestrian/truck; includes occlusion and blur challenges

name: VisDrone2018
format: UAV captured scenes with object detection and tracking annotations; includes pedestrians, vehicles, cyclists

name: UAV123
format: UAV tracking benchmark with high-altitude sequences; includes target disappearance/re-appearance challenges

name: CH-SIMS
format: Chinese multimodal sentiment analysis dataset with aligned text/audio/vision from movies, TV series, and variety shows; sentiment scores range from -1 (strongly negative) to +1 (strongly positive)
notes: Chinese MSA benchmark. Most balanced MSA dataset with only 3.72% modality performance gap. Uses OpenFace2.0 for visual features (709 features) and Librosa for audio features (33 features). Paper: Yu et al., ACL 2020.

name: Gigaword
format: News article first sentence (source) and headline (target) pairs for abstractive summarization

name: SMS Spam Collection
format: SMS texts labeled as ham or spam (CSV format)
notes: Standard SMS spam dataset. Paper uses it as spam detection task.

name: Jfleg
format: Sentence pairs with grammatically correct sentences and their GFL (Grammatical Error Correction) references
notes: Jfleg dataset for grammatical error correction. Paper uses it for grammar correction task evaluation.

name: ScreenSpot
num_samples: 1,272 instruction-screenshot pairs across Web, Desktop, Mobile
eval_time: minutes to hours for full sweep
format: UI screenshots with natural-language pointing instructions and pixel coordinates

name: UI-I2E-Bench
num_samples: 1,477 instruction-screenshot pairs from Web, Windows, Android
format: UI screenshots with natural-language instructions, element coordinates, and fine-grained annotations (element type, implicitness, element-to-screen ratio)
notes: Proposed benchmark by Microsoft Research for GUI instruction grounding. Designed to address limitations of ScreenSpot: lower element-to-screen ratio (0.042 vs 0.088), fine-grained element type annotations, and 63% implicit instructions. Enables detailed performance diagnostics.

name: MOTIF
num_samples: 30,699 screenshots with 320,219 instructions for mobile GUI grounding
format: Mobile UI screenshots with widget captions and interaction annotations for vision-language navigation
