notes: Interactive vision language navigation dataset for mobile GUI. Used as supplementary training data in UI-E2I-Synth paper (2504.11257) alongside AndroidControl for mobile GUI grounding training.

name: Widget-Caption
num_samples: 14,409 screenshots with 38,103 widget captions for mobile UI
format: Mobile UI screenshots with natural language captions describing UI elements
notes: Widget captioning dataset for mobile UI element description. Used as supplementary training data in UI-E2I-Synth paper (2504.11257) for mobile GUI grounding.

name: KnowUnDo
num_samples: Not fully disclosed (synthetic + real privacy/copyright data)
format: Privacy and copyright data with unlearn/retention splits: PU (Privacy Unlearn), PR (Privacy Retain), CU (Copyright Unlearn), CR (Copyright Retain)
metric: Unlearning Success, Retention Success, Perplexity, ROUGE-L

name: EgoExo4D
num_samples: ~1,400 hours egocentric + ~650 hours exocentric video from 888 unique skilled activities
format: First-and third-person video of skilled human activities with step, task, and verb/noun annotations; benchmarks include fine-grained keystep recognition, action anticipation

name: Assembly101
format: Egocentric and exocentric views of people assembling IKEA-style furniture; action steps, mistake annotations, 3D pose

name: Codeforces
num_samples: Recent 12 contests (used in Seed1.5-Thinking paper; specific count not publicly disclosed)
format: Competitive programming problems with official test cases; pass@1 and pass@8 metrics reported
access: https://codeforces.com (original platform); evaluation set to be publicly released by ByteDance Seed
notes: Distinct from CodeContests (DeepMind). Used by Seed1.5-Thinking for evaluating competitive programming ability.

name: Collie
num_samples: ~500+ prompts (from Doubao-1.5 Pro RL training data)
format: Instruction following evaluation covering diverse user scenarios
access: Not publicly available; referenced in Seed1.5-Thinking paper (arXiv:2504.13914)
notes: Used in Seed1.5-Thinking for evaluating non-reasoning task performance; not yet publicly released.

name: Aider Polyglot
num_samples: ~100-200 tasks across multiple languages (C++, Rust, Python, Go, JS, etc.)
format: Multi-language coding tasks with ground-truth tests; agent must implement solutions from scratch in single files
notes: Created by Paul Gauthier for evaluating Aider; tasks require understanding interplay between files across multiple programming languages.

name: CameraBench
format: Internet videos with camera motion annotations: binary labels for 50+ primitives, captions, VQA pairs
license: Research (YouTube Standard license for source videos)
notes: Large-scale benchmark for camera motion understanding in video. Developed taxonomy with cinematographers. Evaluates SfM/SLAM and Vision-Language Models. Fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL achieves 2x improvement over baselines.

name: AV-CIL-FFIA
storage: ~50-80GB (2-second video clips at 1920x1080 25fps + audio at 256kHz downsampled to 64kHz)
eval_time: hours for full incremental learning evaluation across 6 fish species
format: Synchronized audio-visual clips (2-second duration) of fish feeding behavior in real aquaculture tanks. Audio: mel spectrograms (128 mel bins, 2048 Hanning window, 1024 hop size). Video: 16 frames sampled from 2-second clips at 224x224 resolution. Labels: 4 feeding intensity levels (None, Weak, Medium, Strong) for 6 fish species (Tilapia, Black Perch, Jade Perch, Lotus Carp, Red Tilapia, Sunfish).
notes: First audio-visual class-incremental learning dataset for fish feeding intensity assessment. Introduced by HAIL-FFIA paper (arXiv:2504.15171). Collected in real aquaculture environments (Guangzhou, China). Pretrained encoders: S3D (Kinetics-400) for video, PANNs MobileNetV2 (AudioSet) for audio.

name: ZJUL5
format: RGB video + sparse ToF depth (8x8 = 64 points from VL53L5CX ToF sensor) + dense depth ground truth from Intel RealSense 435i; camera poses and 3D meshes via ScanNet protocol
notes: Only public dataset with real sparse ToF sensor data at extremely low resolution (64 points). Provides real measurement noise and outliers not present in synthetic datasets. Used as primary evaluation dataset in ToF-Splatting paper.

name: NAS-Bench-201
num_samples: CIFAR-10: 10K train/10K test, CIFAR-100: 10K/10K, ImageNet-16-120: 151K train/3K test per architecture
format: Precomputed accuracy metrics for ~15,700 CNN architectures on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet-16-120 with fixed search space (4 nodes, 6 edges, 8 operations)
notes: NAS benchmark by Dong & Yang (CVPR 2019). Evaluates DARTS-derived architectures in a fixed search space. Allows fast architecture comparison without full training.

name: nuImages
format: RGB images from 6 cameras with 2D bounding boxes, instance masks, depth, and semantic maps for 23 object categories
metric: mAP (COCO-style) for object detection, mAP for instance segmentation

name: LoveDA
format: Aerial/satellite RGB images with pixel-level land cover annotations (Building, Road, Water, Barren, Forest, Agriculture, Background)
notes: NeurIPS 2021 dataset. Includes urban and rural scenes from multiple Chinese cities. Used for domain adaptive semantic segmentation.

name: Potsdam
format: ISPRS 2D Semantic Labeling Challenge. 5cm GSD aerial images with pixel-level annotations (Impervious Surface, Building, Low Vegetation, Tree, Car, Clutter/Background)
metric: mIoU, Overall Accuracy, mF1, F1 per class
notes: ISPRS benchmark dataset for urban remote sensing semantic segmentation. Potsdam, Germany. Known for fine-grained urban land cover with high intra-class variability.

name: ProteinGym
format: Deep mutational scanning (DMS) substitution assays with fitness scores

name: DisProt
format: Protein disorder annotations (Intrinsically Disordered Regions)

name: RCSB PDB
format: Experimental protein 3D structures (X-ray crystallography, Cryo-EM, NMR)

name: SCOPE (Synthetic COllective Perception)
storage: ~50-100GB (synthetic CARLA data with 3 LiDAR sensors per CAV: HDL64, VLP32, Blickfeld CUBE)
format: Synthetic LiDAR point clouds + 3D bounding box annotations (Car, Van, Pedestrian, Cyclist, Motorbike) in CARLA simulator with improved physical LiDAR model. Each CAV equipped with 3 different LiDAR sensors.
metric: Average Precision (AP) at IoU 0.7 (Car/Van) and IoU 0.5 (Pedestrian/Cyclist/Motorbike)
access: Gamerdinger et al. 2024, IEEE ITSC 2024; https://www.figure-eight.com/scope/
notes: First V2V CP dataset with heterogeneous sensor setups per CAV. Enables systematic study of Sensor2Sensor domain adaptation in collective perception. Multiple LiDAR types per CAV: Velodyne HDL64 (64-layer 360°), Velodyne VLP32 (32-layer 360°), Blickfeld CUBE (52-line solid-state, 70°x30° FoV).

name: VTAB
eval_time: minutes to hours on single GPU
format: Images at varied resolutions (typically 224x224); 50 classes across 5 domains (natural, structured, medical, etc.)

name: PRM800K
format: Math problems with model-generated solutions and human-verified step-level correctness labels from OpenAI's 'Let's Verify Step by Step' (Lightman et al. 2023). Used to train discriminative and generative PRMs.
notes: PRM800K refers to the full dataset with ~712K step labels across ~12K problems. PRM12K is the subset of 12K problems.

name: Math-Shepherd
format: Math problems with step-level process supervision labels obtained via Monte Carlo rollouts. Each step is labeled as correct/incorrect based on whether it leads to the correct final answer.
notes: Used as an alternative to human-annotated step labels for training PRMs. Wang et al., 2023.

name: S-Up3D (Synthetic Up3D)
format: 2D/3D human keypoint coordinates; orthographic projection; ~79 keypoints per sample

name: DeformingThings4D
num_samples: 4 sequences (bull, fox, puma, lioness) with 25-100 frames each; 100 keypoints per frame after downsampling
format: Animated mesh keypoints with 3D ground truth; perspective camera; synthetic animals and humans

name: ZJU-Mocap/RTH
num_samples: ~500 frames per sequence; 100 keypoints per frame; multiple subjects (ZJU-377, ZJU-386, ZJU-387)
format: Multiview synchronized video; 3D keypoints from Neural Body (Peng et al. 2021); perspective camera

name: LVBench
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed; paper mentions video-level and clip-level corpora from long videos
eval_time: Hours for full evaluation with video understanding
format: Questions over long-form or complete videos requiring fine-grained temporal understanding; answers require localized video segments
access: https://github.com/WEst聊聊/LVBench (based on Wang et al., 2025a)
notes: From Wang et al., 2025a (LVBench paper). Used in UniversalRAG (2504.20734) for video RAG evaluation. Queries require retrieval from either full videos or short clips depending on question complexity.

name: MRAG-Bench
format: Vision-centric evaluation for retrieval-augmented multimodal models; queries require image retrieval and understanding
notes: From Hu et al., 2025 (MRAG-Bench paper). Used in UniversalRAG (2504.20734) for image RAG evaluation.

name: VideoRAG-Wiki
num_samples: Not specified; derived from Wikipedia video content
format: Video QA grounded on long-form or complete Wikipedia videos; queries require video retrieval and comprehension
notes: From Jeong et al., 2025 (VideoRAG paper). Used in UniversalRAG (2504.20734) for video RAG evaluation at the full-video granularity level.

name: VideoRAG-Synth
format: Video QA grounded on synthetic videos; queries require video retrieval and comprehension
notes: From Jeong et al., 2025 (VideoRAG paper). Used in UniversalRAG (2504.20734) for video RAG evaluation on synthetic video content.

name: 3DSRBench
num_samples: 2,772 manually annotated VQA pairs across 12 question types
format: Visual question-answering with multiple-choice format for 3D spatial reasoning; questions on height, location, orientation, multi-object relationships
notes: First comprehensive 3D spatial reasoning benchmark for LVLMs. Human-collected VQA data avoiding spurious 2D correlations. Includes height, location, orientation, and multi-object spatial relationship questions.

name: CVBench-3D
num_samples: Part of Cambrian-1 benchmark (thousands of questions)
format: 3D spatial reasoning questions (depth and distance) for evaluating LVLMs
notes: Subset of CVBench benchmark focused on 3D spatial reasoning. Includes depth estimation and distance comparison questions. Used in Cambrian-1 paper (Tong et al., NeurIPS 2024).

name: TMBench
num_samples: 100 instances (main config: alphabet size 5, m=2, max 30 steps)
format: m-Tag system simulation: given production rules and initial queue, predict step-by-step queue states until halt or max steps
metric: Step Accuracy, Step-Weighted Accuracy (SWA), Pass Rate

name: CLIPBenchmark
storage: Varies by dataset (ImageNet, CIFAR, VTAB, etc.)
format: Zero-shot classification and retrieval tasks across 41 diverse datasets including: ImageNet-1K, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, STL-10, CIFAR-10/100, Birds, Cars, Flowers, Pets, Food101, FGVC-Aircraft, EuroSAT, SVHN, GTSRB, Rendered SST2, MSCOCO, Flickr30K, and VTAB subsets
notes: Comprehensive CLIP evaluation benchmark from LAION. Used in CATransformers (Wang et al., 2025) to evaluate CarbonCLIP models. Covers diverse vision-language tasks including zero-shot classification, retrieval, and structured VTAB tasks.

name: CXR-ClinEval
num_samples: ~100 cases (human evaluation); full benchmark size not disclosed
format: Multi-label pathology detection (14 thoracic pathologies + 5 critical), radiology report generation, VQA, differential diagnosis ranking. Input: structured textual CXR representations + clinical instructions. Output: free-text reports, VQA answers, ranked diagnoses.
metric: Macro F1, Micro F1, Report Score (BERTScore + ROUGE-L), VQA Accuracy, MRR
license: Not specified — paper does not release evaluation data
access: Not publicly available — paper-specific benchmark from 2505.01711
notes: Evaluation benchmark used in CXR-TextInter paper (2505.01711). Covers pathology detection, report generation, VQA, and differential diagnosis. Human evaluation by 3 board-certified radiologists on 100 blinded cases.

name: MediInstruct-CXR
format: Instruction-tuning dataset with structured textual chest X-ray representations (T_img) paired with clinically-relevant instruction-response pairs. T_img captures entities, attributes, anatomical locations, and spatial relationships.
access: Not publicly available — paper does not release training data or code
notes: Training dataset used in CXR-TextInter paper (2505.01711). Contains structured text representations of chest X-rays generated by an upstream image-to-text pipeline (f_img2text), not raw images. Availability is unclear — paper does not mention data release.

name: Real-Edit
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed (from MultiReward paper, uses Unsplash images)
format: High-resolution images from Unsplash community with single-turn editing instructions, evaluated via GPT-4o
metric: Following (accuracy + score 0-5), Preserving (accuracy + score 0-5), Quality (accuracy + score 0-5)
notes: Human-aligned evaluation benchmark for instruction-based image editing from MultiReward (ICLR 2025). Uses GPT-4o for automated scoring. The SuperEdit paper evaluates on this benchmark and reports 69.7% overall accuracy and 3.91 overall score.

name: 3DIEBench
format: 3D object renderings (256x256, resized to 128x128) with variations in rotation (SO(3)), floor hue, and lighting. Supports evaluation of invariance (classification) and equivariance (rotation/color prediction).
notes: 3D Invariant Equivariant Benchmark from Garrido et al., 2023. Used in seq-JEPA (2505.03176) for joint evaluation of invariance and equivariance in SSL representations.

name: Tourism
num_samples: 89 total (56 bottom-level, 33 aggregated), 4 hierarchy levels, 36 observations per series
format: Australian tourism hierarchical time series: quarterly visitor nights across regions/states; standard hierarchical forecasting benchmark from Nixtla/statsforecast
notes: Standard hierarchical forecasting benchmark. Used in FlowRec paper (arXiv:2505.03955) for evaluating hierarchical forecast reconciliation methods.

name: Tourism-L
num_samples: 555 total (76,304 bottom-level aggregated to 175), 4-5 hierarchy levels, 228 observations
format: Large-scale Australian tourism hierarchical time series with grouped structure; standard hierarchical forecasting benchmark from Nixtla/statsforecast
notes: Larger version of Tourism benchmark. Used in FlowRec paper (arXiv:2505.03955).

name: Labour
num_samples: 57 total (32 bottom-level, 25 aggregated), 4 hierarchy levels, 514 observations
format: Australian labour force hierarchical time series; standard hierarchical forecasting benchmark from Nixtla/statsforecast
notes: Australian labour force data. Standard hierarchical forecasting benchmark. Used in FlowRec paper (arXiv:2505.03955).

name: Wiki
num_samples: 199 total (150 bottom-level, 49 aggregated), 5 hierarchy levels, 366 observations
format: Wikipedia article views hierarchical time series with hierarchical structure across article categories; standard hierarchical forecasting benchmark from Nixtla/statsforecast
notes: Wikipedia page views with hierarchical aggregation. Standard hierarchical forecasting benchmark. Used in FlowRec paper (arXiv:2505.03955).

name: GRES
format: Satellite/aerial images (512x512) with natural language reasoning segmentation queries and pixel-level segmentation masks
notes: Geospatial Reasoning Segmentation dataset: semi-synthetic dataset for reasoning segmentation in remote sensing. Built from xView dataset using GPT-4o for query generation and GeoSAM for mask generation. Train/val/test splits: 7,205/500/1,500 images.

name: PreGRES
format: Aggregated remote sensing datasets for VLM pre-training: image captioning (NWPU-Captions, RSICD, RSITMD, Sydney-Captions, UCM-Captions), VQA (RSVQA-LR, RSVQA-HR, FloodNet, RSIVQA), visual grounding (DIOR-RSVG), scene classification (NWPU-RESISC45)
notes: PreGRES: pre-training dataset for LISAT, aggregated from existing remote sensing datasets for multimodal geospatial instruction tuning.

name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
format: Multilingual speech corpus derived from LibriSpeech audiobook recordings, expanded to 8 languages (English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Polish)
notes: From Pratap et al. (Interspeech 2020). Used in Miipher-2 paper for multilingual speech restoration evaluation on known languages (MLS test sets).

name: M4
format: Multi-generator, multi-domain, multilingual black-box machine-generated text detection benchmark. Covers 5 domains (News, Story, Review, Code, Scientific) and 7 base models. Texts generated via API-based and open-source LLMs.
access: https://github.com/YuxiaWW/M4 (M4 paper: Wang et al., EACL 2024)

name: MAGE
format: Machine-generated text detection in the wild. Covers 10 domains and 9 base models including GPT-2, ChatGPT, GPT-4, etc. Tests detection under realistic distribution shifts.
access: https://github.com/YafuLi/MAGE (MAGE paper: Li et al., ACL 2024)

name: RealDet
format: Large-scale bilingual (Chinese/English) MGT detection benchmark. Spans 15 textual domains, 22 popular LLMs (black-box and white-box), and includes adversarial texts with paraphrasing and editing attacks. Designed for realistic calibration and superior detection performance.

name: DeepCAD
format: Command sequences representing sketch-and-extrude CAD construction process. Each model is a sequence of parametric commands (Line, Arc, Circle, SOL, Extrude, EOS).

name: Text2CAD
format: DeepCAD models annotated with multiple levels of natural language descriptions (from abstract shape summaries to detailed parametric instructions).

name: Text-to-CadQuery
format: Text2CAD dataset further annotated with executable CadQuery Python code. Generated using Gemini 2.0 Flash with self-correction feedback loop.

name: GENBOT-1K
num_samples: 1,012 procedurally generated robot embodiments (348 humanoids, 332 quadrupeds, 332 hexapods)
format: Procedurally generated robot descriptions with variations in topology (number of knee joints), geometry (link dimensions, body size), and kinematics (joint types, range of motion). Each embodiment is defined as a triplet: G (topology), T (geometry), K (kinematics). Used to study embodiment scaling laws for cross-embodiment robot locomotion generalization.
notes: Dataset introduced in the embodiment scaling laws paper (arXiv:2505.05753). Train/test split: 817 training / 195 held-out embodiments. Sim-to-real transfer demonstrated on Unitree Go2 quadruped and Unitree H1 humanoid.

name: Adience
format: Face images with age category labels; 5-fold cross-validation splits
metric: Accuracy, MAE, Precision, Recall, F1-score (macro average)

name: Flickr-Aesthetics
num_samples: 13706 images from Flickr, rated 1-5 by multiple evaluators
format: Images with median aesthetic rating (1=unacceptable to 5=exceptional); highly imbalanced (65.6% class 3); 5-fold CV
metric: Accuracy, MAE, Precision, Recall, F1-score (macro average)

name: EyePACS-Diabetic-Retinopathy
num_samples: 35126 high-resolution fundus images, 5 DR severity levels (no DR, mild, moderate, severe, proliferative)
format: Fundus images with DR severity labels (0-4); highly imbalanced (73.5% class 0); 10-fold subject-independent CV
metric: Accuracy, MAE, Precision, Recall, F1-score (macro average)

name: VidVRD
format: Video visual relationship detection: videos with triplet <subject, relationship, object> annotations and bounding box trajectories over time. Relationships include actions (e.g., 'riding', 'following'), spatial relations (e.g., 'in front of'), and comparisons (e.g., 'taller than').
metric: mAP (relationship detection), Recall@K, mAP_o (object trajectory detection)

name: VidOR
format: Large-scale video visual relationship detection dataset: videos with triplet <subject, relationship, object> annotations and bounding box trajectories. Similar to VidVRD but significantly larger in scale, covering more object and relationship categories.
metric: mAP (relationship detection), Recall@K, mAP_o (object trajectory detection)

name: NELL
format: Knowledge graph triples (head, relation, tail) for few-shot link prediction. Extracted from Never-Ending Language Learning project. Standard benchmark for few-shot KG completion.

name: FB15K-237
format: Knowledge graph triples (head, relation, tail) for link prediction. Subset of FB15K with inverse relations removed to prevent data leakage. Standard benchmark for KG completion.

name: RICH
num_samples: ~14K samples (RGB images + 3D human bodies + scene meshes)
format: RGB images paired with 3D human bodies (SMPL format) and 3D scene meshes. Captured in controlled indoor environments. Used for training and evaluating dense 3D human-scene contact estimation.
notes: RICH dataset from Huang et al. (CVPR 2022): Capturing and Inferring Dense Full-Body Human-Scene Contact. Used in GRACE paper (arXiv:2505.06575) as one of the primary training and evaluation datasets for HSI task.

name: DAMON
format: RGB images of natural human-scene interactions in the wild with 3D human body and scene annotations. Released with DECO paper for in-the-wild HSI estimation.
notes: DAMON dataset from Tripathi et al. (ICCV 2023): DECO — Dense Estimation of 3D Human-Scene Contact In The Wild. Used in GRACE paper (arXiv:2505.06575) as primary training dataset.

name: 3DIR
format: 3D human-object interaction data with both indoor and outdoor scenes, including multi-object interaction scenarios.
notes: 3DIR dataset from Yang et al. (LEMON, arXiv:2312.08963). Used in GRACE paper (arXiv:2505.06575) for HOI task evaluation. Contains natural scenes with multi-object interactions.

name: PROX
format: RGB-D images of humans in 3D indoor scenes with SMPL-X body fits and manual contact annotations. Used for human pose and shape (HPS) estimation with scene constraints.
notes: PROX (Progressives) dataset from Hassan et al. (ICCV 2019): Resolving 3D Human Pose Ambiguities with 3D Scene Constraints. Used in GRACE paper (arXiv:2505.06575) for downstream HPS regression task evaluation.

name: TUAB
num_samples: 26846 clinical EEG recordings (247728 train, 12315 val, 12277 test)
format: Clinical EEG recordings at 256Hz+ with 23 channels, binary classification (normal vs abnormal)
notes: Temple University EEG Corpus - Abnormal EEG detection. Part of TUH EEG corpus. Used in ALFEE paper as evaluation benchmark.

name: TUEV
format: EEG artifact detection with 6 classes: periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges, generalized periodic epileptiform discharges, spike/sharp wave discharges, artifacts, eye movements, and other events
metric: Balanced Accuracy, Cohen's Kappa, Weighted F1
notes: Temple University EEG Volume - artifact detection. Part of TUH EEG corpus. Used in ALFEE paper.

name: TUSL
num_samples: 222 train, 43 val, 25 test sessions (very small dataset)
format: Seizure detection with 3 classes: seizure, slowing, complex background (21-22 channels)
metric: Balanced Accuracy, Cohen's Kappa, Weighted F1
notes: Temple University Seizure Localization. Very small dataset - tests model's ability to handle limited data. Used in ALFEE paper.

name: SEED
format: Emotion recognition from EEG (60 channels, 10s trials) with 3 classes: positive, neutral, negative emotions
metric: Balanced Accuracy, Cohen's Kappa, Weighted F1
notes: SJTU Emotion EEG Dataset. Emotion recognition from physiological signals. Used in ALFEE paper. Also known as SEED-III.

name: HMC
format: Sleep staging with 5 classes (W, N1, N2, N3, REM) from 4-channel EEG
metric: Balanced Accuracy, Cohen's Kappa, Weighted F1
notes: HMC Sleep Dataset - Montreal Archive of Sleep Studies. Whole-night polysomnographic recordings. Used in ALFEE paper.

name: Workload
format: Mental workload estimation from EEG (19 channels) during mental serial subtraction task, binary classification
notes: Mental workload estimation during arithmetic tasks. Very small dataset - 36 subjects. Used in ALFEE paper.

name: TUEG
format: Large-scale clinical EEG corpus from Temple University Hospital. 60 channels, various durations.
notes: Temple University EEG Corpus (TUEC) - part of pretraining data for ALFEE (25,000 hours total pretraining).

name: BCIC-1A
format: Motor imagery EEG (left hand, right hand, foot) from 43 channels at 1000Hz, 9 subjects
notes: Part of ALFEE pretraining datasets (15 datasets totaling 25,000 hours).

name: SEED-IV
format: Emotion recognition EEG (60 channels, 10s trials) with 4 classes: happy, sad, fear, neutral
notes: Part of ALFEE pretraining. SEED-IV with 4 emotion classes.

name: UCR Time Series Archive
eval_time: minutes to hours per dataset depending on size
format: Univariate time series files (variable length), train/test splits provided

name: PKU PosterLayout
format: E-commerce poster images with text, logo, underlay layout element annotations in bounding box format. Cross-modal image-layout pairs for content-aware layout generation.
metric: Overlay, Alignment, Underlay effectiveness, Non-salient space utilization, Salient space occlusion, Readability (lower is better for most)

name: CGL
format: E-commerce poster dataset with text, logo, underlay, embellishment layout elements. Used in CGL-GAN paper for content-aware layout generation.
metric: Overlay, Alignment, Underlay effectiveness, Content metrics (utilization, occlusion, readability)
access: Available upon request or from original CGL-GAN authors

name: PStylish7
format: Multi-purpose poster dataset covering 7 categories (Paint, Poem, Metro, Movie, Menu, Animal, Instagram) and 8 element types including shape-variant elements (rectangles, ellipses, curves, polygons). First dataset for generalized content-aware layout generation with diverse design intents.
metric: Overlay, Intent coverage, Conflict, Utilization, Occlusion

name: GFIE
num_samples: ~71K frames (59K train, 6K val, 6K test) from 61 subjects
format: Gaze-following in indoor environments dataset. In-the-wild video sequences from indoor locations. Wide range of activities (writing, moving objects, using devices). 360-degree gaze coverage.
notes: Used in DHECA-SuperGaze paper (arXiv:2505.08426). 61 subjects, indoor scenes only, narrower gaze distribution than Gaze360.

name: Waterbench
num_samples: ~6 datasets (Knowledge Understanding, Knowledge Memorization, Finance QA, Longform QA, Multi-news, LCC)
format: Text generation prompts across QA, summarization, and generation tasks with GM (generation metric) and PPL (perplexity) evaluation

name: HEVC
num_samples: Multiple test sequences in Class B (1920x1080), C (832x480), D (416x240), E (1280x720)
format: Standard test video sequences for video compression; Classes B-E with varying resolutions; used in JCT-VC standardization work
metric: BD-Rate (%) vs VTM reference software, PSNR, MS-SSIM

name: MCL-JCV
format: JCT-VC test sequences with 8-bit and 10-bit versions; primarily 1920x1080 resolution; human visual quality judgments

name: Vimeo-90K
format: High-quality video clips from Vimeo; commonly used for video processing tasks including video compression, frame interpolation, super-resolution; training split standard in video compression literature

name: BVI-AOM
format: Video dataset for deep video compression optimization; contains diverse content with varying motion and texture complexity; developed for training learned video compression models

name: HDRTV4K
format: 4K HDR images in BT.2020/PQ1000 encoding with 8 SDR degradation types for SDR-to-HDR evaluation
metric: PSNR / SSIM / HDR-VDP3 / EHL / FHLP / EWG / FWGP

name: HDRTV1K
format: 4K HDR images in BT.2020/PQ1000 encoding for evaluating generalization to unknown SDR degradation types

name: MMHPSD
num_samples: unclear (largest dataset offering both videos and event streams with annotated 3D poses)
format: Video clips and event streams with annotated 3D poses using SMPL body model; supports both video and event-based pose tracking; train/test split provided
license: research use only (from Zou et al. 2021)
access: Refer to original paper: Zou et al., EventHPE: Event-based 3D Human Pose and Shape Estimation, ICCV 2021

name: CityScapes
num_samples: 3000 train + 500 val high-resolution images with pixel-level semantic annotations
storage: ~500MB (fine annotations) to ~10GB (full dataset with coarse annotations)
format: Urban driving scenes with 19 semantic categories; pixel-level segmentation masks; high-resolution (1024x2048) frames

name: MIT-States
format: Images with state-object composition labels (e.g., 'tall building', 'green tree')

name: UT-Zappos
format: Images of shoes with fine-grained attribute-object compositions (12 objects x 16 states)

name: C-GQA
format: Images with attribute-object compositions based on GQA dataset (870 objects x 453 states)

name: TweetEval
format: Tweets labeled for various tasks: emoji, emotion, hate, irony, offensive, sentiment, stance detection

name: LIAR
format: Short statements from politifact.com labeled for truthfulness (6 classes: pants-fire, false, barely-true, half-true, mostly-true, true)

name: HateCheck
format: Functional test suite for hate speech detection models with diverse hate speech templates and non-hateful counterparts

name: Ethos
format: Multi-label hate speech detection dataset with hate/non-hate binary labels and intensity scores

name: ArSarcasm
format: Tweets labeled for sarcasm and sentiment in Arabic and English

name: SALICON
format: COCO images with mouse-tracking fixation data as gaze proxy; fixation locations and duration
notes: SALICON dataset (Huang et al., ICCV 2015). Mouse-tracking as proxy for eye-tracking on COCO images. Used for pretraining in arXiv:2505.10169. Largest saliency dataset for model pretraining.

name: MIT1003
format: Natural images with eye-tracking fixation data; MIT300 is the test set
notes: MIT1003 saliency dataset (Judd et al., ICCV 2009). Standard benchmark for saliency prediction. MIT300 (test set) is part of MIT/Tuebingen Saliency Benchmark. Used in arXiv:2505.10169 for training and evaluation.

name: CAT2000
format: Natural images across 24 categories with eye-tracking fixations
notes: CAT2000 saliency dataset (Borji & Itti, CVPR 2015). Part of MIT/Tuebingen Saliency Benchmark. Used in arXiv:2505.10169 for training and evaluation.

name: COCO-Freeview
format: COCO images with free-viewing eye-tracking fixation data
notes: COCO-Freeview saliency dataset (Chen et al., CVPR 2022). Part of MIT/Tuebingen Saliency Benchmark. Used in arXiv:2505.10169 for training and evaluation.

name: DAEMONS
format: Natural driving scene images with eye-tracking fixation data
notes: DAEMONS dataset (Schwetlick et al., Frontiers in Psychology 2024). Potsdam dataset of eye movements on natural scenes, driving scenarios. Used in arXiv:2505.10169 for training and cross-dataset generalization analysis.

name: FIGRIM
format: Magazine images with eye-tracking fixations during image re-identification task
notes: FIGRIM saliency dataset (Bylinskii et al., Vision Research 2015). Eye movements during image re-identification task on magazine images. Used in arXiv:2505.10169 for training and cross-dataset generalization analysis. First presentation of each image treated as freeviewing data.

name: CAD-120
format: RGB-D activity recognition dataset with 3D human activities and object affordances. Contains indoor scenes with daily activities (making cereal, taking medicine, etc.). Used for cross-dataset generalization testing in GA3CE paper.
notes: Used in GA3CE paper (arXiv:2505.10671) for evaluating generalization to unseen scenes with different camera settings. Ground truth gaze targets are visible in images.

name: GAFA
format: Gaze-from-afar dataset with temporal eye-head-body coordination. Subjects move freely searching for objects. More challenging than GFIE - less frequent object interaction, gaze targets may not be visible. Lacks depth maps.
metric: 3D MAE and 2D MAE (angular error in degrees)
notes: Used in GA3CE paper (arXiv:2505.10671). Single-frame setting tested with zero-shot depth estimation (ZoeDepth). More challenging scenarios with backward-facing subjects, distant subjects, extreme camera angles.

name: FEMNIST
format: Handwritten character and digit images (28x28), naturally partitioned by writer; 62 classes (letters+digits); used in federated learning benchmarks (LEAF)

name: TinyMem
format: Synthetic multiplicative math sequences: max context length 150 tokens, 5 tasks (multiply-by-2, -by-4, -by-6, -by-8, -by-10), 32k train + 1k test per task
access: Generated synthetically per specification in Sakarvadia et al. 2025 (TinyMem paper, arXiv:2501.04513)
notes: From Sakarvadia et al. 2025 (arXiv:2505.11760). Language modeling benchmark for multiplicative math sequences. OOD data created via backdoor trigger on random trigger token sequence.

name: CoreLogic Loan-Level Market Analytics
num_samples: 117,523 loans, ~5M loan-month transitions (filtered subset from 4 ZIP codes in greater LA area)
storage: ~870GB raw full dataset; filtered subset used in paper: ~5-10GB
format: Month-by-month mortgage transition data with 52 features: FICO score, loan balance, interest rate, delinquency status, ZIP code, and macroeconomic indicators. Train/val/test split: 1/1994-6/2009, 7/2009-12/2009, 1/2010-12/2022.
notes: Proprietary mortgage data used in Set-Sequence paper (arXiv:2505.11243). Requires direct license from CoreLogic. Paper uses filtered subset from 4 ZIP codes: 92677 (Orange County), 93065 (Simi Valley), 91709 (Chino Hills), 92336 (Fontana).

name: Synthetic Contagion Task
num_samples: 1000 exchangeable units, 100 time steps, multiple samples
format: Binary features x in {0,1}, 3-state Markov chain with absorbing state (default). Default rate driven by latent factor lambda_t with contagion dynamics: lambda_{x,t+1} = beta * lambda_{x,t} + alpha * N_{x,t}. Parameters: mu=0.001, alpha=4, beta=0.5. Train on variable number of units (1-1000) with log-uniform sampling.
metric: AUC (absorbing state), KL divergence (true vs predicted transition probabilities)
access: Self-generated; parameters described in arXiv:2505.11243 Section 5 and Appendix E
notes: Custom synthetic benchmark mimicking loan default prediction with latent cross-sectional contagion effects. Used to evaluate Set-Sequence model (arXiv:2505.11243) against sequence baselines (LongConv, S4, H3, Transformer, Hyena) and Kalman Filter oracle.

name: NovelQA
format: Multiple-choice QA from novels (88 novels), contexts exceed 200K tokens

name: Marathon
format: Multiple-choice QA with 6 task types, contexts average 100K characters (some >260K)

name: Tiny-ImageNet
format: 256x256 RGB crops from 200 ImageNet subclasses; used in federated continual learning benchmarks (Si-Blurry task partitioning)

name: gRefCOCO
format: Generalized referring expressions for multi-object grounding (train/val/testA/testB)

name: LISA++
num_samples: ~3.3k reasoning segmentation samples over COCO images
format: Reasoning segmentation with complex textual queries requiring multi-step visual reasoning, extends LISA with more diverse expressions

name: ReasonSeg
num_samples: ~1.5k reasoning segmentation samples (979 val + test splits)
format: Reasoning-intensive referring expression segmentation requiring multi-step visual reasoning

name: CountBench
format: Visual counting with natural language queries requiring reasoning about object quantities

name: PixMo-Count
format: Point-based counting with natural language queries (from Molmo/PixMo paper)

name: WIKIDYK
format: Question-Answer pairs (reliability, generality, paraphrase, portability, locality)

name: TUPAC-16
format: Breast cancer H&E whole-slide images with tumor proliferation scores (based on Ki-67 labeling) for MIL regression
notes: Tumor Proliferation Assessment Challenge 2016. Predicting tumor proliferation scores from WSIs. Used in ALTER paper (arXiv:2505.12711) for cancer subtyping.

name: UBC-OCEAN
num_samples: 527 ovarian cancer WSIs from 20+ medical centers
format: Ovarian cancer H&E whole-slide images with 5 histotype labels (high-grade serous, clear-cell, endometrioid, low-grade serous, mucinous) for MIL classification
notes: OCEAN AI Challenge for ovarian cancer histotype diagnosis. Used in ALTER paper (arXiv:2505.12711) for cancer subtyping.

name: PatchGastricADC22
format: H&E gastric adenocarcinoma endoscopic biopsy WSIs with diagnostic captions extracted from pathology reports; patches paired with text descriptions for image-to-text generation
notes: Tsuneki & Kanavati, 2022. Used in ALTER paper (arXiv:2505.12711) for WSI report generation task.

name: TCGA-UCEC
format: TCGA uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma H&E WSIs with RNA-Seq gene expression and survival outcome data for survival prediction
notes: Subset of TCGA used in ALTER paper (arXiv:2505.12711) for survival prediction. Requires GDC access.

name: TCGA-STAD
format: TCGA stomach adenocarcinoma H&E WSIs with RNA-Seq gene expression and survival outcome data for survival prediction
notes: Subset of TCGA used in ALTER paper (arXiv:2505.12711) for survival prediction.

name: TCGA-KIRP
num_samples: 284 WSI-omic pairs (kidney renal papillary cell carcinoma)
format: TCGA kidney renal papillary cell carcinoma H&E WSIs with RNA-Seq gene expression and survival outcome data for survival prediction
notes: Subset of TCGA used in ALTER paper (arXiv:2505.12711) for survival prediction.

name: TCGA-KIRC
num_samples: 218 WSI-omic pairs (kidney renal clear cell carcinoma)
format: TCGA kidney renal clear cell carcinoma H&E WSIs with RNA-Seq gene expression and survival outcome data for survival prediction
notes: Subset of TCGA used in ALTER paper (arXiv:2505.12711) for survival prediction.

name: TCGA-LUAD
num_samples: 469 WSIs (lung adenocarcinoma) with TP53 and EGFR mutation labels
format: TCGA lung adenocarcinoma H&E WSIs with binary gene mutation labels (TP53, EGFR) for mutation prediction from histology
notes: Subset of TCGA used in ALTER paper (arXiv:2505.12711) for gene mutation prediction task.

name: NOAA SPC Storm Reports
format: CSV files with date, time, location (lat/lon), event type for each severe weather report over CONUS
metric: Brier Skill Score (BSS), PRAUC, ROCAUC, reliability diagrams
notes: NOAA Storm Prediction Center severe weather report archive. Binary labels derived: grid point gets label=1 if ≥1 severe report within 40km radius in 24-hour period. Used as ground truth labels for training/evaluating severe weather prediction models in arXiv:2505.11750 (Hua et al., transformer post-processing of Pangu-Weather forecasts).

name: MSAD
format: Untrimmed surveillance videos with frame-level anomaly labels, diverse real-world scenarios

name: Voxpopuli
num_samples: ~400 hours of speech across 15 European Parliament languages
format: 16kHz audio from European Parliament sessions with transcripts; BPE text representation
notes: Used in WIND paper (arXiv:2505.13765) for German ASR evaluation.

name: Slurp
format: 16kHz audio + transcripts with intent/slot annotations for task-oriented (meal booking, reminders, etc.) speech
notes: Used in WIND paper (arXiv:2505.13765) for English task-oriented ASR evaluation.

name: Multilingual Librispeech
num_samples: ~8K hours total across 6 languages (English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese)
format: 16kHz audio + transcripts in multiple languages
notes: Used in WIND paper (arXiv:2505.13765) for German ASR evaluation.

name: ProcThor
format: 3D indoor environments with RGB observations (224x224); continuous 3D actions (dx, dy, dtheta); embodied navigation tasks
metric: navigation success rate, path optimality, state prediction accuracy

name: EdNet
format: Student interactions: questions (assessed) and lectures (non-assessed) with responses
metric: HR@5, NDCG@5, MRR, AUC (for KT and material prediction)

name: Junyi Academy
format: Student interactions with math exercises, hints, and prerequisite relationships
metric: HR@5, NDCG@5, MRR, AUC (for KT and material prediction)

name: BOOM (Benchmark of Observability Metrics)
format: Real-world observability metrics from Datadog internal telemetry. Multivariate series with median 60 variates. Domains: Application, Infrastructure, Database, Networking, Security.

name: L2-ARCTIC
format: 16kHz non-native English read speech with transcripts; speakers from 6 L1 backgrounds (Hindi, Korean, Mandarin, Spanish, Arabic, Vietnamese)

name: CMU-Arctic
format: 16kHz American English read speech with phonetically balanced transcripts; speakers include US, German, Indian, and other backgrounds

name: HEC (Hispanic-English Corpus)
format: 16kHz bilingual Spanish heritage speaker English read speech with transcripts; adult speakers from Central/South America residing in the US

name: SAA (Speech Accent Archive)
format: 16kHz English speech from 200+ first language backgrounds; all speakers read the identical 69-word 'Please call Stella...' paragraph

name: AmBench
num_samples: ~12,000 ambiguous human names × 5 templates per name type = ~60,000 test points
eval_time: hours to days (API rate-limited evaluation across 12+ LLMs)
format: Text snippets (2-sentence templates) containing ambiguous human names; each name is 1 Levenshtein edit distance from a non-human entity (location, organization, syndrome, mineral, bacteria)
metric: Recall (human name detection), False Discovery Rate (FDR), Consistency (across templates)
notes: Novel benchmark for evaluating LLM name recognition under ambiguity (Name Regularity Bias and Benign Prompt Injection). Paper: arXiv:2505.14549 (Pham et al., 2025). Tests 12 state-of-the-art LLMs on privacy-critical name detection. Key finding: 20-40% recall drop on ambiguous names vs baseline.

name: KLAR
num_samples: 1,197 facts across 12 relation categories (e.g., capital_of, continent, country_of_citizenship, religion)
eval_time: minutes to hours (depending on model and number of checkpoints)
format: Multilingual factual knowledge probing dataset with parallel facts in 12 languages. Each fact is a (subject, relation, object) triple with language-specific prompt templates.
notes: Used in arXiv:2505.14824 for tracing multilingual factual knowledge acquisition across OLMo-7B pretraining checkpoints.

name: RETURN
num_samples: 2,492 real-world individuals from Wikipedia, 20 Q&A pairs each (GPT-4 generated)
format: Question-answer pairs about real-world individuals; used for real-world personal data unlearning evaluation. Subset with 400 pairs used as forget/retention sets.
metric: FE (Forgetting Efficacy), RE (Retaining Efficacy), ROUGE, Truth Ratio, Token Entropy, Similarity, Entailment Score
notes: Real-world Personal Data Unlearning. Real-world benchmark for evaluating machine unlearning methods on protecting personal privacy data in LLMs. Unlike TOFU's fictitious profiles, RETURN uses actual Wikipedia individuals.

name: CUAD
format: Legal contracts with expert-annotated QA pairs and evidence spans; contracts avg ~55K tokens
metric: Precision, Recall, F1 for evidence selection; accuracy for generation
notes: Comprehensive NLP dataset for legal contract review. Used in METEORA paper (2505.16014) as a primary evaluation dataset.

name: MAUD
format: Merger & Acquisition agreements (avg ~351K tokens per document) with QA pairs and evidence spans
metric: Precision, Recall, F1 for evidence selection; accuracy for generation
notes: LegalBench-RAG benchmark for M&A agreements. Most complex dataset in METEORA paper (2505.16014) with avg 351K tokens per document.

name: PrivacyQA
format: Privacy policies with QA pairs targeting privacy-related questions; documents avg ~25K tokens
metric: Precision, Recall, F1 for evidence selection; accuracy for generation
notes: Question answering for privacy policies combining computational and legal perspectives. Used in METEORA paper (2505.16014).

name: QASPER
format: Research papers (avg ~6.5K tokens) with QA pairs targeting specific methodological or empirical claims
metric: Precision, Recall, F1 for evidence selection; accuracy for generation
notes: Information-seeking questions anchored in research papers. Used in METEORA paper (2505.16014) as a primary evaluation dataset.

name: AMBER-generative
format: Image description task with object-level hallucination evaluation. Chair (object precision), Cover (object recall), and F1 score (harmonic mean) as metrics.
notes: Part of AMBER benchmark suite. Judge-free benchmark for image description. Also known as AMBER-gen.

name: AMBER-discriminative
num_samples: 14,216 Yes/No questions regarding objects in images
eval_format: Binary Yes/No questions about object presence in images
notes: Part of AMBER benchmark suite. Also known as AMBER-dis or AMBER-yesno.

name: Llava-Bench-in-the-Wild
num_samples: 60 open-ended questions grounded in 24 diverse real-world images
format: Open-ended VQA with GPT-4o evaluation (gpt-4o-2024-05-13)
notes: Also called LLaVA-Bench-Wild or LV. Evaluates models on diverse real-world and abstract image scenarios. Used in LLaVA-1.5 paper.

name: Object HalBench
num_samples: ~1,000+ samples with augmented prompts from Yu et al. (2024a)
format: Object-level completeness and hallucination evaluation. Chairr (response-level hallucination rate), F1 score for balance.
notes: Object hallucination benchmark from Rohrbach et al. (2018), with augmented prompts from Yu et al. (2024a). Also known as ObjectHal or ObjectHallBench.

name: RealworldQA
num_samples: ~700+ real-world images with spatial and commonsense questions
format: Multiple-choice and open-ended VQA about real-world spatial and commonsense reasoning
notes: From xAI's Grok-1.5V release. Evaluates real-world spatial understanding and commonsense reasoning in VLMs.

name: CVBench
format: Vision-centric multiple-choice questions covering depth, color, count, position, and spatial reasoning
notes: Part of Cambrian-1 benchmark (Tong et al., NeurIPS 2024). Also known as Cambrian-1 CVBench. Tests LVLMs on 2D spatial reasoning, counting, color, and depth perception.

name: AQUA-RAT
format: Multiple-choice math word problems with rationales; each problem has a rationale step and multiple answer options
notes: From Ling et al., 2017 (Program induction by rationale generation). Algebraic word problems requiring multi-step reasoning. Used in PMPO paper arXiv:2505.16307 for math reasoning evaluation.

name: SV-COMP
eval_time: seconds to minutes per program (300s timeout in competitions)
format: C programs with pre/post-conditions; verification conditions as Constrained Horn Clauses (CHC)

name: SVHN-LT
num_samples: ~90k train / 26k test (imbalanced splits with gamma in {150, 200})
format: 32x32 RGB digits with long-tailed class imbalance; derived from SVHN by subsampling classes to achieve specified imbalance ratio
access: Derived from http://ufldl.stanford.edu/housenumbers/ using imbalance subsampling protocol from LTSSL literature

name: Adversarial NLI (ANLI)
num_samples: R1: 1,546 train / R2: 4,424 train / R3: 8,134 train (paper uses R1 with 10k sampled train), ~1k test per round
format: Adversarial natural language inference with entailment, contradiction, neutral labels; created via human-and-model-in-the-loop annotation

name: CLadder 1.5
format: Causal reasoning questions with chain-of-thought; tests LLM ability to infer causal relationships from textual descriptions

name: CVDN
num_samples: ~20k dialog-guided navigation episodes across Matterport3D environments
storage: ~100GB (shared Matterport3D panoramic images + CVDN dialog JSONs)
eval_time: hours (run navigation episodes on discrete graph)
format: Vision-and-dialog navigation where the agent follows natural language instructions through multi-turn dialog; uses Matterport3D indoor environments
license: Matterport3D academic license (free, requires registration) + CVDN research use

name: SOON
storage: ~100GB (shared Matterport3D panoramic images + SOON instruction JSONs)
eval_time: hours (run navigation episodes on discrete graph)
format: Scenario-oriented object navigation with long-horizon, instruction following in cluttered indoor scenes; agent must locate target objects based on natural language descriptions
license: Matterport3D academic license (free, requires registration) + SOON CC BY-NC

name: HELMET
num_samples: Diverse application-centered tasks with context lengths up to 128k tokens
format: Hierarchical modular tasks for long-context understanding; model-based evaluation prioritizing complex tasks
notes: Hierarchical Efficient Benchmark for Long Context Evaluation with Modular Units and Comprehensive Taxonomy (Yen et al., 2024). Evaluates long-context models across diverse real-world application tasks up to 128K tokens.

name: RaspBugs
eval_time: hours (training each program up to 10k epochs)
format: Buggy RASP programs with I/O specifications; programs compiled to Transformer models via Tracr
notes: From Silva et al., 2025 (arXiv 2505.17703). Synthetically generated by mutating 6 base RASP programs with 15 mutation operators. Train/val/test split: 80/10/10.

name: RASP
num_samples: 6 reference programs (sort, reverse, hist, most-freq, dyck-1, dyck-2)
format: Domain-specific sequence processing language; RASP programs can be compiled to Transformer models via Tracr
notes: From Weiss et al., 2021. Restricted Access Sequence Processing language for sequence processing tasks. Key property: can be analytically compiled to encoder-style Transformers.

name: Tracr
format: Compiler from RASP programs to Transformer models; programmatically constructs attention from RASP selectors
notes: From Lindner et al., 2023. Analytical deterministic compiler. For fixed vocabulary and sequence length, compiled model is strictly equivalent to the RASP program.

name: Objaverse-XL
format: Large-scale 3D object dataset with multi-view rendered RGB images; shapes with camera poses and metadata

name: ULIP-2
num_samples: Part of ULIP-2 benchmark (3D shape-text-image alignment evaluation)
format: Multimodal 3D understanding benchmark measuring shape-image-text alignment via frozen encoders; uses ULIP-2 score metric

name: Uni3D
num_samples: Part of Uni3D benchmark (large-scale 3D representation evaluation)
format: Unified 3D representation benchmark at scale; evaluates 3D shape encoding quality via frozen vision-language models; uses Uni3D score metric

name: OpenShape
num_samples: Part of OpenShape benchmark (open-vocabulary 3D shape recognition)
format: Open-vocabulary 3D shape classification benchmark; evaluates shape-image alignment using frozen CLIP/DINOv2 encoders; uses OpenShape score metric

name: SPair-71k
format: Image pairs with sparse keypoint correspondences; annotations include keypoints, viewpoint, scale, truncation, occlusion
metric: PCK (Percentage of Correct Keypoints) at various thresholds

name: PF-PASCAL
format: Image pairs from PASCAL VOC with 4-17 keypoints per pair

name: PF-WILLOW
num_samples: 900 image pairs across 5 categories (face, car, motorbike, duck, wineBottle)
format: Image pairs with 10 keypoints per pair; center-aligned images with same viewpoint

name: AP-10K
format: Animal image pairs with 3-17 keypoints; from MS COCO; intra-species, cross-species, cross-family splits
access: https://github.com/Visual-AI/Semantic-Correspondence (original from Zhang et al., AAAI 2021 adapted for correspondence)

name: TSS
format: Image pairs with dense flow field annotations; from FG3DCAr, JODS, PASCAL

name: SC-ImageNet
format: ImageNet images with 32 pseudo keypoint pairs per image pair; for pretraining semantic correspondence

name: ZooplanktonBench
eval_time: 15 hours per model training + hours for evaluation
format: Shadowgraph images + videos with geo-metadata (depth, temperature, salinity, coordinates); bounding box annotations for detection and classification tasks
metric: mAP50, mAP50-95 for detection; accuracy for classification
notes: KDD 2025. Geo-aware zooplankton detection and classification benchmark from northern Gulf of Mexico. Tasks: fine-grained detection/classification, living vs. marine snow binary detection. Tracks: diverse environments (depths 10/25/35m), images+video. Baselines: YOLOv8 (fine-tuned), Grounding DINO (zero-shot), GPT-4V.

name: SAFIM
num_samples: not publicly disclosed (syntax-aware FIM benchmark for Python code completion)
format: Fill-in-the-middle code completion tasks with syntax-awareness; tasks include algorithm-block, control-flow, and API function call completion

name: DeepTumorVQA
num_samples: 395,612 QA pairs (355,962 train + 39,650 test) from 9,262 CT volumes (3.7M slices)
storage: Source datasets ~1-2TB total (17 public CT datasets); benchmark released separately
eval_time: hours per model on test set (928 CT volumes, 39,650 QA pairs)
format: 3D CT volumes (DICOM/nifti) with structured QA pairs in 4 categories: Measurement, Recognition, Visual Reasoning, Medical Reasoning. Both multiple-choice and free-text answer formats.
metric: accuracy (multiple-choice), exact match (free-text categorical), MRA (Mean Relative Accuracy for quantitative numerical prediction)
notes: First large-scale 3D tumor-centric clinical VQA benchmark. Targets abdominal CT scans with 29 question subtypes. Annotations by 23 board-certified radiologists. ArXiv:2505.18915

name: WN18RR
num_samples: 40943 entities, 11 relations, 86835 train, 3034 valid, 3134 test triples
format: Knowledge graph triples (head, relation, tail) for link prediction. Subset of WordNet with inverse relations removed to prevent data leakage.
notes: WordNet subset. Dominated by symmetric/hierarchical relations (synonymy, meronymy). Complex-valued models like RotatE perform well due to natural cyclic structure. Used in RELATE paper (2505.18971).

name: YAGO3-10
num_samples: 123182 entities, 37 relations, 1079040 train, 5000 valid, 5000 test triples
format: Knowledge graph triples (head, relation, tail) for link prediction. Subset of YAGO knowledge base covering people, locations, and movies.
notes: Largest standard KGE benchmark by entity count. High type and entity diversity. RELATE achieves SOTA on YAGO3-10 with MRR 0.521, Hit@10 0.680 (2505.18971).

name: DepthTrack
format: RGB-Depth video pairs for object tracking, from VOT2021-RGBD challenge

name: VOT-RGBD22
format: RGB-Depth video pairs for object tracking, from VOT2022 challenge

name: VastTrack
format: Large-scale visual object tracking dataset with vast category diversity, bounding box annotations

name: TNL2k
format: Large-scale long-term tracking dataset with natural language descriptions, bounding box annotations

name: PhysioNet2012
num_samples: ~12000 ICU patients, 36 physiological signals over 48h + 9 static features
format: Time series of vital signs and lab values (36 signals) with static patient features; binary label for ICU LoS > 72h

name: GossipCop
num_samples: 5464 tree-structured graphs (news articles with social cascade), ~4 features per node
format: Tree-structured social graphs: root=article, subsequent nodes=sharing users; node features: BERT embeddings (768d), word2vec (300d), profile (10d), content (310d)

name: HADES
num_samples: 750 samples across 5 harmful categories (Animal, Privacy, Self-Harm, Violence, Financial)
format: Adversarial images with embedded malicious intent amplified via typography; paired with harmful text instructions
metric: Attack Success Rate (ASR) — proportion of inputs eliciting harmful responses as judged by Llama-Guard-3-8B

name: Derm7pt
format: Dermoscopy images with 7-point checklist concept annotations (8 concept labels per image) and binary disease labels; used for concept-based classification and human-AI deferral experiments
access: https://github.com/jooosts/derm7pt (verify - original paper: Kawahara et al., IEEE J-BHI 2018)
notes: From Kawahara et al., 2018 'Seven-point checklist and skin lesion classification using multitask multimodal neural nets'. Used in DeCoDe paper (2505.19220) for human-AI collaboration experiments with concept-based deferral. The 8 concepts correspond to the 7-point checklist criteria for dermoscopy.

name: DOS (DriveOcclusionSim)
format: Carla-based driving simulation with 4 occlusion-reasoning scenarios: Parked Cars (DOS01), Sudden Brake (DOS02), Left Turn (DOS03), Red Light Infraction (DOS04). Each scenario has 25 diverse cases with varying road layouts and background traffic.
metric: Route Completion (RC), Infraction Score (IS), Driving Score (DS)
access: Released in ReasonNet (arXiv), used in ReasonPlan (arXiv:2505.20024)

name: eICU
format: Multi-center critical care database with structured EHR data (diagnoses, procedures, medications, labs)

name: TWOSIDES
num_samples: ~60k drug-drug interaction pairs from FDA adverse event reports
format: Pairwise drug-drug interaction data with confidence scores and adverse event types

name: GeoQA
format: Multiple-choice geometric question answering with images; tests plane geometry understanding including shape recognition, spatial reasoning, angle/distance computation
notes: Chen et al., 2021. Geometric question answering benchmark for evaluating multimodal numerical reasoning. Each problem includes a geometric diagram and multiple-choice question about the geometry.

name: MM-Math
num_samples: 700 test problems (open-ended geometry questions from middle school exams)
format: Open-ended geometry problems with images requiring step-by-step reasoning; sourced from real middle-school exams; includes easy/medium/hard difficulty splits
notes: Sun et al., 2024 (EMNLP). High discriminative difficulty multimodal math benchmark. The test set used in the MMGeoLM paper contains 700 problems with difficulty splits: Easy, Medium, Hard accuracy rates even for GPT-4o (~55%, ~33%, ~10%).

name: ImageNet-21K
format: ImageNet full dataset with ~14.2M images across 21,841 synsets/classes; used as POOD in adversarial attack papers

name: PubFig
format: Face images from public figures with variations in pose, expression, and lighting; used for face recognition evaluation

name: BMAD
format: Medical imaging datasets with normal/anomaly splits for anomaly detection and localization; includes BraTS2021, BTCV, LiTS, RESC, OCT2017, RSNA
license: Varies by dataset (BraTS: research license, RSNA: open)
notes: Benchmarks for Medical Anomaly Detection. Recent CVPRW 2024 benchmark providing standardized dataset splits for medical anomaly detection reproducibility. Used in hyperbolic anomaly detection paper (arXiv:2505.21228).

name: BraTS 2021
num_samples: Train: 7,500 normal, Valid: 39 norm + 44 anom, Test: 640 norm + 3,075 anom (per BMAD splits)
format: Brain MRI FLAIR sequences for tumor anomaly detection; 3D volumes with brain tumor segmentation labels
notes: RSNA-ASNR-MICCAI BraTS 2021 Benchmark. Used in BMAD (CVPRW 2024) and hyperbolic anomaly detection paper (arXiv:2505.21228). FLAIR sequence used for anomaly detection per BMAD protocol.

name: LiTS
num_samples: ~130 CT scans with liver tumor annotations
format: 3D abdominal CT volumes with liver and tumor segmentation labels
metric: Dice Similarity Coefficient (for segmentation; adapted for anomaly detection)
notes: Liver Tumor Segmentation Benchmark (Bilic et al., Medical Image Analysis 2023). Used in BMAD (CVPRW 2024) evaluation set for liver CT anomaly detection. BTCV used as training set in BMAD.

name: RESC
num_samples: Train: 4,297 normal, Valid: 45 norm + 70 anom, Test: 1,041 norm + 764 anom (per BMAD splits)
format: Retinal OCT images for macular edema segmentation; B-scan OCT volumes with edema labels
notes: Retinal Edema Segmentation Challenge (Hu et al., Medical Image Analysis 2019). Used in BMAD (CVPRW 2024) and hyperbolic anomaly detection paper (arXiv:2505.21228) for retinal OCT anomaly detection.

name: OCT2017
num_samples: Train: 26,315 normal, Valid: 8 norm + 24 anom, Test: 242 norm + 726 anom (per BMAD splits)
format: Large-scale retinal OCT dataset for disease classification; one normal class and three disease classes treated as single anomaly class
notes: Kermany et al. (Cell 2018) OCT dataset. Used in BMAD (CVPRW 2024) and hyperbolic anomaly detection paper (arXiv:2505.21228) for retinal OCT disease classification as anomaly detection.

name: RSNA
num_samples: Train: 8,000 normal, Valid: 70 norm + 1,420 anom, Test: 781 norm + 16,413 anom (per BMAD splits)
format: Chest X-ray images labeled with one normal and eight disease categories treated as single anomaly class
notes: RSNA ChestX-ray8 dataset (Wang et al., CVPR 2017). Used in BMAD (CVPRW 2024) and hyperbolic anomaly detection paper (arXiv:2505.21228) for chest X-ray anomaly detection.

name: GLORYS12 Ocean Reanalysis
num_samples: ~28 years of daily ocean state data (1993-2020)
format: Daily mean ocean state variables: sea salinity (23 depths), sea temperature (23 depths), zonal/meridional velocity (23 depths), sea surface height (surface), with atmospheric forcing from ERA5
license: Free registration at Copernicus Marine Service
notes: GLORYS12 (Global Ocean Physical Reanalysis) provides eddy-resolving ocean state estimation. Used as training/validation/test data in NEURALOM paper (arXiv:2505.21020) for global ocean S2S simulation. Training: 1993-2017, Validation: 2018-2019, Test: 2020.

name: Global Ocean S2S Simulation Benchmark
num_samples: 240 initial conditions (IC) for simulation, 50 ICs for forecasting
format: Autoregressive ocean state prediction at daily steps; evaluates RMSE, ACC, CSI, SEDI at horizons from 10-60 days
notes: Custom benchmark from NEURALOM paper (arXiv:2505.21020) for evaluating global ocean subseasonal-to-seasonal simulation and forecasting. Uses GLORYS12 as ground truth and ERA5 as atmospheric forcing. Tests long-term stability and physical consistency of ML-based ocean models.

name: SIB-200
format: Topic classification dataset with 21 classes, designed for evaluating models on diverse languages
notes: Used in PIXEL-M4 paper (arXiv:2505.21265) for evaluating text classification across 27 languages.

name: Universal Dependencies (UD)
num_samples: varies by language (dozens to thousands per language)
format: Cross-linguistic dependency treebank with POS tags and morphological features
notes: Standard benchmark for dependency parsing. Used in PIXEL-M4 paper across 14 languages.

name: UNER (Universal NER)
format: Unified named entity recognition dataset across multiple languages
notes: Universal NER benchmark used in PIXEL-M4 paper for named entity recognition evaluation.

name: KLUE
format: Korean language understanding benchmark with multiple tasks including NER, RC, STS, NLI
notes: Korean NER task from KLUE benchmark used in PIXEL-M4 paper for cross-lingual transfer evaluation.

name: Imagenette
storage: ~3GB (full resolution); smaller when using 160px or 320px versions
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model size
format: Full-resolution RGB images (various sizes) from 10 easily-distinguishable ImageNet classes

name: GSM-Hard
format: Modified version of GSM8k test split where numbers are replaced with values of larger magnitude to increase difficulty

name: MultiArith
format: Multi-step arithmetic word problems from MAWPS dataset requiring multiple sequential calculations

name: HelpSteer
format: Prompt-response pairs with 5 human-annotated attributes: Helpfulness, Correctness, Coherence, Complexity, Verbosity (0-4 scale)
metric: N/A (training data); evaluated with GPT-4o judge for win rates

name: Toxigen
format: Toxic vs non-toxic prompt pairs for evaluating LLM toxicity detection and detoxification

name: ParaDetox
format: Parallel detoxification dataset: toxic prompts paired with neutral/paraphrased non-toxic versions

name: Qasper
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model and evaluation setup
format: Information-seeking question-answering dataset anchored in research papers. Covers questions about entity existence, yes/no, numeric, and free-form answer types.
metric: Answer F1, Answer EM (exact match), Unanswerable F1

name: RenderMe360
storage: Hundreds of GB (multi-view RGB + depth + cameras)
format: High-fidelity full-head multi-view sequences with 60 camera positions, 12 expressions per subject; used for 3D head avatar reconstruction and novel view synthesis
metric: PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, FID, CSIM (face recognition)

name: PanoHead
format: 3D-aware GAN for full-head synthesis in 360deg using enhanced tri-plane representations; trained on synthetic data; used as baseline in DiffPortrait360 paper

name: SphereHead
format: 3D full-head synthesis with spherical tri-plane representation; uses spherical coordinate system for improved back-view synthesis; baseline in DiffPortrait360 paper

name: LSVQ
eval_time: minutes to hours per full evaluation
format: User-generated videos at diverse resolutions (240P-1080P); MOS annotations per video
license: research use (paper: Ying et al., CVPR 2021)

name: KoNViD-1k
format: YouTube videos at 960x540, sampled from YFCC100M; MOS annotations

name: LIVE-VQC
format: Diverse in-the-wild videos with MOS annotations; resolutions from 240P to 1080P

name: YouTube-UGC
format: YouTube user-generated content videos with MOS annotations; diverse resolutions and content types

name: LPVQ
format: 50 images (treated as static videos) divided into 7x7 non-overlapping grids; each patch annotated with quality score 1-5 (0.5 intervals); 14 expert visual researchers per patch; total 34,300 annotations
license: to be released with KVQ paper

name: Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard (BFCL) Executable
num_samples: 310 test queries (5 categories: Simple-Python, Simple-REST, Multiple, Parallel, Multiple-Parallel)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Python and REST function calling tasks evaluated by execution or AST matching

name: StableToolBench
num_samples: 790 test queries covering 2479 unique APIs across 6 subsets (I1-Inst, I1-Cat, I1-Tool, I2-Inst, I2-Cat, I3-Inst)
eval_time: hours for full evaluation with multiple models
format: Real-world API calls requiring multi-step reasoning with tool interaction

name: IPC 2023 Learning Track
eval_time: hours for a full sweep (5 min per training task, 30 min per test task)
format: PDDL domain/problem files
metric: plan coverage (number of solved tasks), plan length, state expansions

name: HCAST
storage: <1GB for task definitions; full suite not publicly released
eval_time: hours to days (189 tasks × 5 runs × 4 models); human baselines require 1500+ hours of human effort
format: Containerized task environment with instruction string, setup code, and algorithmic scoring function. Tasks span ML engineering, cybersecurity, software engineering, and general reasoning.
metric: Success rate (binary pass/fail) + human-calibrated time (tasks rated from 1min to 8+ hours for humans)
license: Not fully open; 11/189 example tasks released, rest withheld to prevent contamination
notes: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks. Novel benchmark that connects AI agent performance to human task completion time. 140 skilled human baseliners provided 563 attempts totaling 1500+ hours. Key finding: frontier agents succeed 70-80% on tasks taking humans <1hr, <20% on tasks taking >4hrs. From METR (arXiv:2503.17354).

name: L0-Bench
eval_time: minutes to hours (depending on model size and majority voting)
format: Synthetic Python programs with simple operations (arithmetic, control flow, list ops); models generate step-by-step execution traces

name: MC2 (Multilingual Corpus of Minority Languages in China)
num_samples: 101 texts per language (4 languages: Tibetan, Mongolian, Kazakh, Uyghur)
format: Text snippets for language identification of Chinese minority languages
access: Referenced in Zhang et al. (2024a) - ACL 2024

name: τ-bench (tau-bench)
format: Multi-turn conversational agent benchmark with executable Python APIs in retail and airline domains; agent interacts with simulated human user (LM) and programmatic APIs while following domain-specific policies

name: FAST-LIVO2
num_samples: 3 test scenes (Building, Landmark, Sculpture) with sequential LiDAR and camera frames
eval_time: minutes for calibration and NVS evaluation per scene
format: Solid-state LiDAR + single forward-facing camera for handheld SLAM; includes synchronized RGB images, LiDAR point clouds, and approximate odometry poses
metric: Calibration accuracy (rotation/translation error), NVS quality (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS)
notes: FAST-LIVO2: Fast, Direct LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry (Zheng et al., IEEE Trans. Robotics 2024). Used in TLC-Calib paper for evaluating calibration on handheld solid-state LiDAR setup. TLC-Calib paper uses scenes: Building, Landmark, Sculpture.

name: XStoryCloze
format: Cross-lingual narrative commonsense reasoning - given a story premise and two ending options, select the correct ending that logically follows
access: xstorycloze dataset on HuggingFace (Lin et al. 2022)

name: DUMB500
format: Easy questions across 4 domains: Mathematics (arithmetic, comparisons), Conversational Interaction (greetings, commonsense), Programming & Computing (basic coding concepts), Task Execution (paraphrasing, translation). Graded by accuracy for Math/Code and LM-judged for Chat/Task.
metric: accuracy (exact match for Math/Code; LLM-judged for Chat/Task)

name: InfographicsVQA
format: High-resolution infographic images with QA pairs requiring understanding of charts, diagrams, and infographics

name: DUDE (Document Understanding Dataset and Evaluation)
format: Document images with complex QA requiring multi-page reasoning and document-level understanding

name: SROIE (ICDAR 2019 Scanned Receipt OCR)
format: Scanned receipt images for OCR and key information extraction (invoice data)
metric: ANLS, F1 score for entity extraction

name: Visual7W
format: Images with pointing-enabled QA (asking 'which' questions with visual grounding to specific regions)

name: V* Bench (Guided Visual Search)
format: High-resolution SA-1B images with questions requiring precise visual grounding and understanding of fine-grained visual details

name: Deepglobe
format: Satellite imagery (800px) with 7 semantic categories (road, building, vegetation, water, barren, agriculture, car)
notes: Deepglobe 2018 CVPR challenge dataset for road and building extraction from satellite imagery. Used as target domain in CD-FSS benchmarks.

name: IRef-VLA
num_samples: ~8,000+ template-based referring expressions across ScanNet scenes
format: Template-generated 3D referring expressions with spatial relations, color/size attributes; view-independent; enforced one spatial relation per utterance; uses ScanNet 3D scans
license: ScanNet non-commercial research license + IRef-VLA terms

name: Quantitative Verification Benchmark Set (QVBS)
eval_time: seconds to minutes per instance (timeout at 600s)
format: MDP/MC model files in various formats (JANI, PRISM, DTMC, MDP)
metric: varies by instance (reachability probability, expected cost, steady-state, etc.)

name: MetFaces
num_samples: ~1336 high-quality face images from Metropolitan Museum of Art collection
format: High-quality face images from the Met Art dataset, aligned to FFHQ format for OOD evaluation
license: Metropolitan Museum of Art open access policy

name: CHAMMI
num_samples: ~200k microscopy images from Channel-Adaptive Models in Microscopy Imaging benchmark
format: Multi-channel fluorescence microscopy images with domain adaptation benchmarks for microscopy imaging

name: Arcade Learning Environment (ALE)
format: Atari 2600 game ROMs with standardized RL interface

name: Atari Pong
format: Atari 2600 Pong game via ALE

name: Atari Montezuma's Revenge
format: Atari 2600 Montezuma's Revenge via ALE — notoriously sparse reward

name: OCAtari
num_samples: object-centric parsed frames from Atari games
format: Object-centric Atari frames: bounding boxes, velocities, object categories parsed from RAM values

name: VideoEspresso
format: Large-scale chain-of-thought dataset for fine-grained video reasoning via core frame selection. Multiple-choice QA covering causal reasoning, process description, behavior inference.

name: VideoMMMU
num_samples: ~1,500+ QA pairs from multi-discipline professional videos
format: Evaluates knowledge acquisition from multi-discipline professional videos (science, engineering, medicine, etc.). Multiple-choice QA requiring expert-level video understanding.

name: CompAlign
eval_time: hours (depending on T2I model and API rate limits)
format: Text prompts: compositional T2I with 3+ subjects, 3D-spatial relationships, attribute bindings (color, texture)
metric: Aggregated Compositional Accuracy (ACA) via MLLM binary feedback
license: Not specified (paper does not release code)

name: CompBench
eval_time: hours to days depending on model complexity
format: Complex instruction-guided image editing benchmark with 9 tasks across 5 categories: local editing (object removal/addition/replacement), multi-editing (multi-turn/multi-object), action editing, scene spatial editing (location/viewpoint), and complex reasoning. Each sample includes source image, target image, editing instruction, and masks.
metric: PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS for background consistency; CLIP-Score for foreground evaluation; GPT-4o for action/location/viewpoint evaluation
notes: From arXiv:2505.12200. Introduces MLLM-human collaborative framework for data construction and instruction decoupling strategy (location, appearance, dynamics, objects). Source data from MOSE video instance segmentation dataset.

name: MOSE
num_samples: Videos with instance segmentation masks in complex scenes
format: Video Instance Segmentation dataset featuring complex scenes with multi-object masks. Used as source data for CompBench benchmark construction.
notes: From ICCV 2023 paper 'MOSE: A New Dataset for Video Object Segmentation in Complex Scenes'. Contains videos with complex scenes featuring multiple objects with detailed instance masks. Used for constructing CompBench via mask decomposition and frame selection.

name: SVS (Schwartz Value Survey)
format: 57 value-related questions grounded in Schwartz's Theory of Basic Values (10 dimensions: Power, Achievement, Hedonism, Stimulation, Self-Direction, Universalism, Benevolence, Tradition, Conformity, Security)
metric: value vector (10-dimensional, v_i in [0,1]) per model, analyzed via TrueSkill for distinguishability
access: Released in AdAEM paper (arXiv:2505.13531) supplementary materials; original at https://www.value-survey.org/
notes: Baseline benchmark in AdAEM paper. 57 general questions, produces indistinguishable results across LLMs (the informativeness challenge).

name: ValueBench
format: 40 value-related questions for LLM evaluation. Questions are more specific than SVS but still static.
metric: value vector per model, similar to SVS but with improved question specificity
notes: Baseline benchmark in AdAEM paper. Improves over SVS in specificity but still produces indistinguishable results across LLMs from different cultures.

name: ValueDCG
format: 4,561 LLM-generated value-related questions via prompting. Longer than SVS but with lower Self-BLEU (13.93) indicating higher diversity.
metric: value vector per model with TrueSkill aggregation
access: Released in Zhang et al. 2023; referenced in AdAEM paper (arXiv:2505.13531)
notes: Baseline benchmark in AdAEM paper. SVS achieves 52.68 Self-BLEU, ValueBench 26.27, ValueDCG 13.93. All still suffer from informativeness challenge.

name: AdAEM Bench
eval_time: hours per model (depending on number of questions sampled)
format: 12,310 value-evoking questions generated by AdAEM algorithm (Algorithm 1) probing LLM value boundaries. Questions are specific, controversial, and culturally diverse, covering 10 Schwartz value dimensions. Generated using P1={LLaMA-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, DeepSeek-V2.5} and P2={GPT-4-Turbo, Mistral-Large, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, GLM-4, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct}.
metric: 10-dimensional value vector per model (Schwartz dimensions), with TrueSkill-based relative ranking for aggregation. Evaluation uses value classifiers and opinion extraction.
license: To be released (after removing harmful questions)
notes: Core contribution of AdAEM paper (arXiv:2505.13531). Self-extensible: co-evolves with new LLMs by probing their value boundaries. Achieves Self-BLEU=13.42, avg length=15.11 words, semantic similarity=0.44 (higher diversity). Addresses the informativeness challenge that plagues SVS, ValueBench, and ValueDCG.

name: PRIDE
format: Protein backbone structures (PDB format) with train/test splits from CATH and CAMEO
metric: sequence recovery rate (%, primary), TM-score (%), RMSD (Å)
notes: Protein inverse folding benchmark. Training from CATH 4.3, test from CAMEO (medium+hard targets). Used in DS-ProGen paper (arXiv:2505.12511) as primary evaluation benchmark.

name: CAMEO
format: Protein structures from recent PDB depositions, weekly email-held targets
metric: TM-score, LDDT (for structure prediction); recovery rate (for inverse folding)
notes: Continuous protein structure prediction benchmark. Test set for PRIDE benchmark (504 medium/hard targets from July 2021 - March 2022 release period). Used in DS-ProGen paper (arXiv:2505.12511) for evaluation.

name: SPA-Bench
format: Android emulator screenshots with touch/keyboard gestures; task evaluation across 3 difficulty levels; Level 3 represents most complex real-world workflows

name: GUI-KRB
format: Triplets of UI elements, screen states (before/after interaction), and expert-validated keyword sets. Two tasks: Prior Knowledge Assessment (identify UI element functionality from screenshot) and Dynamic Comprehension Assessment (reason about cause-effect logic from state transitions)
metric: Keyword match rate (>=50% of expert-identified keywords)

name: nuScenes-C
format: Corrupted nuScenes validation set with 8 corruptions: Motion Blur, Color Quantization, Low Light (Dark), Brightness, Snow, Fog, Camera Crash, Frame Lost. Each corruption at 3 severity levels.
metric: NDS, mAP, AMOTA, mATE, mASE, mAOE, mAVE, mAAE for 3D detection and tracking

name: KITTI-C
format: Corrupted KITTI validation set with 8 corruptions: Fog, Wet Conditions, Snow, Motion Blur, Missing Beams, Crosstalk, Incomplete Echoes, Cross-Sensor. Each corruption at 3 severity levels.

name: MMLU-ProM
format: 4-choice MC questions from medical/professional domains, a subset of MMLU-Pro focusing on medical topics
notes: Medical category subset of MMLU-Pro. Used as hard-level evaluation benchmark in AlphaMed paper (arXiv:2505.17952). Targets advanced expert-level medical knowledge.

name: GPQA-M
format: Multiple-choice graduate-level biomedical questions requiring expert knowledge, subset of GPQA focusing on medical/bioomedical topics
notes: Biomedical subset of GPQA (Graduate-Level Google-Proof QA). Used as hard-level evaluation benchmark in AlphaMed paper (arXiv:2505.17952). Expert-curated questions designed to resist superficial retrieval.

name: DynaGuard
num_samples: ~1.5K prompts across 4 categories (AI safety, financial advice prohibition, tax advice prohibition, prompt injection)
format: Custom safety policy evaluation with dynamic/adaptable taxonomies; prompts designed to test generalization to novel safety constraints
notes: From Neill et al. 2025. Tests adaptability of guard models to novel safety taxonomies at inference time without retraining.

name: COSA (Controllable Safety Alignment)
format: Contextual safety alignment under domain-specific personas where typical safety assumptions may not apply (e.g., slurs in games, graphic descriptions in legal/film contexts)
notes: From Zhang et al. 2024. Tests whether models can override prior safety assumptions and align with provided safety specifications that may conflict with training taxonomy.

name: SimpleSafetyTests
format: Curated test suite identifying critical safety risks in LLMs across multiple risk categories
