notes: From Vidgen et al. 2023. Designed to complement existing benchmarks by focusing on high-stakes safety-critical failures.

name: OpenAI Moderation API Evaluation
format: Content moderation benchmark using OpenAI's moderation API as evaluation tool; includes diverse harm categories
notes: From Markov et al. 2023. Used as evaluation baseline in this paper for prompt harmfulness classification.

name: Topic-Following (CantTalkAboutThis)
format: Multi-turn dialogues with system instructions specifying allowed/disallowed topics; includes on-topic (safe) and off-topic (unsafe) user turns for dialogue moderation
notes: From Rebedea et al. 2024. Used as auxiliary training data to improve adaptation to custom safety policies. Can be interpreted as dialogue moderation task.

name: WILDGUARDMIX
format: Content safety dataset with diverse risk categories (cybersecurity, hate speech, misinformation, finance, entertainment); includes train/test splits
notes: From Han et al. 2024. One of the two primary training datasets used in this paper. Broader domains than AEGIS 2.0, includes more adversarial prompts (jailbreaks, role-playing).

name: AEGIS 2.0
format: AI safety dataset with risk taxonomy emphasizing sociopolitical content; includes train/test splits
notes: From Ghosh et al. 2025. One of the two primary training datasets. Emphasizes sociopolitical content. Simpler prompt distribution than WILDGUARDMIX.

name: PlotQA
num_samples: 2M+ total, 2K sampled for test in paper
format: Statistical plots (bar, line, pie charts) with QA pairs requiring trend analysis and numerical reasoning

name: TabMWP
num_samples: ~30K total, 1K mini-test split used in paper
format: Tabular math problems combining table parsing and arithmetic reasoning

name: Counting (SuperCLEVR-based)
format: Counting tasks based on SuperCLEVR dataset requiring visual reasoning about object counts

name: RoboMimic
format: Robot manipulation trajectories (RGB images, end-effector poses, actions) in HDF5 format; tasks include Can, Square, Lift; MH version has mixed-quality demonstrations
notes: From Mandlekar et al. 2021. Used for imitation learning policy training and evaluation. MH (Multi-Human) dataset used in SCIZOR paper for mixed-quality curation experiments.

name: Open-X-Embodiment (OXE)
format: Cross-embodiment robot trajectories unified via RLDS format; includes RGB images, actions (7-DoF), and task descriptions; multiple dataset mixtures: Magic Soup, RT-X, RT-1
notes: From Padalkar et al. 2023. Massive cross-embodiment dataset. SCIZOR uses OXE Magic Soup, RT-X, and RT-1 subsets for large-scale VLA (Octo) fine-tuning experiments.

name: Sirius-Fleet
format: Real-world multi-task robot manipulation data collected with visual world model + human intervention; includes RGB images, actions, task descriptions
notes: From Liu et al. 2024. Real-world dataset with mixed autonomous policy and human-corrected demonstrations. Used in SCIZOR paper for real-robot evaluation across 8 tasks.

name: SIMPLER (Simulation Environment for Robot Manipulation)
eval_time: Minutes per task per model checkpoint
format: GPU-accelerated robotic manipulation simulation via Mujoco; tasks: Pick Coke Can, Move Near; provides standardized evaluation protocol with fixed object poses
notes: From Li et al. 2024. Used in SCIZOR paper for evaluating Octo fine-tuned policies on simulated robotic manipulation tasks. Visual-Matching setting used (no lighting/texture variation).

name: NeRF-DS
format: monocular real-world RGB video sequences of dynamic specular objects with annotated camera trajectories, resolution 480x270

name: OpenABCD
num_samples: ~870K AIGs from 29 IP designs across 1,500 synthesis recipes; paper uses ~549 train + ~399 test pairs
format: And-Inverter Graphs (AIGs) at initial, intermediate, and final optimization stages with labels (node counts, delay metrics, synthesis transformation sequences)
metric: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score for subgraph detection; IoU, DICE for boundary detection

name: CoSafe
format: Multi-turn dialogue safety benchmark evaluating coreference resolution in safety-critical conversations; tests whether models can identify and appropriately refuse unsafe requests embedded in conversational context
metric: attack success rate (ASR), safety refusal rate
notes: From Yu et al. 2024 (EMNLP 2024). Used as multi-turn safety baseline in JBDISTILL paper (2505.22037). Evaluates safety under conversational coreference scenarios.

name: CXRTrek
num_samples: 428,966 CXRs with ~11M Q&A pairs across 8 diagnostic stages
storage: ~2TB+ (includes source images from MIMIC-CXR and CheXpert-plus)
format: Multi-stage chest X-ray VQA dataset with 8 sequential diagnostic stages: X-ray Validation, Findings Recognition, Findings Attributes, Relationships, Image Comparisons, Future Risk, Diagnosis Advice, Summarizing. Supports 4 output formats: open-ended, closed-ended, choice, detection (bounding boxes).
license: PhysioNet credentialed access for MIMIC-CXR source; CheXpert-plus license
notes: From CXRTrek paper (arXiv:2505.23143). First benchmark to explicitly simulate radiologist clinical reasoning workflow across 8 sequential stages. Average 26.29 Q&A pairs per sample. Constructed from MIMIC-CXR and CheXpert-plus with GPT-4-enhanced annotation.

name: Rad-ReStruct
num_samples: ~500 chest X-ray studies with structured QA
format: Structured radiology VQA benchmark with hierarchical question-answer pairs covering view recognition, abnormality detection, and report generation. Multi-turn structured format.
notes: Used as external evaluation benchmark in CXRTrek paper (arXiv:2505.23143). CXRTrekNet achieves 91.28% individual Q&A accuracy and 38.60% full report accuracy on this benchmark.

name: CheXpert-plus
num_samples: Hundreds of thousands of CXRs with aligned radiology reports
format: Large-scale chest X-ray dataset with free-text radiology reports. Enhanced version of CheXpert with improved label extraction and broader coverage.
notes: Used as source dataset for CXRTrek training set in CXRTrek paper (arXiv:2505.23143). One of two primary data sources (alongside MIMIC-CXR) for constructing the CXRTrek benchmark dataset.

name: CROHME 2014/2016/2019
format: Handwritten mathematical expression images (INKML format) with LaTeX transcriptions for recognition

name: CROHME 2023
format: Handwritten mathematical expression images with LaTeX transcriptions; expanded version of CROHME benchmark

name: HME100K
format: Real-world handwritten mathematical expression images with LaTeX annotations; diverse handwriting styles and conditions

name: MathWriting
format: Handwritten mathematical expression images (online traces + rendered offline images) with LaTeX; Google Research 2024

name: Im2LaTeXv2 (MathNet)
format: Printed mathematical expression images rendered with 59 diverse LaTeX styles; enhanced from Im2Latex-100k with improved normalization

name: MNE (Multi-level Nested Expression)
num_samples: test subsets N1/N2/N3 organized by structural complexity
format: Handwritten mathematical expression images with LaTeX transcriptions; organized by tree-depth complexity (max nested levels in substructures)
access: Referenced in PosFormer (Guan et al., ECCV 2024)

name: PAIRS
num_samples: 44 key concepts x 4 images (black male, black female, white male, white female) = 176 pairs per category
format: Parallel images varying only in gender and race; designed for studying gender and race bias in VLMs via multiple-choice selection (MCS) tasks
metric: Fairness score (proportion of fair responses), KL divergence (confidence calibration)
notes: From Fraser and Kiritchenko (EACL 2024). Paper: https://aclanthology.org/2024.eacl-long.41/. Used in Fairness Seesaw paper (2505.23798) for evaluating gender and race bias in VLMs.

name: SocialCounterfactuals (SCF)
num_samples: 126 key concepts (occupations) x 4 images = 504 pairs per category
format: Counterfactual image examples with gender and race attributes; designed for studying intersectional social biases in vision-language models
metric: Fairness score (proportion of fair responses), KL divergence (confidence calibration)
notes: From Howard et al. (CVPR 2024). Used in Fairness Seesaw paper (2505.23798) for evaluating gender and race bias in VLMs.

name: LRS2
format: Lip reading sentences: face video clips with audio, from BBC broadcasts. Includes variety of head poses and speaking styles.
metric: LSE-D, LSE-C, ID-P, ID-TC, MOS-Sync, MOS-Nat
notes: Large-scale English audio-visual dataset used for visual dubbing and lip reading. From Chung et al., CVPR 2017.

name: LRS3
format: Lip reading sentences: face video clips with audio, from TED and TEDx talks. More diverse and expressive speaking patterns than LRS2.
metric: LSE-D, LSE-C, ID-P, ID-TC, MOS-Sync, MOS-Nat
notes: Extension of LRS2 with more diverse content from TED and TEDx talks. From Afouras et al., arXiv:1809.00496.

name: LJ-Speech
format: Single-speaker English speech dataset: 13,100 audio clips from public domain audiobooks with transcripts.
notes: Single-speaker corpus used in EdiDub paper for HuBERT feature quantization (k-means clustering). The single-voice codebook nullifies speaker-identity dimensions in the latent space.

name: VoxCeleb2
eval_time: hours to days for full evaluation
format: YouTube celebrity speech video clips with tight head crops and audio. Larger and more diverse than VoxCeleb1.
metric: LSE-D, LSE-C, ID-P, ID-TC, MOS-Sync, MOS-Nat
license: research use only per VoxCeleb terms
notes: Extended VoxCeleb dataset from Chung et al., arXiv:1806.05622. Used in EdiDub paper for creating Vox2-Front and Vox2-Occluded benchmark subsets.

name: Mid-Air
num_samples: 400K+ RGB-D frames (79 min flight, paper uses 6,859 subsampled)
format: Synthetic RGB images and stereo disparity depth maps from Unreal Engine PLE plugin, annotated with 13 semantic classes for low-altitude drone flight segmentation
notes: Multi-modal dataset for extremely low altitude drone flights (Fonder & Van Droogenbroeck, CVPRW 2019). Paper subsampled to 6,859 images at 256x256 (1 frame every 8, spring season). Diverse weather and seasonal conditions. Used in arXiv:2505.24361 for cross-modal knowledge distillation evaluation.

name: ASVspoof 2019 LA
format: 4-second audio clips (16kHz), primary labels (fake/bona fide), attack type metadata
notes: ASVspoof 2019 Logical Access dataset for audio deepfake detection. Used as Experience 0 (E0) in RAIS paper (2505.24486). Contains English speech with various spoofing attacks.

name: VCC 2020
format: 4-second audio clips (16kHz), multi-language speech (English, German, Finnish)
notes: Voice Conversion Challenge 2020 dataset used as Experience 1 (E1) in RAIS paper (2505.24486). Multi-language dataset for speech deepfake detection.

name: InTheWild
format: 4-second audio clips (16kHz), English speech
notes: InTheWild audio deepfake dataset used as Experience 2 (E2) in RAIS paper (2505.24486). Contains more challenging, real-world deepfake examples.

name: CFAD
format: 4-second audio clips (16kHz), Chinese speech
notes: Chinese Fake Audio Dataset used as Experience 3 (E3) in RAIS paper (2505.24486). Contains Chinese speech deepfakes.

name: ACM
format: Citation network from ACM digital library. Node types: Paper, Author, Subject, Term. Edge types: Paper-Paper (citation), Paper-Subject, Paper-Term, Paper-Author. Task: paper node classification.
access: Heterogeneous Graph Benchmark (HGB) from Lv et al., KDD 2021
notes: Standard heterogeneous graph benchmark for HGNN evaluation. Refined version with all citation and reference edges.

name: DBLP
format: Bibliography network from DBLP. Node types: Author, Paper, Term, Conference. Edge types: Author-Paper, Paper-Term, Paper-Conference. Task: author node classification.
access: Heterogeneous Graph Benchmark (HGB) from Lv et al., KDD 2021
notes: Standard heterogeneous graph benchmark. Used for author classification across 4 research areas.

name: IMDB (Heterogeneous)
format: Movie network from IMDB. Node types: Movie, Director, Actor. Edge types: Movie-Director, Movie-Actor. Task: movie genre classification (5 classes).
access: Heterogeneous Graph Benchmark (HGB) from Lv et al., KDD 2021
notes: Heterogeneous movie network. Distinct from the NLP IMDB sentiment dataset.

name: CiteSeer
format: Citation network. Nodes: academic papers. Edges: citation links. Node features: bag-of-words (3,703 dimensions). Task: 6-class paper topic classification.
access: Planetoid dataset (Yang et al., ICML 2016) via torch-geometric or Stanford SNAP
notes: Standard citation network benchmark. Used in HGBA paper for homogeneous graph extensibility experiments.

name: PROTEINS
format: Protein dataset. Nodes: amino acids. Edges: pairs within 6 Angstroms. Task: 2-class graph classification (enzyme vs non-enzyme).
notes: Standard graph classification benchmark. Used in HGBA paper for homogeneous graph extensibility experiments on graph classification.

name: EvalCrafter
format: Text-to-video generation prompts covering diverse scenes, objects, and actions; evaluated using automated metrics CLIPSIM, CLIP-Temp, and DOVER's VQA score
metric: CLIPSIM (text-video alignment), CLIP-Temp (temporal consistency), DOVER VQA (aesthetic and technical quality)

name: GenImage++
num_samples: ~139k images (Flux:6k, Flux-multi:18.3k, Flux-photo:30k, Flux-real:6k, SD1.5-multi:18.3k, SDXL-multi:18.3k, SD3:6k, SD3-photo:30k, SD3-real:6k)
format: Test-only benchmark with AI-generated images from advanced generators (FLUX.1, SD3, SDXL, SD1.5) using diverse prompts including ImageNet labels, long prompts, and style variations
access: Test-only benchmark introduced in paper 2506.00874; images regenerated from paper's generation pipeline
notes: Introduced by Zhou et al. 2025. Designed to test detector generalization against modern DiT-based architectures (FLUX.1, SD3). Subsets include standard prompts, long-prompt comprehension, style diversity, and photorealistic portrait generation.

name: Chameleon-AIGC
num_samples: Not specified in paper (diverse AI-generated images collected in-the-wild)
format: Diverse AI-generated images collected from the wild with real image comparisons
notes: From 'A sanity check for AI-generated image detection' (Yan et al. 2024). Used in paper 2506.00874 to evaluate detector generalization on diverse in-the-wild AI-generated content.

name: Obman
format: Synthetic hand-object interaction images generated by rendering MANO hand meshes and ShapeNet object meshes on LSUN/ImageNet backgrounds; provides 3D hand pose (MANO parameters) and object meshes; used for template-free hand-object reconstruction benchmarks
license: research use (ShapeNet terms for object meshes)
notes: Introduced by Hasson et al. CVPR 2019. Used in TIGeR (arXiv:2506.00953) as one of two main evaluation benchmarks. Contains 2772 meshes from 8 ShapeNet categories with hand poses from GraspIt simulator.

name: MMEB (Massive Multi-modal Embedding Benchmark)
num_samples: 20 datasets for training, 36 for evaluation (662K training samples)
format: Multi-task evaluation across classification, VQA, retrieval, and grounding tasks with instruction-guided multimodal embeddings
notes: From Jiang et al. (VLM2Vec). Standard benchmark for evaluating MLLM-based multimodal embedding models. Training subset (MMEB-train) used for fine-tuning. Evaluation covers 20 in-distribution and 16 out-of-distribution datasets.

name: M3ToolEval
format: Multi-turn function-calling with code executor; Calculation environment (Travel Planner, DNA Sequencer, Message Decoder, Trade Calculator tools); Web Browsing environment (text-based web navigation)
notes: Multi-turn function-calling benchmark. From Wang et al. (2024). Calculation environment is fully observable; Web Browsing is partially observable.

name: SpuCo Birds
num_samples: ~15k images (natural bird images with water/land backgrounds)
format: Bird images (waterbird/landbird) with natural backgrounds (water/land), 4 test groups: waterbird-water, waterbird-land, landbird-water, landbird-land. Training subset has only 2 groups (waterbird-water, landbird-land), creating spurious background-feature correlation.

name: Spurious ImageNet
format: Subset of ImageNet with 100 classes where each class has a spurious feature (e.g., object appears with consistent background texture). Test set includes images with the spurious feature but without the true class object, measuring classifier reliance on spurious correlations.
metric: spuIN mAUC (mean spurious AUC over classes)

name: ACS (Acceptability Code-Switching) Benchmark
num_samples: Train: 7,501 minimal pairs, Val: 1,932 minimal pairs, Test: 1,000 minimal pairs per language pair (11 language pairs: de-en, da-en, es-en, fr-en, it-en, id-en, nl-en, sv-en, tr-en, tr-de, zh-en)
eval_time: minutes for CSntax-GNN; hours for LLM baselines
format: Minimal pairs of code-switching sentences. Each pair contains a naturally-occurring CS sentence and a synthetically manipulated version (language of one word changed at the switch point). Bilingual human judgments available for all pairs.
metric: Accuracy (which sentence in the minimal pair is more acceptable as natural CS)
notes: Acceptability Code-Switching benchmark for evaluating syntactic theories of code-switching. Minimal pairs of naturally-occurring vs. synthetically-manipulated CS sentences. Introduced in Sterner & Teufel (2025, ACL). Used as main benchmark in CSntax-GNN paper (Sterner & Teufel, ACL 2025).

name: SMN4Lang
storage: ~200-300GB (fMRI + MEG voxel time series + stimuli transcripts)
format: Paired fMRI (2s TR) and MEG recordings while subjects listened to Mandarin news broadcasts; aligned with transcript word onsets
license: Research use; contact Wang et al. Sci Data 2022 for access

name: LPPC-fMRI
num_samples: 112 subjects across 3 languages (49 English, 35 Chinese, 28 French), ~168 total hours
format: fMRI (2s TR) while subjects listened to The Little Prince in their native language; aligned with word onsets
license: Research use; contact Li et al. Sci Data 2022 for access

name: Broderick2018
format: EEG (high-density) while subjects listened to The Old Man and the Sea narrative; aligned with word-level transcripts
license: Research use; contact Broderick et al. Curr Biology 2018
access: Available via request from Trinity College Dublin

name: SparrKULee
format: EEG while subjects listened to Dutch audiobook; aligned with word-level transcripts
license: Research use; contact Accou et al. Data 2024 for access

name: RepoEval
num_samples: ~3 real-world repositories for API-level and line-level completion
format: Repository-level code completion tasks: line-level, API-level, and function-body completion from real-world repositories

name: HotPotQA
format: Multi-hop question answering requiring reasoning across multiple documents; includes sentence-level supporting facts for supervision

name: MM-NIAH (Multimodal Needle-in-a-Haystack)
format: Multimodal needle-in-a-haystack: specific information embedded in long multimodal (image+text) contexts; evaluates retrieval of hidden information

name: CoIN
num_samples: 6 image QA tasks (VQAV2, TextVQA, OCR-VQA, ScienceQA, VizWizVQA, GQA); extended version adds AI2D, AOKVQA-MC, OKVQA, RSVQA-LR (10 tasks); video QA version includes MSVD-QA, MSRVTT-QA, ActivityNet-QA
format: Continual instruction tuning benchmark for VLMs. Tasks evaluated sequentially in order; model tested on all seen tasks at each step. Metrics: ACC (average accuracy), BWT (backward transfer / forgetting), FWT (forward transfer / generalization), At (plasticity / immediate task accuracy)
license: Varies by constituent dataset (CC BY 4.0, Apache 2.0, etc.)
notes: Continual Instruction Tuning benchmark for multimodal LLMs from NeurIPS 2024 D&B track. Base model used in this paper: PaliGemma-3B. Used in arXiv:2506.03189 for evaluating PAM (Parameter Alignment for Merging) on CL in VLMs.

name: Infinity-Doc-400K
format: Rendered scanned document pages paired with Markdown ground-truth; spans financial reports, medical reports, academic papers, books, magazines, web pages, and synthetic documents

name: ScanNet-1500
eval_time: minutes for pose estimation per pair
format: Selected image pairs from ScanNet RGB-D indoor scenes with known camera poses. Used for two-view relative pose estimation evaluation. Pairs selected for co-visible regions.
metric: AUC@5°, AUC@10°, AUC@20° for pose error (max of rotation and translation error in degrees)
access: https://github.com/ScanNet/ScanNet (original); pairs curated from Superglue/LoFTR evaluations
notes: Subset of ScanNet used for two-view geometry estimation benchmarks. Originally introduced with LoFTR (Sun et al., CVPR 2021). Used in Dense Match Summarization paper (arXiv:2506.02893) for indoor scene evaluation. Inlier threshold 2.5 pixels.

name: WxBS
format: Wide-baseline stereo image pairs with provided ground-truth correspondences. Designed to test matching under extreme viewpoint changes, illumination variations, and repetitive structures. Fundamental matrix estimation benchmark.
metric: Recall@10px (percentage of correspondences with errors below 10 pixels), AUC for fundamental matrix error
notes: Wide Baseline Stereo Generalizations benchmark. Mishkin et al., BMVC 2015. Used in Dense Match Summarization paper (arXiv:2506.02893) for uncalibrated (fundamental matrix) evaluation. Particularly challenging due to large viewpoint changes and texture-poor regions.

name: HueManity
num_samples: 83,850 generated Ishihara-style images (numeric + alphanumeric recognition tasks)
format: Ishihara-style dot pattern images embedding alphanumeric strings; exact-match accuracy scoring
notes: Benchmark for fine-grained visual perception in MLLMs. Tests ability to identify alphanumeric characters embedded in Ishihara-style dot patterns. Key finding: best MLLM (GPT-4.1) achieves only 33.6% on numeric task and 3% on alphanumeric, vs 99.4% human accuracy. Dataset generated procedurally with CIEDE2000 color difference metric for systematic difficulty control.

name: MedExQA
num_samples: ~773 QA pairs across 4 specialties (biomedical engineering, clinical laboratory science, clinical psychology, occupational therapy)
format: Medical multiple-choice questions with human-written explanations from medical textbooks and academic literature. Each QA pair includes question, 4 answer options, correct answer, and reference explanations.
notes: Introduced by Kim et al. 2024. Designed for medical question answering with multiple explanations. Speech Language Pathology subset excluded due to inconsistencies between questions and explanations.

name: MMR-V
eval_time: hours (1,257 questions with variable frame sampling)
format: Long-form YouTube videos (7-3771s) with manually annotated multiple-choice questions requiring long-range multi-frame multimodal reasoning; implicit/explicit reasoning taxonomy

name: EgoPAT3D-DT
format: RGB-D egocentric videos of hand-object interactions with contact/separation timestamps

name: DeskTIL
num_samples: 150 video sequences (50 per desk clutter level)
format: RGB-D egocentric videos of hand-object interactions at a desk with contact/separation annotations
license: To be determined (new benchmark from paper)
access: Not yet released (paper proposes this benchmark)

name: MMMU-Pro
format: More robust multi-discipline multimodal understanding benchmark; 10-option multiple choice QA across 30 subjects requiring expert-level knowledge
notes: Yue et al., 2024. Enhanced version of MMMU with 10-option questions (vs 4-option) for more robust evaluation.

name: CMMMU
format: Chinese massive multi-discipline multimodal understanding benchmark; expert-level QA across multiple disciplines in Chinese
notes: Zhang et al., 2024. Chinese counterpart to MMMU benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on Chinese multimodal understanding.

name: Financial Phrase-Bank
format: Short financial news sentences (from LexisNexis) labeled with 3-class sentiment (positive/neutral/negative) by 5-8 finance-savvy annotators; includes inter-annotator agreement levels

name: CG-AV-Counting
num_samples: 1,027 questions across 497 long videos (>10 min each)
eval_time: hours (1,027 samples with dual black-box/white-box evaluation)
format: Long videos (>10 min) with multimodal counting queries (visual-only, audio-only, visual-reference audio-query, audio-reference visual-query, joint audio-visual); includes fine-grained clue annotations (timestamps, bounding boxes)
metric: Accuracy, OBOA, MAE, RMSE (black-box); WCS tIoU/cIoU (white-box)
notes: Clue-grounded audio-visual counting benchmark for MLLMs. Covers event, object, and attribute counting targets. Dual evaluation: black-box (end-to-end counting) and white-box (reasoning with explicit evidence). Introduced in arXiv:2506.05328.

name: WAVES (Watermark Analysis Via Extensive Sets)
format: Benchmark for evaluating watermark robustness under various image distortions: geometric (rotation, resized-crop, erasing), photometric (brightness, contrast), degradation (JPEG, Gaussian blur, Gaussian noise)
metric: ASR (Attack Success Rate), EAR (Error Attack Rate), PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS
notes: WAVES benchmark from An et al. (ICML 2024). Used in arXiv:2506.04879 to evaluate robustness of invisible backdoor triggers under real-world image distortions.

name: MIRFLICKR
format: 1M images collected from Flickr with associated user tags, containing diverse visual content. Used for training watermark embedding models (StegaStamp, RoSteALS).
notes: MIRFLICKR dataset used in arXiv:2506.04879 for training StegaStamp watermark model (100k subset) and RoSteALS training.

name: SAKURA
format: Audio clips with textual prompts for multi-hop reasoning on speaker gender, spoken language, speaker emotion, and animal sound attributes (500 samples per attribute)
notes: Benchmark for evaluating multi-hop reasoning of large audio-language models (Interspeech 2025). Used in AudioLens (arXiv:2506.05140) as the primary evaluation dataset for studying auditory attribute perception in LALMs.

name: MMTU
eval_time: hours (API inference) to days (local model inference)
format: Standardized triplet format: <Instruction, Input-Table(s), Ground-truth answer>. Supports execution-based evaluation (SQL, Python), structured output evaluation (JSON), and accuracy/F1 metrics.
notes: Massive Multi-Task Table Understanding benchmark. Curated from 52 existing datasets across data management and programming languages communities. Covers 25 real-world table tasks including column transformation, table matching, data cleaning, table join, NL-to-SQL, table QA, KB mapping, etc. Even frontier models (GPT-5, DeepSeek-R1) score only ~70% and ~58% respectively.

name: HEST-1k
num_samples: 74 whole-slide images across 10 organs (IDC=4, PRAD=23, PAAD=3, SKCM=2, COAD=6, READ=4, CCRCC=24, HCC=2, LUNG=2, LYMPH=4)
eval_time: minutes per sample for gene expression prediction
format: H&E-stained whole-slide images paired with spatial transcriptomics gene expression data (top 50 highly variable genes). Technologies: Xenium, Visium. Patient-stratified cross-validation splits.
metric: Pearson correlation (between predicted and measured gene expression)
notes: From Jaume et al. (2024). Used in STFlow paper (arXiv:2506.05361) for spatial transcriptomics prediction from histology images.

name: STImage-1K4M
num_samples: 146 whole-slide images across 7 organs (Breast=81, Brain=22, Skin=4, Mouth=16, Prostate=7, Stomach=12, Colon=4)
eval_time: minutes per sample for gene expression prediction
format: H&E-stained whole-slide images paired with spatial transcriptomics gene expression data. Technology: Visium. Random 8:1:1 train/val/test split at slide level.
metric: Pearson correlation (between predicted and measured gene expression)
notes: From Chen et al. (2024a). Used in STFlow paper (arXiv:2506.05361) for spatial transcriptomics prediction from histology images.

name: CoNLL-2009 (English)
format: Dependency-based SRL with predicate-argument structures; English
access: https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2012T03 (LDC), or CoNLL shared task page

name: CoNLL-2009 (Chinese)
format: Dependency-based SRL with predicate-argument structures; Chinese
access: https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2012T03 (LDC), or CoNLL shared task page

name: CoNLL-2012 (English)
format: Span-based SRL derived from OntoNotes; English

name: CPB1.0 (Chinese Proposition Bank 1.0)
format: Span-based SRL; Chinese
access: Chinese Proposition Bank (CPB) - available via LDC or research institutions

name: ESConv
format: Multi-turn emotional support dialogue dataset with seeker-supporter conversations; annotations include emotional strategies, responses, and problem types
metric: Human evaluation across multiple dimensions (Empathy, Informativeness, Identification, Comforting, Suggestion, Overall) plus GPT-4-based ranking
notes: Introduced by Liu et al. (2021). Standard benchmark for emotional support conversation research. Used for training and evaluation in IntentionESC paper (arXiv:2506.05947).

name: RTLLM
format: RTL (Verilog) code generation from natural language specifications; tests functional correctness of generated hardware designs
access: https://github.com/AIoT-MLSys-Lab/RTLLM (estimated from Lu et al., ASP-DAC 2024)
notes: RTLLM: Open-source benchmark for design RTL generation with large language model. From Lu et al., ASP-DAC 2024. Used in ScaleRTL paper (arXiv:2506.05566) to evaluate RTL code generation. Contains diverse RTL coding problems across complexity levels.

name: PersonalRewardBench
num_samples: 854 users (131 Chatbot Arena + 723 PRISM); 18,043 total preference pairs
eval_time: hours (depending on model size and trials)
format: User-stratified pairwise preference data for evaluating personalized reward models; filtered for personalizable queries with LLM-as-Judge disagreement
license: CC BY 4.0 (derived from Chatbot Arena and PRISM)
notes: Introduced by Ryan et al. 2025. Curated from Chatbot Arena (33K users filtered to 131) and PRISM (1,396 users filtered to 723) via user filter (>=5 pairs), personalizable filter (GPT-4o-mini), and quality/disagreement filter (5 LLM judges). 40/10/50 train/val/test user split. Tests personalization of LLM-as-Judge and fine-tuned reward models.

name: MultiPL-E
num_samples: 164 samples per language (HumanEval translated to 18 programming languages)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model size
format: Code completion tasks from HumanEval translated to C++, C#, PHP, Bash, Java, JavaScript, Rust, Go, TypeScript, and more
notes: From Ben Allal et al. 2022. Multi-language version of HumanEval. Paper uses C++, C#, PHP, Bash, Java, JavaScript subsets.

name: AURORA
num_samples: ~50K+ video frame pairs with action annotations (across MagicBrush, Action-Genome, Something-Something, WhatsUp, Kubric subsets)
format: Video frame pairs (source, target observations) with linguistic action descriptions, formatted as (o_s, a, o_t) triplets for forward dynamics prediction and (o_s, o_t, a) for inverse dynamics prediction
notes: AURORA is a dataset of action-annotated video frame pairs for learning action-centric image editing. Used as the core training and evaluation dataset in the paper. AURORA-BENCH is the evaluation benchmark derived from this dataset. From Krojer et al. (2024), NeurIPS Spotlight Paper.

name: Action-Genome
num_samples: ~10K+ video frames with scene graph annotations
format: Video frames annotated with scene graphs (objects, attributes, relationships) and actions. Frame pairs with action descriptions as (o_s, a, o_t) triplets.
notes: Subset of AURORA-BENCH used for evaluating action-centric next-observation prediction. Focuses on real-world human actions captured in indoor scenes.

name: WhatsUp
format: Video frame pairs (o_s, o_t) with spatial action descriptions in language form, e.g., 'move the book under the table'. Part of AURORA-BENCH.
metric: GPT4o-as-judge for spatial reasoning and action editing
notes: AURORA-BENCH subset focusing on spatial reasoning — actions that require understanding spatial relations between objects in a fixed scene.

name: SpatialMQA
format: Multi-view spatial reasoning questions requiring understanding of spatial relations (e.g., left/right, above/below) from visual input
notes: Spatial reasoning benchmark used to evaluate transfer of FDP capabilities to broader spatial understanding tasks. From Liu et al. (2025).

name: EmbodiedSpatial-Bench
format: Embodied AI tasks requiring spatial understanding from visual observations, testing generalization of VLM world models
access: referenced in paper as Du et al. (2024), ACL Findings
notes: Embodied spatial reasoning benchmark to test whether FDP training improves spatial understanding in embodied agents. From Du et al. (2024).

name: MULTIVENT 2.0
num_samples: 101K multilingual videos with ~1.5K human-annotated queries (public split)
eval_time: hours per model for full evaluation
format: Event-centric videos with ASR transcripts, OCR text, metadata, and text queries requiring retrieval across multiple modalities

name: MULTIVENT 2.0++
num_samples: 371,644 synthetic modality-targeted query-document pairs (367,644 train + 4,000 val), 1,504 test queries from MULTIVENT 2.0
storage: Inherits from MULTIVENT 2.0 plus ~few MB for synthetic queries
format: Synthetically generated modality-specific queries for video, ASR, OCR, and metadata; built on top of MULTIVENT 2.0 unannotated videos; used to train CLAMR for dynamic modality selection

name: DesignBench
eval_time: hours to evaluate full benchmark across 9 models
format: UI mockup images + ground truth code + modification instructions + issue annotations
metric: CLIP, SSIM, CSR, CMLS, CMCS, MLLM-as-Judge scores
notes: Multi-framework multi-task benchmark for MLLM-based front-end code generation. Covers React, Vue, Angular, and vanilla HTML/CSS. Tasks: design generation (UI image to code), design edit (modify existing code), design repair (fix UI issues). From arXiv:2506.06251.

name: Wireframe
num_samples: ~5K annotated images with line segments and junctions
format: Images of man-made environments with annotated wireframe line segments and junctions

name: CryoBench
num_samples: IgG-1D: 100K particles (100 states x 1K images); IgG-RL: 100K particles (100 states x 1K images); Ribosembly: 335K particles (16 states)
storage: ~50-100GB estimated (128x128 particle images with CTF parameters)
format: Synthetic cryo-EM particle images (128x128 pixels) with ground-truth 3D structures, poses, and CTF parameters. SNR=0.01.
notes: Benchmark for heterogeneous cryo-EM reconstruction. Introduced by Jeon et al. (NeurIPS 2024). Includes conformational heterogeneity (IgG-1D, IgG-RL with dihedral angle variation) and compositional heterogeneity (Ribosembly with progressive subunit assembly). Ground-truth labels enable quantitative evaluation.

name: EMPIAR-10076
num_samples: 131,899 particle images (320x320 pixels, 1.31 Å pixel size)
format: Raw cryo-EM particle images of E. coli large ribosomal subunit assemblies. 4 major assembly states identified.
notes: EMPIAR (Electron Microscopy Public Image Archive) entry for E. coli LSU assembly intermediates. Used for experimental evaluation in CryoSPIRE paper.

name: EMPIAR-10180
num_samples: 327,490 raw images (139,722 filtered subset used, 320x320 pixels, 1.69 Å pixel size)
format: Raw cryo-EM particle images of Pre-Catalytic Spliceosome. Conformationally heterogeneous dataset.
notes: EMPIAR entry for Pre-Catalytic Spliceosome. Used for experimental evaluation in CryoSPIRE paper.

name: MSQA
num_samples: ~hundreds of QA pairs across multiple scene domains (ScanNet, 3RScan, ARKitScenes)
format: Multi-scale situated 3D question answering benchmark evaluating QA across different scene domains, with question types including counting, existence, attribute, spatial, navigation, and others

name: Beacon3D
num_samples: ~thousands of QA pairs across 3RScan and MultiScan scene domains
format: Robust 3D QA evaluation benchmark for out-of-domain generalization across diverse indoor scene domains (3RScan, MultiScan). Evaluates both case-centric and object-centric metrics.
access: Referenced in LEO-VL paper (Huang et al., 2025b) as arXiv submission

name: CLIMATEVIZ
format: Chart images + captions + claims with labels (support/refute/NEI) + knowledge graph explanations (h,r,t triplets)
metric: accuracy, macro-F1, BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE-L, BERTScore
notes: First large-scale benchmark for scientific fact-checking on real-world climate charts requiring statistical reasoning. From Su et al. (arXiv:2506.08700). Claims require multi-hop statistical reasoning (79% need 3+ reasoning types). Evaluates VLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5, o3, InternVL, Qwen2.5-VL, LLaMA-4, Matcha). Human performance: 89.3-92.7% accuracy.

name: StepEval-Audio-360
format: Audio query-response pairs with human voice recordings in Chinese (Mandarin, Sichuan, Cantonese dialects), English, and Japanese; evaluated across 9 dimensions: singing, creativity, role-playing, logical reasoning, voice instruction following, voice understanding, gaming, speech emotion control, language ability
metric: MOS (Mean Opinion Score) 1-5 for naturalness and task completion by expert human evaluators
notes: Comprehensive benchmark for LALMs in human-AI audio interaction. Released by StepFun. Used as the primary evaluation benchmark for Step-Audio-AQAA (arXiv:2506.08967), which outperforms Kimi-Audio and Qwen-Omni on most dimensions.

name: DyCheck
num_samples: 7 long monocular videos (200-400 frames each) with iPhone capture + 2 synchronized novel-view cameras
format: Casual monocular videos with synchronized novel-view cameras for dynamic novel-view synthesis evaluation; includes covisibility labeling between input and novel-view cameras
metric: PSNR, LPIPS (for view synthesis quality); per-frame and trajectory-level evaluation
license: research use (paper: Hang Gao et al., NeurIPS 2022)
notes: DyCheck benchmarks dynamic novel-view synthesis from casual monocular videos. iPhone subset provides ground-truth novel views for quantitative evaluation. Paper also uses dynamic mask evaluation (DynMask) for foreground-only comparison.

name: VinDr-Mammo (Full-Field Digital Mammography)
num_samples: 20,000 mammography images (~13,942 healthy images from Siemens Mammomat Inspiration after filtering)
format: Full-field digital mammography (FFDM) DICOM images in DICOM format; BI-RADS categories; healthy vs lesion annotations; CC and MLO views
notes: From Nguyen et al. (2023). Used in MAMBO paper (2506.08677) for training diffusion models on healthy mammograms. Training restricted to healthy images only.

name: RSNA Screening Mammography Breast Cancer Detection
num_samples: 54,706 mammography images from 10 different machines (single machine ID 49 used: 14,898 images)
format: Full-field digital mammography images; cancer detection labels; CC and MLO views; diverse tissue types
notes: From RSNA (2024). Used in MAMBO paper (2506.08677) for training and evaluation. Resolution ~4096x3328 pixels.

name: InBreast
num_samples: 410 full-field digital mammograms (107 with masses for anomaly segmentation)
format: Full-field digital mammography (FFDM); pixel-wise lesion annotations (masses, calcifications, asymmetries, distortions); biopsy-confirmed labels
notes: From Moreira et al. (2012). Used in MAMBO paper (2506.08677) for zero-shot anomaly segmentation evaluation. Lesion types: masses (107 images), asymmetries, distortions, calcifications.

name: CLEVRER
format: Synthetic videos of colliding objects with 4 question types (descriptive, explanatory, predictive, counterfactual)
notes: Collision events for video representation and reasoning. Counterfactual questions ask what would happen if certain objects were removed. Introduced by Yi et al. (ICLR 2019).

name: CRAFT
eval_time: minutes to hours for API-based evaluation
format: Videos of falling/sliding objects with causal questions including counterfactual
access: https://github.com/tayfun/ CRAFT (referenced in paper as arXiv:2012.04293)
notes: Causal Reasoning About Forces and Interactions. Benchmark for causal reasoning about physical events. Introduced by Ates et al. (2020). Counterfactual questions include 6 types requiring multiple counterfactual simulations.

name: S-MedQA
format: Multiple-choice clinical QA (4 options) combining MedQA and MedMCQA with EU medical specialty annotations; covers Gastroenterology, Cardiology, Obstetrics/Gynecology, Neurology, Infectious Diseases, Pediatrics
notes: Specialty-aware clinical QA benchmark combining MedQA and MedMCQA with specialty mappings. Used in Testoni & Calixto (2026) for LLM uncertainty quantification.

name: CoVLA (Comprehensive Vision-Language-Action Dataset)
num_samples: 10,000 front-view 30s driving videos (300K frames) at 20Hz, with ego trajectory and language annotations
format: Front-view RGB videos (1208x1928 downsampled to 512x512), 4-second past ego trajectory (16 steps at 4Hz), 5-second future ego trajectory (20 steps at 4Hz), auto-generated language captions (critical objects, explanation, meta-behavior)
notes: CoVLA: Comprehensive Vision-Language-Action Dataset for Autonomous Driving. Japanese driving data collected in Tokyo area. Used for VLT (Vision-Language-Trajectory) pretraining in Poutine (arXiv:2506.11234). Enables next-token prediction over vision, language, and trajectory tokens. Shows strong zero-shot transfer to US driving data (WOD-E2E).

name: ChatDoctor
format: Patient symptom descriptions paired with doctor responses for medical Q&A and chat-completion fine-tuning
notes: Medical dialogue dataset from Li et al. (2023). Base dataset for PropInfer benchmark (arXiv:2506.10364) which adds property labels for gender (29,791 samples), mental disorder, digestive disorder, and childbirth.

name: PropInfer
num_samples: Varies by task: gender task uses 6500 training + 14791 aux; medical diagnosis uses 50000
eval_time: Hours per model (includes fine-tuning, generation, labeling)
format: Property inference attack evaluation: black-box generation attack and grey-box word-frequency shadow-model attack against fine-tuned LLMs
metric: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) between predicted and ground-truth property ratios
notes: Benchmark for evaluating property inference attacks on LLMs fine-tuned on ChatDoctor. Two fine-tuning modes: Q&A (SFT) and Chat-Completion (CLM-FT). Properties: gender (female ratio 30/50/70%), mental disorder (5.10%), digestive disorder (12.68%), childbirth (10.6%). From Huang et al. (arXiv:2506.10364).

name: TACRED
format: Sentence-level relation extraction dataset with entity mentions marked by position-aware attention. Entities tagged with subject/object markers and types.
notes: Standard general-domain RE benchmark (Zhang et al., 2017). Used in entity bias studies including SCM (Wang et al., 2023a) and VIB (Mensah et al., arXiv:2506.11381). OOD evaluation uses entity replacement.

name: REFinD
format: Financial domain relation extraction dataset with entity types specific to finance (org:money:revenue, pers:title:title, etc.).
notes: Financial RE dataset (Kaur et al., SIGIR 2023). Used in VIB-based entity bias mitigation paper (Mensah et al., arXiv:2506.11381). Contains entity-replaced OOD test sets.

name: LOGIPLAN
eval_time: 1-2 hours for full evaluation across 9 models with 5 runs
format: Synthetic relational graphs with parametric complexity (objects 3-50, relations up to 300, cycle depths 0-24)
notes: LOGIPLAN evaluates LLM logical planning and relational reasoning via three tasks: Plan Generation (construct valid directed graphs), Consistency Detection (identify cycles/contradictions), Comparison Question (determine relation validity). Also evaluates self-correction via 'Are you sure?' prompt. From Cai et al. 2025.

name: Travel-Sim
num_samples: 112 (16 traveler types x 7 Chinese cities x 1-3 day duration)
eval_time: hours (simulation-based, ~20K tokens/sample, ~$12 per full run for Gemini 2.5 API)
format: Agent-based travel simulation: LLM-powered traveler agent (Gemini 2.5) executes plans in event-driven sandbox with stamina engine, real-world map data, and travel blog context; evaluates multi-granularity feedback across 5 dimensions (experience, interest, arrangement, stamina, cost) at per-POI, per-day, and per-trip levels
metric: CPH (comprehensiveness), CPL (completeness), FEA/TPSS (feasibility/trajectory similarity), PER (personalization, composite of 5 criteria x 3 granularities)
license: Academic Use Only (Red Note/Xiaohongshu content + Google Gemini terms)
access: Not yet released (coming soon per paper)
notes: Novel agent-based simulation benchmark for travel planning that captures causal dependencies in itineraries (unlike static rule-based benchmarks). Introduced by Yang et al. (arXiv:2506.12421). Travel-Sim evaluates plans by simulating actual travel execution via traveler agent, capturing emergent behaviors (e.g., skipping activities due to fatigue). Maps causal dependencies between planned and simulated trajectories.

name: EDOS
format: Online sexism detection: EDOS-A (binary), EDOS-B (3-class), EDOS-C (11-class) with explanatory justification labels
notes: SemEval 2023 Task 10 dataset for explainable detection of online sexism. Used in Refract ICL paper (arXiv:2506.12346) as EDOS-A (binary) and EDOS-B (3-class) classification tasks.

name: COUNTFACT
format: Counterfactual product reviews in English, German, and Japanese with binary sentiment labels
notes: Counterfactual detection dataset for multilingual product review sentiment analysis. Used in Refract ICL paper (arXiv:2506.12346) for multi-class text classification across English, German, Japanese.

name: MTOP
format: Multilingual task-oriented semantic parsing: intent classification and slot filling in 6 languages (English, German, Spanish, French, Hindi, Thai)
notes: MTOP: Comprehensive Multilingual Task-Oriented Semantic Parsing Benchmark. Used in Refract ICL paper (arXiv:2506.12346) as MTOP-intent for multi-class classification.

name: DDI13
format: Drug-drug interaction extraction from PubMed; 5 interaction types (advise, effect, int, mechanism, null)
notes: Drug-Drug Interaction corpus from SemEval 2013 Task 9. Used in Refract ICL paper (arXiv:2506.12346) for relation classification.

name: XML-MT
num_samples: ~13K train / 1K dev / 1K test per language pair
format: Structured documentation translation with XML markup annotations for domain-specific terminology
notes: High-Quality Multilingual Dataset for Structured Documentation Translation. Language pairs: English-Finnish (en-fi) and English-Japanese (en-ja). Used in Refract ICL paper (arXiv:2506.12346) for machine translation.

name: AF-SENTIMENT
format: Aspect-free sentiment classification dataset
access: Not publicly released (referenced in Refract ICL paper)
notes: Aspect-free sentiment classification. Used in Refract ICL paper (arXiv:2506.12346) as a binary classification task with smaller number of output classes.

name: 7Scenes
num_samples: 7 scenes (chess, fire, heads, office, pumpkin, kitchen, stairs), ~500-1000 RGB-D frames per scene
format: RGB-D images with camera poses for scene-level 3D reconstruction and camera relocalization
metric: Accuracy, Completion, Normal Consistency (for 3D reconstruction); re-localization error (for relocalization)
notes: Microsoft RGB-D dataset for indoor scene reconstruction. Used in Test3R (arXiv:2506.13750) for 3D reconstruction evaluation with sparse views (3-5 views per scene). Ground truth camera poses and depth maps available.

name: NRGBD
format: RGB-D images for neural surface reconstruction; used in Test3R paper with 2-4 views per scene
notes: Neural RGB-D Surface Reconstruction dataset. Used in Test3R (arXiv:2506.13750) for 3D reconstruction evaluation with sparse multi-view inputs.

name: HMDB51
format: Short video clips labeled with human action classes (diverse sources: movies, YouTube, etc.)
notes: HMDB51 is a large human motion database. Used for few-shot action recognition evaluation in this paper. Standard split: 3570 train / 3530 test clips. Paper: Wang et al. 2015.

name: garak (LLM Security Probing Framework)
eval_time: Minutes to hours depending on model size and number of probes
format: Red-teaming framework that generates adversarial prompts and scores Attack Success Rate (ASR) based on model compliance with malicious intent. Probe categories: ANSI Escape, DAN Roleplay, Prompt Injection, Adversarial Suffix, TAP, XSS, Malware Generation.
metric: Attack Success Rate (ASR) — proportion of probes resulting in successful compliance with malicious intent
notes: Open-source LLM security probing framework from NVIDIA (Derczynski et al., 2024). Used in arXiv:2506.13726 to evaluate reasoning vs non-reasoning model security. Not a traditional benchmark but a red-teaming tool.

name: HHH-Alignment
num_samples: ~3k preference pairs (estimated, from HH-RLHF Harmless/Helpful/Honesty evaluation splits)
format: Pairwise preference evaluation across Harmless, Helpful, and Honesty dimensions; derived from Anthropic HH-RLHF evaluation data. Used in RewardBench evaluation as out-of-distribution test for reward models.
notes: HHH-Alignment benchmark evaluates reward models on Harmless, Helpful, and Honest preference prediction. Used as OOD evaluation in GRAM paper (arXiv:2506.14175) alongside RewardBench. Sub-categories: Harmless, Helpful, Honesty.

name: DPST (Deep Photo Style Transfer)
format: Photograph pairs for content and style images. Created by Luan et al. (2017). Lacks ground truth stylized images, contains potential scene mismatches, and includes some artistic paintings rather than purely photorealistic transfers.
notes: Deep Photo Style Transfer dataset (Luan et al., 2017). Used as a generalization test set in SA-LUT paper (2506.13465). Note: this dataset has known limitations (no ground truth, some non-photorealistic styles) — authors of SA-LUT introduced PST50 to address these gaps.

name: ELI-WHY
eval_time: minutes to hours (depends on number of explanations generated)
format: Question-explanation pairs with educational level labels (elementary, high school, graduate); includes GPT-4-generated, web-retrieved, and human-curated explanations
metric: Perceived Background Match (% of explanations where intended educational level matches perceived level); % Informative Explanations; readability metrics (Flesch-Kincaid, Linsear Write, Dale-Chall, TE Score)
notes: Benchmark for evaluating pedagogical utility of LLM explanations. Questions generated via few-shot GPT-4 prompting from 50 seed questions (Sulik et al. 2023), filtered by crowdworkers. Key finding: GPT-4 explanations match intended educational level only ~50% of the time (vs 79% for human-curated).

name: PhilEO Bench
num_samples: Not specified in paper; n-shot evaluation protocol with varying number of samples per country
storage: Not specified (evaluation benchmark, not pretraining data)
format: Sentinel-2 multispectral satellite imagery 128x128 tiles with 10 spectral bands; three downstream tasks: building density regression, road density regression (pixel-wise RMSE), land cover segmentation with 11 classes (Overall Accuracy)
notes: Introduced in Fibaek et al. 2024. Used for evaluating geospatial foundation models in n-shot settings (1-1000 shots). Tasks: building/road density estimation (regression) and land cover mapping (11-class segmentation using ESA WorldCover reference).

name: MajorTOM
num_samples: Approximately 60TB of unlabeled global Sentinel-2 data; subset used is 23TB
storage: ~23TB for the 23TB subset used in paper (full dataset ~60TB)
format: Cloud-free Sentinel-2 snapshots covering every location on Earth, including oceans and land ice; multi-spectral 10-band imagery at 10m resolution
notes: Largest existing ESA Sentinel-2 dataset providing cloud-free snapshot of every location on Earth. The 23TB subset used in the paper spans land, oceans, and ice. Temporal coverage spans a decade with random time steps.

name: FastTOM
format: Sentinel-2 multi-spectral imagery subset of MajorTOM containing only land areas (excluding oceans and ice)
notes: 2TB subset of MajorTOM 23TB, containing only land and excluding oceans and ice. More task-specific for terrestrial downstream tasks like road/building density and land cover.

name: PhilEO Globe
format: Sentinel-2 L2A imagery focused only on land (excluding oceans and ice); four time steps per location (one per season)
notes: 0.5TB dataset provided with PhilEO Bench. Seasonal structure (4 time steps per location) makes it particularly effective for land cover classification tasks.

name: AirGapAgent-R
num_samples: 4,160 prompts (20 synthetic user profiles × 26 fields × 8 scenarios)
eval_time: minutes to hours for full evaluation across models
format: Synthetic user profiles with privacy scenarios; measures utility (shares when appropriate) and privacy (does not share when inappropriate)
metric: Utility and Privacy scores (binary: shares appropriate data / withholds inappropriate data)
notes: Open-source reconstruction of unreleased AirGapAgent benchmark (Bagdasarian et al., 2024). Used in Leaky Thoughts (arXiv:2506.15674) to evaluate privacy leakage in reasoning traces of LLMs and LRMs.

name: AgentDAM
num_samples: Not fully specified; multiple task domains (shopping, Reddit, GitLab)
eval_time: Up to 18 hours per split on 2×H100 GPUs
format: Agentic benchmark: models interact with simulated web environments via text accessibility tree; privacy evaluated per action using gpt-4o-mini
metric: Task success rate + privacy score per action
license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (with MIT components like VisualWebArena)
access: https://github.com/arpit2/AgentDAM or similar (original authors: Zharmagambetov et al., 2025)
notes: Evaluates contextual privacy in agentic settings. Used in Leaky Thoughts (arXiv:2506.15674) for agentic evaluation of LRM privacy.

name: EGD-CXR
num_samples: 1,083 chest X-ray images with synchronized eye-tracking data and radiology report transcription
format: Chest X-ray DICOM images paired with eye-tracking fixations (x, y, duration, timestamps) and dictated radiology reports with sentence-level timestamps for alignment
metric: N/A (raw data for downstream task; downstream tasks: multilabel classification of perceptual errors)
notes: Expert gaze data chest X-ray dataset. Contains synchronized eye-tracking from an experienced radiologist reading CXRs, with dictation transcripts time-aligned to gaze data. Used as base dataset for this paper's simulated perceptual error dataset.

name: TORQUE
format: passage + question groups asking temporal relations between events; answers are event spans

name: TB-Dense
format: document with two event mentions; classify temporal relation into 6 types (Before/After/Simultaneous/Includes/Is Included/Vague)

name: MICCAI FLARE 2022
num_samples: 50 CT scans (40 for training/context, 10 for testing with 922 annotated slices)
format: Abdominal CT scans with 10-organ segmentation annotations (Liver, Right Kidney, Spleen, Pancreas, Aorta, IVC, Gallbladder, Esophagus, Stomach, Left Kidney)

name: MVTec LOCO AD
num_samples: 3644 images from 5 categories (Breakfast Box, Screw Bag, Pushpins, Splicing Connectors, Juice Bottle)
format: Industrial images with pixel-annotated logical and structural anomalies; training/validation sets contain only anomaly-free images; test set contains both normal and abnormal samples
notes: MVTec Logical Constraints Anomaly Detection dataset. Introduced by Bergmann et al. (IJCV 2022). Contains both logical anomalies (violations of logical/geometric constraints) and structural anomalies (visible defects). Approximately 1:1 ratio of logical to structural anomalies. Used as primary benchmark in NPGMF paper (2506.18544).

name: Skywork-SWE
num_samples: 10,169 validated Python GitHub issue-fix instances from 2,531 repositories
format: GitHub issues with failing tests, gold patches, and dedicated runtime environment Docker images for automated unit-test validation
metric: N/A (training data; evaluated on SWE-bench Verified)
notes: Large-scale SWE training dataset. Each instance has executable Docker environment for test validation. Collected 8,209+ successful agent trajectories used to train Skywork-SWE-32B. From arXiv:2506.19290.

name: SENT140
num_samples: ~1.6M tweets (183 clients (authors) with ~72 samples average; naturally partitioned by author)
format: Tweets with binary sentiment labels (positive/negative), 140-character limit; federated partition by author from LEAF benchmark (Caldas et al. 2018)
access: https://github.com/TalwalkarLab/leaf (LEAF benchmark, Caldas et al. 2018); original: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/kazanova/sentiment140
notes: Sentiment140 (Sentences of 140 characters) is a Twitter sentiment dataset used in federated learning benchmarks (LEAF). Used in FedBKD (arXiv:2506.20245) with 183 clients, 2 classes, ~72 samples per client average.

name: PathMMU
num_samples: 9,677 test Q&A pairs with 7,213 images; 1,156 test-tiny subset
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model size
format: Pathology VQA: multiple choice questions with expert-validated answers across 5 categories (PubMed, SocialPath, EduContent, Atlas, PathCLS)

name: DDxBench
num_samples: 150 H&E stained WSIs with 52 unique diagnoses
eval_time: Minutes per slide for multi-agent analysis
format: Open-ended differential diagnosis benchmark: multi-image understanding with representative tumor ROIs from whole slide images
access: Not publicly released (curated from in-house database)

name: UniToPatho
format: Colorectal polyp classification: 6 tissue types (Normal, hyperplastic polyp, tubular adenoma high/low-grade dysplasia, tubulo-villous adenoma high/low-grade dysplasia)

name: HiCervix
format: Cervical cytological cell classification: 29 classes organized into 3 hierarchies; first hierarchy has 4 categories (atypical squamous cell, NILM, atypical glandular cell, organism)

name: ShotBench
format: Multiple-choice QA on cinematography dimensions: shot size, framing, camera angle, lens size, lighting type, lighting condition, composition, camera movement
notes: Benchmark for evaluating VLMs on cinematography language understanding. Sources from 200+ Oscar-nominated films. Evaluated 24 VLMs; GPT-4o achieves <60% average accuracy.

name: ShotQA
format: Multiple-choice QA pairs with cinematography labels derived from movie images and video clips. Covers 8 dimensions: shot size, framing, camera angle, lens, lighting type/condition, composition, camera movement.
license: Not clearly specified (derived from movies; annotations released)
notes: Large-scale training dataset for cinematography understanding in VLMs. Used to train ShotVL via SFT + GRPO.

name: V3DBench
num_samples: 70 videos covering 6 editing categories (pose editing, rotation, scaling, translation, texture modification, object composition)
eval_time: minutes per video for full pipeline (mesh reconstruction ~90min + inference ~1min per video)
format: Input videos sourced from Pexels, DAVIS, and generated videos; evaluated using Fram-Acc (CLIP-based), Tem-Con (temporal consistency), and CLAP Score (CLIP-APpeariance: Fram-Acc x DINO similarity)
metric: Fram-Acc (frame-wise editing accuracy via CLIP), Tem-Con (temporal consistency via cosine similarity), CLAP Score (Fram-Acc x DINO(input,output)), User Study EQ/SC/VP rankings
notes: Introduced by Shape-for-Motion (arXiv:2506.22432, SIGGRAPH Asia 2025). Designed to evaluate fine-grained 3D-aware video editing capabilities including pose editing, rotation, scaling, translation, texture modification, and object composition. GPT-4o used to generate source/target/instruction prompts from edited keyframes.

name: DF2K
format: Paired high-resolution images for image restoration tasks; DIV2K: 2K resolution diverse natural images, Flickr2K: diverse Flickr images
license: DIV2K: NTIRE challenge research-only; Flickr2K: unknown
notes: Combined DIV2K + Flickr2K training set commonly used for image restoration. Used in StableCodec (arXiv:2506.21977) for training extreme image compression model. DF2K_train = DIV2K_train (800) + Flickr2K_train (2650).

name: ToolBench
num_samples: 3225 original tools, filtered to ~1067 functional tools and 212 valid test queries (paper's filtered subset)
eval_time: hours for full evaluation with multiple models; paper runs ~200 queries per experimental condition
format: Real-world REST API calls via RapidAPI, requiring multi-step reasoning with tool interaction; evaluated via task completion rate
metric: task completion rate (pass/fail judged by GPT-4o following ToolBench evaluation protocol)

name: I-HAZE
format: Artificial hazy/clean indoor image pairs produced by professional haze generators for dehazing evaluation

name: O-HAZE
format: Real hazy/clean outdoor image pairs for dehazing evaluation

name: Fattal's
format: Real-world hazy images without ground-truth for dehazing evaluation (perceptual quality metrics only)

name: HSTS-Synth
format: Synthetic hazy/clean image pairs (RESIDE benchmark, HSTS subset) for dehazing evaluation

name: HSTS-Real
format: Real-world hazy images without ground-truth (RESIDE benchmark, HSTS subset) for dehazing evaluation

name: URHI
format: Real hazy images without ground-truth (RESIDE benchmark, real-world hazy images) for dehazing evaluation

name: ITS (RESIDE)
format: Synthetic indoor hazy-clear pairs (RESIDE benchmark, Indoor Training Set) for dehazing training

name: Medical-Diff-VQA
format: Chest X-ray image pairs (current and past) with QA pairs covering 7 categories: abnormality, location, type, level, view, presence, and difference. Supports difference visual question answering simulating radiologist workflow.
notes: From Hu et al., PhysioNet 2023. Designed for AI to compare current and past chest X-rays like radiologists. Supports Assessment-Diagnosis-Intervention-Evaluation clinical workflow.

name: PreferenceHack
num_samples: 6000 total (80 train + 920 eval per split x 6 splits: Length, Format, Positivity language splits + Image+Length, Image+Format, Image+Positivity multimodal splits)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Paired preference triples (prompt, preferred_response, rejected_biased_response) testing reward model susceptibility to length bias, format bias, and positivity bias in language and multimodal settings
metric: Accuracy: reward model must correctly prefer non-biased response over biased alternative
license: CC BY 4.0 (base datasets: HH-RLHF, TLDR, Alpaca, SUGARCREPE)

name: SUGARCREPE
eval_time: N/A (source dataset for PreferenceHack multimodal splits)
format: Image-caption pairs with compositional distractor captions for evaluating vision-language compositional understanding

name: IllusionBench
format: Images of abstract shapes (airplane, bicycle, bird, bottle, car, cat, dog, dolphin, fork, guitar, mug, panda, paper clip, sailboat, scooter, teapot) embedded in 11 naturalistic scenes (bazaar market, city, medieval village, museum, Times Square, underwater ruins, cloud, forest, ocean, origami, sand dune)
metric: shape recall (% correct shape super-class), scene recall (% correct scene super-class)
notes: Tests abstract shape recognition in vision-language models. Evaluates whether models rely on global shape cues vs. scene/texture cues. Introduced by Hemmat et al. (NeurIPS 2025).

name: Geirhos Shape-Texture Cue-Conflict
format: Cue-conflict stimuli where texture and shape cues are mismatched (e.g., an object with airplane shape but elephant skin texture). Images generated from 16 ImageNet categories using style transfer.
metric: shape bias = N_shape / (N_shape + N_texture), classification accuracy on cue-conflict images
notes: Standard benchmark for measuring shape-vs-texture bias in CNNs and vision models. Shape bias near 0.90-0.96 is human-level; standard CNNs typically score 0.20-0.40.

name: ecoset
format: Ecologically motivated image dataset for deep learning, designed to better model human vision than ImageNet
notes: Developed by Mehrer et al. (PNAS 2021). Categories are basic-level (e.g., dog, car not dog breed). Designed to reduce anthropocentric bias compared to ImageNet.

name: mini-ecoset
num_samples: 0.28M images, 112 categories (including 12 added to match cue-conflict categories)
format: Subset of ecoset for rapid experimentation and hyperparameter tuning
notes: Smaller version of ecoset for quick ablation studies. Used in paper 2507.03168 for hyperparameter sweep before scaling to full ecoset.

name: RS-LVF
num_samples: ~1,000 aerial images with point clouds and road labels
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Aerial images with LiDAR point clouds (projected to image coordinates via calibration file) and per-pixel road segmentation labels. Binary road segmentation task with severe class imbalance.
metric: mIoU, mAcc (mean Intersection over Union, mean accuracy)
access: Not publicly linked in paper (reference [46] in DIDB-ViT paper arXiv:2507.02222)
notes: Road segmentation dataset from bird's-eye view perspective. Used in DIDB-ViT binary ViT paper for aerial road segmentation evaluation. Point clouds provide additional depth information for road vs. non-road classification.

name: BAIR Robot Pushing
format: 15fps video clips of robotic arm pushing objects; 256x256 resolution; temporal redundancy with repeating objects and motions

name: Taxi1500
num_samples: 1077 (860 train/106 dev/111 test) per language across 1502 languages
format: Topic classification dataset; Bible domain; 6 classes; average 28 words per sample; 80/10/10 splits

name: SIB200
num_samples: 1004 (701 train/99 dev/204 test) per language across 205 languages
format: Topic classification dataset; WikiMedia domain (WikiNews, WikiJunior, WikiVoyage); 7 classes; average 21 words per sample; 80/10/10 splits; derived from Flores-200 DEV/DEVTEST sets

name: TAB-ECHR
format: Hand-annotated European Court of Human Rights case documents with 8 PII entity types (PERSON, CODE, LOC, ORG, DEM, DATETIME, QUANTITY, MISC)
metric: Perplexity, Attack Success Rate (ASR), LLM-as-a-judge win-rate for document privatization
notes: Text Anonymization Benchmark. Used for evaluating differentially private inference methods on legal documents. 16.40% private characters, 4,773 total private entities.

name: MACCROBAT 2020
format: Healthcare-focused named entity recognition dataset with medical PII entities. 41 privacy groups, 22,841 total private entities.
metric: Perplexity, Attack Success Rate (ASR) for document privatization
notes: Medical PII dataset used for evaluating privacy-preserving methods. Higher private token density (55.69%) than TAB-ECHR. Used in DP-FUSION paper (arXiv:2507.04531) for benchmarking.

name: LoCoMo
eval_time: hours for full benchmark with multiple models
format: Multi-turn conversation evaluation with memory tasks: single-hop, multi-hop, temporal reasoning, open-domain questions
notes: Evaluating very long-term conversational memory of LLM agents. Used in MemOS paper (2507.03724) for end-to-end evaluation.

name: LongMemEval
format: Long-term interactive memory benchmark with categories: single-session preference, single-session assistant, temporal reasoning, multi-session, knowledge update, single-session user
notes: Benchmarking chat assistants on long-term interactive memory. Used in MemOS paper (2507.03724).

name: PreFEval
format: Personalization evaluation with 0-turn and 10-turn scenarios; measures preference unaware error, preference hallucination, inconsistency, unhelpful response, personalized response rate
notes: Do LLMs recognize your preferences? Evaluating personalized preference following in LLMs. Used in MemOS paper (2507.03724).

name: PersonaMem
format: Dynamic user profiling and personalized responses; precision evaluation with 1-in-4 choice format
notes: Know me, respond to me: Benchmarking LLMs for dynamic user profiling and personalized responses at scale. Used in MemOS paper (2507.03724).

name: InteriorVerse
num_samples: 47,745 total (45,073 train + 2,672 test) indoor synthetic scenes
storage: ~30-50GB estimated (synthetic RGB + 5-channel intrinsic GT per scene)
eval_time: minutes for full test set evaluation
format: Synthetic indoor scene dataset with ground-truth albedo, metallic, roughness, normal, depth; from Zhu et al. SIGGRAPH Asia 2022

name: IIW (Intrinsic Images in the Wild)
format: Indoor photographs with per-pixel relative reflectance judgments (pairwise comparisons); Bell et al. ACM TOG 2014

name: DIODE (Dense Indoor and Outdoor Depth)
num_samples: ~227K total (219K train + 8.3K val); indoor + outdoor scenes
format: High-resolution RGB-D images; Vasiljevic et al. arXiv:1908.00463 (2019)

name: MPII Human Pose
format: 2D human pose images with articulated body keypoint annotations (16 joints). Images sourced from YouTube videos.
notes: Standard benchmark for 2D human pose estimation (Andriluka et al. CVPR 2014). Used in paper 2507.04726 for pose-conditioned ControlNet backdoor experiments with OpenPose skeleton extraction.

name: TRITONBENCH
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on kernel complexity
format: Triton kernel generation tasks with test cases and reference implementations
metric: Call Accuracy, Execution Accuracy, Speed Up (fast_p)

name: KERNELBENCH
num_samples: 250 PyTorch ML workloads (Level 1: 100 single-kernel, Level 2: 100 fusion, Level 3: 50 full architecture)
eval_time: hours depending on model and kernel complexity
format: PyTorch-to-Triton kernel generation tasks with performance evaluation against PyTorch baseline
metric: Compilation Accuracy, Execution Accuracy, fast_p (percentage of correct kernels with speedup > p)

name: TCGA-BLCA
format: TCGA bladder urothelial carcinoma H&E WSIs with RNA-Seq gene expression, CNV, mutation status, and survival outcome data for multimodal survival prediction
notes: Subset of TCGA used in MurreNet paper (arXiv:2507.04891) for survival prediction. Six genomic sub-sequences: protein kinases, tumor suppressor genes, oncogenes, cell differentiation markers, transcription factors, cytokines and growth factors.

name: TCGA-COADREAD
format: TCGA colon adenocarcinoma and rectum adenocarcinoma H&E WSIs with RNA-Seq gene expression, CNV, mutation status, and survival outcome data for multimodal survival prediction
notes: Subset of TCGA used in MurreNet paper (arXiv:2507.04891) for survival prediction.

name: DiLiGenT
num_samples: 10 objects (bear, buddha, cat, cow, harvest, pot1, pot2, reading, goblet, ball2)
format: Ground-truth normal maps and depth maps from calibrated photometric stereo; ideal pinhole camera; 512x612 images
metric: Mean Absolute Depth Error (MADE) in mm

name: Visual Genome (VG)
format: Images with scene graph annotations (150 object categories, 50 predicate categories); used for Scene Graph Generation (SGG) and PSG tasks
metric: R@m, mR@m (recall and mean recall at m ground truth boxes)

name: PSG Dataset
storage: ~5-10GB (derived from COCO with additional PSG annotations)
format: Panoptic scene graph annotations derived from COCO; 80 thing categories, 53 stuff categories, 56 relationship predicates; pixel-level panoptic segmentation + scene graph relations
metric: R@m, mR@m (recall and mean recall at m threshold)

name: INTERACTION Dataset
format: Multi-agent trajectory prediction dataset with high-definition maps featuring lane structures, crosswalks, intersections, roundabouts, and highway ramps. Each scenario contains 1s past + 3s future trajectories sampled at 10Hz. Focuses on highly interactive driving scenarios with adversarial and cooperative agent interactions.

name: Unlearn Canvas
num_samples: 20 classes x 60 styles = 1,200 stylized image concepts
eval_time: hours (requires generating images with T2I model + classifier evaluation)
format: High-resolution stylized images with 20 artistic/object classes and 60 styles; used for evaluating style and class unlearning in diffusion models
metric: FID, IRA (In-domain Retain Accuracy), CRA (Cross-domain Retain Accuracy), UA (Unlearn Accuracy)
notes: Benchmark for machine unlearning evaluation in generative models; introduced by Zhang et al. 2024. Used in KSCU paper (2507.06526) for class and style unlearning evaluation.

name: FSC-147
format: Images with box-level annotations and density maps for class-agnostic object counting; text prompts for counting

name: CARPK
num_samples: ~90000 cars from 4 different parking lots (drone imagery)
format: Aerial/drone images of parking lots with vehicle box annotations

name: PUCPR+
format: Fixed-camera parking lot images with vehicle box annotations

name: HICO-DET
format: images + HOI annotations (human-verb-object triplets)

name: V-COCO
format: images + HOI annotations (29 verb classes)

name: THU EACT-50
storage: ~2-3GB estimated (event streams at 1280x800, 2-5s duration per sample)
format: Event camera recordings with per-event polarity and timestamp; actions include full-body movements, hand gestures, and multi-player interactions
license: Research use (IEEE TPAMI 2023 - Gao et al.)
notes: Large-scale event-based action recognition dataset recorded directly with event camera. Hard action pairs (put on/off glasses), triplets (sit down/stand up/sit and stand). Standard split: train on subset, test on held-out subjects.

name: DVSGesture
format: DVS128 event camera recordings of 11 upper-body gesture classes performed under 24 illumination conditions
notes: DVSGesture dataset for event-based gesture recognition. Originally 11 gesture classes recorded with DVS128 camera. Widely used baseline for event-based action/gesture recognition.

name: MME-Realworld
eval_time: minutes to hours for full evaluation
format: High-resolution real-world images with perception and reasoning tasks in multiple-choice format (A-E options)
notes: Introduced by Zhang et al. (arXiv:2408.13257). Specifically designed to evaluate LMMs on high-resolution real-world scenarios. Categories include OCR, Remote Sensing, Diagram/Table, Video Monitoring, and Autonomous Driving. Used as in-distribution benchmark in MGPO paper (arXiv:2507.05920).

name: MFNet
num_samples: ~30,000 RGB-infrared image pairs from autonomous driving scenarios
format: Multi-spectral scene images (RGB + infrared) for semantic segmentation. Aligned image pairs from autonomous driving.

name: DroneVehicle
num_samples: ~25,000 RGB-infrared image pairs captured from drone platforms
format: RGB-infrared image pairs captured from drones for vehicle detection and counting in aerial scenarios. Multi-modal drone imagery.

name: MASK Disinformation
format: Fact-checking and disinformation detection prompts testing resistance to conspiracy theories and false narratives; open-ended generation evaluated by LLM judge
access: Not publicly released (paper: arXiv:2507.21919 — warmth training causes reliability degradation)
notes: MASK Disinformation benchmark used to evaluate warm vs. original models on resistance to promoting conspiracy theories and false narratives. Used in Ibrahim et al. (2025) study on warmth-reliability trade-offs.

name: HEIPOR
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed; hundreds of hyperspectral surgical images estimated
storage: ~1-3GB estimated (hyperspectral images with 25-369 spectral bands per image)
format: Hyperspectral surgical images with pixel-level segmentation annotations (tumour and tissue classes)
access: Referenced in SAMSA paper (MICCAI 2025); data access requires contact with authors

name: HIB
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed; hundreds of hyperspectral brain images estimated
storage: ~1-3GB estimated (hyperspectral images with high spectral dimensionality)
format: Hyperspectral brain images with pixel-level segmentation annotations (tumour and normal tissue classes)
access: Referenced in SAMSA paper (MICCAI 2025); data access requires contact with authors

name: SlimBrain SB-X
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed; likely hundreds of images based on SlimBrain database description
storage: ~2-5GB estimated (Ximea snapshot camera, 25 spectral bands, 660-950nm range)
format: Hyperspectral brain images (Ximea snapshot, 25 bands) with pixel-level segmentation; 5 classes: Healthy, Blood, Tumour, Meninges, Unlabelled
license: Research use (Scientific Data 2025, Martín-Pérez et al.)
access: SlimBrain database: Martín-Pérez et al., Scientific Data, 2025

name: SlimBrain SB-H
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed; likely hundreds of images based on SlimBrain database description
storage: ~5-10GB estimated (Headwall Hyperspec VNIR E-Series, 369 effective spectral bands, 400-1000nm)
eval_time: minutes to hours for full evaluation
format: Hyperspectral brain images (Headwall linescan, 369 bands) with pixel-level segmentation; 5 classes: Healthy, Blood, Tumour, Meninges, Unlabelled
license: Research use (Scientific Data 2025, Martín-Pérez et al.)
access: SlimBrain database: Martín-Pérez et al., Scientific Data, 2025

name: WISE
format: Structured prompts across 25 subdomains testing world knowledge including cultural common sense, spatio-temporal reasoning, and natural science
metric: WiScore - novel quantitative metric for assessing knowledge-image alignment
notes: World Knowledge-Informed Semantic Evaluation for text-to-image generation. Tests whether T2I models can understand text prompts containing complex semantics and world knowledge.

name: YTVIS (YouTube Video Instance Segmentation)
format: Real-world daily-life videos from YouTube with per-frame instance segmentation masks and class labels; used for video object segmentation and tracking

name: MOVi-C
format: Kubric-generated synthetic videos with daily objects on complex backgrounds; fixed camera setup; used for unsupervised object discovery and segmentation

name: MOVi-D
format: Kubric-generated synthetic videos with daily objects on complex backgrounds; more complex textures and bouncing/falling objects; used for unsupervised object discovery

name: nvBench
num_samples: ~6,000+ samples (exact number varies by train/test split; derived from nl2sql benchmarks)
storage: ~20-50GB estimated (multiple database schemas with tables for natural language to visualization generation)
format: Table + natural language query + ground truth VQL (Visualization Query Language); evaluated by executing generated VQL against the database
metric: Chart Accuracy, Axis Accuracy, SQL Accuracy, Data Accuracy, All Accuracy
access: https://github.com/nl2vis/DeepVIS (supplemental); original nvBench from Luo et al. SIGMOD 2021
notes: NL2VIS benchmark for natural language to visualization generation. nvBench-CoT is the CoT-augmented version used in DeepVIS (arXiv:2508.01700). nvBench 2.0 (Luo et al. 2025) extends the original with multiple valid VQLs per query.

name: UniversalFakeDetect
format: Binary real vs fake classification dataset. Training: ProGAN 4-class. Testing: 19 subsets from ProGAN and other 18 generators (CycleGAN, BigGAN, StyleGAN, GauGAN, StarGAN, DeepFakes, SITD, SAN, CRN, IMLE, Guided, LDM, Glide, DALLE, etc.)

name: YouCook2
format: YouTube cooking videos with temporally localized sentence annotations for dense video captioning
notes: Dense video captioning dataset used in TimeExpert (arXiv:2508.01699). Each video contains multiple temporal segments with corresponding natural language descriptions. From Zhou et al., AAAI 2018.

name: LIVECell
num_samples: 5239 images, 1.6M+ annotated cells across 8 cell types
format: High-resolution phase-contrast microscopy images (520x704 pixels) with pixel-level instance segmentation annotations for cell detection and segmentation
notes: Large-scale dataset for label-free live cell segmentation. 8 cell types with varied shapes and densities. Used as primary benchmark in IAUNet paper.

name: EVICAN2
num_samples: 5237 images, ~52,959 annotated cell and nucleus instances
