format: Heterogeneous microscopy images across brightfield, phase contrast, and fluorescence modalities with cell/nucleus instance annotations; test set categorized by difficulty (easy, medium, difficult)
notes: Balanced dataset for cell and nucleus segmentation. Training/validation: 4640 partially annotated images; test: 98 fully annotated images. Used in IAUNet paper for multi-difficulty evaluation.

name: ISBI2014
format: Overlapping cervical cytology images (512x512 pixels) with high-quality pixel-level annotations for nuclei and cytoplasm segmentation
notes: Overlapping Cervical Cytology Image Segmentation Challenge dataset. 45 synthetic for training, 90 for validation, 810 for testing. Used in IAUNet paper.

name: Revvity-25
format: High-resolution brightfield microscopy images (1080x1080 pixels) with detailed cell border annotations including overlapping regions; avg 60 polygon points per cell (up to 400 for complex structures)
metric: AP, AP50, AP75, AP_S, AP_M, AP_L
license: Introduced in IAUNet paper (2025) - contact authors for access
notes: Novel dataset from IAUNet paper with precise annotations for cell borders and overlaps. First dataset with detailed annotations for overlapping cell borders in brightfield microscopy. 55 train / 55 test split.

name: PIAD (Part-level Interactive Affordance Dataset)
num_samples: N/A (point cloud + RGB image pairs with affordance annotations; seen/unseen splits)
eval_time: minutes to hours for full evaluation
format: 3D point clouds with affordance masks + reference RGB images + affordance text labels
license: Research use (associated with IAGNet, Yang et al. 2023b)

name: 3D-AffordanceNet
num_samples: N/A (point clouds with affordance annotations for 3D objects)
format: 3D point clouds with per-point affordance labels

name: TarTanAir
format: RGB-D video sequences from diverse environments with depth and poses for VDSR/VSLAM

name: DyDToF
format: Direct Time-of-Flight (dToF) video RGB-D sequences with noise for depth super-resolution

name: Tecnick
format: High-quality test images at multiple resolutions (1200x1200, 900x600, etc.) for image processing benchmarks including compression, denoising, and interpolation
notes: Asuni et al., STAG 2014. Used in CMIC (arXiv:2508.02192) for image compression evaluation at 1200x1200 resolution.

name: NL4Opt
format: Natural language problem description -> solver-ready code (LP/MILP); evaluated by comparing optimal solution values
metric: Solution Accuracy (proportion of correctly identified optimal solutions)
notes: NL4Opt Competition benchmark for formulating optimization problems from natural language descriptions. Original 289 instances, cleaned to 214 by Xiao et al. 2025. Further corrected by OptiTrust paper (2508.03117). Metric: |f_optitrust - f_label| <= epsilon.

name: EasyLP
format: Natural language problem description -> solver-ready code (LP/MILP); evaluated by comparing optimal solution values
notes: Part of MAMO benchmark (Huang et al. 2024). Easy linear programming problems. 652 original instances, cleaned to 545. No errors detected by OptiTrust paper.

name: ComplexLP
format: Natural language problem description -> solver-ready code (LP/MILP + some nonlinear); evaluated by comparing optimal solution values
notes: Part of MAMO benchmark (Huang et al. 2024). Higher difficulty LP/MILP with some nonlinear problems. 211 original instances, cleaned to 111. OptiTrust corrected 3 instances.

name: NLP4LP
format: Natural language problem description -> solver-ready code (LP/IP); evaluated by comparing optimal solution values
notes: From OptiMUS benchmark (AhmadiTeshnizi et al. 2024). Linear and integer programming with lengthy descriptions. 344 original instances, cleaned to 178. No errors detected by OptiTrust paper.

name: ReSocratic
format: Natural language problem description -> solver-ready code (LP/NLP/MILP); evaluated by comparing optimal solution values
notes: OptiBench comprehensive benchmark (Yang et al. 2025). Linear/nonlinear programming with tabular data. 605 original instances, cleaned to 405. OptiTrust corrected 3 instances.

name: ComplexOR
format: Natural language problem description -> solver-ready code (complex OR scenarios); evaluated by comparing optimal solution values
notes: From Chain-of-Experts paper (Xiao et al. 2023). Challenging optimization problems including combinatorial tasks. 37 original instances, cleaned to 18 (50% removed due to errors). OptiTrust corrected 2 instances. Most challenging dataset - all methods <65% accuracy.

name: IndustryOR
format: Natural language problem description -> solver-ready code (industrial optimization); evaluated by comparing optimal solution values
notes: Industrial benchmark (Tang et al. 2024) covering 13 industries. 100 original instances, cleaned to 42. OptiTrust corrected 1 instance. Error rate originally as high as 54%.

name: ViViD
format: Video sequences of people with paired garment images for video virtual try-on evaluation

name: Wild-TryOnBench
eval_time: minutes per method (human evaluation adds hours)
format: Diverse in-the-wild videos with complex motions, camera movements, dynamic backgrounds; paired with target garment images for video virtual try-on
metric: Human evaluation: Garment Preservation, Physical Realism, Temporal Consistency (0-5 scale each)

name: IDEOINST
format: Opinion-elicitation instructions on 6 political topics (Crime, Economy, Gender, Immigration, Race, Science) paired with left-leaning and right-leaning responses

name: Political Compass
format: 61 statements about economic policies and social values; respondents choose between strongly agree to strongly disagree

name: IDRlabs Ideologies Test
format: 29 statements covering economics, society, culture, diplomacy; test-takers express agreement/disagreement and receive ideology matching percentages

name: Ego4D-v2
format: Egocentric video with multi-task annotations including long-term action anticipation; observed 8 segments + 5 predicted future action sequences of 20 verb-noun pairs each
metric: Edit distance (ED) for verb, noun, and action prediction

name: EPIC-Kitchens-55 (EK-55)
format: Egocentric cooking videos with verb-noun action annotations; multi-label classification evaluation at varying observation horizons (P% = 25, 50, 75)
metric: Mean Average Precision (mAP) across all, frequent, and rare actions

name: JailBreakV-28K
num_samples: 28K total (20K text-based + 8K image-based jailbreak attacks); 280 mini subset used in paper evaluation
format: Benchmark for assessing MLLM robustness against jailbreak attacks; includes text-based LLM transfer attacks and image-based MLLM jailbreak attacks
notes: From Luo et al. 2024 (arXiv:2408.04444). Paper uses the 280 mini subset for evaluation due to dataset size.

name: MultiJail
num_samples: 315 English red-team prompts paraphrased into 9 non-English versions; English split used in paper
format: Multilingual jailbreak benchmark; English prompts paraphrased into multiple languages to investigate LLM safety in multilingual settings
notes: From Deng et al. 2024. Paper uses only the English split (315 prompts) for evaluation.

name: Creative Writing (Trivia QA)
num_samples: trivia QA pairs (exact number not specified in paper; sampled for evaluation)
format: Creative writing tasks based on trivia questions; evaluates whether models correctly incorporate accurate trivia answers into creative writing outputs
metric: accuracy (proportion of correct trivia answers mentioned in model's creative response)
notes: From Wang et al. 2024 (arXiv:2407.01062) on multi-persona self-collaboration. Used in Evo-MARL paper (arXiv:2508.03864) for helpfulness evaluation alongside MATH.

name: SWE-rebench
format: GitHub issues with reproducible Docker environments, ground-truth patches, and validation test suites

name: SOTOPIA-all
num_samples: 90 scenarios with 2 agent combos per scenario
format: Interactive social reasoning with goal-driven multi-agent dialogue scenarios

name: FineGym
format: Fine-grained action videos from gymnastics/fitness competitions with temporal annotations
notes: FineGym is a dataset for fine-grained action recognition. Used for few-shot action recognition in arXiv:2508.03695. Provides temporal-localization quality data for gym activities. Paper: Shou et al. 2021.

name: BPPLib
num_samples: ~600+ instances across multiple classes (Scholl, IRUP, NonIRUP, etc.)
eval_time: minutes to hours per instance depending on size
format: Bin packing instances in standard text format; classes include Scholl, IRUP, NonIRUP variants
metric: Bin packing gap (solution bins vs lower bound)

name: TSPLib
eval_time: minutes to hours per instance depending on size
format: TSPLIB format (.tsp, .atsp files); includes symmetric/asymmetric TSP, Hamiltonian cycle problems
metric: TSP optimality gap (solution tour vs known optimum or LKH baseline)

name: CVRPLib
num_samples: ~100+ instances across multiple sets (A, B, E, F, M, P, X)
eval_time: minutes to hours per instance depending on size
format: CVRP instances in standard format; sets A/B/E/F/M/P/X with varying vehicle capacities and customer demands
metric: CVRP gap (solution distance vs LKH baseline or known optimum)

name: Online Bin Packing (OBP)
num_samples: 128 training + 30 test instances per typical setup
format: Sequences of item sizes (float) and bin capacity; items arrive online one-by-one
metric: Relative gap to lower bound of optimal bin count
access: Generated procedurally following Romera-Paredes et al. 2024 and Liu et al. 2024c

name: Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP)
num_samples: 128 training + 80 test instances per typical setup
format: Node coordinates in [0,1]^2 plane; clustered or uniform distributions
metric: Relative gap to LKH-3 baseline or known optimum
access: Generated procedurally following Bi et al. 2022

name: Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP)
num_samples: 256 training + 128 test instances per typical setup
format: Depot + customer coordinates in [0,1]^2, demands, vehicle capacity; uniform distribution
access: Generated procedurally; follows standard CVRP generation protocols

name: NarrativeQA
format: Reading comprehension on long narrative texts (books, movie scripts); questions require understanding entire story/summary; answers are free-form text
notes: Used in LongBench (arXiv:2308.14508) and AttnTrace (arXiv:2508.03793) for evaluating long-context LLM capabilities.

name: QMSum
num_samples: ~1,300 meetings with queries / ~30k annotated query-summary pairs
format: Query-based multi-domain meeting summarization; given a meeting transcript and a query, generate a summary relevant to the query
notes: Used in LongBench (arXiv:2308.14508) and AttnTrace (arXiv:2508.03793) for evaluating long-context LLM meeting summarization capabilities.

name: SpeechRole-Data
num_samples: 111k speech-to-speech dialogue samples (89,461 train, 21,993 OOD, 392 test) across 98 roles
storage: ~500GB-1TB (111k dialogues, ~1079 hours of speech at 16kHz mono, plus role metadata, speaker embeddings, TTS-synthesized audio)
format: Speech-to-speech role-playing dialogues with reference audio for voice cloning. Each sample: role profile, reference voice clip, multi-turn speech dialogue. 78 train roles + 20 OOD roles + 98 test roles.
license: Research (Genshin Impact assets permitted for non-commercial academic research; some source material restricted)
notes: From Jiang et al., arXiv:2508.02013. Synthesized using CosyVoice2 (role speech) and VolcEngine TTS (user speech). Reference voices from Genshin Impact and other audiovisual sources. Dialogue deduplication using semantic similarity (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 for English, text2vec-bge-large-chinese for Chinese).

name: SpeechRole-Eval
num_samples: 392 test instances (196 single-turn + 196 multi-turn, 4 per role across 98 roles)
storage: ~50-100GB (test audio + reference responses for pairwise evaluation)
eval_time: hours per model (392 pairwise evaluations using Gemini-2.5-Pro as LLM judge)
format: Speech role-playing evaluation using pairwise LLM-based scoring. Gemini-2.5-Pro judges test response vs high-quality reference response on 8 metrics: IA, CC, SF, SN, PC, EA, PeC, KC. Metrics: Instruction Adherence, Conversational Coherence, Speech Fluency, Speech Naturalness, Prosody Consistency, Emotion Appropriateness, Personality Consistency, Knowledge Consistency.
metric: Pairwise score ratio (test_score / ref_score) per metric, averaged over N=392 instances; Overall = average of 8 metric scores
notes: From Jiang et al., arXiv:2508.02013. LLM-based evaluation using Gemini-2.5-Pro as judge. Validated against human annotations with Spearman correlation ρ > 0.37 across all 8 metrics. Covers English and Chinese roles. Evaluates both cascaded (ASR+LLM+TTS) and end-to-end SRPA systems.

name: ChatHaruhi
num_samples: ~32k dialogues (paper states ~62 characters with 9,000+ dialogues; other sources report ~20-32k)
format: Text-based role-playing dialogues in Chinese and English, generated using ChatGPT from TV/film character scripts. Each role includes persona description, dialogue examples, and Q&A pairs.
access: https://github.com/CM营销er/ChatHaruhi (original repo); paper uses version from Li et al., 2023
notes: From Li et al. (arXiv:2308.09597). 18 characters from ChatHaruhi were incorporated into SpeechRole-Data (arXiv:2508.02013) as source role profiles for dialogue generation. ChatHaruhi pioneered large-scale text role-playing dialogue data construction from TV/film/animation characters.

name: Food101
format: 101 food categories with ~1000 images per class

name: OxfordPets
format: 37 pet categories (12 cat breeds, 25 dog breeds) with species and breed labels

name: FGVC-Aircraft
format: 100 aircraft variants with model labels

name: DeepGlobe
format: 1024x1024 RGB satellite images with 7-class land cover segmentation masks (urban, agriculture, rangeland, forest, water, barren, unknown). PNG masks matching image dimensions.
notes: Introduced at CVPR 2018 (Demir et al.). Used as a target domain dataset in cross-domain few-shot segmentation benchmarks. Highly distinct visual domain from natural image datasets, making it challenging for domain adaptation.

name: ParsGLUE
num_samples: ~6 tasks (PerSent, FarsTail, PEYMA, PQuAD, ParsiNLU-MC, ParsiNLU-TE)
format: Persian GLUE benchmark covering sentiment analysis (PerSent), NLI (FarsTail), NER (PEYMA), QA (PQuAD), multiple choice QA (ParsiNLU-MC), and textual entailment (ParsiNLU-TE). Average score reported.

name: Hamshahri-2
format: Persian news corpus, part of the Hamshahri-2 collection for language modeling. Genre: News. ZWNJ usage: 12.3%.

name: Wikipedia-fa
format: Persian Wikipedia dump for language modeling. Genre: Encyclopedia. ZWNJ usage: 11.2%.

name: VOA Persian
format: Voice of America Persian news corpus for language modeling. Genre: News. ZWNJ usage: 9.8%.

name: MirasText
format: Persian literature text corpus for language modeling. Genre: Literature. ZWNJ usage: 14.1%.

name: Ganjoor
format: Persian poetry corpus from Ganjoor for language modeling. Genre: Poetry. ZWNJ usage: 16.8%.

name: Twitter-fa
format: Persian Twitter/social media corpus for language modeling. Genre: Social Media. ZWNJ usage: 3.2%.

name: Scientific-fa
format: Persian scientific/academic text corpus for language modeling. Genre: Academic. ZWNJ usage: 15.6%.

name: YouTube Video Highlight Detection
num_samples: ~600 videos across 6 categories (100 videos per category: news, sports, music, etc.)
format: YouTube videos with frame-level binary highlight annotations per video; standard train/test splits provided with dataset
license: YouTube terms / research use (dataset from Sun et al., ECCV 2014)
notes: Video highlight detection dataset introduced in 'Ranking Domain-Specific Highlights by Analyzing Edited Videos' (Sun et al., ECCV 2014). 6 categories. Used in Highlight-TTA paper (arXiv:2508.04924) as one of three benchmark datasets.

name: StoryER
num_samples: 45,948 story pairs (pointwise ratings with multi-aspect scores)
storage: ~50-100GB (stories from WritingPrompts with multi-dimensional quality annotations)
format: Story pairs with ground-truth multi-aspect scores (Coherence, Ending, Style, Character Development, Empathy) on 1-5 Likert scale. Also provides human-written reasoning for some samples.
metric: Pearson correlation, Spearman correlation, Kendall correlation, MSE, F1-Score
notes: From Chen et al. (2023). Used as primary training and evaluation benchmark in EvolvR paper. StoryER-Scale subset used.

name: HANNA
format: Stories with direct multi-aspect ratings on 1-5 Likert scale across 6 dimensions: Relevance, Coherence, Empathy, Surprise, Engagement (Interestingness), Complexity.
metric: Pearson correlation, Spearman correlation, Kendall correlation, MSE, F1-Score
notes: From Chhun, Suchanek, and Clavel (2024). Used as training benchmark and source for story generation experiments in EvolvR paper.

name: OpenMEVA
storage: ~5-10GB (stories with single holistic score per story)
format: Stories with single holistic Overall Quality score on 1-5 Likert scale. Aspects (Relevance, Fluency, Coherence, Commonsense) are subsumed into the holistic score.
metric: Pearson correlation, Spearman correlation, Kendall correlation
notes: From Guan et al. (2021). Used for zero-shot generalization testing in EvolvR paper. Lower correlation scores observed due to single holistic score format.

name: ASAP++
format: Essays (8 topics, 3 genres: narrative/argumentative/source-dependent) with holistic and multi-trait scores

name: EAR-Bench (OmniEAR)
eval_time: hours per model (2800 scenarios x 3 runs)
format: Text-based environment simulation with graph-structured state, 214 action types, dynamic tool-capability binding, multi-agent coordination
metric: task success rate (SR), step count, relative step ratio (RSR) vs expert
notes: From Wang et al. 2025 (arXiv:2508.05614). Evaluates embodied agent reasoning: physical property reasoning (weight, temperature, material), dynamic tool acquisition, and implicit multi-agent collaboration based on physical constraints. Tasks span single-agent (Direct Command, Tool Use, Attribute Reasoning, Compound Reasoning) and multi-agent (Explicit/Implicit/Compound Collaboration).

name: DELIVER
eval_time: hours for full training and evaluation
format: RGB, Depth, LiDAR point cloud, and Event camera modalities for general scene semantic segmentation. Arbitrary-modality semantic segmentation benchmark.
access: Zhang et al. 2023b (CVPR 2023) - Delivering Arbitrary-Modal Semantic Segmentation
notes: DELIVER dataset introduced in 'Delivering Arbitrary-Modal Semantic Segmentation' (CVPR 2023). Supports arbitrary combinations of RGB, Depth, LiDAR, and Event modalities. Used as primary evaluation dataset in CHARM paper (2508.03060).

name: MCubeS
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed (multimodal material segmentation dataset)
eval_time: hours for full training and evaluation
format: RGB, Near-Infrared (NIR), Degree of Linear Polarization (DoLP), and Angle of Linear Polarization (AoLP) modalities for material segmentation.
access: Liang et al. 2022 (CVPR 2022) - Multimodal Material Segmentation
notes: MCubeS dataset introduced in 'Multimodal Material Segmentation' (CVPR 2022). Supports RGB, NIR, DoLP, and AoLP modalities for material segmentation. Used as evaluation dataset in CHARM paper (2508.03060).

name: MUSES
eval_time: hours for full training and evaluation
format: RGB, Event camera, and LiDAR point cloud modalities for driving scenarios under uncertainty. Multi-sensor semantic perception dataset.
access: Brodermann et al. 2024 (ECCV 2024) - MUSES: The Multi-sensor Semantic Perception Dataset for Driving Under Uncertainty
notes: MUSES dataset introduced in 'MUSES: The Multi-sensor Semantic Perception Dataset for Driving Under Uncertainty' (ECCV 2024). Supports RGB, Event, and LiDAR modalities for autonomous driving. Used as evaluation dataset in CHARM paper (2508.03060).

name: CP-Bench
num_samples: 101 constraint programming problems (30 optimization, 71 decision) from CSPLib, CPMpy examples, Kjellerstrand models, and APLAI-KULeuven
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on problem complexity and model
format: Markdown problem descriptions with input data, required output variables, and ground-truth CPMpy models for validation
metric: accuracy (constraint satisfaction + optimal objective value matching)
license: Research use (original sources: CSPLib, CPMpy, etc.)
notes: Introduced by Michailidis et al. (arXiv:2506.06052). Szeider (2026, arXiv:2508.07468) provided clarified version with 31 problem clarifications and 19 ground-truth corrections. Problems cover scheduling, assignment, sequencing, graph, combinatorial design.

name: PrinciplismQA
eval_time: hours per model for full sweep
format: MCQAs (4-option multiple choice) + open-ended cases with keypoint rubric-based evaluation
metric: MCQA accuracy (%), open-ended practice score (0-1 normalized score via LLM-as-a-Judge)

name: MedSafetyBench
format: MCQAs focused on medical safety refusal scenarios

name: MedEthicsQA
format: medical ethics MCQAs

name: TABLETOP
format: Real tabletop photographs with occlusion-ordered RGBA object layers (2-6 objects per scene, 512x512 resolution)
metric: LPIPS / CLIP Score (amodal completion), ARI (visible segmentation)

name: CObL Synthetic Training Set
format: Synthetic tabletop scenes with occlusion-ordered RGBA object layers, generated via Blender + ControlNet-depth pipeline from 600 Adobe Substance 3D assets (750 configs x 3 texture sets)

name: ClevrTex
format: Texture-rich synthetic scenes with ground truth depth, albedo, normal, and semantic segmentation; CObL uses camera/lighting/ground plane positions from ClevrTex

name: RFMiD
format: Retinal fundus photographs with multi-label disease annotations (45 disease classes including DR, ARMD, MH, etc.)
notes: Retinal Fundus Multi-Disease Image Dataset (Pachade et al., 2021). Used for diabetic retinopathy and multi-disease classification. Paper: arXiv:2109.09882.

name: REFUGE
format: Retinal fundus images with glaucoma annotations (cup-to-disc ratio, Fovea location, glaucoma classification)
notes: REtinal FUGE Challenge (Orlando et al., Medical Image Analysis 2020). Glaucoma assessment from fundus photographs. Used in CLIPin paper for medical domain evaluation.

name: MESSIDOR
format: Retinal fundus images with diabetic retinopathy grading (0-4 scale) and macular edema annotations
notes: MESSIDOR database (Decenciere et al., 2014). French ophthalmology dataset for diabetic retinopathy grading. Used in CLIPin paper for medical domain evaluation.

name: PASCAL VOC2007
format: JPEG images with 20 object class annotations; classification, detection, and segmentation tasks
notes: PASCAL VOC 2007 benchmark for object classification and detection. Distinct from PASCAL VOC 2007+2012 combined. Used in CLIPin paper for linear probing and zero-shot classification evaluation.

name: MUGE
format: Chinese e-commerce image-text pairs from Taobao platform; images with product descriptions and titles
notes: MUGE (Multi-modal e-Commerce Giant-scale) dataset: Chinese e-commerce image-text pairs used for multimodal training in CLIPin paper. Used alongside COCO for natural domain experiments.

name: LCSTS (Large-Scale Chinese Short Text Summarization)
num_samples: ~2M pairs (full dataset); 500 samples used in SAEMARK paper evaluation
format: Chinese short text summaries: each sample is a short text paired with a summary; evaluation uses completion-style prompts
metric: Accuracy, F1, Recall (detection metrics per watermark paper)
notes: From Hu et al. 2015 (arXiv:1506.05865). Used in SAEMARK paper (arXiv:2508.08211) for Chinese multilingual watermarking evaluation. Task framed as completion in the paper (given prompt, generate continuation).

name: BIGGen-Bench
format: Fine-grained LLM evaluation using LLM-as-judge; 5-point Likert scale pairwise comparisons across diverse domains
metric: Spearman correlation with human ratings; pairwise win-rate
notes: From Kim et al. 2024 (arXiv:2406.05761). Used in SAEMARK paper (arXiv:2508.08211) for text quality evaluation of watermarked outputs. Measures quality degradation from watermarking using LLM judges.

name: ManiSkill3
eval_time: 1M steps training takes ~24h on L40s GPU
format: GPU-parallelized robotics simulation with RGB observations, physics-based control (SAPIEN/MuJoCo), supports manipulation tasks (lift, pick, push, pull, poke, place, transport)
notes: GPU-parallelized robotics simulation and rendering benchmark for generalizable embodied AI (Tao et al., RSS 2025). Used in SegDAC paper (arXiv:2508.09325) for visual RL generalization benchmark with 12 perturbation types (camera, lighting, color, texture) across 3 difficulty levels. Tasks include LiftPegUpright, PickCube, PokeCube, PullCube, PullCubeTool, PushCube, UnitreeG1PlaceAppleInBowl, UnitreeG1TransportBox.

name: Isharah-1000
format: Pose-based skeletal keypoints (86 2D landmarks per frame) extracted from unconstrained smartphone videos; gloss-level and text annotations

name: SignEval-2025 CSLR Challenge
num_samples: Isharah-1000 evaluation split (signer-independent and unseen-sentences tracks)
format: Standardized CSLR evaluation on Isharah-1000 benchmark with SI and US tracks
access: ICCV 2025 Multimodal Sign Language Recognition Workshop (Luqman et al., 2025)

name: TCGA-RCC
num_samples: ~937 kidney cancer WSIs (Clear cell, Papillary, Chromophobe RCC subtypes)
format: TCGA kidney cancer H&E whole-slide images with RCC subtype labels for MIL multi-class classification
notes: Used in MOC (Xiang et al., MICCAI 2025) for few-shot WSI classification. 937 WSIs split into training/val/test with 20 val and 70 test samples per split.

name: KMMLU
format: 4-choice MC (Korean-language adaptation of MMLU)
notes: Korean translation of MMLU. Used in arXiv:2508.10355 for evaluating Korean-language academic knowledge. From Lee et al. (Smoothie-Qwen, 2025).

name: grpo_math_kor_42k
format: Korean math problem/solution pairs with reasoning traces for RL training; correctness programmatically verifiable
notes: Korean math dataset used for RL fine-tuning in arXiv:2508.10355.

name: sft-deepseek-v3-r1-1by5-reasoning-mixed-30k
format: Korean reasoning-intensive prompts with 1:5 ratio of reasoning to non-reasoning; reasoning distilled from DeepSeek-R1, non-reasoning from DeepSeek-V3-0324
notes: Korean SFT dataset from arXiv:2508.10355 covering math, science, and programming in Korean.

name: MPDD (Multi-scale Pose-invariant Pattern Defect)
num_samples: ~5,500 training + ~1,000 test images across 6 industrial object categories
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: High-resolution industrial images with pixel-level anomaly masks; pose-invariant pattern defect detection; categories include metal nuts, screws, etc.
notes: Multi-scale Pose-invariant Pattern Defect dataset for industrial anomaly detection. Used in IAD-R1 paper (arXiv:2508.09178) as one of 6 evaluation benchmarks.

name: DAGM
num_samples: ~1,700+ images across 10 synthetic texture defect categories
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Synthetic texture images with weak labels for surface anomaly detection; 10 texture classes each with normal and defective samples; created for DAGM workshop competition
notes: DAGM (Deutsche Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Mustererkennung) texture anomaly detection benchmark. Introduced by Wieler & Hahn (DAGM 2007). Used in IAD-R1 paper (arXiv:2508.09178) as surface texture evaluation benchmark.

name: SDD (Tabernik Surface Defect)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Industrial surface defect images with pixel-level anomaly segmentation masks; multiple defect types including scratches, holes, cracks
notes: Surface Defect Database introduced by Tabernik et al. (Journal of Intelligent Manufacturing, 2020). Used in IAD-R1 paper (arXiv:2508.09178) as surface texture evaluation benchmark.

name: HellaSWAG
format: Sentence completion (commonsense reasoning) — given a context, choose the most plausible ending from 4 options
notes: Commonsense reasoning benchmark testing everyday situations. Often used as an evaluation target for tokenization efficiency since it benefits from multi-word unit capture.

name: CLADDER
num_samples: ~1,906 test samples (Rung1: Association, Rung2: Intervention, Rung3: Counterfactual)
format: Synthetic causal reasoning questions with formal DAG notation, symbolic reasoning steps, and ground-truth answers across three cognitive levels of causal inference

name: WIQA
num_samples: ~36,000 questions (212 used in paper after filtering)
format: Procedural text with 'what if' perturbation questions assessing causal reasoning about multi-step processes; includes INPARA (in-paragraph) and EXOGENOUS (out-of-paragraph) perturbation types

name: PandaSet
num_samples: 103 scenes with LiDAR and multi-camera data
eval_time: ~1 hour per scene for 3DGS training on RTX 4090
format: Synchronized LiDAR point clouds and camera images (6 cameras) with 3D annotations
notes: Large-scale multimodal autonomous driving dataset. Used in InstDrive (arXiv:2508.12015) for 3D instance segmentation via 3D Gaussian Splatting.

name: RCAEval
num_samples: 90 fault injection incidents (RE2-OnlineBoutique microservice app, 12 services, 5 target services × 6 fault types × 3 rounds)
eval_time: hours for full evaluation across all incidents
format: Multi-modal telemetry (per-pod metrics time-series, raw log streams, distributed trace snapshots) from controlled fault injection in microservice systems; includes ground-truth root cause labels (service + failure type)
metric: Accuracy@1 (Top-1), Avg@3, Avg@5, SURE-Score (causal soundness, actionability, incident specificity, clarity)
access: https://github.com/alibaba/RCAEval or referenced from Wu et al.
notes: RCA benchmark for microservice systems. Paper: Wu et al. 'RCAEval: A Benchmark for Root Cause Analysis in Microservices.' Used in GALA paper (arXiv:2508.12472) for evaluating multi-modal RCA methods.

name: CAIL2018
format: Chinese legal case records with facts, charges, and judgments; tasks include legal article prediction (SPP-F), criminal charge prediction (CCP), sentencing prediction (SLP)
notes: Chinese AI and Law 2018 dataset. Large-scale legal dataset for judgment prediction. From Xiao et al. (2018). Used in LegalDelta (arXiv:2508.12281) as training data.

name: JEC QA
format: Chinese legal domain question answering; multi-choice and fill-in questions covering legal knowledge and reasoning
notes: Legal-domain QA dataset. From Zhong et al. (AAAI 2020). Used in LegalDelta (arXiv:2508.12281) as training data.

name: DiscLaw
format: Legal reasoning tasks including PAE (legal article prediction), NJE (judgment prediction), LBK (legal knowledge), CAS (case analysis), CAC (calculation); evaluated by accuracy/F1/Jaccard
notes: DiscLaw benchmark for legal reasoning from Shengbin Yue et al. (2023). Used in LegalDelta (arXiv:2508.12281) for both in-domain and out-of-domain evaluation.

name: Reasoning Gym
num_samples: 100 reasoning task types across games, algorithms, graphs, arithmetic, geometry, and logic
format: Procedurally generated reasoning problems with verifiable rewards via code execution; tasks include maze solving, shortest path, puzzle solving, bitwise operations, propositional logic, and more
notes: Used in OptimalThinkingBench (arXiv:2508.13141) for UnderthinkingBench tasks. Provides diverse reasoning tasks with programmatic verification.

name: SLUE-VoxPopuli
num_samples: 5000 train / 1753 dev / 1842 test utterances (~15h train / 5h dev / 5h test)
eval_time: hours for fine-tuning, minutes for eval
format: Orated English speech from European Parliament (VoxPopuli) with NER and NEL annotations; NER task: entity phrase + entity tag pairs; NEL task: named entity time-stamps
metric: NER: micro-averaged F1; NEL: frame-F1 and word-F1

name: CMB
num_samples: ~280K total questions; ~19K case-based subset after filtering (train: 15465, val: 1940, test: 1935)
format: Chinese multiple-choice clinical questions across 6 domains and 28 subcategories; case-based subset used for interactive doctor-patient simulation with atomic fact decomposition

name: XSUM
format: Extreme summarization task - produce one-sentence summary from news article; evaluated with ROUGE scores and length compliance metrics

name: MT-Bench-LI
format: MT-Bench prompts augmented with three target lengths from GPT-4 Turbo, Claude 3 Opus, and Mistral Large first-turn answers; measures strict length compliance
metric: Exact Match, MAE, MALD, LLM-as-Judge quality score
notes: Derived from MT-Bench by adding length constraints. Used in arXiv:2508.13805 (CAPEL) for length-controlled generation evaluation.

name: LIFEBench
num_samples: 10 target lengths (16-8192 tokens) x 4 task categories
format: Length instruction following benchmark with Equal-To, At-Most, and At-Least tracks; covers diverse generation tasks and target lengths up to 8192 tokens
metric: Length Deviation, Length Score, Exact Match
notes: Introduced by Zhang et al. 2025. Used in arXiv:2508.13805 (CAPEL) for evaluating exact length generation at very long targets.

name: Flores-200
format: Language-parallel translation benchmark extending Flores-101 to 200 languages; human-translated sentences covering diverse domains

name: HouseCat6D
format: Large-scale multi-modal category-level 6D object perception dataset with 194 high-fidelity 3D object models across 10 household categories, captured in 41 real scenes
metric: mAP (3D IoU @25%, 50%), rotation error (5°, 10°), translation error (5cm, 10cm)

name: RawVDemoiré
num_samples: 300 video clips (250 train + 50 test), 60 frames each
format: Paired moiré/clean video clips in both RAW (RGGB bayer, 640×360) and sRGB (1280×720) domains
notes: Video demoiréing benchmark. Contains hand-held captured screen videos with moiré patterns. Pseudo GT RAW frames derived from sRGB conversion.

name: VDemoiré
num_samples: 290 video clip pairs, 60 frames each at 1280×720
format: Paired moiré/clean sRGB video clips
access: Refer to Dai et al., CVPR 2022 paper
notes: Video demoiréing benchmark in sRGB domain. Designed for evaluating temporal consistency in demoiréing.

name: WFLW
num_samples: 7500 train + 2500 test images, 98 landmarks per face
format: Face images with 98 landmark annotations; includes challenging subsets (large pose, expression, illumination, make-up, occlusion, blur)
metric: NME (Normalized Mean Error), FR (Failure Rate), AUC

name: COFW
num_samples: 1345 train + 507 test images, 68 landmarks per face
format: Face images with 68 landmark annotations; includes occluded faces
metric: NME (Normalized Mean Error), FR (Failure Rate), AUC

name: 300W
num_samples: 3148 train + 689 test images (common: 554, challenging: 135), 29 landmarks per face
format: Face images with 29 landmark annotations; common and challenging subsets
metric: NME (Normalized Mean Error), FR (Failure Rate), AUC

name: SafeBench
num_samples: 800 scenarios (8 base traffic scenarios × 10 routes × 10 adversarial scenarios)
format: RL-based AV agents (PPO, SAC, TD3) evaluated in CARLA simulator under adversarial scenarios; metrics include collision rate (CR), overall score (OS), safety/functionality/etiquette dimensions
metric: Collision Rate (CR, higher=better adversarial), Overall Score (OS, lower=better adversarial)
notes: Benchmark platform for safety evaluation of autonomous vehicles. From Xu et al. (NeurIPS 2022). Used in SCENGE paper (arXiv:2508.14527) as primary evaluation framework.

name: MetaDrive
format: Lightweight driving simulator with procedurally generated traffic scenarios; supports RL training and evaluation; multi-agent traffic with diverse vehicle/road configurations
metric: Collision rate, route completion, driving score
notes: Used in SCENGE paper (arXiv:2508.14527) to demonstrate cross-simulator generalizability of generated adversarial scenarios.

name: TREC 2020 Health Misinformation Track
num_samples: 46 topics (COVID-19 health misinformation), Common Crawl news corpus
storage: ~1-2GB (topics + qrels; corpus is external Common Crawl snapshot)
format: Health-related queries with expert annotations classifying documents as helpful (credible/factual) or harmful (misleading/false). Documents labeled with preference codes from -2 (credible but wrong) to 4 (credible and correct).
metric: nDCG, preference-based evaluation, MHDR (Mean Help-Defeat Rate)
notes: Used in FSAP adversarial attack paper (arXiv:2508.15283). 22 topics with both helpful and harmful documents used after filtering.

name: TREC 2021 Health Misinformation Track
num_samples: 35 topics (general medical misinformation), C4 noclean corpus
storage: ~2-5GB (topics + qrels; corpus is external C4 snapshot)
format: Health treatment queries with expert annotations. Documents labeled with preference codes from -3 (credible but wrong) to 12 (credible and correct). Binary stance indicating whether treatment helps or harms the condition.
metric: nDCG, preference-based evaluation, MHDR (Mean Help-Defeat Rate)
notes: Used in FSAP adversarial attack paper (arXiv:2508.15283). 27 topics with both helpful and harmful documents used after filtering.

name: AccessEval
num_samples: ~300-600 unique queries (6 domains × 10 conditions × ~5-10 queries per combination, estimated from paper)
eval_time: hours for 8 models on H100 cluster
format: Structured queries in neutral and disability-aware forms across 6 business domains (Education, Finance, Healthcare, Hospitality, Media, Technology); 9 disability categories; 5 demographic attributes per query
metric: Response rate (%), demographic prediction distribution; not accuracy-based
license: Not yet released — promised on acceptance (ICCV 2025)
access: Will be released by Panda et al. — contact: Srikant Panda, Amit Agarwal, Hitesh Laxmichand Patel (BITS Pilani / Oracle AI)

name: SeedTTS-Eval
format: TTS evaluation benchmark with test-zh, test-en, test-hard subsets; evaluates speech quality, speaker similarity, and content consistency
notes: TTS evaluation benchmark from ByteDance. Used in GOAT paper (arXiv:2508.15442) for hallucination evaluation using ASR-based CER.

name: WenetSpeech4TTS
format: Chinese speech audio with transcriptions for TTS training
notes: Large-scale Chinese speech corpus from WeNet team. Used in GOAT paper (arXiv:2508.15442) as training data (1000 randomly selected samples).

name: MusiQue
format: Multi-hop questions composed from single-hop questions, requiring multi-step reasoning over multiple Wikipedia paragraphs
notes: MuSiQue: Multihop Questions via Single-hop Question Composition (Trivedi et al., 2022). Used in DeepResearcher (Zheng et al., 2025) as one of 7 QA sub-datasets.

name: SODA10M
num_samples: ~10M unlabelled images + ~12K labelled images (2K Clear server + ~10K Overcast/Rainy clients)
storage: ~30-50GB (10M unlabeled frames for self-supervised pretraining, with labeled subset for evaluation)
format: Autonomous driving images from diverse weather/lighting conditions; object detection with 6 categories (Pedestrian, Cyclist, Car, Truck, Tram, Tricycle); unlabeled frames for self/semi-supervised learning

name: 3DPW
format: RGB video frames from in-the-wild with SMPL parameters and 3D joint annotations; includes outdoor scenes with complex backgrounds

name: BEDLAM
format: Large synthetic dataset of bodies exhibiting detailed lifelike animated motion with SMPL parameters and accurate 3D pose annotations

name: TED Talks Parallel Sentences
num_samples: 152,938 parallel sentences across 4 languages (en, de, fr, nl), forming 917,628 sentence pairs (152,938 × 6 language pairs)
format: Parallel sentences extracted from TED talk scripts; used to train cross-lingual autoencoder for debiasing paper (arXiv:2508.17948)

name: Amazon CDs and Vinyl (5-core, Sequential Rec)
format: User-item interaction sequences from Amazon CDs & Vinyl category; 5-core filtering (>=10 interactions per user/item); features include item title, band/artist name, rating, timestamp

name: DevAI
format: Multi-requirement software engineering tasks with DAG-structured dependencies, ground-truth solutions, and structured requirements
metric: Dependency-aware requirement satisfaction rate, guided improvement rate
notes: Original DevAI from Zhuge et al. 2024 (Agent-as-a-Judge). This paper enhances DevAI with verified ground-truth solutions, enabling structured multi-turn interactive evaluation with interviewer LLM providing targeted hints.

name: CPTAC-LUAD
format: CPTAC lung adenocarcinoma H&E whole-slide images with 5-year recurrence labels; used as independent external validation cohort in PathRosetta paper (arXiv:2508.16742)
notes: Used in PathRosetta (arXiv:2508.16742) for external validation of recurrence prediction model on independent cohort with different slide preparation and scanning protocols.

name: TuSimple
format: Highway driving scene video clips with lane markings annotated as polylines. Each clip contains 40 consecutive frames; lane labels are provided for every frame in the clip.
metric: Accuracy, False Positive Rate (FPR), False Negative Rate (FNR)
notes: Lane detection benchmark. Used in the tdIF SNN paper (arXiv:2508.20392) for evaluating ultra-low latency SNN-based lane detection.

name: CULane
num_samples: 88925 train + 34680 test images across 9 urban/highway scenarios
format: Urban and highway traffic scene images with lane markings annotated as line segments/polylines. 9 categories: crosswalk, intersection, curb, sidewalk, lane reduction, toll plaza, traffic light, highway, N/A.
metric: F1 score, Precision, Recall (IoU-based line matching with fixed line width)
notes: Large-scale lane detection benchmark. Used in the tdIF SNN paper (arXiv:2508.20392) for evaluating ultra-low latency SNN-based lane detection at 5 time-steps.

name: VisualBodyToBMI
format: Full-body images with BMI labels derived from height/weight metadata; 70/15/15 train/val/test split common
metric: MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error), MAE (Mean Absolute Error)
access: Reference: Jiang & Guo (2019) IEEE TIFS; contact authors for dataset access
notes: Primary benchmark for BMI/body weight estimation from full-body images. Used in Jin et al. (2022) and paper 2508.20534. Prior best: MAPE ~9.37% (Jin et al. 2022). Paper 2508.20534 achieves 8.56% MAPE with fine-tuning.

name: WayBED (WayBetter BMI Estimation Dataset)
num_samples: 84,963 smartphone images from 25,353 individuals (71,322 after filtering)
format: Front-facing full-body smartphone photos with self-reported weight and scale-photo verified weigh-in; filtered by person detection, bounding box ratio, and posture clustering using Detectron2
metric: MAPE, MAE for BMI and weight estimation
license: Research use only (available on request from WayBetter)
access: Available on request from WayBetter; not publicly released due to privacy requirements. Code open-source at https://github.com/im-ethz/DigitalScale
notes: Proprietary large-scale dataset from WayBetter weight-loss app. Gender: 49% female, 9% male, 42% not reported. Paper 2508.20534 achieves MAPE 7.9% on this dataset with DenseNet-201 (new SOTA on WayBED).

name: EMTD
num_samples: 110 720P speech videos (upper body and hands); longest video 74 seconds; 23.64% exceed 15 seconds
format: High-resolution speech video dataset for audio-driven portrait video generation with upper body and hands; well-suited for long-duration evaluation
metric: FID, FVD, Sync-C, Sync-D, FSIM, HKC, HKV
access: https://github.com/MRzzm/EchoMimicV2 (EMTD associated with EchoMimicV2 paper, Meng et al. 2024)
notes: Used as primary evaluation dataset in InfinityHuman paper. Contains diverse full-body talking videos enabling assessment of identity consistency, hand accuracy, and lip-sync in long-duration generation.

name: AndroidControl-Low
num_samples: Part of AndroidControl dataset (Li et al., 2024b); same ~15K demonstrations / ~14.5K tasks; focuses on low-level atomic actions (click, scroll, type) rather than high-level instructions
storage: ~60GB of screenshots and instructions (shared with AndroidControl-High)
format: Low-level natural language instructions with Android screenshots and typed actions; step-by-step action prediction
metric: step success rate, action type accuracy, grounding
notes: Low-level split of AndroidControl. SWIRL paper evaluates Interactor on AndroidControl-Low as standalone low-level executor (Table 4).

name: GUI-Act
num_samples: ~3,000+ GUI grounding samples across web and desktop tasks (Chen et al., 2024)
format: Natural language instructions with UI screenshots for web and desktop GUI grounding; predicts action type + parameters
notes: Part of GUICourse suite. SWIRL evaluates on GUI-Act-Web and GUI-Act-Desktop as cross-domain low-level transfer benchmarks (Table 3).

name: OmniAct
num_samples: ~5,000+ samples across desktop and web tasks (Kapoor et al., 2024)
storage: ~30-50GB of UI screenshots and action logs
format: Multimodal input (screenshot + instruction) with action outputs (type, coordinates) for desktop and web automation
metric: step success rate, action accuracy, grounding
notes: Enables multimodal generalist autonomous agents for desktop and web. SWIRL evaluates Interactor on OmniAct-Web and OmniAct-Desktop as cross-domain benchmarks (Table 3).

name: CMATH
num_samples: ~1,500 Chinese elementary school math problems with answers (Wei et al., 2023)
format: Chinese elementary school math problems with numeric answers; multiple choice or free-response
notes: Chinese Elementary School Math Test (Wei et al., 2023). Used by SWIRL as cross-domain math benchmark alongside MATH500 and GSM8K (Table 5).

name: BCSS (Breast Cancer Semantic Segmentation)
format: H&E-stained whole-slide images (WSIs) of triple-negative breast cancers with pixel-level semantic segmentation annotations (tumor vs non-tumor); sourced from TCGA
notes: Breast Cancer Semantic Segmentation dataset. From Amgad et al. (2019). Used in MorphGen (arXiv:2509.00311) for single-domain generalization evaluation in histopathology.

name: Swiss Federal Supreme Court (SFSC) Opinions
format: Swiss Federal Supreme Court decisions in German, covering criminal and private law domains. Used in arXiv:2509.00529 for role-conditioned summarization evaluation.

name: Swissblawg Expert Summaries
format: Expert-written legal summaries from Swissblawg, a prominent Swiss law blog. CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 Switzerland license. Used as neutral real-world baseline in arXiv:2509.00529 for evaluating role-conditioned LLM summaries.

name: NExTQA
format: Short videos (~1 min) with multiple-choice QA testing causal and temporal reasoning (e.g., 'before X, what happened?', 'why did Y happen?')

name: VSIBench
format: 3D spatial understanding benchmark for VLMs testing viewpoint-invariant spatial reasoning from 2D images
notes: Benchmark for evaluating 3D spatial understanding in vision-language models. Used in Robix paper (arXiv:2509.01106) to evaluate embodied spatial reasoning.

name: SpatialBench
format: Benchmark for spatial understanding in embodied tasks using VLMs
notes: Spatial reasoning benchmark for embodied AI. Part of EmbSpatial-Bench suite. Used in Robix paper (arXiv:2509.01106).

name: DA-2k
format: Depth-aware spatial reasoning benchmark for VLMs
notes: Depth-aware 2k benchmark for spatial reasoning. Used in Robix paper (arXiv:2509.01106).

name: LVIS-MG
format: Large-vocabulary instance segmentation with referring expression grounding
notes: LVIS-MiniGrounding benchmark for open-vocabulary object detection and grounding. Used in Robix paper (arXiv:2509.01106).

name: VisualWebBench
format: Web page understanding and visual grounding benchmark
notes: Benchmark for web page understanding and grounding in VLMs. Used in Robix paper (arXiv:2509.01106).

name: Pixmo-Point
format: Point-based object localization and counting tasks
notes: Part of Pixmo suite for point-based object localization. Used in Robix paper (arXiv:2509.01106).

name: Where2Place
format: Object placement/arrangement understanding benchmark
notes: Visual reasoning benchmark for object placement decisions. Used in Robix paper (arXiv:2509.01106).

name: Agibot-ER
num_samples: 598 samples (97 task verification + 120 action affordance + 381 next action prediction)
format: Real-world task reasoning benchmark derived from Agibot dataset with manual annotations for task status verification, action affordance, and next action prediction
notes: Novel embodied reasoning benchmark created by Robix authors from Agibot data. Used to evaluate task-centric reasoning in robots. From arXiv:2509.01106.

name: OpenEQA
num_samples: Not disclosed (scenes from HM3D and ScanNet)
format: Embodied question answering in 3D environments (HM3D and ScanNet scenes)
notes: Open-vocabulary Embodied QA benchmark. Split into HM3D and ScanNet splits. Used in Robix paper (arXiv:2509.01106).

name: EgoTaskQA
format: Egocentric video QA for understanding human tasks in first-person view
notes: Egocentric task understanding QA benchmark. Used in Robix paper (arXiv:2509.01106).

name: ERQA
format: Edge-restoration quality assessment for video super-resolution adapted for embodied reasoning
notes: Embodied reasoning QA benchmark. Used in Robix paper (arXiv:2509.01106).

name: RefCOCOu
format: Unified referring expression comprehension benchmark
notes: RefCOCOu (UMD) split. Used in Robix paper (arXiv:2509.01106).

name: CV-Bench
format: CV-specific benchmark with 2D and 3D spatial reasoning tasks from images
notes: Computer vision benchmark for spatial reasoning. Used in Robix paper (arXiv:2509.01106).

name: SAT
format: Spatial understanding benchmark testing 3D spatial reasoning from 2D images
notes: Spatial Allen Telescope benchmark for 3D spatial understanding. Used in Robix paper (arXiv:2509.01106).

name: NextQA
format: Temporal action reasoning QA from video
notes: Next-question answering for video-based temporal reasoning. Used in Robix paper (arXiv:2509.01106).

name: SQuAD 2.0
format: Wikipedia passages with extractive answer spans, augmented with 50,000+ adversarially-written unanswerable questions
notes: SQuAD 2.0 (Rajpurkar et al., ACL 2018) extends SQuAD 1.1 with unanswerable questions, requiring models to detect unanswerability rather than always providing an answer.

name: FActScore
num_samples: 6,500 generations from 13 models evaluated in original paper
format: Long-form text generations decomposed into atomic facts; each fact checked for entailment/contradiction against retrieved evidence via NLI model
metric: FActScore = proportion of atomic facts supported by reliable evidence; FActScore@high-precision threshold
notes: FActScore (Min et al., EMNLP 2023) evaluates long-form factuality by breaking text into atomic claims and measuring entailment against retrieved evidence. Used in UniCR paper for semantic correctness supervision.

name: MISATO
format: Protein-ligand MD trajectories: 100 frames sampled from 8ns MD simulations. Each frame contains all-atom 3D coordinates for protein-ligand complex. Focuses on ligand dynamics within the binding pocket.
metric: Bond/Angle MAE/MSE, Steric Clash scores, RMSF correlation, RMSF values
access: Siebenmorgen et al., Nature Computational Science 2024; https://www.nature.com/articles/s43588-024-00695-4
notes: Machine learning dataset of protein-ligand complexes for structure-based drug discovery. Used in BioMD paper (arXiv:2509.02642) for evaluating ligand dynamics within binding pocket.

name: DD-13M
format: Ligand unbinding trajectories: ~480 frames per trajectory showing ligand dissociation from protein binding pocket to protein surface. Used for evaluating ligand unbinding pathway generation.
metric: Bond/Angle MAE/MSE, Steric Clash scores, Unbinding Path RMSD, Unbinding Success Rate (@1, @5, @10)
notes: Enhanced sampling, public dataset and generative model for drug-protein dissociation dynamics. Used in BioMD paper (arXiv:2509.02642) for evaluating ligand unbinding pathway generation. Achieves 97.1% unbinding success rate with BioMD.

name: WebQuestions
format: Open-domain question answering over Freebase KB; requires entity linking and multi-hop reasoning over KG triples
notes: Original dataset from Berant et al. 2013. Based on Freebase KB. Used in AnchorRAG paper (2509.01238) as one of four evaluation benchmarks.

name: Laval Indoor
format: HDR equirectangular environment maps of indoor scenes with corresponding perspective crops. Standard benchmark for lighting estimation. Evaluated via three-sphere protocol (diffuse, matte, mirror spheres).
notes: From Gardner et al. (2017). Widely used for indoor lighting estimation. LuxDiT uses 289 test HDRIs same as prior works.

name: Laval Outdoor
format: HDR equirectangular environment maps of outdoor scenes with concentrated sunlight. Subset of HDRdb outdoor with sunny scenes selected by Hold-Geoffroy et al. (2019).
metric: si-RMSE, angular error, n-RMSE, peak angular error (PAE)
notes: From Hold-Geoffroy et al. (CVPR 2019). Used for outdoor lighting estimation including peak light direction evaluation.

name: Cube++
num_samples: 100 processed JPEG images with SpyderCube annotations
format: Images captured with SpyderCube for illumination estimation and color constancy. Evaluated via Lambertian rendering of cube white faces under estimated lighting.
metric: RMSE, angular error on rendered cube faces
access: https://www.color.ee.psu.edu/ cube/ (Ershov et al., IEEE Access 2020)
notes: From Ershov et al. (2020). Used in LuxDiT for lighting estimation evaluation on color constancy-style tasks.

name: Objects with Lighting
num_samples: Real-world foreground objects with distant HDR environment lighting
format: Masked real objects placed in known environments with ground truth distant HDR lighting. Enables evaluation via three-sphere protocol for lighting estimation from foreground objects.
notes: From Ummenhofer et al. (3DV 2024). Used in LuxDiT for lighting estimation from foreground objects (separate from environment maps).

name: WEB360
num_samples: 2000+ panorama videos for training, 12 for evaluation
format: 360-degree panoramic videos from indoor/outdoor scenes. Projected to perspective views for training. Used for temporal consistency in video lighting estimation.
metric: N/A (training data), angular error for evaluation
notes: From Wang et al. (CVPR 2024). LuxDiT uses 2000 panorama videos for training and 12 LDR panoramic videos for temporal consistency evaluation.

name: WMT2020 Chinese-English
eval_time: hours for full evaluation with quality estimation models
format: Chinese→English news translation test set with system-level outputs from multiple teams; evaluated using MQM annotations
metric: MQM, Pearson/Kendall correlation with human rankings

name: MQM (Multidimensional Quality Metrics)
format: Human annotation framework for MT quality evaluation using error categories (accuracy, fluency, style) with severity scoring; used as gold-standard reference in WMT competitions

name: COMET-Kiwi
eval_time: minutes to hours for sentence-level QE on WMT-scale test sets
format: Reference-free sentence-level quality estimation model (Unbabel/Unbabel 2022); predicts HTER-style quality scores; used as alignment scoring backbone in Align-then-Slide

name: COMET-22 (XCOMET-22)
eval_time: minutes to hours for sentence-level QE
format: Unbabel's 2022 quality estimation model; predict sentence-level quality scores; used as alignment scoring backbone variant in Align-then-Slide ablation

name: LaBSE (Language-Agnostic BERT Sentence Embedding)
eval_time: minutes to hours for sentence-level similarity scoring
format: Google's language-agnostic sentence embedding model; used for sentence alignment scoring in Align-then-Slide ablation; produces multilingual sentence similarity scores

name: MNRE
format: Social media posts with images; text-image pairs annotated with relations between textual entities (head entity, relation, tail entity)
notes: Multimodal Neural Relation Extraction dataset. Images serve as auxiliary context for extracting relations between textual entities. Proposed by Zheng et al. (ICME 2021).

name: MORE
format: Text-image pairs with visual objects; relations between textual entities and visual objects (entity-object relations)
notes: Multimodal Object-Entity Relation Extraction dataset. Introduces entity-object relation extraction where one entity is textual and the other is a visual object. Proposed by He et al. (ACM MM 2023).

name: UMRE
num_classes: 28 relation types (3 types: entity-entity, object-object, entity-object)
format: Text-image pairs with annotated entities and objects; unified multimodal relation extraction task covering intra-modal (text-text, image-image) and inter-modal (text-image) relations
notes: Unified Multimodal Relation Extraction dataset. First unified MRE dataset handling entity-entity, object-object, and entity-object relations simultaneously. Proposed by Lin et al. (ACM MM 2025).

name: OpenOOD
num_samples: ~NINCO: 2,000+ classes; SSB-hard: ~80 classes (source from Vaze et al. 2021)
format: Comprehensive OOD detection benchmark with near-OOD datasets (NINCO, SSB-hard) and far-OOD datasets (iNaturalist, Texture, OpenImage-O). Tests OOD detection under varying difficulty levels.
notes: Primary OOD detection benchmark used in ANTS paper (2509.03951). NINCO (Bitterwolf et al. 2023) provides diverse near-OOD classes; SSB-hard (Vaze et al. 2021) provides superclass-level OOD.

name: NINCO
format: Near-OOD detection dataset: classes that are semantically and visually similar to ImageNet-1K classes but not part of it. Used as near-OOD benchmark in OpenOOD.
notes: From Bitterwolf et al. (arXiv:2306.00826). Part of OpenOOD benchmark for evaluating OOD detection in near-distribution scenarios.

name: SSB-hard
format: Superclass-level OOD benchmark: classes grouped into ~80 superclasses distinct from ImageNet-1K's 1000 classes. More challenging near-OOD setting.
access: https://github.com/step功能/SSB (referenced in Vaze et al. 2021)
notes: From Vaze et al. (2021) 'Open-set Recognition: A good closed-set classifier is all you need?' Part of OpenOOD for hard near-OOD detection evaluation.

name: Stanford-CARS
format: Fine-grained car classification dataset with 196 car models across 8 major categories (Convertibles, Coupes, etc.). Train/test split by manufacturer.
notes: Krause et al. (2013). Used as an additional ID dataset in ANTS paper for OOD detection evaluation.

name: APRICOT
num_samples: 873 test images with physical adversarial patches
format: Photos with physical adversarial patches trained to create nonexistent objects; patches have varying shapes and are placed on real-world objects

name: INRIA-Person
format: Person detection dataset with bounding box annotations; widely used for adversarial patch attack/defense evaluation

name: NuminaMath-1.5
format: Large-scale math problem dataset; used in BFS-Prover-V2 (arXiv:2509.06493) for autoformalization into ~3M Lean4 problems for neural theorem proving training.
notes: Subset of NuminaMath dataset used in BFS-Prover-V2 paper. Combined with NuminaMath-CoT and Goedel-Prover data to form the 3M problem training corpus.

name: CogEdit
num_samples: 1,174 VQA questions (curated from GQA, MSVD, VizWiz)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model size
format: VQA instances with editing prompts covering 3 meta-cognitive levels: Counterfactual-Driven, Boundary-Constraint, Noise-Robust. Each instance includes image, editing text prompt, original output, and target output.
notes: Novel benchmark for evaluating meta-cognitive knowledge editing in MLLMs. Introduces 3 capability tiers (Self-Awareness, Boundary Monitoring, Reflective Thinking) to assess whether editing methods possess metacognitive abilities beyond standard cognitive editing (Reliability/Generality/Locality).

name: MMEdit
num_samples: ~1,000+ editing instances across E-VQA and E-IC subtasks
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model size
format: Multimodal editing instances: image + text prompt pairs requiring model knowledge update. E-VQA based on VQAv2; E-IC based on COCO Captions.
notes: Cognitive multimodal knowledge editing benchmark. Standard benchmark for evaluating whether editing methods can update MLLM knowledge while preserving Reliability (editing success), Generality (generalization), and Locality (unchanged unrelated knowledge).

name: DCASE2025 Task 3 (Track B: Stereo SELD)
format: Stereo WAV audio + perspective video; FOA-derived stereo signals; multi-track labels (class, DOA azimuth, distance, on/off-screen)
metric: F1 (F_{<=20deg/1} and F_{<=20deg/1/on}), DOAE (Direction of Arrival Error in degrees), RDE (Relative Distance Error), On/Off-Screen Accuracy
notes: DCASE 2025 Challenge Task 3 Track B: Stereo Sound Event Localization and Detection with Source Distance Estimation. Shifted from traditional FOA/MIC formats to stereo from frontal video content. Azimuth range limited to [-90deg, 90deg]. Audio-visual track (B) requires predicting on/off-screen source activity. Paper used this benchmark.

name: FSD50K
num_samples: ~51K audio clips (20.1h total, mean duration ~1.4s per clip)
format: Audio clips (0.1-30s) with single-label or multi-label sound event annotations from 200 classes; derived from AudioSet
notes: Freesound Dataset 50K. Human-labeled open dataset of sound events. Used in this paper as source audio for synthetic SELD data generation via SpatialScaper. Paper: Fonseca et al., IEEE/ACM TASLP 2022.

name: STARSS23 (Sony STARSS)
format: 360-degree ambisonics audio + 360-degree video; multi-track labels with class, azimuth/elevation DOA, distance, on/off-screen for each event
notes: Audio-visual dataset of spatial recordings of real scenes with spatiotemporal annotations of sound events. Used as source for stereo video generation in DCASE2025 Task 3. Paper: Shimada et al., NeurIPS 2023.

name: SciRepEval
num_samples: 19 tasks across 4 formats (Proximity, Regression, Query, Classification)
format: Scientific paper representation evaluation benchmark covering classification, regression, proximity, and query tasks
metric: nDCG, MAP, Avg. P, K Tau, Wt. F1, F1 (varies by task)
notes: Multi-format benchmark for scientific document representations. Used in FLeW paper (arXiv:2509.07531) as one of two main evaluation benchmarks.

name: MDCR (Multi-Field Citation Recommendation)
format: Citation recommendation dataset across 19 academic fields; evaluate by MAP and Recall@5
notes: Used in FLeW paper (arXiv:2509.07531) to evaluate across 19 academic fields for citation recommendation.

name: Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG)
num_samples: Millions of papers with citation relationships
format: Large-scale academic paper corpus with citation graph, paper metadata, abstracts; used for training scientific document representation models
notes: Base corpus for FLeW paper (arXiv:2509.07531); used to construct citation graph for structural sampling and obtain title/abstract metadata.

name: Open-ASQA
format: Audio instruction data from AudioSet, AudioCaps, FSD50K, FreeSound, LibriTTS, VGGSound, VoxCeleb. Multiple-choice QA pairs.
access: https://github.com/LTU-AS/ASQA (from LTU-AS paper, Gong et al., 2023)
notes: Largest publicly available audio instruction dataset at time of development. Used as primary training corpus for Falcon3-Audio (arXiv:2509.07526).

name: AIR-Bench Foundational
format: Instruction-following tasks across speech, sound, and music. Single-choice Q&A format.
metric: accuracy (correct content match, treating invalid generations as incorrect)
notes: AIR-Bench Foundational covers 19 distinct tasks: vocal sound classification, acoustic scene classification, sound QA, music instruments/genre/note/emotion/QA, speech grounding, spoken language ID, speaker gender/age recognition, emotion recognition, speech entity recognition, intent classification, speaker number verification, synthesized voice detection. Falcon3-Audio-7B scores 54.0 average vs Qwen2-Audio Instruct at 44.0 (arXiv:2509.07526).

name: AIR-Bench Chat
format: Open-ended audio question answering across speech, sound, music, and mixed audio types.
metric: GPT-4 Turbo scoring (1-10 scale, averaged with position-bias mitigation)
notes: AIR-Bench Chat uses GPT-4 Turbo (gpt-4-0125-preview) as evaluator. Falcon3-Audio-7B scores 6.20 average (arXiv:2509.07526).

name: FreeSound
format: Freesound audio clips with labels. Used as data source for Open-ASQA.
notes: Used as data source for Open-ASQA training set in Falcon3-Audio (arXiv:2509.07526).

name: EventHallusion
format: Binary QA and open-ended QA evaluating hallucination in VideoLLMs; categories: entire, mix, misleading; videos range from few seconds to 30 seconds
notes: Benchmark for diagnosing event hallucinations in VideoLLMs. Proposed by Zhang et al. (arXiv:2409.16597). Used in VPS paper (arXiv:2509.08016) to evaluate fine-grained motion perception and hallucination mitigation.

name: FE240hz
format: High frame rate RGB-Event tracking dataset captured with DAVIS346 camera (346x260 resolution). Focus on real-world challenges: low lighting, high dynamic range, motion blur, fast object motion. Event frames accumulated between consecutive RGB frames.

name: COESOT
format: Large-scale RGB-Event tracking dataset with broader target categories (vehicles, pedestrians, animals including birds, monkeys, elephants). Captured with DAVIS346 camera.

name: TUS-REC
num_samples: 1,248 freehand 2D US forearm scans from 53 volunteers (training: 50 subjects/1176 scans, test: 3 subjects/72 scans)
format: 2D US image sequences with probe trajectory ground truth (6-DoF poses as 4x4 homogeneous matrices or 6D parameterization)
metric: GPE (Global Point Error, mm), LPE (Local Point Error, µm), FDR (Final Drift Rate, %), Max Drift (mm)
notes: Trackerless 3D Freehand Ultrasound Reconstruction Challenge from MICCAI 2024. Median scan length 546 timesteps (~27 seconds). Average translational distance 167mm. Scan shapes include linear and non-linear (wavy) trajectories.

name: EMNS (/imz/ corpus)
format: Audio (emotive narrative storytelling) + transcripts
notes: EMNS corpus: emotive single-speaker dataset for narrative storytelling in games, television, and graphic novels. Used as out-of-domain evaluation dataset in WhisTLE paper (arXiv:2509.10452).

name: EmoV-DB
format: Audio (emotional speech) + transcripts
notes: Emotional Voices Database: controlling emotion dimension in voice generation systems. Used as out-of-domain evaluation dataset in WhisTLE paper (arXiv:2509.10452).

name: ST-AEDS (Free ST American English corpus)
format: Audio (American English) + transcripts
notes: Free ST American English corpus used as out-of-domain evaluation dataset in WhisTLE paper (arXiv:2509.10452). Small dataset for accented English speech.

name: EABI (English Accents in the British Isles)
num_samples: multiple speakers across British Isles accents
format: Audio (British Isles accents) + transcripts
notes: Open-source Multi-speaker Corpora of the English Accents in the British Isles (LREC 2020). Used as out-of-domain evaluation dataset in WhisTLE paper (arXiv:2509.10452).

name: Value Portrait (VP)
num_samples: 520 query-response pairs from 104 real-world queries (ShareGPT, LMSYS, Reddit, Dear Abby)
format: Psychometrically validated scenario-response pairs with construct annotations (Schwartz values + Big Five traits); responses validated via human correlation study (681 participants)
metric: log-probability of construct-expressing responses; Spearman rho, NDCG for cross-method comparison
notes: Used in arXiv:2509.10078 to compare generation probability profiles vs. questionnaire profiles for LLM psychometrics. Each query has 5 candidate responses tagged with Schwartz value or Big Five personality constructs.

name: AncientDoc
num_samples: ~3,000 pages, 5 tasks (OCR, vernacular translation, reasoning-QA, knowledge-QA, linguistic variant QA)
format: Chinese ancient document images with QA annotations; page-level OCR ground truth; vernacular translation references; QA pairs for reasoning/knowledge/linguistic tasks
metric: CER, Char Precision/Recall/F1 (OCR); CHRF++, BERTScore, GPT-4o Score (QA tasks)
notes: First benchmark for Chinese ancient documents. Covers 14 document types (biography, Confucianism, astronomy/math, medical, poetry, etc.), ~100 books, from Warring States to Qing dynasty. Evaluates VLMs on OCR, translation, and multi-level QA tasks.

name: CoCoNUTS
format: Peer review texts with ternary labels (Human/Mix/AI) based on content composition, and six fine-grained categories (HW, HWMT, HWMP, HWMG, MG, MGMP)
metric: macro F1, accuracy, false positive rate
license: not stated (code and data promised publicly available at github.com/Y1hanChen/COCONUTS)

name: HMMT24
format: Harvard-MIT Math Tournament 2024 short-answer problems curated as 30 prompt set
metric: answer accuracy (32 sampled generations per question)

name: ISOLET
format: Spoken letter recognition: 26 classes (A-Z), each speaker pronounces all 26 letters twice; features: 617 spectral, peak, and phoneme features

name: UCI-HAR
format: Human activity recognition from smartphone sensors (accelerometer + gyroscope); 6 classes (walking, walking_upstairs, walking_downstairs, sitting, standing, laying); 3-axis raw signals at 50Hz, 2.56s sliding windows

name: BrowseComp
num_samples: 1,266 (full set); 266-sample subset used during RL training for fast eval
eval_time: hours-days (requires multi-turn strategic web search via Serper API; 128-turn limit per instance)
format: Challenging benchmark for browsing agents requiring long-horizon reasoning and deep search across multiple blurry entities; questions designed to require hours of expert-level search; evaluation uses LLM-as-judge (Llama-3.1-70B) to verify final answer against ground truth
notes: Introduced by Wei et al. (arXiv:2504.12516). Proprietary models like OpenAI DeepResearch achieve 51.5%; best open-source models historically scored below 10%. DeepDive-32B (arXiv:2509.10446) achieves 15.3%, setting a new open-source SOTA at its time of publication.

name: BrowseComp-ZH
eval_time: hours (requires multi-turn strategic web search in Chinese)
format: Chinese-language version of BrowseComp; same challenging deep search requirements but Chinese web sources; evaluation uses LLM-as-judge
notes: Introduced by Zhou et al. (arXiv:2504.19314). DeepDive-32B (arXiv:2509.10446) achieves 29.7% on this benchmark.

name: Xbench-DeepSearch
format: Deep search benchmark covering diverse factual domains; requires strategic multi-hop web browsing and evidence synthesis; evaluation uses LLM-as-judge
notes: From Xbench-Team (2025). DeepDive-32B (arXiv:2509.10446) achieves 51.8% on this benchmark, outperforming many proprietary models.

name: SEAL-0
eval_time: hours (requires strategic web search and result selection)
format: Benchmark requiring models to recognize and select among different search results; tests ability to distinguish relevant from irrelevant web content; evaluation uses LLM-as-judge
notes: Introduced by Pham et al. (arXiv:2506.01062). DeepDive-32B (arXiv:2509.10446) achieves 25.5% on this benchmark.

name: Design2Code
num_samples: 484 real-world webpage screenshots with HTML/CSS ground truth
format: Webpage screenshots paired with front-end code (HTML/CSS); used to evaluate MLLM UI2Code generation quality
metric: CLIP Score, BLEU, Block Match, Text Similarity, Position Similarity, Color Similarity
notes: First real-world benchmark for UI2Code with 484 manually curated webpages from Common Crawl. Introduced by Chen et al. Used in EfficientUICoder (arXiv:2509.12159) as primary evaluation benchmark.

name: WebCode2M
format: Large-scale dataset of webpage screenshots with corresponding HTML/CSS code; includes WebCode2M-short, WebCode2M-mid, WebCode2M-long splits
notes: Large-scale UI2Code dataset for training and evaluation. Used in EfficientUICoder (arXiv:2509.12159) with 100 samples each from short/mid/long splits as test set.

name: MILLSTONE
num_samples: 105930 prompts per model (107 issues x 6 prompt templates x 11 argument configurations x 15 trials for 5 models; 9900 per model for 4 additional models on 10 controversial issues)
eval_time: days to weeks depending on API rate limits
format: Structured prompts with neutral question templates + in-context pro/con arguments; response is A/B stance classification
metric: open-mindedness score (0-100, higher = more swayed by arguments)
license: Not publicly released at paper submission
access: Contact authors; source data from Encyclopedia Britannica ProCon (publicly available)
notes: Benchmark for measuring LLM susceptibility to in-context arguments on 107 contentious issues. Introduced in arXiv:2509.11967 (MILLSTONE: How Open-Minded Are LLMs?). Source: Encyclopedia Britannica ProCon website. Arguments are human-written, non-adversarial, from authoritative sources with citations.

name: GraphInstruct
eval_time: minutes to hours (depends on LLM backend)
format: Synthetic graph reasoning questions with ground-truth answers; graphs specified as edge lists; tasks include cycle detection, connectivity, bipartite check, topological sort, shortest path, maximum triangle sum, maximum flow, subgraph matching, indegree/outdegree calculation
access: https://github.com/hanklee97121/GRRAF/ (released by paper authors); originally from Chen et al. 2024 (GraphWiz)

name: DragBench
format: Images with user-provided drag instructions (handle and target point pairs) for point-based image editing

name: BGL
num_samples: ~4.7M log entries (BGL dataset); session-level: 8000 entries; template-level: 3046 unique templates
format: Unstructured system log entries with anomaly labels (normal/abnormal); chronological split for train/test
notes: Blue Gene/L supercomputer log dataset. Contains labeling errors (225 corrected by RationAnomaly authors). Used for log anomaly detection benchmark.

name: Spirit
num_samples: ~70M log entries (Spirit dataset); session-level: 8000 entries; template-level: unique templates from Spirit
format: Unstructured system log entries with anomaly labels (normal/abnormal); Spirit system log from HPC cluster; chronological split
notes: Spirit supercomputer log dataset. Part of LogHub collection. Contains labeling errors corrected by RationAnomaly authors.

name: LogHub
format: Collection of system log datasets from HPC systems, distributed systems, and operating systems; standardized extraction pipelines
notes: Large-scale log dataset collection introduced in arXiv:2008.06448. Includes BGL, Spirit, ThunderBird, and other widely-used log anomaly detection datasets.

name: RANZCR-CLiP
format: Chest X-ray images with annotated catheter and line positions (ETT, NGT, CVC, chest tube, etc.) for segmentation
notes: Public dataset for lines and tubes segmentation in chest X-rays. Used in arXiv:2509.12818 as holdout evaluation set. From Tang et al., Scientific Data 2021.

name: CoRE MOF 2019
format: Crystallographic Information Files (CIF) for MOF structures with properties from GCMC simulations
metric: MAE for N2 adsorption capacity, N2/CO2 separation selectivity
notes: Computation-Ready, Experimental MOF database. Chung et al. 2019, J. Chem. Eng. Data 64, 5985. Used for gas adsorption/separation benchmarks.

name: IZA Zeolite Database
format: Crystallographic Information Files (CIF) for zeolite frameworks
notes: International Zeolite Association database of known zeolite framework types. Each framework type can have multiple cation positions and Al distributions.

name: QMOF
format: MOF structures in CIF/JSON with DFT-computed band gaps and other electronic properties
notes: Quantum-MOF database. Rosen et al. 2021, Matter 4, 1578. Contains MOF structures with DFT-computed band gaps, used for electrical conduction prediction proxy.

name: CoRE MOF N2/CO2 Binary Adsorption Dataset
num_samples: ~5000 MOF structures with binary gas adsorption data
format: GCMC simulation results for CO2/N2 binary mixture adsorption in MOFs
metric: MAE for N2 and CO2 uptake in mixed-gas conditions
notes: Newly constructed dataset by authors of arXiv:2509.15908 using gRASPA software. Simulated CO2/N2 binary adsorption at 1 bar total pressure on CoRE MOF 2019 structures.

name: Gecko
num_samples: Not publicly specified; diverse prompt set with fine-grained categories for text-to-image evaluation
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Text-to-image prompt set covering diverse generation aspects; used for human preference evaluation and Gecko score (alignment metric)
metric: Gecko score (alignment), human preference win rate

name: GenAI-Bench
num_samples: Not publicly specified; compositional text-to-visual generation prompts
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Text-to-visual generation benchmark with compositional prompts for evaluating text alignment and visual quality

name: MARIO-eval
num_samples: Not publicly specified; text rendering prompts for evaluating legible text in generated images
format: Text-to-image benchmark focused on text rendering legibility; prompts request specific text to appear in generated images
metric: Human preference win rate (text rendering quality)

name: GeckoNum
num_samples: Not publicly specified; numerical reasoning prompts requiring counting skills
format: Text-to-image benchmark for evaluating numerical reasoning (counting objects/entities) in generated images

name: DIQA-5000
format: Document images (1600x1600) with multi-dimensional quality ratings: overall quality, sharpness, color fidelity (MOS from 15 raters per image)

name: SmartDoc-QA
format: Smartphone-captured document images with OCR-based quality metrics (CACC, WACC)

name: ImageWoof
format: A 10-class subset of ImageNet-1K consisting of more challenging dog breed classes: Australian terrier, Border terrier, Samoyed, Tibetan terrier, Rhodesian ridgeback, Dingo, Golden retriever, English foxhound, Old English sheepdog, Siberian husky. Images at 500px resolution.

name: Audiocite
num_samples: ~2800 hours of read French speech (full dataset)
format: 16kHz French read speech audiobooks with transcripts
license: CC BY 4.0 (per Felice et al., LREC-COLING 2024)
notes: French read speech corpus from Audiocite.net (Felice et al., LREC-COLING 2024). The paper subsamples to ~1000h of audio, balanced by gender. Comparable to LibriLight for English.

name: Weibo-19
format: Chinese Weibo posts with text, images, and comments; binary rumor/non-rumor labels
access: https://github.com/ICTMCG/NEP or request from dataset authors
notes: Multimodal rumor detection dataset from Weibo (Chinese Twitter). Used in TriSPrompt paper (arXiv:2509.19352).

name: Pheme
format: Twitter tweets with text, images, and comments across 5 breaking news events; binary rumor/non-rumor labels
notes: Multimodal rumor detection dataset from Twitter. Used in TriSPrompt paper (arXiv:2509.19352).

name: Weibo-17
format: Chinese Weibo posts with text and images (no comments); binary rumor/non-rumor labels
notes: Multimodal rumor detection dataset from Weibo (Chinese Twitter). Only has text+image modalities (no comments). Used in TriSPrompt paper (arXiv:2509.19352).

name: UA-Speech
num_samples: ~16 speakers x ~300 utterances each (approx 9 hours total)
eval_time: hours for ASR training and evaluation
format: Audio recordings of dysarthric speech (16 speakers with varying intelligibility levels) with orthographic transcripts at utterance and word levels
access: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, requires data agreement
notes: Dysarthric Speech Database for Universal Access Research (Kim et al., Interspeech 2008). 16 speakers with cerebral palsy causing dysarthria, categorized by intelligibility levels (high, medium, low, very low). Standard benchmark for impaired speech ASR.

name: BF-Sprache
