num_samples: 505 isolated words from a single child speaker with Apert syndrome
format: German isolated-word recordings from a pediatric speaker with Apert syndrome; semantic re-chaining applied to create continuous speech for foundation model compatibility
access: Available from authors upon request / ethical approval
notes: From Pokel et al. (DiSS 2025). German impaired speech dataset with longitudinal clinical logopedic reports for validation. Semantic re-chaining concatenates isolated words into coherent sentences for use with continuous speech ASR models.

name: 2D Kolmogorov Flow (Lippe et al. 2023)
eval_time: minutes to hours per model for 99-step autoregressive rollout
format: 2D vorticity fields on 128x128 periodic grid, Navier-Stokes pseudospectral simulation
metric: Relative L2 error at 1-step, 60-step, and 99-step autoregressive rollout
license: Open-source (from Lippe et al. 2023 PDE-Refiner paper)

name: 2D Decaying Isotropic Turbulence (Takamoto et al. 2022)
eval_time: minutes per model for 19-step autoregressive rollout
format: 2D decaying isotropic turbulence vorticity fields on 64x64 periodic grid
metric: Relative L2 error at 1-step, 10-step, and 19-step autoregressive rollout; energy spectrum fidelity
license: Open-source (from Takamoto et al. 2022 PDEBench paper)

name: Prometheus-T (Wu et al. 2024b)
storage: ~80GB (32x480 sensor arrays, temperature and flue gas concentration fields)
eval_time: hours per model for multi-step forecasting
format: Fire dynamics simulation via FDS: 2D tunnel cross-section with temperature and flue gas concentration fields at 32x480 resolution
metric: Relative L2 error on in-distribution and out-of-distribution (OOD) physical environments
license: Research use (from Wu et al. 2024b Prometheus paper)

name: LOKI
format: Zero-shot evaluation benchmark for MLLMs to detect synthetic data across multimodal contexts. Includes Image Judgment Task where models identify synthetic or real images across categories: Scene, Animal, Person, Object, Medicine, Doc, Satellite
notes: Introduced by Ye et al. 2024. Comprehensive evaluation for MLLM synthetic data detection across diverse, unseen categories. Zero-shot tested in ThinkFake paper.

name: 3D-FRONT
num_samples: 5,616 indoor scenes with layout and semantic annotations
storage: ~100-200GB (rendered panoramic videos at 256x512, 40 frames per scene)
format: Indoor 3D scenes with furniture layouts and semantic annotations; rendered as panoramic videos via cubemap-to-equirectangular projection; camera trajectories generated within each scene
notes: Used in CamPVG (arXiv:2509.19979) for training camera-controlled panoramic video generation. Scenes rendered with camera trajectories to produce 40-frame panoramic video clips at 256x512 resolution.

name: Spoken StereoSet
format: Audio-based stereotype benchmark evaluating bias toward speaker in SpeechLLMs (speech pairs with male/female voices)
notes: From Lin et al. (2024a) at IEEE SLT. Designed to evaluate semantic gender bias in speech-integrated LLMs. Used as one source for Gender-Stereotypical category in arXiv:2509.21125 acoustic-based gender differentiation study.

name: P4D (Prompting4Debugging)
eval_time: hours (requires running T2I inference + NudeNet detection)
format: Adversarial text prompts discovered through automated prompt engineering with unconstrained diffusion models; designed to bypass concept erasure methods
metric: Attack success rate (ASR) via NudeNet detection; lower is better for erased model
notes: Red-teaming benchmark for concept erasure methods; P4D-N-16 is the nudity subset with 151 prompts used in SNCE paper (2509.21008) and RECE paper

name: MoralExceptQA
format: Challenge set of rule-breaking moral scenarios, each labeled as 'permissible' or 'not permissible'

name: UNIMORAL
num_samples: ~thousands of moral dilemma scenarios across 6 languages
format: Multilingual dataset of moral dilemmas annotated with human decisions, reasoning, emotions, and moral values across six languages
notes: Used in this paper (arXiv:2509.21443) to train a regressor mapping (scenario, action) pairs to MFQ2 moral value scores for analyzing inherent moral values in LLM decisions.

name: Target-QA
num_samples: Hundreds of cancer cell lines (stratified by TCGA cancer types)
storage: Estimated 100-500GB+ (multi-omic data for hundreds of cancer cell lines)
format: Query (cell line, disease, multi-omic features, subgraph context) with CRISPR-prioritized gene target answers
metric: NDCG, MRR, Recall, Precision, Hit@5, Hit@10
access: Released by authors on Huggingface/GitHub (per paper abstract)

name: DepMap (Cancer Dependency Map)
num_samples: ~1000 cancer cell lines with CRISPR screens
format: CRISPR gene essentiality scores, multi-omic profiles (genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics)

name: BioMedGraphica
format: Text-attributed knowledge graphs with protein-protein interactions and disease-target relationships
access: Referenced by GALAX paper (Zhang et al., 2025)

name: PedDep
storage: Small (<10GB for 31 cell lines with multi-omic + CRISPR data)
format: Multi-omic profiles and CRISPR-based targets for pediatric cancer cell lines
metric: Same as Target-QA (NDCG, MRR, Recall, Precision, Hit@K)
access: Referenced in GALAX paper - external validation dataset

name: T2I-CompBench
format: Compositional text-to-image prompts testing compositional relations (binding attributes to objects, spatial relationships,否决逻辑colors, textures), textures, and complex logical negation
metric: CLIPScore, attribute binding accuracy, compositional success rate
notes: From Huang et al. (NeurIPS 2023). Comprehensive benchmark for open-world compositional text-to-image generation. Tests whether T2I models can correctly bind attributes, handle spatial relations, and understand complex logical constraints.

name: HRS-Bench
format: Holistic evaluation prompts assessing high-level reasoning, commonsense, and world knowledge in T2I generation across 18 categories including objects, actions, scenes, text rendering, and spatial reasoning
notes: From Bakr et al. (ICCV 2023). Holistic, reliable and scalable benchmark for text-to-image models. Evaluates high-level reasoning and commonsense knowledge beyond simple attribute binding.

name: TIFA
format: Text-to-image faithfulness evaluation via VQA. Prompts paired with automatically generated questions about objects, attributes, counts, and spatial relations in the generated image.
notes: From Hu et al. (ICCV 2023). Text-to-Image Faithfulness Evaluation with Question Answering. Uses VLM to ask specific questions about generated images to verify prompt-image consistency.

name: OpenWebTextCorpus
format: Open-source replication of GPT-2's training corpus; web text scraped from URLs shared on Reddit with score >= 3, deduplicated and quality filtered

name: GENESISGEO-1M
format: Multimodal records pairing rendered geometry diagrams with formal construction DSL, predicate DSL descriptions, auxiliary constructions (), and complete DDAR proof traces. Each problem includes , , , blocks.
access: Not yet released (promised with paper arXiv:2509.21896)
notes: Large-scale synthetic dataset for visual geometric reasoning. Generated with automated synthesis pipeline using a C++ DDAR symbolic engine. Problems require auxiliary constructions and include machine-checkable proof traces. Enables joint learning of diagram understanding, symbolic reasoning, and proof generation.

name: IMO-30
format: Formalized IMO geometry problems in DSL format, paired with ground-truth proof traces
notes: Benchmark of 30 IMO geometry problems introduced in AlphaGeometry (Trinh et al., Nature 2024). Used to evaluate geometry theorem proving systems. GenesisGeo-2B solves 29/30 on this benchmark.

name: IMO-95
format: Formalized IMO geometry problems from the Newclid repository, with constructions supported by AlphaGeometry
notes: Subset of formalized IMO problems from Newclid (Sicca et al., 2024). Contains 95 problems covering a broader range of IMO difficulty. GenesisGeo-2B solves 63/95 on this benchmark.

name: HAGeo-409
format: Geometry problems in formal DSL format covering high-school and Olympiad difficulty
notes: Larger benchmark of 409 high-school and Olympiad-level geometry problems from HAGeo (Duan et al., 2025). 5 problems excluded whose constructions are unsupported by AlphaGeometry. GenesisGeo-2B solves 278/409 on this benchmark.

name: Physion
num_samples: 200+ synthetic scenes with ground truth physics
format: Synthetic 3D scenes with ground truth physical properties; evaluates physical commonsense prediction in terms of object interactions, collisions, stability; scenes include multi-object interactions with varying material properties
metric: n/a (dataset); physical plausibility metrics for evaluation

name: Physics101
format: Unlabeled videos of 101 everyday objects with varying material properties (shapes, colors, sizes); 5 physical scenarios: fall, liquid, multi, ramp, spring; used to study physical properties learning from videos
metric: n/a (dataset); MSE for motion forecasting evaluation

name: MMIU
format: Multiple-choice QA for multi-image understanding; 52 tasks across 7 types of multi-image relationships

name: PrincipleBench
format: Human-annotated binary principles (clarity, accuracy, relevance, no repetition, language alignment, essential information, requirements complete) with pairwise chosen/rejected responses. Principles are reworded from HelpSteer3-Preference validation subset. Includes single-turn and multi-turn (up to 10 prior turns) prompts across General, STEM, Code (14 languages), and Multilingual (13 languages).
metric: Micro-averaged pairwise accuracy (GenRM correct only when both chosen-first and rejected-first orders agree)
access: Not publicly released at time of publication (arXiv:2509.21319)
notes: Benchmark introduced in RLBFF paper (arXiv:2509.21319) to measure reward model adherence to specific principles. Top performers: Flexible Principles ScalarRM (91.6%), Flexible Principles GenRM (83.8%).

name: BarExamQA
format: Multiple-choice legal questions from practical bar exams, paired with gold passage documents for legal reasoning
notes: Legal reasoning benchmark from Zheng et al. (2025). Used in RLAG paper (2509.20162) for evaluating knowledge embedding in legal domain.

name: DEEPTRACEREWARD
num_samples: 3,318 fake + 3,318 real videos; 4,334 deepfake trace annotations
format: AI-generated and real videos with fine-grained spatiotemporal deepfake trace annotations: bounding boxes, onset/offset timestamps, natural language explanations, and category labels across 9 artifact types
metric: Overall score = (Accuracy + Explanation_score + BBox_IoU + (100 - Time_distance)) / 4; plus individual metrics: Accuracy, Fake/Real Accuracy, BBox IoU, BBox Distance, Time Distance
notes: First fine-grained benchmark for human-perceived deepfake trace detection in AI-generated videos. 9 trace categories: Object Distortion, Sudden Blurring, Object Trajectory, Redundant Object, Object Merging, Object Splitting, Background Distortion, Object Disappearance, Unexpected Move. From arXiv:2509.22646 (Fupp et al., Princeton/UPenn).

name: BraTS-Reg
num_samples: Multiple pre-/post-operative MRI pairs from glioma patients (exact number varies by subset)
storage: ~5-10GB (multimodal brain MRI: T1, T1ce, T2, FLAIR, plus follow-up scans)
format: Multimodal brain MRI volumes (T1, T1-weighted with contrast, T2, FLAIR) from pre- and post-operative glioma patients; used for evaluating registration uncertainty in the presence of tumor resection

name: Learn2Reg ThoraxCBCT
num_samples: Multiple CBCT/CT thoracic pairs (exact number varies by challenge year)
storage: ~10-20GB (thorax CBCT and CT volumes with different fields of view)
format: Paired thorax CBCT and CT volumes from lung cancer patients; CBCT has limited FOV and more artifacts compared to planning CT; used for evaluating registration uncertainty under FOV mismatch

name: SEEDBench
num_samples: ~19K multiple-choice questions over images and videos
format: Multiple-choice QA for multimodal understanding covering image comprehension, video understanding, knowledge competence, etc.
notes: SEEDBench (Li et al., 2023a) used in Uni-X paper (arXiv:2509.24365) for multimodal understanding evaluation.

name: EgoProceL
num_samples: 62 hours of egocentric video, 130 users, 16 tasks
format: Head-mounted egocentric videos of procedural tasks (cooking, assembly) with frame-level key-step annotations. Tasks from CMU-MMAC, EGTEA-GAZE+, MECCANO, EPIC-Tents. Contains background frames, non-monotonic step ordering, and repeated actions.
metric: F1-score, temporal IoU for key-step detection and alignment

name: ProceL
format: Third-person instructional videos for procedure learning. Tasks: clarinet, PB&J sandwich, salmon, jump car, toilet, tire change, tie-tie, coffee, iPhone battery, repot plant, chromecast, CPR.
metric: F1-score, temporal IoU for key-step detection

name: MECCANO
num_samples: 20 videos, 17 key-steps for industrial assembly tasks
format: Egocentric videos of human-object interactions in an industrial-like domain. Assembly tasks with foreground ratio ~0.50, some missing and repeated key-steps.

name: EPIC-Tents
num_samples: 29 videos, 12 key-steps for camping tent assembly
format: Egocentric videos of tent assembly procedures. Significant background content (foreground ratio ~0.63), ~14% missing steps, ~73% repeated steps.

name: CMU-MMAC
num_samples: Multi-modal recordings across multiple subjects performing kitchen and mechanical tasks
format: Multi-modal dataset: RGB video, motion capture, accelerometer, gyroscope, EMG, audio. Tasks include cooking (brownie, eggs, pizza, salad, sandwich) and other procedural activities.

name: Panda70m
format: Large-scale video dataset with captions generated using multiple cross-modality teachers; covers diverse video content
notes: Used as training data for DC-AE-V in DC-VideoGen paper. Subset was used, not full 70M.

name: OpenVid1m
format: Large-scale high-quality dataset for text-to-video generation
notes: Used as training data for DC-AE-V in DC-VideoGen paper.

name: OVBench
format: MC streaming video QA pairs for online video understanding with past memory, real-time perception, and future prediction tasks

name: ODV-Bench
format: MC video QA pairs for real-time streaming video understanding in autonomous driving scenarios. Covers static target, dynamic target, and multi-agent interaction tasks.

name: OnlineIT
num_samples: ~490K instances (32K general + 89K drive + other source datasets)
format: Streaming video instruction-tuning dataset with OnlineIT-general (spatial, temporal, spatiotemporal, event perception tasks) and OnlineIT-drive (autonomous driving scenarios). Used to train StreamForest for streaming video understanding.

name: MMHalBench
num_samples: ~500 questions across 8 question types and 12 object categories
format: VQA benchmark for hallucination detection in VLMs; GPT-4.1-mini as evaluator to score response quality and hallucination rate

name: WildVision
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Evaluates real-world user preference alignment for VLMs with human preference annotations; reports reward score and win rate

name: RLHF-V-Dataset
format: Fine-grained segment-level human preference data for VLM alignment; contains image-text pairs with preferred/rejected responses; covers outputs from Qwen-VL-Chat, InstructBLIP, LLaVA-13B; diverse image types including everyday scenes, WikiArt, landmarks, scene texts

name: ToTG-Bench
format: Long video temporal grounding benchmark with task-oriented (implicit) natural language queries requiring temporal localization. Covers 35 video domains and 12 task categories (perception and reasoning tasks).

name: V-STaR
format: Video spatio-temporal reasoning benchmark with explicit temporal description queries. Videos range from 15s to 59.2 min, covering 9 domains.

name: CG-Bench
format: Clue-grounded question answering benchmark for long video understanding. Covers 14 video domains with perception tasks on videos up to 1.8 hours.

name: VideoR1
format: Video reasoning dataset used for training VideoR1 (reinforced video reasoning in MLLMs). Used as source for ToTG-Pile construction.

name: FineVideo
format: Large-scale video dataset used for fine-tuning video MLLMs. Used as source for ToTG-Pile construction in TimeScope paper.

name: Visual Genome
num_samples: ~108K images with ~5.4M region descriptions, ~3.8M object annotations, ~2.8M relationships, ~1.8M attributes
format: Dense image annotations with region descriptions, object bounding boxes, relationships, attributes, and WordNet synonyms. Used for fine-tuning MLLM-based re-ranking scorers in ZS-CIR.
notes: Used for LoRA fine-tuning of MLLM scorer in SETR (arXiv:2509.26012). Relation triplets (subject, predicate, object) are converted into region-level captions for training binary yes/no semantic relevance scorer.

name: Hypersim
storage: ~50-100GB (synthetic indoor scenes with detailed depth GT)
format: Synthetic indoor scenes with precise depth, surface normals, and RGB; used for depth completion training
notes: Photorealistic synthetic dataset for indoor scene understanding (Roberts et al., ICCV 2021). Used as primary training set in DEPTHOR++ paper.

name: ZJU-L5
num_samples: ~1000+ frames with dToF (ST VL53L5CX 8x8) and RGB pairs
format: Raw dToF signals (ST VL53L5CX) and RGB pairs with ground truth from Intel RealSense 435i; dToF resolution 8x8, RGB 480x640
notes: dToF depth dataset from Li et al. (ECCV 2022). dToF captured with ST VL53L5CX, GT from Intel RealSense 435i. Used as primary evaluation benchmark in DEPTHOR++.

name: Hammer
format: Multi-sensor indoor dataset: RealSense L515 (dToF), Lucid Helios HLS003S-001 (iToF), RealSense D435; high-precision GT from Einscan-SP and Faro Focus S70 scanners with 3D rendering and AESUB Blue spray
notes: High-precision 3D dataset for depth benchmarking (Jung et al., CVPR 2023). RealSense L515 dToF data used as input in DEPTHOR++ experiments.

name: Mirror3D-NYU
format: NYUv2 depth maps with manually corrected mirror regions; ground truth refined in specular/transparent surface areas
notes: Mirror-corrected version of NYUv2 for depth refinement in specular regions (Tan et al., CVPR 2021). Used for evaluating anomaly detection on mirror surfaces.

name: NYUv2
format: Indoor RGB-D video with Kinect v1; depth maps and RGB images at 640x480; includes semantic labels and surface normals
notes: Standard depth estimation benchmark (Silberman et al., ECCV 2012). Used for qualitative evaluation in DEPTHOR++.

name: CV-Cities
num_samples: 223,736 panorama-satellite image pairs across 16 cities, 13 countries
format: Cross-view image pairs: ground-level panorama and corresponding satellite view with geolocation metadata (city, latitude, longitude). Spans 4 daily scenes (city, natural, water, occlusion).
access: Huang et al., 2025 — IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
notes: Used in Geo-R1 (arXiv:2510.00072) as the primary training dataset for both SFT scaffolding and GRPO cross-view pairing task.

name: GeoChain
num_samples: 1.46M Mapillary street-level images with 21-step CoT sequences, 30M+ QA pairs; test subset 2,088 images
format: Template-based chain-of-thought geospatial reasoning benchmark. Tasks span 13 subproblems: geographical (hemisphere, continent), environmental (coast, terrain, desert), sociocultural (language, city/town), and geolocation (state/province, city).
notes: Zero-shot evaluation benchmark for Geo-R1. 15 of 20 cities are out-of-distribution. Geo-R1 significantly outperforms base Qwen2.5-VL-7B across all 13 sub-tasks.

name: IMAGEO-Bench
num_samples: IMAGEO-GSS: 6,152 images from 396 cities (global); IMAGEO-UPC: 2,928 images (US-wide)
format: Standardized image geolocalization benchmark for VLMs requiring step-by-step visual reasoning (evidence from landmarks, text/signage, cultural cues, spatial context) with JSON output format including predicted address, lat/lon, and confidence.
metric: city accuracy, country/state accuracy, mean/median great-circle distance (km)
notes: Zero-shot OOD benchmark. Geo-R1 achieves SOTA among open-source models on both GSS and UPC subsets.

name: RSTeller-NAIP
num_samples: 490 NAIP aerial images from US Agricultural Land (RSTeller subset)
format: High-resolution US NAIP aerial imagery (4-band, 448x448 at 0.6m ground sample distance) evenly distributed across the United States. Used for aerial image geolocation OOD evaluation.
access: Ge et al., 2025 — ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
notes: RSTeller: Scaling up visual language modeling in remote sensing with rich linguistic semantics.

name: CLEVR
format: Synthetic 3D-rendered scenes with ground-truth object attributes (color, shape, material, size, position); each image paired with compositional language questions about object relationships and attributes
notes: CLEVR (Johnson et al., 2017): diagnostic dataset for compositional language and elementary visual reasoning. TextCAM paper uses a small balanced subset (400 images) over red/blue x cube/ball combinations to test concept alignment under controlled attribute shifts.

name: ProteinShake-GO
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model size
format: Protein structures (PDB format) with Gene Ontology molecular function annotations. Multi-label classification task. Evaluated by Fmax metric.
license: Research use (underlying data from PDB, UniProt, GO)
notes: Used in BIOBLOBS (arXiv:2510.01632) for protein function prediction. Structure split uses 0.7 similarity threshold to reduce leakage.

name: ProteinShake-EC
format: Protein structures with Enzyme Commission top-level class labels. Multi-class classification (oxidoreductases, transferases, hydrolases, lyases, isomerases, ligases).
notes: Used in BIOBLOBS (arXiv:2510.01632). EC dataset evaluates structural understanding of enzyme catalytic mechanisms.

name: ProteinShake-SCOP-FA
format: Protein structures with SCOP (Structural Classification of Proteins) family-level annotations. Multi-class classification of protein folds.
notes: Used in BIOBLOBS (arXiv:2510.01632) for fold-level protein structure classification.

name: Mind2Web
num_samples: 2,000+ open-ended tasks, 137 websites across 31 domains; 1,009 training instances; test splits: Cross Task (252), Cross Website (177), Cross Domain (912)
storage: Not publicly disclosed; HTML content + action traces stored as JSON (~10-50GB estimated)
eval_time: Hours for full evaluation across all splits
format: Natural language instructions paired with website HTML snapshots, actions (CLICK/TYPE/SELECT), and candidate elements. Tasks require multi-step web navigation.
metric: Operation F1 (Op.F1), Element Accuracy (Ele.Acc), Step Success Rate (SR)
notes: First dataset for generalist web agents following language instructions on any website. Used in cross-platform generalization evaluation in PAL-UI paper.

name: TAU (Taiwan Audio Understanding)
storage: ~400MB (702 compressed audio clips, median 9.43s each, max 30s)
eval_time: minutes to hours (depends on model and hardware)
format: 4-option multiple-choice questions about Taiwanese soundmarks; audio clips with MCQ items; questions designed to be unanswerable from transcripts alone
license: Not publicly released at paper submission; contact authors for access
access: Contact authors (National Taiwan University); promised open release
notes: Cultural audio understanding benchmark for Taiwanese soundmarks. Introduces localized non-semantic audio evaluation for LALMs. 10 culturally distinctive categories. Human topline: 84% single-hop / 83.3% multi-hop. Best model (Gemini 2.5 Pro): 72.4% / 73.9%. All models far below human. From Lin et al. (arXiv:2509.26329).

name: RAGTruth
storage: ~500MB-2GB (source docs + model outputs + hallucination span annotations)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model size
format: Source documents, model-generated responses, human-annotated hallucination spans with start/end positions; 3 tasks: summarization, QA, data-to-text

name: Wikitext-2
format: Word-level language modeling benchmark from Wikipedia articles (PTB preprocessing). Train/valid/test splits. Smaller than Wikitext-103 for faster experiments.

name: EleutherAI LM Harness
format: Unified evaluation framework for language models across multiple benchmarks: BoolQ, RTE, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, OpenbookQA, and others. Provides standardized prompting and evaluation protocol.

name: MMRL30k
format: Multimodal math reasoning training dataset with image-question-answer pairs for RLVR fine-tuning of VLMs. Used to train DUPL, GRPO, and other multimodal RLVR methods.
access: From Zhu et al., 2025a (MMRL paper); likely available via project repository
notes: Training dataset for multimodal RLVR. From Zhu et al. (2025a). Used as training data in DUPL paper (arXiv:2510.01444). Approximately 30K samples.

name: TRIDENT
num_samples: 2,652 harmful prompts across finance, law, and medicine domains
format: Harmful prompts testing adherence to professional ethics (AMA medical code, ABA legal code, finance ethics); evaluated using harmfulness scores (1-5 scale)
metric: harmfulness score (lower is better), safety score (%)
access: https://github.com/{} or paper Hui et al. 2025
notes: From paper 'TRIDENT: Towards Robust Safety Alignment in LLMs' (Hui et al., 2025). Grounded in professional codes of conduct. Used in INVTHINK paper (2510.01569) for evaluating safety in high-stakes professional domains.

name: ReD Bench
format: Images with region-level drag instructions: source region masks paired with target centroid points. Includes point-to-region alignment, task tags (relocation, deformation, rotation), and contextual descriptions/intent prompts
metric: MD (mean distance), IF (image fidelity via LPIPS)
notes: Region-based Dragging Benchmark introduced by DragFlow (arXiv:2510.02253). Designed for evaluating region-level drag editing methods with explicit task categories and intent prompts. Complements DragBench-DR for point-based evaluation.

name: mArenaHard v2.0
eval_time: hours (for full pairwise evaluation with LLM judge)
format: Challenging user queries from Chatbot Arena, machine-translated into 23 languages. Win-rate measured via LLM judge (GPT-4o) comparing to Gemini2.5-Pro/Flash baselines.
metric: Win-rate (%) against commercial baselines, length-controlled win rate
notes: Used in FusioN paper (2510.00931) for multilingual open-ended generation evaluation. Subset of 11 languages used: en, de, fr, es, ru, ja, zh, ar, ko, pt, it.

name: WMT24++
num_samples: Source prompts from WMT 2024 shared task, expanded to 55 languages/dialects
format: Machine translation prompts (English to 10 target languages used in FusioN paper: ar, de, es, fr, it, ja, ko, pt, ru, zh). Quality measured by XComet-XL.
notes: Expanded version of WMT24 covering 55 languages. FusioN paper evaluates en-to-X translation on 10 language pairs using XComet-XL as the metric.

name: GeoFactX
num_samples: Geography-based factual reasoning prompts (train + test splits, 5 languages: en, hi, ja, sw, th)
format: Geography factual QA with human-verified answers. Includes reasoning trace quality scoring via LLM judge (GPT-4o) and answer correctness evaluation.
access: Shared by authors per FusioN paper acknowledgments
notes: Used in FusioN paper (2510.00931) for multilingual factual reasoning evaluation. FusioN consistently outperforms BoN on 4/5 languages. Languages not officially supported by fusor (Command A) still show FusioN benefits.

name: FAKEPEDIA
storage: ~1-2GB (long contexts averaging ~704 tokens single / ~1409 tokens dual)
eval_time: hours (Feature Ablation is slow on long contexts)
format: Encyclopedic single-hop QA with templated facts spanning 45 Wikidata-style relations. Each instance contains a question, a conflicting context (counterfactual), and optionally an irrelevant context. Used to test whether models prefer parametric memory or provided context.
notes: From Monea et al. (2024) ACL. The paper reconstructs instances across Conflicting, Irrelevant, Double-Conflicting, and Mixed setups for HE evaluation.

name: WORLDCAPITAL
storage: ~100MB (short contexts averaging ~38 tokens single / ~76 tokens dual)
format: Purely geographical questions under single relation (capital-of). Each instance contains a question, a made-up conflicting capital context, and optionally an irrelevant context from another country.
notes: From Yu et al. (2023) EMNLP. Used for studying parametric vs contextual knowledge in LMs.

name: CONFLICTQA
storage: ~500MB-1GB (long contexts averaging ~593 tokens single / ~1190 tokens dual)
format: Multi-domain QA across 7 relations (e.g., occupation, genre, founded-year). Contains contradictory context passages and noise context passages to test knowledge conflicts in LMs.
notes: From Xie et al. (2024) ICLR. Used for evaluating LLM behavior under knowledge conflicts.

name: EvalPlus
format: Rigorous code generation evaluation with 80x more test cases than original HumanEval (HumanEval+) and 35x more for MBPP (MBPP+); pass@1 for correctness plus efficiency evaluation
notes: Rigorous evaluation framework for LLM4Code. Augments HumanEval and MBPP with significantly more comprehensive test suites for more reliable pass rate measurement.

name: Omni-MATH
format: Competition-level mathematical olympiad problems with reference solutions; diverse difficulty levels from AMC to IMO
notes: Large-scale mathematical olympiad benchmark covering a wide range of competition math difficulty levels. Used in self-evolving LLM papers for evaluating mathematical reasoning.

name: Q-BioLip
format: Quaternary structure-based protein-ligand interaction database. Provides 3D structures of protein-ligand complexes with binding annotations. Used in NS-PEP (2510.03326) for peptide-protein complex data.

name: PepBDB
format: Comprehensive structural database of biological peptide-protein interactions. Provides 3D structures of peptide-protein complexes. Used in NS-PEP (2510.03326) combined with Q-BioLip for peptide design training data.

name: Q-Bench
format: Image-quality QA pairs (Yes-or-No, What, How question types) covering distortion types and low-level visual concerns. Evaluation via VLM-as-judge using VLMEvalKit.
notes: Benchmark for general-purpose foundation models on low-level vision. Introduced by Wu et al. (arXiv:2309.14181). Designed for explainable IQA — models must provide quality descriptions and answers.

name: AesBench
num_samples: VAL set with aesthetic quality assessment pairs
format: Image aesthetic QA pairs with AESA (aesthetic score), AESE (aesthetic explanation), AESP (aesthetic preference) metrics. Evaluation via VLMEvalKit.
notes: Benchmark for image aesthetics perception evaluation of MLLMs. From Huang et al. (ACM MM 2024). AESExpert model uses this for training data.

name: Q-Instruct
storage: ~200-500GB (image QA pairs with quality-related questions and answers)
format: Instruction-following pairs: (image, question about quality, answer with distortion/quality explanation). Covers blur, noise, color artifacts, and other low-level distortions.
notes: Large-scale instruction-tuning dataset for low-level visual perception. From Wu et al. (CVPR 2024). Used by IQA-Select (arXiv:2510.03880) as the primary training dataset.

name: AesExpert
format: Multi-typed instruction pairs for image aesthetics: composition, color, lighting, clarity. Instruction-following format with aesthetic descriptions aligned to human ratings.
notes: Multi-modality foundation model dataset for image aesthetics perception. From Huang et al. (ACM MM 2024). IQA-Select (arXiv:2510.03880) uses this as secondary training dataset.

name: CONTRAPROST
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed; benchmark covers ~7 prosodic phenomena pairs (contrastive emphasis, focus, etc.) in English-to-DE and English-to-ES
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on number of language pairs evaluated
format: Paired utterances differing only in prosodic emphasis (same transcript, different acoustic realization); requires distinct translations

name: Europarl-ST
num_samples: ~427 hours, 412k utterances across 8 European languages (DE, ES, FR, IT, NL, PL, PT, RO)
format: Speech utterances from European Parliament sessions aligned with translations in multiple languages

name: OMol25
num_samples: 100M+ DFT calculations (Neutral split ~34M charge-neutral singlet structures)
format: 3D molecular structures with DFT energies and forces at wB97M-V/def2-TZVPD level of theory; supports up to 350 atoms, 83 elements
notes: Open Molecules 2025 dataset from Meta FAIR. Comprehensive molecular dataset for structure-to-energy-and-forces (S2EF) prediction. Includes small molecules, biomolecules, metal complexes, electrolytes with varied charges, spin states, conformers.

name: Pile-10K
format: 10,000 prompt subset of The Pile dataset for evaluating language model representations; includes diverse text sources (ArXiv, Pile-CC, etc.)
metric: n/a (used for probing analyses, not benchmark evaluation)
notes: Introduced by Neel Nanda (2022). Used in this paper for cumulant analysis experiments.

name: DM Mathematics
num_samples: ~99 prompts used in paper (from a larger DeepMind math dataset)
format: Mathematical prompts from DeepMind mathematics dataset; used for comparing cumulant profiles between mathematical and general text processing in LLMs
access: DeepMind mathematics dataset (deepmind-mathematics), available on HuggingFace
notes: Subset of the DeepMind mathematics dataset. In this paper, 99 math prompts are used vs 570 Pile-CC prompts for comparing mathematical vs general text processing.

name: Piqa
format: Binary-choice physical commonsense QA: select the goal that makes physical sense given a context. Tests understanding of physical properties and everyday physical reasoning.
notes: Physical commonsense QA dataset (Bisk et al., 2020). Available via HuggingFace.

name: FATE (Formal Algebra Theorem Evaluation)
num_samples: ~200-300 total (FATE-H: ~50 final exam problems; FATE-X: ~50 PhD/research-level problems)
eval_time: hours depending on sample budget and method
format: Natural language algebraic mathematics problems (final exams and PhD qualifying exams) for auto-formalization to Lean 4; FATE-H contains undergraduate final exam problems, FATE-X contains PhD qualifying exam and research literature problems
metric: compiler success rate (passes Lean compilation); final accuracy (passes both compilation and semantic correctness check)
notes: Introduced by Jiang et al. (2025). FATE-H = formalization accuracy on final exam problems; FATE-X = formalization accuracy on PhD qualifying exam and research literature problems. Aria paper (2510.04520) adds Homological Conjectures dataset of 14 real-world mathematical conjectures.

name: ETH/UCY
num_samples: 5 scenes (ETH, HOTEL, UNIV, ZARA1, ZARA2), ~1536 pedestrians at 2.5Hz
format: 2D pedestrian trajectory coordinates (x, y) in world coordinates; scene segmentation masks for semantic context; standard train/test split via leave-one-scene-out protocol
metric: ADE (Average Displacement Error), FDE (Final Displacement Error)
notes: Standard trajectory prediction benchmark. Paper uses leave-one-scene-out evaluation (train on 4 scenes, test on held-out). Pedestrian trajectories from top-down view at 2.5Hz. SDD and ETH/UCY are the two primary benchmarks for momentary (2-frame) trajectory prediction.

name: SDD (Stanford Drone Dataset)
num_samples: 8 aerial scenes, multiple agent types (pedestrians, cyclists, vehicles)
format: Bird's-eye view RGB frames from drone; per-frame bounding box trajectories of agents; scene aerial images with semantic context; standard train/val/test splits
metric: ADE (Average Displacement Error), FDE (Final Displacement Error)
notes: Aerial drone dataset for trajectory prediction in campus environments. Higher pedestrian density and more complex interactions than ETH/UCY. Used as secondary benchmark for momentary trajectory prediction in Diffusion2 paper.

name: DyVal
num_samples: 900 (9 depth-width pairs × 100 questions each; depth and width each range from 2 to 4)
format: Synthetic math reasoning problems (linear equations) generated via tree-based DAGs; depth = number of reasoning steps, width = number of operations per node
notes: Dynamic evaluation benchmark for LLM reasoning (arXiv:2311.07260). The paper uses linear equation problems with controllable depth and width defined by the DAG structure.

name: DW2
num_samples: 2500 (500 keyword sets × 5 K values {4,8,12,16,20}; split into 5 entropy quintiles of 100 each)
format: Creative writing benchmark: write K coherent sentences using K keywords drawn from 23 O*NET occupation groups; depth = number of sentences K, width = normalized Shannon entropy of keyword domain distribution
metric: composite writing score (standard score × LLM-evaluated quality score)
access: Not released; must be recreated from paper description (keywords from O*NET 2019 taxonomy, 23 occupation groups)

name: Value Kaleidoscope (VK)
num_samples: 31K scenarios with 218K <scenario, perspective> pairs (174K train, 22K test)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model size
format: Hypothetical moral scenarios paired with ethical/moral perspectives. Each scenario has one or more perspectives. Task: determine if perspective 'supports', 'opposes', or 'neither supports nor opposes' the scenario.
notes: Used in arXiv:2510.04045 (Zhang et al., 2025) for steerable pluralistic alignment. Human-written CoT traces available for training.

name: MiniWoB++
format: Synthetic web UI tasks with DOM observations, accessibility tree, and high-level actions (click, fill, select, scroll, hover). Each task tests a specific UI interaction pattern.
notes: Used in JEF-Hinter paper (arXiv:2510.04373) for evaluating web agent robustness. Short-horizon precision tasks with simple HTML interfaces. Paper uses DOM directly (not AXTree) since it is small enough.

name: WorkArena-L1
format: Enterprise knowledge-work tasks on ServiceNow platform: multi-step form filling, navigation, filtering, sorting. Observations via accessibility tree (AXTree). Actions: click, fill, select, scroll.
notes: Used in JEF-Hinter paper (arXiv:2510.04373). Tests within-environment generalization across different goals. ServiceNow platform provides realistic enterprise software interface with complex navigation hierarchies.

name: GLOBAL-MMLU (medicine subset)
num_samples: ~420 samples per language (medicine subset, 0-shot accuracy evaluation)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Multilingual multiple-choice benchmark evaluating cultural and linguistic biases in medical domain. Medicine subset covers medical knowledge across 15+ languages. 4-choice MC format.
notes: Used in multilingual MoE routing paper (Bandarkar et al., arXiv:2510.04694) for evaluating cross-lingual transfer in math and medicine domains.

name: τ²-bench (tau-squared-bench)
num_samples: ~300+ tasks across 4 domains (mock, airline, retail, telecom)
format: Dual-control evaluation framework for conversational agents: agent interacts with simulated user (LM) and external tools/APIs. Tasks span mock scenarios, airline booking/management, retail customer support, and telecom services. Measures end-to-end task completion.

name: SOCIALHARMBENCH
num_samples: 585 prompts across 7 sociopolitical categories and 34 countries
format: Harmful sociopolitical prompts covering Censorship & Information Control, Human Rights Violations, Political Manipulation & Election Interference, Historical Revisionism, Propaganda & Disinformation, Surveillance & Monitoring, and War Crimes & Crimes Against Humanity. Includes standard, opinion elicitation, and historical reference prompt types.
metric: Attack Success Rate (ASR) via HarmBench and StrongREJECT classifiers
notes: Introduced in Pandey et al. (arXiv:2510.04891). First adversarial benchmark targeting sociopolitical vulnerabilities in LLMs. Evaluates models across temporal (centuries) and geographic (34 countries) dimensions. Uses dual-classifier evaluation: HarmBench (capability exposure) and StrongREJECT (alignment robustness).

name: BioHopR
format: Multi-hop multi-answer reasoning benchmark over PrimeKG knowledge graph; tasks require traversing 1 or 2 hops to find correct answers

name: Reuters
format: TF-IDF features on 2000 most frequent words across 4 root categories (CCAT, ECAT, GCAT, MCAT)
access: Preprocessed version from DEC paper (Xie et al., 2016)

name: RCV1-10
format: Text document subset with 10 categories from RCV1 corpus, TF-IDF features

name: LS-PCQA
num_samples: 104 reference + 24,024 distorted point clouds (33 distortion types at 7 severity levels); ~930 samples with psychometrically-collected true MOSs, rest are pseudo-MOSs
storage: ~200-500GB (point clouds with millions of points each)
format: 3D point clouds (with color attributes) + MOS quality scores; distortions include compression, noise, downsampling, etc.

name: SJTU-PCQA
num_samples: 9 reference + 378 distorted samples (7 distortion types at 6 severity levels)
format: 3D point clouds + MOS quality scores; distortions include projection-based impairments
license: Research use (Yang et al., IEEE TMM 2021)

name: WPC (Watermarked Point Cloud)
format: Colored 3D point clouds + MOS quality scores; distortions include noise, downsampling, compression, and watermarking-related impairments
license: Research use (Liu et al., IEEE TVCG 2022)

name: Wiki10-31K
num_samples: ~20K documents, 31K labels (10K frequent labels used, 8K supported + 2K novel actions)
format: Extreme classification dataset; documents with multi-label annotations, preprocessed with SBERT embeddings
metric: Policy value, safety violation rate, novelty (in the paper's custom evaluation)

name: APPFORGE
storage: ~10-15GB (F-Droid seed apps ~2-5GB + Android SDK/emulator ~5-10GB + task specs <100MB)
eval_time: ~5-15 min per app per model (compilation + APK install + test execution + fuzzing); full 12-model x 101-task evaluation takes ~1-2 weeks on single machine
format: Natural language app specification -> JSON of code files -> APK compilation -> Android emulator test execution + fuzzing. Four metrics: compilation rate, test pass rate, crash rate, functional success rate.
metric: Compilation Success Rate, Test Pass Rate (macro-avg), Crash Rate, Functional Success Rate (Pass@1)
license: Open-source (F-Droid apps with various OSS licenses)
access: https://app-forge.github.io (benchmark website); standalone Docker for out-of-box evaluation
notes: First benchmark for evaluating LLMs on full Android app development from scratch. Sourced from real-world F-Droid apps. Tasks range from beginner (single-activity) to advanced (multi-component, architectural complexity). Reveals fundamental limitations: best model (GPT-5-High) achieves only 18.8% functional success rate. Paper: arXiv:2510.07740

name: NormAd
format: Daily-life scenario MCQ: determine whether a behavior is acceptable in a specified culture. Requires understanding of cultural knowledge and values.

name: WorldValuesBench
num_samples: ~64 countries, 260 questionnaire items per participant from World Values Survey Wave 7
format: Predict participants' survey responses given demographic attributes. Uses Likert scale questionnaire items.

name: HDRNeRF
num_scenes: 8 forward-facing scenes with HDR images and per-image exposure values
format: Forward-facing captures with HDR RGB images, camera poses, and per-image exposure times for view synthesis with varying exposure

name: Eyeful Tower v2
num_scenes: Multiple room/apartment-scale scenes with HDR images
format: High-quality VR captures with HDR images enabling exposure simulation; scenes include offices and apartments for room-scale view synthesis

name: ToolAlpaca
num_samples: 3938 tool-use instances across 50 categories (103 test samples used in paper)
format: Synthetic tool-learning benchmark with function calling in JSON format. Tests tool selection and argument generation.
metric: Accuracy (exact match and soft-match for function name + arguments)
notes: Used in arXiv:2510.07841 (TT-SI paper) for evaluating test-time self-improvement on tool-use agents.

name: NexusRaven
format: Function-calling benchmark for single, nested, and parallel API calls across 65 APIs in cybersecurity/enterprise domain.
notes: Used in arXiv:2510.07841 (TT-SI paper) for evaluating test-time self-improvement on tool-use agents.

name: SealTool
format: Self-instruct tool learning benchmark. Tests precision in tool selection, output format adherence, and adaptability. Uses Alpaca-style instruction format.
metric: Accuracy (soft-match for function name + arguments, ignoring case/morphology)
notes: Used in arXiv:2510.07841 (TT-SI paper) as main benchmark. Includes official ~13k training split for SFT comparison.

name: API-Bank
num_samples: 314 multi-turn dialogues with 753 API calls (316 Level 1+2 test samples used)
format: Multi-turn user-agent dialogues requiring conversational state tracking and tool calls. Tests handling of noisy/incomplete inputs.
notes: Used in arXiv:2510.07841 (TT-SI paper) for evaluating test-time self-improvement on multi-turn tool-use agents.

name: SemanticPOSS
format: LiDAR point cloud sequences with per-point semantic labels for street scenes; collected in Chinese urban environments under diverse geographic and environmental conditions; used as target domain for cross-domain generalization in DGLSS-NL
metric: mIoU per class and mean IoU

name: AFRISPEECH-200
num_samples: ~200 hours of audio across 120 African accents (10 accents used in paper)
eval_time: minutes per model for WER evaluation
format: English speech from African accent speakers with transcripts; train/dev/test splits provided
notes: Pan-African accented English speech corpus. Used in arXiv:2510.08047 (Pseudo2Real) for ASR domain adaptation evaluation.

name: BIGCODEARENA
eval_time: 5 months for data collection; evaluation via API inference
format: Crowdsourced pairwise human preference on LLM-generated code with real-time sandbox execution. Covers 10 languages and 8 execution environments.
notes: Open human evaluation platform for code generation via execution. Built on Chatbot Arena + E2B sandbox. Allows users to execute LLM-generated code and judge quality based on execution results.

name: BIGCODEREWARD
format: Reward model evaluation benchmark for code generation. Tests alignment between reward models and human preferences on code quality judgments.
notes: Evaluates how well reward models judge code quality compared to human preferences. Part of BIGCODEARENA paper (arXiv:2510.08697).

name: AUTOCODEARENA
format: Automated LLM evaluation benchmark for code generation using LLM-as-a-Judge with execution feedback. 600 prompts sampled from BIGCODEARENA distribution.
notes: Automates BIGCODEARENA evaluation using LLM-as-a-Judge with execution results. Uses 600 representative prompts for efficient evaluation. From BIGCODEARENA paper (arXiv:2510.08697).

name: ETIS-LARIBPOLYPDB
num_samples: 196 colonoscopy images with polyp segmentation masks
format: High-resolution colonoscopy frames + binary polyp segmentation masks

name: OWOD Split
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed; uses PASCAL VOC 2007/2012 + MS COCO images with class splits into 4 incremental tasks
format: Object detection benchmark built on PASCAL VOC 2007/2012 + MS COCO; 80 object classes split across 4 non-overlapping incremental tasks; known classes increase per task while unknown classes represent future tasks
metric: mAP (known classes), U-R (unknown recall), HAcc (hierarchy accuracy for categorized unknowns)
access: Standard OWOD benchmark; contact authors or find splits in OW-DETR repository
notes: Open-World Object Detection benchmark split. Classes distributed relatively evenly across tasks. Used in BOUND paper (arXiv:2510.09173) and ORE, UC-OWOD, PROB papers.

name: OW-DETR Split
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed; uses PASCAL VOC 2007/2012 + MS COCO images with semantic class groupings into 4 incremental tasks
format: Object detection benchmark built on PASCAL VOC 2007/2012 + MS COCO; classes grouped by semantic similarity within tasks (e.g., all animals in Task 1); evaluated with U-R, mAP, HAcc
metric: mAP (known classes), U-R (unknown recall), HAcc (hierarchy accuracy)
access: Standard OWOD benchmark; contact authors or find splits in OW-DETR repository
notes: OWOD benchmark variant from OW-DETR paper (Gupta et al., CVPR 2022). Differs from standard OWOD Split by grouping semantically similar classes in same task. Used in BOUND paper (arXiv:2510.09173).

name: FACTAPPEAL
format: News sentences with span-level XML-style annotations: Fact_With_Appeal / Fact_Without_Appeal labels + source type (Expert, Witness, Official, Active Participant, Direct Evidence, Expert Document, News Report), named/unnamed modifier, direct/indirect quote, plus contextual attributes (Source Attribute, Recipient, Appeal Time, Appeal Location). 18 tag categories total.
notes: Novel task of Epistemic Appeal Identification: detecting whether factual statements are anchored by external sources/evidence. Introduced by Mor-Lan et al. (2025). Best model (Gemma 2 9B) achieves macro-F1=0.73 on the 18-tag span-level classification task.

name: GIR-Bench
eval_time: 1-2 hours for full evaluation on 21 models
format: Image generation and editing prompts with task-specific evaluation: DINOv3 similarity for UGC, object detection for T2I numerical/spatial, OCR for text rendering, FID for visual puzzles, IoU for editing tasks
metric: task-specific metrics (accuracy, similarity, FID, IoU) per sub-benchmark

name: MimicMe
num_samples: 5,000 distinct subjects, each with ~20 expressions captured via 3dMD face capture system (~60,000 vertices per scan)
format: 3D facial scans in PLY/OBJ format with per-vertex RGB and depth; metadata includes gender, age, ethnicity. ImHead paper filters to 4,000 clean identities for their curated dataset.
access: MimicMe (Papaioannou et al., ECCV 2022) - request access from authors
notes: MimicMe: A Large Scale Diverse 4D Database for Facial Expression Analysis (ECCV 2022). Used as the source dataset for imHead's curated 4K identity head dataset. The paper applies FLAME fitting + NPHM fitting + NICP registration to complete the full head and produce their final training data.

name: interPlan
format: Closed-loop planning benchmark with specially augmented out-of-distribution traffic scenarios requiring dense interaction; evaluates reactive mode with IDM-controlled neighboring vehicles
metric: Overall Score combining nudge around, high traffic density, and jaywalk scenario performance

name: ExpVid
format: Scientific experiment videos (JoVE) with MCQ and fill-in-the-blank QA pairs across 3 hierarchical levels
metric: Top-1 accuracy (MCQ), Jaccard similarity (sequence generation), Blank-level accuracy (fill-in-blank)

name: ConjectureBench
eval_time: hours to days depending on sample budget
format: Paired informal-formal Lean 4 mathematical problems designed to evaluate conjecturing capability. Problems rephrased to require numerical, algebraic, or true/false conjecture answers. Supports 'seen' (conjecture provided) and 'unseen' (conjecture must be inferred) settings.
metric: ConJudge (LLM-as-a-Judge for conjecture presence in autoformalization), equiv_rfl (Lean tactic rfl for standalone conjecture equivalence), Typecheck, BEq+, LLM Grader

name: SciSafeEval
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Harmful medical/biosecurity prompts covering drug interactions, dosage calculation, side-effect identification, and contraindication analysis. Paper used LLM-as-Judge to filter for highest harmfulness levels.
notes: Safety evaluation benchmark for LLM alignment in scientific tasks. Medicine subset used in Deep Research security analysis (arXiv:2510.11851) to evaluate biosecurity risks of DR agents. Original benchmark has broader coverage across scientific domains.

name: DeepBlending
num_samples: 3 real-world indoor scenes with free-viewpoint RGB images
format: Posed RGB images for free-viewpoint synthesis in indoor scenes
notes: From Hedman et al. 2018. Used for free-viewpoint image-based rendering. Scenes: realistic indoor environments with complex geometry and textures.

name: Python-by-Contract
format: Python solutions for introductory programming tasks with annotated functional contracts (preconditions/postconditions)
metric: bug detection rate, false alarm rate
notes: Python-by-Contract dataset (Zhang et al., FSE 2022). Collects Python solutions for 55 tasks from Advent of Code 2020 and ETH Zurich introductory programming course. Each solution has manually annotated reference contracts. Contains 59 buggy solutions. Used in NL2Contract paper (arXiv:2510.12702) to evaluate LLM-generated contracts for real bug detection.

name: Air-to-Pred-Occ
num_samples: 200 scenes (170 train + 30 val), 4 UAVs, ~32k synchronized images
format: CARLA-based virtual dataset with 4 UAVs at 50m altitude monitoring 100m x 100m intersection; 1600x900 RGB images; 3D occupancy annotations at 0.4m voxel resolution; 7 semantic classes: free, others, ground, building, vegetation, vehicle, road
access: Available upon request from Air-Co-Pred authors; custom occupancy annotations generated using CARLA mesh export + 3D point cloud annotation tool
notes: Extended from Air-Co-Pred (Wang et al., 2024) with 3D occupancy annotations. Used as one of three evaluation datasets in MCOP (arXiv:2510.12679). No direct public download — need to obtain Air-Co-Pred and regenerate occupancy labels.

name: UAV3D-Occ
num_samples: 1000 scenes (700 train + 150 val + 150 test), 5 UAVs, ~700k synchronized images estimated
format: CARLA + AirSim synthetic dataset with 5 UAVs at 60m altitude covering urban/suburban environments, 112x112m range; 800x450 RGB images; 3D occupancy annotations at 0.4m voxel resolution; 7 semantic classes: free, others, ground, building, vegetation, vehicle, road
access: Available upon request from UAV3D authors; custom occupancy annotations generated using CARLA mesh export + ray-casting
notes: Extended from UAV3D (Ye et al., NeurIPS 2024) with 3D occupancy annotations. Used in MCOP (arXiv:2510.12679). No direct public download — need to obtain UAV3D and regenerate occupancy labels.

name: GauUScene-Occ
num_samples: ~0.908 km2 area with 4 UAV trajectories, high-resolution RGB images at 5472x3648
format: Real-world drone dataset (subset 'Russian Building' from GauUScene v2) with 4 UAV trajectories at up to 150m altitude; 5472x3648 RGB images with camera poses and point clouds; 3D occupancy annotations at 2m voxel resolution (coarser due to large scale); 7 semantic classes: free, others, ground, building, vegetation, vehicle, road
license: Research use (derived from GauUScene v2, Xiong et al., 2024)
access: Available upon request from GauUScene authors; custom occupancy annotations generated using Occ3D methodology (mesh reconstruction + semantic labels + ray-casting)
notes: Extended from GauUScene v2 (Xiong et al., 2024) with 3D occupancy annotations. Real-world evaluation dataset in MCOP (arXiv:2510.12679). GauUScene v2 available at https://github.com/nbxxx/GauU-Scene; occupancy annotations require significant additional effort.

name: CGBENCH
num_samples: 783 total eval samples (VCI E-Score: 205, VCI E-Ver: 242, GCI: 336)
eval_time: 1-2 hours for full evaluation across 8 models
format: JSON with query/paper text/VCEP guidelines/SOP specifications; outputs require structured extraction (evidence codes, met/not met, evidence tuples)
metric: Precision@5, Recall@5, F1, Normalized MAE, ΔStrength, Structure Adherence
notes: Evaluates LLMs on clinical genetics literature interpretation: VCI Evidence Scoring (assigning ACMG/AMP evidence codes), VCI Evidence Verification (determining if evidence criteria are met), GCI Experimental Evidence Extraction (extracting structured evidence from papers). Built from ClinGen Evidence Repository. Benchmark reveals frontier models still struggle with fine-grained evidence interpretation.

name: VMCBench
eval_time: hours per model for full evaluation
format: Unified multiple-choice VQA benchmark composed of 20 diverse datasets covering general VQA, reasoning, document/chart understanding, and OCR tasks. Each subset has multiple-choice answers.
notes: Introduced in Zhang et al. (2025) CVPR. Stanford HAI benchmark for evaluating VLMs on diverse visual question answering tasks. Used in CLIP vs DINO controlled study paper (arXiv:2510.11835) as the primary VLM evaluation benchmark.

name: DataComp
num_samples: 12.8M images (full); various subset sizes used (1M, 10M, 128M, etc.)
storage: ~100GB for 10M subset; varies by subset size
format: Image-caption pairs from Common Crawl with associated captions. Standardized dataset for controlled experiments in vision-language pretraining. Multiple scales: DataComp-1M, DataComp-10M, DataComp-128M, DataComp-400M+.
notes: Introduced in Gadre et al. (2023) NeurIPS. Used in the controlled CLIP vs DINO study (arXiv:2510.11835) with a 10M-image subset to isolate the effect of language supervision vs self-supervision on vision encoder quality.

name: OVEN (Open-domain Visual Entity Recognition)
num_samples: 6,063,945 training samples; 15,888 test entities (8,355 seen, 7,533 unseen)
storage: OVEN combines 14 source datasets (ImageNet21k-P, iNaturalist2017, Cars196, SUN397, Food101, Sports100, Aircraft, Oxford Flower, Google Landmarks v2, VQA v2, Visual7W, Visual Genome, OK-VQA, Text-VQA). Estimated hundreds of GB to 1TB+ for full image data.
eval_time: hours for full evaluation on entity split
format: Given an image and text query, predict the Wikidata QID of the depicted entity. Entity split: from image recognition datasets. Query split: from VQA datasets.
metric: Top-1 accuracy (seen entities), Top-1 accuracy (unseen entities), Harmonic mean (HM)
license: OVEN: research use (Hu et al., ICCV 2023). Source datasets have varying licenses.
notes: Open-domain visual entity recognition benchmark linking images to Wikidata QIDs. Introduced by Hu et al. (2023). KnowCoL (this paper) achieves HM=38.8% vs prior best Auto-VER-14B at HM=28.9%.

name: ASearcher
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed; training dataset for search agent RL
storage: Not publicly disclosed; estimated similar scale to HotpotQA training set
format: High-quality QA instances for training search agents with long-horizon reasoning; synthesized via prompt-based LLM agent
notes: Beyond ten turns: Unlocking long-horizon agentic search with large-scale asynchronous RL (Gao et al., arXiv:2508.07976). Used as RL training data in MemAct paper (2510.12635).

name: Cambridge Landmarks
num_samples: 5 scenes (GreatCourt, KingsCollege, OldHospital, ShopFacade, StMarysChurch), hundreds to thousands of images per scene
eval_time: minutes to hours per scene for localization evaluation
format: Outdoor images with ground-truth camera poses (6-DoF) from SfM; images are街道-level photos of Cambridge historic buildings
metric: median translation error (cm), median rotation error (degrees)
notes: Introduced by Kendall et al. (2015) PoseNet. Standard benchmark for visual camera relocalization. Used extensively for Scene Coordinate Regression (SCR) methods including ACE, DSAC*, and MACE. Ground-truth poses reconstructed via SfM.

name: IntentionBench
num_samples: 138,803 data points across 350 mixed sessions (~77 hours of mixed on/off-task activity)
storage: ~50-100GB (compressed JPEG screenshots at quality=85, 2s intervals, from 50 task instructions across 14 applications and 32 websites)
format: Screen capture (JPEG) + app metadata + URL + user intention + clarification Q&A + distraction score + on/off-task label. Each data point = one screenshot every 2 seconds with associated context.
metric: accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score (distraction detection at 0.5 threshold)
license: Will be publicly released by authors
access: https://intentassistant.github.io (code); IntentionBench to be released publicly
notes: Novel dataset introduced in INA paper (CHI 2026). Synthesized from 50 focused sessions (authors executing task instructions without distraction) mixed into 350 sessions with natural transition points. Intention from one session paired with activity from another to create realistic on/off-task transitions. Used to evaluate INA distraction detection: accuracy=0.878, F1=0.845 with full system (clarification+feedback).

name: OPENESTIMATE
eval_time: 1-4 hours for full evaluation across 6 models on 178 variables (parallelizable)
format: Structured natural language prompts asking LLM to specify Gaussian (N(mu, sigma^2)) or Beta (alpha, beta) distribution parameters as Bayesian priors; evaluated for accuracy (MAE, error ratio, win rate) and calibration (ECE)
metric: MAE, Error Ratio, Win Rate vs statistical baseline, Expected Calibration Error (ECE), posterior win rate
access: https://github.com/mit000/OpenEstimate (inferred; paper states 'we release our code, benchmark dataset, and evaluation framework')
notes: Introduced in Renda et al. (2026). Benchmark for evaluating LLMs on probabilistic estimation under uncertainty using real-world tabular data. Variables are derived from Glassdoor (labor economics), PitchBook (finance), and NHANES (public health) to avoid information leakage from training data. Key finding: LLM-elicited priors are often inaccurate and overconfident, performing roughly on par with 5 samples from the true distribution.

name: NHANES (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey)
num_samples: Thousands of individuals per survey cycle (cross-sectional, ~5000-10000 participants per 2-year cycle)
format: Tabular data: demographic, dietary, examination, laboratory, and questionnaire data on US individuals. Variables include health measurements, blood tests, BMI, etc.
notes: CDC National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Used in OPENESTIMATE (Renda et al., 2026) to construct health-domain estimation variables (74 variables). Publicly available government dataset.

name: PitchBook (Private Market Data)
num_samples: Millions of private company records (venture capital, private equity, M&A)
format: Tabular data on private companies: funding rounds, valuations, deal sizes, sector, geography, employee counts, etc.
access: https://wrds-www.wharton.upenn.edu/ (Wharton Research Data Services); individual access via PitchBook subscription
notes: PitchBook Data (2024). Used in OPENESTIMATE (Renda et al., 2026) to construct finance-domain estimation variables (61 variables). REQUIRES PAID INSTITUTIONAL SUBSCRIPTION - major access barrier for reproducibility.

name: Glassdoor (Labor Market Data)
num_samples: Millions of job postings and salary reports
format: Tabular data on job postings: salaries, job titles, company info, location, employee reviews, benefits, etc.
access: Glassdoor.com (typically requires institutional subscription for bulk data access)
notes: Used in OPENESTIMATE (Renda et al., 2026) to construct labor economics-domain estimation variables (43 variables). Access typically requires institutional subscription; not publicly freely available in bulk.

name: WebAggregatorQA
num_samples: ~10K training tasks (200 reserved for human-annotated test set)
format: Multi-step web research QA pairs requiring information aggregation (not just retrieval); spans 12 domains, diverse tools (search, visit, file read, screenshot), and aggregation operations (element, set, temporal, scientific analysis)

name: WebWalkerQA
format: Web traversal benchmark requiring LLM agents to navigate websites and find specific information

name: XBench
format: Agent productivity benchmark with profession-aligned real-world evaluations

name: LOCOMO
format: Long-term conversational memory benchmark with multi-hop, temporal, and open-domain questions; LLM-as-a-Judge accuracy

name: AggQA
format: Memory benchmark for data analysis tasks with tabular data discretely embedded in ~56K-token dialogues; requires numerical reconstruction and aggregation; evaluated via LLM-as-a-Judge accuracy

name: BizFinBench
format: Business-driven real-world financial benchmark for evaluating LLMs; source data for AggQA financial domain questions

name: Hist-AI Colorectal Dataset
num_samples: 77,182 annotated patches from 1,719 WSIs, 13 morphological classes
format: H&E-stained colorectal histology patches with expert annotations for 13 tissue morphology classes: High-Grade Adenocarcinoma, Low-Grade Adenocarcinoma, High-Grade Adenoma, Low-Grade Adenoma, Fat, Hyperplastic Polyp, Inflammation, Mucin, Smooth Muscle, Necrosis, Sessile Serrated Lesion, Stroma, and Vascular Structures
notes: Publicly available dataset for training morphology classifiers in colorectal cancer computational pathology. Used in PRISM paper (arXiv:2510.14800) to train morphology-informed feature extractor.

name: Alliance Cohort (CALGB 89803)
format: H&E-stained whole slide images from stage III CRC patients with 5-year survival labels. Treatment: 5FU/LV vs CPT-11/5FU/LV adjuvant chemotherapy. Scanned at 40x (0.25 um/pixel) using Aperio Digital Pathology Scanner.
metric: AUC, Accuracy, Sensitivity, Specificity, C-index, Hazard Ratio (5-year overall survival)
license: Restricted - requires research agreement with Alliance for Clinical Trials in Oncology
access: Data obtained directly from Alliance for Clinical Trials in Oncology (NCT00003835)
notes: Clinical trial CALGB 89803 comparing adjuvant IFL vs FL alone in stage III colon cancer. Used in PRISM paper (arXiv:2510.14800) as primary training/evaluation dataset. IRB approval: Ohio State University IRB #2018C0098.

name: MARIS (Marine Open-Vocabulary Instance Segmentation)
num_samples: ~16K underwater images (5,712 train + 10,439 val), 158 fine-grained categories across 9 super-classes
format: Underwater images with pixel-accurate instance-level masks. Categories include marine organisms (fish, coral, invertebrates), artificial objects, and substrates.
metric: mAP, AP50, AP75 for instance segmentation; evaluated on Intersection (seen), Open-Vocabulary (unseen), and Overall classes
notes: First large-scale fine-grained benchmark for underwater open-vocabulary instance segmentation (UOVIS). Supports both in-domain (train on MARIS) and cross-domain (train on COCO) evaluation settings. Addresses color attenuation, semantic misalignment challenges in underwater scenes.

name: SVA-Eval-Human
num_samples: 38 real hardware debugging challenges with human-verified ground truth fixes
format: RTL code (SystemVerilog/Verilog) + counter-example traces + failing properties (SVAs) + human-verified ground truth fixes
metric: Quality@Best, NDCG@5, MRR, Kendall's tau (hypothesis quality); Pass@1, Pass@5 (fix generation)
access: Not publicly released; obtained from authors of DAC 2025 paper (arXiv reference [36])
notes: Curated collection of 38 real hardware debugging challenges from diverse designs (arithmetic units to complex system-level modules). Each includes counter-example trace, buggy RTL code, and ground truth fix verified by human experts. Used in FVDebug paper (2510.15906) as primary evaluation benchmark.

name: CVA6 RISC-V Processor
num_samples: 2 FV failure cases (MMU ghost response, LSU transaction ID mismatch)
format: RTL code (SystemVerilog) for CVA6 RISC-V processor; FV counter-examples from AutoSVA project
metric: Hypothesis quality metrics (Quality@Best, NDCG@5, MRR, Kendall's tau)
notes: Production-grade RISC-V processor design used in FVDebug paper (2510.15906) for evaluating on complex processor failures. MMU case: 3 RTL files, 695 LOC, 172 graph nodes, 76 signals. LSU case: 7 RTL files, 1918 LOC, 170 graph nodes, 122 signals.

name: CircuitNet
format: chip layout images (Macro Region, RUDY, RUDY Pin) + text config/log features
metric: SSIM, NRMSE, PeakNRMSE, PLCC, SRCC, KRCC (for congestion prediction)

name: NSD (Natural Scenes Dataset)
num_samples: 30,000+ trials across 4 subjects (8,859 training + 982 test images per subject)
format: Preprocessed 3D fMRI voxel patterns (BOLD responses) paired with COCO images viewed by subjects
metric: PixCorr, SSIM, LPIPS, CLIP, Inception V3 (for image reconstruction)

name: BOLD5000
format: 3D fMRI voxel patterns paired with images from COCO and ImageNet
metric: PixCorr, SSIM, LPIPS, CLIP, Inception V3

name: GOD (Generic Object Decoding)
format: 3D fMRI voxel patterns paired with images from 200 ImageNet categories
metric: PixCorr, SSIM, LPIPS, CLIP, Inception V3

name: Math500
format: Competition math problems (MATH benchmark subset, difficulty levels 1-5) with LaTeX-formatted problem statements and final answers
access: likely available on HuggingFace (tau/math500 or from MATH dataset)
notes: 500-problem subset of the MATH dataset (Hendrycks et al., 2021). Used in GRPO analysis paper (2510.15990) for benchmarking LLM math reasoning; Qwen2.5-7B showed +31.2% gain after GRPO.

name: PharmDB
format: Drug-disease association pairs for drug repurposing; multi-hop reasoning paths over knowledge graph
notes: K-paths reasoning benchmark for drug repurposing (Abdullahi et al., 2025). Used in GRPO analysis paper (2510.15990) for benchmarking clinical-domain OOD generalization; Llama-3.1-8B showed +16.7% gain on PharmDB vs only +1.4% on Math500.

name: GenPoster-100K
format: High-fidelity poster images with layer-parseable element annotations. Each poster has structured metadata including element types, bounding boxes, underlay/overlay relationships, and background images.
metric: Overlay, Alignment, Underlay effectiveness, Content metrics, Aesthetic scores

name: CodeTransOcean
num_samples: ~6000+ code snippets across 6 languages, 30 translation pairs
eval_time: hours to days for full evaluation across all language pairs
format: Source code snippets in C, C++, C#, Java, Go, Python with input-output test suites for functional verification
notes: Comprehensive multilingual benchmark for code translation. Used for many-shot ICL code translation experiments (arXiv:2510.16809).

name: Real3D-AD
num_samples: 12 categories, 4 normal training samples per category, 100 test instances per category
format: 3D point clouds (PLY format) with normal/abnormal labels for industrial anomaly detection
notes: Real-world high-resolution 3D anomaly detection dataset. Training samples captured via full 360-degree scans; test samples from single-view perspectives. From Liu et al., NeurIPS 2023.

name: Anomaly-ShapeNet
num_samples: 1600 samples across 40 categories, 4 normal training samples per category
format: 3D point clouds (offline synthetic anomaly generation) for anomaly detection and localization
notes: Synthetic 3D anomaly detection benchmark. From Li et al., CVPR 2024. Enables scalable 3D anomaly detection via 3D anomaly synthesis and self-supervised learning.

name: OCRBench
format: Comprehensive OCR benchmark for VLMs testing text recognition, document understanding, and visual reasoning over embedded text in images; covers diverse document types and languages
notes: OCRBench from Liu et al. (2024b) — distinct from OCRBench v2 which focuses on table parsing. Used in VisionSelector (arXiv:2510.16598) for evaluating token compression methods.

name: Cambrian-737K
format: Large-scale vision-centric multimodal dataset with diverse images and captions designed for training VLMs; used for vision-language alignment in Cambrian-1 (Tong et al., 2024)
notes: Training dataset used in VisionSelector (arXiv:2510.16598). Subsets used: OCRVQA, ChartQA, and 10% COCO (~144K samples total for their training).

name: HonestyBench
storage: ~500GB-1TB (560k QA pairs with 21 responses each, annotated with correctness and self-consistency signals)
format: Free-form factual QA pairs with confidence scores (self-consistency-based) and correctness annotations; evaluates LLM honesty alignment via AUROC and ECE metrics
notes: Introduced by EliCal paper (arXiv:2510.17509). Consolidates 10 QA datasets (NQ, TQ, HQ, 2Wiki, ParaRel for training; SQuAD, WQ, CWQ, MuSiQue, PopQA for OOD eval). For each QA pair: 1 greedy + 20 sampled responses annotated with semantic consistency (via Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct) and correctness. Supports universal honesty alignment training and evaluation.

name: HIATUS HRS1
format: Query-candidate document pairs with cross-genre authorship attribution labels; foreground documents written specifically for HIATUS program across 5 genres

name: HIATUS HRS2
format: Medium-length document version of HIATUS cross-genre authorship attribution benchmark; same 5-genre cross-genre setting as HRS1 but with shorter documents (median ~200 words)

name: MultiON Challenge
num_samples: 100 episodes (minival) in 20 HSSD scenes, each episode has sequence of 3 target objects
format: Multi-object navigation tasks in photorealistic 3D environments (HSSD). Natural language instructions specifying target objects with spatial relationships (e.g., 'Find the red candle on the nightstand'). RGB-D observations (256x256), GPS+Compass sensor.
metric: Success Rate (SR), Progress (Pr), Success Rate per Attempted Target (SRAT), False Positive Rate (FP), Terminate-Not-Found Rate (TNF)
notes: CVPR 2024 challenge for multi-object navigation with spatial language. Winner: IntelliGO Labs. DIV-Nav (arXiv:2510.16518) evaluates on the minival split.

name: HSSD (Habitat Synthetic Scenes Dataset)
num_samples: ~30K diverse indoor 3D scenes from real-world homes
format: Photorealistic 3D indoor scenes (apartments, houses) with RGB-D panoramas, semantic annotations, and navigation graphs. Used as the environment substrate for MultiON benchmark and Habitat-Matterport 3D (HM3D) benchmarks.
access: https://github.com/Sh荡链接TianweiYue/HSSD or via Habitat ecosystem
notes: DIV-Nav (arXiv:2510.16518) evaluates navigation in HSSD scenes for the MultiON benchmark. Scenes are photorealistic and include diverse real-world object arrangements.

name: COCO-Stuff27
format: Images with pixel-level semantic segmentation annotations (172 classes: 80 thing + 92 stuff classes)
notes: Semantic segmentation benchmark derived from COCO 2017. Used in SSL dense representation learning papers (e.g., DINO, iBOT, MAE). COCO-Stuff27 refers to the version with 27 superclasses or the 2017 split.

name: LexChain_eval
format: Structured legal reasoning evaluation: 7 scoring dimensions (Plaintiff, Defendant, Dispute, Statute, Liability, Damages, Judgment). GPT-4o judges model responses against gold-standard answers.
notes: First dedicated benchmark for evaluating legal reasoning in Chinese civil tort law. Covers 45 distinct tort subcategories. Evaluation uses GPT-4o as judge. Paper: arXiv:2510.17602.

name: LexChain_train
num_samples: ~10,600 Chinese court decision documents for tort cases
format: LexChain-style reasoning chain data: structured legal reasoning chains with legal element identification, liability analysis, and judgment summarization. Generated using DeepSeek-V3 with human validation (consistency 0.973, coherence 0.993).
notes: Training dataset of ~10,600 court decisions enriched with LexChain-style reasoning chains. Used for SFT_LC and DPO_LC training. Paper: arXiv:2510.17602.

name: Law-Bench
num_samples: Not fully disclosed; covers multiple legal tasks including Legal NER and Criminal Damages Calculation
format: Multi-task legal AI benchmark evaluating LLM capabilities across various legal knowledge and reasoning tasks.
metric: Task-specific metrics (F1 for NER, accuracy for damages calculation, etc.)
notes: Referenced in LexChain paper (arXiv:2510.17602) for cross-task generalization evaluation. Paper: Fei et al., 2024, EMNLP.

name: PICABench
format: Image editing test cases with region-annotated QA pairs evaluating physical realism across 8 sub-dimensions (Optics, Mechanics, State Transition)
notes: ArXiv 2510.17681. Evaluates physical realism in image editing: light propagation, reflection, refraction, light-source effects, deformation, causality, global state transition, local state transition. Uses GPT-5 or Qwen2.5-VL-72B as VLM judge with per-case region-level human annotations.

name: PICA-100K
storage: ~50-100GB (regenerated on-the-fly using FLUX T2I + Wan I2V)
format: Synthetic image editing triplets: source image + instruction + edited image, derived from video frames (first/last frames as edit pairs)
notes: ArXiv 2510.17681. 105K synthetic editing samples generated using FLUX.1-Krea-dev (T2I) + Wan2.2-14B-I2V (I2V) + GPT-5 (instruction expansion). Covers 8 physics categories. Used to fine-tune FLUX.1-Kontext-dev and Qwen-Image-Edit for improved physical realism.

name: HT-Step
num_samples: 600 validation videos across 120 seen activities (5 videos per activity)
format: Instructional videos from HowTo100M aligned with WikiHow step descriptions; step-level temporal grounding annotations

name: Ego4D Goal-Step
format: Egocentric instructional videos with hierarchical annotations: goals break down into steps, steps into substeps; step-level temporal grounding

name: VMAS (Vectorized Multi-Agent Simulator)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on task complexity
format: Multi-agent 2D physics simulation with configurable tasks (Navigation, Balance, Buzz Wire, Transport)
notes: Open-source vectorized simulator for multi-agent RL research. Used in R2BC paper (2510.18085) for 4 cooperative tasks with 2-3 agents.

name: NeuCLIR24
num_samples: ~10M documents (Chinese ~3M, Russian ~5M, Persian ~2M, all translated to English) + complex user requests with annotated nuggets
format: Complex user requests (avg 51.95 ± 19.46 words) decomposed into sub-queries; document relevance judgments (binary) at nugget level; multilingual document corpus (translated to English)
notes: TREC 2025 NeuCLIR track. Used in arXiv:2510.18633 for evaluating bandit-based document selection in RAG query decomposition. User requests have discourse operators (exclusion, negation) requiring decomposition into sub-queries.

name: ResearchyQuestions
num_samples: 100k complex Bing questions (non-factoid, multi-perspective) with hierarchical decomposition into headers and sub-queries
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on corpus size
format: Complex user questions decomposed hierarchically over two levels: headers (first-level sub-queries) and sub-queries (second-level); document relevance labels at document level
notes: Introduced by Rosset et al. (2024). Used in arXiv:2510.18633 for evaluating hierarchical correlated bandits on query decomposition. Filtered to instances with >=10% relevant documents, yielding ~140 evaluation instances.

name: Auto-ARGUE
format: Framework for evaluating LLM-generated long-form reports on dimensions: citation relevance, citation support, nugget coverage, sentence support
metric: Citation Support, Nugget Coverage, Sentence Support, Citation Relevance
notes: Auto-ARGUE framework from Walden et al. (2025), arXiv:2509.26184. Used in arXiv:2510.18633 to evaluate downstream report generation quality when using bandit-selected documents for RAG.

name: WEBDEVJUDGE
num_samples: 654 instances (web development query + paired implementations + preference labels)
eval_time: 1-2 hours for full evaluation with API parallelism
format: Quadruple (Q, Wa, Wb, lp): web development query + two web implementations + annotated preference label. Supports static (code + screenshot) and interactive (agent navigation) evaluation.
metric: Agreement rate with human expert preferences (pairwise comparison)

name: WebDevJudge-Unit
format: Diagnostic dataset for feasibility verification: web code + verification task + expected result + feasibility label

name: webdev-arena-preference-10k
num_samples: 10501 user queries with paired code outputs + user preferences
