format: Raw web development queries with paired model outputs and user-provided preference labels; source data for WEBDEVJUDGE benchmark

name: MAPF benchmark (Stern et al. 2019)
num_samples: 25 random scenarios per map per agent count; maps include maze-128-128-10, room-64-64-8, warehouse-20-40-10-2-1, warehouse-20-40-10-2-2, den312d; agent counts from 10 to 10000
eval_time: seconds to minutes per instance (30s timeout in standard evaluation)
format: Grid-based maps (.map files) with scenario files (.scen) specifying start/goal positions per agent. Standard MAPF benchmark from Stern et al. 2019 (SoCS). Metrics: flowtime (sum-of-costs), runtime, success rate.
notes: Standard MAPF benchmark from the 'Multi-Agent Pathfinding: Definitions, Variants, and Benchmarks' paper (Stern et al. 2019). Used extensively in MAPF literature including LaCAM, PIBT, LNS2, and guidance-based papers.

name: PHOENIX-2014T
format: German Sign Language (DGS) weather forecast videos with parallel German text. Standard SLT benchmark.
access: https://www.phonetik.uni-muenchen.de/~f穿梭/Projects/SLR/Corpora/corpus.html (original); widely available via SLT papers
notes: Camgoz et al., 2018. Widely used sign language translation benchmark. Video resolution and signer setup compatible with SpaMo visual block.

name: CSL-Daily
format: Chinese Sign Language (CSL) corpus for daily communication with parallel Chinese text. Standard SLT benchmark.
notes: Zhou et al., 2021. High-resolution videos with moderate signer-camera distance; best suited for SpaMo global visual features.

name: AutumnBench
eval_time: 2-4 hours for core evaluation with API models
format: Grid-world POMDP environments defined in Autumn DSL; three task types: masked frame prediction, change detection, planning
metric: Binary accuracy (MFP, planning), penalized accuracy (change detection)

name: EcomEval
format: Question-answer pairs (multiple-choice and open-ended), multilingual (7 languages), multimodal tasks with images
metric: LLM-as-judge scoring (0-3 scale converted to 0-100 percentage)
notes: Shopee's multilingual and multimodal e-commerce benchmark for LLM evaluation. Covers 6 categories: Ecom QA, Shopping Concepts, User Understanding, Shopping Reasoning, Ecom Generation, Ecom Multimodal. 37 tasks including 8 multimodal. 7 languages: English, Chinese, Indonesian, Vietnamese, Thai, Malay, Portuguese. Difficulty-aware evaluation design with easy/medium/hard task levels.

name: Pov-ray Light Field
num_samples: 900 scenes (800 train / 100 test), 11x11 sub-aperture images per scene
format: Synthetic light field dataset with known camera geometry. Each scene has 121 sub-aperture images on a regular grid.
notes: Used to train iIBR (arXiv:2510.20132). Paper: Heber & Pock, CVPR 2016.

name: Stanford Light Field Archive
format: Real-world light field dataset captured with camera array. Known camera geometry.
notes: New Stanford Light Field Archive. Used for evaluation in iIBR paper (arXiv:2510.20132).

name: 4DLF (4D Light Field)
num_samples: Not fully disclosed, 9x9 sub-aperture images per scene
format: Synthetic 4D light field dataset with known camera geometry.
notes: Used for evaluation in iIBR paper (arXiv:2510.20132). Paper: Honauer et al., ACCV 2016.

name: NeRF LLFF
num_samples: 8 forward-facing scenes with unstructured multi-view images
format: Real-world forward-facing scenes captured with handheld camera. Dense views needed to construct light field.
notes: Local Light Field Fusion dataset. Used for evaluation (with ZipNeRF preprocessing) in iIBR paper (arXiv:2510.20132). Paper: Mildenhall et al., SIGGRAPH 2019.

name: CT-RATE
num_samples: 25,692 chest CT scans from 21,304 patients (~20k train, ~1,304 test)
eval_time: minutes to hours for full evaluation
format: 3D chest CT volumes with paired free-text radiology reports. Each CT resampled to 0.75x0.75x1.5mm and cropped/padded to 512x512x241. Reports include findings and impression sections.
metric: BLEU, METEOR, F1 (clinical accuracy), CRG, FID, FVD, CLIP score
license: Research use (CC BY 4.0 or similar, check source)
notes: Largest public 3D medical imaging dataset with paired image-text data. Used for both report generation and text-to-CT synthesis tasks. From Hamamci et al. (2024).

name: Rad-ChestCT
num_samples: Not fully disclosed; multi-label annotations on chest CT volumes
format: 3D chest CT volumes with binary multi-label findings annotations (no text reports). Used for out-of-distribution generalization testing.
notes: Draelos et al. (2021). Used as out-of-distribution validation in BTB3D paper. Only binary labels available, no text reports.

name: SMAC (StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge)
format: StarCraft II multi-agent RL environment with partial observability. Agents control units to defeat enemy units.

name: LBF (Level-Based Foraging)
num_samples: Grid-world with configurable agent/food counts (e.g., 3 agents + 3 food, 4 agents + 2 food)
format: Grid-based multi-agent cooperative environment where adjacent agents must pool their levels to collect food items

name: MTIL (Multimodal Task Incremental Learning)
num_samples: 11 diverse vision datasets (Aircraft, Caltech101, CIFAR100, DTD, EuroSAT, Flowers102, Food101, MNIST, OxfordPets, StanfordCars, SUN397)
format: Sequential 11-task learning benchmark for evaluating continual learning on CLIP. Metrics: Transfer (zero-shot on unseen tasks), Avg. (average accuracy during training), Last (final accuracy capturing forgetting).
metric: Transfer accuracy, Average accuracy, Last accuracy
access: From Zheng et al. (2023), arXiv:2308.12765. Individual datasets accessible via their original sources.
notes: Primary benchmark for NuSA-CL paper (Jo & Kim, arXiv:2510.21175). Tests ability to learn new tasks sequentially while preserving CLIP's zero-shot transfer capabilities.

name: Oxford Flowers 102
format: 102 flower categories with 10-258 images per class
notes: Oxford Flowers 102 (Nilsback & Zisserman, 2008). Used in MTIL benchmark for continual learning evaluation.

name: HO3D
storage: ~5-10GB (RGB videos of hand-object interactions with 3D hand/object annotations)
format: Monocular RGB video sequences of hand-object interactions with ground-truth 3D hand and object poses

name: OpenMathInstruction-2
num_samples: ~1M+ (full dataset; Lookahead paper used 12,189 train + 1,354 val samples)
format: Math word problems with verified solutions; generated via large-scale LLM self-instruction from GSM8K and MATH datasets
notes: OpenMathInstruct-2 dataset used for training data construction in Lookahead routing paper (arXiv:2510.19506). See Toshniwal et al., ICLR 2025.

name: Self-Oss-Instruct-SC2
num_samples: ~1.2M (full dataset; Lookahead paper used 3,335 train + 1,000 val samples)
format: Python programming tasks with unit tests; derived from The Stack v2 via Self-OSS-Instruct filtering and SC2 (Self-Consistency with Code Execution) processing
notes: Self-Oss-Instruct-SC2 dataset (from Starcoder 2 / Stack v2) used for training data construction in Lookahead routing paper (arXiv:2510.19506). See Lozhkov et al. 2024.

name: WikiQA
format: Real Bing query logs paired with candidate answer sentences from Wikipedia; designed for answer sentence selection

name: TIBMD@MUC
storage: ~2-5GB (16kHz mono WAV audio + Tibetan script transcripts)
format: 16kHz mono WAV audio recordings (formal and colloquial read speech) in 8 Tibetan language varieties, transcribed in Tibetan script; varieties include Amdo (Xiahe, Aba, Qinghai), Kham (Changdu, Dege, Yushu), and Ü-Tsang (Lhasa, Shigatse)
access: Available from the original paper Zhao et al. (2020) — Int. J. Comput. Sci. Eng., 22(2-3):297-304
notes: Used in arXiv:2510.22485 (Liang & Zerong, 2026) for studying tonogenesis continuum via pitch-flattening ASR. Yushu excluded due to insufficient data (only 0.77 hours). The paper uses ~2 hours per variety for training and ~30 min for testing.

name: 3DMEAD
num_samples: 47 speaker identities, 8 emotion categories (neutral + 7 emotions), 3 intensity levels (weak/medium/strong), 30 short sentences per emotion level, 40 neutral sentences per subject. Mesh sequences at 25 fps.
storage: ~60-80GB (reconstructed 3D meshes from MEAD video dataset, FLAME parameter format)
format: 3D facial mesh sequences in FLAME 3DMM parameterization (53-dim per frame: 50 expression coefficients + 3 jaw rotations). Reconstructed from MEAD 2D videos using DECA and MICA.
metric: MVE, LVE, FDD, MEE, CE, Diversity (vertex-space metrics)
notes: 3DMEAD: 3D MEAD is a large-scale emotional 3D facial mesh dataset reconstructed from the MEAD (Multimodal Emotional) audio-visual dataset. Used for speech-driven emotional facial animation. Paper: Danecek et al. SIGGRAPH Asia 2023.

name: MEAD
num_samples: 60+ speaker identities (multiple ethnicities, ages 20-45), 8 emotion categories (neutral + 7 emotions), 3 intensity levels, 60 sentences per emotion level. High-resolution 2D video recordings at 30fps.
storage: ~500GB-1TB+ (raw video recordings, multiple angles per subject)
format: High-quality 2D video recordings of actors speaking with emotional expressions. Original source for 3DMEAD reconstruction. Multi-view setup (31 cameras in some configurations).
access: https://github.com/MichaelJin4/MEAD (unofficial) or request from dataset authors (Wang et al. 2020)
notes: MEAD: Multimodal Emotional Dataset. Large-scale emotional audio-visual dataset. Source dataset for 3DMEAD (reconstructed 3D meshes). Original paper: Wang et al. ECCV 2020. Used as the basis for 3DMEAD which is used in LSF-Animation (2510.21864).

name: XLFM-Zebrafish
num_samples: 22,581 light field images (3 free-swimming zebrafish, 13 fixed zebrafish with 7 for train/val, 6 for testing)
eval_time: minutes to hours per evaluation run
format: Light field microscopy images captured via XLFM (eXtended Light Field Microscopy) system; each light field contains N×N sub-aperture views. Volumetric ground truth obtained via Richardson-Lucy deconvolution.
notes: First standardized benchmark for XLFM 3D reconstruction (He et al., 2025, arXiv:2510.22577). Includes zebrafish neural imaging data at 10fps and 1fps sampling rates across free-swimming and immobilized conditions.

name: H2B-Nemos
num_samples: Zebrafish neural activity recordings using H2B-Nemos genetically encoded calcium indicator (distinct zebrafish line and optical setup from XLFM-Zebrafish)
format: Light field microscopy data acquired with NeMOs calcium indicator, distinct from XLFM-Zebrafish dataset optical setup. Used for cross-domain generalization testing of XLFM-Former.
notes: Cross-domain generalization dataset for XLFM-Former (He et al., 2025, arXiv:2510.22577). Tests zero-shot reconstruction on unseen zebrafish line and optical configuration.

name: RGBNT201
num_samples: 14361 (4787 images per modality x 3 modalities: RGB, NIR, TIR)
format: Spatially aligned RGB, NIR, and TIR image triplets for multi-modality person re-identification captured on university campus with 4 non-overlapping cameras. 141 train / 30 val / 30 test identities.

name: RGBNT100
num_samples: 51750 (17250 image triples x 3 modalities: RGB, NIR, TIR)
format: Spatially aligned RGB, NIR, and TIR image triples for multi-spectral vehicle re-identification captured under uniform conditions. 50 vehicles training, 50 testing. RGB/NIR at 1920x1080, TIR at 640x480 @ 25fps.

name: MSVR310
num_samples: 6261 (2087 triplet samples x 3 modalities: RGB, NIR, TIR)
format: Spatially aligned RGB, NIR, and TIR image triplets for multi-spectral vehicle re-identification captured under diverse challenging conditions. RGB captured by 360 D866 camera (day) and Mi8 phone (night), NIR by 360 D866, TIR by FLIR SC620 at 640x480.

name: VGGFace2-HQ
num_samples: ~600k+ (full VGGFace2 ~3.1M images, VGGFace2-HQ is high-quality curated subset)
format: Large-scale face dataset with identity labels; multiple images per identity under varying poses, lighting, and expressions. VGGFace2-HQ is a high-quality subset.
notes: Used for training ID2Face face anonymization method (arXiv:2510.24213). Requires registration.

name: ImageNet-16H
num_samples: 32431 human predictions on 1200 natural images, 16 classes, 4 noise levels
format: Human prediction sets on 16-class image classification at varying noise levels (ω ∈ {80, 95, 110, 125})
notes: From Steyvers et al. (2022) PNAS. Used for studying human-AI complementarity in image classification. Multiple human annotations per image with perturbed noise levels.

name: DDXPlus
num_samples: Not specified in paper (synthetic patient records)
format: Synthetic patient records with demographics, symptoms, antecedents linked to differential diagnosis list; formed from medical knowledge base and rule-based diagnostic system
notes: From Fansi Tchango et al. (NeurIPS 2022). Used for medical decision-making tasks with LLMs. Human prediction sets formed using top-k strategy from differential diagnosis list.

name: Twin-2K-500
format: Survey responses from 2500 individuals (500 questions each) used to build digital twin personas for preference research; includes demographics, attitudes, and behavioral data
access: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.17479 (Toubia et al. 2025) — data agreement required

name: Robotouille
eval_time: minutes per task instance, hours for full eval (10 seeds × 10 instances × 20 tasks)
format: Text-based embodied cooking task environment requiring multi-step reasoning; synchronous mode (linear action execution) and asynchronous mode (concurrent subtask interleaving)

name: MetaUrban
storage: Estimated hundreds of GB (large-scale urban micromobility simulator)
format: Simulator for urban micromobility with PointNav and SocialNav tasks; multi-view RGB + LiDAR observations; robot embodiment (wheelchair)
metric: SR (Success Rate), SPL (Success weighted by Path Length), SNS (Social Navigation Score), CC/Cost (Cumulative Cost)
access: Not publicly confirmed released at paper submission

name: Sekai
format: Web-scale urban travel/navigation videos parsed from internet, paired with trajectory data for VLA training
access: Referenced in paper (arXiv:2506.15675), not confirmed publicly released

name: LongVU
format: Long video-language dataset for VideoQA tasks; used for scene understanding pre-training in UrbanVLA

name: Brain Tumor MRI Dataset
format: MRI scans of brain tumors with multi-class labels (meningioma, glioma, pituitary). Available at multiple resolutions and slices.
notes: Kaggle dataset used in Med-Hammer (arXiv:2510.24976) to evaluate Rowhammer-induced Trojan attacks across medical imaging modalities. Paper fine-tunes MobileViT, ResNet18, DeiT-S, and Swin-Transformer on this dataset.

name: Avito
format: User search logs with item lists; task: item-wise CTR prediction
access: public dataset from avito.ru competition/research collaboration

name: Kuaishou
format: User request logs with user features, candidate items, and exposed items; task: predict chosen items from 10 exposed items
access: not publicly available — internal Kuaishou industrial dataset

name: GMMLU
num_samples: ~14K per language (test), 6 languages (ES, ID, KO, EL, ZH, AR) + English = ~84K total test samples
format: 4-choice multiple-choice questions across academic and professional subjects; language-specific versions of the same universal knowledge questions
access: Singh et al. (2025) - 'Global MMLU: Understanding and addressing cultural and linguistic biases in multilingual evaluation' (ACL 2025)

name: BLEND
num_samples: ~19K-21K per language (test), 6 languages (ES, ID, KO, EL, ZH, AR) = ~120K total test samples
format: 4-choice multiple-choice questions evaluating culturally and regionally specific everyday knowledge; each question has language-specific correct answers reflecting local cultural context
access: Myung et al. (2024) - 'BLEND: A benchmark for LLMs on everyday knowledge in diverse cultures and languages' (NeurIPS 2024 D&B Track)

name: LongCite-45k
format: Long-context QA pairs with fine-grained sentence-level citations generated via CoF (Coarse to Fine) pipeline
metric: Citation precision/recall/F1 (used as training data for citation generation)
notes: LongCite-45k is a large-scale SFT dataset for long-context QA with citations (LQAC), used in Zhang et al. (2024) to train LongCite-8B and LongCite-9B models.

name: DiagBench
eval_time: hours to days (multi-turn evaluation across 2257 cases, up to 12 turns per case)
format: Structured patient cases with initial inquiry, physician-verified reference trajectories, and weighted evaluation rubrics. Sources: MIMIC-IV (750, ICU/ED), PMC-OA (631, case reports), MTSamples (379, outpatient), DDXPlus (497, differential diagnosis).
metric: Diagnosis accuracy, examination recommendation hit ratio/F1, weighted rubric score
license: Research use (MIMIC-IV PhysioNet credentialed; PMC-OA PMC OA terms; DDXPlus research; MTSamples fair use)
notes: Multi-center benchmark for interactive multi-turn diagnostic agents. 399 cases annotated with 3318 physician-authored rubrics. Paper: arXiv:2510.24654.

name: MTSamples
num_samples: 5043 transcribed reports (379 retained in DiagBench after filtering)
format: Transcribed medical reports across 40 specialties (Surgery, Cardiovascular, Orthopedic, Gastroenterology, Neurology, etc.)
notes: Transcribed medical transcription sample reports. Used as outpatient data source in DiagBench (arXiv:2510.24654). Approximately 50% filtered during structured extraction due to incomplete information.

name: GlobalQA
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed; 4 task types (TopK, Count, Sort, MinMax)
format: Corpus-level reasoning tasks requiring aggregation across entire document collections; answers require global reasoning not local retrieval

name: MBench
num_samples: 9 evaluation dimensions across 3 pillars (Motion Generalization, Motion-Condition Consistency, Motion Quality)
format: Hierarchical benchmark for 3D human motion generation evaluation. Motion Generalization: rare/unseen actions with descriptive prompts. Motion-Condition Consistency: semantic fidelity via VLM. Motion Quality: temporal (jitter, foot contact) and frame-wise (body penetration, pose naturalness).
metric: Motion Condition Consistency score, Motion Generalizability score, Jitter Degree, Dynamic Degree, Foot Floating, Foot Sliding, Body Penetration, Pose Quality (NRDF)
license: Research use (code and benchmark to be publicly available)
access: To be released with ViMoGen paper (arXiv:2510.26794)
notes: New benchmark introduced in ViMoGen paper. Uses VLM (vision-language model) for automated evaluation aligned with human judgment. Designed to go beyond FID by providing fine-grained multi-dimensional assessment of motion generation models.

name: PubLayNet
format: document images + bounding box annotations for layout elements (text, title, list, figure, table)
metric: COCO-style box-based mAP, IoU, Maximum IoU (mIoU)

name: SlideVQA
format: slide images + bounding box annotations + VQA-style question-answer pairs for document visual question answering
metric: IoU, Maximum IoU (mIoU), Content Ordering Score (COS)

name: DNSMOS P.835
format: Deep Noise Suppression Mean Opinion Score - non-intrusive perceptual speech quality metric derived from P.835 human ratings
notes: DNSMOS P.835 is a neural network-based non-intrusive metric for evaluating audio quality of speech. Used in SP-MCQA paper (2510.26190) for audio quality assessment of TTS outputs. Paper: Reddy et al., ICASSP 2022.

name: SP-MCQA-Eval
format: NPR news-style audio with manual MCQ annotations - questions examine key information (dates, names, numbers, locations, events)
metric: SP-MCQA ACC (accuracy %), WER, S-SIM, DNSMOS P.835
notes: Novel TTS evaluation benchmark assessing key-information accuracy beyond word-level metrics. Audio sourced from NPR news. Annotators listen to speech and answer MCQs about key information. Demonstrates gap between WER and practical intelligibility for SOTA TTS models.

name: GR-1
format: MuJoCo simulation with GR-1 humanoid robot (29 DoF: 17 arm/waist + 6 DoF per hand). Egocentric head camera RGB. Tabletop manipulation tasks.
notes: Humanoid robot benchmark for dexterous tabletop manipulation. From NVIDIA GR00T N1 paper (arXiv:2503.14734, 2025). Tasks include pick-and-place and articulated object manipulation (drawers, microwaves).

name: RadarScenes
storage: ~10-20GB (radar point clouds with point-wise moving object annotations)
format: Automotive radar dataset with 4D radar point clouds (x, y, z, Doppler velocity) and point-wise annotations for moving objects; designed for moving object segmentation in autonomous driving scenarios

name: LIVECODEBENCH
num_samples: ~1,600+ total problems (contamination-free evaluation; paper uses 76 SEEN + 93 UNSEEN for specific evaluations)
format: Holistic and contamination-free evaluation of LLMs for code. Problems sourced from Codeforces and LeetCode from 2024/10 to 2025/4. Includes problem descriptions, reference solutions, and test cases. Evaluates pass@1 and pass@k.
notes: Introduced in Jain et al., 2025 (ICLR 2025). Contamination-free: problems are from after training cutoffs. Used in HarnessLLM (arXiv:2511.01104) for bug-finding evaluation.

name: SYNTHETIC-1
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed; large-scale synthetic data for verified reasoning
format: Synthetic data generated at scale for verified reasoning tasks. Includes problem descriptions, ground-truth solutions, and verification signals. Used for training code and math reasoning models.
notes: Introduced by Prime Intellect (2025) for scaling distributed synthetic data generation for verified reasoning. Used in HarnessLLM (arXiv:2511.01104) as training data source for RL training of test harness generators.

name: TACO (Code)
format: Python programming problems with problem descriptions, ground-truth reference solutions, and test cases. Topics cover diverse algorithmic categories.
notes: TACO: Topics in Algorithmic Code Generation Dataset (Li et al., 2023). Distinct from the egocentric video TACO dataset also in this registry. Used in HarnessLLM (arXiv:2511.01104) as training data source.

name: Codeforces MatrixStudio
num_samples: Large dataset of Codeforces Python submissions (specific count not disclosed)
format: Codeforces competitive programming problems with Python submissions from the MatrixStudio dataset on HuggingFace. Includes problem descriptions and reference solutions.
notes: HuggingFace dataset of Codeforces Python submissions. Used in HarnessLLM (arXiv:2511.01104) as training data source for RL training of test harness generators.

name: DHMC-LUNG
num_samples: 159 WSIs from Duke University Medical Center (lung adenocarcinoma)
eval_time: Hours for feature extraction; minutes for MIL evaluation
format: Whole-slide images (H&E stained lung adenocarcinoma) with slide-level subtype/grade labels for MIL classification
access: Referenced in Wei et al. (Scientific Reports 2019, DOI: 10.1038/s41598-019-40035-5); available upon request or via TCGA-LUSC for similar lung cancer WSI data
notes: Duke University Medical Center lung adenocarcinoma WSI dataset. Used in PG-CIDL (arXiv:2511.01304) for lung adenocarcinoma classification. Original paper: 'Pathologist-level classification of histologic patterns on resected lung adenocarcinoma slides with deep neural networks' (Wei et al., Scientific Reports 2019).

name: Vidur
eval_time: minutes per experiment (each routing config evaluation takes seconds to minutes in simulation)
format: Open-source distributed LLM serving simulator; models arbitrary LLM inference workloads on GPU clusters; outputs per-request latency, TTFT, TPOT, throughput metrics
metric: RT (response time), TTFT, TPOT, Slowdown, P90 TTFT
notes: Vidur is the simulator used in the Glia paper (arXiv:2510.27176) for evaluating request routing, batch scheduling, and autoscaling algorithms for distributed LLM inference. Simulates Llama-3-8B on 4xA10 or Llama-3.3-70B on 8xH100.

name: ShareGPT (LLM inference workload)
num_samples: ~90K conversation pairs (ShareGPT dataset of real ChatGPT/GPT-4 user conversations)
format: Real user conversation data from ShareGPT containing LLM inference request patterns (prompt lengths, decode lengths, inter-arrival times) used as workload input for LLM serving simulators
notes: ShareGPT dataset used as the LLM inference workload in the Glia paper (arXiv:2510.27176). Workload characteristics include skewed and heavy-tailed sequence length distributions.

name: DebateBias-8K
num_samples: 8400 prompts (1200 per domain × 4 domains: Women's Rights, Backwardness, Terrorism, Religion)
eval_time: ~2-4 hours per model (8400 prompts × 3 repeats = 25,200 responses via API)
format: Open-ended debate-style prompts with structured format: two expert roles (Modern-region vs Stereotyped-region), demographic group selection from 5 groups (Western, Arabs, South Asians, Indians, Africans), 3 debate points per prompt. Prompt is given in one of 7 languages (English, Chinese, Arabic, Hindi, Korean, Swahili, Nigerian Pidgin).
metric: Demographic attribution percentage — percentage of debates where each demographic group is assigned the stereotyped vs modern role. Under uniform baseline, each group would receive ~20%.
access: Will be released at arXiv:2511.01187 (Saeed et al., 2025)
notes: Novel multilingual debate-style bias benchmark. Elicits open-ended generation rather than forced-choice. Evaluates 4 models: GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Haiku, DeepSeek-Chat, LLaMA-3-70B. Key finding: all models show severe stereotypes despite safety alignment; bias intensifies in low-resource languages.

name: S2Looking
num_samples: 5000 image pairs (3500 train, 500 val, 1000 test) at 1024x1024 pixels
format: Bitemporal satellite side-looking image pairs (0.5-0.8m/pixel) covering globally distributed rural areas with off-nadir angles, featuring building change masks

name: SECOND
format: Bitemporal aerial image pairs from Chinese cities (Hangzhou, Chengdu, Shanghai) with semantic change annotations for 6 land-cover classes: building, low vegetation, tree, water, playground, bare ground

name: SPOT THE BALL
num_samples: 150 curated images (50 soccer, 50 basketball, 50 volleyball) + 3000 generated soccer images
eval_time: hours per model per prompting strategy (150 images x multiple samples)
format: Sports images with ball removed, overlaid with 6x10 alphanumeric grid. Task: predict grid cell of removed ball. Multiple metrics: accuracy, Euclidean error, Wasserstein distance, near-player rate, overlap rate, center ratio, normalized entropy.
metric: accuracy (grid cell prediction), Euclidean error (pixels), Wasserstein distance (distribution alignment), behavioral metrics (NR, OR, CR, entropy)
access: [REDACTED in paper — authors state code and dataset available]
notes: Benchmark for visual social inference in VLMs (Balamurugan et al., 2025, arXiv:2511.00261). Tests ability to infer hidden ball location from social cues (gaze, pose, body orientation) in sports scenes. Humans achieve 20-34% accuracy vs VLMs <=17%. Models use heuristics (center bias, near-player) while humans use social cues.

name: ABO (Amazon Buildings Objects)
num_samples: ~8000 objects with multi-view RGB images (8-24 views per object), 3D meshes, and physical property annotations (mass, material labels, part segmentation)
storage: ~50-100GB (full dataset with 3D models); paper uses 100 sampled scenes (~5-10GB)
eval_time: minutes per object for full reconstruction pipeline
format: Amazon product listings with multi-view catalog images, 3D meshes in OBJ format, material part labels, and ground-truth mass in kg. Splits by object complexity (single-material, multi-material, challenging).
metric: Mass estimation: ADE (Absolute Deviation Error), ALDE (Absolute Log-Deviation Error), APE (Absolute Percentage Error), MnRE (Mean Relative Error). Lower is better for all except ALDE where higher is better.
access: https://github.com/de水果忍法/abo-dataset or https://amazon-bos-bucket.s3.amazonaws.com/index.html (original ABO dataset, Collins et al. CVPR 2022)
notes: Introduced by Collins et al. in 'ABO: Dataset and Benchmarks for Real-World 3D Object Understanding' (CVPR 2022). Used by NeRF2Physics and PUGS for physical property reasoning benchmarks. AURA evaluates on 100 randomly sampled scenes.

name: UCSF-PDGM
format: Preoperative 3D mpMRI (FLAIR, T1, T1-CE, T2) with multi-class tumor segmentation maps following BraTS protocol (ED, ET, NET). Ground-truth IDH mutation status and molecular subtypes provided.
notes: University of California San Francisco Preoperative Diffuse Glioma MRI dataset. Used in arXiv:2511.03376 (CIM-LLM) for zero-shot IDH mutation prediction. 83% IDH-wildtype (GBM).

name: TCGA-LGG
format: Preoperative 3D mpMRI (FLAIR, T1, T1-CE, T2) with segmentation labels. 100% IDH-mutant, lower-grade gliomas.
notes: The Cancer Genome Atlas Lower-Grade Glioma collection. Used in arXiv:2511.03376 (CIM-LLM). All subjects are IDH-mutant astrocytomas or oligodendrogliomas (WHO grade 2-3).

name: TCGA-GBM
format: Preoperative 3D mpMRI (FLAIR, T1, T1-CE, T2) with segmentation labels. 100% IDH-wildtype glioblastomas.
notes: The Cancer Genome Atlas Glioblastoma Multiforme collection. Used in arXiv:2511.03376 (CIM-LLM). All subjects are IDH-wildtype GBM (WHO grade 4).

name: EGD (Erasmus Glioma Database)
format: Structural MRI scans, WHO 2016 subtypes, and tumor segmentations. Contains both LGGs and HGGs; 35% IDH-mutant.
access: https://selfnoise.research.x Dijkgraaf et al., Data in Brief, 2021
notes: Erasmus Glioma Database. Used in arXiv:2511.03376 (CIM-LLM) for zero-shot IDH prediction. Notably, this dataset lacks ground-truth multi-class segmentation maps, demonstrating the pipeline works with automated segmentation.

name: IvyGAP (Ivy Glioblastoma Atlas Project)
format: Preoperative MRI with detailed anatomic region segmentations. 97% IDH-wildtype (GBMs).
notes: Ivy Glioblastoma Atlas Project. Used in arXiv:2511.03376 (CIM-LLM). High proportion of IDH-wildtype GBMs limits sensitivity calculations for IDH-mutant detection.

name: UPenn-GBM
format: De novo Glioblastoma patients from University of Pennsylvania Health System. Multi-parametric MRI volumes. 100% IDH-wildtype.
notes: UPenn-GBM dataset. Used in arXiv:2511.03376 (CIM-LLM). All subjects are IDH-wildtype GBM, so sensitivity for IDH-mutant is undefined (single-class cohort).

name: OOLONG-synth
num_samples: 400 questions per context length (8 datasets x 50 questions each); context lengths from 1K to 4M tokens
eval_time: hours per model depending on context length and API rate limits
format: Synthetic long-context inputs constructed from ICL text classification datasets (Spam, TREC, AGNews, IMDB, etc.) with user ID and date metadata; questions require counting, user-specific, and temporal aggregation reasoning
metric: soft scoring (0.75^|y-hat-y| for numeric answers, exact match for labels/dates/strings, set overlap for lists)
notes: OOLONG (arXiv:2511.02817): Benchmark for Evaluating Long Context Reasoning and Aggregation Capabilities. Two-split design: OOLONG-synth uses synthetic ICL-based tasks; OOLONG-real uses Critical Role D&D transcripts. All frontier models score below 50% at 128K context.

name: OOLONG-real
num_samples: ~300+ questions across single-episode and multi-episode settings; context lengths 55K to 1.3M tokens
eval_time: hours per model depending on context length and API rate limits
format: Real-world conversational data from Critical Role D&D transcripts (CRD3); questions require counting, enumeration, and indexing over dice rolls, spells, and character actions across episodes
metric: soft scoring (0.75^|y-hat-y| for numeric answers, exact match for strings, set overlap for lists)
license: Not specified (code and data released on GitHub)
notes: OOLONG-real uses fan-compiled CritRoleStats annotations as gold answers. Questions cover counting, enumeration, and indexing tasks over D&D game statistics (dice rolls, spell casting, character actions). No model exceeds 50% accuracy at 128K context on OOLONG-real.

name: WILD (in-the-Wild Image Linkage Dataset)
num_samples: ~20K total (10K closed-set: 5K train / 2K val / 3K test + 10K open-set test-only from 10 additional generators)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: High-quality synthetic face images from 20 generators (10 closed-set: Adobe Firefly, DALL-E 3, FLUX.1, FLUX.1.1 Pro, Freepik, Leonardo AI, Midjourney, SD 3.5 Large, SD XL Turbo, StarryAI; 10 open-set: DALL-E 1, DeepAI, HotpotAI, NVIDIA Sana, Stable Cascade, SD Attend&Excite, StyleGAN, StyleGAN2, StyleGAN3, Tencent Hunyuan). 1,000 prompts applied uniformly. Post-processed variants with 1-3 steps of compression/crop/resize/rotation/blur/photometric/grayscale/super-resolution.
metric: Macro AUC (per-class AUC averaged), EER (Equal Error Rate), Overlap Coefficient (OVL)
notes: Designed for synthetic image attribution — identifying which generator produced a given image. Includes both closed-set (known generators) and open-set (unseen generators) evaluation. WILD paper: Bongini et al., VERIMEDIA Workshop at IJCNN 2025.

name: Meta-World
format: 50 distinct robotic manipulation tasks with multi-task learning setup. Tasks include button presses, drawer open/close, object pickup, peg insertion, door manipulation, etc. Each task has language instructions and success criteria.
notes: Benchmark for multi-task and meta reinforcement learning. Used in Evo-1 paper (arXiv:2511.04555) as one of three main evaluation benchmarks. Tasks divided into Easy (28), Medium (11), Hard (6), and Very Hard (5) difficulty levels.

name: QMOOD Metrics
format: Quality Model for Object-Oriented Design: 6 high-level quality attributes (Reusability, Flexibility, Understandability, Effectiveness, Extendibility, Functionality) computed from 11 lower-level design metrics (DCC, CAM, CIS, DSC, DAM, ANA, NOM, NOP, NOH, MOA, MFA) based on ISO 9126 specification
metric: Quality Improvement Rate (QI) percentage, computed via formula: QI(Aq) = (Aq(p') - Aq(p)) / |Aq(p)| * 100
notes: QMOOD is a hierarchical software quality model used in RefAgent (arXiv:2511.03153) to evaluate software design quality before/after refactoring. Paper: Bansiya & Davis, IEEE Trans. Software Engineering 2002.

name: RefGen
format: Search-based refactoring tool that implements efficient refactoring scheduling based on partial order reduction. Operates in simulation mode to identify refactoring opportunities without applying changes to actual code.
metric: Refactoring opportunity identification (class-level, method-level), design quality improvement estimation via QMOOD metrics
notes: Baseline comparison tool in RefAgent (arXiv:2511.03153). Used to compare multi-agent refactoring identification against search-based optimization approach. Paper: Morales et al., J. Systems & Software 2018.

name: BreakHis
format: Breast cancer histopathology H&E stained images; labels form depth-3 tree (root -> benign/malignant -> 8 subtypes: adenosis, fibroadenoma, phyllodes tumor, tubular adenoma; ductal, lobular, mucinous, papillary carcinoma)
metric: top-1 accuracy, HF1, H-Acc, parent-distance violations

name: HAM-10000 (HAM-10K)
num_samples: 10015 dermoscopic skin lesion images from 7 lesion categories
format: Dermoscopic skin lesion images; clinically motivated trees: (i) benign vs malignant and (ii) melanocytic/keratinocytic/vascular above 7 leaves
metric: top-1 accuracy, HF1, H-Acc, parent-distance violations

name: InShop (DeepFashion In-Shop)
num_samples: 52712 images of 7982 items with train/query/gallery splits
format: Clothing images with catalog category metadata (dresses, skirts, tops, jeans, outerwear); shallow hierarchy: category -> item
metric: R@5 (Recall at 5), HF1, H-Acc, parent-distance violations

name: GSM-PLUS
format: GSM8K test split with rule-based adversarial perturbations: numerical substitution, operation modification, and similar transformations. Evaluates LLM robustness to well-formed adversarial variations of grade-school math problems.
metric: accuracy (compared with GSM8K baseline to measure performance drop)
notes: From Li et al. (ACL 2024). Used in RIDE paper (2511.04120) as a baseline comparison for rule-based perturbation methods.

name: Ref-LERF
num_samples: ~40-80 queries across 4 scenes (Ramen, Figurines, Teatime, Kitchen)
storage: ~50-100GB (multi-view calibrated RGB images for 4 scenes + 3DGS data)
eval_time: 1-2 hours per scene for CaRF training + evaluation
format: Multi-view calibrated RGB images + free-form text queries + mIoU evaluation

name: LERF-OVS
num_samples: Class-level queries across 4 scenes (same scenes as Ref-LERF)
format: Multi-view calibrated RGB images + class-level text queries + mIoU evaluation

name: 3D-OVS
num_samples: 5 categories (Bed, Bench, Room, Sofa, Lawn) with per-category evaluation
format: Large-scale 3D scenes with multi-view images + category-level text queries + mIoU evaluation

name: Places205
format: Scene images with category labels for transfer learning evaluation

name: VOC07
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Object detection annotations (20 classes) for multi-label image classification and detection tasks

name: RGB-D Scenes v2
num_samples: 14 scenes; 1,748 training / 236 validation / 497 testing image-point-cloud pairs
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on registration method
format: RGB-D video sequences of indoor furniture scenes with depth frames and RGB images; point cloud fragments created from consecutive depth frames; camera poses provided
metric: Inlier Ratio (IR), Feature Matching Recall (FMR), Registration Recall (RR), Patch Inlier Ratio (PIR)
notes: Indoor RGB-D dataset for image-to-point cloud registration (A2SI paper, arXiv:2511.05965). Scenes 1-8 for training, 9-10 for validation, 11-14 for testing. Pairs selected with at least 30% overlap. Used in 2D3D-MATR, B2-3D, and A2SI papers.

name: VOST
num_samples: curated from Ego4D and EPIC-Kitchens; val split: 70 videos, avg 22.3 sec at 60fps, 114 masklets at 5fps
eval_time: minutes per model for val split
format: Egocentric videos with object segmentation masks (masklets); transformations from actor-object interactions
metric: J (Jaccard), Jtr (Jaccard over last 25% frames), Precision, Recall

name: VOST-TAS
num_samples: 57 video instances, 108 transformations, 293 annotated resulting objects (extended from VOST val)
format: VOST val with explicit transformation annotations: temporal boundaries (start/end frames), action verb descriptions, resulting objects with segmentation masks and text descriptions
metric: T_P (temporal precision), T_R (temporal recall), S_V (action verb accuracy), S_O (object accuracy), H_ST (spatiotemporal recall), H (overall recall)

name: VSCOS
num_samples: val split: 98 videos, avg 7.5 sec at 60fps, object masks at 1fps; curated from EPIC-Kitchens
eval_time: minutes per model for val split
format: Egocentric videos with object state-changing segmentation masks from EPIC-Kitchens

name: M3-VOS
num_samples: 479 videos, 526 masklets, avg 14.3 sec at 30fps; models object phase transitions (gas/liquid/solid)
eval_time: minutes per model for full evaluation
format: Videos with object phase-change segmentation masks; limited camera motion (from online videos)

name: PURE (Physiological Rate Estimation)
format: Facial videos at 640x480 30Hz with ground-truth HR from CMS50E pulse oximeter at 60Hz. Activities: sitting still, talking, slow head movement, quick head movement, small/medium head rotation.
metric: MAE, RMSE, MAPE, Pearson r for heart rate (bpm)
notes: PURE dataset for remote photoplethysmography. Used in arXiv:2511.05946 (Reperio-rPPG) and many other rPPG papers. Subject-exclusive 5-fold cross-validation is standard evaluation protocol.

name: UBFC-rPPG
format: Facial videos at 640x480 30fps from webcam with ground-truth PPG from CMS50E pulse oximeter. Subjects played a time-sensitive math game to induce natural HR variation.
metric: MAE, RMSE, MAPE, Pearson r for heart rate (bpm)
notes: UBFC-rPPG dataset for remote photoplethysmography. Indoor recording with natural lighting variations (sunlight + artificial). Standard split: first 30 subjects for training, remaining 12 for testing.

name: MMPD (Multi-domain Mobile Video Physiology)
format: Mobile phone videos at 320x240 covering diverse skin tones (Fitzpatrick III-VI), lighting (LED-high, LED-low, incandescent, natural), and activities (stationary, head rotation, talking, walking). Ground-truth HR from pulse oximeter.
metric: MAE, RMSE, MAPE, Pearson r for heart rate (bpm); also HRV metrics (IBI, SDNN, SD1/SD2)
notes: MMPD is the most diverse and challenging rPPG dataset, covering real-world variations in skin tone, lighting, and motion. Used in arXiv:2511.05946 (Reperio-rPPG) for cross-dataset generalization testing.

name: Argoverse2
num_samples: 1000 driving logs, 15s each @ 20Hz, 7 cameras per log, log-level 3D vectorized map
format: Multimodal urban driving dataset with 7 surround-view cameras, LiDAR, and 3D vectorized maps with lane centerlines and topology
metric: TOPO F1, JTOPO F1, APLS, SDA, TOP_ll (centerline graph metrics)

name: Expresso
num_samples: ~4 speakers x 6 emotions = 24 expressive speech utterances (from paper: 4 speakers, 6 emotions each)
format: Expressive speech resynthesis dataset with controlled affective conditions: happy, laughing, sad, confused, enunciated, whisper. Four speakers (2M/2F, self-identified young). Used for evaluating emotional voice-based bias in audio LLM clinical decision-making.
notes: From Nguyen et al. (arXiv:2308.05725). Used in MedVoiceBias (arXiv:2511.06592) for emotional variability in voice-based clinical bias assessment. All 4 speakers expressed each of the 6 emotions.

name: EpBench (Episodic Memory Benchmark)
eval_time: minutes to hours for full evaluation
format: Synthetic books generated chapter-by-chapter from event templates; queries require episodic memory recall across spatiotemporal contexts with recurring actors/locations

name: PRISM-Bench
format: Text-to-image prompts across 6 categories: Imagination, Text Rendering, Style, Affection, Composition, Long Text. Scored with GPT-4.1-Vision for alignment and aesthetics.
notes: From Fang et al. (arXiv:2509.09680, 2025). Designed to expose alignment gaps that saturate on earlier benchmarks. PRISM-Bench-Licensed is the filtered variant removing copyrighted/unlicensed concepts. Used in FIBO paper (2511.06876).

name: ContraBench
format: Text-to-image prompts with contextual contradictions — atypical relations that conflict with common sense co-occurrences
notes: From Huberman et al. (arXiv:2506.01929, 2025). Probes robustness to atypical relations in text-to-image generation. Used in FIBO paper (2511.06876) to demonstrate contextual contradiction handling.

name: Whoops
format: Synthetic and compositional images with common sense violations for vision-language model evaluation
notes: From Bitton-Guetta et al. (ICCV 2023). Breaking common sense: Whoops! benchmark of synthetic and compositional images. Used in FIBO paper (2511.06876).

name: OMMO
num_samples: Outdoor multi-modal scenes with multiple calibrated RGB images
format: Large-scale outdoor multi-modal dataset with posed RGB images for novel view synthesis and implicit scene reconstruction
notes: From Lu et al. 2023. A large-scale outdoor multi-modal dataset and benchmark for novel view synthesis and implicit scene reconstruction. Used in ConeGS (arXiv:2511.06810) evaluation.

name: BI-OQA (Burst Image Objective Quality Assessment)
num_samples: 2237 burst sequences, 30543 images, 176288 annotations across denoising and super-resolution downstream tasks
storage: ~50-80GB estimated (RAW burst sequences at high resolution)
eval_time: minutes to hours for full evaluation
format: Burst image sequences (RAW format, 14 frames each) with per-frame quality scores derived from downstream task model performance (PSNR variation)
metric: SRCC (Spearman Rank Correlation Coefficient) with relaxed thresholds (R0, R0.02, R0.05, R0.1)
license: Research use (derived from BurstSR and HDR+ datasets)
access: Paper: arXiv:2511.07958; Original datasets: BurstSR (GitHub: algvirtual/DeepBurstSR), HDR+ (Google HDR+ dataset)
notes: From paper: Burst Image Quality Assessment (BuIQA). Ground truth derived from 8 downstream models: 4 denoising (HDR21, INN, DBD, BPN) and 4 super-resolution (EBSR, BSRT, DBSR, BIP). Also includes 1204 synthesized RAW bursts.

name: BI-SQA (Burst Image Subjective Quality Assessment)
num_samples: 5109 burst sequences, 15284 images across subjective downstream tasks
format: Burst image sequences with per-frame quality scores from human annotators (pairwise comparisons and normalized scores)
license: Research use (derived from Photo-Triage and SPAQ datasets)
access: Paper: arXiv:2511.07958; Original datasets: Photo-Triage (Chang et al. 2016), SPAQ (Fang et al. 2020)
notes: From paper: Burst Image Quality Assessment (BuIQA). Quality scores normalized to [0,1] range. 4175 sequences from Photo-Triage, 934 sequences from SPAQ.

name: BurstSR
num_samples: Not specified in paper (burst sequences for super-resolution)
format: RAW burst image sequences for super-resolution
notes: Deep burst super-resolution dataset (Bhat et al., CVPR 2021). Used as one of the sources for BI-OQA in BuIQA paper (arXiv:2511.07958).

name: HDR+
num_samples: Not specified in paper (burst sequences from mobile cameras)
format: RAW burst image sequences from mobile cameras with HDR processing
notes: Burst photography for HDR and low-light imaging dataset (Hasinoff et al., ACM ToG 2016). Used as source for BI-OQA in BuIQA paper (arXiv:2511.07958).

name: Photo-Triage
num_samples: ~11000 images from smartphone photography, grouped into burst sequences
format: Burst image sequences with individual frame quality annotations from human raters
notes: Automatic photo triage dataset. Used as source for BI-SQA in BuIQA paper (arXiv:2511.07958).

name: SPAQ (Smartphone Photography Quality Assessment)
num_samples: ~11000 smartphone images with subjective quality annotations
eval_time: minutes to hours for full evaluation
format: Individual smartphone images with perceptual quality scores from human annotators
notes: Perceptual quality assessment of smartphone photography dataset. Used as source for BI-SQA in BuIQA paper (arXiv:2511.07958). In this paper, visually similar samples were grouped to form burst sequences.

name: BigO(Bench)
num_samples: 3105 problems (311-problem test set used in paper)
format: Python coding problems with formal I/O specs, unit tests, and inferred time/space complexity labels
notes: Benchmark for evaluating LLM code generation with controlled time/space complexity. Designed to study algorithmic complexity and runtime behavior of LLM-generated code. From Chambon et al., 2025 (arXiv:2503.15242). Used in Dynamic Stability of LLM-Generated Code (arXiv:2511.07463).

name: GEOM-DRUGS
num_samples: ~450k molecules (drug-like) with multiple 3D conformations each, ~2M+ total conformers
format: 3D coordinates, atomic types, partial charges, bond information, energy annotations (DFT/GFN2-xTB)
metric: Atom stability, molecule stability, validity, RMSD, relaxation energy (ΔErelax) after geometry optimization
notes: Energy-annotated molecular conformations for drug-like molecules (Axelrod & Gomez-Bombarelli, Scientific Data 2022). Used in Nikitin et al. 2025 benchmark protocol for 3D molecular generation. Paper evaluated 5000 molecules following the protocol.

name: SceneFun3D
storage: ~10-20GB (3D point clouds with dense affordance and motion annotations)
format: 3D point cloud scenes with element-level affordance masks, motion types, and motion axis directions annotated per instruction
metric: mIoU, AP, AP50, AP25, +T (motion type accuracy), +TD (motion type + direction accuracy)
notes: From Delitzas et al., CVPR 2024. Fine-grained affordance grounding and motion estimation in 3D indoor scenes. Used in AffordBot (arXiv:2511.10017).

name: SUPERB
num_samples: Various speech tasks (ASR, SV, ER, etc.)
format: Multi-task benchmark for Speech Processing Universal PERformance Benchmark. Covers: ASR (LibriSpeech), Speaker Verification (VoxCeleb), Emotion Recognition (IEMOCAP), and more.
notes: SUPERB: Speech Processing Universal Performance Benchmark (Yang et al., Interspeech 2021). Evaluates frozen speech foundation model representations on multiple downstream tasks. Used extensively in arXiv:2511.08389 for evaluating model/layer fusion methods.

name: ML-SUPERB
format: Multilingual Speech Universal PERformance Benchmark. Mono-1h: 1 hour per language for 13 languages. Multi-1h: 1 hour per language for 143 languages.
notes: ML-SUPERB: Multilingual extension of SUPERB (Shi et al., Interspeech 2023). Tests speech foundation models on multilingual ASR with limited training data. Used in arXiv:2511.08389 for evaluating fusion methods across languages.

name: SACRED-Bench
num_samples: ~8,545 training samples + 2,481 test samples across SSO/SAO/MSD attack types
format: Speech-audio compositional red-teaming benchmark with 3 attack types: Speech-Speech Overlap (SSO), Speech-Audio Overlap (SAO), Multi-Speaker Dialogue (MSD). SSO mixes harmful and benign speech with cross-fade at tuned volume/speed/overlap; SAO mixes benign speech with harmful non-speech audio; MSD embeds harmful content in multi-speaker dialogues with benign textual trigger. Permission questions (Yes-No) for SSO/SAO, open-ended questions for MSD.
notes: From Yang et al. 2025 (arXiv:2511.10222). Train: 6,640 SSO + 986 SAO + 919 MSD. Test: 400 SSO + 1,364 SAO + 717 MSD. HCS (harmless control set): 400 samples. Sources: harmful instructions from AdvBench/MM-SafetyBench/HarmBench, benign speech from VoiceBank-DEMAND, speech synthesis via ChatTTS.

name: VoiceBank-DEMAND
format: Multi-speaker English speech corpus used as source of benign speech carriers in SSO and SAO attack construction.
notes: From Veaux et al. (INTERSPEECH 2016). High-quality clean speech from diverse speakers. Used as benign speech carrier in SACRED-Bench SSO and SAO attacks (Yang et al., arXiv:2511.10222).

name: JALMBench
num_samples: SSJ subset: 246 samples; AMSE subset: 100 samples with 18 edits each = 1,800 inputs
format: Benchmark for evaluating jailbreaking attacks on audio language models. Contains SSJ (Speech Semantic Jamming) and AMSE (Audio Manipulation-based Speech Editing) subsets.
notes: From Peng et al. 2025 (arXiv:2505.17568). Used in SACRED-Bench paper (Yang et al., arXiv:2511.10222) for cross-method comparison: Speech Insertion (SSJ subset) and Speech Editing (AMSE subset) vs SACRED-Bench attacks.

name: ColosseumBench
num_samples: 20 manipulation tasks with spatial perturbation variations (MO-Size, RO-Size, Camera-Perturb)
format: simulated robotic manipulation tasks with multi-view RGB-D observations under spatial perturbations

name: SlideSpeech
format: Audio (16kHz) + slide-derived OCR texts + transcripts. Multimodal conference videos (720p video, synchronized slides, textual keywords).
notes: From Wang et al., ICASSP 2024. Large-scale slide-enriched audio-visual corpus for contextualized ASR. Training subsets: L95 (473h) and S95 (161h). Contains OCR-derived contextual keywords from conference presentation slides.

name: SST-5
format: Single-sentence movie reviews with fine-grained sentiment labels (5 classes: very negative, negative, neutral, positive, very positive)
notes: Stanford Sentiment Treebank fine-grained version (Socher et al. 2013). Train/val/test split: 8,544/1,101/2,210. Used in arXiv:2511.10675 (TopK+L2D ICL demonstration selection).

name: CR
format: Customer review sentences with binary sentiment labels (positive/negative)
notes: Customer reviews dataset (Ding, Liu, and Yu 2008). Train/test split: 3,394/376. Used in arXiv:2511.10675 (TopK+L2D ICL demonstration selection).

name: Subj
format: Single sentences with binary subjectivity labels (subjective/objective)
notes: Subjectivity classification dataset (Wang et al. 2018). Train/test split: 8,000/2,000. Used in arXiv:2511.10675 (TopK+L2D ICL demonstration selection).

name: AgNews
format: News articles with 4-class topic labels (World, Sports, Business, Sci/Tech)
notes: AgNews topic classification dataset (Zhang, Zhao, and LeCun 2015). Train/test split: 120,000/7,600. Used in arXiv:2511.10675 (TopK+L2D ICL demonstration selection).

name: AdvancedIF
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Expert-written prompts with corresponding rubric criteria; evaluated by LLM judge (o3-mini or finetuned verifier) checking binary satisfaction per criterion
metric: Percentage of responses that fully satisfy all rubric criteria per category (CIF, CC, SS); overall average across categories
notes: From Meta Superintelligence Labs (arXiv:2511.10507). Three categories: Complex Instruction Following (CIF, 402 dialogs), Multi-turn Carried Context (CC, 736 dialogs), System Prompt Steerability (SS, 507 dialogs). Human-written prompts and rubrics. Best SOTA models achieve ~75%, indicating significant room for improvement.

name: MultiChallenge
format: Multi-turn conversation prompts with instance-level rubrics; evaluated by LLM judge
notes: From Deshpande et al. (ACL 2025 Findings). Realistic multi-turn conversation evaluation benchmark challenging to frontier LLMs. Used as out-of-distribution evaluation benchmark in RIFL paper (arXiv:2511.10507).

name: PG-19
num_samples: ~22K books (65M words train, ~3K books valid, ~3K books test)
eval_time: minutes to hours for perplexity evaluation
format: Books from Project Gutenberg with language modeling train/valid/test splits (no OCR, no segmentation)

name: MSCOCO (captioning/retrieval)
num_samples: ~164K images (train 83K, val 5K, test 41K for online server); each image has 5 human-written captions
format: Images with 5 captions each for image-text retrieval and captioning tasks; MSCOCOKarpathy split for retrieval and captioning

name: ZDT
format: Synthetic Pareto front points in R^d, generated via NSGA-II or similar MOO algorithm
metric: hypervolume, uniformity, coverage, directed coverage (quality measures for representative subset selection)
access: https://www.egr.unlv.edu/~sde/papers/ZDT.pdf; also via pymoo library (Blank & Deb, IEEE Access 2020)
notes: Zitzler-Deb-Thiele benchmark suite for multiobjective optimization (Zitzler et al., EMO 2000). Widely used for evaluating multiobjective evolutionary algorithms. Used in Boehmer & Wittmann (arXiv:2511.10716) for Pareto pruning experiments.

name: DTLZ
num_samples: 7 test instances (DTLZ1-DTLZ7), scalable number of objectives (paper uses 3)
format: Synthetic Pareto front points in R^d, generated via NSGA-II or similar MOO algorithm
metric: hypervolume, uniformity, coverage, directed coverage (quality measures for representative subset selection)
access: https://www.eMOO.es/download.php?file=benchmark-DTLZ; also via pymoo library (Blank & Deb, IEEE Access 2020)
notes: Deb-Thiele-Laumanns-Zitzler benchmark suite for scalable multiobjective optimization test problems (Deb et al., CEC 2002). Used in Boehmer & Wittmann (arXiv:2511.10716) for Pareto pruning experiments with 3 objectives.

name: PGMORL
format: Pareto fronts from simulated agents performing simple tasks evaluated under two objectives
access: https://github.com/any送り/Xu2020Pareto (referenced in paper as PGMORL from Xu et al., 2020)
notes: Pareto Grammar Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning benchmark from Xu et al. (AAAI 2020). Used as realistic benchmark in Boehmer & Wittmann (arXiv:2511.10716). Pareto fronts from RL agent task optimization.

name: DFEW
format: Video clips (in-the-wild) with clip-level emotion labels: Happiness, Sadness, Neutral, Anger, Surprise, Disgust, Fear
access: https://github.com/minliu5566/DFEW or request from authors (Jiang et al., ACM MM 2022)
notes: Dynamic Facial Expression in the Wild. Large-scale DFER benchmark from Jiang et al. (ACM MM 2022). 5-fold cross-validation protocol. Used in TG-DFER (arXiv:2511.10958) as one of two main benchmarks.

name: FERV39k
format: Video clips (in-the-wild) with clip-level emotion labels: Happiness, Sadness, Neutral, Anger, Surprise, Disgust, Fear. Organized into 4 broad scenarios and 22 detailed contexts.
access: https://github.com/MUKAI-PLAB/FERV39K or request from authors (Wang et al., CVPR 2022)
notes: Facial Expression Recognition in Videos, ~39k clips. Largest in-the-wild DFER dataset from Wang et al. (CVPR 2022). Train/test split protocol (no overlap). Used in TG-DFER (arXiv:2511.10958) as one of two main benchmarks.

name: WikiTableQuestions (WTQ)
format: Semi-structured table QA: natural language questions over Wikipedia tables requiring compositional semantic parsing and multi-step reasoning

name: LC-QuAD 2.0
num_samples: ~19k train + ~4.8k test (original); curated single-binding subset used in paper: ~5.1k train + ~1.3k test
format: Complex multi-hop question answering over Wikidata knowledge graph; natural language questions paired with SPARQL queries and answers
notes: LC-QuAD 2.0: Large-scale Complex Question Answering over Wikidata Dataset. From Saha et al. (ACL 2019). This paper uses a curated executable single-answer subset filtered by re-executing gold queries against Wikidata HDT dump (2023-12-21).

name: LDCTIQA2023
format: Low-dose CT slices with radiologist-assigned MOS scores on 0-4 rubric (0: bad, 1: poor, 2: fair, 3: good, 4: excellent). Training set: 1000 images, Test set: 300 images.
metric: PLCC (Pearson correlation), SROCC (Spearman rank correlation), KROCC (Kendall rank correlation)
access: Published in Medical Image Analysis journal (Lee et al., 2025)

name: AMR Bank
format: Sentence-level AMR graphs (penman notation) with PropBank-aligned rolesets for predicates and general roles for nouns (:poss, :part, :consist-of, etc.)
license: LDC (for LDC releases); some newer releases via penman open source
notes: Abstract Meaning Representation Bank. AMR encodes sentence-level semantics as rooted, labeled graphs. Used in paper for coverage analysis — QA-Noun captures ~99% of AMR noun arguments plus additional implied relations.

name: FactScore
num_samples: 500 Wikipedia/Bio生成 sentences from Min et al., 2023 (paper benchmark); uses GPT-4o for atomic fact generation
format: Given a generated text (e.g., biography, summarization), decompose into atomic facts and evaluate precision via GPT-4o entailment
metric: FActScore = (number of entailed atomic facts) / (total number of generated facts)
notes: Fine-grained atomic evaluation of factual precision in long-form text generation (Min et al., EMNLP 2023). Used in paper as a baseline for semantic decomposition granularity comparison.

name: DecompScore
num_samples: 1000 sentences from FactScore benchmark; metric applied to any decomposition
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on decomposition method
format: Given a sentence decomposition (QA pairs or atomic facts), measures: (1) number of generated units, (2) non-redundant count after CORE filtering, (3) entailed count via GPT-4o entailment. Final score = Entailed / Non-Redundant
metric: Entailed sub-claims per sentence (higher = more granular, valid decomposition)
notes: Reference-based evaluation of sentence decompositions into atomic facts (Wanner et al., 2024). Used in paper to compare granularity of QA-Noun+QA-SRL vs FactScore and R-ND. Paper shows QA-Noun+QA-SRL achieves ~130-150% higher DecompScore than fact-based baselines.

name: CORE
format: Postprocessing framework for decomposition methods; detects and clusters redundant or paraphrastic QA pairs across different parsers
metric: N/A (used to filter redundant QA pairs before computing DecompScore)
notes: Robust Factual Precision with Informative Subclaim Identification (Jiang et al., ACL 2025). Used in paper to avoid double-counting overlapping QA pairs from QA-Noun (nouns) and QA-SRL (verbs). CORE ensures faithful count of unique atomic facts in the unified decomposition.

name: QA-Noun
num_samples: 1686 sentences, 2029 noun predicates, 4869 total arguments across train/dev/test (50/10/40 split)
format: Sentence-level annotations with noun mentions marked, each annotated with QA pairs from 9 question templates (Possessive, Location, Partitive/Membership x2, Copular, Sub-Specification, Property, Quantity, Time). Stored as JSONL with sentence, noun index, and list of QA pairs.
metric: UA F1 (unlabeled argument detection), SRA (semantic role accuracy)
notes: Released by paper (Tseytlin et al., 2025). 9 question templates covering noun-centered semantic relations. Double-annotated evaluation set, single-annotated training set. Annotation cost ~$1.75/predicate for evaluation, ~$0.35/predicate for training.

name: QA-SRL
num_samples: ~19K sentences (QA-SRL Bank 2.0; larger than QA-SRL 1.0 with ~3.5K)
format: Sentence-level QA pairs where questions are derived from PropBank rolesets; answers are spans from the sentence
metric: UA F1, precision, recall for argument detection
notes: Question-Answer driven Semantic Role Labeling (He et al., EMNLP 2015). The paper's QA-Noun is designed to complement QA-SRL by covering noun-centered relations. The paper uses the QA-SRL parser (Klein et al., 2022) to produce verbal QA pairs in the unified decomposition.

name: QANom
num_samples: ~2K sentences with deverbal nominalizations (Klein et al., 2020)
format: QA pairs for deverbal nouns derived from verb predicates; uses extended PropBank roleset for nominalizations
notes: Question-answer driven SRL for nominalizations (Klein et al., COLING 2020). Extends QA-SRL to handle nominalized verbs (e.g., 'analysis', 'development'). Part of the QASem framework that QA-Noun extends.

name: DVS-Gesture
format: Event camera recordings of human hand gestures captured with Dynamic Vision Sensor (DVS). Events are 4-tuples (t, x, y, p) with timestamp, coordinates, and polarity.
notes: IBM DVS Gesture dataset. Event-based gesture recognition dataset. Used in PACE paper (arXiv:2511.12095) for evaluating SNN dataset distillation. 11 gesture classes including hand waves in different directions.

name: CIFAR10-DVS
format: Event-camera recordings generated by replaying CIFAR-10 static images on a monitor while inducing saccade-like camera motions. Events are 4-tuples (t, x, y, p).
notes: Converted from original CIFAR-10 dataset via event camera replay. Used in PACE paper (arXiv:2511.12095) for evaluating dataset distillation on SNNs. 10 classes, same train/test split as CIFAR-10.

name: SUN RGB-D
format: RGB-D indoor scene images with pixel-level semantic annotations, includes data from NYU Depth V2 and Berkeley B3DO

name: PACS
format: Images in 4 domains (Photo, Art Painting, Cartoon, Sketch) with 7 classes (dog, elephant, giraffe, guitar, horse, house, person)

name: VLCS
format: Images from 4 datasets (PASCAL VOC 2007, LabelMe, Caltech101, SUN09) with 5 overlapping classes (bird, car, chair, dog, person)

name: OLID
format: English tweets labeled binary (offensive/non-offensive) or with fine-grained labels (target, target type, target category)

name: Aloha MuJoCo
num_samples: Bimanual manipulation tasks (cube transfer, peg insertion) with scripted and human kinesthetic demonstrations
format: MuJoCo-based bimanual manipulation; RGB-D observations, joint positions, actions; language task descriptions

name: Franka Kitchen (Multi-stage Manipulation)
num_samples: Multi-stage household manipulation tasks with sequential objectives
format: Franka Panda manipulation tasks in kitchen environment; language goal instructions; RGB-D observations; sequential task completion

name: ChartEditVista
format: (chart_image, editing_instruction, modified_chart_code) triplets; 31 chart types, 6 editing task types
metric: RARM metrics: Exec (executability), TR (text), LR (layout), Col (color), Type, Avg score
access: Not publicly released at time of paper (arXiv:2511.15266)

name: ChartEdit
format: (chart_image, editing_instruction, modified_chart_code) triplets; 19 chart types, 6 editing task types

name: ChartMimic
format: (source_chart_image, target_chart_image, natural_language_instruction, target_code) for chart-to-code generation; 22 chart types

name: ChartCoder-160k
format: (chart_image, chart_code, chart_description) for chart-to-code generation

name: GRCh38 (Human Reference Genome)
format: FASTA DNA sequences, chromosomes 1-22, X, Y, MT

name: OpenGenome2
format: Multi-species genome sequences across all domains of life (bacteria, archaea, eukaryotes, viruses)
license: Various per source; compiled by Arc Institute
access: Request access via Arc Institute; not publicly released at paper time (Brixi et al., bioRxiv 2025)

name: MSL39 Viral Dataset
format: FASTA viral genome sequences; used as out-of-distribution test set in Focus paper (absent from OpenGenome2 training data)
metric: Compression fidelity metrics (L1, L2, Hellinger, JS, KL divergence)
access: Public NCBI viral genomes; specific MSL39 collection described in Focus paper (arXiv:2511.14694)

name: SafeRBench
num_samples: 1,128 harmful queries balanced across 6 categories and 3 risk levels
eval_time: Hours for full benchmark (19 models × 1,128 queries); minutes per model
format: Harmful queries with category + risk-level annotations; LRM outputs (reasoning trace + answer) evaluated via GPT-4o micro-thought segmentation and LLM-graded risk/execution scores
metric: 10 safety dimensions: Risk Density, Defense Density, Intention Awareness, Safe Strategy Conversion (SAS metrics); Not-Explicit-Refusal, Risk Level, Execution Level (RES metrics); Response Complexity, Trajectory Coherence, Risk Reduction (holistic metrics)
access: None — no code or dataset release accompanying paper arXiv:2511.15169
notes: First end-to-end safety benchmark for Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) that evaluates safety across the full reasoning trace + answer pipeline, not just final outputs. Introduces Micro-Thought Analysis (GPT-4o-based chunking into 6 intent labels) and the Safety-Helpfulness Paradox observation. Dataset not publicly released; requires recreating harmful query annotations following the paper's methodology.

name: SPBench
format: Multi-turn doctor-patient dialogues with 8-dimensional evaluation criteria (QC, CC, CD, RC, LC, LN, CS, PD)
metric: 5-point Likert scale per dimension, rescaled to 100
license: Research use (cases from published SP training books)
access: Not publicly released — data from Standardized Patient training books (Manual for Writing Standardized Patient Cases; A Practical Tutorial for Standardized Patients)

name: ZInD (Zillow Indoor Dataset)
num_samples: ~67,448 RGB 360-degree panoramas across 1,575 unfurnished residential homes
format: 360-degree indoor panoramas with annotated 3D room layouts, 2D bounding boxes for windows/doors/openings, merged room layouts, 3D camera poses, and 2D floor plans
license: Academic/non-commercial use; requires registration and API token
notes: Used as background source for rendering in adversarial clothing paper (2511.16020). Paper uses 1,000 ZInD images as background pool for training and 1,000 for testing.

name: FairCLIP Glaucoma (Harvard Glaucoma Fairness)
num_samples: 10000 (7K train / 2K val / 1K test) fundus (SLO) images with demographic annotations
format: Retinal fundus (SLO) images with clinical notes, annotated with gender (Male/Female), race (White/Black/Asian), ethnicity (Hispanic/Non-Hispanic/Unknown), and glaucoma diagnosis labels
metric: Accuracy / Average Disparity (AD) across demographic groups
notes: Curated from Harvard Glaucoma Fairness dataset for fairness evaluation in medical imaging. Used in FADS paper (arXiv:2511.15986) as primary benchmark for evaluating fairness-aware ICL in MLLM medical image reasoning.

name: CheXpert Plus
format: Chest X-ray images curated from CheXpert dataset, balanced subsets focusing on edema, pleural effusion, and pneumothorax classification, with demographic annotations
license: Stanford University Dataset Research Use Agreement (free, same as CheXpert)
notes: Balanced subset of CheXpert created in FADS paper (arXiv:2511.15986) for fairness evaluation. Derived from original CheXpert (Stanford Hospital data), with 2,500 samples per disease (1,250 positive, 1,250 negative) to address class imbalance in original CheXpert.

name: LSDIR
format: Large-scale image restoration dataset containing diverse high-quality images for training super-resolution and restoration models; derived from LAION with quality filtering
notes: Large Scale Dataset for Image Restoration (Li et al., CVPR 2023). Used as primary training dataset for ODTSR alongside FFHQ subset.

name: RealCE-val
format: Paired real-world Chinese-English scene text LR/HR image pairs for STISR evaluation; center-cropped to 512x512
metric: NED (Normalized Edit Distance), PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, MANIQA
notes: Validation set of RealCE benchmark (Ma et al., ICCV 2023). Chinese-English scene text image super-resolution dataset. ODTSR evaluates on this dataset without training on it specifically, demonstrating cross-domain generalization.

name: PanNuke
storage: ~3GB (histopathology images with nuclei instance segmentation and classification masks)
format: Histopathology images covering 19 tissue types with nuclei instance segmentation and classification; split into 5381 train + 2523 validation images
notes: PanNuke dataset used in CORA paper (arXiv:2511.17755) for histopathology reasoning segmentation experiments.

name: MLE-bench
format: Kaggle competition format: training data, test sets, submission formats, evaluation scripts
metric: medal rate (bronze/silver/gold), valid submission rate, normalized score, percentile, ELO
notes: Machine Learning Engineering Benchmark. Evaluates autonomous AI agents on 75 Kaggle ML tasks spanning CV, NLP, time series, tabular, multimodal. Each task has 24-hour execution limit. Used in this paper (arXiv:2511.15593) to study ideation diversity in AI research agents.

name: MMSVG-Illustration
eval_time: minutes per image for vectorization pipeline
format: Rasterized SVG images with per-pixel layer index ground truth (encoded in RGB); curated from MMSVG dataset
metric: Ordering consistency (pixel pair depth order accuracy), MAE, MSE vs. ground truth layer indices

name: SVGX-Core-250k
eval_time: minutes per image for vectorization pipeline
format: SVG vector graphics with layered path structure; used for out-of-domain generalization testing
metric: Ordering consistency (pixel pair depth order accuracy), MAE, MSE vs. ground truth layer indices

name: MileBench
format: Multi-image long-context benchmark with 4 task types: Temporal Multi-Image (T), Semantic Multi-Image (S), Needle-in-a-Haystack (NH), and Image Retrieval (IR). Each sample contains multiple images with accompanying text.
notes: Multimodal long-context benchmark from Song et al. (arXiv:2404.18532). Used in FlashCache paper (arXiv:2511.16786) as primary benchmark for KV cache compression evaluation.

name: MUIRBench
format: Robust multi-image understanding benchmark covering 12 diverse tasks (scene understanding, temporal ordering, visual retrieval) and 10 categories of inter-image relations. Each example pairs an answerable instance with a minimally modified unanswerable variant.
notes: Comprehensive benchmark for robust multi-image understanding in MLLMs (Wang et al., arXiv:2406.09411). Used in FlashCache paper (arXiv:2511.16786) for KV cache compression evaluation.

name: HR-Bench
format: High-resolution visual question answering benchmark with two sub-tasks: Fine-grained Single-instance Perception (FSP) for attribute recognition/OCR/spatial reasoning, and Fine-grained Cross-instance Perception (FCP) for map/chart understanding. Provided in 8K and 4K resolution settings.
notes: High-resolution VQA benchmark for MLLMs (Wang et al., AAAI 2025). Used in FlashCache paper (arXiv:2511.16786) for evaluating KV cache compression under high-resolution inputs.

name: FAVOR-Bench
num_samples: 1,776 videos, 8,184 close-ended QA pairs across 6 tasks
format: Fine-grained video motion understanding benchmark with 6 motion-centric sub-tasks (AS, HAC, SAD, MAD, CM, NSM) covering both egocentric and third-person perspectives. Both close-ended (MC) and open-ended (GPT-assisted caption) evaluation.
notes: Fine-grained video motion understanding benchmark (Tu et al., arXiv:2503.14935). Used in FlashCache paper (arXiv:2511.16786) for video KV cache compression evaluation.

name: MUSIC-21
format: Synchronized audio-visual recordings of 21 musical instruments; video clips segmented into 1-second non-overlapping windows
notes: Subset of MUSIC dataset (MUsic InStrument Classification). From Zhao et al. ICCV 2019. Used in DAVDD (arXiv:2511.17890) for audio-visual dataset distillation.

name: AVE
format: Audio-visual event video clips from 28 event categories, segmented into 1-second non-overlapping windows with synchronized annotations
notes: Audio-Visual Events dataset from Tian et al. ECCV 2018. Used in DAVDD (arXiv:2511.17890) for audio-visual dataset distillation.

name: VTUAV
storage: ~500GB-1TB (estimated; large-scale UAV video dataset with RGB and thermal modalities)
format: Visible-Thermal UAV Tracking: A Large-scale Benchmark and New Baseline (Zhang et al., CVPR 2022). RGB-Thermal video pairs captured from UAVs with bounding box annotations. Includes short-term (ST) and long-term (LT) tracking subsets.
notes: VTUAV benchmark introduced in 'Visible-Thermal UAV Tracking: A Large-scale Benchmark and New Baseline' (Zhang et al., CVPR 2022). Used for RGBT tracking evaluation in CADTrack paper.

name: FUNSD (Form Understanding in Noisy Scanned Documents)
format: Scanned form images with annotated text regions, key-value pairs, and entity labels for form understanding
metric: ANLS, F1 score for entity extraction

name: CORD (Consolidated Receipt Dataset for Post-OCR Parsing)
format: Receipt images with OCR annotations for key information extraction (merchant, date, total, items)
metric: ANLS, F1 score for field-level extraction

name: STE-VQA (Scene Text Extraction Visual Question Answering)
num_samples: ~23K QA pairs on natural scene images
format: Natural scene images containing embedded text with QA pairs requiring understanding of scene text in context

name: RICO (Mobile App Dataset for Data-Driven Design)
num_samples: 72,294 mobile app screenshots with UI hierarchies
format: Mobile UI screenshots with annotated UI element hierarchies and semantic labels for mobile UI understanding
metric: ANLS for VQA tasks, element classification accuracy

name: M4-ViteVQA
storage: ~50-100GB (text-rich videos with OCR and detection annotations)
format: Videos with questions requiring reading small, transient text cues; includes OCR tokens and object detection results with bounding boxes

name: MP-DocVQA
format: Multi-page documents with questions requiring understanding across pages; tests long-range textual grounding

name: SlidesVQA
format: Slide presentations with questions requiring understanding of slide content, layout, and text; tests fine-grained visual grounding in presentations

name: FUNSD
format: Noisy scanned forms with questions requiring understanding of form structure, entity linking, and spatial relationships between text fields
metric: ANLS (for VQA task), F1 for entity extraction

name: CORD
format: Scanned receipts with structured key-value fields (menu items, prices, totals) for post-OCR parsing and information extraction

name: SciQ
format: 4-choice science questions from biology, physics, chemistry, and earth science

name: ArenaHard
format: Real-world user queries with reference answers for LLM evaluation

name: GeneralThought
format: Text reasoning problems with model reasoning traces; spans multiple domains and task types
metric: N/A (reasoning trace dataset); correctness evaluated via AlpacaEval

name: ClaimSpect
format: Real-world biomedical and geopolitical nuanced claims converted to questions for reasoning evaluation

name: BLAB
format: Long-form audio reasoning tasks for audio-language models

name: MMAU-Pro
format: Deep reasoning in speech, audio, music, and their mix

name: Zebra-CoT
format: Vision-language reasoning traces with chain-of-thought; real-world traces from online math/physics/coding/chess + synthetic VLM-generated traces

name: Aesthetic-Eval@4096
format: 4K text-to-image generation evaluated with multiple metrics: FID, HPSv3, PickScore, ArtiMuse, CLIP Score, Q-Align, MUSIQ
metric: FID (lower better), HPSv3 (higher better), PickScore (higher better), ArtiMuse (higher better), CLIP Score (higher better), Q-Align (higher better), MUSIQ (higher better)

name: MultiAspect-4K-1M
format: 4K images with VLM-based quality/aesthetic scores (Q-Align, ArtiMuse), bilingual captions (English/Chinese via Gemini-2.5-Flash + Hunyuan-MT-7B), classical IQA signals (flatness, Shannon entropy), subject tags, and character presence flags
access: Not released — must be recreated following the paper's data curation pipeline
notes: Constructed by the UltraFlux authors (arXiv:2511.18050) from ~6M source images using VLM-driven filtering (Q-Align, ArtiMuse), YOLOE-based human-centric augmentation, and bilingual captioning. Includes structured metadata for resolution- and AR-aware sampling. The single biggest blocker for reproduction.

name: TumEmo
format: Image-text pairs crawled from social media, annotated based on emotions
access: Contact authors of Yang et al. 2021 (Image-Text Multimodal Emotion Classification via Multi-View Attentional Network)

name: FI (Flickr & Instagram)
format: Images labeled with 8 emotion categories (Mikels心理学 study)

name: Emotion-6
format: Images with 6 emotion categories

name: UnbiasedEmo
format: Images with 6 emotion categories, addressing dataset bias

name: WebEmo
num_samples: ~52K images with hierarchical labels (2/7/25 emotion categories)
format: Images labeled with Parrot hierarchical emotion model (2 basic, 7 second-level, 25 fine-grained categories)

name: Emotic
num_samples: ~23K images with 26 fine-grained emotion categories + VAD ratings
format: Images with multiple emotion labels and 10-scale Valence-Arousal-Dominance ratings; requires both context and humans

name: IAPS (International Affective Picture System)
format: Standardized images with 9-scale VAD (Valence-Arousal-Dominance) ratings from psychological study

name: ABO-500
storage: ~50-100GB (multi-view RGB images, segmentation masks, physical measurements)
format: Amazon Berkeley Objects dataset — multi-view RGB images, segmentation masks, physical measurements (mass, dimensions) for consumer products. Curated 500-item subset from full ABO dataset used for physical property estimation benchmarking.
metric: ADE, ALDE, APE, MnRE (mass estimation metrics)

name: RUGD
format: RUGD (Real-Unstructured-Grassland Driving) dataset — unstructured outdoor environments for autonomous navigation. RGB images with terrain labels for off-road robotics perception.

name: RELLIS-3D
format: RELLIS-3D dataset — unstructured outdoor terrain (REEFF terrain) with multi-modal data (RGB, depth, LiDAR) and terrain annotations for off-road autonomous navigation. Includes annotated labels for different terrain types.

name: MIT Fabric Properties
format: MIT Fabric Properties dataset — physical fabric properties (stiffness, friction, etc.) paired with multi-view images. Used for stiffness estimation evaluation in PhysGS paper (arXiv:2511.18570).
metric: ADE, ALDE, APE, MnRE (stiffness estimation metrics)
access: Contact MIT researchers or see NeRF2Physics paper for dataset access

name: LAV-DF
format: Audio-visual deepfake dataset for temporal forgery localization; videos with frame-level manipulation annotations (p in {0,1}^t per frame, boundary info b)

name: AV-Deepfake1M
eval_time: hours to days for full evaluation
format: Large-scale LLM-driven audio-visual deepfake dataset for temporal forgery localization; test set labels not publicly released (evaluation via Codabench)

name: RT-MV Tenkici (RTMV)
