format: Pre-trained 3DGS assets of synthetic Lego tree scenes; used in V3DG composed scene benchmarks
metric: n/a (training data); evaluated via PSNR/SSIM/FLIP in downstream rendering
license: Research use (contact V3DG authors for assets)

name: MGB-2 (Arabic Multi-Genre Broadcast)
format: Arabic broadcast audio with transcriptions; MSA with dialectal mix; from MGB challenges (Ali et al., 2016b)
notes: Part of Arabic Multi-Genre Broadcast challenges. Used in paper 2511.18774 for MSA ASR evaluation.

name: MGB-3 (Egyptian Dialect Broadcast)
num_samples: ~6 hours of Egyptian dialect Arabic speech
format: Egyptian dialect broadcast audio with transcriptions; from MGB-3 challenge (Ali et al., 2017)
notes: External dialectal evaluation data in paper 2511.18774. Egyptian dialect is substantially different from MSA.

name: MGB-5 (Moroccan Dialect Broadcast)
num_samples: ~6 hours of Moroccan dialect Arabic speech
format: Moroccan dialect (Darija) broadcast audio with transcriptions; from MGB-5 challenge (Ali et al., 2019)
notes: External dialectal evaluation data in paper 2511.18774. Moroccan dialect is highly divergent from MSA with heavy code-switching.

name: Casa-Dialects
format: Conversational Arabic speech from YouTube local TV series; 5 dialects: Algerian (ALG), Jordanian (JOR), Palestinian (PAL), Emirati (UAE), Yemeni (YEM); native speaker annotations
license: Research use (in-house data from Waheed et al., 2024a)
notes: In-house dataset from paper 2511.18774 covering underrepresented Arabic dialects. Represents 4 major regions: North African, Levantine, Gulf, and Yemeni. Not publicly released; requires request to authors.

name: LaMP (Large Language Model Personalization)
num_samples: ~5000 users across 7 tasks (paper uses 5: LaMP-1 to LaMP-5)
format: Text-based user personalization tasks: binary/multi-class classification, regression, text generation, with user historical interaction data
metric: Accuracy, F1, MAE, RMSE, ROUGE-1, ROUGE-L (task-dependent)

name: ResearchQA
format: Long-form open-ended scientific research QA requiring synthesis over up-to-date scientific literature; responses evaluated using human-written rubrics

name: AstaBench-ScholarQA-CS2 (SQAv2)
format: Scientific literature synthesis benchmark requiring multi-paragraph reports with citations; evaluates rubric coverage, answer precision, citation precision/recall
metric: Rubric score, Answer score, Citation precision, Citation recall
access: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.21652 (Bragg et al., 2025) or https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.14199 (Asai et al., 2024)

name: SearchArena
format: 24K real-world conversations between users and search-augmented LLMs across diverse domains; used as SFT/RL training prompts

name: OpenScholar
format: 55K scientific research-oriented queries collected from a deep research assistant demo; used as SFT/RL training prompts

name: RaR (Rubrics as Rewards)
format: Dataset of rubric-based RL prompts from Gunjal et al. (2025); used to enhance data diversity in RL training

name: GeneticDiseasesQA
format: 47 questions derived from expert-curated information about 24 disease-causing genetic variants; centered on gene therapy eligibility assessment; requires evidence attribution
metric: Final Answer (whether expert-annotated facts mentioned), Evidence Quality, Evidence Synthesis, Evidence Support

name: RIST (Real Image Sequence Trajectories)
num_samples: ~1,000+ images across 28 trajectories (AutoDriving: 15 trajectories x 5 categories x 10 images; RoboTasking: 13 trajectories x 2 categories x 10 images)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on number of targets and models evaluated
format: Sequential image frames (1920x1080 JPG for AutoDriving, 320x180 JPG for RoboTasking) with fine-grained semantic category labels and contextually-relevant target action annotations per category
metric: Attack Success Rate (ASR) — token match in content and order between output and target
license: Research use (to be released by authors)
notes: Introduced in SAUP/Semantic Router paper (arXiv:2511.20002). Curated from OpenDV-2K, ONCE (AutoDriving) and DROID (RoboTasking). Designed as fine-grained semantic stress test for semantic-aware universal perturbations against MLLM-based agents.

name: BrushBench
eval_time: minutes to hours for full evaluation
format: Natural and artificial images with human-annotated segmentation-based masks and captions. Used for image inpainting evaluation.
metric: SSIM, LPIPS, FID, PSNR, HPS v2, IR, AS, CLIP

name: VLMBlinds
format: Visual perception VQA with multiple-choice questions testing robustness and low-level visual understanding
notes: VLMBlinds benchmark evaluates VLM perception robustness. Used in CodeV paper (arXiv:2511.19661) to test primitive perception tasks. Compares tool-using and non-tool-using VLMs on visual question answering requiring fine-grained perception.

name: HRBench-4K
format: High-resolution images (up to 4K) with visual question answering; tasks include fine-grained visual search, localization, and attribute recognition
metric: VQA accuracy, FSP accuracy, FCP accuracy
notes: High-resolution image perception benchmark (4K) from Wang et al. AAAI 2025. Part of HRBench suite (HRBench-4K, HRBench-8K) testing MLLMs on fine-grained visual reasoning at high resolution. FSP = Fine-grained Search Performance, FCP = Fine-grained Classification Performance. Used in CodeV paper (arXiv:2511.19661).

name: HRBench-8K
format: High-resolution images (up to 8K) with visual question answering; tasks include fine-grained visual search, localization, and attribute recognition at extreme resolution
metric: VQA accuracy, FSP accuracy, FCP accuracy
notes: High-resolution image perception benchmark (8K) from Wang et al. AAAI 2025. Part of HRBench suite testing MLLMs on fine-grained visual reasoning at extreme resolution. More challenging than HRBench-4K due to higher resolution. Used in CodeV paper (arXiv:2511.19661).

name: MathVision-Mini
format: Visual math competition problems with visual context and reasoning requirements
notes: Mini variant of MathVision (MATH-Vision) benchmark used in CodeV paper (arXiv:2511.19661) for math reasoning evaluation. MathVision is a benchmark of math competition problems with visual context across 16 mathematical disciplines.

name: RMVDB (Robust Multi-View Depth Benchmark)
num_samples: image tuples from KITTI, ETH3D, ScanNet, DTU, Tanks&Temples
storage: not disclosed (uses subsets of underlying datasets)
format: Posed multi-view RGB image tuples with metric depth ground truth for depth and 3D reconstruction evaluation

name: MultiPathQA
eval_time: hours (per model, depending on API-based or local inference)
format: WSI-level multiple-choice visual question-answering across five diagnostic tasks: organ classification (GTEx, 20-way), cancer diagnosis (TCGA, 30-way), cancer grading (PANDA, 6-way), SlideBenchVQA (197 questions), and ExpertVQA (128 pathologist-authored questions). Questions require multi-scale spatial reasoning over gigapixel WSIs.
license: Research use (benchmark released on HuggingFace; underlying WSI data governed by TCGA/GTEx/PANDA access agreements)
access: Released on HuggingFace (exact URL not provided in paper; mentioned as publicly available)
notes: MultiPathQA: New benchmark from GIANT paper (arXiv:2511.19652). Introduced to evaluate LMMs on WSI VQA. Includes five tasks: ExpertVQA (128 pathologist-authored questions on 76 TCGA WSIs), TCGA Cancer Diagnosis (221 questions), GTEx Organ Classification (191 questions), PANDA Grading (197 questions), SlideBenchVQA (197 questions from SlideChat pipeline). ExpertVQA is the first pathologist-authored WSI VQA benchmark.

name: ExpertVQA
num_samples: 128 multiple-choice questions from 76 TCGA WSIs covering 20 diagnostic categories
eval_time: hours per model depending on inference method
format: Pathologist-authored WSI-level VQA benchmark. Questions written by two practicing pathologists (one resident, one attending) requiring direct image interpretation and multi-scale spatial reasoning. Each question has 4 multiple-choice options and verified correct label. Covers 20 diagnostic categories.
license: TCGA data use agreement; benchmark released on HuggingFace
access: Released on HuggingFace as part of MultiPathQA (arXiv:2511.19652)
notes: ExpertVQA: The first pathologist-authored WSI VQA benchmark, introduced in the GIANT paper (arXiv:2511.19652). Questions require the model to navigate and interpret WSIs directly, mirroring how pathologists examine slides. 76 unique TCGA WSIs from 76 patients across 20 diagnostic categories. On ExpertVQA, GPT-5 with GIANT achieves 62.5% accuracy, outperforming TITAN (43.8%) and SlideChat (37.5%).

name: GTEx (Histology Slides)
num_samples: ~25,713 histology slides from ~980 non-diseased donors across 30+ organ types
eval_time: hours for WSI processing and feature extraction
format: H&E histology slides from non-diseased donor tissues across multiple organ types. All slides underwent quality control for tissue integrity, autolysis, and processing artifacts. Used for organ classification (20-way) in MultiPathQA.
license: dbGaP access required; GTEx data use agreement
notes: GTEx (Genotype-Tissue Expression) project provides histology slides from non-diseased donor tissues. Used in GIANT paper (arXiv:2511.19652) for the MultiPathQA organ classification task (20-way classification). Paper used 191 GTEx WSIs from 173 donors. Requires dbGaP data access agreement.

name: Toys4K
num_samples: ~4000 user-created 3D toy objects (paper uses 500 after cleaning)
format: User-created 3D toy objects rendered with random camera poses and Poly Haven HDRI lighting. Used for single-image 3D generation evaluation.
metric: PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS (2D); Chamfer Distance/F-score (3D geometry); Symmetry F1
access: https://github.com/stStojanov/shape-disentanglement (original); cleaned version used in Cue3D paper (arXiv:2511.22121)
notes: Toys4K is a dataset of user-created 3D toy objects from Stojanov et al. (CVPR 2021). Used in Cue3D paper (arXiv:2511.22121) alongside GSO for evaluating single-image 3D generation methods. The paper manually removes geometrically trivial objects (e.g., boxes) and balances over-represented categories, resulting in 500 objects for evaluation.

name: Zeroverse
num_samples: procedurally generated (paper uses subset from GSO-like objects)
format: Procedurally generated combinations of textured primitive shapes (cubes, spheres, cylinders, etc.) with rich local geometric detail but no semantic meaning. Designed to test shape meaningfulness in single-image 3D generation.
metric: PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS (2D); Chamfer Distance/F-score (3D geometry); Symmetry F1
notes: Zeroverse is a procedurally generated dataset from LRM-zero paper (arXiv:2406.03476), consisting of random assemblies of textured primitive shapes. Significantly deviates from the training distribution of single-image 3D methods. Used in Cue3D paper (arXiv:2511.22121) to test how shape meaningfulness affects generalization. All methods collapse on Zeroverse with distinct failure modes.

name: VLABench
format: Language-conditioned robotics manipulation tasks requiring visual grounding, commonsense reasoning, and multi-step planning; evaluates selection tasks (Select Toy, Select Fruit, Select Painting, Select Poker, Select Mahjong) and physical reasoning
notes: Large-scale benchmark for language-conditioned robotics manipulation with long-horizon reasoning tasks (Zhang et al., arXiv:2412.18194). 100 task categories covering grid texture perception, spatial reasoning, commonsense/world knowledge, semantic understanding, and physical laws. Used in E_0 paper (arXiv:2511.21542) as a primary evaluation benchmark alongside LIBERO and ManiSkill.

name: Prompt2Sign
format: British Sign Language (BSL) videos with parallel English text prompts for multi-channel sign language production. Used in adversarial training and sign language generation papers.
access: https://github.com/yz-LiuHai/Prompt2Sign (referenced in Saunders et al. BMVC 2020)
notes: Saunders, Camgoz, Bowden, BMVC 2020. Used as benchmark in EASL (arXiv 2511.22135) paper alongside PHOENIX14T.

name: REFINEBENCH
num_samples: 1,000 problems across 11 domains with 9,898 checklist items (avg 9.9 per problem)
eval_time: hours per model (5 turns, both self-refinement and guided refinement settings)
format: Multi-turn refinement benchmark with checklist-based evaluation; supports self-refinement (no feedback), guided refinement (full checklist feedback), and partially guided refinement (partial feedback); evaluator LM (GPT-4.1) assesses responses against binary checklist items
metric: Pass_t (all checklist items correct = 1, else 0) and Acc_t (ratio of correct checklist items); both reported per turn t=1..5
notes: Novel benchmark evaluating LLM refinement capability (self-refinement vs guided refinement) across Math (32%), Humanities/Social Science (19%), Statistics (16%), Law (14%), Physics (7%), CS/AI (5%), Chemistry (2%), Other (2%), Engineering (1%), Biology/Medicine (1%), Economics/Business (1%). Key finding: frontier models achieve only 29-31% on self-refinement but 90%+ on guided refinement, indicating they cannot self-refine effectively without explicit feedback.

name: QuickBird-2 Pansharpening Benchmark
num_samples: Standard benchmark subset (multiple panchromatic + multispectral image pairs)
format: Panchromatic (high-res, ~0.6m GSD) + multispectral (lower-res, ~2.4m GSD) satellite image pairs for pansharpening evaluation; reduced-resolution and full-resolution evaluation protocols
metric: PSNR, SSIM, ERGAS, SAM, SCC, Q8, HQNR
access: http://www.reseaustarch.space.cn/Dataset.html or standard pansharpening benchmarks (Vivone et al. IEEE Geoscience 2020)
notes: Standard pansharpening benchmark using QuickBird-2 satellite data. Used in SP-I2I paper (arXiv:2511.22668) for evaluating unpaired pansharpening against paired methods (DCPNet, CANConv, PanCrafter). QuickBird-2 provides 4-band multispectral (R,G,B,NIR) at ~2.4m and panchromatic at ~0.6m GSD.

name: GF-2 (Gaofen-2) Pansharpening Benchmark
num_samples: Standard benchmark subset (multiple PAN + MS image pairs from GF-2 satellite)
format: Panchromatic (high-res) + multispectral (lower-res) image pairs from China's Gaofen-2 Earth observation satellite for pansharpening evaluation; 64x64 MS crops with 256x256 PAN crops per standard protocol
metric: PSNR, SSIM, ERGAS, SAM, SCC, Q4, HQNR
notes: GF-2 (Gaofen-2) is China's high-resolution Earth observation satellite with 1m panchromatic and 4m multispectral bands. Used in SP-I2I paper (arXiv:2511.22668) as secondary pansharpening benchmark. The paper notes training uses small 64x64 MS / 256x256 PAN crops which limits semantic context for unpaired methods.

name: JunoCam2HST
num_samples: 9421 JunoCam images + 5936 HST OPAL images (256x256 crops from 16000x16000 projected tiles)
storage: ~100-500GB estimated (12-bit JunoCam strips + 16000x16000 projected tiles + 256x256 crops)
eval_time: Minutes for evaluation on Perijove 18 held-out set
format: Unpaired image pairs: high-resolution uncalibrated JunoCam source images (256x256 crops) and lower-resolution calibrated HST OPAL target images (256x256 crops). No spatial/temporal correspondence between domains. Spans 10 latitudinal zones of Jupiter.
metric: SSIM, PSNR (spatial fidelity vs source); chi^2 (spectral fidelity vs target)
license: Public NASA data (JunoCam raw, HST OPAL); dataset to be released upon publication
access: Promised upon publication at arxiv.org/xxxxx (no URL at submission time)
notes: Custom dataset from SP-I2I paper (arXiv:2511.22668) for photometric calibration of JunoCam using HST as calibration reference. JunoCam lacks absolute photometric calibration; HST OPAL provides calibrated reference. Training: Perijoves 16,17,19,20,21,22 + HST Cycle 26. Test: Perijove 18. Significant preprocessing required: 12-bit decompanding, jitter correction, temporal alignment, cylindrical projection, Gaussian high-pass flattening.

name: FMA-small (Free Music Archive)
format: MP3 audio files across 8 genres
notes: Used in arXiv:2511.21577 (HarmonicAttack) for cross-domain audio watermark removal evaluation. Musical content provides diverse spectral structure for testing watermark transfer from speech to music domains.

name: OpenSafari
num_samples: 11,481 training clips + 787 test clips (from ~12K curated FPV drone videos)
storage: ~500GB-1TB estimated (720p FPV drone videos at 24fps, 15s per video)
format: In-the-wild FPV drone videos with rigorously verified camera trajectories (COLMAP SfM poses); multi-stage geometric and kinematic validation; captions via Qwen2.5-VL-7B
metric: FVD, LPIPS (video quality); MEt3R, Reconstruction-Rate (3D consistency); AUC@30, AUC@15, CosSim (trajectory following)
notes: Curated by Chou et al. (2025) for camera-controlled video generation research. Emphasizes aggressive 6-DoF FPV motion, strong parallax, complex outdoor layouts — differs from existing benchmarks (RealEstate10K, Minecraft) that focus on slow/indoor motion. Dataset not yet publicly released at paper time.

name: MegaUnScene
num_samples: 476 Internet scenes (UnScenePairs: 3,883 pairs across 458 scenes; UnScenePairs-t: 2,432 pairs across 387 scenes; UnSceneRecon: 100 reconstructions across 96 scenes with metric scale)
storage: ~100-200GB estimated (476 scenes with multiple images and reconstructions)
format: Unconstrained Internet photo collections with COLMAP SfM poses and depth maps. Three test sets: (1) UnScenePairs: rotational motion pairs with K=5 mutual nearest neighbors, categorized Large/Small/None overlap; (2) UnScenePairs-t: pairs with larger camera translations (K=50); (3) UnSceneRecon: 100 reconstructions with human-annotated metric scale via Google Maps cross-reference.
metric: MRE (Median Rotation Error in degrees), RA15/RA30 (Rotation Accuracy at 15/30 degree thresholds), MTE (Median Translation Error), ACC/CMP (Accuracy/Completeness in meters for reconstruction)
notes: MegaUnScene: New benchmark from Emergent Extreme-View Geometry in 3D Foundation Models paper (arXiv:2511.22686). Curated from Internet scenes unseen by existing 3DFMs (MegaScenes excluded). Enables systematic evaluation of 3DFMs under unconstrained, in-the-wild conditions for both extreme relative pose estimation and dense 3D reconstruction. Scenes sourced from Wikimedia Commons with Doppelgangers++ and MASt3R-SfM for reconstruction.

name: sELP (extreme Landmark Pairs)
format: Curated image pairs from MegaDepth with minimal to no visual overlap, annotated with COLMAP SfM ground-truth relative poses. Subdivided into Large, Small, and None overlap categories.
metric: MRE (Median Rotation Error in degrees), RA15/RA30 (Rotation Accuracy at 15/30 degree thresholds), MTE (Median Translation Error)
access: From Bezalel et al. CVPR 2025 (https://github.com/han治安l/expler)
notes: sELP (extreme Landmark Pairs): Benchmark for extreme rotation estimation in the wild, introduced by Bezalel et al. CVPR 2025. Derived from MegaDepth with image pairs curated for non-overlapping or minimal-overlap conditions. Previously SOTA was ExRot. The Emergent Extreme-View Geometry paper (arXiv:2511.22686) establishes new SOTA on this benchmark with fine-tuned 3DFMs.

name: CruxEval-Output
format: Code execution reasoning: predict function output given input
notes: CruxEval: LLM code execution reasoning benchmark from ByteIR. Tests forward reasoning (predict output from input). Used in Verified-Code-CoT paper (arXiv:2512.00127) to evaluate trace-grounded CoT training. Base Qwen2.5-Coder-7B achieves 45.3% on this benchmark.

name: CruxEval-Input
format: Code execution reasoning: predict function input given output
notes: CruxEval: LLM code execution reasoning benchmark from ByteIR. Tests backward reasoning (predict input from output). Used in Verified-Code-CoT paper (arXiv:2512.00127) to evaluate trace-grounded CoT training. Base Qwen2.5-Coder-7B achieves 47.5% on this benchmark.

name: WebUOT-1M
num_samples: 1M+ frames, large-scale underwater object tracking benchmark
format: Underwater video sequences with bounding box annotations for single object tracking; covers diverse marine organisms, vehicles, and objects across varying water conditions and depths
metric: Success AUC, Precision AUC, mIoU, CSC, GAS

name: UOT32
format: Challenging underwater tracking sequences featuring fish, divers, and underwater equipment across environments with varying visibility
metric: Success AUC, Precision AUC, mIoU, CSC, GAS

name: UTB180
format: High-quality underwater tracking sequences emphasizing difficult cases such as poor visibility, color distortion, and occlusion by marine life
metric: Success AUC, Precision AUC, mIoU, CSC, GAS

name: UW-COT-220
format: Underwater camouflaged object tracking sequences spanning diverse lighting, clarity, and object categories
metric: Success AUC, Precision AUC, mIoU, CSC, GAS

name: Brackish MOT
num_samples: Multiple video sequences in brackish water environments
format: Multi-object tracking dataset in brackish water with bounding box annotations; supports MOT evaluation in addition to SOT

name: InterBench
format: Curated test set of 100 images with interaction prompts covering Environmental Interactions (weather, physical events), Actor Actions (primitive/composite), and Entity & Object Appearances (animals, vehicles, humans). Evaluates interaction fidelity using VLM-based scoring.
metric: Trigger Rate (binary), Align, Fluency, Scope, End-State, Physics (all multi-level ordinal)

name: TRANSIENTTABLES
num_samples: 3,971 questions, 14,000+ tables, 1,238 entities across multiple time periods
eval_time: minutes to hours (depending on API inference speed)
format: Temporal question answering over evolving Wikipedia infobox timelines. Questions require temporal reasoning across multiple table snapshots (e.g., 'Who was India\'s cricket captain before Rohit Sharma?', 'How many Tests did India play between 2020 and 2023?'). Domains include countries, cricket teams, cricketers, economy, equestrian, government agencies, table tennis players, golfers, field hockey, and riders.
notes: Introduced by Shankarampeta et al. (2025). Evaluates LLMs on temporally evolving semistructured tables from Wikipedia infoboxes. The best baseline (Gemini-2.5-Pro with IRE+CoT) achieves 68.89 EM. This paper (Evidence-Guided Schema Normalization) achieves 80.39 EM using text-to-SQL approach with normalized 3NF schemas.

name: Jester
format: Short video clips of human hand gestures, crowdsourced to evaluate fine-grained temporal motion sensitivity

name: ARID
format: RGB-D videos captured in low-light conditions for action recognition robustness testing

name: IARD
num_samples: ~500 videos (5 actors x 5 actions x multiple viewpoints)
format: Controlled recordings of 5 actors performing 5 actions from multiple viewpoints; designed for identity-invariant and viewpoint-invariant motion understanding

name: MoM (Melody or Machine)
storage: ~120-200GB (estimated: 130k songs at ~30s avg length, 24kHz stereo audio)
eval_time: hours (F1 evaluation on full test set)
format: Full-song audio files (MP3/AAC), 24kHz, trimmed to 90s; three tiers: Real (65,475 songs), Fully Fake (53,922 songs), Mostly Fake (real lyrics + AI audio, voice clones)
metric: F1 score, Accuracy (primary metric: F1 for imbalanced OOD test sets)
license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (synthetic songs); YouTube links for real songs (no redistribution)
notes: Largest and most diverse synthetic music detection benchmark. Key innovation: dedicated OOD test set (Riffusion, Suno v4, Suno v3, Yue, Voice Clones) distinct from training set (Suno v3.5, Udio v1.5, Diffrythm, Suno v2). 82% English, multilingual songs. Includes human cover songs to challenge natural stylistic variations. Human evaluation ELO: MoM synthetic tracks (1016.35 avg) outperform SONICS (894.60). Authors demonstrate prior SOTA (SpecTTTra) drops to 53-69% F1 on OOD content. From arXiv:2512.00621.

name: SONICS
eval_time: hours (F1 evaluation on full test set)
format: Full-song audio, 16kHz, English songs with male vocal bias
notes: Prior SOTA synthetic music detection benchmark. ~97k songs evenly split real/synthetic from Suno v2-v3.5 and Udio v32/v130. Shows saturation: multiple top models achieve near-perfect scores (~0.97+ F1). Lacks multilingual content, has male vocal bias, only 2 generators. Used as comparison baseline in MoM paper. From Rahman et al. (2025).

name: RH20T
num_samples: over 110,000 robot manipulation sequences, ~20TB total data, ~50M+ image frames
format: Multi-modal: RGB, depth, force/torque, audio, low-level robot state and action signals, synchronized human demonstration videos, language descriptions
notes: Robot-Human demonstration in 20TB (Fang et al., 2023). Large-scale real-world robotic manipulation dataset with 140+ tasks. Used in AFRO paper (2512.00074) for out-of-domain pretraining on a Franka subset.

name: Brainweb
num_samples: 20 T1-weighted brain MR volumes, 362 slices each; 10/5/5 train/val/test split by volume
format: Simulated T1-weighted brain MR images with ground truth; supports arbitrary undersampling patterns for CS-MRI evaluation

name: MRBrainS13
num_samples: 20 MR imaging cases (T1-weighted); 5/7/8 train/val/test split; 48 slices per volume
format: T1-weighted brain MR images; supports arbitrary undersampling patterns for CS-MRI evaluation

name: Market-1501
format: Person re-identification images with identity labels and camera IDs

name: SYSU-MM01
format: Visible-infrared person re-identification images with identity labels

name: Occluded-ReID
format: Occluded person re-identification images with identity labels

name: MARS
format: Video-based person re-identification tracklets with identity labels

name: HITSZ-VCM
format: Visible-infrared cross-modality video person re-identification

name: PersonSyn
num_samples: Large-scale (derived from Market-1501, MSMT17, SYSU-MM01, Occluded-ReID, MARS, HITSZ-VCM)
format: Multi-reference controllable pedestrian generation dataset with 2D/3D poses, disentangled backgrounds, viewpoint labels, textual attributes, reference image sets

name: EgoLifeQA
eval_time: Hours for full evaluation with retrieval
format: Week-long egocentric video with QA requiring recalling events, tracking objects, and reasoning over long-term activities. Five categories: EntityLog, EventRecall, HabitInsight, RelationMap, TaskMaster.
access: https://github.com/EGO-LLM/EgoLife (based on Yang et al., CVPR 2025)
notes: From Yang et al., 2025 (EgoLife paper). Tests models' capability to understand and remember everyday life from week-long video recordings. Same video as Ego-R1 Bench but different question formulation.

name: Ego-R1 Bench
eval_time: Hours for full evaluation with retrieval
format: Week-long egocentric video with multi-step tool-augmented reasoning QA. Same video as EgoLifeQA but focuses on reasoning chains. Five categories: EntityLog, EventRecall, HabitInsight, RelationMap, TaskMaster.
notes: From Tian et al., 2025 (Ego-R1 Bench paper). Targets multi-step tool-augmented reasoning over ultra-long egocentric video. Uses same 44.3h video as EgoLifeQA.

name: HippoVlog
num_samples: 1,000 multiple-choice QA pairs across 25 vlog videos
eval_time: Hours for full evaluation with retrieval
format: Daily vlog videos requiring continuous audiovisual event understanding. Four categories: Auditory (reasoning over audio/transcript), Visual (visual content), Auditory+Visual (cross-modality), Summarization (long-term synthesis).
notes: From Lin et al., 2025 (HippoVlog paper). Evaluates multimodal (audio+visual) understanding over ~27min vlog videos. Tests both modality-specific and cross-modality reasoning.

name: olmOCR-Bench
format: end-to-end document parsing evaluation across diverse document types (ArXiv, scans, tables, etc.)

name: XDocParse
eval_time: hours per model for full multilingual evaluation
format: real-world documents spanning 126 languages for end-to-end multilingual parsing evaluation
metric: Overall Edit, Text Edit, Formula Edit, Table TEDS, Table Edit, Reading Order Edit

name: MMLU-redux
format: 4-choice MC (curated subset of MMLU with corrected labels)
notes: Curated subset of MMLU with corrected labels. Used in arXiv:2512.02807 (SR-GRPO) for STEM evaluation.

name: H2U3D
num_samples: 31k QA pairs across 900 HM3D scenes (30k train, 1k val); plus 9k CoT reasoning samples
storage: HM3D: ~15-20GB; H2U3D annotations: <100MB; Habitat-Sim rendered images: variable (regeneratable)
format: 3D Visual Question Answering for house-scale multi-floor indoor environments. Questions categorized into 6 types: Position (35.5%), Color (31.6%), Material (15.6%), Counting (13.3%), Shape (3%), State (3%). Each sample includes multi-floor BEV images, hierarchical zoomed regions, close-up rendered views, and chain-of-thought reasoning traces.

name: MindCube
format: Multiple-choice questions testing spatial reasoning by reconstructing spatial mental models from limited views
notes: MindCube (Yin et al., ICCV 2025 workshop): spatial reasoning benchmark testing LLM ability to construct internal spatial mental models from partial views. Categories include Around, Among, and Rotation types. Paper evaluates on tiny split (~1K samples). Used in Argos paper (arXiv:2512.03438) to evaluate spatial reasoning.

name: EmbodiedBench
num_samples: ~300 test samples for EB-Alfred; not disclosed for EB-Habitat
format: High-level task completion and planning in AI2-THOR (Alfred) and Habitat 2.0 (Habitat) environments; tests agent ability to compose and execute skills like pick up, open, slice, find objects
notes: EmbodiedBench (Yang et al., 2025): comprehensive benchmarking suite for vision-driven embodied agents spanning AI2-THOR and Habitat 2.0. EB-Alfred sub-task evaluates high-level task completion across Base, Commonsense, Complex, Visual, Spatial, and Long-horizon categories. EB-Habitat focuses on object rearrangement based on language queries. Used in Argos paper (arXiv:2512.03438).

name: EB-Alfred
num_samples: ~300 test samples (evenly split across Base, Commonsense, Complex, Visual, Spatial, Long-horizon)
format: High-level household task planning and completion in AI2-THOR; agents compose skills (pick up, open, slice, find) to complete multi-step tasks
notes: EB-Alfred sub-task of EmbodiedBench. Tests agent ability to compose and execute high-level skills over diverse household tasks. 6 categories: Base, Commonsense, Complex, Visual, Spatial, Long-horizon. Used in Argos paper (arXiv:2512.03438) where Argos achieves 24.7% on Complex vs 16.7% for Video-R1.

name: EB-Habitat
format: High-level object rearrangement based on language queries in Habitat 2.0 simulator
notes: EB-Habitat sub-task of EmbodiedBench. Focuses on high-level object rearrangement in the Habitat 2.0 environment. Used in Argos paper (arXiv:2512.03438) for embodied task planning evaluation alongside EB-Alfred.

name: CounterCurate
format: Hard positive/negative image-caption pairs for evaluating ambiguous spatial relations; curated from Flickr30K using GPT-4V and DALL-E 3 to generate semantically plausible but incorrect captions/images
notes: CounterCurate (Zhang et al., 2024): designed to evaluate physical and semantic visio-linguistic compositional reasoning through counterfactual examples. Tests models' ability to differentiate correct vs incorrect spatial relations. Used in Argos paper (arXiv:2512.03438) where Argos achieves 85.3% vs 61.4% for base Qwen2.5-VL-7B — a 20%+ gain.

name: NGSIM US Highway 101
format: Vehicle trajectory data (position, velocity, heading at 10Hz); 640m highway section with 5 main lanes + 1 auxiliary lane

name: BABEL
num_samples: ~2500 sequences, ~64 hours of motion from AMASS with frame-level action labels
format: 3D human motion from AMASS with frame-level action labels (e.g., 'walk turn jump'). Long sequences segmented and annotated for multi-action streaming evaluation.
metric: FID, R-Precision, Diversity, MM-Dist, PJ, AUJ
notes: Action-centric annotation of AMASS motion. Used for streaming motion generation evaluation where text prompts change within sequences. From CVPR 2021 (Punnakkal et al.).

name: Natural Questions (NQ)
format: Real Google natural language queries with Wikipedia answers; requires identifying the answer span within a Wikipedia article

name: Musique
format: Multi-hop questions requiring reasoning over multiple facts from different paragraphs; built by composing single-hop questions from TriviaQA and WebQuestions

name: Drag100
format: Extended drag editing benchmark with 100 diverse images. Evaluates drag accuracy using DAI (Drag Accuracy Index) at different threshold gamma values (1, 5, 10, 20) and GScore, complementing DragBench's MD metric.
notes: Introduced by DragDiffusion (Shi et al., CVPR 2024). Used alongside DragBench for comprehensive evaluation of drag-based editing methods. GScore averages DAI across gamma thresholds 1, 5, 10, 20.

name: AVSpeech
format: Audio-visual speaker talking-head clips. Speaker-independent audio-visual model for speech separation. Used as training data for Live Avatar (arXiv:2512.04677) after filtering for clips >10s.

name: GenBench
num_samples: GenBench-ShortVideo: 100 test samples (~10s each); GenBench-LongVideo: 15 test videos (each >5 minutes)
format: Synthetic benchmark for audio-driven avatar generation created using Gemini-2.5 Pro, Qwen-Image, and CosyVoice. Diverse character styles: photorealistic humans, animated characters, anthropomorphic non-humans. Views: frontal, profile, half-body, full-body.
metric: ASE (aesthetic), IQA (perceptual quality), Sync-C/Sync-D (audio-visual sync), Dino-S (identity consistency)
notes: Benchmark introduced in Live Avatar paper (arXiv:2512.04677) for standardized evaluation of long-form avatar generation. GenBench-ShortVideo tests 10s clips; GenBench-LongVideo tests 5+ minute videos for long-horizon stability.

name: PFL-DocVQA
num_samples: 336842 QA pairs on 117661 pages (36916 documents from 6574 providers)
storage: <2GB for subset used in paper (~1000 samples with 5 QA pairs each)
format: Document images (invoices) with question-answer pairs for privacy-preserving DocVQA evaluation
license: Research (per cited paper Tito et al., ICDAR 2024)
notes: Privacy-aware DocVQA dataset from Tito et al. (ICDAR 2024). Contains real invoices. Paper used a subset of N=1000 samples with M=5 QA pairs each. The full dataset was used for privacy attack evaluation; authors merged Blue Team/Red Team splits.

name: VL-RewardBench
num_samples: Not fully disclosed (spans general multimodal instructions, hallucination detection, and complex reasoning tasks)
format: Preference pairs for evaluating VLM judges across dimensions: general instructions, hallucination detection, reasoning, VQA. Combines human-verified and AI-annotated preference labels.
notes: From Li et al. (2025b). Used in paper 2512.05145 (Self-Improving VLM Judges) as primary evaluation benchmark. Paper reports base model 0.383 → iteration 4: 0.538 accuracy.

name: Multimodal RewardBench
num_samples: 5,211 preference pairs covering both long-form and short-answer formats
format: Preference pairs with labels derived from ground-truth correctness or high-quality human expert annotations. Evaluates VLM judges across dimensions: general, knowledge, reasoning, safety, VQA.
notes: From Yasunaga et al. (2025). Also known as MMRB in paper 2512.05145. Paper reports base model 0.499 → iteration 4: 0.539 accuracy.

name: TexVerse
storage: TexVerse 4K and 8K subsets (larger than standard Objaverse renders)
format: 3D objects with high-resolution textures (4K and 8K), used for fine-grained local detail refinement evaluation

name: MJHQ-5K
format: Aesthetic-quality-oriented text-to-image generation benchmark; 5K prompts for evaluating FID, ImageReward, CLIPQA, CLIPScore, PSNR
metric: FID (lower is better), ImageReward (higher is better), CLIPScore (higher is better)
notes: MJHQ benchmark (Zhang et al., ICCV 2023); 5K subset used for T2I evaluation in TreeQ paper (2512.06353) with FLUX-Schnell model. Full MJHQ-30K has 30K samples.

name: DESOBAV2
num_samples: 21,575 scenes with 28,573 image tuples (27,823 training, 750 testing)
format: Composite images with foreground object masks and shadow annotations. Contains both BOS (background-object-shadow) and BOS-free settings.
notes: Shadow generation benchmark for composite images. Introduced in SGDiffusion (Liu et al., CVPR 2024). Used for evaluating physics-grounded shadow generation in arXiv:2512.06174.

name: PVF-10
num_samples: 5,579 annotated crops from 8 distinct PV plants, 10 fault classes
format: High-resolution UAV thermal and RGB crops of PV modules with 10 fine-grained fault classes (hotspots, diode issues, cell cracks, etc.)
metric: mAP@0.5, mAP@[0.5:0.95], Macro-F1, Recall, Dup-FP rate
notes: Public PV inspection benchmark from Lysyi et al. Used as primary benchmark in arXiv:2512.06504. Features multi-palette thermal data and fine-grained defect taxonomy.

name: STHS-277
num_samples: 277 full-frame thermographic images with snail-trail and hotspot annotations
format: Full-frame radiometric thermal images of PV modules with environmental metadata, annotated with bounding boxes for panel instances and defects
metric: mAP@0.5, mAP@[0.5:0.95], Macro-F1, Recall, Dup-FP rate
notes: Public PV thermography dataset. Extended with bounding box annotations in arXiv:2512.06504 for end-to-end object detection. Used as secondary benchmark alongside PVF-10.

name: Kinetix
num_samples: synthetic physics-based control tasks, generated data from mixture of expert policies
eval_time: minutes to hours for full evaluation (2048 rollouts per data point)
format: Physics-based manipulation tasks in MJX/IsaacGym; data generated by mixture of expert policies for training flow matching policies
license: MIT (code); generated data for research use
notes: Dynamic benchmark for evaluating real-time execution of action chunking flow policies. Used in RTC (arXiv:2506.07339) and training-time RTC (arXiv:2512.05964) papers. 4-layer MLP-Mixer with H=8 prediction horizon is standard architecture used in benchmarks. Evaluation uses 2048 rollouts per data point with binary success rate.

name: MFF (Multi-Focus Image Fusion Dataset)
num_samples: ~100 image pairs (grayscale and color), various resolutions
format: Multi-focus image pairs with ground truth fused images. Each pair has images focused at different distances; ground truth is the all-in-focus image.
access: Released with MFF fusion benchmark papers

name: RealMFF (Realistic Multi-Focus Dataset)
num_samples: ~60 image pairs with real multi-focus blur
format: Real multi-focus image pairs captured with optical lenses, providing more realistic blur patterns than synthetic data.
access: Released with RealMFF paper (realistic multi-focus fusion benchmark)

name: SICE (Sequence of Illuminant Exposure)
num_samples: ~600 exposure sequences, multiple images per sequence at different EV levels
format: Multi-exposure image sequences for exposure fusion. Contains images at various exposure levels (e.g., -3EV to +3EV).
access: Released with SICE multi-exposure fusion paper

name: M3FD (Multi-Modality Fusion Dataset)
format: Multi-modality fusion dataset with infrared-visible image pairs, used for fusion and downstream task evaluation.

name: Who&When (WW)
format: Multi-agent session logs with agent/step-level failure attribution annotations; used for evaluating failure localization in LLM multi-agent systems
notes: Failure attribution dataset for LLM multi-agent systems. Contains execution logs annotated with ground-truth failure agents and steps. WW-HC = Hand Crafted subset, WW-AB = AssistantBench subset, WW-GAIA = GAIA subset.

name: AssistantBench
format: Real-world web-based tasks requiring multi-step tool use and reasoning (browser automation, file manipulation, email); evaluated on multi-agent systems
notes: Benchmark for evaluating web agents on realistic, time-consuming tasks. Used in DoVer paper for failure analysis of multi-agent systems.

name: GSMPlus
format: Mathematical problem-solving benchmark evaluating LLM robustness; includes perturbations of GSM8K problems requiring multi-step reasoning
notes: Comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLM robustness as mathematical problem solvers. Used in DoVer paper for AG2-based MathChat experiments.

name: InterHuman
num_samples: Not reported in paper; multi-human MoCap dataset with fine-grained text annotations
format: Multi-human motion capture data with text annotations for two-person interactions (walking, hugging, punching, bowing, etc.)
metric: R-precision, FID, Multimodal Distance (MM Dist), Diversity, Multimodality
notes: Used in InterAgent (arXiv:2512.07410) as the primary training and evaluation dataset for physics-based multi-agent humanoid control.

name: SpatialVid
num_samples: ~7000 videos with spatial annotations (validation split used for evaluation in WorldReel paper)
format: High-quality raw videos with spatial annotations including camera poses, depth, and foreground masks. Used for 4D video generation evaluation. Filtered from Panda-70M by SpatialVid.
notes: Large-scale video dataset with spatial annotations. Used as evaluation benchmark in WorldReel (arXiv:2512.07821). Validation split contains 500 general-motion and 500 complex-motion videos for 4D generation assessment.

name: MM-CoT
eval_time: hours for full evaluation across multiple VLMs
format: Discriminative verification task: given image/video and candidate triadic event chains (A→B→C), select the unique valid chain satisfying both visual grounding and logical coherence
metric: Chain selection accuracy (strict correct/incorrect per instance)
notes: MM-CoT (Zhang et al., 2025) benchmarks visual chain-of-thought reasoning by testing whether VLMs can verify reasoning chains for visual fidelity (Φ_vis) and logical coherence (Φ_log). Distractors are adversarial, targeting one constraint violation each. Reveals gap between generative fluency and true reasoning fidelity.

name: PersonaGym
num_samples: 10k auto-generated persona-specific questions across 200 personas and 150 environments
eval_time: hours (10k questions x 3 runs per evaluation)
format: Role-playing queries with 5 evaluation dimensions: Expected Action (EA), Linguistic Habits (LH), Persona Consistency (PC), Toxicity Control (TC), Action Justification (AJ)

name: RoleMRC
format: Role-playing and instruction-following tasks across Free Chat, On-scene MRC Dialogues, Ruled Chats; 5 dimensions: Knowledge Range (KR), Style Compliance (SC), Nested Instruction-following (NI), Multi-turn Instruction-following (MT), Instruction Priority (IP)

name: OpenCharacter
format: Synthetic dialogues for role-playing agent training with diverse persona settings

name: HEAD-QA
format: Multiple-choice healthcare questions in Spanish and English (English subset used); 4 answer options per question
notes: Healthcare multi-choice Q&A dataset. Paper: Vilares and Gómez-Rodríguez, 2019. Used in AutoMedic paper (arXiv:2512.10195) for clinical conversational agent evaluation.

name: MMCNP (Middle-Mile Consolidation Network Design Problem)
num_samples: 600 instances total (480 train, 120 validation, 100 test per paper; large and hard variants)
eval_time: 1000 seconds per instance (as per paper evaluation)
format: MILP (.mps format) — parametric MIP instances varying commodity demands
license: Research use (instances to be released via Distributional MIPLIB)
access: https://github.com/caidog1129/ID-PaS; instances to be released at https://sites.google.com/usc.edu/distributional-miplib/
notes: Real-world logistics optimization: planning transportation capacity from vendors to fulfillment centers. Large setting: 50 facilities, 2000 paths, 400 arcs, 300 commodities. Hard setting: 200 facilities, 24000 paths, 1000 arcs, 6000 commodities.

name: SLAP (Strategic Locomotive Assignment Problem)
num_samples: 600 instances total (480 train, 120 validation, 100 test per paper; large and hard variants)
eval_time: 1000 seconds per instance (as per paper evaluation)
format: MILP (.mps format) — parametric MIP instances varying locomotive bound constraints
license: Research use (instances to be released via Distributional MIPLIB)
access: https://github.com/caidog1129/ID-PaS; instances to be released at https://sites.google.com/usc.edu/distributional-miplib/
notes: Real-world rail network optimization: assigning locomotives to fixed train schedules on US-wide railway network. Large setting: 1000 nodes, 40000 arcs. Hard setting: 8000 nodes, 50000 arcs.

name: Distributional MIPLIB
num_samples: Multi-domain library of parametric MIP instances
format: MILP instances in standardized format (.mps/.lp)
metric: Varies by instance type (primal gap, optimality gap, runtime)
notes: Multi-domain library of parametric MIPs for ML-guided optimization research, developed by Huang et al. (2024). MMCNP and SLAP are subsets. Instances have fixed underlying structure with varying parameters (demands, costs, capacities).

name: GenomicBenchmarks
num_samples: Not explicitly reported; eukaryotic genomes benchmark with multiple species
format: Genomic sequences with classification labels for various tasks including human vs non-human, chromosome-specific tasks, and regulatory element detection
notes: Used in Derf paper (2512.10938) for evaluating HyenaDNA and Caduceus DNA sequence models. Benchmark contains multiple genomic classification tasks of varying sequence lengths and species.

name: HEAR Benchmark
format: 21 diverse audio tasks: speech commands, emotion recognition, speaker verification, music classification, bioacoustic detection, etc. Evaluates frozen audio encoders with linear probes.
notes: Holistic Evaluation of Audio Representations (Turian et al., NeurIPS 2022). Evaluates frozen audio encoder quality via linear probe adaptability. VOCSIM paper (arXiv:2512.10120) achieves SOTA on 5/7 evaluated HEAR tasks using frozen Whisper-large-v3 embeddings with linear probes.

name: OPV-Bench
format: Math reasoning chain-of-thought verification benchmark with 2202 test cases across K-12, Highschool Competition, and Undergraduate difficulty levels; tests ability to identify the first erroneous step in summarized reasoning solutions
metric: F1, Accuracy (Precise/Approximate/Rough criteria for identifying error positions)

name: MeViSv2 (MeViS)
format: RGB video sequences with per-frame instance segmentation masks, language expressions (text + audio) referring to objects via motion descriptions, supports single-target / multi-target / no-target expressions
metric: J&F (IoU + F-measure), N-acc. (no-target accuracy), T-acc. (target accuracy)
notes: MeViS: Motion Expression Video Segmentation dataset. MeViSv2 (TPAMI 2025) is an expanded version of MeViSv1 (ICCV 2023). Supports RVOS, AVOS (audio-guided VOS), RMOT (referring multi-object tracking), and RMEG (referring motion expression generation) tasks. Key differentiator: expressions focus on motion rather than static attributes, requiring temporal reasoning.

name: Refer-YouTube-VOS
format: RGB video sequences with per-frame instance segmentation masks and referring expressions (text)
notes: Large-scale referring video object segmentation dataset based on YouTube-VOS-2019. Expressions are typically first-frame or full-video descriptions rich in static attributes. Single-target only (one expression refers to one object). Used as baseline dataset in MeViS paper (arXiv:2512.10945).

name: A2D Sentence
format: RGB video sequences with per-frame instance segmentation masks and sentence-level action descriptions
notes: A2D (Actor and Action Video Segmentation) dataset with natural language sentences. Each expression refers to an actor performing an action. Used in MeViS paper (arXiv:2512.10945) as an evaluation benchmark. Models are pre-trained on Ref-COCO/+g then fine-tuned on A2D Sentence following standard protocol.

name: J-HMDB Sentence
format: RGB video sequences (HMDB51 subset) with per-frame segmentation masks and sentence-level action descriptions
notes: J-HMDB (Joint-annotated HMDB) dataset with natural language sentences. A subset of HMDB51 with frame-level segmentation annotations and sentence descriptions. Used only for evaluation (not training) in MeViS paper (arXiv:2512.10945).

name: LongStoryEval
format: Book-level summaries with structured reviews organized by evaluation aspects, metadata (titles, genres, premises), reviewer profiles
notes: First benchmark for evaluating book-length stories (>100K tokens, avg 121K tokens). Introduces hierarchical evaluation criteria structure with 8 top-level aspects and 20 sub-aspects derived from real reader feedback on Goodreads. Due to copyright, only book-level summaries are released, not full book content.

name: Flickr8k
format: 8,000 images from Flickr with 5 human-generated captions each; commonly used for image captioning and image-to-image translation tasks
access: Widely available on HuggingFace (e.g., datasets/咯咯哒/flickr8k)
notes: Used in LoGoColor (arXiv:2512.09278) as supplementary training data for the multi-view diffusion model's color distribution learning.

name: MinneApple
num_samples: 670 images (468 train, 100 val, 102 test; ~28,179 annotated apple instances)
format: RGB images with PNG instance masks (pixel values encode instance IDs); YOLO-format polygon annotations
metric: F1-score, Precision, Recall at IoU thresholds (primary: IoU=0.15)
notes: Dense apple instance segmentation dataset from commercial orchards. Used in paper arXiv:2512.11884 (SAM3 vs YOLO11 comparison). Primary evaluation at IoU=0.15 due to dense scene characteristics.

name: 3D-GRAND
num_samples: ~142K QA pairs over diverse 3D indoor scenes
storage: Large-scale 3D scene dataset (hundreds of GB to TB scale)
format: 3D scene point clouds with spatial question-answer pairs covering embodied interaction, navigability, distance estimation, and spatial relations
metric: Binary accuracy, GPT-4 scores for open-ended generation

name: 3D-MM-Vet
num_samples: Not explicitly reported; evaluates 3D multimodal understanding across recognition, knowledge reasoning, language generation, spatial awareness, and embodied interaction
format: 3D object point clouds with embodied interaction QA; GPT-4 evaluation
metric: GPT-4 scoring for comprehensive 3D understanding assessment

name: Cap3D
format: 3D objects with natural language captions; derived from ShapeNet, Objaverse, and Amazon Basic Objects (ABO) datasets

name: MultiWOZ 2.4
num_samples: ~8,500 train dialogues, 1,000 test dialogues across 5 domains (restaurant, hotel, train, attraction, taxi)
format: Multi-turn dialogues between user and system, annotated with belief states, dialogue acts, and API calls. User goals specify constraints and requests across multiple domains.
metric: Task success rate (LLM-as-judge), Average dialogue turns
notes: Multi-domain task-oriented dialogue benchmark. Enhanced version of MultiWOZ 2.0 with annotation corrections. Used in arXiv:2512.13154 (MAC paper) for evaluating multi-agent clarification framework.

name: MedCase
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed; open-ended clinical case-based questions
format: Open-ended questions from complex real-world clinical case reports; requires multi-step diagnostic reasoning
notes: Used in MedCEG paper (arXiv:2512.13510) as in-domain benchmark. Tests multi-step clinical diagnostic reasoning from real clinical case reports. Open-ended format is more challenging than MCQ.

name: DiagArena
format: Challenging patient cases sourced from clinical reports in 10 top-tier medical journals (Lancet, NEJM, etc.); 28 medical specialties; multiple-choice and open-ended diagnostic reasoning questions
notes: DiagnosisArena (DiagArena) used in MedCEG paper (arXiv:2512.13510) as out-of-domain benchmark. Designed to mirror real-world clinical practice complexity, surpassing simplified MCQ-only medical benchmarks.

name: MMLU-H
num_samples: Varies by subset (medical subsets: Clinical Knowledge, College Medicine, Professional Medicine, Medical Genetics, College Biology, Anatomy)
format: Multiple-choice questions; medical subsets of MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2020)
notes: Medical subsets of MMLU used in MedCEG paper (arXiv:2512.13510) as out-of-domain benchmark. Tests expert-level knowledge in specialized medical and biology domains.

name: MMLU-Pro-H
num_samples: Varies by subset (medical subsets of MMLU-Pro)
format: Multiple-choice questions; health-focused subsets of MMLU-Pro (Wang et al., 2024, NeurIPS 2024)
notes: Health-focused subsets of MMLU-Pro used in MedCEG paper (arXiv:2512.13510) as out-of-domain benchmark. MMLU-Pro addresses limitations of original MMLU with domain-expert rewritten and validated questions.

name: Lightwheel
format: High-quality articulated 3D meshes with accurate articulation annotations in URDF format, spanning 13 categories (Microwave, Dishwasher, Electric Kettle, Refrigerator, Blender, Oven, Stand Mixer, Toaster, Toaster Oven, Coffee Machine, Stove, Stovetop, Range Hood)

name: V2X-Real
num_samples: 33,000 LiDAR frames, 1.2M annotated 3D bounding boxes, up to 4 agents per scene
format: Real-world multi-agent V2X cooperative perception dataset with LiDAR point clouds and 3D bounding box annotations for vehicle, pedestrian, and truck detection; supports vehicle-centric and infrastructure-centric evaluation
notes: V2X-Real is a large-scale real-world dataset for V2X cooperative perception collected using two connected automated vehicles and two smart infrastructures. The dataset includes multi-class annotations (vehicle, pedestrian, truck) and supports both V2V and I2I communication scenarios.

name: TableVisBench
eval_time: hours (depending on reflection rounds and model)
format: Table-to-infographic generation benchmark with 800 challenging instances across 5 evaluation dimensions: Data Accuracy (DA), Text Rendering (TR), Relative Relationship (RR), Additional Information Accuracy (AA), Aesthetic Quality (AQ)
metric: Composite score = (DA + TR + RR + AA + 10*AQ) / 5, range 0-100
notes: Creative table visualization benchmark evaluating models on faithful data-to-visual mapping from markdown tables to infographic images. Paper: ShowTable (arXiv:2512.13303).

name: SPARC IBD
num_samples: 3322 H&E whole slide images from intestinal mucosal biopsies
storage: Estimated hundreds of GB to TB (WSIs at high resolution)
format: H&E whole slide images (WSIs) with inflammation labels derived from macroscopic tissue appearance
license: Research (requires application to Crohn's & Colitis Foundation IBD Plexus)
access: Available upon application to Crohn's & Colitis Foundation (https://www.crohnscolitisfoundation.org/)
notes: Discovery cohort for IMILIA paper (2512.13440). Multi-centered longitudinal study of adult IBD patients. 31% prevalence of inflamed samples. Labels derived from macroscopic tissue appearance (normal / possible inflammation / severe inflammation).

name: FINBB
num_samples: 314 H&E whole slide images from Finnish biobanks
format: H&E whole slide images (WSIs) with inflammation labels from macroscopic tissue appearance
access: Access through Finnish Biobank Cooperative (FINBB) and Fingenious service (www.fingenious.fi)
notes: External validation cohort for IMILIA paper (2512.13440). 59.2% UC, 40.8% CD patients. 95% inflamed prevalence (significant label shift from discovery cohort). Samples from colon (76.4%), ileum (20%), ileum/colon intersection (1.6%).

name: IBDColEpi
num_samples: 140 H&E WSIs (132 used for external validation after excluding 8 with insufficient tissue)
eval_time: N/A (training data for EpiSeg, external validation for Chowder)
format: H&E WSIs with pixel-level epithelium annotations. 'Active' disease = presence of intraepithelial granulocytes.
metric: ROC-AUC for inflammation prediction; Average Precision for epithelium segmentation
notes: Used for EpiSeg training (epithelium segmentation) in IMILIA paper (2512.13440). 41% active disease prevalence. No UC/CD categorization provided. Spatial resolution: 0.5 micrometer per pixel (MPP) for EpiSeg training tiles (1022x1022).

name: HAM10000
format: Dermoscopic skin lesion images with age, gender metadata and histopathology-confirmed labels
notes: Used in CMAC-MMD paper (arXiv:2512.15249) for dermatology fairness analysis. Stratified by age (0-40, 41-60, 60+) and gender to create 6 intersectional subgroups.

name: BCN20000
format: Dermoscopic skin lesion images with demographic metadata for external validation
notes: Used in CMAC-MMD paper (arXiv:2512.15249) for external validation of dermatology fairness analysis. Dataset from Hospital Clínic de Barcelona.

name: OfficeHome
num_samples: ~65,000 images across 4 domains (Real_World, Clipart, Product, Art) with 65 object classes
format: Images organized by domain and class; standard UDA benchmark
metric: accuracy (per domain pair), average accuracy across all pairs
notes: UDA benchmark from Venkateswara et al. 2017. Contains 4 domains with significant style variations. Used in C-DGPA (arXiv:2512.16164) and many other UDA methods.

name: Office31
num_samples: ~4,110 images across 3 domains (Amazon, Webcam, DSLR) with 31 object classes
format: Images organized by domain and class; classic UDA benchmark
metric: accuracy (per domain pair), average accuracy across all pairs
notes: Classic UDA benchmark from Saenko et al. 2010. Smaller and simpler than OfficeHome. Used in C-DGPA (arXiv:2512.16164) and widely across UDA literature.

name: VisDA-2017
num_samples: ~150,000 synthetic-to-real images across 12 classes (train: synthetic renderings, validation: real-world photos)
format: Synthetic training images, real-world validation images; standard synthetic-to-real UDA benchmark
metric: accuracy (per class), average accuracy across classes
notes: Synthetic-to-real domain adaptation benchmark from Peng et al. 2018. Large domain gap between synthetic training and real validation data. Used in C-DGPA (arXiv:2512.16164) and many UDA methods.

name: Spider 2.0-lite
num_samples: 233 evaluation samples (subset of Spider 2.0 with full public schema information)
storage: ~10-50GB estimated (large enterprise databases with up to 23K columns)
format: Real-world enterprise Text2SQL workflows with extremely large schemas (up to 381 tables, 23K columns); multiple SQL dialects (BigQuery, Snowflake, SQLite); evaluated by execution accuracy
notes: Spider 2.0-lite is a partially released subset of Spider 2.0 with 233 evaluation samples. Spider 2.0 contains 632 Text2SQL workflow problems reflecting realistic enterprise scenarios with much larger and more complex schemas than earlier corpora.

name: PIE-Bench
num_samples: 300+ prompt pairs total (40 ChangePose subset used in SynPS)
format: Text-image editing prompt pairs with source/target prompts, covering pose change, layout change, style transfer, object manipulation, etc.
metric: MLLM-based judgment (GPT-4o, GPT-5, Gemini-2.5-Pro) and CLIP score
notes: Benchmark for text-guided image editing evaluation. SynPS (arXiv:2512.14423) evaluates on the ChangePose subset (40 prompts). From Ju et al. (ICLR 2024), PnP Inversion paper.

name: Non-Rigid Editing Benchmark
format: Text-image editing prompt pairs for non-rigid editing covering pose changes, body-shape variations, facial expression changes, and viewpoint shifts
metric: MLLM-based judgment (GPT-4o, GPT-5, Gemini-2.5-Pro) and CLIP score
notes: Curated by SynPS authors (arXiv:2512.14423) to supplement PIE-Bench for more diverse non-rigid editing evaluation. 200 prompts generated by GPT-5 covering more diverse edit types than PIE-Bench ChangePose.

name: KalshiBench
format: Binary prediction market questions (yes/no) from Kalshi exchange with verifiable real-world outcomes, temporally filtered to post-training-cutoff events
metric: Brier score, ECE, MCE, accuracy, F1, BSS, OCR@tau
notes: New benchmark introduced in arXiv:2512.16030 for evaluating LLM epistemic calibration. Uses CFTC-regulated prediction market questions with unambiguous ground truth. Temporal filtering ensures no memorization contamination.

name: VECBench
format: Unified benchmark grouping 6 VEC datasets into ID and OOD test splits for VER and VSA tasks; training split uses FI/WebEmo/EmoSet; test split adds Abstract/Artphoto/UnbiasedEmo
metric: Accuracy, macro-F1 (emotion prediction); ECE, Brier score, AUC (confidence estimation)
notes: Introduced in EmoCaliber (arXiv:2512.15528). Unifies FI, WebEmo, EmoSet for training; Abstract, Artphoto, UnbiasedEmo for OOD testing. Tasks: Visual Emotion Recognition (VER, 6/7/8-class) and Visual Sentiment Analysis (VSA, 2-class).

name: EmoSet
format: Large-scale visual emotion dataset with rich attributes; images labeled with 8 Mikels emotion categories
notes: Large-scale emotion dataset (Yang et al., ICCV 2023). Used in EmoCaliber VECBench training split.

name: Abstract (Machajdik & Hanbury)
format: Artistic images composed purely of color-texture combinations, labeled with Mikels 8 emotions
notes: Out-of-domain test set in VECBench (EmoCaliber, arXiv:2512.15528). Pure abstract art for OOD generalization testing.

name: Artphoto
format: Artistic photographs from art-sharing platforms, labeled with Mikels 8 emotions
notes: Out-of-domain test set in VECBench (EmoCaliber, arXiv:2512.15528). Artistic photos for OOD generalization testing.

name: FFHQ-UV-Intrinsics
storage: ~200-400GB (1024x1024 UV textures, 6 PBR maps per identity: diffuse albedo, surface normal, specular intensity, ambient occlusion, translucency, raw diffuse colour)
format: Aligned UV-textured face dataset extending FFHQ-UV with MoSAR inverse-rendering outputs; provides light-normalized diffuse albedo and 5 additional PBR passes at 1024x1024
metric: Masked MSE, SSIM, LPIPS, FID (per pass)
access: Available from paper authors (Dib et al., CVPR 2024, MoSAR study). See: https://github.com/afourcad/FFHQ-UV-Intrinsics
notes: Pseudo-ground-truth — maps are output of MoSAR inverse-rendering pipeline, not light-stage measurements. Used as training supervision for MAGINet in paper 2512.16511.

name: IU X-Ray
format: Chest X-ray DICOMs paired with free-text radiology reports (frontal and lateral views); reports include findings and impression sections
notes: Publicly available chest X-ray dataset from Indiana University. Commonly used for medical report generation alongside MIMIC-CXR. Standard 70/10/20 train/val/test split. Paper: Demner-Fushman et al., JAMIA 2015.

name: GSM-Symbolic
num_samples: 5000 (100 templates × 50 instances each, split into train/val/test)
format: Math word problem templates with instances; evaluates chain-of-thought reasoning
notes: Derived from GSM8K with 100 diverse templates, each having 50 instances. Designed to test mathematical reasoning with controllable difficulty variation. Used in arXiv:2512.16914 (CCA paper) for evaluating targeted sub-network updates.

name: Language-Table
format: Real-robot table-top manipulation dataset with language instructions, multi-view RGB frames from 2-3 cameras, end-effector poses, and robot state. Covers 44 tasks including pick, place, push, pull, open, close operations.
notes: Interactive Language: Talking to Robots in Real Time (Lynch et al., RAL 2023). Used in LVP paper (arXiv:2512.15840) as a source dataset for training video model. After filtering, 71K clips retained.

name: AgiBot-World
format: Large-scale real-robot manipulation dataset collected with teleoperation across diverse tasks including pick-and-place, pouring, pushing, drawer opening, cloth manipulation, tool use, and multi-stage tasks. Multi-view RGB, depth, wrist camera, and language instructions.
notes: AgiBot World Colosseo: A Large-Scale Manipulation Platform for Scalable and Intelligent Embodied Systems (Bu et al., arXiv:2503.06669, 2025). Used in LVP paper (arXiv:2512.15840) as a source dataset for training. After filtering, 863K clips retained — the largest component of LVP-1M.

name: Ego4D-ASD
format: Frame-level binary labels (active speaker / not speaking) per face track in egocentric video

name: WASD (Wilder Active Speaker Detection)
format: Frame-level binary labels across 5 challenging categories: Optimal, Speech Impairment, Face Occlusion, Human Voice Noise, Surveillance

name: UniTalk
format: Frame-level binary labels targeting 4 challenges: underrepresented languages, high ambient noise, crowded scenes, difficult combinations

name: RoboTwin-2.0
format: Dual-arm collaborative manipulation tasks in digital twin simulation with domain randomization across 5 axes (clutter, lighting, background, tabletop height, language)
notes: RoboTwin 2.0 benchmark from arXiv:2506.18088. 50 dual-arm tasks, 5 robot embodiments, 731 object instances across 147 categories. Used for training and evaluation in MiVLA paper (2512.15411) with easy/hard evaluation modes.

name: EgoDex
format: Egocentric video with paired 3D hand and finger tracking data collected using Apple Vision Pro; 194 different tabletop manipulation tasks (tying shoelaces to folding laundry)
notes: EgoDex: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from Large-Scale Egocentric Video (arXiv:2505.11709). Used as pre-training data source for human behavioral priors in MiVLA paper (2512.15411). Provides real-world human action knowledge without requiring robot hardware.

name: VFHQ
format: High-quality video face dataset for talking head / portrait animation; training/test split provided
notes: Used as the primary training and evaluation dataset in SynergyWarpNet (arXiv:2512.17331) for portrait animation. Also used in LivePortrait (arXiv:2407.03168). VFHQ stands for Video Face HQ.

name: MomaGraph-Bench
num_samples: 1,446 multi-view images, 352 task-oriented scene graphs spanning 1,315 instances, 294 diverse indoor scenes
format: Multi-choice VQA; tests 6 reasoning capabilities across 4 tiers (T1-T4): Action Sequence, Spatial, Object Affordance, Precondition & Effect, Goal Decomposition, Visual Correspondence
notes: From arXiv:2512.16909 (MomaGraph paper). First benchmark for jointly evaluating spatial-functional scene graph reasoning and task planning. Tiers: T1 (single-step), T2 (two complementary steps), T3 (multi-step/preconditioned), T4 (dynamic replanning). Unseen environments only.

name: MomaGraph-Scenes
num_samples: ~1,050 task-oriented subgraphs, 6,278 multi-view RGB images, 350 scenes, 93 task instructions
format: JSON subgraph annotations with multi-view RGB images; nodes include objects and part-level elements, edges include 6 functional types (OPEN OR CLOSE, ADJUST, CONTROL, ACTIVATE, POWER BY, PAIR WITH) and 9 spatial types
notes: From arXiv:2512.16909 (MomaGraph paper). First dataset jointly modeling spatial and functional relationships with part-level annotations. Sources: manually collected real-world data, re-annotated SceneFun3D and OpenFunGraph, AI2-THOR simulation. Covers 4 room types: kitchen, living room, bedroom, bathroom.

name: OpenFunGraph
format: 3D scene graphs with open-vocabulary functional relationships between objects in indoor environments
notes: From Zhang et al., CVPR 2025. Open-vocabulary functional 3D scene graphs for real-world indoor spaces. Re-annotated and used as data source in MomaGraph-Scenes (arXiv:2512.16909).

name: VFHQ (Video Face Super-Resolution HQ)
format: High-quality video face dataset for portrait animation training; in-the-wild monocular video dataset at 512x512 resolution

name: PFHQ (Pseudo Face HQ)
format: Blind face restoration dataset used for in-the-wild monocular portrait training at 512x512 resolution

name: FEED (Facial Expression with Extreme Disentangling)
format: Extreme expression dataset used as benchmark driving videos in DeX-Portrait paper for cross-reenactment evaluation

name: ava-256 (Codec Avatar Studio)
format: Multi-view portrait video dataset from Codec Avatar Studio; used for joint training with NeRSemble at 512x512 resolution

name: LUNA16
num_samples: 888 chest CT scans, 1,626 pulmonary nodules with annotations
format: 3D CT volumes with nodule bounding boxes; malignancy labels from histopathology or 6-year follow-up
metric: FROC (Free-Response ROC) for detection; AUC for malignancy classification

name: LUNA25
num_samples: 1,993 patients, 3,792 CT scans, 5,899 nodules with malignancy labels
format: 3D CT volumes with nodule annotations; malignancy verified by histopathology or long-term follow-up >=6 years
metric: AUC for malignancy risk estimation; FROC for detection

name: LNDbv4
num_samples: 294 low-dose chest CT scans, 1,132 nodules with annotations
format: 3D CT volumes with nodule segmentations and radiologist suspicion labels
metric: Dice for segmentation; AUC for malignancy classification

name: NSCLCR (NSCLC Radiomics)
num_samples: 415 pre-treatment CT scans from NSCLC patients with tumor segmentations
format: 3D CT volumes with radiation-oncologist-delineated gross tumor volumes (GTV); clinical metadata including age, gender, TNM staging, histology

name: DLCS24 (Duke Lung Cancer Screening 2024)
num_samples: 1,613 low-dose chest CT scans, 2,487 nodules with 3D bounding boxes
format: 3D CT volumes with clinically actionable nodules (>=4mm, Lung-RADS 2022); radiologist-verified labels with histopathology or follow-up outcomes
metric: FROC for detection; AUC for malignancy classification

name: IMD-CT (Integrated Multiomics CT)
num_samples: 2,036 chest CT scans, one annotated pulmonary nodule per patient
format: 3D CT volumes with single nodule annotations; predominantly malignant (80.1%); mean nodule diameter ~30mm
metric: AUC for malignancy classification; Dice for segmentation

name: SWE-EVO
num_samples: 48 evolution tasks from 7 open-source Python projects
storage: <1GB (task definitions); execution environments inherited from SWE-bench
eval_time: days (full agent evaluation across multiple models)
format: Release notes and versioned code snapshots with multi-step modification requirements and test suites (avg 874 tests per instance)
metric: Resolved Rate (binary pass/fail), Fix Rate (soft metric for partial progress)
notes: Benchmark for evaluating coding agents on long-horizon software evolution scenarios (multi-file changes across versions), contrasting with SWE-Bench's single-issue resolution. Paper: arXiv:2512.18470. Key finding: GPT-5 achieves only 21% on SWE-EVO vs 65% on SWE-Bench Verified.

name: Dafny2Verus
format: Formally verified Dafny problems translated into Verus/Rust with preconditions and postconditions. Each spec requires generating Rust code with proof annotations that pass the Verus SMT-based verifier.
notes: Used in PSV-VERUS paper (arXiv:2512.18160) as the seed corpus for self-play training. Translated from Dafny to Verus following the AlphaVerus pipeline.

name: MBPP-Verified
format: MBPP (Mostly Basic Python Programming) problems adapted with executable Rust+Verus specifications and proofs. Each task includes formal specs with preconditions and postconditions that Verus can verify.
access: Derived from MBPP (Austin et al., 2021) via verified adaptation process in Yang et al. 2025a and Misu et al. 2024
notes: Used in PSV-VERUS paper (arXiv:2512.18160) as a held-out test set for transfer learning evaluation.

name: HumanEval-Verified
format: Python HumanEval tasks translated into Verus/Rust. Multi-function programs decomposed into independently verifiable functions with formal pre/postconditions.
notes: Used in PSV-VERUS paper (arXiv:2512.18160) as a held-out test set. Decomposed from original Python HumanEval (Chen et al., 2021) into Verus format.

name: GroundingME
eval_time: hours per model (1,005 samples across 25 models)
format: Visual grounding samples with high-resolution images (1,500-7,680 px), long descriptions (median 40 words), and multi-dimensional challenge taxonomy: Discriminative (distinguishing similar objects), Spatial (complex relational descriptions), Limited (occlusions/tiny objects), Rejection (ungroundable queries)
notes: New benchmark from arXiv:2512.17495 (Li et al., 2025). Designed to expose visual grounding gaps in MLLMs. Best model (Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B) achieves only 45.1% accuracy. Most models score 0% on rejection tasks. Uses SA-1B and HR-Bench source images.

name: Ref-L4
format: Referring expression comprehension benchmark with long, descriptive sentences as queries for increased difficulty
notes: From Chen et al. (CVPR 2025). Introduces longer, more descriptive referring expressions to increase reasoning complexity beyond RefCOCO series. Nearly 90% accuracy achieved by top MLLMs, indicating saturation.

name: Ref-ZOM
format: Referring expression comprehension with simple negative samples to test model's rejection ability
notes: From Hu et al. (ICCV 2023). First benchmark to introduce negative samples for testing rejection capability in visual grounding.

name: CLEVR-Ref+
format: Referring expressions in synthetic CLEVR environment for diagnosing compositional reasoning
notes: From Liu et al. (CVPR 2019). Synthetic visual reasoning benchmark for compositional referring expression comprehension. Diagnoses whether models understand spatial/attribute composition.

name: RefCrowd
format: Referring expressions in crowded scenes for fine-grained discrimination
notes: From Qiu et al. (ACM MM 2022). Focuses on fine-grained discrimination in crowded scenes where multiple similar objects exist.

name: HC-RefLoCo
format: Long, compositional referring expressions for visual grounding
notes: Long and complex referring expressions for visual grounding, designed to increase task difficulty beyond simple phrase-based benchmarks.

name: Iris
format: 4 numeric features (sepal length/width, petal length/width), 3 classes (Setosa, Versicolor, Virginica)

name: OpenHumanVid
format: Large-scale high-quality dataset of talking-head videos for audio-driven human animation; covers varied speakers, emotions, and speaking styles. Li et al., CVPR 2025.
notes: Used as Stage 1 training data in ActAvatar (arXiv:2512.19546).

name: SpeakerVid-5M
format: Large-scale high-quality dataset for audiovisual dyadic interactive human generation. Zhang et al., arXiv:2507.09862.
notes: Used as Stage 1 training data in ActAvatar (arXiv:2512.19546), combined with OpenHumanVid for 500K diverse talking-head videos.

name: DWPose (Whole-Body Pose Estimation)
format: Real-time whole-body pose estimation model (2D keypoints); variants: DWPose-t/s/m/l with 0.5G-10.1G FLOPS. Yang et al., ICCV 2023.
notes: Used in ActAvatar (arXiv:2512.19546) for Stage 2 motion magnitude computation and video selection (filtering videos with significant movement for structured annotation dataset).

name: RLCausal
num_samples: 8000 train / 2000 dev / 8000 test per query level (association, intervention, counterfactual)
storage: ~1-2GB (synthetically generated; only stores graph specs and queries)
format: Structured probabilistic causal inference queries over 10-node binary DAGs with fully specified CPTs; three query levels (association/intervention/counterfactual); answers computed via variable elimination
metric: Accuracy (exact match within total variation distance t=0.01)

name: Google-IMO-AnswerBench
format: Google DeepMind olympiad benchmark released November 2025; 400 problems (100 each from algebra, combinatorics, geometry, number theory) from national/regional/international olympiad competitions; questions are semantically rewritten to prevent memorization

name: ST-Bench
num_samples: 30 story scripts (300 video prompts total, 8-12 per story)
eval_time: hours for full metric suite (aesthetic, prompt following, consistency scoring)
format: GPT-5 generated story scripts with per-shot text prompts, first-frame prompts, and scene-cut indicators
metric: Aesthetic Quality (LAION aesthetic predictor), Prompt Following (ViCLIP global/single-shot), Cross-shot Consistency (ViCLIP overall/top-10 pairs), human preference

name: Longest6 v2
num_samples: 36 routes of approximately 2km each across six CARLA towns
eval_time: hours for full closed-loop evaluation per run
format: Long-form closed-loop driving evaluation in CARLA 0.9.15; routes are approximately 2km each with diverse traffic and weather scenarios
metric: Driving Score (DS = RC x IS), Route Completion (RC), Infraction Score (IS)

name: Town13 Validation
num_samples: 20 routes on unseen town (Town13), average 12.39km long, featuring ~100 scenarios per route of 38 different types
format: Closed-loop CARLA evaluation on held-out town (Town13) not seen during training; tests generalization to novel environments
metric: Driving Score (DS), Normalized Driving Score (NDS = RC x I where I is distance-normalized IS), Route Completion (RC), Infraction Score (IS)
notes: Among the most challenging CARLA benchmarks; tests sim-to-real generalization since Town13 is withheld during training.

name: SafeAgentBench
num_samples: ~150+ scenarios across contextual unsafe, temporal unsafe, safe, and jailbreak categories
format: Benchmark for safe task planning of embodied LLM agents in AI2-THOR. Includes unsafe instruction dataset (contextual risks), long-horizon unsafe instruction dataset (temporal risks), safe instruction dataset, and jailbreak attack dataset. Metrics: ARR (Accurate Refusal Rate), ESR (Execution Success Rate), SPR (Safe Planning Rate).
metric: ARR (Accurate Refusal Rate), ESR (Execution Success Rate), SPR (Safe Planning Rate)
notes: From arXiv:2412.13178. Evaluates safety of VLM-driven embodied agents (ReAct, ProgPrompt, Reflexion) against contextual risks (immediate situational hazards) and temporal risks (sequential hazards over time). Simulated in AI2-THOR environment.

name: AI2-THOR
format: Interactive 3D environment for visual AI. Photorealistic indoor scenes (kitchen, living room, bedroom, bathroom) where embodied agents can navigate and interact with objects. Used as simulation backend for embodied agent task planning and safety evaluation.
notes: From Kolve et al., arXiv:1712.05474. Standard embodied AI simulation platform. Supports household tasks with object manipulation, navigation, and multi-agent scenarios. Used as backend for SafeAgentBench and RoboSafe evaluations.

name: Mini-ARC
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Grid-based visual reasoning puzzles (reduced-scale ARC). Input-output demonstration pairs with test input; model predicts test output. Smaller grids, fewer colors than full ARC.
notes: Reduced-scale variant of ARC (Chollet, 2019) for isolating reasoning under easier perception. Used in paper arXiv:2512.21329 to study perception vs. reasoning in VLMs.

name: ACRE (Abstract Causal REasoning)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Symbolic visual reasoning for causal induction. Tasks consist of demonstrations showing object presence/absence and corresponding pink board state (activated/deactivated/underdetermined). Model predicts board status for new configurations.
notes: Designed for causal induction from visual inputs. Used in paper arXiv:2512.21329 to study perception vs. reasoning in VLMs.

name: BAXBENCH
format: Backend application scenarios with OpenAPI specs, functional tests, and end-to-end security exploits; evaluated via REST API in Docker containers
notes: Human expert-written benchmark for evaluating LLM code generation security and correctness. Detects critical vulnerabilities via executing end-to-end exploits. From Vero et al., 2025.

name: AUTOBAXBENCH
eval_time: ~2 hours per scenario generation; evaluation time varies by model
format: LLM-generated backend security scenarios with OpenAPI specs, functional tests, and security exploits; framework-agnostic via REST API
notes: Auto-generated extension of BAXBENCH via AUTOBAXBUILDER pipeline. 11 CWE classes covered (excluding CWE-400 due to reliability concerns). Generated by GPT-5 orchestration LLM. From von Arx et al., 2026 (arXiv:2512.21132).

name: SWE-smith
