format: Large-scale synthetic SWE training data generated via SWE-smith framework; instances include issue descriptions and ground-truth patches for training software engineering agents
notes: Used in CAT paper (arXiv:2512.22087) as one of two training data sources (20k instances). Yang et al., 2025b.

name: SWE-ReBench
format: Automated pipeline for task collection and decontaminated evaluation of software engineering agents; generates synthetic SWE instances for training and evaluation
notes: Used in CAT paper (arXiv:2512.22087) as one of two training data sources (20k instances). Badertdinov et al., 2025.

name: GamiBench
num_samples: 372 crease patterns (186 regular + 186 impossible) with 744 VQA MCQ sets across 3 tasks
eval_time: minutes to hours (744 VQA MCQ evaluations per model)
format: 2D crease patterns (SVG/render) paired with 3D folded mesh renders from 6 canonical viewpoints; 3 VQA task types: 3D fold prediction, viewpoint consistency, impossible fold detection; MCQ format with 4 options + E
metric: Accuracy (normal folds), Viewpoint Consistency (VC, conditional re-test accuracy across views), Impossible Fold Selection Rate (IFSR, false positive rate on valid folds)

name: RealText
format: Text-centric document images with multi-task annotations: (1) binary forgery detection labels, (2) pixel-level forgery masks (bounding boxes), (3) structured textual explanations of forgery cues (visual + logical). Annotations generated via PR2 multi-agent pipeline (Perceiver, Reasoner, Reviewer).
metric: M-F1 (macro-average of Detection F1, Grounding mF1, Explanation BS(F1)); also Accuracy, F1, mIoU, CSS, BERTScore F1
license: Not yet publicly released at paper submission (promised publicly available)
notes: First public benchmark for explainable text-centric forgery analysis with unified detection, grounding, and explanation annotations. From LogicLens paper (arXiv:2512.21482). The dataset includes both visual and logical anomaly cues. RealText-test has 5397 images with train/test split. Subsumes samples from T-IC13, T-SROIE, DocTamper, OSFT, ICDAR2019-ReCTS, COCO-Text, and LSVT after filtering.

name: LVOS
num_samples: 720 videos (420 train / 140 val / 160 test), 296,401 frames, 407,945 pixel-level annotations
format: RGB video sequences with per-frame instance segmentation masks for long-term video object segmentation

name: SEVIR (Storm Event Imagery)
format: Multi-modal weather imagery (VIL radar, satellite IR/VIS), 384kmx384km regions, 4 hours/event at 5-min intervals (48 frames). Shi et al. 2015; Veillette et al. NeurIPS 2020.
notes: Used in STLDM (arXiv:2512.21118), Earthformer (NeurIPS 2022), LDCast, PreDiff, DiffCast for precipitation nowcasting evaluation.

name: HKO-7 (Hong Kong Radar)
format: CAPPI radar reflectivity at 2km altitude, 256km radius centered at Hong Kong, 6-min intervals. Shi et al. NeurIPS 2015. Paper uses 5 input frames -> 20 output frames.
license: Research use (data sharing agreement with Hong Kong Observatory)
notes: Used in STLDM (arXiv:2512.21118) and other precipitation nowcasting papers (ConvLSTM, PredRNN, DiffCast, etc.).

name: MeteoNet (France Radar)
format: Radar and satellite observations in France (NW and SE regions), 550kmx550km, 5-min intervals. Larvor et al. 2020. Paper uses 5 input frames -> 20 output frames.
license: Research use (data sharing agreement with Meteo-France)
notes: Used in STLDM (arXiv:2512.21118) and DiffCast (CVPR 2024) for precipitation nowcasting evaluation.

name: MultiNews
format: Multi-document summarization: input is multiple news articles (avg ~2,196 tokens) on the same topic; output is a summary sentence
notes: From Fabbri et al., ACL 2019. Large-scale multi-document summarization dataset. Average input is ~10 news articles per topic. Used in AHA paper (arXiv:2512.22562) for zero-shot evaluation with avg generation of ~157 tokens.

name: B&J Benchmark (Bones and Joints Benchmark)
num_samples: 1245 questions (129 knowledge recall + 101 clinical note interpretation + 203 radiological image interpretation + 203 diagnosis generation + 203 treatment planning + 203 diagnosis reasoning + 203 treatment reasoning) across 42 musculoskeletal diseases and 7 anatomical sites
storage: ~50-100GB estimated (203 real clinical cases with X-ray/MRI/CT images)
format: 7 task types: MCQ (knowledge recall, clinical note interpretation, radiological image interpretation) and open-ended (diagnosis generation, treatment planning, diagnostic reasoning, treatment reasoning); plus adversarial Task VIII for text-image inconsistency detection
metric: Accuracy (MCQ); GPT-4o-judged accuracy (open-ended); manual expert evaluation (subset)
notes: Clinical reasoning benchmark for VLMs and LLMs in musculoskeletal/sports medicine. Evaluates 11 VLMs and 6 LLMs. Key finding: VLMs achieve >90% on MCQ but <60% on open-ended multimodal tasks; medical-specific VLMs show no consistent advantage over general-purpose models; severe text-driven hallucinations in VLMs when text and images conflict.

name: AInsteinBench
storage: ~50-200GB (Docker environments for PySCF, Qiskit, Einstein Toolkit, AMReX, OpenMM, RDKit)
eval_time: days (full evaluation across multiple models); hours per model for all 244 tasks
format: Agentic evaluation: LLM agent interacts with Docker containers via bash commands, edits files, runs tests. Tasks are real PRs and synthesized feature implementations from scientific codebases.
metric: Issue resolution rate (pass@k for agent trajectories)
license: GitHub OSS licenses for repos; benchmark code is Apache 2.0 or similar
notes: Benchmark for evaluating LLM agents as scientific computing development agents. Spans quantum chemistry (PySCF), quantum computing (Qiskit), computational astrophysics (Einstein Toolkit), fluid dynamics (AMReX), molecular dynamics (OpenMM), and cheminformatics (RDKit). arXiv:2512.21373 (Dec 2025).

name: AGIQA-1K
format: AI-generated images with MOS quality annotations

name: AGIQA-3K
format: AI-generated images from 6 T2I models (AttnGAN, DALLE2, GLIDE, Midjourney, SD, SDXL) with MOS for perceptual quality and prompt alignment

name: AIGCIQA2023
format: AI-generated images with MOS for perceptual quality, authenticity, and prompt consistency

name: TID2013
format: Reference images with 24 types of distortions at multiple levels; full-reference IQA

name: SIQAD
format: Screen content images with distortions; no-reference IQA for screen content

name: AndroidLab
num_samples: 726 training tasks + 138 validation tasks across 9 Android apps (Calendar, Zoom, Bluecoins, PiMusic, Maps.me, Contacts, Cantook, Clock, Setting)
storage: ~20-30GB for Android AVD disk images + task definitions
eval_time: hours for full evaluation on 138 validation tasks
format: Natural language task instructions with Android AVD trajectories; XML tree representations for state; actions include Tap, Swipe, Type, Long Press, Home, Back, and submit
metric: Success Rate (SR), Sub-Goal Success Rate (Sub-SR), Reversed Redundancy Ratio (RRR), Reasonable Operation Ratio (ROR)

name: NuInteract
num_samples: ~1.5M multi-view image-language pairs from ~8K nuScenes scenes
format: Multi-view camera images (6 cameras) with language annotations for 2D perception, 3D visual grounding, region description, and planning tasks; derived from nuScenes
metric: BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, CIDEr for captioning; mAP, F1, MIoU for 2D grounding; mAP, F1, Acc for 3D grounding; Accuracy for planning
access: https://github.com/是你好啊/NuInteract (paper reference; dataset access may require request)

name: EvalMuse-40K
num_samples: 40K image-prompt pairs with element-level binary annotations
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Large-scale benchmark for text-to-image alignment evaluation with element-level annotations (objects, attributes, locations); each element labeled as aligned (1) or unaligned (0) by multiple annotators; elements with scores >= 0.5 considered aligned

name: RichHF
num_samples: Not publicly specified; keyword-level annotations over diverse prompt styles
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Rich human feedback benchmark for text-to-image generation; provides keyword-level annotations across diverse prompt styles; evaluates on annotated subset using accuracy

name: MHaluBench
num_samples: Not publicly specified; claim-level annotations with element-level decomposition
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Multimodal hallucination benchmark; provides claim-level annotations; adapted for fine-grained evaluation by decomposing prompts into semantic elements via GPT-4 and generating binary verification questions with human annotations following EvalMuse-40K protocol

name: Dense Material Segmentation (DMS)
format: RGB images with dense material segmentation labels covering indoor and outdoor scene materials
notes: Dense Material Segmentation dataset by Upchurch and Niu (ECCV 2022). Provides per-pixel material labels for indoor and outdoor scenes. Used in GSCG paper (arXiv:2512.23024) merged with COCO Panoptic to create unified 175-label ontology for joint panoptic and material segmentation via OneFormer.

name: TNL2K
num_samples: 2000 video sequences, 663 word-level natural language descriptions; 1300 train / 700 test split
format: Video sequences with bounding box annotations and natural language descriptions (words/phrases describing targets). Designed for vision-language object tracking.

name: TNLLT
num_samples: 50 long video sequences with 15 challenging attributes (occlusion, deformation, motion blur, illumination variation, fast motion, low resolution, out-of-view, background clutter, etc.); training + test splits
format: Long video sequences for long-term vision-language tracking with natural language descriptions and 15 annotated challenge attributes.

name: CIFAR-10-C
format: CIFAR-10 test images with 19 common corruptions at 5 severity levels (total 19*5=95 corruptions)

name: CIFAR-10-P
format: CIFAR-10 test images with 5 common perturbations (noise, blur, weather, digital) across multiple severity levels

name: IF-Bench
format: Prompts with one or more verifiable constraints covering word-count limits, formatting, counting, copying, and sentence/word/character manipulations

name: CFBench
format: Chinese benchmark with 200+ real-world scenarios, 50+ NLP tasks, multiple constraints organized into 10 primary categories and 25+ subcategories, multi-dimensional evaluation

name: InfoBench
format: Five constraint types (Content, Linguistic, Style, Format, Number), each instruction has multiple constraints

name: ComplexBench
format: Hierarchical taxonomy with 4 constraint types, 19 constraint dimensions, and 4 composition types

name: MulDimIF
format: Multi-dimensional constraint framework with 3 constraint patterns, 4 constraint categories, 4 difficulty levels, code-verifiable ground truth

name: FollowBench
num_samples: Not disclosed (multi-level fine-grained constraint test set)
format: Multi-level fine-grained instruction following benchmark with 5 constraint types: Content, Situation, Style, Format, Example. Explicitly models constraint elements from user instructions.

name: TOMATO
format: Video clips with questions assessing visual temporal reasoning capabilities in multimodal foundation models; tests understanding of temporal ordering and causality
notes: Benchmark for assessing visual temporal reasoning in VLMs. From Shangguan et al. 2024. Used in DNA-Train paper (arXiv:2512.24271) as a general video understanding benchmark.

name: TVBench
format: Redesigned video-language evaluation benchmark covering diverse video understanding tasks
notes: TVBench from Cores et al. 2024. Redesigned video-language evaluation. Used in DNA-Train paper (arXiv:2512.24271) as a general video understanding benchmark.

name: DualityVidQA
storage: ~200-500GB (100 hours of video, 81K unique video clips)
format: Paired real-counterfactual video QA pairs for training and evaluating MLLM hallucination mitigation. SFT split: 54K real + 50K counterfactual QA pairs. RL split: 20K shared-question contrastive pairs (40K QA total, one question with different answers for real vs CF video). Test set: 600 paired samples with 4 categories (counter physical, object/scene deformation, causal reversal, attribute change).
metric: accuracy (pairwise: correct on both real and CF videos)
notes: Dataset introduced by Huang et al. in DNA-Train paper (arXiv:2512.24271). Designed to reduce hallucinations in MLLMs via counterfactual video generation. Built using DualityForge framework with VACE and FLUX-Kontext video editing.

name: HoVer
num_samples: ~26K claims (estimated from paper description, 2-4 hop reasoning)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Many-hop fact extraction and claim verification dataset built on Wikipedia. Each instance contains: claim, supporting facts (entity references to Wikipedia articles), label (SUPPORTED/NOT_SUPPORTED), num_hops (2-4).
notes: HoVer (HOppy VERification) from Jiang et al., EMNLP 2020. Used in ADOPT paper (2512.24933) as a multi-step pipeline benchmark alongside HotPotQA. Challenges models to extract facts from multiple Wikipedia articles and verify claims.

name: WiAR
num_samples: WiFi CSI data for 6 activity classes (walk, forward kick, side kick, sit down, squat, bend)
format: Channel State Information (CSI) time series from commercial WiFi devices (IEEE 802.11n); per-subcarrier amplitude and phase across multiple antennas
notes: Public WiFi-based activity recognition benchmark from Guo et al., IEEE Access 2019. Used in paper arXiv:2601.02203 (CSI-ResNet-A) as a cross-domain transfer target. 6-class classification: walk, forward kick, side kick, sit down, squat, bend.

name: Omni-Math
format: Olympiad-level mathematical reasoning benchmark with diverse topics and longer reasoning chains; requires compositional mathematical skills; accuracy evaluated via LLM Judge (xVerify)

name: AYA dataset
num_samples: Not disclosed (multilingual instruction dataset covering 100+ languages)
storage: ~GB scale (subset of 14 languages used in homotokens paper)
format: Multilingual instruction-response pairs for instruction fine-tuning
notes: From Singh et al. 2024. Used in homotokens paper (arXiv:2601.02867) for multilingual fine-tuning experiments with 14-language subset.

name: Cosmopedia
num_samples: 25B+ tokens (multiple subsets used: Khan Academy, Stanford, Stories, Web Samples v2, AutoMathText, WikiHow)
storage: ~500GB+ for full dataset; paper uses subsets totaling ~10-20GB for experiments
format: Large-scale synthetic dataset generated by Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 for domain adaptation. Subsets include Khan Academy (educational content), Stanford (course outlines), Stories (commonsense knowledge), Web Samples v2 (web content), AutoMathText (math/science), WikiHow (procedural content).
notes: Used in arXiv:2601.02751 (WBC MIA paper) for fine-tuning experiments across 6 subsets. Each subset provides 10k training samples for membership inference attack evaluation.

name: PET-Bench
format: SUV-normalized pure PET volumes (3D) converted to 2D coronal slices with hierarchical QA pairs across 5 levels: Tracer Identification, Image Quality Assessment, Organ Recognition, Abnormality Detection, Disease Diagnosis
metric: Multiple-choice answer accuracy (Level 1-5); auxiliary CoT plausibility scoring
notes: First large-scale PET benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on functional imaging. Multi-site (8 international centers), multi-tracer (FDG, PSMA, FAPI, MET). Hierarchical VQA design isolating functional perception from structural priors. From Ye et al. 2026 (arXiv:2601.02737).

name: AutoPET III
format: 3D PET-CT volumes with tumor segmentation masks
notes: Public PET/CT dataset used as one data source in PET-Bench. Part of the AutoPET challenge for fully automated lesion segmentation.

name: HASOC 2020
format: Twitter text with binary HATE/NOT HATE labels; used for Hindi and English hate speech detection in HASOC shared task

name: HASOC 2021
format: Twitter text with binary HATE/NOT HATE labels; follow-up to HASOC 2020

name: HOLD-Telugu
format: YouTube comments in Telugu (Latin script, transliterated to Telugu script) with binary HATE/NON-HATE labels; from DravidianLangTech 2024 shared task

name: HateXplain
format: English hate speech posts with word/phrase-level span annotations (rationales) plus HATE/NOT HATE/OFFENSIVE labels; first benchmark dataset with human rationales for hate speech detection
metric: accuracy, F1, token-level F1, IOU-F1, comprehensiveness, sufficiency

name: HateBRXplain
format: Brazilian Portuguese hate speech posts with human-annotated rationales; benchmark for explainable hate speech detection in Brazilian Portuguese
metric: accuracy, F1, token-level F1, IOU-F1, comprehensiveness, sufficiency

name: X-MuTeST
format: Multilingual hate speech dataset (Hindi, Telugu, English) with binary HATE/NOT HATE labels and token-level human rationale annotations explaining classification decisions; rationales annotated by native speakers with iterative refinement
metric: accuracy, F1, macro-F1, token-level F1, IOU-F1, comprehensiveness, sufficiency

name: SWE-Bench Multilingual
num_samples: Not disclosed (multilingual version of SWE-Bench covering issues in multiple programming languages)
format: GitHub issues with failing tests and patches, extended to multiple programming languages
notes: Multilingual extension of SWE-Bench from SWE-smith paper (Yang et al., 2025). MiMo-V2-Flash achieves 71.7% on this benchmark.

name: MRCR
num_samples: Not disclosed (latent structure queries for long-context evaluation)
format: Long-context tasks requiring reasoning over latent structure within very long contexts (up to 128K tokens)
notes: Michelangelo long-context benchmark. Evaluates models on tasks requiring understanding of implicit structure within long contexts. MiMo-V2-Flash achieves 45.7% on MRCR (4-needles, 128K max).

name: Tau2-Bench
num_samples: Not disclosed (tool-use tasks in dual-control environments)
format: Tool-use tasks across domains (Telecom, Retail, Airline) requiring state inference and data propagation
notes: Evaluating conversational agents in dual-control environments. MiMo-V2-Flash achieves 80.3% overall (95.3% Telecom, 79.5% Retail, 66.0% Airline).

name: HyperCOD
storage: ~100-200GB (350 HSI cubes, 1240×1680 spatial resolution, 200 spectral bands in .mat format)
eval_time: minutes to 1 hour for 70 test images at 19 FPS inference speed
format: Hyperspectral image cubes (.mat), binary segmentation masks (.png), pseudo-RGB images (.jpg). 200 spectral bands spanning 400-1000nm.
notes: First hyperspectral camouflaged object detection benchmark. Features diverse natural environments (grasslands, snowfields, etc.) with challenging scenarios: minimal objects, complex shapes, dynamic lighting, object occlusion, cluttered backgrounds.

name: BESPOKE-MetaEval
num_samples: Meta-evaluation set with user interaction history and search history; multiple response candidates per query with 1-5 scale scores across personalization aspects
eval_time: hours (depending on model and evaluation settings)
format: User interaction history, search history, query, multiple response candidates with multi-aspect scores (Need Alignment, Content Depth, Tone, Style)
notes: From Kim et al. (arXiv:2509.21106, 2025). BESPOKE benchmark provides user interaction and search history for personalized LLM evaluation. Used as OOD benchmark in P-CHECK paper.

name: BFCL V4
format: Tool/API function calling benchmark with multiple categories: Overall, Web Search, Memory, Single (Live), Single (Non-Live), Multi. Evaluates multi-turn tool interactions.
notes: BFCL V4 updated Nov 2025. Used in SCRIBE paper (2601.03555) for tool-use evaluation. Results may differ from prior baselines evaluated on earlier versions.

name: ToolACE
num_samples: ~26K diverse API pool for tool calling
format: Automatic agentic pipeline generated tool-learning data for training LLMs in function calling. Contains 26,507 diverse APIs with corresponding dialogue samples.
notes: Used in SCRIBE paper (2601.03555) as training data for tool-use RL. From Liu et al., 2024.

name: LLM4LLM
num_samples: ~2,100 prompts across multiple task dimensions, 50,400 images from 24 T2I models
format: Large-multimodal model evaluation benchmark for text-to-image generation. Uses two fine-tuned LLM judges to compute Perception (clarity, authenticity, aesthetics) and Correspondence (text-image alignment) scores.
metric: Perception score, Correspondence score, Overall All score
notes: Also referred to as LMM4LMM in some sources. Evaluates T2I generation quality using LMM-based judges.

name: EvalAlign
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed; tested on 24 T2I models
format: MLLM-based evaluation benchmark for text-to-image faithfulness and text-image alignment. Uses fine-tuned MLLMs with detailed scoring instructions to assess image faithfulness.
notes: From Tan et al., 2024. Fine-tuned MLLMs for evaluating image faithfulness and text-image alignment in T2I generation.

name: Clotho
num_samples: 3,839 dev + 1,045 val + 1,045 eval = 5,929 total clips (15-30 seconds each, 5 captions per clip)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Audio clips (15-30s) with 5 human-written captions each
metric: METEOR, CIDEr, SPICE, SPIDEr, SPIDEr-FL, FENSE

name: WavCaps
num_samples: 403,050 audio clips (a few seconds to over 1 minute each)
format: Audio clips collected from AudioSet, BBC Sound Effects, FreeSound, and SoundBible with audio captions
license: Mixed (per source: AudioSet CC BY 4.0, BBC Sound Effects restricted, FreeSound per-file, SoundBible per-file)

name: MineDojo
eval_time: hours to days per task (long-horizon tasks)
format: Minecraft embodied agent benchmark with JavaScript-based Mineflayer API for motor control; tasks specified in natural language with goal predicates; supports tech tree progression from wooden tools to diamond tools
metric: iteration count (steps to complete task), task success rate, skill retention rate
notes: MineDojo from Fan et al., NeurIPS 2022 (Outstanding Paper Award). Used as primary benchmark in Voyager (Wang et al., 2024a) and PSN (arXiv:2601.03509) papers. Tech tree mastery is a standard evaluation task.

name: WildRGB-D
format: In-the-wild RGB-D video sequences with camera poses, depth maps, and point cloud ground truth for 3D scene generation and reconstruction
metric: Accuracy, Completeness, Chamfer Distance (for geometry); PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS (for appearance)
notes: Used in Gen3R (arXiv:2601.04090) for evaluating 3D scene generation and reconstruction. Provides in-the-wild RGB-D sequences with ground truth geometry for benchmarking geometry generation quality.

name: HeCBench
format: HPC kernel source code (C/C++, OpenMP, SYCL) with reference implementations; evaluates GPU offload correctness and performance
metric: GPU time speedup vs reference implementations; compilation success rate; correctness validation

name: Rodinia
num_samples: 7 kernels used in paper (full suite has ~20+ benchmarks)
format: Heterogeneous computing benchmarks with CPU/GPU implementations in OpenMP, CUDA, OpenCL; covers domains including bioinformatics, medical imaging, graph analytics, etc.
metric: GPU time speedup vs reference; compilation and correctness rates

name: NAS Parallel Benchmarks
num_samples: 6 kernels used in paper (BT, CG, EP, FT, LU, MG from full NPB suite)
format: NAS parallel benchmarks (NPB): structured HPC kernels (BT=block tridiagonal, CG=conjugate gradient, EP=embarrassingly parallel, FT=fast Fourier transform, LU=lower-upper Gauss-Seidel, MG=multigrid) with highly optimized reference implementations
metric: GPU time speedup vs expert reference; compilation and correctness validation

name: ParEval
format: Benchmark for evaluating LLM parallel code generation quality; tests CUDA to OpenMP translation fidelity with compilation success and numerical correctness validation
metric: Compilation rate; validation success rate; code-only vs end-to-end evaluation
access: Referenced in Nichols et al. 2024a (ParEval paper)

name: NUAA-SIRST
format: Infrared images with pixel-level binary masks for small target detection
metric: IoU, nIoU, Pd (Probability of Detection), Fa (False Alarm Rate)

name: IRSTD-1k
num_samples: 1000 infrared images (80% train / 20% test split), 512x512 resolution
format: Infrared images with pixel-level binary masks for small target detection, covering cluttered backgrounds and low SNR scenarios
metric: IoU, nIoU, Pd (Probability of Detection), Fa (False Alarm Rate)

name: BBH
format: Diverse set of 23 challenging BIG-Bench tasks where language models underperform humans; 3-shot chain-of-thought prompting

name: HUGSIM
num_samples: 345 test scenarios across 4 difficulty levels (Easy, Medium, Hard, Extreme)
storage: ~50-100GB (reconstructed 3D environments from KITTI-360, nuScenes, PandaSet, Waymo)
format: Photorealistic closed-loop simulator for E2E driving; scenarios reconstructed as 3D environments in which the planner perceives via RGB cameras and controls the ego agent; zero-shot evaluation protocol
metric: RC (Road Completion), HD-Score (combines RC with NC, DAC, TTC, comfort)
license: Research use (KITTI-360, nuScenes, PandaSet, Waymo terms)

name: SimScale
num_samples: 185k+ synthetic planning scenarios with pseudo annotations from PDM-Closed
format: Synthetic driving data generated via simulation for scaling experiments; provides pseudo ground-truth annotations for training autonomous driving models; used to supplement NAVSIM training data

name: BBH (BIG-Bench Hard)
format: Diverse challenging tasks from BIG-Bench where LLM performance lags human performance; includes 23 core tasks (tracking_shuffled_objects, logical_deduction_five_objects, etc.)

name: A-OKVQA
format: Visual question answering requiring external knowledge and multi-step reasoning. Questions have multiple correct answers. Answers are free-form text, not multiple choice.
notes: A-OKVQA dataset (Schwenk et al., 2022) used as training data in SceneAlign paper (arXiv:2601.05600). Selected for challenging open-ended questions requiring both visual grounding and external knowledge.

name: MME-RealWorld
format: Real-world multimodal understanding benchmark with perception and grounding tasks in complex real-world scenarios designed to be challenging for humans.
notes: MME-RealWorld (Zhang et al., 2024b) used in SceneAlign paper (arXiv:2601.05600) for evaluating real-world visual grounding.

name: EMMA-mini
format: Enhanced Multimodal Reasoning benchmark testing multi-step compositional reasoning in multimodal models. Evaluates reasoning chains, not just final answers.
notes: EMMA-mini (Hao et al., 2025) used in SceneAlign paper (arXiv:2601.05600) for evaluating multimodal reasoning.

name: Hallusion-Bench
format: Diagnostic benchmark for entangled language hallucination and visual illusion in large vision-language models. Includes question-level, figure-level, and assertion-level evaluations.
metric: aAcc, fAcc, qAcc (attention accuracy, figure accuracy, question accuracy)
notes: Hallusion-Bench (Guan et al., 2024) used in SceneAlign paper (arXiv:2601.05600) for evaluating hallucination robustness.

name: AutoMonitor-Bench
num_samples: 3,010 annotated test instances (Safety & Permission Violations: 1,172; Sycophancy & Bias: 962; Specification Gaming: 876)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model size
format: Paired benign-misbehavior instances: each task instance has both a misbehavior trajectory and a benign trajectory, evaluated with Miss Rate (MR) and False Alarm Rate (FAR)
metric: Miss Rate (MR), False Alarm Rate (FAR), MR-FAR trade-off
notes: New benchmark introduced by Yang et al. (2026) for evaluating LLM-based misbehavior monitors. Covers three misbehavior categories: Safety & Permission Violations, Sycophancy & Bias, and Specification Gaming. Also includes a 153,581-sample SFT training corpus.

name: WikiMIA
num_samples: ~varies by model size and sequence length (Wikipedia-based)
format: Membership inference benchmark for LLMs using Wikipedia texts with temporal timestamps to distinguish member vs non-member; evaluates original and paraphrased settings; supports variable sequence lengths (32, 64, 128)

name: EffiBench-X
num_samples: 623 algorithmic problems from AtCoder, Codeforces, and LeetCode
storage: ~50-100GB with test cases in Python and C++
eval_time: hours to days depending on number of problems and candidate budget
format: Competitive programming problems with strict time/memory limits and comprehensive test cases in Python and C++
metric: ET (Execution Time ratio), MP (Memory-Peak ratio), MI (Memory-Integral ratio) relative to human reference solutions
access: https://github.com/QuantaAlpha/EvoControl (reproduced in paper); original at arXiv:2505.13004

name: Ultra-Low-Dose PET (UDPET) Challenge
format: 3D whole-body PET volumes in SUV units; paired normal-dose and ultra-low-dose (1/20, 1/50, 1/4 dose) acquisitions from Siemens Biograph Vision Quadra
notes: Ultra-Low-Dose PET denoising challenge dataset. 18F-FDG PET scans. Used in WCC-Net paper (arXiv:2601.07093) for whole-body low-dose PET denoising evaluation.

name: BenSMOT
format: Multi-object tracking videos with semantic interaction tags and brief scene descriptions. Supports both geometric tracking (bounding boxes) and semantic reasoning (interaction labels). Part of Grand-SMOT.
metric: HOTA, DetA, AssA, IDF1, MOTA (geometric); BLEU, METEOR, CIDEr (semantic)
notes: Original semantic MOT dataset from Li et al. (ECCV 2024). Used as training source for Grand-SMOT and as evaluation split. Contains interaction tags (e.g., 'following', 'fighting') and brief scene context descriptions.

name: Grand-SMOT
num_samples: 4.8K videos, 25K tracks, 2.3M frames, 854 classes (merged TAO + BenSMOT taxonomy)
format: Large-scale semantic multi-object tracking benchmark with dual-stream dense narratives: video-level environmental captions and instance-level behavior descriptions. Combines TAO (open-world) and BenSMOT (standard) splits.
metric: HOTA, DetA, AssA, IDF1, MOTA (BenSMOT split); TETA (LocA, AssocA, ClsA) for TAO split; GPT-4o Semantic Score for semantic quality
notes: Proposed in LLMTrack (arXiv:2601.06550). Addresses semantic scarcity in MOT by providing dense, context-aware narrative annotations. Built by semantic expansion of BenSMOT and hierarchical generation on TAO using Qwen3-VL-32B, followed by Vision-Language Critic (MiniCPM-V 4.0) quality assurance (94% acceptance rate, Cohen's kappa=0.85).

name: VideoDR
num_samples: 100 video samples across 6 semantic domains (Daily Life 33%, Economics 16%, Technology 15%, Culture 15%, History 11%, Geography 10%)
storage: <500MB (100 video clips + QA pairs + archived web evidence)
eval_time: hours per model (100 samples with multi-round search)
format: Video-conditioned open-domain factoid QA requiring cross-frame visual anchor extraction, interactive web search, and multi-hop reasoning over joint video-web evidence. Each sample: video V, question Q, browser search tool S, answer A. Difficulty stratified (Low/Mid/High) based on human success rate.
notes: First video deep research benchmark (arXiv:2601.06943). Task: given a video and question, models must extract multi-frame visual anchors, use browser search to locate open-web evidence, and perform multi-hop reasoning to produce verifiable answers. Evaluates 6 MLLMs under Workflow and Agentic paradigms. Human upper bound ~50.4% accuracy. Key finding: Agentic not consistently superior to Workflow; effectiveness depends on model's ability to maintain initial video anchors over long retrieval chains.

name: CMExam
format: Multiple-choice Chinese medical exam questions from Chinese National Medical Licensing Examination
access: Public dataset, used in MLB benchmark (arXiv:2601.06193)

name: CHIP-CDN
format: Clinical diagnosis normalization task in Chinese
access: Public dataset, used in MLB benchmark (arXiv:2601.06193)

name: CMeEE
format: Chinese Medical named entity recognition
access: Public dataset, used in MLB benchmark (arXiv:2601.06193)

name: CHIP-CDEE
format: Chinese clinical event extraction
access: Public dataset, used in MLB benchmark (arXiv:2601.06193)

name: CMeIE
format: Chinese medical information extraction (semantic relationship identification)
access: Public dataset, used in MLB benchmark (arXiv:2601.06193)

name: MLB (Medical LLM Benchmark)
format: Multi-dimensional medical LLM evaluation with MCQ, open-ended, and scenario-based tasks across 22 datasets. Five dimensions: MedKQA, MedSE, MedRU, SmartServ, SmartCare.
notes: MLB: Scenario-driven benchmark for evaluating LLMs in clinical applications. 22 datasets (17 proprietary, 5 public). Curated by 300 physicians from Grade-A tertiary hospitals in China. Includes SFT-trained judge model (19k expert annotations) for open-ended evaluation, achieving 92.1% accuracy and 81.3% Cohen's Kappa.

name: PX-CLCD
format: Bitemporal remote sensing image pairs for cultivated land change detection. Captures agricultural land-use changes with multi-class or binary change masks.
access: Paper: Miao et al.; cultivated land change detection dataset

name: WaterCD
num_samples: 1,149 image pairs (765 train, 207 val, 177 test) at 512x512 pixels
format: Bitemporal remote sensing image pairs (10m resolution) for water body change detection. Binary change masks for water/non-water regions.
access: Paper: Li et al.; water resources change detection dataset

name: CDD (Seasonal)
num_samples: 16,000 image pairs (10k train, 3k val, 3k test) at 256x256 pixels
format: Bitemporal remote sensing image pairs capturing seasonal changes (cropped from larger images). Binary change masks. Used for detecting both real changes and seasonal variations.
access: Paper: Lebedev et al.; change detection dataset for remote sensing

name: MaMuJoCo (Multi-Agent MuJoCo Environment)
format: Multi-agent extension of MuJoCo continuous control tasks. Agents control articulated bodies (Hopper, HalfCheetah, Ant) in cooperative tasks with centralized training and decentralized execution. Supports varying data quality (medium-replay, medium, expert, mixed).
license: DeepMind research terms (MuJoCo license required for MuJoCo)
notes: Introduced in Peng et al. (2021) FACMAC paper. Used in LOGO paper (arXiv:2601.07463, AAMAS 2026) for offline multi-agent RL evaluation alongside SMAC.

name: ConcurrentQA
format: multi-hop QA over public/private knowledge graphs; compositional questions requiring multiple reasoning steps

name: Senorita-2M
num_samples: ~2M videos with instruction-based editing annotations; grounding subset used in RefVFX paper has 100K+ videos with foreground-background segmentation masks
storage: ~100GB+ for grounding subset (100K+ videos at original resolution)
format: High-quality video clips with human-annotated editing instructions and segmentation masks (from SegmentAnything). The grounding subset provides foreground-background segmentation for selective effect application.

name: KIT-ML
num_samples: ~4,000 3D human motion sequences with text annotations
format: 3D human motion in BVH format with paired text descriptions
notes: KIT Motion-Language Dataset from Plappert et al., Big Data 2016. Used in GeoMotionGPT (arXiv:2601.07632) for motion-language alignment evaluation alongside HumanML3D.

name: ANHIR (Automatic Non-rigid Histological Image Registration)
num_samples: 481 image pairs (230 training with ground truth, 251 test evaluated via official server)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on method
format: Multi-stain histopathology image pairs (18 staining protocols, 8 tissue types) with landmark-based ground truth for rTRE evaluation
metric: rTRE (relative Target Registration Error as % of image diagonal), robustness (% successful registrations)
notes: ANHIR challenge from Borovec et al., IEEE TMI 2020. Used in SAR-Net paper (arXiv:2601.08875) for cross-domain histopathology registration evaluation.

name: DELIBERATIONBENCH
format: Question-answer pairs with verifiable reference answers across factual, reasoning, and domain-specific categories at easy/medium/hard difficulty levels
metric: Win rate (pairwise comparison by LLM judge)
access: Paper: arXiv:2601.08835 (no code or benchmark data released)
notes: Benchmark for evaluating multi-LLM deliberation protocols against best-of-N selection baseline. Key finding: best-single selection achieves 82.5% win rate vs 13.8% for best deliberation protocol (6x gap). Uses council of 5 models (GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-Haiku, Gemini-2.0-Flash-001, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-Nemo) with GPT-4o as judge.

name: R-TOFU
num_samples: 200 synthetic author profiles × 20 QRA triples each (4000 total)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model and method
format: Synthetic author profiles with question-reasoning-answer triples; sensitive content explicitly annotated; supports forget01/forget05/forget10 protocols
metric: ROUGE-L, cosine similarity, entailment score (utility/forgetting); MCS (Multi-Decoding Consistency Score); MIA-A/MIA-C (Membership Inference Attack AUC)
notes: First benchmark specifically designed for evaluating unlearning in large reasoning models (LRMs) with chain-of-thought reasoning. Extends LLM unlearning to CoT-level intervention. Supports multiple decoding strategies (DefaultThink, ZeroThink, LessThink). Used in STaR paper (arXiv:2601.09281).

name: DrugEHRQA
num_samples: 5,559 structured + 5,693 unstructured + 27,795 multimodal QA pairs (based on MIMIC-III)
format: Drug-related multimodal QA dataset leveraging both structured EHR tables and unstructured clinical notes from MIMIC-III. Supports structured-only, unstructured-only, and multimodal evaluation.

name: EHRSQL
num_samples: ~4,606 question-SQL pairs (MIMIC-III); filtered to 1,410 with executable gold SQL
format: Text-to-SQL benchmark on MIMIC-III with diverse, realistic clinical questions emphasizing temporal reasoning and complex SQL structures.

name: EHRNoteQA
num_samples: 962 QA pairs spanning 10 clinically meaningful categories (MIMIC-IV)
format: Clinical QA benchmark over discharge summaries from MIMIC-IV. Questions require reasoning over free-text clinical narratives.

name: YNHHQA (Yale New Haven Hospital QA)
num_samples: 100 physician-curated patient-trajectory questions from Yale New Haven Hospital (OMOP CDM)
format: Real-world clinical QA benchmark for longitudinal trajectory reasoning. Three categories: lab trajectories, medication dosing/timing, and lab-drug correlations. Physician-validated via chart review.
access: Not publicly available; institutional dataset from Yale New Haven Hospital

name: ScreenSpot-v2
num_samples: Not fully disclosed; extends ScreenSpot with more diverse interface layouts and interaction patterns across Web, Desktop, Mobile
eval_time: minutes to hours for full sweep
format: UI screenshots with natural-language pointing instructions and pixel coordinates

name: OS-Atlas
num_samples: ~13M UI element annotations across Android, Desktop, Web platforms
format: UI screenshots with element-level bounding box annotations, element types, and interaction affordances; supports cross-platform GUI grounding

name: OS-Genesis
num_samples: Not fully disclosed; large-scale UI automation dataset for agent training
format: UI screenshots and interaction data for training GUI agents; supports autonomous UI navigation and grounding

name: GUI-R1
num_samples: Not fully disclosed; RL training dataset for GUI grounding agents
format: GUI interaction trajectories with natural language instructions and ground-truth actions for reinforcement learning
access: To be confirmed (referenced in GUI-Eyes paper arXiv:2601.09770; original from Luo et al. 2025)

name: AndroidControl
num_samples: Not fully disclosed; Android GUI task dataset for agent evaluation
format: Android UI screenshots with task instructions and action annotations for mobile GUI agent training and evaluation
access: To be confirmed (referenced in GUI-Eyes paper arXiv:2601.09770; original from Li et al. 2024)

name: EQ-Bench3
num_samples: ~300+ scenarios with multi-dimensional emotional intelligence evaluation
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on number of samples and judge model
format: LLM-judged emotional intelligence scenarios with 7 sub-dimensions: DoI, ER, DE, WRM, HL, PEI, SD; each sub-dim scored 0-20, Overall 0-100
notes: From Paech (2023, 2025). Used in PERM paper (arXiv:2601.10532) for evaluating empathetic LLM responses. LLM-judged benchmark using detailed rubrics.

name: AI City Challenge 2025
num_samples: 32+ cameras, multi-category objects (pedestrians, forklifts, NovaCarter robots, Transporter robots, FourierGR1T2 and AgilityDigit humanoids)
format: Multi-camera video streams with 3D bounding box annotations and track IDs for multi-target multi-camera (MTMC) tracking in infrastructure environments
metric: HOTA (Higher Order Tracking Accuracy), DetA, AssA, LocA
notes: 9th AI City Challenge. Focus: outside-in multi-camera 3D object tracking in large-scale infrastructure (warehouses, hospitals). Track: Multi-Camera 3D Tracking. arXiv:2601.10819 achieves HOTA 45.22 (online, camera-only SOTA).

name: GLEE
format: structured game outcomes (payoffs, equilibria, agent messages) across Bargaining, Negotiation, Persuasion games
metric: Fairness (quadratic deviation from equal split), Efficiency (welfare), game-specific metrics

name: IAM (English Handwriting)
format: English handwritten word images from IAM database (Marti and Bunke, 2002). Standard split: training, validation, test.

name: HWDB1.0 (CASIA Handwriting Database)
format: Chinese handwritten word images from CASIA HWDB1.0 (Liu et al., 2011). Used for training cross-lingual handwriting retrieval models.

name: MedCalc-Bench
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Patient notes + medical calculation questions; evaluated via exact-match accuracy
notes: Medical calculation reasoning benchmark. From Khandekar et al. 2024. Each instance consists of a patient note and a question asking to compute a clinical value.

name: Instruction Induction
num_samples: 24 original + 12 novel tasks (paper uses 20 total), 100 samples per task
format: Few-shot instruction generalization: given input-output examples, generate natural language instruction; evaluated via BERTScore
notes: Benchmark for instruction induction: inferring task instructions from input-output examples. From Honovich et al. 2022. Paper uses 8 original + 12 novel tasks.

name: ADI-17
num_samples: 3,033 hours training (~17 dialects), ~2 hours per dialect for test and validation sets
format: Arabic speech audio with dialect labels (17 dialects of Arabic). Train: ~3,033h. Test/Val: ~2h per dialect.
notes: Arabic Dialect Identification dataset from ICASSP 2020 (Shon et al., 2020). Used in CTC-DID paper (arXiv:2601.12199) for low-resource Arabic DID experiments.

name: Casablanca
num_samples: ~17 hours total (~1 hour per dialect from ~17 dialects)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on evaluation setup
format: Arabic speech audio with dialect labels for multidialectal Arabic speech recognition and dialect identification. ~1 hour per dialect.
notes: Casablanca dataset from ACL 2024 (Talafha et al., 2024). Used for zero-shot evaluation in CTC-DID paper (arXiv:2601.12199). No Casablanca training data was used in CTC-DID experiments.

name: BlenderGym
format: Initial code-generated 3D scenes with target images; tasks include blend shape, placement, geometry, lighting, material editing

name: SlideBench
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model capability
format: Text instructions with asset images for python-pptx slide generation; tasks evaluate execution accuracy, reference-based and reference-free metrics
metric: Execution success rate, element/content/color/position accuracy, text/image/layout/color scores
access: Referenced in autopresent paper (Ge et al., CVPR 2025)

name: BlenderBench
format: Challenging 3D scene tasks: (1) camera adjustment, (2) multi-step editing, (3) compositional editing; requires VLM to write Blender Python code iteratively
metric: Photometric Loss (PL), Negative-CLIP Score (N-CLIP), VLM Score (0-5 scale for task completion and visual quality)

name: ConditionalQA
num_samples: ~1,000 questions (860 train + 140 dev, binary Yes/No classification)
format: Complex reading comprehension dataset with conditional answers. Questions require multi-step reasoning over long documents with conditional logic. Binary (Yes/No) classification focus.
notes: From Sun et al. (ACL 2022). Used in PPA-Plan paper (2601.11908) for long-context reasoning evaluation.

name: LongReason
format: Synthetic long-context reasoning benchmark via context expansion. Questions require reasoning over very long documents (16K-32K tokens) with sparsely distributed evidence.
notes: From Ling et al. (2025). Used in PPA-Plan paper (2601.11908) as a primary evaluation benchmark.

name: MOVi-E
format: Kubric-generated synthetic videos with daily objects on highly complex backgrounds; highest object count in MOVi suite (11-23 objects per scene); used for unsupervised object discovery and segmentation

name: SSL3D
eval_time: hours for fine-tuning per downstream task
format: 3D brain MRI volumes with multiple contrasts and timepoints; downstream tasks include 4 segmentation and 3 classification tasks
metric: Dice score for segmentation, accuracy for classification
access: Challenge at MICCAI 2025; dataset from Wald et al. arXiv:2412.17041
notes: Self-Supervised Learning for 3D Medical Imaging Challenge. First rigorous evaluation of SSL foundation models for neuroimaging. Organizers fine-tuned submitted pre-trained models for downstream tasks.

name: arXiv Preprints (Full Corpus)
format: Preprints with abstracts, metadata (authors, affiliations, submission dates) across math, physics, CS, EE, quantitative biology, statistics, economics
license: arXiv license (non-commercial for heavy API use)

name: bioRxiv Preprints
format: Preprints across biology and life sciences subfields with abstracts, metadata, submission dates

name: SSRN Preprints
format: Working papers in social sciences, law, and humanities with abstracts and metadata

name: ICLR-2024 Peer Reviews
format: Peer review reports with reviewer scores, acceptance status, submitted papers across machine learning

name: Semantic Scholar Citations
format: Paper metadata with citation networks, author information, publication venues

name: arXiv Online Access Logs
storage: ~5-10TB estimated (user IDs, paper IDs, referral sources, timestamps)
format: User-level access data with arXiv document IDs, referral sources (Google, Bing), timestamps; connected to user IDs for longitudinal analysis
access: Not publicly available; obtained directly from arXiv for the study

name: DERM12345
num_samples: 12,345 dermatoscopic images (9,860 training, 2,485 testing) from clinical sources in Turkiye
storage: ~5-10GB estimated (dermoscopy images at typical clinical resolution)
format: Dermatoscopic skin lesion images with hierarchical taxonomic labels: 40 subclasses, 15 main classes, 5 superclasses (mapped to 4 active for binary/4-class tasks), and binary malignancy label
metric: Weighted F1-Score, Balanced Accuracy (used in benchmark evaluation)
access: Yilmaz et al., Scientific Data 2024 (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-024-03828-7); used in arXiv:2601.12382 hierarchical dermatology benchmark
notes: Large-scale dermatology dataset with 40 fine-grained lesion subclasses. Used to benchmark 10 foundation models (DINOv2, DINOv3, CLIP, ResNet-50, MedSigLip, BiomedCLIP, MedImageInsights, MONET, PanDerm, Derm Foundation) via frozen embedding extraction + lightweight adapter classifiers.

name: MMDR-Bench (Multimodal Deep Research Bench)
storage: <50MB prompts + metadata; images vary by task
format: Image-text bundles: textual query + set of images requiring multimodal deep research report synthesis with citation-grounded evidence use
metric: FLAE (report quality: readability, insightfulness, structure), TRACE (citation faithfulness: consistency, coverage, textual fidelity, visual evidence fidelity), MOSAIC (multimodal integrity: semantic alignment, visual data interpretation accuracy, VQA)
notes: From arXiv:2601.12346. Evaluates multimodal deep research agents on end-to-end report generation with visual evidence grounding. 140 tasks split into Daily (40) and Research (100) regimes. FLAE+TRACE+MOSAIC evaluation pipeline with Gemini-2.5-Pro as primary judge. 25 models evaluated including single-modal, multimodal, and deep research agent baselines.

name: MultiPER-Enterprise
format: Query-permission pairs with department-specific reference answers across 5 enterprise departments (HR, Finance, Legal, Sales, R&D); split into reference set (anchor construction) and evaluation set
metric: PVR (Permission Violation Rate), ISS (In-Scope Satisfaction), Fluency, SP (Semantic Preservation), AASR (Adversarial Attack Success Rate)
access: Not yet publicly released; authors promise anonymized templates and evaluation scripts

name: MPII-INF-3DHP
format: Multi-view RGB video frames with 2D and 3D joint annotations (17 joints); indoor studio and outdoor scenes for in-the-wild evaluation

name: SportsCap
num_samples: ~15K frames from sports videos (gymnastics, parkour, etc.)
format: Monocular RGB video frames with 3D joint annotations (17 joints) for complex full-body rotations; fine-grained action understanding labels
access: IJCV 2021 (Chen et al.) — contact authors for dataset access

name: CooperBench
storage: ~100-200GB (12 open-source repository snapshots with feature pools and test suites)
eval_time: days (full evaluation across multiple models and task configurations)
format: Collaborative coding tasks: each task assigns two agents different features to implement on the same repository state. Agents communicate via real-time messaging tool and execute in isolated Docker containers. Success measured by git merge compatibility + passing unit tests for both features.
metric: Cooperation success rate (merged patch passes both agents' unit tests); comparison with Solo baseline (single agent implementing both features); coordination gap analysis
notes: Introduced in arXiv:2601.13295. Evaluates multi-agent cooperation in coding tasks. 652 tasks across 12 libraries in Python, TypeScript, Go, and Rust. Key finding: 'curse of coordination' - agents achieve ~30% lower success rates when cooperating vs solo. Tasks are grounded in real open-source repositories with expert-written tests.

name: STaRK
num_samples: ~20k queries across 3 graphs (AMAZON: ~5.9k train/1.5k val/1.6k test; MAG: ~8k train/2.7k val/2.7k test; PRIME: ~6.2k train/2.2k val/2k test)
storage: ~500GB-1TB+ (3 text-rich heterogeneous KGs: AMAZON ~1M entities/9.4M relations/592M tokens; MAG ~1.9M entities/39.8M relations/213M tokens; PRIME ~129k entities/8.1M relations/32M tokens)
eval_time: hours to days depending on agent budget
format: KG retrieval queries with entity-level ground truth; graphs contain typed nodes and relational edges with text attributes

name: LH-VLN
num_samples: ~18k training trajectory slices (5 steps each), test set with unseen tasks and scenes
storage: ~5-10GB (instruction JSONs + navigation trajectories), requires HM3D scenes (~30-80GB)
eval_time: hours (online evaluation with step-by-step environment interaction)
format: Long-horizon multi-stage vision-language navigation in continuous 3D environments (HM3D scenes). Agent receives task instructions and navigates through multiple sub-goals. Data includes panoramic RGB-D observations, navigation graphs, and action trajectories.
metric: SR (Success Rate), ISR (Independent Success Rate), CSR (Conditional Success Rate), CGT (CSR weighted by ground truth trajectory length), APS (Actions Per Second for inference efficiency)
notes: LH-VLN (Long-Horizon Vision-Language Navigation) from Song et al. 2025 (CVPR). Multi-stage navigation task requiring sequential goal reaching. FantasyVLN (2601.13976) evaluates on this benchmark. Requires HM3D scenes for environment simulation.

name: MediTOD
num_samples: 231 doctor-patient dialogues (filtered for effective turns with intents of Inform, Inquire, Diagnose)
format: Real-world doctor-patient dialogues in English with comprehensive annotations; dialogues annotated with complex relationships between dialogue content and corresponding clinical attributes; original multi-turn medical history taking conversations
metric: Diagnosis accuracy, confidence correlation (Pearson/Spearman), AUROC, AUPRC
notes: From Saley et al. (EMNLP 2024 Findings). Real-world medical dialogue dataset for medical history taking. Contains annotated doctor-patient conversations with labeled intents. Used in arXiv:2601.15645 (MedConf paper) for medical LLM confidence estimation benchmark. Filtered to dialogues with >10 conversational turns for evaluation.

name: ICD-Bench
format: 4-choice MCQ (medical multiple choice questions) with chain-of-thought reasoning traces and ground-truth KG paths; stratified by hop length (2-5 hops), difficulty level (1-5), and ICD-10 category (15 categories)
notes: Introduced in Dedhia et al. (arXiv:2507.13966). Evaluates compositional multi-hop medical reasoning. Test set for zero-shot generalization of RL-trained medical QA models. Training data uses 1-3 hop paths; evaluation uses 2-5 hop paths to test compositional generalization.

name: UMLS (Unified Medical Language System)
format: Knowledge graph of biomedical concepts as (head, relation, tail) triples; integrates SNOMED CT, RxNorm, UMLS Metathesaurus, and other biomedical ontologies
metric: n/a (used as knowledge source and reward signal generator)
notes: NIH National Library of Medicine resource. Used as the source of axiomatic triples for generating medical QA training data and as the implicit reward model for KG path-alignment rewards in KG-RL approaches.

name: Machine Personality Inventory (MPI-120)
num_samples: 120 Likert items (10 scales, 12 items each for OCEAN traits)
format: 5-point Likert questionnaire covering Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism (OCEAN); adapted from IPIP Goldberg (1999); MIT-licensed

name: Anthropic-Eval Persona Subset (ANTHR-8k)
format: Multiple-choice personality assessment items from Anthropic's evaluation suite; covers OCEAN traits

name: MapEval-API
num_samples: Unspecified number of questions; spans 180 cities across 54 countries
storage: ~1-2GB (API-based evaluation, no local data storage required beyond cache)
eval_time: ~10-30 minutes for full evaluation depending on number of questions
format: API-based evaluation: agents invoke map tools (geocoding, place search, routing, trip planning) to answer geospatial questions. Four task categories: Place Info, Nearby, Routing, Trip.
metric: Accuracy (correct API call sequence and final answer)
notes: API-based geospatial reasoning benchmark from MapEval. Requires access to map APIs (Google Maps or similar) for execution. Evaluates agents on structured tool invocation for geospatial tasks.

name: MapQA
num_samples: 3,154 question-answer pairs spanning nine question types
storage: ~100MB-1GB (QA pairs + OpenStreetMap data for Southern California and Illinois)
format: Open-domain geospatial QA dataset based on OpenStreetMap data. Nine question types: Adjacent, Amenities, Amenities-Around, Amenities-Around-Specific, Compare-Closer, Distance, and others.
access: Li et al. (2025) arXiv:2503.07871; OpenStreetMap data
notes: Text-to-SQL style POI retrieval benchmark with diverse geospatial constraints. Built on OpenStreetMap covering Southern California and Illinois.

name: Lichess Masters Database
storage: ~50-100GB (public export of rated games, puzzles, evaluations)
format: PGN game records with FEN positions, move sequences, player ratings, timestamps
metric: N/A (used for training proximity estimation, not evaluation)

name: MISCITEBENCH
num_samples: 6350 miscitation instances across 254 JCR subject categories
format: Citation pairs: citing context + cited source with taxonomy-aligned error codes (AT/CV/CM/SE/EC). Surface-level (3810) and deep-level (2540) instances.
metric: Acc-pass@3 (joint accuracy + diagnostic faithfulness), Token Economy
notes: From BIBAGENT paper (arXiv:2601.16993). Cross-disciplinary benchmark for miscitation detection with 5-category taxonomy. Knowledge-blank design to prevent memorization. Evaluates both accessible (full-text) and paywalled (community consensus) regimes.

name: MMTEB
format: text retrieval and text embedding tasks across multilingual settings
metric: retrieval metrics (nDCG, MAP, etc.) and clustering/classification metrics

name: AliMeeting
format: Multi-channel far-field 8ch audio (16kHz WAV) with transcription and speaker diarization for Mandarin meeting conversations (2-4 speakers per session, 15-30 min sessions)
notes: M2MeT ICASSP 2022 challenge dataset. Used in SpatialEmb paper (arXiv:2601.18037) for multi-channel multi-speaker ASR. Training uses only Train-Ali-far (far-field, 8-channel).

name: MULTITQ
format: Temporal KG (s,p,o,t) quadruples + QA pairs
access: 公开发布 (see paper for source)

name: TIMELINEKGQA-CRON
format: Temporal KG with temporal interval reasoning + QA pairs
access: 公开发布 (see paper for source)

name: TIMELINEKGQA-ICEWS-ACTOR
format: Temporal KG for international relations + QA pairs
access: 公开发布 (see paper for source)

name: MUC-4
format: Document-level event extraction with structured templates. Six event types: Attack, Arson, Bombing, Murder, Robbery, Forced Work Stoppage. Documents are news articles about geopolitical conflict in South America.
access: Original: LDC. Previously used in Chen et al. (2023) ITERX paper. Parallel data available via Gantt et al. (2024) MultiMUC.
notes: Classic document-level information extraction benchmark. Foundation for template-based event extraction. Introduced in 1992 MUC conference.

name: MultiMUC
num_samples: 1700 documents x 6 languages (English + Arabic, Farsi, Korean, Russian, Chinese)
format: Multilingual extension of MUC-4. Same event types and template structure as MUC-4, with parallel annotations in 6 languages. Enables cross-lingual evaluation of document-level IE.
access: Gantt et al. (2024) EACL. Available at https://github.com/ or via paper's supplementary materials.
notes: Introduced by Gantt et al. (2024). Enables controlled multilingual and cross-lingual template extraction evaluation.

name: BETTER
num_samples: Unspecified number of documents with complex templates
format: Document-level event extraction with complex multi-template schemas. Six template types: Protests, Terrorism, Epidemics, Disasters, Displacement, Corruption. Substantially longer documents and more intricate templates than MUC-4.
access: Mckinnon and Rubino (2022) LREC. Available via IARPA BETTER program.
notes: IARPA BETTER program dataset. Much more complex than MUC-4 with finer-grained argument structures. Paper uses it for zero-shot evaluation only due to document length.

name: ITBench
num_samples: 35 SRE diagnostic scenarios (covering misconfigurations, resource exhaustion, and cascading failures in microservice/Kubernetes environments)
storage: ~1-10GB (Kubernetes observability snapshots: logs, metrics, traces, events, configs per scenario)
eval_time: minutes to hours per scenario depending on investigation complexity and model
format: Multi-modal telemetry snapshots from Kubernetes-based microservice applications (otel-demo and similar); includes alerts, events, service logs, metrics, distributed traces, config specs, and topology graphs; ground-truth root cause entities and propagation chains in YAML/JSON
metric: RC Entity F1/Recall (root cause entity identification), RC Reasoning F1/Recall (causal mechanism explanation), Pass@k, Majority@k
license: Research use (Jha et al., 2025 — original paper for ITBench evaluation)
access: Referenced from Jha et al., 2025 (ICML 2025). May require request to authors for dataset access.
notes: ITBench: benchmark for evaluating AI agents on diverse real-world IT automation tasks including SRE diagnostic investigations. Paper: Jha et al., 'ITBench: Evaluating AI Agents Across Diverse Real-World IT Automation Tasks' (ICML 2025). Used as primary evaluation in EoG paper (arXiv:2601.17915).

name: POIE (Visual Information Extraction in the Wild)
format: Visual documents in the wild with key information extraction annotations; tests generalization across document types

name: WildReceipt
num_samples: Unspecified receipt images with spatial dual-modality graph annotations
format: Receipt images with key-value pair annotations using spatial dual-modality graph reasoning; evaluates graph-based key information extraction
access: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14470 (Spatial Dual-Modality Graph Reasoning for Key Information Extraction)

name: Oxford Flowers-102
format: 102 flower categories; 6,552 training, 818 test images; used with DiffusionCLIP for semantic mutations in C-SAM paper

name: MedMentions-ST21pv
format: PubMed abstracts with UMLS concept annotations using ST21-pv semantic types

name: QUAERO-MEDLINE
num_samples: MEDLINE titles with French biomedical entity annotations
format: French medical text with UMLS concept annotations

name: QUAERO-EMEA
num_samples: European Medicines Agency documents with French biomedical entity annotations
format: French EMA documents with UMLS concept annotations

name: SPACCC
format: Spanish clinical case reports with SNOMED-CT annotations (diseases, symptoms, procedures)

name: RewardBench2
format: Enhanced reward model benchmark with more realistic human queries and global Best-of-N evaluation protocol; evaluates reward models and LLM-as-Judge methods
notes: RewardBench2 from Malik et al. 2025. Upgrade over RewardBench with higher difficulty and diversity. Designed to correlate more strongly with downstream RLHF performance.

name: RM-Bench
format: Robustness benchmark testing whether reward models judge based on content rather than style; focuses on subtle content differences and stylistic biases
notes: RM-Bench from Liu et al. 2025a. Tests reward model robustness under subtle content differences. Each query is associated with multiple responses (6 in the paper), making unified criteria particularly beneficial.

name: Skywork-Reward-Preference-80K-v0.2
format: Pairwise preference dataset with query, chosen response, rejected response. Used for training reward models and GRMs.
notes: Skywork reward preference dataset from Liu et al. 2024a (Skywork paper). Used in CE-RM (arXiv:2601.20327) as the base dataset, filtered to ~5.7K high-quality instances for training.

name: Tulu 3
num_samples: ~50K training prompts used in the paper
format: Post-training dataset of diverse prompts for RL fine-tuning; includes real-world user queries from ChatBot Arena
notes: Tulu 3 dataset from Lambert et al. 2025a. Used in CE-RM (arXiv:2601.20327) as RL training prompts for downstream policy optimization experiments.

name: CCL-Bench
format: Real-world images from China with fine-grained location annotations, scene categories (rural/urban/aerial/close-up), and difficulty levels (easy/medium/hard)

name: Im2GPS3K
format: Images paired with geographic coordinates for image geolocation evaluation

name: MP16-Reason
format: Street view images with reasoning-oriented annotations for geolocation

name: MSP-Podcast
format: Non-acted English conversational speech from podcasts with audio + manual transcripts; segment-level third-party activation/valence labels

name: MuSE (Multimodal Stressed Emotion)
format: Non-acted audiovisual English monologues with Whisper transcripts; momentary self-report activation/valence ratings at monologue level
notes: V1.3 used in paper. Self-reports are momentary (real-time) rather than retrospective, leading to weaker alignment with third-party labels compared to IEMOCAP's retrospective self-reports.

name: EuroParlST
format: Speech audio + translations for multiple European languages
notes: Multilingual speech translation corpus from parliamentary debates. Used in SpeechMapper paper (arXiv:2601.20417) for ST evaluation across en-es, en-fr, en-de, en-it language pairs.

name: SpokenSQUAD
num_samples: Spoken questions and answers from SQUAD
format: Speech audio + question-answer pairs from SQUAD dataset
notes: Spoken version of SQUAD for evaluating spoken question answering. Used in SpeechMapper paper (arXiv:2601.20417) for SQA evaluation.

name: LibriSQA
format: Speech audio + question-answer pairs derived from LibriSpeech
access: Referenced from Zhao et al. 2025 (IEEE TAI)
notes: Novel dataset for spoken question answering with LLMs, derived from LibriSpeech. Used in SpeechMapper paper (arXiv:2601.20417) for SQA evaluation (Part I and Part II test sets).

name: Book100
format: Real book images captured with smartphone cameras paired with high-quality reference scans; diverse languages, content types, lighting, and viewing angles
access: Promised public release with BookNet paper (arXiv:2601.21938)

name: Book3D
format: Synthetic book images rendered using Blender with 3D book mesh models; source content from arXiv academic papers across 8 domains (CS, Econ, EE, Math, Physics, QB, QF, Stats); includes dense UV coordinate maps, flow fields, 3D coordinate maps, and segmentation masks at 1200x800 resolution
access: Promised public release with BookNet paper (arXiv:2601.21938)

name: VDR-Bench
num_samples: Not fully specified (test-mini split used in paper)
format: Vision-DeepResearch benchmark for evaluating multimodal deep-research capabilities; requires multi-turn, multi-entity, multi-scale visual and textual search; tests long-horizon reasoning with dozens of steps and hundreds of search interactions

name: MMSearch-Plus
num_samples: Not fully specified (single-image subset used in paper)
format: Benchmark for provenance-aware search for multimodal browsing agents; extends MMSearch with more challenging instances requiring cross-modal retrieval and verification; requires strategic planning and sequential evidence synthesis

name: ForenSynths
num_samples: ~480k images (8 GAN generators: ProGAN, StyleGAN, StyleGAN2, BigGAN, CycleGAN, StarGAN, GauGAN, Deepfake)
format: AI-generated and real images from 8 different GAN architectures with binary labels; images generated using ImageNet class labels

name: HIFI-Gen
num_samples: 15k images (3k per generator: SDv3.5, SDXL, SDv2.1, Flux.1 Dev, Z-Image)
format: High-fidelity AI-generated images from 5 modern diffusion/Flow-matching models using ImageNet class labels; designed to test generalization against state-of-the-art generators

name: DreamSubject-14K
format: Subject images with precise segmentation masks. Curated from Object365 categories: diverse descriptions generated with Qwen2.5-1M for each Object365 category, 5 images generated per description with Flux.1-dev, filtered by Qwen2.5-VL for quality, then subjects localized with Grounding DINO and refined with SAM2.
access: not publicly released (reconstructable from Object365 + Flux.1-dev + Grounding DINO + SAM2)

name: Game of 24
format: Given 4 integers, find an arithmetic expression using +, -, *, / to equal 24
access: https://github.com/YoheiYo/Game-of-24 (original); also in ToT paper repository

name: RGBX-Grounding
num_samples: 7,432 multi-image grounding samples (59k images) across thermal, depth, and event modalities
storage: ~10-20GB (RGBX-Grounding processed dataset); source RGBX tracking datasets total ~150-200GB
format: Multi-image grounding samples: 2 template images (RGB + X modality) + 6 search images, with bounding box annotations and VM-CoT reasoning traces. Supports modality-known and modality-unknown evaluation settings.
metric: Acc@0.5 (IoU > 0.5 correctness averaged across sequence frames)
access: Constructed from 5 public RGBX tracking datasets (VisEvent, DepthTrack, RGBD2022, RGBT234, LasHeR) — see individual dataset entries
notes: From RGBX-R1 paper (arXiv:2602.00504). First benchmark for multimodal grounding across thermal infrared, depth, and event modalities. Uses Acc@0.5 as metric. Includes VM-CoT reasoning annotations generated via Qwen2.5-VL-32B with UAV prompting strategy.

name: Metaculus Forecasting Platform
num_samples: 393 resolved questions used in paper, platform has thousands
format: binary/multiple-choice forecasting questions with resolution criteria

name: CogSense-Bench
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Multiple-choice VQA with images across 5 cognitive dimensions: Fluid Intelligence, Crystallized Intelligence, Visuospatial Cognition, Mental Simulation, Visual Routines
notes: Comprehensive visual cognition benchmark for MLLMs assessing 5 cognitive dimensions grounded in cognitive science theory. Used in paper 2602.01541 (Cognition-MLLM). Training dataset CogSense-Dataset-105K contains 105K pairs from Bongard-LOGO, Bongard-HOI, Bongard-RWR+, MaRs-VQA, PGM, RAVEN, CVR, KiVA, STARE, ARC-AGI, ARC-AGI-2.

name: SugarCrepe++
format: Binary yes/no questions with semantic and lexical alterations - harder compositional splits including more complex attribute binding and spatial reasoning
notes: Enhanced version of SugarCrepe with harder compositional splits. Used in PolyGen (2602.01370) as a key benchmark for evaluating compositional reasoning. Paper: Dumpala et al., NeurIPS 2024.

name: VisEval
format: Natural language to visualization code generation benchmark. Each sample contains NL query + visualization specification (VIS). Evaluation checks code validity (renders correctly), legality (matches query requirements), and readability. Pass rate = fraction of results passing both validity and legality checks.
access: https://github.com/chanch-zh/VisEval (verify exact URL from Chen et al. 2024 paper)

name: DABench (InfiAgent-DABench)
num_samples: 257 data analysis questions mapped to 68 CSV files
format: LLM agent benchmark for executable data analysis tasks. Questions cover descriptive statistics, feature engineering, correlation analysis, regression, and ML. Each entry has NL question, analysis concepts, execution constraints, and exact answer template in JSON Lines format. Evaluation is exact-match accuracy.

name: WCEP-10
format: Multi-document summarization: input is clusters of news articles on the same event; output is a short human-written summary. From Wikipedia Current Events Portal.
notes: From Ghalandari et al. (2020). Multi-document summarization dataset pairing news article clusters with short summaries.

name: TQABench
num_samples: ~10K QA pairs (8K split used in paper)
format: Multi-table question answering: input is a relational database schema + natural language question; output is a textual answer. Tests complex query reasoning over multiple tables.
notes: From Qiu et al. (2024). Multi-table QA benchmark for evaluating LLMs on complex relational data queries.

name: QBench2
format: Low-level visual perception on image pairs: pairwise visual comparison tasks testing models on comparative judgment and cross-image reasoning.
notes: From Zhang et al. (2024). Benchmark for evaluating low-level visual perception of MLLMs on pairwise inputs.

name: MIRB
format: Multi-image reasoning: tasks requiring comparison, analysis, and reasoning across multiple images. Covers perception, world knowledge, reasoning, and multi-hop reasoning.
notes: From Zhao et al. (2024). Benchmark for evaluating LVLMs on multi-image comparison and reasoning tasks.

name: CoCoNot
format: Taxonomy of contextual non-compliance in LLMs: incomplete requests, unsupported requests, indeterminate requests, humanizing requests, and safety-related requests
notes: From Brahman et al. 2024. Used in this paper for studying non-safety forms of refusal beyond conventional safety cases.

name: Shanghai Radar
num_samples: Unknown (radar observations over Yangtze River Delta)
format: Composite Reflectivity (CR) radar data, 460x460 grid covering ~460km x 398km, reflectivity range 0-70 dBZ. Input: 6-min intervals, output: 12-min intervals. Preprocessed to 128x128 for experiments.
access: Public dataset from Shanghai Central Meteorological Observatory (SCMO)
notes: From Chen et al. 2020 'A Deep Learning-Based Methodology for Precipitation Nowcasting With Radar' (Earth and Space Science). Used in WADEPre (arXiv:2602.02096) for precipitation nowcasting evaluation.

name: BrowseComp-zh
eval_time: hours per model (requires multi-step web search and browsing)
format: Chinese language web browsing benchmark for deep research agents; extends BrowseComp to Chinese language queries

name: MOCHEG
num_samples: 1642 (test split, after filtering NEI; 817 positive + 825 negative claims)
format: End-to-end multimodal fact-checking dataset with claims, evidence, and verdict labels (True/False/NEI). From SIGIR 2023.
notes: Used in DECEIVE-AFC (arXiv:2602.02569) for adversarial claim attack evaluation against search-enabled LLM-based fact-checking systems.

name: Prophet Arena
format: Future prediction questions with binary/multinomial outcomes, candidate lists, and bid-price snapshots
notes: Live benchmark from Yang et al., 2025 (arXiv:2510.17638). Agents predict probabilities of future events and are evaluated longitudinally over 10 weeks. Strict time-based retrieval enforced to prevent information leakage.

name: XBench-DeepResearch
format: Deep research tasks requiring web search and multi-step reasoning
notes: From Chen et al., 2025 (arXiv:2506.13651). XBench suite component for evaluating LLM agents on deep research tasks. Used in LIVE-EVO paper to test generalization beyond future prediction.

name: SimpleRL-Zoo
format: Math reasoning prompts from GSM8K and MATH datasets, used for RL training in SimpleRL-Zoo (Zeng et al., 2025a). SimpleRL-Hard is for stronger models, SimpleRL-Easy for weaker models.
access: https://github.com/afe校/.SimpleRL-Zoo or similar open source release
notes: Training dataset used for math RL in Modular Gradient Surgery paper (arXiv:2602.02301). 8523 samples total.

name: Wildchat
format: Chat conversations from WildChat dataset, covering Code, Creative writing, and general chat. Used as training data for chat RL in the MGS paper.
notes: Training dataset for chat domain RL in Modular Gradient Surgery paper (arXiv:2602.02301). 7544 samples.

name: Nemotron
format: Instruction following data constructed from Nemotron dataset, with scoring utilities from IFEval. Used as IF training data in MGS paper.
license: NVIDIA AI Foundation Models Community License
notes: Training dataset for instruction following domain in Modular Gradient Surgery paper (arXiv:2602.02301). 7930 samples.

name: IFBench
num_samples: not disclosed (IFBench dataset from Pyatkin et al., 2025)
format: Instruction-following benchmark with constraint-based evaluation. Used alongside IFEval for IF evaluation in MGS paper.
notes: IFBench from Pyatkin et al. (2025), used as an instruction-following evaluation benchmark in Modular Gradient Surgery paper (arXiv:2602.02301).

name: CreativeWriting
num_samples: not disclosed (curated set of creative writing prompts)
format: Creative writing evaluation benchmark with open-ended generation prompts. Evaluated with LLM judge for quality assessment.
access: referenced as CreativeWriting benchmark in MGS paper; verify public availability
notes: Creative writing benchmark used as an open-ended chat evaluation in Modular Gradient Surgery paper (arXiv:2602.02301).

name: CoderEval
format: Code generation tasks extracted from real-world GitHub repositories; requires pragmatic context-aware code generation
notes: Benchmark from Yu et al. (ICSE 2024) for pragmatic code generation with pre-trained models. Tasks extracted from real-world repositories requiring context-aware generation. Used in CAM paper (arXiv:2602.02138) for evaluating multi-agent code generation systems.

name: HARDVS
storage: ~20-40GB estimated (event streams at high temporal resolution)
format: Event camera recordings with per-event polarity and timestamp; 300 daily action classes performed by 5 subjects
notes: Large-scale event-based action recognition dataset (HARDVS: Human Activity Recognition with Dynamic Vision Sensors). Revises earlier datasets by adding more action classes and subjects. Standard split: train on subset, test on held-out subjects.

name: DailyDVS-200
num_samples: 22,046 sequences (200 daily action categories, 14 environmental challenges)
format: Event camera recordings with per-event polarity and timestamp; 200 daily action categories with 14 environmental challenges including camera motion and illumination changes
notes: DailyDVS-200 benchmark for event-based action recognition, featuring 200 daily action categories and 14 environmental challenge conditions. Designed to test robustness to camera motion and illumination variations.

name: WebGen-Bench
format: natural language user instructions → interactive websites
notes: Benchmark for evaluating LLMs on generating interactive and functional websites from user instructions; uses GUI-agent judge to evaluate frontend; source of user instructions for FullStack-Bench (arXiv:2602.03798). Paper: Lu et al., 2025b.

name: FullStack-Bench
num_samples: 101 user instructions, 647 frontend test cases, 604 backend test cases, 389 database test cases
eval_time: hours-days (per model, 101 websites × hundreds of test cases)
format: natural language user instructions → full-stack websites (frontend + backend + database); agent judges evaluate each aspect
metric: frontend accuracy, backend accuracy, database accuracy (all YES/NO), appearance score
notes: Benchmark for evaluating full-stack website generation agents; tests frontend, backend, AND database functionalities separately; includes database interaction validation for frontend/backend tests; built on WebGen-Bench user instructions; paper: FullStack-Agent (arXiv:2602.03798).

name: STILL
num_samples: ~1000+ reasoning traces (paper filters to traces >4096 tokens for training)
format: Long-form reasoning traces (math, coding, summarization tasks) generated by Qwen3-4B; each trace contains problem, reasoning steps, and final answer; filtered to >4096 tokens for training
notes: Imitate, Explore, and Self-Improve (Min et al., 2024, arXiv:2412.09413). Used in ForesightKV (arXiv:2602.03203) as training data for KV cache eviction scoring model. Paper filters traces exceeding 4096 tokens to ensure long-form reasoning quality.

name: COPA
format: Choice of Plausible Alternatives: given a premise and two choices, select the correct causal consequence. Commonsense causal reasoning task.
notes: From Gordon et al., 2012, SemEval 2012 Task 7. Used in AUSteer paper (arXiv:2602.04428) for commonsense reasoning evaluation.

name: MAWPS
format: Math word problem repository: arithmetic word problems requiring numerical reasoning. Evaluates model ability to solve math problems with or without reasoning steps.
access: https://github.com/arkilpatel/SVAMP or original MAWPS at https://github.com/nigyar/MAWPS
notes: From Koncel-Kedziorski et al., 2016, NAACL. Used in AUSteer paper (arXiv:2602.04428) for math problem solving evaluation. SVAMP is a subset with structural variations.

name: BPO
num_samples: ~100-500 prompts (prompts from Liang et al., 2024; evaluation protocol from Zheng et al., 2023)
eval_time: hours (requires GPT-5-mini judge for win-rate evaluation)
format: Black-box Prompt Optimization: evaluates LLM alignment with human-preferred behaviors via automatic win-rate evaluation using GPT-5-mini as judge. Prompts test instruction following and response quality.
access: Prompts from Liang et al. 2024 (ACL); evaluation follows Zheng et al. 2023 mt-bench protocol
notes: From Cheng et al., 2024, ACL. Used in AUSteer paper (arXiv:2602.04428) for open-ended generation alignment evaluation.

name: REAL275
