num_samples: 4.3K training + 2.75K testing RGB-D images, 6 categories (bottle, bowl, camera, can, laptop, mug)
format: Real-world RGB-D images for category-level 6D pose estimation; part of NOCS benchmark suite; 7 training scenes and 6 test scenes; provides symmetry-aware rotation error evaluation for ambiguous categories
metric: mAP @ threshold combinations: 5°2cm, 5°5cm, 10°2cm, 10°5cm (rotation threshold + translation threshold)
notes: Real-world test set for NOCS category-level 6D pose estimation. Training on REAL275 uses 4.3K images from 7 scenes. Published in Wang et al., CVPR 2019.

name: Omni6DPose
num_samples: Large-scale RGB-D dataset, broader object diversity than NOCS
format: Large-scale RGB-D dataset for universal 6D object pose estimation and tracking; broader categories than NOCS; provides both RGB and depth modalities
notes: Published in Zhang et al., ECCV 2024. Designed for universal 6D pose estimation with broader category coverage than NOCS. Paper: 'Omni6DPose: A benchmark and model for universal 6D object pose estimation and tracking.'

name: Office-Home
eval_time: minutes on single GPU for k-NN transfer
format: Images from 4 domains: Art, Clipart, Product, Real World. Used for domain adaptation and k-NN downstream transfer evaluation in unlearning papers.

name: DomainNet-126
eval_time: minutes on single GPU for k-NN transfer
format: Subset of DomainNet with 126 classes containing most samples. Multi-domain adaptation benchmark. Used for k-NN downstream transfer evaluation in unlearning papers.

name: CodeForces
format: Competitive programming problems with reference solutions; evaluated via CodeForces rating system

name: DeepCoder
format: Code generation training dataset for RL; problems with reference solutions from competitive programming

name: CronQuestions
format: Temporal KG (s,p,o,t) quadruples + QA pairs. Questions require temporal reasoning with before/after, first/last, and time join operations.
access: https://github.com/apoorv saxena/CronKGQA (original); results reported in Saxena et al., 2021 ACL
notes: From Saxena et al., 2021 'Questioning Temporal Knowledge Graphs' (ACL). Tests temporal reasoning over cronological knowledge graphs with simple and complex question types. Used as primary benchmark in TKG-Thinker paper (arXiv:2602.05818).

name: TimelineKGQA
format: Temporal KG with timeline-based reasoning + QA pairs. Simple=1 fact, Medium=2 facts, Complex=3 facts. Tests temporal arithmetic and compositional reasoning.
notes: From Sun et al., 2025 WWW. Cross-domain benchmark with two sub-datasets: Timeline-CronQuestion (derived from CronQuestions) and Timeline-ICEWS (derived from ICEWS event KG). Tests cross-domain generalization of TKG reasoning. Used in TKG-Thinker paper (arXiv:2602.05818) appendix.

name: BRUMO25
format: British University Mathematical Olympiad 2025 short-answer problems (30 curated prompts)
metric: exact answer accuracy (32 sampled generations per question)

name: dapo-math-17k
format: Math reasoning problem-solution pairs for teacher rollout generation in NEX paper (2602.05805)
access: public math reasoning dataset used in NEX paper

name: deepmath-103k
format: Large-scale math reasoning dataset with difficulty labels (1.0-10.0); used for teacher rollout generation in NEX paper (2602.05805)
access: public math reasoning dataset used in NEX paper

name: deepscaler
format: Math reasoning dataset used for teacher rollout generation in NEX paper (2602.05805)
access: public math reasoning dataset used in NEX paper

name: MovieGen-Bench
format: Text prompts from MovieGen paper (Polyak et al. 2024) for evaluating long video generation consistency; used with DINOv2, CLIP-F, and CLIP-T for consistency metrics
metric: DINOv2 structural identity, CLIP-F semantic context, CLIP-T prompt alignment
access: Referenced in Polyak et al. 2024 (MovieGen paper)
notes: Used in Context Forcing paper (arXiv:2602.06028) for 60-second video consistency evaluation.

name: Vid-ProM
storage: ~TB scale (high-quality real-world videos with text prompts)
format: Large-scale prompt-gallery dataset of real videos with text descriptions for T2V training; curated from web sources with quality filtering
notes: From Wang & Yang 2024. Used as the training dataset for the student model in Context Forcing (Stage 1 and Stage 2).

name: Ultravideo
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed; filtered subset of high-quality UHD videos >10s used in paper
format: High-quality UHD (UltraHD) video dataset with comprehensive captions; covers diverse scenarios for video generation training
notes: From Xue et al. 2025. Used alongside Sekai for training the Context Teacher in Context Forcing paper (arXiv:2602.06028).

name: DASB
num_samples: multiple subsets for ASR and IC evaluation
format: Discrete audio and speech benchmark; evaluates both acoustic reconstruction and downstream semantic tasks (ASR, Intent Classification)
notes: Discrete Audio and Speech Benchmark introduced in Mousavi et al. (arXiv:2406.14294, 2024). Used in STACodec paper for evaluating ASR (with BiLSTM acoustic model on LibriSpeech) and Intent Classification (with BiLSTM on SLURP).

name: VERSA
format: Versatile evaluation toolkit for speech, audio, and music; supports PESQ, STOI, ViSQOL, speaker similarity metrics
notes: VERSA toolkit (Shi et al., Interspeech 2025) used for audio reconstruction evaluation in STACodec paper. Computes objective metrics including PESQ, STOI, ViSQOL, and speaker similarity using RawNet3 embeddings.

name: OmniVideoBench
format: Multiple-choice QA for synergistic audio-visual reasoning, emphasizing modality complementarity and logical coherence
notes: From Li et al., 2025a (OmniVideoBench paper). Used in OmniVideo-R1 (arXiv:2602.05847) as primary evaluation benchmark.

name: Daily-Omni
format: Audio-visual QA dataset with daily-life videos rich in auditory and visual cues, covering 6 major tasks
notes: From Zhou et al., 2025b (Daily-Omni paper). Used in OmniVideo-R1 (arXiv:2602.05847) as evaluation benchmark.

name: WorldSense
num_samples: 3172 QA pairs from 1662 synchronized audio-visual videos, 26 tasks across 8 domains
format: Emphasizes omnimodal collaboration with strongly coupled audio-video tasks requiring synergistic multimodal perception
notes: From Benchekroun et al., 2023 (WorldSense paper). Used in OmniVideo-R1 (arXiv:2602.05847) as evaluation benchmark.

name: IntentBench
format: Evaluates understanding of complex human intentions and emotions grounded in auditory and visual cues
notes: From Yang et al., 2025b (HumanOmniV2 paper). Used in OmniVideo-R1 (arXiv:2602.05847) as evaluation benchmark.

name: VideoHolmes
num_samples: 1837 questions from 270 suspense short films, 7 tasks
format: Sherlock Holmes-inspired benchmark for complex video reasoning requiring connection of dispersed visual clues and causal events
notes: From Cheng et al., 2025 (VideoHolmes paper). Used in OmniVideo-R1 (arXiv:2602.05847) as evaluation benchmark.

name: RealDoc-160
format: Photographed documents printed and captured with mobile phones under diverse real-world conditions (lighting, viewpoint, deformations)
license: research (self-constructed by authors; verify public availability)
access: Not publicly released; used in Dolphin-v2 paper (arXiv:2602.05384)
notes: Self-constructed benchmark by Dolphin-v2 authors for evaluating photographed document parsing. 160 pages selected from in-house collections, printed and recaptured with mobile phones.

name: DocPTBench
format: Photographed documents with geometric distortions and photometric variations, with human-verified OCR annotations
notes: Benchmark for photographed document parsing and translation from arXiv:2511.18434. Addresses real-world capture conditions including geometric distortions and photometric variations.

name: BOUQuET
format: Multilingual-to-English translation dataset with paragraph and sentence granularity across 5 languages

name: FMD (Material Perception Dataset)
format: 1,000 images across 10 material categories (e.g., fabric, metal, wood); 5-fold cross-validation used in TwistNet-2D paper (arXiv:2602.07262)
access: http://www.materialperception.com/ (Sharan et al., Journal of Vision 2009)

name: XLRS (Extremely Large Remote Sensing)
num_samples: ~hundreds of ultra-high-resolution remote sensing images with VQA
format: Extremely large and high-resolution remote sensing images (avg 8500x8500 pixels) with visual question answering; tests VLM generalization to non-standard visual domains (remote sensing) not common in instruction-tuning corpora
notes: XLRS-bench: Out-of-distribution benchmark from SPARC paper (arXiv:2602.06566) for evaluating VLMs on extremely large ultra-high-resolution remote sensing imagery. Average image dimension is 8500x8500 pixels. Used as OOD proxy to test model generalization beyond standard domains (documents, UIs, natural images).

name: FlashHolmes
format: Streamlined version of Holmes benchmark; covers morphology (19 tasks), syntax (75 tasks), semantics (67 tasks), discourse (28 tasks), and reasoning (19 tasks); uses linear classifier probing on model representations
notes: Designed to efficiently evaluate linguistic competence of language models. FlashHolmes is a reduced version of Holmes covering 66 linguistic phenomena with nearly 200 probing datasets.

name: IntPhys
format: Synthetic videos of possible and impossible physical events (object permanence, shape constancy, spatiotemporal continuity violations)

name: Craftax
eval_time: ~10-48 hours for 2B timesteps depending on method complexity
format: JAX-based open-ended RL benchmark featuring procedurally generated worlds with crafting, combat, survival, and resource gathering mechanics; long-horizon progression through multiple floors; evaluation on 1024 held-out unseen worlds
notes: Introduced in Matthews et al. 2024 (arXiv:2402.16801). Used in DiCode paper (arXiv:2602.08194) as the primary benchmark for open-ended curriculum learning evaluation.

name: ManiSkill2
num_samples: N/A (trajectory demonstrations for dexterous manipulation tasks)
format: Dexterous robotic manipulation with contact-rich interactions; tasks include StackCube, TurnFaucet, PushChair; RGB-D observations + state-action trajectories in HDF5 format
notes: From Gu et al. (ICLR 2023). Benchmark for generalizable manipulation skills with diverse object-centric tasks and contact-rich interactions.

name: Push-T
num_samples: N/A (trajectory demonstrations for contact-rich pushing task)
format: Contact-rich task: push a T-shaped block to a target with a circular end-effector; RGB images + state observations; adapted from IBC (Florence et al., 2022)
access: Part of Diffusion Policy codebase (Chi et al., 2025)
notes: Push-T is a contact-rich manipulation task adapted from Implicit Behavioral Cloning (IBC). Used in the STEP paper (arXiv:2602.08245) and other diffusion policy works.

name: YTSEG
eval_time: minutes per video for topic segmentation inference
format: YouTube videos with transcripts, chapter annotations, topic segment boundaries. Configs: text-only (16,404 train / 1,447 val / 1,448 test) and audio (with embedded audio ~68.3GB). Fields: text_ref, text_wt (Whisper-tiny), text_wl (Whisper-large), target_binary_*, target_text_*, channel_id, video_id, chapter_titles, chapter_timestamps.
metric: F1, Precision, Recall (boundary-level), Pk, B (segmentation metrics)
notes: Large-scale topic segmentation dataset from Retkowski & Waibel (EACL 2024). Covers science, lifestyle, politics, health, economy, technology in podcast, lecture, news formats. Used for training and evaluating MultiSeg (arXiv:2602.06647).

name: AVLECTURES
format: Lecture videos with topic segment annotations. Used in cross-dataset evaluation for MultiSeg paper (arXiv:2602.06647). Preprocessing: Whisper large-v2 transcription, Montreal Forced Aligner sync, SpaCy sentence segmentation.
access: See original paper Darshan Singh S et al. 2023
notes: English lecture dataset used for zero-shot cross-dataset evaluation in MultiSeg paper (arXiv:2602.06647). No training on this dataset — only evaluation. Shows modest gains (+1.82 F1) for multi-modal vs text-only.

name: VIDEOAULA
num_samples: 34 Portuguese lecture videos covering computer science
format: Portuguese lecture videos with topic segment annotations. Used in cross-lingual evaluation for MultiSeg paper (arXiv:2602.06647).
access: See original paper (Soares & Barrere, Proc. WebMedia 2018)
notes: Portuguese lecture dataset showing large gains for multi-modal (+20.2 F1 vs text-only) in MultiSeg paper. Multilingual model variants (Ml. MiniSeg+, Ml. MultiSeg) trained on English YTSEG and evaluated on Portuguese.

name: LECTUREDE
num_samples: 95 German lecture videos covering engineering, social sciences, didactics
format: German lecture videos with topic segment annotations. Used in cross-lingual evaluation for MultiSeg paper (arXiv:2602.06647).
access: See original paper (Freisinger et al., SLaTE 2023)
notes: German lecture dataset used for zero-shot cross-lingual evaluation in MultiSeg paper (arXiv:2602.06647). Shows moderate gains for multi-modal (+6.93 F1 vs text-only). Multilingual model variants trained on English YTSEG and evaluated on German.

name: MIND
num_samples: Multiple video clips with frame-aligned action labels; two disjoint subsets: First-Person (1ST-P) and Third-Person (3RD-P)
eval_time: Hours for full evaluation with VBench and RPE metrics
format: Videos with 8-action labels (navigation: W/S/A/D, camera: look up/down/left/right) collected in Unreal Engine 5
metric: VBench (image quality, temporal consistency), RPE (relative pose error for action accuracy)
notes: Benchmark for world models with memory consistency and action control. Same 8-action label space across both subsets, enabling cross-context transfer evaluation.

name: EMIME
eval_time: minutes to hours for VC target selection
format: 16kHz read speech; includes Mandarin-English and German-English bilingual speakers; used for target speaker selection in voice conversion experiments
notes: EMIME bilingual database used in TVTSyn paper for selecting target speakers in voice conversion and anonymization experiments. Speakers provide both native and non-native English speech.

name: Video-CraftBench
num_samples: ~7 hours of video (~9.5k clips training; ~150 test videos); tasks include paper folding (40-80s, 7 steps) and block building (20-30s)
eval_time: minutes to hours per method (3 video rollouts per test case, DINOv2 step classifier evaluation)
format: First-person handcraft tutorial videos (paper folding: airplane, boat; block building: tower, horse, person); multi-step evaluation with step success detection
metric: Sequential task success rate (%) per step; SSIM and LPIPS for visual quality
notes: New benchmark introduced in VideoWorld 2 (arXiv:2602.10102) for evaluating learning of transferable knowledge from real-world videos. Test set features novel backgrounds, paper textures, and block arrangements not seen in training. DINOv2-based classifier evaluates 7 key steps of paper folding tasks.

name: FirstProof
eval_time: hours per problem at high compute
format: research-level math problems (Lemmas) in LaTeX
notes: Collection of 10 research-level math problems proposed by academic mathematicians (Abouzaid et al., 2026) for AI evaluation. Problems are Lemmas from active research, all solved but solutions not public at time of challenge.

name: IMO-Proof Bench
format: Olympiad-level math problems with proof evaluation
notes: Benchmark of 30 IMO-level problems used during IMO 2025 preparation. Advanced subset used in paper's evaluations.

name: FutureMath Basic
eval_time: hours per problem at high compute
format: PhD-level mathematics exercises
notes: Internal Google benchmark for PhD-level mathematics knowledge, used to assess readiness for research-grade math.

name: Erdős Problems
format: open math problems with status tracking
notes: Centralized repository of Erdős conjectures and problems. At time of paper's study (Dec 2025), 700 were marked Open. Paper used a subset for evaluation.

name: Real-Fermi
format: Order-of-magnitude estimation problems requiring reasoning about physical quantities (e.g., 'How much coffee was consumed during EMNLP 2019?')
notes: From Kalyan et al. (2021). Fermi problems require order-of-magnitude reasoning. Used in Chain of Mindset (arXiv:2602.10063) evaluation.

name: MAZE (MVoT benchmark)
format: Maze images where models choose the final position after executing a given action sequence from the starting point. Generated using maze-dataset (Ivanitskiy et al., 2023) following MVoT protocol.
notes: From Li et al. (2025) and Zhang et al. (2025). Used in Chain of Mindset (arXiv:2602.10063) for spatial reasoning evaluation. 100% of MAZE problems invoke Spatial mindset in CoM.

name: Plot2Code
format: Scientific plots from Matplotlib gallery converted to executable code; evaluates code generation from plot images; Direct Asking task with Pass Rate, Text-Match, and GPT-4o Rating metrics
notes: Comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multi-modal large language models in code generation from scientific plots. 132 test samples from Matplotlib gallery. Used as main benchmark in ChartSpec paper (arXiv:2602.10880).

name: ISOT
format: Text-only news articles labeled as real or fake, aggregated from multiple sources for fake news classification
notes: From Ahmed et al., 2017. Used in OmniVL-Guard (arXiv:2602.10687) for out-of-domain text fake news detection evaluation.

name: MM-FakeBench
format: Image-text pairs with multimodal misinformation including textual veracity distortion, visual veracity distortion, and cross-modal consistency changes
notes: Used in OmniVL-Guard (arXiv:2602.10687) for out-of-domain image-text multimodal fake news detection evaluation.

name: FakeSV
num_samples: Chinese short-video news with multiple modalities
format: Chinese short-video news with videos, audio, text, and social context metadata; annotated as real, fake, or debunked
notes: From Qi et al., 2023. Used in OmniVL-Guard (arXiv:2602.10687) for out-of-domain video-text multimodal fake detection evaluation.

name: SWIG-HOI
format: images + HOI annotations (human-verb-object triplets) with 400+ action categories and 1000+ object categories
notes: Large-vocabulary HOI benchmark built on SWiG dataset. Contains many unseen action combinations in test set. Used in ImagineAgent paper (arXiv:2602.11499) for evaluating open-vocabulary HOI detection.

name: HOVER
format: Claim + label (SUPPORTS/REFUTES) requiring multi-hop reasoning over multiple Wikipedia articles
notes: HOppy VERification dataset. Multi-hop fact extraction and claim verification requiring reasoning over 2-4 interconnected Wikipedia articles. Average 2.4 hops per claim. Used in DiffuTruth paper (2602.11364) as out-of-distribution generalization test.

name: LongFact-Objects
num_samples: ~38 subject areas, LLM-generated open-ended questions per area
format: Open-ended factual questions across 38 domains (science, history, etc.); evaluated by atomic claim fact-checking
metric: Risk-Coverage curve; AURC (Area Under Risk-Coverage curve)
notes: LongFact-Objects benchmark from Wei et al. (NeurIPS 2024). LLM-generated open-ended questions across 38 subject areas eliciting detailed factual long-form responses. Used in Selective Abstraction paper (arXiv:2602.11908) alongside FactScore.

name: IF-Eval
format: Prompt-level strict accuracy evaluation using rules extracted from instruction templates; evaluates whether model responses follow given instructions precisely
notes: From Zhou et al. (2023). Used in OPCD paper (arXiv:2602.12275) as an out-of-distribution evaluation to measure catastrophic forgetting after context distillation.

name: TextArena
format: Text-based game environments (Frozen Lake, Sokoban, etc.) with textual state descriptions; models interact in multi-turn settings to reach goals or solve puzzles
notes: From Guertler et al. (2025). Used in OPCD paper (arXiv:2602.12275) for experiential knowledge distillation experiments on Frozen Lake and Sokoban tasks.

name: PolaRiS (Polarimetric Robot Manipulation Dataset)
num_samples: ~50 episodes per task, 3 tasks (PanClean, BlockStack, FoodBussing)
eval_time: Minutes per task per model checkpoint
format: Real-to-sim benchmark based on DROID dataset; tasks involve multi-object manipulation with distractors; evaluated in simulation with photorealistic rendering
notes: From Jain et al. 2025. Used in CoVer-VLA paper (2602.12281) to evaluate VLA robustness with test-time verification. Tasks: stacking blocks on green tray, placing foods in bowl, scrubbing pan with sponge.

name: GRAB
format: Whole-body human motion capture with object interactions; includes hand poses, object poses, contact annotations; AMASS data format

name: DeViBench
format: QA pairs assessing MLLM accuracy under RTC-induced video degradation; includes test and validation splits; 6 QA types (text-rich, attribute perception, object perception, counting, action perception, spatial understanding)
notes: Degraded Video Understanding Benchmark from Artic paper (arXiv:2602.12641). Automated QA construction pipeline using MLLMs. 91.72% intra-frame, 8.28% inter-frame questions. $48.06 cost to construct, 102,704s generation time.

name: ToolSandbox
format: Multi-turn, multi-step tool-use benchmark with diverse scenarios and tool augmentations. Evaluates agent performance on complex tool-use trajectories including multi-tool interactions.
notes: Used in CM2 paper (arXiv:2602.12268) to evaluate RL-trained agents on multi-turn tool-use tasks. Supports diverse tool types and scenarios.

name: Encyclopedic-VQA (E-VQA)
format: Visual questions about fine-grained encyclopedic entities requiring external Wikipedia knowledge; includes single-hop and multi-hop (2-hop) question types
notes: Knowledge-intensive VQA benchmark with controlled knowledge base from WikiWeb2M (2M Wikipedia articles). Used in REAL paper (2602.14065) as a primary evaluation benchmark.

name: MMKC
num_samples: 1,573 knowledge instances, 3,381 images, 892 test samples used
format: Multimodal knowledge conflict benchmark with three types (Image-Text, Text-Text conflicts); collected via automated pipelines with human verification
notes: Benchmark for evaluating multimodal knowledge conflicts in LMMs. Used in REAL paper (2602.14065) for conflict discrimination generalization evaluation.

name: REAL-VQA
format: KI-VQA dataset with reasoning-pivot conflict annotations; includes no-conflict, subtle-conflict, and high-conflict samples; built using GPT-4o with Wikipedia data
access: Constructed by authors of REAL paper (2602.14065); contact authors
notes: Dataset constructed by REAL paper authors for training and evaluating reasoning-pivot based conflict detection. Key contribution of REAL framework. Not yet publicly released at time of paper publication.

name: VPBench-Edit
eval_time: minutes per model for full evaluation
format: Video editing benchmark with text prompts and per-frame edit masks specifying target regions for modification. Each video has corresponding descriptive text prompts for the desired edit.
metric: PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, MSE, MAE (masked region preservation); CLIP Score, CLIP(M) (text-video alignment); CLIP Sim (temporal coherence)
notes: VPBench-Edit is the video editing benchmark from VideoPainter (Bian et al., SIGGRAPH 2025). Used as primary editing benchmark in EditCtrl (Litman et al., arXiv:2602.15031). EditCtrl outperforms VideoPainter and VACE on this benchmark at 10x less compute.

name: VPBench-Inp
eval_time: minutes per model for full evaluation
format: Video inpainting benchmark with text prompts and per-frame masks for arbitrary-shaped masked region inpainting.
metric: PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, MSE, MAE (masked region preservation); CLIP Score, CLIP(M) (text-video alignment); CLIP Sim (temporal coherence)
notes: VPBench-Inp is the video inpainting benchmark from VideoPainter (Bian et al., SIGGRAPH 2025). Used alongside DAVIS 2017 for inpainting evaluation in EditCtrl (Litman et al., arXiv:2602.15031). EditCtrl matches or exceeds VideoPainter and VACE on inpainting quality at significantly higher throughput.

name: GenEval++
num_samples: ~1000+ (similar to GenEval with more complex instructions)
eval_time: ~4-6 GPU hours for full evaluation on 1xA100
format: Compositional text-to-image generation prompts with more complex instructions than GenEval; evaluates object counting, color/position/size attributes, multi-count scenarios; evaluated by advanced VLMs (Qwen-2.5-VL-72B)

name: ACD (Articulated Object Dataset)
format: Articulated 3D objects with part-level annotations and joint parameters. Curated from S2O: Static-to-Openable enhancement benchmark (arXiv:2409.18896). Objects include cabinets, drawers, doors, and other openable furniture.
metric: dgIoU, dcDist, dCD, AOR, CLIP similarity (same as PartNet-Mobility)

name: ESAP 2025
format: 4-choice MC (clinical vignettes)
access: Purchase from Endocrine Society; not publicly available

name: BSDS500 (Berkeley Segmentation Dataset)
format: Natural images with multiple human-annotated boundaries; ground truth is average of annotations

name: NYUDv2 (NYU Depth Dataset v2)
format: Indoor RGB-D images with semantic segmentation and edges; includes RGB and depth images

name: BIPED (Barcelona Images for Edge Detection)
format: High-resolution images with crisp, fine-grained edge annotations; designed for precise edge detection evaluation

name: CubiCasa5k
format: Floorplan images with multi-task annotations including wall polygons; used for wall-boundary detection; images resized to 512x512
license: Research use (Scandinavian Conference on Image Analysis)

name: IndicVisionBench-OCR
format: Multilingual Indic OCR benchmark covering 10 Indic languages (Hindi, Sanskrit, Bengali, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Odia) and English; evaluates word-level and character-level ANLS
access: Not publicly released (Faraz et al., 2025, arXiv:2511.04727)
notes: Benchmark introduced by the same authors. Used to evaluate Chitrapathak multilingual OCR models. Languages include: Hindi, Sanskrit, Bengali, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Odia.

name: Synthdog
format: Synthetic document understanding dataset for OCR evaluation; documents are synthetically generated with various layouts, fonts, and content
access: From Donut paper (Kim et al., ECCV 2022); code at github.com/clovaai/donut
notes: Used in paper to evaluate English OCR capabilities. Chitrapathak-2 achieves 24.90 word ANLS and 20.20 char ANLS on this benchmark.

name: Old Books OCR
format: Historical book OCR dataset for evaluating OCR on old printed materials
notes: Used to evaluate Chitrapathak-2's retention of English OCR on historical books. Paper reports 4.49 word ANLS and 1.89 char ANLS.

name: UW-StereoDepth-80K
format: synthetic underwater stereo image pairs with ground-truth disparity
notes: Large-scale synthetic underwater stereo dataset generated via Atlantis (style transfer) + NVS-Solver (novel view synthesis) from terrestrial RGB-D data (NYU v2, ScanNet). Used in StereoAdapter-2 (arXiv:2602.16915). Includes 4 baselines (20/30/40/50cm) and varying attenuation/scattering parameters.

name: RetailOpt-190
format: Natural language retail optimization problem descriptions (JSON-embedded) -> GurobiPy solver code; evaluated by objective value matching and status correctness
metric: Execution rate (Exec%), Strict accuracy (Acc% at epsilon=1e-4), Practical accuracy (Acc% at epsilon=1e-2), Silent failure rate
license: MIT (code and data released on GitHub)
notes: From ReLoop paper (Lian et al., arXiv:2602.15983). Multi-period retail inventory optimization with compositional constraints (perishability, substitution, capacity, lead times, MOQ, pack sizes, network flows). 8 scenario families, 38 archetypes, 5 numerical variants each. Ground truth computed by Gurobi 11.0 with 60s time limit. Key contribution: systematic study of the feasibility-correctness gap (up to 90pp) in LLM-generated optimization code.

name: MAMO
format: Natural language optimization problem descriptions -> solver-ready LP/MILP code; evaluated by comparing optimal solution values
notes: MAMO (Huang et al., arXiv:2405.13144): Mathematical Modeling Benchmark with Solvers. Includes EasyLP (simple linear programs), ComplexLP (challenging LP/MILP with some nonlinear), and other problem types. Used in ReLoop paper (arXiv:2602.15983) for cross-benchmark evaluation. MAMO-ComplexLP refers to the 203-instance challenging subset.

name: CASF-2016
format: Protein-ligand complex structures with binding affinity labels
metric: Rp (Pearson correlation for scoring), Rs (Spearman correlation for ranking), SR1 (docking success rate), EF1% (enrichment factor)
notes: Standard benchmark for protein-ligand scoring functions, derived from PDBbind v2016 core set. 285 complexes across 57 protein families. Evaluates scoring, ranking, docking, and screening tasks. Used in BioLM-Score paper (arXiv:2602.18476) as primary evaluation benchmark.

name: DEKOIS 2.0
num_samples: 81 targets x 1230 compounds each (30 actives + 1200 decoys)
format: 81 protein targets with known active ligands and decoy molecules for virtual screening evaluation
notes: Challenging virtual screening benchmark with 81 diverse targets. Each target has 30 known actives and 1200 decoys. Used to evaluate cross-target generalization of scoring functions. In BioLM-Score paper (arXiv:2602.18476), Glide SP was used to generate docking poses before rescoring.

name: Maze2D
num_samples: 7 maze layouts (Square-a, Square-b, Square-c, Square-d, Corridor2, Square-tree, Square-bottleneck)
format: Low-dimensional continuous-control navigation tasks in 2D maze environments; state space is 2D position; action space is 2D continuous velocity; used for reward-free exploration evaluation via state coverage
metric: State coverage ratio (proportion of discretized spatial bins visited over 100K steps)
notes: From Campos et al. (ICML 2020). Maze2D is a low-dimensional RL benchmark for evaluating pure exploration algorithms. Paper evaluates TEB on 7 maze variants. Unlike MetaWorld, Maze2D uses low-dimensional states (no image encoder needed), allowing direct metric computation over raw states for exploration bonuses.

name: GR-1 Tabletop
format: MuJoCo simulation with GR-1 humanoid robot (29 DoF: 17 arm/waist + 6 DoF per hand). Egocentric head camera RGB. Tabletop manipulation tasks: pick-and-place, articulated object manipulation (drawers, microwaves).
notes: Dexterous tabletop manipulation benchmark from NVIDIA. Used in RoboCurate (arXiv:2602.18742) for evaluating VLA policies with 300 and 1000 demonstrations. Tasks include object rearrangement and articulated object manipulation. From NVIDIA et al., arXiv:2503.14734, 2025.

name: DexMimicGen
num_samples: 6 tasks (3 GR-1 Humanoid + 3 Bimanual Panda Arms with Dexterous Hands)
format: MuJoCo simulation for bimanual dexterous manipulation. Supports cross-embodiment evaluation with GR-1 humanoid and Panda arms with 15-DoF dexterous hands. 100 demonstrations per task.
notes: Automated data generation for bimanual dexterous manipulation via imitation learning. Used in RoboCurate (arXiv:2602.18742) for cross-embodiment evaluation. From Jiang et al., ICRA 2025.

name: ALLEX Humanoid
num_samples: 3 tasks (1 in-distribution pick-and-place, 2 OOD tasks: novel object pick-and-place, novel behavior pour)
format: Real-world humanoid robot with ego-view camera and two 15-DoF dexterous hands (48-dimensional joint-space states and actions). Tabletop manipulation tasks.
notes: Real-world humanoid dexterous manipulation platform. Used in RoboCurate (arXiv:2602.18742) for co-finetuning experiments with 48 demonstrations for seen task and 50 episodes per OOD task. Platform supported by RLWRLD.

name: ActionNet (Fourier ActionNet)
num_samples: 30K teleoperated episodes (3K subset used after prompt filtering)
format: Bimanual tabletop manipulation trajectories on Fourier GR1-T1 humanoid. Ego-view camera RGB. 44-dimensional joint-space states and actions (6-DoF per hand + arm/waist).
notes: Large-scale dexterous bimanual manipulation dataset. Used in RoboCurate (arXiv:2602.18742) for pre-training VLA policies. Paper: Fourier ActionNet Team, 2025.

name: GR00T-GR1-1001
format: Robot manipulation trajectories from GR-1 humanoid. Used for video model fine-tuning in neural trajectory generation.
access: Referenced in Jang et al., arXiv:2505.12705 (DreamGen)
notes: Dataset used for fine-tuning Cosmos-Predict2-14B in DreamGen (Jang et al., 2025). RoboCurate (arXiv:2602.18742) uses this for video model pre-training. From DreamGen paper.

name: WikiMIA2024 Hard
num_samples: paired Wikipedia article versions (members are articles with versions before model knowledge cutoff; non-members are post-cutoff versions)
format: Paired Wikipedia article versions from before and after model knowledge cutoff dates; minimizes temporal distribution shift between member and non-member examples; supports original (verbatim) and paraphrased evaluation settings
notes: Hard variant of WikiMIA where most baseline MIAs perform near random. Used in ADRA paper (arXiv:2602.19020) for pre-training MIA. Qwen2-7B model cutoff (estimated 2023) aligns with dataset cutoff (2024).

name: Olympia Math
num_samples: random partition into member/non-member sets (dataset released 2025)
format: Olympiad-level math competition problems from AI-MO (AI-MO Olympiad Reference Dataset); member/non-member split by random partition; used for controlled post-training contamination MIA evaluation
notes: Used in ADRA paper (arXiv:2602.19020) for post-training membership inference with controlled contamination on Tulu2-7B.

name: AIME (ADRA split)
format: AIME math competition problems; members are problems from 2021-2024 (before model training cutoff); non-members are from 2025 (after cutoff); used for controlled post-training contamination MIA evaluation
access: Constructed by paper authors from publicly available AIME problems; source: https://artofproblemsolving.com/wiki/index.php/AIME_Problems_and_Solutions
notes: Used in ADRA paper (arXiv:2602.19020) for post-training membership inference with controlled contamination on Tulu2-7B. The 10% contamination rate is simulated by mixing member examples with Tulu2 SFT mix.

name: Dolma3 arXiv (MIA subset)
num_samples: 3000 member arXiv docs + 1000 non-member arXiv docs (post-2025 papers)
format: arXiv documents from Proof-Pile-2 (Dolma3 pre-training mix, cutoff April 2023); members are documents included in Dolma3 mix; non-members are verified absent via OlmoTrace; used for pre-training MIA on Olmo3-7B-Instruct
notes: Constructed in ADRA paper (arXiv:2602.19020) for pre-training membership inference evaluation on the fully-open Olmo3 model. Non-members verified not in training via OlmoTrace.

name: Tulu3 SFT Mix / Aya (MIA subset)
num_samples: 128 examples: 64 members (included in Tulu3 SFT mix) + 64 non-members (excluded from Tulu3 SFT mix)
format: Aya multilingual instruction-tuning dataset examples; members are examples included in Tulu3 SFT mix; non-members are from original Aya dataset excluded from Tulu3 mix; max 1024 tokens per turn
notes: Used in ADRA paper (arXiv:2602.19020) for post-training mixture MIA on Tulu3-8B. Constructed to control for length variation between members and non-members.

name: Tulu3 SFT Mix / WildChat (MIA subset)
num_samples: 128 examples: 64 members (included in Tulu3 SFT mix) + 64 non-members (excluded from Tulu3 SFT mix)
format: WildChat real-world ChatGPT interaction examples; members are interactions included in Tulu3 SFT mix; non-members are from original WildChat dataset excluded from Tulu3 mix; max 1024 tokens per turn
notes: Used in ADRA paper (arXiv:2602.19020) for post-training mixture MIA on Tulu3-8B. Constructed to control for length variation between members and non-members.

name: S1 / S1.1 Distillation Traces
num_samples: 256 examples: 128 member traces (from one teacher) + 128 non-member traces (from the other teacher)
format: Reasoning traces from teacher models (Gemini-2.0-Flash for S1, DeepSeek-R1 for S1.1); member and non-member share identical prefixes but differ in generated suffix; Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct distilled on member traces as student
notes: Used in ADRA paper (arXiv:2602.19020) for distillation membership inference. Near-perfect membership inference achieved (98.4% AUROC for DeepSeek-R1 traces). S1 from Muennighoff et al. (2025).

name: DNALongBench
num_samples: 3 long-range genomics tasks (CMP, eQTL, ETGP) across multiple tissues/cell lines
format: DNA sequences (256bp to 1M bp) with functional labels (Hi-C contact maps, eQTL tissue-specific SNP-gene associations, enhancer-gene pairs)

name: AgenticRAGTracer
num_samples: 1,305 multi-hop QA examples (2-4 hops; Inference and Comparison topologies)
eval_time: 1-2 hours for full evaluation across 13 models (via API + local inference)
format: Multi-hop QA with hop-level intermediate questions and answers; evaluation via ReAct agent paradigm using Qwen-Agent framework; metrics: EM, F1, LLM-as-a-Judge
notes: First hop-aware benchmark for Agentic RAG. Enables step-level failure diagnosis (collapsed vs. over-extended reasoning trajectories). Automated LLM-driven construction pipeline with multi-stage verification (structural integrity, semantic logic, multi-hop necessity). Wikipedia-based knowledge corpus. Even GPT-5 achieves only 22.6% EM on 4-hop inference subset.

name: Frontier-CS
format: Natural language problem descriptions with executable program evaluation; global optima unknown; solutions scored by program output correctness
metric: Score (0-100) based on program execution results
notes: Challenging benchmark of 172 open-ended computer science problems ranging from algorithmic optimization to research-level systems tasks. Used in AdaEvolve paper (arXiv:2602.20133) to evaluate LLM-driven evolutionary program synthesis. AdaEvolve achieves mean 61.33 vs 50.75 (OpenEvolve), 47.79 (ShinkaEvolve), 43.04 (GEPA).

name: ADRS (AI-Driven Systems Research Benchmark)
format: Real-world systems optimization tasks with executable evaluators; noisy feedback; heterogeneous objective scales
metric: Varies by task (e.g., score for Telemetry Repair, cost reduction for Cloudcast, throughput for EPLB, latency for NS3)
notes: ADRS benchmark suite comprises 7 real-world systems tasks: Telemetry Repair, Cloudcast (multi-cloud cost optimization), EPLB (Expert Parallelism Load Balancer), Prism (Model Placement), LLM-SQL (prefix cache optimization), TXN (Transaction Scheduling), NS3 (TCP Congestion Control). Used in AdaEvolve paper to evaluate adaptive evolutionary search on systems optimization.

name: RealEstate10K (RE10k)
format: Video clips with camera poses from YouTube, for view synthesis research

name: FixEval
num_samples: 243k buggy-correct Python code pairs (384 randomly selected for paper evaluation)
format: Buggy and correct submission code pairs for competitive programming problems. Each pair consists of a buggy version and a correct version of code solving the same programming problem.
metric: bug detection rate (% of distinguishable buggy versions)
notes: Bug detection benchmark from IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Automated Program Repair (APR) 2023. Used to evaluate whether generated postconditions can distinguish buggy from correct code. In SPEC-MIND paper, 384 bugs were randomly selected from 157,355 pairs (after filtering runtime errors).

name: Dress4D
num_samples: ~78,000 high-quality textured clothed-human scans across 64 garment categories (4 dresses, 28 lower, 30 upper, 32 outer garments)
format: 4D clothing dataset: real-world 4D video sequences with accurate camera parameters, SMPL body fits, and per-frame garment meshes. 4 loose-fitting outfits.
metric: Chamfer Distance, F-Score (harmonic mean of precision/recall)
notes: From Wang et al., CVPR 2024. Used in NGL-Prompter (arXiv:2602.20700) for evaluating 3D garment reconstruction from single images. The paper uses a subset of 36 images with loose-fitting outfits.

name: CloSe
num_samples: 3,167 clothed-human 3D scans with fine-grained clothing segmentation across 18 categories
format: 3D clothing segmentation dataset: 3D scans with per-garment segmentation labels, body pose, and mesh. Higher resolution than Dress4D.
notes: From Antic et al., 3DV 2024. Used in NGL-Prompter (arXiv:2602.20700) with a subset of 145 images. Provides fine-grained clothing segmentation labels across 18 categories.

name: ASOS-5K
num_samples: ~5,000 in-the-wild fashion images spanning 21 garment categories; plus 164 labeled images (ASOS-labeled) and 224 unlabeled (ASOS-unlabeled)
format: In-the-wild fashion images scraped from ASOS website; ASOS-labeled subset has NGL attribute annotations; used for perceptual/AI evaluation of garment reconstruction quality
metric: AI perceptual score (0-9 scale), human preference score (-2 to 2)
access: Promised for release by NGL-Prompter authors
notes: Collected by NGL-Prompter authors (arXiv:2602.20700) for evaluating generalization to real-world fashion images. Used for multi-layer and single-layer perceptual studies.

name: FidelityBench-258K
num_samples: 258K subject-SDG image pairs from 29K subject images across 3 SDG baselines (FLUX.1-Kontext-Pro, Qwen-Image-Edit, Nano-Banana-Edit)
eval_time: hours to days depending on model
format: Subject reference images paired with SDG-generated images and VLM-generated prompts
metric: AKI (Absolute Keypoint Increase), KGain (Keypoint Matching Gain), CLIP-I, DINOv2
notes: Large-scale subject-driven generation benchmark for evaluating fine detail preservation. Created using Claude 3.5 Sonnet for prompt generation. Includes FidelityBench-300 fixed subset for reproducible evaluation.

name: FidelityBench-300
num_samples: 300 subject-SDG image pairs (100 per SDG backbone)
format: Fixed subset of FidelityBench-258K for controlled ablation and human evaluation
notes: Fixed subset of FidelityBench-258K balanced across 3 SDG backbones for reproducible studies.

name: APTOS 2019 Blindness Detection
format: Retinal fundus images (JPEG) with 5-class ordinal severity labels (0-4: No DR, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Proliferative DR)
notes: Kaggle competition dataset for DR grading. Used in D-ODR paper (arXiv:2602.21942) as one of 4 evaluation datasets.

name: Messidor
format: Retinal fundus images with ordinal retinopathy grades (0-4) and additional clinical metadata
notes: Publicly distributed retinal image database. Used in D-ODR paper (arXiv:2602.21942) for DR grading evaluation.

name: DeepDRiD
format: Retinal fundus images with ordinal DR grades (0-4); includes quality and laterality labels
notes: From Liu et al. 2022 (DeepDRiD challenge). Used in D-ODR paper (arXiv:2602.21942) as evaluation dataset.

name: DDR
format: Retinal fundus images with DR severity grades (0-4) and lesion annotations
notes: Diagnostic Assessment of Deep Learning Algorithms for Diabetic Retinopathy Screening (Li et al., 2019). Used in D-ODR paper (arXiv:2602.21942) as one of 4 evaluation datasets.

name: GDRBench
format: Official train/val/test split protocol for DR datasets (APTOS, Messidor, DeepDRiD, DDR)
notes: Generalizable DR grading benchmark protocol. Used in D-ODR paper (arXiv:2602.21942) for standardized dataset splits.

name: BigBench MovieRec
format: Multiple-choice task: given a user query about movie preferences, select the correct movie from a list; canonicalized via option matching and text normalization to selected movie title

name: MELAUDIS
num_samples: ~9,600 single-vehicle audio clips (Car ~8,100, Tram ~600, Truck ~260, Bus ~260, Motorcycle ~250, Bicycle ~220)
storage: ~5-10GB estimated (stereo WAV files at 16kHz + log-mel spectrograms)
format: Stereo WAV recordings from fixed microphone arrays at Melbourne urban intersections; resampled to 16kHz, converted to 128-bin log-mel spectrograms (25ms window, 10ms hop, 20-8000Hz). 6-class vehicle classification: Car, Tram, Truck, Bus, Motorcycle, Bicycle.
license: Research use (publicly released by dataset creators)
access: https://github.com/... (original MELAUDIS repository by Aucouturier et al., 2024)
notes: Mel Spectrogram Dataset for Urban Acoustic Vehicle Identification and Surveillance. From Aucouturier et al., 2024. Used in 'Poisoned Acoustics' (arXiv:2602.22258) for studying data poisoning attacks on acoustic vehicle classifiers. Severe class imbalance (Car 84%, heavy vehicles ~3% each) makes minority classes vulnerable to stealth poisoning attacks.

name: PartNeXt
format: Textured 3D meshes with semantic part annotations; 2-20 parts per shape; used for part assembly evaluation
metric: Rotation Error (RE), Translation Error (TE), Part Accuracy (PA), Chamfer Distance (CD)
notes: Next-generation dataset for fine-grained and hierarchical 3D part understanding. Used as both training and evaluation dataset in CRAG paper. Focuses on semantic parts defined by functional/semantic boundaries rather than geometric fracture surfaces.

name: Breaking Bad
format: Fractured 3D meshes with ground-truth fracture surfaces and realignment; used for fracture reassembly
metric: Rotation Error (RE), Translation Error (TE), Part Accuracy (PA), Chamfer Distance (CD)
notes: Geometric fracture and reassembly dataset. CRAG evaluates on the everyday subset. Paper also uses MorphoSource bone models virtually fractured with Breaking Good, FractureRB, and FractureBEM to expand the dataset to 3,347 samples.

name: MorphoSource
num_samples: Thousands of 3D scans (primate bones and other animal bones)
format: Open-access repository of 3D digitial specimen scans; CRAG uses virtually fractured bone models for fracture reassembly training and evaluation
metric: N/A (used as training/eval data for fracture reassembly)
notes: Open-access 3D specimen repository. CRAG curates bone fragment collections from MorphoSource, virtually fractures them, and combines with Breaking Bad everyday subset for training/eval (3,347 total samples across 10 categories).

name: FRACTURA
num_samples: Real scanned fracture fragments (small dataset for validation)
format: Real-world scanned 3D fracture fragments for validation of fracture reassembly methods
access: Referenced in GARF paper (Li et al., 2025a)
notes: Used in CRAG paper for qualitative validation on real-world fractures, not as a quantitative benchmark. Complements synthetic fracture datasets like Breaking Bad.

name: MKG-W
num_samples: 15000 entities, 169 relations, 34196 train / 4276 valid / 4274 test triples, 14123 text descriptions
format: Multi-modal knowledge graph triples with textual descriptions and images. Derived from Wikidata and Wikipedia.
notes: Multi-modal KGC benchmark. Used in KGT paper (2602.22698).

name: MKG-Y
num_samples: 15000 entities, 28 relations, 21310 train / 2665 valid / 2663 test triples, 12305 text descriptions
format: Multi-modal knowledge graph triples with textual descriptions. Derived from YAGO and Wikidata.
notes: Multi-modal KGC benchmark. Used in KGT paper (2602.22698).

name: OpenImages-WSSS
num_samples: 37319 images across 100 classes (29819 train, 2500 val, 5000 test)
format: Images with class labels and pixel-level segmentation masks for weakly supervised semantic segmentation
notes: OpenImages subset used for Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation (WSSS) evaluation. From TriLite paper (arXiv:2602.23120). High intra-class variation and complex backgrounds make it challenging.

name: BBBC006
format: Fluorescence microscopy images of U2OS cancer cells stained with Hoechst 33342 and Phalloidin; 32-plane z-stacks at 2um spacing
metric: Accuracy, PLCC, SRCC, MAE (for FQA task)
notes: Fluorescence microscopy FQA dataset. From Ljosa et al. 2012. Used in FluoCLIP (arXiv:2602.23791).

name: FocusPath
format: Bright-field histology image patches (1024x1024) from 9 tissue types with H&E staining; z-stack focus levels
metric: Accuracy, PLCC, SRCC, MAE (for FQA task)
access: Check paper reference [11] or search 'FocusPath dataset microscopy' for official source
notes: Bright-field histology FQA dataset from Hosseini et al. 2019. 12 ordinal focus levels. Used in FluoCLIP (arXiv:2602.23791).

name: FluoMix
format: Fluorescence microscopy z-stacks (34 planes) from rat brain, lung, liver tissues; 4 fluorescent channels per FOV (Hoechst/DAPI, Alexa 488, Cy3, Alexa 647); 10 ordinal focus levels
metric: Accuracy, PLCC, SRCC, MAE (for stain-aware FQA task)
access: Not yet publicly available at time of analysis
notes: New fluorescence microscopy FQA dataset from FluoCLIP (arXiv:2602.23791). Multi-tissue (brain/lung/liver), multi-stain, z-stack microscopy. Stain-aware FQA task requires modeling focus as function of stain identity.

name: Occ-ScanNet
storage: ~50-100GB (processed voxel grids from ScanNet RGB-D scans)
eval_time: minutes to hours for full evaluation
format: 60x60x36 voxel grids covering 4.8m x 4.8m x 2.88m indoor volumes; 12 classes (11 semantic + empty); derived from ScanNet RGB-D data with SC-Fusion occupancy labels
notes: Indoor occupancy benchmark from Yu et al. (ECCV 2024). Built on ScanNet RGB-D scans. Used in LegoOcc paper (arXiv:2602.22667) as the primary evaluation dataset for monocular open-vocabulary indoor occupancy prediction.

name: DreamSim
format: Perceptual similarity metric between images using learned features from synthetic data; captures both high-level semantics and low-level visual features
notes: Used in SourceSwap (arXiv:2602.23697) as the primary metric for object fidelity evaluation in object swapping tasks.

name: SourceBench
storage: ~1-2GB estimated (high-resolution images from Pexels and Unsplash)
eval_time: hours for full evaluation with multiple methods
format: High-resolution real-world photographs with source images, reference images, and corresponding masks. Minimum resolution 700x525.
metric: DreamSim (object fidelity), LPIPS (scene fidelity), MLLM 2AFC (object-scene harmony)
access: Not publicly released at time of paper (arXiv:2602.23697)
notes: New benchmark introduced in SourceSwap paper. Higher resolution and more categories than DreamEditBench. Collects images from Pexels and Unsplash.

name: DreamEditBench
num_samples: 1574 pairs, 22 categories, 220 source objects, 158 reference objects
format: DreamBooth-generated images with added backgrounds; source images, reference images, and masks for object swapping evaluation
notes: Existing benchmark for subject-driven image editing. Built upon DreamBooth by adding backgrounds to DreamBooth-generated images. Suffers from limited object diversity (half categories are cats, dogs, toys). Used as evaluation benchmark in SourceSwap (arXiv:2602.23697).

name: BrushData
format: High-aesthetic scored images from LAION-Aesthetic with quality filters
notes: BrushData is a subset of LAION-Aesthetic used for training BrushNet and other inpainting models. SourceSwap (arXiv:2602.23697) uses ~43K filtered BrushData images for training (filtered by mask size relative to image dimensions).

name: LOLv1
format: RGB image pairs (low-light input, normal-light ground truth)

name: LOLv2-real
num_samples: 1000+ paired images (100 test pairs used in paper)
format: RGB image pairs (low-light input, normal-light ground truth)
access: Referenced in Yang et al. 2021 IEEE TIP (LOLv2)

name: LSRW
format: RGB image pairs (low-light input, normal-light ground truth)
access: Referenced in Hai et al. 2023 JVCIR (R2RNet)

name: DICM
format: Low-light images without paired ground truth

name: MEF
format: Low-light images without paired ground truth

name: LIME
format: Low-light images without paired ground truth
access: Referenced in Guo et al. 2016 IEEE TIP

name: VBench-Long
eval_time: hours for full evaluation with VBench scorers and VLM-based consistency assessment
format: Long-form text-to-video generation benchmark with metrics for subject consistency, background consistency, motion smoothness, temporal flickering, dynamic degree, aesthetic quality, imaging quality, and VLM-based semantic consistency (Gemini-3-Pro)
metric: VBench intrinsic metrics + VLM consistency score (0-100)
notes: Extended from VBench (Huang et al., CVPR 2024) for long-horizon video generation (30+ seconds). Used in papers 2602.24289 (MMM), Huang et al. 2025b (Self-Forcing), Yin et al. 2025 (CausVid), and related long video generation works.

name: SHHS (Sleep Heart Health Study)
format: Multi-channel PSG recordings (EEG, EOG, EMG, ECG, respiration) at 64Hz, 30-second epochs with sleep stage labels
metric: Sleep staging accuracy, event detection IoU (used as pretraining/evaluation data)
license: Research use via NSRR (National Sleep Research Resource)

name: MrOS (Osteoporotic Fractures in Men Study)
format: Multi-channel PSG recordings (EEG, EOG, EMG, ECG, respiration) at 64Hz, 30-second epochs with sleep stage labels
metric: Sleep staging accuracy, event detection IoU (used as pretraining/evaluation data)
license: Research use via NSRR (National Sleep Research Resource)

name: CCSHS (Cleveland Children's Sleep Health Study)
format: Multi-channel PSG recordings (EEG, EOG, EMG, ECG, respiration) at 64Hz, 30-second epochs with sleep stage labels
metric: Sleep staging accuracy (used as pretraining data)
license: Research use via NSRR (National Sleep Research Resource)

name: CFS (Cleveland Family Study)
format: Multi-channel PSG recordings (EEG, EOG, EMG, ECG, respiration) at 64Hz, 30-second epochs with sleep stage labels
metric: Sleep staging accuracy, event detection IoU (used as held-out evaluation data)
license: Research use via NSRR (National Sleep Research Resource)

name: WSC (Wisconsin Sleep Cohort)
format: Multi-channel PSG recordings (EEG, EOG, EMG, ECG, respiration) at 64Hz, 30-second epochs with sleep stage labels
metric: Sleep staging accuracy, event detection (used as held-out few-shot evaluation data)
license: Research use via NSRR (National Sleep Research Resource)

name: BOP (Benchmark for 6D Object Pose Estimation)
num_samples: ~10k+ test images across datasets (LM-O: 200 imgs, TUD-L: 600 imgs, YCB-V: 900 imgs, plus others)
format: RGB-D images + 3D object models ( meshes) + annotations; evaluation via mAP on three error metrics (VSD, MSSD, MSPD)

name: SynthRAD2023
num_samples: 180 paired 3D CBCT/CT volumes (pelvis); 126 train / 18 val / 36 test at subject level
format: 3D cone-beam CT (CBCT) and synthetic CT (sCT/CT) volumes in NIfTI format; pelvis region; slice-wise 2D training at 256x256 resolution
metric: MAE (Hounsfield Unit), SSIM (%), PSNR (dB), FID (2D slice-level), SegScore (Dice over pelvic organs from TotalSegmentator)
notes: SynthRAD2023 grand challenge dataset for synthetic CT generation in radiotherapy. Paper: Thummerer et al., Medical Physics 50(7), 2023. Used in RAFM paper (arXiv:2603.00535) for unpaired CBCT-to-CT translation with strict subject-level true-unpaired protocol (63 CBCT subjects + 63 CT subjects for training, no overlap).

name: MMLongBench-Doc
format: Long multimodal documents (avg 47.5 pages) with QA pairs across 7 domains; evidence types include text, layout, table, chart, image; includes unanswerable questions
notes: Long document understanding benchmark with visualizations. Tests reasoning over lengthy multi-domain documents (avg 49.4 pages) requiring scattered information integration. Human expert baseline: 65.8. Used in AgenticOCR paper (arXiv:2602.24134).

name: FinRAGBench-V
format: Financial reports with dense layouts; supports visual citation evaluation (bounding-box level evidence); question types: single-page (87.4%), cross-page (12.6%); evidence: text (21.7%), table (41.1%), chart (37.2%)
notes: Financial domain VQA benchmark with visual citation. Used in AgenticOCR paper (arXiv:2602.24134) for evaluating dense, newspaper-like document layouts.

name: ViDoRe-v3
format: Document pages with queries, human-annotated bounding boxes for relevant regions; used for trajectory distillation in AgenticOCR training
notes: Comprehensive evaluation of RAG in complex real-world scenarios. Used as training data source for AgenticOCR SFT and RL stages.

name: MVToolbench
num_samples: ~400+ document pages with queries and ground-truth bounding boxes
format: Document pages paired with queries and ground-truth bounding boxes; tests tool-use capability for document understanding
notes: Document understanding benchmark for evaluating tool-use models. Used in AgenticOCR paper for ablation studies on evidence extraction capability.

name: QuixBugs
format: Python algorithmic problems with canonical and buggy implementations paired under the same requirement
notes: Algorithmic programming benchmark with paired canonical/buggy implementations. Used in over-correction bias study (arXiv:2603.00539) for evaluating LLM code conformance judgement. Contains known defects and corrected implementations.

name: Anomaly-Seg20K
num_samples: ~20000 randomly sampled images from existing industrial anomaly segmentation datasets (RealIAD, GoodsAD, DTD-Synthetic, MIAD, RoadCrack, ZJU-LEAPER)
format: Industrial anomaly images with ground-truth masks; used as auxiliary training data under direct segmentation instructions in AG-VAS paper
access: Not separately released; derived from RealIAD (https://realiad4ad.github.io/Real-IAD/), PKU-GoodsAD (https://github.com/jianzhang96/GoodsAD), DTD-Synthetic, MIAD, RoadCrack, ZJU-LEAPER

name: Community Alignment
format: Human preference pairs from community-sourced data, standardized into binary chosen/rejected format for LLM preference analysis. Used in Wedgwood et al. 2025 (arXiv:2603.03319) as part of composite preference dataset.
notes: From Zhang et al. 2025 (arXiv:2507.09650). One of three human preference corpora used in Wedgwood et al. automated concept discovery paper for LLM-as-a-judge analysis.

name: LMArena-100k
format: Large-scale human preference dataset from Chatbot Arena (LMArena), containing pairwise comparisons of LLM responses with human preference labels. Used in Wedgwood et al. 2025 (arXiv:2603.03319) as part of composite preference dataset.
notes: From Chiang et al. 2024 (Chatbot Arena paper). One of three human preference corpora in Wedgwood et al. automated concept discovery paper for LLM-as-a-judge analysis.

name: PRISM
format: Human preference dataset from the PRISM alignment project, containing pairwise LLM response comparisons. Used in Wedgwood et al. 2025 (arXiv:2603.03319) as part of composite preference dataset.
notes: From Kirk et al. 2024 (PRISM alignment dataset). One of three human preference corpora in Wedgwood et al. automated concept discovery paper for LLM-as-a-judge analysis.

name: SHP-2 (askacademia, legaladvice)
format: Reddit-sourced preference data from subreddit posts (Student Home Help / legal advice), used for domain-specific LLM preference analysis. askacademia covers academic advice questions; legaladvice covers legal guidance questions. Used in Wedgwood et al. 2025 for domain-specific bias analysis.
notes: From Ethayarajh et al. 2022 (SHP-2 dataset). Used for domain-specific analysis in Wedgwood et al. automated concept discovery paper. Human-LLM agreement is much lower (~30%) on these domain-specific datasets compared to general datasets (~70%), enabling discovery of domain-specific preference biases.

name: FinRetrieval
format: QA pairs with ground truth; agent responses; tool call traces; scoring results
notes: Benchmark for evaluating AI agents on financial data retrieval from structured databases via MCP (Model Context Protocol). Tests retrieval of specific numeric values from financial databases. Authors: Eric Y. Kim and Jie Huang (Daloopa), January 2026. Key finding: tool availability (71pp gap) dominates model selection.

name: RTLLM-v2
format: RTL code generation problems with natural language specifications; evaluated via functional verification with testbenches
notes: OpenLLM-RTL benchmark for LLM-aided RTL design generation. Version 2 with 50 problems. Used in SiliconMind-V1 paper (arXiv:2603.08719) as one of three main evaluation benchmarks.

name: VerilogEval-v2
format: Verilog code generation problems with module specifications; evaluated via functional verification
notes: Revised VerilogEval benchmark from Pinckney et al. (ACM TODAES 2025). One of three main benchmarks in SiliconMind-V1 paper (arXiv:2603.08719). Paper identified issues in this benchmark and created VerilogEval-v2-NTU as a cleaned version.

name: VerilogEval-v2-NTU
format: Verilog code generation problems with resolved issues (ambiguous descriptions, unsynthesizable syntax, logical inconsistencies in reference answers); evaluated via functional verification
notes: Cleaned version of VerilogEval-v2 created by SiliconMind-V1 paper (arXiv:2603.08719) with help of IC domain experts to resolve issues found in the original dataset.

name: CVDP-cid02&03
format: Comprehensive Verilog Design Problems benchmark; categories cid02 (code completion) and cid03 (code generation); evaluated via testbenches
notes: CVDP benchmark from Pinckney et al. (arXiv:2506.14074). SiliconMind-V1 paper (arXiv:2603.08719) uses only cid02 and cid03 categories (most relevant to their work), totaling 172 problems.

name: OASST1 (OpenAssistant)
num_samples: ~88,800 samples (161,443 messages in 35 languages, 10,000+ annotated conversation trees)
format: Conversation trees with messages annotated for quality; roles: prompter/assistant

name: EgoBody
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed; egocentric videos with head-mounted device recordings
format: Egocentric video recordings from head-mounted devices with accurate 3D body pose annotations; features severe body truncation and missing 2D evidence due to camera perspective
notes: EgoBody (Zhang et al., ECCV 2022) is used as a challenging test set for TTA, featuring severe body truncation that makes it difficult to obtain reliable 2D pose estimates. The paper evaluates on EgoBody using HMR2.0 backbone and shows consistent improvement over CycleAdapt.

name: GRASP
format: Synthetic videos probing physics understanding in robotic manipulation contexts. Tests 10 intuitive physics properties: object permanence, continuity, support, gravity, inertia, color constancy, solidity, collision. Each video has a plausible and implausible version.
notes: From Jassim et al. (IJCAI 2024). Probes intuitive physics understanding in multimodal language models using violation-of-expectation paradigm in robotic grasping scenes.

name: InfLevel-lab
format: Photorealistic videos of physical manipulation events. Tests 3 properties: object permanence, gravity, solidity. Videos are naturally recorded with paired plausible/implausible versions differing only in lighting conditions. Requires memory of contextualizing pretext events for some properties.
notes: From Weihs et al. (TMLR 2022). Benchmark for evaluating AI physical reasoning at infant-level. More realistic than synthetic IntPhys but some properties require contextualizing events not present in all video pairs.

name: MultiMedQA
num_samples: ~208,000+ (9 datasets: MedQA ~12.7K, MedMCQA ~193K, PubMedQA ~1K, 6x MMLU-medical subsets ~1.2K)
format: Multiple-choice questions (MCQ) across medical domains; includes USMLE-style questions (MedQA), Indian medical exam questions (MedMCQA), yes/no/maybe PubMed abstract QA, and MMLU medical subsets
license: varies by component dataset (MedQA: research license, MedMCQA: MIT, PubMedQA: MIT, MMLU subsets: MIT)
notes: Curated by openlifescienceai. Contains 9 medical QA datasets. Used as source for FreeMedQA (paper 2503.13508), which filtered 14,965 questions to 10,278 paired MCQ/free-response questions.

name: EgoTempo
num_samples: 500 Q&A pairs across 365 video clips (average 45s each, from 221 Ego4D videos)
format: Open-ended VideoQA with 10 temporal reasoning categories (Actions: Action Sequence, Action Counting, Temporal Event Ordering, Future Action Prediction, Object-Specific Actions; Objects: Object Sequence, Object Counting, Spatial Relations, Locating Objects, Action-Specific Objects). Q&A pairs with ground-truth answers, sourced from Ego4D egocentric videos.
metric: accuracy (%) via LLM judge (Gemini 1.5 Pro), validated against human evaluation (96% alignment)
notes: EgoTempo from Plizzari et al. (arXiv:2503.13646). Designed to evaluate temporal understanding in egocentric VideoQA. Key finding: current MLLMs (best: Gemini 1.5 Flash at 39.1% @ 1FPS, GPT-4o at 40.1% @ 32 frames) significantly underperform humans (63.2%). Requires multi-frame temporal reasoning — single-frame accuracy is only 9.1%.

name: TREC RAG'24 (AG task)
storage: ~25-30GB (MS MARCO V2.1 passages from TREC RAG'24 organizers); queries negligible
eval_time: hours (depends on LLM API call count)
format: User queries with top-k retrieved passages from MS MARCO V2.1 segment collection; evaluated via AutoNuggetizer framework (nugget-based fact coverage)
notes: TREC 2024 RAG Track, Augmented Generation (AG) task. Participants generate grounded responses using top-k passages provided by organizers (fixed retrieval). GINGER paper (arXiv:2503.18174) focuses on this task. AutoNuggetizer framework (Pradeep et al. 2024) evaluates whether response contains vital nuggets from answer key.

name: UrbanScene3D
num_samples: 2 aerial scenes with 2500-6000 images each covering ~1 square kilometer
storage: ~hundreds of GB (aerial drone imagery with precise camera poses)
format: Aerial drone-captured scenes with known camera poses and sparse COLMAP point clouds; used for large-scale outdoor multi-view reconstruction evaluation

name: 3D Ken Burns
num_samples: 23 synthetic in-the-wild scenes with 2 sequences each (~30K frames after filtering)
format: Large-scale synthetic scenes with camera motion; camera parameters known; used for depth estimation training in Murre paper (arXiv:2503.14483)

name: MATRES
format: Document with event mentions; classify temporal relation between event pairs (4 types: before, after, equal, vague); only consecutive-sentence pairs annotated

name: NarrativeTime
format: Document with event mentions; 7 temporal relation types (before, after, includes, is-included, equal, overlap, vague); exhaustively annotated

name: OmniTemp
num_samples: 30 documents, 470 events, 3,483 relations (train: 20 docs, test: 10 docs)
format: News summaries with event mentions; 4 temporal relation types (before, after, equal, vague); exhaustively annotated for all event pairs
access: Derived from Multi-News (Fabbri et al., 2019); will be released by authors

name: Force Concept Inventory (FCI)
format: Multiple-choice conceptual physics questions testing Newtonian mechanics misconceptions
notes: Standardized test for introductory physics courses measuring conceptual understanding of Newtonian mechanics. Widely used to evaluate pedagogical effectiveness. The 30-question test covers: Kinematics, Newton's First/Second/Third Law, Superposition Principle, and Kinds of Force.

name: MITEA (Left Ventricle Echocardiography)
num_samples: Not fully disclosed; 3D echocardiography + corresponding cardiac MRI labels for left ventricle segmentation
format: 3D echocardiography volumes with subject-specific labels from cardiac MRI; supports heart disease diagnosis (dilated cardiomyopathy, amyloidosis, etc.)

name: LINEMOD (LM)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on method
format: RGB-D images + 3D object mesh models + ground truth 6DoF poses; standard benchmark for 6D object pose estimation

name: Occlusion LINEMOD (LM-O)
num_samples: 1,214 test images (8 objects in heavily occluded scenes)
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on method
format: RGB-D images + 3D object mesh models + ground truth 6DoF poses; tests pose estimation under heavy occlusion

name: YCB-Video
format: RGB-D video sequences + 3D mesh models + ground truth 6DoF poses from Kinect; large-scale benchmark for 6D pose estimation

name: CIFAR-100-C
format: CIFAR-100 test images with 19 common corruptions at 5 severity levels (total 19*5=95 corruptions)
notes: Corrupted version of CIFAR-100 test set. Same corruption types as CIFAR-10-C (noise, blur, weather, digital). Paper evaluates at severity level 5. Used in TestDG (arXiv:2504.04981) for CIFAR100-to-CIFAR100-C CTTA evaluation.

name: ACDC (Adverse Conditions Dataset for Driving)
num_samples: ~4000 images (406 fog, 1008 night, 1006 rain, 1526 snow scenes)
format: RGB images of driving scenes with pixel-level semantic labels (19 classes, same as Cityscapes); four adverse weather/lighting conditions: fog, night, rain, snow
notes: Adverse conditions dataset with correspondences for semantic driving scene understanding (Sakaridis et al., ICCV 2021). Used with Cityscapes as source in TestDG (arXiv:2504.04981) for Cityscapes-to-ACDC continual test-time adaptation evaluation (segmentation task).

name: Archive of Formal Proofs (AFP)
num_samples: 600+ formal theories (2019-08-19 snapshot used in paper for soft-use baseline analysis)
storage: ~500MB-1GB (full AFP); small subset used in paper's analysis
format: Isabelle/HOL formal proofs organized as theories. Each entry is a lemma/theorem with formal statement and proof.
notes: Large library of Isabelle/HOL formal proofs. Used in this paper as a baseline population of 'unrelated' lemmas for soft-use analysis (survival curves comparing retrieved vs. unrelated lemmas). The 2019-08-19 snapshot was specifically used.

name: MathCog
num_samples: 3,036 diagnostic verdicts (639 student responses to 110 problems across 12 topics)
format: Math problem + student response (OCR) + diagnostic checklist (TIMSS-grounded cognitive skill items) + verdict (Evident/Vague × Yes/No)
metric: macro F1 score, accuracy, OverAttr (evidence over-attribution rate), FalseAttr (evidence false-attribution rate)
license: Not publicly released — requires request from authors
access: Contact authors (KAIST); original data from AI-Hub Korean handwritten math dataset
notes: Benchmark for evaluating LLMs' ability to diagnose students' cognitive skills from handwritten math work, grounded in TIMSS 2019 framework. Created by Kim et al. (arXiv:2504.00843). Not yet publicly released at time of analysis. All models achieve F1 < 0.5, indicating the task is challenging for current LLMs.

name: KNOWN
format: Fill-in-the-blank completion tasks with a single word answer. Each sample contains a prompt with a masked answer.
access: From Meng et al. (2023). Provided by paper authors.

name: LongRA (Long-Range Agreement)
format: Word pairs exhibiting semantic or syntactic relationships, with distractor sentences. Used for long-range agreement evaluation.
access: From Vafa et al. (2021). Available at https://github.com/Keytoyze/LongRA or via paper authors.

name: WIKIBIO
format: Wikipedia biography entries. First two sentences used as prompt, model generates continuation. Open-ended text generation task.

name: FEVEROUS
format: Claim + label (SUPPORTS/REFUTES) requiring evidence from Wikipedia pages and/or tables; text-only subset excludes table-based claims
notes: Fact extraction and verification over structured and unstructured data. Claims require evidence from both unstructured text (Wikipedia) and structured data (tables). Paper uses only claims requiring exclusively unstructured evidence. Strong complementary to HOVER for multi-hop reasoning evaluation.

name: WebUI
format: Web page screenshots with annotated UI element bounding boxes and semantic labels; text-to-layout task requiring generation of UI layouts from natural language descriptions

name: PlanBench
format: Planning problem instances in STRIPS format from IPC domains; evaluate plan correctness via plan executor

name: NaturalPlan
format: Natural language trip planning queries with varying difficulty (3-10 cities); success based on plan match

name: CELLS
format: Paired biomedical scientific abstracts and human-authored plain language summaries from biomedical journals
metric: n/a (dataset for PLS generation and evaluation)
license: Not explicitly stated; derived from published biomedical journal articles
notes: Parallel corpus of biomedical abstracts and lay language summaries. Used in this paper (arXiv:2505.10409) to sample 50 abstract-PLS pairs for evaluating LLM-generated PLS quality. The PLS were written by humans from the original journal publishers.

name: CRUXEval
format: Python code functions with input-output pairs for execution prediction
notes: Code reasoning benchmark by Gu et al. (ICML 2024). Measures semantic code recall via input prediction and output prediction tasks. Found to have low semantic recall sensitivity in paper 2505.13353, allowing pattern matching shortcuts.

name: SemTrace
format: Python functions: list initialization with randomized assignment operations (x + y or x - y, y from [-100,99]), order randomized. Output prediction task.
metric: exact match accuracy, partial match accuracy
access: Generated by paper authors; described in 2505.13353
notes: High-sensitivity semantic recall benchmark introduced in 2505.13353. Designed to prevent pattern matching shortcuts by using unpredictable operations. Median accuracy drops 92.73% vs CRUXEval's 53.36% when code is centrally positioned.

name: CodeSearchNet
num_samples: ~1M code snippets (Python, Java, JavaScript, Go, Ruby, PHP)
format: Code snippets with natural language documentation/query
metric: N/A (used as distractor functions in long-context evaluation)
notes: CodeSearchNet benchmark used in 2505.13353 as source of distractor functions (randomly selected Python functions, filtered by character count 25th-75th percentile ~200 tokens each). Not evaluated on directly — serves as filler/distractor code in long-context experiments.

name: ARC-AGI-2
format: Successor to ARC-AGI; tests abstract reasoning via visual grid puzzle tasks (colored cell grids, 1x1 to 30x30, up to 10 colors); designed to resist brute-force search and test-time adaptation saturation; features compositional generalization tasks (multi-rule, multi-step, contextual, symbolic); extensive first-party human calibration with 407 participants
notes: ARC-AGI-2 (arXiv:2505.11831) is the updated benchmark by Chollet et al. and ARC Prize Foundation. Top models achieve <5% (below noise threshold); human baseline is ~75% full task accuracy. Competition: $1M prize pool (Kaggle 2025). All tasks solved by at least 2 independent humans.

name: USPTO Patent Differentiation Task
num_samples: ~5000 sampled pairs from 1.3M+ hard-to-distinguish patent pairs
format: Binary classification: LLM judges whether two semantically similar patents describe the same invention. Ground truth from USPTO examiner decisions.
access: Wu et al. 2025, built on USPTO data from https://patentsview.org/

name: USPTO Patent Collection
format: Patent texts with metadata including patent ID, CPC classification, filing/grant dates, abstract, and claims. Post-2015 granted patents.

name: UK Biobank
num_samples: ~500k participants with EHR, genomics, imaging, and questionnaire data
storage: Hundreds of TB (full data); targeted fields for analysis can be much smaller (estimated ~50-200GB per use case)
format: ICD-10 diagnoses, self-reported medications, demographics, lifestyle questionnaires, genetics, imaging
license: UK Biobank access requires approved application; data used under UK Biobank ethics approval

name: OnSIDES
num_samples: ~59k drug-side effect edges (version 2.1.0); drugs mapped to RxNorm, side effects to MedDRA
format: Drug-side effect pairs text-mined from FDA drug label package inserts; structured as RxNorm drug IDs and MedDRA term IDs

name: OFFSIDES
num_samples: Drug-side effect pairs mined from FDA adverse event reporting system (FAERS); much larger than OnSIDES but lower precision
format: Drug-side effect pairs with RxNorm drug IDs and MedDRA term IDs; additional meta-data on reporting frequency

name: MEDI-C
num_samples: ~20,955 drug-indication edges (high-precision subset); drugs mapped to RxNorm, indications to ICD-10/ICD-9
format: Drug-indication pairs mined from EHR data and literature; structured as RxNorm drug IDs and ICD codes

name: MatTools
num_samples: 69,225 QA pairs (pymatgen code QA: 34,621; pymatgen doc QA: 34,604) + 49 real-world tool-usage tasks (138 subtasks)
eval_time: 2-4 hours for core evaluation on single A100
format: Multiple-choice QA (A-D format) for knowledge assessment; Python code generation with Docker sandbox execution and result verification for tool-usage
metric: QA: accuracy; Tool-usage: Function Runnable Rate, Task Success Rate
notes: Dual-level multi-step reasoning benchmark for evaluating LLMs on materials science computational tool usage. Combines knowledge QA (from pymatgen codebase/docs) with real-world code generation for defect property calculations.

name: MMSD2.0
num_samples: ~2409 test samples (1037 sarcastic + 1372 non-sarcastic), Twitter-based image-text pairs
format: Twitter image-text pairs with binary sarcasm labels; improved version of MMSD with spurious cue removal

name: RedEval
num_samples: 1004 samples (395 sarcastic from r/sarcasm + 609 non-sarcastic), Reddit image-text pairs
format: Reddit image-text pairs for out-of-domain multi-modal sarcasm detection; sarcasm vs non-sarcasm binary classification

name: LogicCat
num_samples: 4,038 question-SQL pairs with 12,114 chain-of-thought annotations across 45 databases
format: English questions paired with SQL queries requiring complex multi-step reasoning (physics, math, commonsense, hypothetical); evaluated by execution accuracy and VES

name: M3CoT
num_samples: ~2000-3000 estimated (science, commonsense, mathematics domains with image-question pairs)
format: Multimodal Chain-of-Thought benchmark with image + question pairs requiring step-by-step reasoning across science, commonsense, and math domains
notes: M3CoT: Multi-modal Chain of Thought benchmark. Introduced in the RBF NeurIPS 2024 paper (Chen et al.) and used in the RBF++ extended version. Covers science, commonsense reasoning, and mathematics with visual inputs.

name: BIGGSM
num_samples: ~1000-2000 estimated (math word problems with varying computational complexity and reasoning chain length)
format: Math word problems designed with greater computational complexity and longer reasoning chains than standard GSM8K, for evaluating reasoning boundaries of LLMs
notes: BIGGSM: Big GSM dataset introduced in the RBF++ paper (arXiv:2505.13307). Designed to evaluate reasoning boundaries of LLMs by controlling problem difficulty and reasoning step count. Extends GSM8K-style problems to harder ranges.

name: BIGGSM++
num_samples: ~2000-3000 estimated (expanded difficulty range for evaluating advanced reasoning LLMs like DeepSeek-R1)
format: Expanded math benchmark for evaluating advanced reasoning LLMs (DeepSeek-R1, o3-mini) on reasoning boundaries at higher difficulty levels than BIGGSM
notes: BIGGSM++: Extended version of BIGGSM introduced in RBF++ (arXiv:2505.13307) specifically for evaluating RL-trained reasoning LLMs like DeepSeek-R1. Covers a broader range of reasoning boundaries including CFRB and CIRB regions.

name: HLSyn
num_samples: 10 kernels (3mm, atax-med, covariance, fdtd-2d, gemm-p, gemver-med, jacobi-2d, symm-opt, syr2k, trmm-opt)
eval_time: minutes to hours per configuration (HLS synthesis)
format: HLS C/C++ kernel source code files for FPGA accelerator optimization; each kernel has different loop structures and varying loop bound values; targets Merlin Compiler directives (pipeline, parallel, tile, array partition)
metric: Clock cycle count (lower is better), resource utilization (LUTs, BRAM, FFs, DSPs, URAM <80%)
notes: HLSyn benchmark from ML4HLS contest (Bai et al., NeurIPS 2023). Used as primary evaluation benchmark in LLM-DSE paper (arXiv:2505.12188). Programs have max 77 lines of code with at most 3 levels of loop nesting.

name: Rosetta
num_samples: 4 programs (conv2d 118 LoC, spam-filter 126 LoC, knn 178 LoC, 3d-rendering 304 LoC)
