eval_time: minutes to hours per configuration (HLS synthesis)
format: HLS C/C++ programs for FPGA accelerator optimization; larger and more complex than HLSyn (up to 304 lines of code with up to 7 levels of nested loops); targets Merlin Compiler directives
metric: Clock cycle count (lower is better), resource utilization
access: Referenced in Zhou et al., FPGA 2018; https://github.com/K obalicek/rosetta
notes: Rosetta benchmark suite (Zhou et al., FPGA 2018). Used for scalability evaluation in LLM-DSE paper (arXiv:2505.12188). Programs have 118-304 LoC with up to 7 levels of nested loops, compared to max 77 LoC in HLSyn.

name: DECEPTIONDECODED
num_samples: 12,000 image-caption-article triplets (2,000 original news × 6 intent categories)
storage: ~50-100GB (images at news resolution + captions + reference articles)
eval_time: hours for full evaluation across 14 VLMs
format: Triplets {image, caption, trustworthy article} with labels for misleading/non-misleading, manipulation source (text/image), and creator desire (8 societal influence categories)
metric: Accuracy (misleading intent detection, source attribution); F1 (creator desire inference)
license: Restricted to verified researchers under usage agreement
access: Not yet publicly released at time of analysis; contact authors for access

name: MMFakeBench
num_samples: ~varies by split (1,000 validation samples: 700 fake, 300 real)
format: Mixed-source multimodal fake news (image-caption pairs) with binary fake/real labels

name: VisualNews
num_samples: ~large-scale (news images + captions + articles across multiple topics)
format: Multimodal news with images, captions, articles, and topic annotations from trustworthy sources
access: Liu et al. (2021) — Visual News: Benchmark and Challenges in News Image Captioning, EMNLP 2021

name: CHARTMUSEUM
format: Chart images (928 unique real-world charts from 184 sources) with expert-annotated QA pairs across visual, textual, synthesis, and visual/text reasoning types; human-curated questions without LLM assistance
notes: New chart QA benchmark from arXiv:2505.13444. Designed to test LVLM visual vs. textual reasoning. Human accuracy 93%, best model Gemini-2.5-Pro 63%, best open-source Qwen2.5-VL-72B 38.5%. All models show 35-55% accuracy drop on visual vs. textual reasoning questions.

name: ChartQAPro
format: Chart QA benchmark with diverse and challenging questions for chart understanding
notes: More diverse and challenging version of ChartQA benchmark (arXiv:2501.0xxxx). Referenced in ChartMuseum paper (arXiv:2505.13444) as a prior benchmark. Does not effectively distinguish frontier model performance (models cluster near saturation).

name: HighLowQualityCounselling (HLQC)
eval_time: minutes per transcript for AutoMISC evaluation
format: Text transcripts of MI counselling sessions scraped from public websites, covering smoking cessation, alcohol reduction, and substance use
metric: MISC summary metrics: %MI-Consistent (%MIC), Reflection-to-Question Ratio (R:Q), %Change Talk (%CT)
notes: Used as comparison baseline in MIBot paper (arXiv:2505.17362) to validate AutoMISC metrics. Designed for automatic evaluation of counselling quality.

name: ESSAYBENCH
num_samples: 728 Chinese essay prompts (Argumentative, Narrative, Descriptive, Expository)
eval_time: hours (depends on number of models and judge)
format: essay prompts with genre labels, instruction type (Open-Ended/Constrained)
metric: LLM-as-a-judge fine-grained scoring with genre-specific traits and dependency-weighted aggregation

name: MegaHan97K
eval_time: hours for full evaluation across 9 methods
format: Character images (96x96) with labels; three subsets: handwritten (~900K), historical (~400K), synthetic (3.3M)
notes: Mega-category Chinese character recognition dataset with 97,455 categories (6x prior art). First dataset to fully support GB18030-2022 standard. Includes general and zero-shot evaluation splits. Closest prior: M5HisDoc with 16,151 categories.

name: SpookyBench
num_samples: 451 synthetic videos (210 text, 156 object images, 57 dynamic scenes, 28 shapes)
storage: ~1-2GB for 451 videos at 960x540 resolution, ~7s avg duration
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on number of VLMs evaluated; ~4-15 min per 7B model
format: Synthetic videos where individual frames appear as noise but content becomes visible through temporal motion patterns. Four categories: text (words), shapes, object images, dynamic scenes. Videos generated using opposing motion noise patterns and depth-based threshold animation.
metric: Exact match accuracy between VLM response and ground truth label. Flexible matching for object/scene categories accepting semantically equivalent responses.
notes: Novel benchmark isolating purely temporal understanding in VLMs by eliminating spatial cues. All tested VLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini, Qwen, InternVL, LLaVA, etc.) achieve 0% accuracy while humans achieve 98%. Exposes 'time blindness' as a fundamental limitation of current video-language models that rely on spatial feature extraction first. arXiv:2505.24867

name: NSR-1K
format: Text-to-image prompts for Novel Spatial Reasoning evaluation. Spatial category tests 2D spatial relations; Count category tests object count accuracy. Objects detected via GLIP and compared against prompt-specified count and spatial relations.
metric: Object detection accuracy (UniDet for T2I-CompBench, GLIP for NSR-1K), center-point distance for spatial errors
notes: Novel Spatial Reasoning 1K benchmark from LayoutGPT (Feng et al., NeurIPS 2023). Used in ComposeAnything (arXiv:2505.24086) for evaluating compositional T2I generation on spatial and count categories.

name: Gaussian Outpainting (GO) Benchmark
num_samples: 50 ScanNet++ validation scenes, 16 novel camera poses per scene, 5 repeated runs
storage: Based on ScanNet++ (~1.3TB) plus rendered outputs
eval_time: hours for full benchmark (requires inpainting + growing + rendering for each pose)
format: Novel view synthesis benchmark for 3D Gaussian splatting with expanded field-of-view. Evaluates both RGB fidelity (FID) and semantic plausibility (mIoU) in outpainted regions.
metric: FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) for visual fidelity; mIoU (mean Intersection over Union) for semantic segmentation in outpainted regions

name: MQUAKE
format: Multi-hop QA questions testing knowledge editing; exact-match evaluation

name: CLUTRR
format: Inductive reasoning from text using family relationship graphs; multiple choice QA

name: NQSWAP
format: Entity-based knowledge conflicts: context conflicts with parametric memory; exact-match evaluation

name: MACNOISE
format: Counterfactual noise knowledge conflicts: context vs. parametric memory; exact-match evaluation

name: ADVANCED-AI-RISK
format: Multiple-choice QA probing behavioral traits: corrigibility, hallucination, myopic reward, survival instinct

name: CORRIGIBILITY
format: Multiple-choice QA: whether model accepts corrections and adapts to user feedback

name: HALLUCINATION
format: Multiple-choice QA: avoid fabricating information vs. factual responses (GPT-4 generated)

name: MYOPIC-REWARD
format: Multiple-choice QA: short-term vs. long-term reasoning

name: SURVIVAL-INSTINCT
format: Multiple-choice QA: self-preservation bias vs. task focus

name: WARP Symbolic Constraint Generalisation Benchmark
num_samples: 671 instances (20 Java programs, each with prompts at multiple input sizes)
eval_time: minutes per model for full evaluation (671 instances)
format: Each instance: Java program + incremental constraints at small input sizes (n in {2,4,8}) + ask for constraint at larger n (up to 30). Ground-truth constraints verified by Z3 SMT solver. Format: SMT-LIB v2.
metric: Accuracy = proportion of generated SMT constraints that are both syntactically valid and solver-equivalent to ground-truth (bidirectional UNSAT test via Z3)
notes: From arXiv:2506.08171. Tests LLMs' ability to generalise worst-case symbolic path constraints from small to large input sizes. Programs include QuickSort, BinarySearch, Dijkstra, MergeSort, TowerOfHanoi, etc. Difficulty tiers: small/medium/large jumps in input size.

name: WARP Fine-tuning Dataset
num_samples: Not specified (synthetically generated from 20 Java programs using SPF-WCA)
format: Java programs paired with worst-case path constraints for small input sizes, generated by SPF-WCA symbolic execution. Format: program code + SMT-LIB constraint pairs.
notes: From arXiv:2506.08171. Used to fine-tune WARP-1.0-3B (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct) with RLSGF/GRPO. Constraints generated by SPF-WCA ensure formal correctness of ground-truth labels.

name: ORT (Out-of-distribution Robustness Test)
num_samples: 200 targets; 12294 forget set + 22758 retain set evaluation entries across 4 task formats
format: 4 task formats (Simple QA, Fill-in-the-Blank, Multiple Choice, Subtoken QA) for evaluating form-independent unlearning on real-world individuals
notes: Introduced Form-Dependent Bias problem in LLM unlearning. Benchmarks unlearning methods across diverse knowledge expression formats to test robustness. Partially sourced from RWKU dataset.

name: GIQ (Geometric IQ Test)
eval_time: hours per model (full evaluation across 4 task types)
format: Synthetic renderings (Mitsuba PBR renderer, 256×256) and real-world photographs (Nikon D3500, 6000×4000) of 224 polyhedra including Platonic, Archimedean, Catalan, Johnson solids, stellations, and compounds; with 3D mesh files
metric: Varies by task: balanced accuracy (symmetry detection), accuracy (mental rotation, zero-shot classification), qualitative assessment (3D reconstruction)
notes: Benchmark for evaluating 3D geometric reasoning of vision foundation models. Four evaluation tasks: (1) Monocular 3D reconstruction (Shap-E, Stable Fast 3D, OpenLRM), (2) 3D symmetry detection via linear/non-linear probing, (3) Mental rotation test (Shepard-Metzler style), (4) Zero-shot polyhedron classification (frontier VLMs). Key finding: SOTA models fail to reconstruct even basic Platonic solids; frontier VLMs achieve <20% on Johnson/Catalan solids.

name: UnAV-100
num_samples: 10,790 untrimmed videos / 30,059 audiovisual events / 126+ video hours
format: untrimmed videos with dense audio-visual event annotations across 100 categories

name: HAIM-MIMIC-MM
storage: Part of MIMIC-IV (~1.3TB total for MIMIC-IV); adds chest X-rays + processed multimodal data
eval_time: Hours for full evaluation across 5 clinical tasks
format: Multimodal clinical data: clinical notes (radiology, echo, EKG reports), tabular demographics, time-series vital signs/labs, chest X-ray images. Derived from MIMIC-IV critical care database.
metric: AUC for classification (pleural effusion, cardiomegaly, pneumonia, 48-hour mortality); AUC/MAE for regression (length of stay)
notes: Used in xHAIM paper (arXiv:2507.00205) for evaluating multimodal clinical prediction with explainability. The full MIMIC-IV dataset requires credentialing via PhysioNet.

name: CinePile
format: Third-person movie videos (~2min40sec each) with multiple-choice QA generated by LLMs; includes hard split and subtitle/visual description data
notes: Long video QA dataset from movies. Used in arXiv:2507.00033 (Moment Sampling for Video LLMs).

name: AVATAR (Audio-Visual localizAtion benchmark for a spatio-TemporAl peRspective in video)
format: Video clips (avg 10s) with per-frame bbox and instance segmentation annotations for sound-emitting objects; 4 evaluation scenarios: Single-sound, Mixed-sound, Multi-entity, Off-screen; also Cross-event subset
metric: CIoU (Consensus IoU), AUC (Area Under Curve), TN (True Negative percentage for Off-screen)
access: Not officially released at time of paper (arXiv:2507.04667)
notes: Introduces 4 novel evaluation scenarios not covered by prior AVL benchmarks: (1) Single-sound: single visible sound source, (2) Mixed-sound: overlapping multiple audio sources, (3) Multi-entity: multiple similar objects but only one sounding, (4) Off-screen: sound source outside camera frame. Key contribution is temporal evaluation - unlike prior image-level benchmarks, AVATAR evaluates video-level localization with high temporal resolution.

name: S3D (Structured3D)
num_samples: 3,296 synthetic houses with fully furnished 3D renders, perspective images, and 2D floor plans
eval_time: n/a (dataset for training/eval of localization methods)
format: Photorealistic synthetic 3D houses with 2D floor plans, room types (bedroom, living room, etc.), semantic annotations (wall, window, door per pixel/ray). Perspective images at 1280x720 with 80-degree FoV. Used in SemRayLoc (arXiv:2507.09291) and F3Loc for floorplan-based camera localization.
metric: Recall@0.1m, Recall@0.5m, Recall@1m, Recall@1m@30deg (camera localization accuracy)
license: Research use; available via official website
notes: Synthetic dataset of 3,296 houses. Each house has multiple rooms with furniture, 2D floor plans, and rendered perspective images. Room type prediction accuracy is 72.1% in SemRayLoc. The fully furnished perspective dataset is the standard split used for localization benchmarks.

name: Hemolytik
num_samples: ~2000+ experimentally validated hemolytic and non-hemolytic peptide sequences (filtered to 1926 with numeric HC50 values in AmpLyze)
format: Peptide sequences with hemolytic/non-hemolytic annotations and HC50 (hemolytic concentration) values

name: GRBENCH
num_samples: 1740 questions across 5 domains (Academic, E-Commerce, Healthcare, Legal, Literature)
eval_time: minutes per model for full evaluation
format: Knowledge graphs (node/edge typed) with QA pairs at 3 difficulty levels (easy, medium, hard); healthcare has only easy/medium
notes: From arXiv:2404.07103 (Graph-CoT). Multi-domain benchmark for evaluating LLM graph reasoning. Graphs have typed nodes and edges with textual attributes. Questions range from single-node lookup to multi-hop traversal and shared-neighbor reasoning.

name: RewardMATH
format: Math preference dataset with pairwise preferences for training reward models on mathematical reasoning; contains problems with chosen/rejected solution responses
notes: RewardMATH dataset from Kim et al. 2024. Used in paper 2507.07981 for training and evaluating reward models on math tasks.

name: LEEC
num_samples: 15,919 legal documents with 155 extra-legal factor labels
format: Chinese legal documents with expert-annotated extra-legal factors (demographic, socioeconomic, procedural) for fairness research
metric: Used for downstream fairness evaluation tasks
notes: Legal Element Extraction Corpus from Xue et al. IJCAI-24. Source dataset for JudiFair paper. Covers Chinese criminal cases with detailed extra-legal factor annotations.

name: JudiFair
num_samples: 177,100 unique case facts across 65 labels and 161 label values
eval_time: hours for full evaluation across multiple models
format: Counterfactually-generated judicial case facts with 65 labels covering substance/procedure factors and demographic/non-demographic attributes. Based on Chinese criminal law context.
metric: Inconsistency rate, Bias (regression with fixed effects), Imbalanced Inaccuracy (MAE/MAPE)
notes: From paper 'LLMS ON TRIAL: EVALUATING JUDICIAL FAIRNESS FOR LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS' (Hu et al., 2025). Evaluation benchmark for LLM judicial fairness in Chinese legal system. Uses counterfactual prompting to assess bias and inconsistency.

name: GREEN
format: Generative Radiology Report Evaluation and Error Notation; LLM-based evaluation metric for radiology reports using GPT-4o-as-judge
notes: Ostmeyer et al., EMNLP 2024. Used in MICCAI 2024 AMOS-MM challenge.

name: RaTEScore
format: Radiology Report Generation metric combining clinical entity recognition and RadGraph-based relationship extraction
notes: Zhao et al., arXiv:2406.16845. Used alongside GREEN for medical report evaluation.

name: AMOS-MM
num_samples: 1687 cases (1287 train, 400 val); 3D CT volumes with findings/impressions
format: 3D CT volumes with structured radiology reports covering chest, abdomen, pelvis; from Shenzhen hospitals
notes: MICCAI 2024 Abdominal Multi-Organ Benchmark - Multimodal variant. Ji et al., NeurIPS 2022 (original AMOS).

name: OTS (RESIDE)
format: Synthetic outdoor hazy-clear pairs (RESIDE benchmark, Outdoor Training Set) for dehazing training

name: Dense-Haze
format: Real-world hazy/clear image pairs with dense homogeneous haze for dehazing evaluation

name: NH-HAZE
format: Real-world non-homogeneous hazy/clear image pairs for dehazing evaluation

name: YouRef
num_samples: 18 celebrities with HQ videos (720x720) and reference face images
format: High-quality videos of celebrities extracted at 720x720 resolution; reference face images from Google/Bing; includes light and heavy degradation settings with ground truth
metric: PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, CLIP-IQA, MUSIQ, LIQE, IDS (ArcFace cosine similarity)
notes: Face video restoration dataset from arXiv:2507.10293 (Show and Polish). Two variants: YouRef-light (first-order degradation) and YouRef-heavy (second-order degradation). Used to evaluate IP-FVR method.

name: FOS-V (Face Video Restoration Benchmark)
num_samples: 20 celebrities with facial clips and reference face images
format: Real-world heterogeneous scenarios (interviews, sports, nature footage, vintage films) filtered for facial clips with corresponding reference face images
metric: CLIP-IQA, MUSIQ, LIQE, E_warp (flow warping error)
notes: Real-world face video restoration dataset from arXiv:2507.10293 (Show and Polish), derived from FOS-V dataset (Ziyan Chen et al., arXiv:2404.19500). Used for evaluating IP-FVR on real-world degradation scenarios.

name: DevMap
num_samples: ~500-1000 OpenCL kernels with performance annotations on CPU/GPU
format: OpenCL source code + LLVM IR graph + device labels (CPU/GPU performance)

name: POJ-104
num_samples: ~10K C++ programs across 104 algorithm classes (~100 programs per class)
format: C++ source code files with algorithm class labels; LLVM IR can be compiled from source

name: Chouhan et al. 2D Leaf Dataset
format: 2D leaf RGB images with segmentation masks
access: https://doi.org/10.1109/ISCON.2019.8903813 (paper); repository: practice towards plant conservation with plant pathology

name: DeformLeaf
format: 3D reconstructed leaf meshes (base + deformed states) with dense correspondences, plus 2D base shape images
metric: n/a (training + test data for leaf reconstruction)

name: TACoS
storage: ~5-10GB pre-extracted features (raw videos from MPII Cooking dataset ~20GB)
format: Cooking activity videos from MPII with sentence descriptions for temporal moment localization; requires fine-grained action understanding in long videos
license: MPII research use (based on MPII Cooking dataset)

name: NevIR
format: Query-document pairs with contrastive queries; each sample has two queries with one relevant document each
metric: Right Rank (RR) — percentage of correctly ranked query-document pairs; chance=25%
notes: Negation in Neural Information Retrieval (Weller et al., 2024, EACL). Based on CONDAQA (Ravichander et al., 2022). Tests whether models can correctly rank documents for queries involving negation.

name: ExcluIR
format: Exclusion-type queries with multiple supporting documents; modified version of HotpotQA
notes: Exclusionary Neural Information Retrieval (Zhang et al., 2024). Tests models on exclusion-type queries like 'Apart from X, what other films has actor Y appeared in?'

name: CANNOT
format: Sentence pairs with semantic similarity scores; designed for negation-aware MT evaluation
metric: Spearman correlation (ρ) between cosine similarity and ground truth similarity scores
notes: Negation-aware evaluation dataset (Anschütz et al., 2023, INLG). Contains minimal pairs differing in negation. Reports Spearman correlation as metric.

name: M3-Counterfactual
format: Counterfactual statement pairs from biomedical literature; reformatted as text-similarity task with scores: original-negation=-1, original-no-evidence=0, original-hedged=1
notes: Subset of M3 dataset (Otmakhova et al., 2022, EMNLP). Tests model robustness to counterfactual modifications including negation, no-evidence, and hedging in biomedical statements.

name: HedgeTriple
num_samples: 248K contrastive triples (31K anchors × 4 negation + 2 hedging outputs each)
format: Contrastive triples: anchor sentence paired with hedged variant (positive) and negated variant (negative). Generated by GPT-3.5 from 50K anchor sentences using linguistically-grounded taxonomies.
notes: From paper 'Learning Robust Negation Text Representations' (Truong et al., 2025, arXiv:2507.12782). Anchor sentences sourced from SNLI, MultiNLI, sentence-compression, Simple Wikipedia, COCO Captions. Negation types: verbal, absolute, affixal, lexical (Pullum & Huddleston taxonomy). Hedging types: single-word and multi-word cues (Crompton taxonomy).

name: MHAD (UTD Multimodal Human Action Dataset)
num_samples: 861 video sequences (8 subjects, 27 actions, 4 repeats each)
format: Video sequences captured with Microsoft Kinect at 640x480 pixels, standardized to 10-frame clips for sequential disentanglement evaluation.
metric: Swap-based joint accuracy, static-only accuracy, dynamic-only accuracy, cross-leakage rate
notes: Used in DiViD (arXiv:2507.13934) for evaluating unsupervised static-dynamic disentanglement in video.

name: MEAD (Multimodal Emotional Audio-visual Expression)
num_samples: ~30 subjects performing 8 facial expressions (anger, fear, disgust, happiness, sadness, surprise, contempt, neutral), varying video lengths
format: Facial video sequences at 128x128 resolution (cropped), standardized to 15-frame clips. Faces detected using Haar Cascades and cropped.
metric: Swap-based joint accuracy, static-only accuracy, dynamic-only accuracy, cross-leakage rate
notes: Used in DiViD (arXiv:2507.13934) for evaluating unsupervised static-dynamic disentanglement for facial expressions.

name: NExT-GQA
num_samples: 5417 videos, 10531 annotated temporal segments for 8911 QA pairs
storage: ~50-100GB (shares videos with NExT-QA plus temporal annotations)
format: Visually-grounded video QA benchmark extending NExT-QA with precise temporal segment annotations; focuses on temporal (Tem.) and causal (Cau.) reasoning with IoP and tIoU grounding metrics

name: HIDE
format: Paired blurry/sharp image pairs for human-aware motion deblurring; test set only (no official training split); motion blur captured from real-world scenes

name: RealBlur
format: Real-world blurry/sharp image pairs captured with dual-camera system; RealBlur-R subset: real camera blur; RealBlur-J subset: synthetic blur generated from real images; 980 test pairs per subset

name: RB2V Street
format: Paired blurry/sharp street scene images derived from video sequences using unsupervised ordering; high-resolution street-level imagery

name: RSBlur
format: Realistic blur dataset with paired blurry/sharp images; blur synthesized using 3D-aware motion estimation to match real-world blur characteristics; diverse scene types

name: TCIA Osteosarcoma
format: RGB histopathology images (1024x1024x3) of osteosarcoma tissue slides; 3 classes: Non-Tumor, Non-Viable/Necrotic Tumor, Viable Tumor

name: TextDetoxEval
num_samples: 900 toxic inputs (100 per language × 9 languages), outputs from 20 detoxification systems, ~16,600 total pairs
format: Multilingual text detoxification dataset: toxic sentences paired with system-generated detoxified outputs and human annotations for fluency, content similarity, and style transfer accuracy across 9 languages (Amharic, Arabic, Chinese, English, German, Hindi, Russian, Spanish, Ukrainian)
metric: Spearman correlation with human judgments for fluency, content similarity, and toxicity dimensions; joint metric combining all three
notes: Released as part of CLEF 2024 Text Detoxification Shared Task. Used in arXiv:2507.15557 for multilingual evaluation of text detoxification metrics.

name: DialogueEvaluation-2022
num_samples: 875 toxic sentences (Russian), outputs from 15 detoxification systems
format: Russian text detoxification dataset from first shared task on detoxification: toxic sentences from social media (Odnoklassniki, Pikabu, Twitter) with crowdsourced non-toxic rewrites. Human annotations for fluency, content preservation, and style transfer quality.
metric: Spearman correlation with human judgments for fluency, content preservation, and toxicity reduction
access: https://github.com/s-nlp/paradetox (related); original dataset from Dementieva et al., 2022
notes: First Russian detoxification shared task (RUSSE-2022). Complement to TextDetoxEval. Used in arXiv:2507.15557 for Russian-specific evaluation.

name: DafnyBench
format: Dafny source code with formal specifications; evaluated by Dafny verifier pass rate
notes: Prior benchmark for formal software verification in Dafny (Loughridge et al., 2024). Passes if generated specifications verify against the Dafny verifier.

name: DafnyComp
format: Compositional Dafny programs assembled from LeetCode functions with autoformalized ground-truth specifications; evaluated by Dafny verifier
metric: verification rate, spec superiority rate (SSR), pass@128
notes: Benchmark introduced in Re:Form (2025) for evaluating compositional generalization in formal specification generation. Programs require multi-function chain specifications, testing out-of-domain generalization.

name: Waymo Open Dataset
num_samples: ~1,150 sequences (2030 scenes) with 390k LiDAR frames and synchronized images from 5 cameras + 64-beam LiDAR with intensity
format: Sensor suite recordings: RGB images (1920x1280) + 64-beam LiDAR point clouds with intensity values; poses; 3D bounding boxes
metric: PSNR / SSIM / LPIPS / LiDAR intensity RMSE (task-dependent)

name: WebVision-1.0
num_samples: 2.4M images (real-world noisy labels from web scraping)
format: Web-scale images with noisy labels from ImageNet 1000 classes; ~30% estimated noise rate
metric: top-1/top-5 accuracy on WebVision validation and ILSVRC2012 clean validation

name: FBP5500 (SCUT-FBP5500)
storage: ~2-5GB (aligned facial images, resolution varies by source)
format: Facial images with continuous beauty scores (1-5 range); standard 5-fold cross-validation protocol
metric: Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC), Mean Absolute Error (MAE)
notes: Facial Beauty Prediction benchmark dataset from South China University of Technology. Used in Diff-FBP (arXiv:2507.20363) as the primary evaluation benchmark. Images have beauty scores assigned by human raters.

name: mGeNTe
format: English source sentences with gender-ambiguous and unambiguous instances; provides two alternative target translations per sentence (one with explicit gender marking, one gender-avoiding). Languages: ES, DE, IT, EL.
notes: From Savoldi et al. 2025 (arXiv:2501.09409). Used in paper 2507.18338 alongside WinoMT for evaluating gender bias via uncertainty quantification in MT.

name: ETH-UCY
num_samples: 5 subsets (ETH, HOTEL, UNIV, ZARA1, ZARA2) with ~1500 pedestrians
format: Pedestrian trajectory coordinates (x,y) in world coordinates; each subset captured from different environments (university campus, hotel, street)

name: Stanford Drone Dataset (SDD)
num_samples: ~20,000 aerial images with ~11,000 trajectories across 20 scenes
format: Bird's-eye view RGB aerial images from drone footage with pedestrian/bicyclist trajectory bounding boxes and identities

name: RMTBench
num_samples: 8156 utterances from 80 characters, 8000+ dialogue rounds in English and Chinese
eval_time: hours for full evaluation across 10 models
format: Multi-turn user-centric role-playing dialogues; 5 user-intent scenarios (character understanding, character maintenance, implicit user intentions response, user preference awareness, sensitive behavior handling); 7 evaluation dimensions (emotional expression, emotional comprehension, plot advancement, character understanding, character maintenance, security, user preference awareness)
metric: LLM-as-judge scoring (Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct) validated against human annotations; 1-5 scale per dimension
notes: User-centric bilingual role-playing benchmark. Shifts from character-centric to user-intent-driven evaluation. arXiv:2507.20352.

name: EarthReason
eval_time: minutes for evaluation on test set
format: Remote sensing images with QA pairs (6 questions per sample, avg 20.86 words/question), bounding boxes, and pixel-level segmentation masks. Also supports region-level and contour-level annotations via Mask2Bbox and Mask2Contour transformations.
metric: gIoU, cIoU (pixel-level); Acc@0.5, gIoU (region-level); F1@1, F1@3, ASD, HD (contour-level)
notes: Released alongside SegEarth-R1 (Li et al., 2025). Used for geospatial pixel reasoning, region reasoning, and contour reasoning. Contains 28 categories of remote sensing objects.

name: RSVG (Remote Sensing Visual Grounding)
num_samples: Not specified in RemoteReasoner paper (referenced from Zhan et al. 2023)
format: Remote sensing images with referring expressions and bounding box annotations for visual grounding tasks.
access: Referenced from Zhan et al. 2023 (IEEE TGRS)
notes: Used in RemoteReasoner paper for zero-shot visual grounding evaluation. Training set explicitly excluded from RemoteReasoner training.

name: RRSISD (Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation)
num_samples: Not specified in RemoteReasoner paper (referenced from Liu et al. 2024b)
format: Remote sensing images with referring expressions and pixel-level segmentation masks for referring expression segmentation.
notes: Used in RemoteReasoner paper for zero-shot referring expression segmentation evaluation. Training set explicitly excluded from RemoteReasoner training.

name: GenoTEX
num_samples: 1,384 GTA (gene-trait association) problems across 913 datasets and 132 human traits
eval_time: minutes per problem (code execution on CPU); ~307s per GTA problem end-to-end with LLM agents
format: Gene expression analysis tasks: dataset selection, data preprocessing (microarray/RNA-seq), statistical analysis (Lasso regression for gene identification); evaluated via AUROC, F1, CSC, GSEA
metric: AUROC, F1 score, Composite Similarity Correlation (CSC), Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) Enrichment Score
notes: Currently the only comprehensive benchmark for gene expression analysis automation via LLM agents. Curated ground truth by professional bioinformaticians. Evaluates full pipeline from raw data to biological insights.

name: Adept
format: Sentence pairs differing by one adjectival modifier; 3-class labels (less likely, equally likely, more likely)
access: Available from Emami et al. ACL 2021 paper or contact authors

name: MCIF (Multimodal Crosslingual Instruction Following)
num_samples: 100 scientific talks (~10 hours of video, ~17k words)
eval_time: hours for full evaluation of 23 models on single GPU
format: Multimodal: scientific talk videos (mp4), audio (16kHz wav), transcripts, QA pairs, summaries in 4 languages (EN/DE/IT/ZH). Tasks: recognition (ASR), translation (MT/ST), QA, summarization across text/speech/video modalities.
notes: First human-annotated crosslingual multimodal instruction-following benchmark from scientific talks. Evaluates 23 LLMs/SpeechLLMs/VideoLLMs/MLLMs. Source: ACL 2023 papers. arXiv:2507.19634.

name: HaloQuest
format: Visual question answering dataset designed to probe multimodal hallucinations in vision-language models; images paired with questions about visual content
notes: From Wang et al., 2024e. Used in MoHoBench (arXiv:2507.21503) as one of two image sources for generating unanswerable visual questions.

name: MoHoBench
eval_time: hours for full evaluation of 28 models
format: Unanswerable visual questions benchmark for evaluating honesty in MLLMs; 4 categories (Context Dependent, False Premises, Subjective/Philosophical, Vague Description); evaluated with refusal rate, refusal rationality, and helpfulness metrics
metric: Refusal Rate, Refusal Rationality Score (1-10), General Helpfulness Score (1-10)
notes: First systematic benchmark for honesty in MLLMs via unanswerable visual questions. From Zhu et al., 2025 (arXiv:2507.21503). Evaluates 28 MLLMs including both proprietary (o1, GPT-4o) and open-source models.

name: DOLOMITES
num_samples: 519 task templates across 25 domains (1857 concrete input/output examples after expert revision)
eval_time: hours for full evaluation with multi-turn QA
format: Domain-specific long-form methodical tasks with <objective, procedure, input, output_specification> quadruples. Tasks span 25 professional domains (medicine, law, engineering, humanities, etc.). Evaluation via LLM judge checking checklist items.
metric: Writing task score (MATCH-based checklist coverage by frozen LLM judge)

name: QMSUM
num_samples: ~232 meetings (104 train, 68 val, 60 test) with 1725 query-summary pairs
format: Multi-domain meeting transcripts (academic, industry, public policy) with query-based human-written summaries. Each meeting has multiple query-summary pairs testing different information needs.

name: DocBench
num_samples: 229 PDF documents, multiple question-answer pairs across 5 domains (academia, finance, government, laws, news)
format: PDF documents with questions of 4 types: text, multimodal, metadata, unanswerable; evaluated via LLM judge (Llama3.1-70B-Instruct)
notes: Used in arXiv:2507.20804 (MMGraphRAG) as a primary benchmark. MMGraphRAG achieves 76.8% accuracy vs NaiveRAG 59.5% and GraphRAG 52.3%.

name: MMLongBench
num_samples: 135 long PDF documents from 7 domains, questions covering text/charts/tables/layout/figures
format: Long PDF documents with multimodal QA; evaluates single-page and multi-page evidence; evaluated via LLM judge
notes: MMLongBench-Doc from arXiv:2508.07105. Used in arXiv:2507.20804 (MMGraphRAG). MMGraphRAG achieves 38.8% accuracy / 34.1% F1 vs M3DOCRAG 21.0% accuracy.

name: CMEL
num_samples: 1,114 alignment instances from news (87), academia (475), and novels (552)
format: Document images with text-based KG + image-based KG (scene graphs); evaluated via micro/macro accuracy for cross-modal entity linking
notes: Cross-Modal Entity Linking dataset. Addresses gap in CMEL benchmarks (MATE uses synthetic 3D scenes). Used to validate SpecLink method: 51.8% micro / 59.2% macro accuracy vs DBSCAN 45.2% / 46.1%.

name: GlobalOpinionQA
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Multiple-choice subjective QA with role-dependent ground truths (countries as roles); answers vary by stakeholder perspective; questions cover global opinion topics
notes: Introduced by DURMUS et al. (2024). Used in MultiRole-R1 (arXiv:2507.20187) for training and evaluating subjective reasoning with perspective diversity.

name: CALI
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on model
format: Cultural natural language inference: premise-hypothesis pairs with role-dependent ground truths based on cultural context; tests cultural reasoning and perspective-taking
notes: Cultural Aware Natural Language Inference benchmark introduced by Huang & Yang (EMNLP 2023). Used as OOD evaluation in MultiRole-R1 (arXiv:2507.20187) for cross-cultural reasoning generalization.

name: COCOA-cls
format: Images with amodal instance segmentation annotations (visible + occluded regions); 80 categories from COCO
notes: Amodal segmentation benchmark based on MS COCO. Contains occlusions with varying levels. Used in VELA (arXiv:2508.01661) paper.

name: D2SA
format: Shopping scenario images with amodal instance segmentation annotations; 60 categories
notes: Amodal segmentation benchmark for shopping/self-checkout scenarios with intrinsic occlusions from overlapping merchandise. Used in VELA (arXiv:2508.01661) paper.

name: KINS
format: Street scene images with amodal instance segmentation annotations based on KITTI; includes depth and instance masks
notes: Amodal segmentation benchmark based on KITTI for autonomous driving scenarios. Used in VELA (arXiv:2508.01661) paper.

name: HRIPBench
format: QA pairs (question + answer + evidence) across 3 task types: safety boundary check (yes/no classification), quantitative questions (numerical values with units), polysubstance use risks (risk level classification). Each pair includes verbatim source evidence for automated fact-checking.
metric: Response rate, accuracy, precision, recall, F1, AUC-ROC, BERTScore, ROUGE-1, ROUGE-L, BLEU; tolerance-based scoring for quantitative questions; underestimation/overestimation metrics for risk classification
license: Research use (sources are publicly accessible harm reduction resources)
access: arXiv:2507.21815 (code/data not yet publicly released at time of analysis)
notes: HRIPBench evaluates LLMs' accuracy and safety risks in providing harm reduction information to people who use drugs (PWUD). Introduces 3 evaluation tasks and 2 schemes (Instruction-following and RAG). The benchmark reveals significant safety risks in SOTA LLMs for this domain. From Wang et al. 2025.

name: MEMERAG
format: Multilingual QA-to-answer pairs from MIRACL with human annotations for faithfulness and relevance in RAG settings
notes: ACL 2025 meta-evaluation benchmark for multilingual RAG. Native languages: EN, DE, ES, FR, HI. Used in STEMF paper (arXiv:2507.20752) for evaluating multilingual faithfulness evaluators.

name: mFACE
format: Article-summary pairs with human annotations for factual consistency evaluation across languages
notes: Multilingual factual consistency evaluation benchmark. Native languages: AR, EN, ES, FR, HI. Used in STEMF paper (arXiv:2507.20752) for evaluating Arabic faithfulness.

name: FRANK
num_samples: ~4892 (3063 factual + 1829 non-factual) from CNN/DM and XSum
format: Article-summary pairs with sentence-level factuality annotations; translated to ar, de, es, fr, it
notes: FRANK benchmark for factuality in abstractive summarization (Pagnoni et al., NAACL 2021). Native English, machine-translated to 5 languages. Used in STEMF paper (arXiv:2507.20752) for evaluating faithfulness across 7 languages.

name: WikiLingua
format: Article-summary pairs from WikiHow in 18 languages including EN, ES, PT, FR, DE, RU, IT, ID, NL, AR, VI, ZH, TH, JA, KO, HI, CS, TR
notes: Cross-lingual abstractive summarization dataset (Ladhak et al., EMNLP 2020). Used as training data in STEMF paper (arXiv:2507.20752) for generating synthetic multilingual faithful/corrupt summary pairs.

name: ObjectNet
format: Real-world object images with testing conditions that differ significantly from ImageNet (background, rotation, imaging conditions). Evaluates out-of-distribution robustness.
notes: Introduced by Barbu et al. (NeurIPS 2019). Used in TUNA (ICCV 2025, arXiv:2508.08165) as a challenging OOD benchmark for class-incremental learning with pretrained models.

name: JUFE-10K
format: Omnidirectional (360-degree) images with non-uniform distortions including brightness discontinuity, Gaussian blur, Gaussian noise, and stitching artifacts; MOS quality scores
notes: Large-scale OIQA dataset focused on non-uniform distortion scenarios. Used in HGAT-OIQA paper (arXiv:2508.09843). 20 viewports sampled per image for viewport-based evaluation.

name: OIQ-10K
format: Omnidirectional (360-degree) images with mixed distortion types: non-uniform distortion, global distortion, and no perceptible distortion; MOS quality scores
notes: Large-scale OIQA dataset covering diverse distortion types. Used in HGAT-OIQA paper (arXiv:2508.09843). 20 viewports sampled per image for viewport-based evaluation.

name: CSO-21K
num_samples: 21,649 topic pairs (4 classes: supertopic, subtopic, same-as, other)
format: Manually annotated research topic relationship triples extracted from CSO ontology. Train: 15,154 / Val: 2,166 / Test: 4,239.
notes: Novel benchmark from Pisu et al. 2025 (arXiv:2508.04213). Gold standard extracted from manually validated portions of CSO. Used to evaluate research topic relationship classification.

name: AIDA-KG
storage: ~TB (25M papers with metadata; full KG downloadable)
format: RDF knowledge graph covering papers, patents, authors, affiliations, venues, topics (CSO), industrial sectors. Queryable via SPARQL or downloadable.
notes: Academia/Industry Dynamics Knowledge Graph. Used in Sci-OG (Pisu et al. 2025) to extract topic occurrence and co-occurrence features for relationship classification.

name: ENCQA
eval_time: 1-4 hours for full evaluation across 9 VLMs
format: Synthetic chart images (bar charts, scatter plots, dot plots) with QA pairs targeting 6 visual encoding channels (position, length, area, color quantitative, color nominal, shape) and 8 tasks (retrieve value, find extrema, find anomaly, filter values, compute derived values, correlate values). Questions designed to require visual reasoning over encodings, not text extraction.
metric: accuracy (relaxed match within 5% for numeric; exact match for multiple choice; set equality for lists)
access: Not confirmed — paper states benchmark website but no URL provided in arXiv preprint
notes: From arXiv:2508.04650 (Mukherjee et al., Apple/Stanford). Tests VLMs on visual encoding sensitivity rather than chart types. Key finding: model performance varies significantly across encodings within same task; model size does not consistently improve performance. ENCQA is notable for systematic coverage of encoding-task matrix derived from visualization literature.

name: FinanceBench
format: Financial question answering grounded on publicly traded company disclosure documents; categories include numerical reasoning, logical reasoning, and information extraction
notes: Islam et al. (2023). Used in Active Reading paper (2508.09494) for expert domain adaptation experiments.

name: SimpleWikiQA
format: Subset of SimpleQA (Wei et al., 2024) filtered to questions with Wikipedia reference documents; tests adversarial tail factual recall
notes: Created by Active Reading paper authors (2508.09494) as a Wikipedia-grounded subset of SimpleQA for expert domain experiments.

name: DReSS
num_samples: Panoramic streetview imagery across multiple globally distributed cities
format: Ground-view panoramas collected from multiple continents with associated metadata
notes: DReSS (Panwang Xia et al., ISPRS 2025) provides panoramic streetview imagery from globally distributed cities. Used as source for DReSS-D and the proposed CVFM benchmark in ViewBridge (arXiv:2508.10716).

name: DReSS-D
num_samples: Geometrically aligned ground-satellite pairs with per-pixel depth maps from 6 globally distributed cities
eval_time: minutes to hours depending on method
format: Ground-view panoramas + satellite imagery + per-pixel depth maps with 3-DoF pose labels; supports same-area and cross-area protocols
notes: DReSS-D (Zhang et al., arXiv:2508.05369) is a reprocessed, geometrically aligned version of DReSS with satellite images and depth maps. Used as training data and evaluation benchmark in ViewBridge (arXiv:2508.10716).

name: CVFM
num_samples: 32,509 ground-satellite image pairs with pixel-level correspondences
storage: ~5-10GB estimated (pairs without full imagery, which comes from DReSS)
format: Ground-view panoramas + satellite images with dense pixel-level correspondences generated via depth projection; manually verified by 3 experts
metric: percentage of correct correspondences at 5/10/15 pixel thresholds on satellite image
access: Not yet released (proposed by ViewBridge paper)
notes: CVFM: Cross-View Fine-grained image Matching benchmark proposed in ViewBridge (arXiv:2508.10716). First benchmark with pixel-level ground-satellite correspondences. Derived from DReSS/DReSS-D using depth maps to project ground pixels onto satellite images. Enables systematic evaluation of fine-grained cross-view matching algorithms.

name: EgoHumans
format: Egocentric multi-view RGB videos of human activities with accurate 3D pose annotations and camera parameters. Features both large-scale outdoor scenes (badminton, tennis, volleyball) and small indoor environments (basketball, fencing, lego, tagging).
metric: MPJPE, PA-MPJPE, GA-MPJPE, camera pose errors (TE, s-TE, AE, RRA, CCA, s-CCA)
notes: Egocentric 3D multi-human benchmark introduced by Khirodkar et al. (ICCV 2023). Used in HAMSt3R (arXiv:2508.16433) and concurrent methods (HSfM, UnCaliPose) for evaluating joint human pose estimation and camera pose recovery from unstructured multi-view egocentric video.

name: HuMMan
format: Multi-modal 4D human dataset with RGBD video, motion capture markers, SMPL parameters, and depth maps. Subjects perform diverse poses in studio environments.
notes: Multi-modal 4D human dataset for versatile sensing and modeling (Cai et al., ECCV 2022). Used as training data in HAMSt3R (arXiv:2508.16433) for human-centric 3D reconstruction.

name: TAAROFBENCH
format: role-play scenario tuples with culturally expected response annotations; evaluated via GPT-4 judge
metric: accuracy (binary: response meets cultural expectation or not)

name: WavelengthEval
format: JSON with concept pairs, target values, clues, and human judgments (40 per problem)
metric: absolute difference (task accuracy), Wasserstein distance (distribution similarity), Pearson correlation (human-model correlation)
notes: Benchmark for evaluating LMs' pragmatic reasoning via Wavelength communication game. Tasks: comprehension (given clue, guess value) and production (given value, generate clue). Collected 708 human participants via Prolific for ground-truth judgments. Based on the public Wavelength game (linlu-qiu/wavelength-eval, Qiu et al. 2025).

name: SimplerEnv
num_samples: Multiple robot platforms (WidowX, UR5, Franka) with varied task suites
format: Simulation benchmark for evaluating real-world robot manipulation policies. Designed to closely mirror real-world physical dynamics and visual appearances. Includes Visual Matching setting that minimizes sim-to-real gap. Tasks include pick-place, stacking, and manipulation of various objects.

name: Argoverse 2 Sensor
num_samples: 1000 scenes (750 train/150 val/100 test), ~15-56s duration each
format: Multimodal urban driving dataset with 7 surround-view cameras, 2 LiDAR sensors, radar sweeps, and HD maps. Includes 3D bounding boxes, trajectory data, and map annotations.
notes: Full sensor dataset. Used as the base for ArgoTweak (arXiv:2509.08764) which provides realistic map priors paired with this sensor data.

name: Argoverse 2 Map Change Dataset
num_samples: 799 train / 111 val / 133 test scenes with map change annotations
format: HD map change detection dataset pairing stale map priors with current sensor data. Includes global, frame-level, and element-level change annotations. Train split has scripted synthetic priors; val/test have real-world priors.
metric: mACC (coarse change detection accuracy), mAP (map element average precision)
notes: Lambert & Hays (NeurIPS 2021 D&B). Provides real-world stale map priors for val/test only. Used as foundation for ArgoTweak (arXiv:2509.08764) which extends it with ground-truth updated maps and realistic synthetic priors for training.

name: ArgoTweak
num_samples: 697 train / 102 val / 111 test scenes (~56s avg), ~1.37M element-level annotations
storage: ~100-200GB (ArgoTweak annotations + Argoverse 2 base maps; requires Argoverse 2 Sensor for full data)
format: First dataset with realistic map priors + current sensor data + ground-truth updated HD maps. Features bijective change mapping framework with element-level atomic change annotations (geometry, markings, type, insertion, deletion). Baseline model + evaluation toolkit (mAPC, mACC metrics) included.
metric: mAPC (change-aware mean Average Precision), mACC (change detection accuracy)
notes: Wild et al. (arXiv:2509.08764). Closes sim2real gap in prior-aided HD mapping. Enables standardized training/evaluation of prior integration approaches with explainable element-level change annotations.

name: SHREC'19
num_samples: 44 human 3D scans with 430 annotated test pairs
format: 3D human mesh scans with ground-truth semantic correspondences between pairs; used for evaluating non-isometric shape correspondence methods

name: SHREC'20
num_samples: 40 animal 3D shapes in diverse poses with expert-labeled non-isometric correspondences
format: 3D mesh models of animals in varied poses with ground-truth semantic correspondences; tests generalization to non-isometric deformations and cross-pose matching
metric: correspondence accuracy, geodesic error, edge distortion ratio

name: ShapeNet Part
num_samples: ~50,000 annotated ShapeNet models across 13 part categories (airplane, cap, chair, earphone, guitar, knife, lamp, motorbike, mug, pistol, rocket, skateboard, table)
eval_time: minutes to hours for co-segmentation evaluation
format: 3D mesh models with per-vertex part labels; each shape annotated with category-specific part segments; widely used for part segmentation and co-segmentation tasks

name: AIME 2025
format: 15 short-answer olympiad-style questions (American Invitational Mathematics Examination 2025)
notes: AIME 2025 benchmark used in Calibrated Reasoning paper (arXiv:2509.19681) for evaluating best-of-N and self-reflection with Explanatory Verifier.

name: LeetCode
format: Programming problems with descriptions, reference solutions, and test cases. Diverse difficulty levels and algorithmic categories.
notes: LeetCode dataset used in Calibrated Reasoning paper (arXiv:2509.19681) as training data source (coding subset). Curated version from Skywork-OR1-RL-Data used to avoid empty/corrupted test cases.

name: Skywork-OR1-RL-Data
num_samples: Not publicly disclosed (large-scale RL training dataset)
format: Curated math and coding problems for RL training. Sources include NuminaMath, TACO, and LeetCode with automated correctness verification.
notes: Skywork Open Reasoner RL training dataset. Used as foundation dataset in Calibrated Reasoning paper (arXiv:2509.19681). Authors applied additional filtering: removed multi-answer, multi-choice, proof-based questions; used sympy parsing for single numeric answers; filtered by LLM-as-a-judge quality assessment.

name: QuanTemp
format: Real-world numerical claims with evidence retrieved via BM25 + reranking; verdict labels: True/False/Conflicting
metric: per-class F1, macro F1, weighted F1
notes: First benchmark for complex numerical fact-checking claims (V et al., SIGIR 2024). Claims contain quantitative and temporal elements requiring compositional/numerical reasoning.

name: ClaimDecomp
format: Real-world compositional claims decomposed into yes/no sub-questions; verdict: TRUE/FALSE/CONFLICTING
metric: per-class F1, macro F1, weighted F1
notes: Benchmark for fact-checking compositional real-world claims via sub-question decomposition (Chen et al., EMNLP 2022). Tests generalization of fact-checking methods across claim types.

name: MODMA
num_samples: 53 subjects (24 MDD + 29 controls), 139 epochs per subject
storage: ~1-3GB raw EEG (128 channels, 250Hz, 280s per subject); <100MB processed features
format: 128-channel HydroCel Geodesic Sensor Nets EEG, resting-state, eyes-closed, 5-minute recordings at 250Hz. Preprocessed to 280s with 0.3-30Hz FIR filtering, ICA artifact removal, segmented into 4s epochs with 50% overlap.
license: Research use (public dataset on Harvard Dataverse)
notes: MODMA dataset used in ELPG-DTFS paper (arXiv:2509.24860) for EEG-based major depressive disorder detection. Binary classification: MDD vs healthy controls. 10-fold subject-wise cross-validation standard evaluation protocol.

name: ZSRE
format: Question-answer pairs derived from Wikipedia via distant supervision; question-style prompts for evaluating knowledge editing
access: https://github.com/SwannaButt/RippleEdits (RIPPLEEDITS repo); original ZSRE from Levy et al., 2017

name: PARAREL
format: Entity-relation-attribute triplets derived from Wikidata; used for computing entity-specific subspaces via SVD in knowledge editing

name: CHED
num_samples: ~1,000 edit instances with diverse prefix contexts
format: Knowledge editing test set evaluating robustness of edited facts under diverse prefix contexts (rewrite, paraphrase, neighborhood prompts)
access: https://github.com/holi-lab/SUIT (SUIT repo); original from Park et al., 2025 (ACL 2025 Findings)

name: RIPPLEEDITS
num_samples: ~1,000 edit instances with logical ripple relations
format: Knowledge editing test set measuring whether edits correctly propagate to associated facts across multiple logical relations

name: MuSLR-Bench
eval_time: hours for full evaluation with all models
format: Image + text pairs with formal logic annotations, ground-truth reasoning chains, Truth Evaluation (True/False/Unknown) and Multiple Choice questions
notes: First benchmark for multimodal symbolic logical reasoning. Combines formal logic (propositional, first-order, non-monotonic) with joint image+text inputs. 7 domains, 35 atomic logic rules, 976 logical combinations, reasoning depths 2-9. From arXiv:2509.25851.

name: nocaps
format: Images with novel object captions, requiring describing objects not in COCO training set
notes: Novel object captioning at scale dataset. Used as image source in MuSLR benchmark (arXiv:2509.25851).

name: RVL_CDIP
format: Document images with text (15 categories: letter, form, email, handwritten, advertisement, etc.)
notes: RVL-CDIP document classification dataset. Used as image source in MuSLR benchmark (arXiv:2509.25851).

name: VisuLogic
format: Vision-centric logical reasoning benchmark with visual contexts, multiple-choice questions
notes: VisuLogic benchmark for evaluating visual reasoning in multi-modal LLMs. Related work in MuSLR paper (arXiv:2509.25851).

name: SALMON
format: Suite for acoustic language model evaluation. Tests acoustic consistency (speaker, gender, sentiment, background, room factors) and semantic-acoustic alignment. Pairwise preference evaluation where model must assign higher likelihood to natural recording vs. one with mid-utterance factor change.
notes: SALMON benchmark from Maimon et al., ICASSP 2025. Used in CAST paper (arXiv:2509.26276) to evaluate acoustic consistency and alignment of speech LMs.

name: ARCH
num_samples: ~6 datasets (ESC-50, US8K, VIVAE, RAVDESS, SLURP, EMOVO)
format: Benchmarking representations for speech, music, and acoustic events. Linear probe evaluation on frozen LM features across content-leaning (ESC-50, US8K, SLURP) and prosody-leaning (VIVAE, EMOVO, RAVDESS) tasks.
access: Based on La Quatra et al., ICASSPW 2024
notes: ARCH benchmark from La Quatra et al., ICASSPW 2024. Used in CAST paper (arXiv:2509.26276) for linear probe analysis of internal representations.

name: LibriLight
format: Unlabeled English audiobook recordings (LibriVox) curated to be relatively clean. No transcripts. 96k hours originally, 57k hour clean subset commonly used.
notes: Primary training dataset for CAST paper (arXiv:2509.26276), ~57k hours combined with People's Speech clean subset.

name: People's Speech
format: Large-scale diverse English speech recognition dataset with conversational and broadcast data. Clean subset filtered for training.
notes: Secondary training dataset for CAST paper (arXiv:2509.26276). Clean subset (~20k hours) added to LibriLight (~57k hours) for ~77k hours total training.

name: VIVAE
format: Vocal imitations and affect expression dataset. Contains acted vocal imitations of various emotions and sound effects. Used in ARCH linear probe evaluation.
notes: Part of ARCH benchmark suite. Used in CAST paper (arXiv:2509.26276) linear probe evaluation for prosody-leaning tasks.

name: EMOVO
format: Italian acted emotion speech database with 7 emotions (anger, disgust, fear, joy, sadness, surprise, neutral). Used in ARCH linear probe evaluation.
notes: Part of ARCH benchmark suite. Used in CAST paper (arXiv:2509.26276) linear probe evaluation for prosody-leaning tasks.

name: RAVDESS
format: Ryerson Audio-Visual Database of Emotional Speech and Song. Contains 24 actors expressing 8 emotions (neutral, calm, happy, sad, angry, fearful, surprise, disgust) in both speech and song modalities. Used in ARCH linear probe evaluation.
notes: Part of ARCH benchmark suite. Used in CAST paper (arXiv:2509.26276) linear probe evaluation for prosody/mixed tasks. Shows +6 point improvement with semantic-distilled initialization at 100% training stage.

name: RoboSuite
format: Standardized robot simulation benchmark using MuJoCo physics; tasks include Lift, Pick Place Can, Assembly Square; supports RGB-only and RGB-D observations; configurable camera poses for viewpoint generalization studies
notes: RoboSuite is a widely used robot manipulation benchmark built on MuJoCo. From Zhao et al. (RSS 2023) for ACT paper. This paper (Jiang et al., 2510.02268) creates fixed and randomized variants of RoboSuite tasks to study viewpoint generalization with and without camera pose conditioning.

name: RealBench
eval_time: 1-2 hours per scene for per-scene optimization methods
format: Reference images (1-5 per scene), target image with missing regions, binary mask, ground-truth completion
metric: PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, DreamSim, DINO, CLIP
access: From RealFill authors (Tang et al., TOG 2024)

name: QualBench
format: Reference images, target image with missing regions, binary mask; no ground-truth (user study evaluation)
metric: User study scores (1-5) on realism, consistency, structural/color coherence
access: From RealFill authors (Tang et al., TOG 2024)

name: SPBench-SI
format: Single-image spatial reasoning benchmark constructed from ScanNet validation scenes. Tests absolute distance, object size, relative distance, relative direction.
access: research (paper introduces; validation set scenes from ScanNet)
notes: Proposed in SpatialLadder paper (arXiv:2510.08531). Scene-level separation ensures zero overlap with training data.

name: SPBench-MV
format: Multi-view spatial reasoning benchmark from ScanNet validation scenes. Tests object counting, absolute distance, object size, relative distance, relative direction across 8 viewpoints.
access: research (paper introduces; validation set scenes from ScanNet)
notes: Proposed in SpatialLadder paper (arXiv:2510.08531). Scene-level separation ensures zero overlap with training data.

name: SPAR-Bench
format: Comprehensive spatial perception and reasoning benchmark with 20 diverse tasks spanning single-view, multi-view, and video modalities.
notes: From Zhang et al. (2025). Out-of-domain benchmark in SpatialLadder paper (arXiv:2510.08531).

name: ViewSpatial-Bench
format: Perspective-dependent spatial understanding benchmark from ScanNet and MS-COCO validation datasets. Tests camera-perspective and person-perspective spatial reasoning.
notes: From Li et al. (2025a). Out-of-domain benchmark in SpatialLadder paper (arXiv:2510.08531).

name: SpatialLadder-26k
format: Multimodal spatial reasoning dataset: object localization (5,929), single-image (5,929), multi-view (5,752), video (9,000). Constructed from ScanNet 3D scenes and SR-91k videos using 3D-to-2D transformation pipeline.
notes: Training dataset for SpatialLadder (arXiv:2510.08531). Seven spatial dimensions: relative direction, relative distance, absolute distance, object size, counting, room size, appearance order.

name: GRIT
storage: ~200GB+ estimated (14M image-text pairs with bounding boxes)
format: Image-text pairs with bounding box annotations and corresponding nouns/phrases. Automatically annotated.
notes: Used as pretraining corpus for PHyCLIP, HyCoCLIP, and MERU. Paper reports 14M pairs obtained (out of 20.5M documented due to outdated links).

name: VL-CheckList
format: Hard negative captions generated by altering objects, attributes, or relations in ground-truth captions. Tests compositional understanding.
notes: Used in PHyCLIP and HyCoCLIP to evaluate compositional understanding. Object subset tests noun replacement difficulty by location and size.

name: CUB-200-2011 (CUB-2011)
format: Caltech-UCSD Birds 200-2011: 200 bird species with image-level and part-level annotations
notes: Fine-grained bird classification dataset. Used in PHyCLIP zero-shot classification evaluation as a fine-grained benchmark.

name: Country211
format: Images paired with country-of-origin labels. Part of CLIP evaluation suite.
notes: Fine-grained country classification benchmark used in PHyCLIP zero-shot classification. Evaluates zero-shot transfer to geographic classification.

name: Calvin
format: Simulation benchmark for language-conditioned long-horizon robot manipulation. Four environments (A, B, C, D). Trains on A/B/C, evaluates on D (ABC-D split). Single third-person RGB image input.
metric: Average length of completed sub-task sequences (Avg. Len)
notes: CALVIN benchmark (Zutschi et al., 2022). Evaluates multi-stage language-conditioned manipulation. Used in UniCoD (arXiv:2510.10642) for long-horizon manipulation evaluation. UniCoD achieves 4.11 avg. length vs UP-VLA's 4.08.

name: Fractal
num_samples: ~100k+ real robot demonstrations (subset used in SimplerEnv)
format: Real-world robot manipulation dataset with language instructions. Used in SimplerEnv-Google Robot evaluation. Fractal dataset with diverse manipulation tasks.
notes: Fractal is a real-world robot manipulation dataset used in RoboVLM (Liu et al., 2025) and SimplerEnv (Google Robot setting). Referenced in UniCoD (arXiv:2510.10642) as one of the training data sources and evaluation benchmarks.

name: IOI 2025
eval_time: minutes to hours per submission (depends on solution complexity and IOI time/memory limits)
format: Competitive programming problems in C++/Python; evaluated with official IOI grader; subtask-level scoring (max 100 points per problem); up to 50 submissions per problem
metric: Score@K (max score across K submissions); final score out of 600 (gold threshold ~400-450 depending on year)
notes: International Olympiad in Informatics 2025. Six problems with 2-12 subtasks each, requiring algorithmic solutions under strict time/memory constraints. Top human contestants score ~590/600 (gold threshold is typically top ~50%). AlphaCode2 and OpenAI o1-ioi/o3 have achieved gold-level performance on prior IOI benchmarks.

name: WereBench
format: Multiple-choice QA (speech evaluation, 5 dimensions) + vote alignment (decision evaluation)

name: NLST (National Lung Screening Trial)
num_samples: ~72,000 chest CT scans from ~26,000 patients (1-3 scans per patient at baseline and follow-up)
format: Low-dose chest CT volumes without associated reports. Used as image-only dataset for self-supervised pretraining. Multiple reconstruction kernels available.
notes: National Lung Screening Trial. Used for MAE pretraining in COLIPRI (arXiv:2510.15042). Large-scale image-only chest CT dataset enabling self-supervised learning. From NLST Research Team (2011).

name: LiTS (Liver Tumor Segmentation)
num_samples: 131 training liver CT scans (Task 3 of MSD)
format: 3D abdominal CT scans with liver and liver tumor segmentations. Resampled to 1mm isotropic for COLIPRI experiments.
notes: Medical Segmentation Decathlon Task 3. Used for segmentation fine-tuning evaluation in COLIPRI (arXiv:2510.15042). From Simpson et al. (2019).

name: KiTS23 (Kidney Tumor Segmentation 2023)
format: 3D abdominal CT scans with kidney, tumor, and cyst segmentations. Resampled to 1mm isotropic for COLIPRI experiments.
notes: Kidney Tumor Segmentation Challenge 2023. Used for segmentation fine-tuning evaluation in COLIPRI (arXiv:2510.15042). From Heller et al. (2023).

name: HVS (Hepatic Vessel Segmentation, MSD Task 8)
num_samples: 303 training hepatic vessel CT scans (Task 8 of MSD)
format: 3D abdominal CT scans with hepatic vessel and adjacent tumor segmentations. Resampled to 1mm isotropic for COLIPRI experiments.
notes: Medical Segmentation Decathlon Task 8 (Hepatic Vessel Segmentation). Used for segmentation fine-tuning evaluation in COLIPRI (arXiv:2510.15042). From Simpson et al. (2019).

name: Sample100
format: Commercial music recordings (hip-hop queries, reference/noise songs)
access: Released by Van Balen et al. (CMMR 2013), used in subsequent works [12, 14]

name: SamplePairs
format: 100 commercial music pairs (diverse genres: pop, electro, hip-hop) + 5,434 MTG-Jamendo songs as noise candidates
license: Not clearly specified (released with paper code)
access: Released by authors alongside paper code

name: AlpacaFarm
num_samples: ~100 evaluation prompts (paper uses 100); full dataset has 10K+
eval_time: hours (depending on model and number of generations)
format: Simulation framework for methods that learn from human feedback. Uses LLM-as-a-judge to evaluate instruction-following models at scale. Paper: Dubois et al., 2023.
metric: Win rate vs reference model (Llama); reward model scores

name: ACDC (Autonomous Driving)
format: Adverse conditions driving dataset: fog, rain, night, snow; 19-class semantic labels; captured in Swiss cities

name: GTA5
format: Extracted from video game; US cities; 19-class semantic labels; 24966 images

name: Synscapes
format: Photorealistic synthetic dataset for street scene parsing; designed to mimic Cityscapes; 25000 images

name: UrbanSyn
format: High-effort synthetic driving dataset; designed to mimic Cityscapes distribution; 7539 images
access: Request from authors (Gómez et al., Neurocomputing 2025)

name: VEIS
format: Low-effort synthetic dataset; created by single person in one day; 3018-image subset used (every 10th frame from video); European city streets

name: University-1652
num_samples: ~50K+ images (702 locations training, 950 locations testing; drone + satellite views)
format: Multi-view drone and satellite images for cross-view geo-localization. Each location has one satellite image and multiple oblique drone views at different altitudes and azimuths.
notes: First drone-based geo-localization benchmark. Used in MobileGeo (arXiv:2510.22582) as the primary benchmark. Train: 702 locations. Test: 950 locations. Drone images captured at 3 heights and 18 azimuths per location.

name: SUES-200
format: Multi-height multi-scene cross-view image benchmark. Aerial photography captured by drones at different flight heights (150m, 200m, 250m, 300m) in real-world scenes.
notes: SUES-200: A Multi-Height Multi-Scene Cross-View Image Benchmark across Drone and Satellite (Zhu et al., IEEE T-CSVT 2023). Used in MobileGeo (arXiv:2510.22582) for zero-shot domain adaptation evaluation (train on University-1652, test on SUES-200).

name: Trans10k
format: Transparent object images (glass, etc.) with pixel-level masks for segmentation. From Xie et al. (ECCV 2020).
notes: Transparent object segmentation dataset. Used for glass detection (GD) task in Controllable-LPMoE paper (arXiv:2510.21114).

name: GDD
format: Glass detection dataset with diverse real-world scenes. Images with glass region segmentation masks.
notes: Glass detection dataset. Used for glass detection (GD) task in Controllable-LPMoE paper (arXiv:2510.21114).

name: OfficeBench
format: Office automation benchmark evaluating cross-application workflows using Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Email, Calendar tools. Tasks require multi-step tool orchestration across office applications.
notes: From Wang et al., 2024. Used in Simia-Agent paper (2511.01824) to evaluate agent training via LLM-simulated environments.

name: APIGen-MT
num_samples: ~5k training trajectories (~1.5k for airline, ~3.5k for retail)
format: Multi-turn tool-use dataset for agent training. Contains realistic API interactions in airline (flight changes, cancellations) and retail (order management, returns) domains.
notes: From Prabhakar et al., 2025. Used as seed dataset in Simia-Agent paper (2511.01824) for trajectory synthesis.

name: MADRAS
format: Bird's-eye view (zenithal) video trajectories from Festival of Lights 2022 in Lyon, France; 9 diverse urban crowd scenes; pedestrian 2D coordinates at video framerate; scene segmentation maps; leave-one-scene-out evaluation protocol
metric: ADE (Average Displacement Error), FDE (Final Displacement Error), minADE, minFDE, AUC, Collision Rate
notes: High-density crowd trajectory dataset (up to 4 pedestrians per square meter). Used in VISTA paper (2511.10203) for multi-agent trajectory prediction in dense crowds. Introduced by Dufour et al., Scientific Data 2025.

name: HiddenAgenda
format: Multi-turn dialogue stealth/sabotage tasks where model pursues hidden objectives; adapted variant used with model-as-user simulation
metric: Hidden objective completion rate, LLM monitor suspiciousness score, interrogation F1

name: SHADE-Arena
format: Agentic tool-use stealth/sabotage evaluation suite with 20+ tools per task; model pursues hidden objective while appearing to work on user-specified objective
metric: Hidden objective completion success rate, evasion success rate, LLM monitor suspiciousness score

name: NRC VAD Lexicon v2 (MWE-VAD)
num_samples: ~55k total (~10k MWEs + ~25k new unigrams + ~20k from v1)
format: Word and multiword expression VAD scores (real-valued, -1 to 1 scale)
license: Research use (free for research, no redistribution)
notes: Extension of NRC VAD Lexicon v1 (Mohammad, 2018) adding ~10k MWEs and ~25k unigrams. Annotations via Mechanical Turk with 9 annotators per term. SHR > 0.95 for all dimensions. Created by Saif M. Mohammad, NRC Canada (2025).

name: UAVid
num_samples: 420 images from 30 video sequences (8000 train + 2800 val patches at 512x512)
format: UAV semantic segmentation dataset; oblique-view aerial imagery at 50m altitude; 8 classes: building, road, static car, tree, low vegetation, human, moving car, clutter; includes scale variation, motion blur, occlusions
notes: Used in AdaptFly (2511.11720) for UAV semantic segmentation under domain shift.

name: VDD (Varied Drone Dataset)
num_samples: Not specified in paper; standardized at 2048x1024 resolution
format: UAV aerial dataset covering rural, industrial, diverse low-altitude environments; varied flight altitudes and perspectives; 7 classes: Others, Wall, Road, Vegetation, Vehicle, Roof, Water; significant domain shifts across lighting, terrain, object appearances
notes: Used in AdaptFly (2511.11720) for cross-domain UAV semantic segmentation. Paper 2511.17890 also references VDD.

name: BIMCV-R
num_samples: ~3,000+ CT scans (exact number not specified in paper)
storage: ~tens of GB estimated (3D lung CT volumes)
format: 3D lung CT scans paired with radiology reports. Used for text-to-image and image-to-text retrieval evaluation. Paper notes quality issues: some images depict localizer scans or non-lung body regions.
notes: From Chen et al., MICCAI 2024. BIMCV-R: A Landmark Dataset for 3D CT Text-Image Retrieval. Used in brat paper (2512.18679) as an external validation benchmark to test framework generalizability to other 3D medical imaging modalities.

name: ForgeryNet
num_samples: ~60k training + 14k test + 14k val videos (Standard subset); 5.6k train + 700 test + 700 val (Balanced subset)
eval_time: hours for full evaluation on Standard subset
format: Videos with frame-level and video-level forgery labels. Supports multiple manipulation techniques (inpainting, splicing, etc.). Standard subset is long-tailed; Balanced subset has uniform class distribution.
metric: AP@0.5, AP@0.75, AP@0.95 (Average Precision at tIoU thresholds)
notes: From He et al., CVPR 2021. A versatile benchmark for comprehensive forgery analysis including image and video manipulation detection and localization.

name: TVIL
num_samples: Not publicly specified; specialized video inpainting scene dataset
format: Videos with frame-level manipulation labels for video inpainting forgery localization. Constructed by removing objects at random time intervals using advanced inpainting algorithms.
metric: AP@0.5, AP@0.75, AP@0.95 (Average Precision at tIoU thresholds)
notes: Temporal Video Inpainting Localization benchmark. Specialized for video inpainting scenes only. Used in DDNet paper (2601.01784) and UMMAFormer paper for temporal forgery localization evaluation.

name: AdvFake-News-Please
num_samples: ~10K+ (seed real articles + adversarial fake variants across multiple generators and rounds)
eval_time: minutes per full evaluation (5000 detector evaluations)
format: Real news articles paired with adversarial fake variants; also includes cross-attacker test set with GPT-5.3 Instant generated fakes
access: Released by Chen et al. 2025 in 'Real-time factuality assessment from adversarial feedback' (ACL 2025)

name: News-Please
format: Real news articles scraped from multiple news sources; used as both training seed articles and retrieval corpus for RADAR

name: DanceTrack
num_samples: 100 video sequences with ~1M bounding box annotations
format: Multi-object tracking dataset of dance videos with diverse styles (classical, street, pop, sports). Characterized by visually similar performers, frequent occlusions, and fast non-linear motion.
notes: CVPR 2022. Dominated by end-to-end trackers in literature. Challenging due to uniform appearance (dancers in similar costumes) and diverse non-linear motion patterns.

name: SportsMOT
num_samples: ~500 video sequences spanning basketball, volleyball, football
format: Large-scale multi-object tracking dataset in multiple sports scenes. Highly non-linear motion with frequent accelerations, decelerations, and direction changes.
notes: ICCV 2023. Sports scenes with visually similar players and challenging motion patterns.

name: SoccerNet-Tracking
format: Multi-object tracking dataset and benchmark in soccer videos. Player tracking across diverse match scenarios and camera viewpoints.
notes: CVPR 2022. Related to SportsMOT in domain and visual characteristics. TDLP uses dataset-provided YOLOX detector.

name: BEE24
num_samples: Multiple bee video sequences under natural conditions
format: MOT benchmark for ecological scenarios with bees. Crowded scenes, frequent occlusions, rapid irregular motion, near-identical appearances. Non-human domain with fundamentally different visual and motion characteristics.
notes: TIP 2025. Most challenging benchmark in terms of motion prediction with dense interactions, occlusions, and highly irregular trajectories.

name: Tableau Public Stories
num_samples: 20 curated reports (18 topics), ~113 tables per report on average
format: Data-driven analytical reports with interleaved text and charts from Tableau Public; includes underlying CSV tables, report titles as analysis requests
metric: Layout Rationality, Readability, Text-Chart Consistency, Textual Information Depth, Informativeness, Visual Consistency
notes: Used in EvidFuse paper (arXiv:2601.05487) for evaluating text-chart interleaved report generation.

name: Our World in Data (OWID)
num_samples: 20 curated reports (18 topics), ~109 tables per report on average
format: Data-driven analytical reports from Our World in Data with interleaved text and charts; includes underlying CSV tables, report titles as analysis requests
metric: Layout Rationality, Readability, Text-Chart Consistency, Textual Information Depth, Informativeness, Visual Consistency
notes: Used in EvidFuse paper (arXiv:2601.05487) for evaluating text-chart interleaved report generation.

name: USAFacts
num_samples: 20 curated reports (18 topics), ~87 tables per report on average
format: Data-driven analytical reports from USAFacts with interleaved text and charts; includes underlying CSV tables, report titles as analysis requests
metric: Layout Rationality, Readability, Text-Chart Consistency, Textual Information Depth, Informativeness, Visual Consistency
notes: Used in EvidFuse paper (arXiv:2601.05487) for evaluating text-chart interleaved report generation.

name: CASIA-B
num_samples: ~124 subjects, 11 view angles (0-180 degrees), ~6 conditions per subject (NM/BG/CL)
format: RGB video sequences of walking subjects from multiple viewpoints; conditions include normal walking (NM), carrying bag (BG), and wearing coat (CL)
notes: Standard gait recognition benchmark; widely used since 2006. 124 subjects with 11 viewing angles.

name: CCPG
format: RGB video sequences for cloth-changing gait recognition; testing scenarios include CL-FULL (full clothing change), CL-UP (upper garment change), CL-DN (lower garment change)
notes: Cloth-Changing gait dataset specifically designed to evaluate robustness to clothing variations. Paper being analyzed (LMGait) achieves 88.5% mean Rank-1 on CCPG.

name: SUSTech1K
num_samples: ~1000 subjects, multiple conditions (visibility, view angles, occlusions, environments)
format: Large-scale RGB gait dataset with diverse environmental conditions including clothing changes, night vision, different viewpoints, and occlusions
notes: Large-scale gait recognition benchmark (SUSTech1K) with diverse real-world conditions. Paper being analyzed (LMGait) achieves 97.1% mean Rank-1 on SUSTech1K.

name: GovReport
num_samples: 973 U.S. government reports with expert-written abstractive summaries
format: Long document summarization dataset with human-written reference summaries
metric: MAE (length control), PM (precision match), LLM-as-judge quality scores

name: ELI5
format: Long-form question answering with reference answers from Reddit ELI5
metric: MAE (length control), PM (precision match), LLM-as-judge quality scores

name: FActScore Biographies
format: Biography generation from Wikipedia facts; evaluates factual precision of generated text
metric: FActScore (atomic fact precision), coherence, MAE (length control)

name: Gait3D
format: Silhouette-based gait sequences captured in the wild with 3D representations; includes diverse walking conditions, views, and clothing changes. Evaluation uses rank-1, rank-5, and mAP.
notes: From Zheng et al., CVPR 2022. Gait recognition in the wild with dense 3D representations. Large-scale in-the-wild gait dataset with challenging conditions.

name: GREW
format: Large-scale in-the-wild gait dataset with diverse camera views and walking conditions. Silhouette-based gait recognition benchmark.
notes: From Zhu et al., ICCV 2021. Gait recognition in the wild benchmark. Largest in-the-wild gait dataset at time of release with 20K training identities.

name: EHRSHOT
num_samples: ~980 patients with longitudinal EHR data spanning decades; 4 clinical prediction tasks
storage: ~50-200GB+ (estimated; longitudinal records with thousands of events per patient; 2.3x more events and 95.2x more encounters per patient than MIMIC-IV)
eval_time: hours per model for full evaluation across 4 tasks
format: MEDS-compatible structured EHR data with structured clinical events (diagnoses, medications, lab results, procedures); each event has code, value, and timestamp
metric: Accuracy, Macro-F1, per-class F1 for clinical prediction tasks
license: PhysioNet credentialed data use agreement (free but requires application)
notes: Introduced in Wornow et al. 2023 (NeurIPS). Distinct from MIMIC-III/IV in that it captures longitudinal patient records across general hospital care (not just ICU/emergency), spanning multiple decades with thousands of events per patient. Tasks: Long Length of Stay, 30-day Readmission, Acute MI, Anemia.

name: ChaosNLI
format: NLI premise-hypothesis pairs with dense human label distributions (100 annotators per item). For each item, a probability distribution over labels (Entailment/Neutral/Contradiction for MNLI/SNLI; binary choice for alphaNLI) is provided as ground truth, capturing collective human uncertainty and annotator disagreement.
metric: Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD) vs. human judgment distributions, accuracy, Spearman rho
notes: From Nie et al., EMNLP 2020. Each instance annotated by 100 crowdworkers to capture label distributions rather than single majority-vote labels. Paper 2601.03154 uses ChaosNLI to evaluate whether CoT reasoning helps LLMs model human label variation (HLV). Subsets: MNLI, SNLI, alphaNLI.

name: alphaNLI (Abductive NLI)
