format: Abductive reasoning task: given a beginning and ending observation, choose the more likely hypothesis (binary choice). Produces 2-d label distributions from 100 annotators.
notes: From Bhagavatula et al., ICLR 2020. Used in ChaosNLI (Nie et al., 2020) as binary-choice variant. Paper 2601.03154 evaluates reasoning LLMs on alphaNLI to test distributional alignment under ambiguity.

name: False-Completion Benchmark Suite
format: 8 robotic manipulation tasks on LIBERO with 3 perturbation families: Object Drop, Distractor Swap, Object Relayout

name: TRIP-Bench
num_samples: Not disclosed (multi-turn travel planning tasks with Easy/Mid/Hard splits, and 4 hard subsets: LIT/FIT/AIS/PMR)
eval_time: hours per model (150+ tool calls, 200k+ tokens per episode)
format: Multi-turn travel planning dialogues with user simulator, 18 tools (attractions, hotels, flights, trains, restaurants, general utilities), rule-based evaluation with feasibility/soundness/user constraint checking
metric: OverallStrict (I(feas=0 and sound=0 and user=0)), OverallLoose (I(feas=0 and sound<=2 and user<=1))
notes: Long-horizon interactive agent benchmark in travel planning. Up to 15 user turns, 150+ tool calls, 200k+ token contexts. Best models achieve ~50% loose / ~18% strict on Easy split. From Meituan/Fudan/PKU et al. (2026).

name: UserBench
num_samples: Not disclosed (interactive agent evaluation with user-centric tasks)
format: Interactive agent tasks with user behavior modeling including intent ambiguity and behavioral diversity
notes: An interactive gym environment for user-centric agents. Introduces intent ambiguity and behavioral diversity in multi-turn tool-use settings. Used as comparison baseline in TRIP-Bench paper.

name: VitaBench
num_samples: Not disclosed (versatile interactive tasks in real-world applications)
format: Versatile interactive tasks requiring tool use in real-world application scenarios
notes: Benchmarking LLM agents with versatile interactive tasks in real-world applications. Features dynamic interactions and longer horizons. Used as comparison baseline in TRIP-Bench paper.

name: COMPASS
num_samples: Not disclosed (multi-turn tool-mediated planning and preference optimization)
format: Multi-turn tool-mediated planning tasks with preference optimization
notes: A multi-turn benchmark for tool-mediated planning and preference optimization. Combines tool use, planning, and dynamic user preferences. Used as comparison baseline in TRIP-Bench paper.

name: CRUXEVAL-I
format: Code execution and reasoning tasks requiring functional correctness of generated code

name: OpenThoughts-114K
format: Chain-of-thought reasoning traces from DeepSeek-R1, covering math, science, code domains
notes: Used for training k-SAEs on model activations in IPG paper (arXiv:2602.02313). Released by OpenThoughts project (arXiv:2506.04178).

name: CoQA
format: Conversational QA pairs in JSON with passage context; multi-turn dialogues
notes: Conversational Question Answering dataset from Stanford. Used in hallucination detection paper (arXiv:2601.19918). Paper uses dev set of 7,983 QA pairs.

name: COLLIE-v1
num_samples: Not fully disclosed; covers multiple constraint types at sentence and paragraph levels
format: Constrained text generation tasks defined by formal grammars; includes sentence-level tasks (character counting, word inclusion/positioning) and paragraph-level tasks (multi-sentence constraints)

name: EquInfer
format: Equation correctness evaluation in scientific paper context. Each instance contains 4 equation candidates (1 correct) with surrounding paper context before and after the equation. Simulates paper review process.
notes: Subtask of AAAR-1.0 benchmark (arXiv:2410.22394). Used in PRIN paper (arXiv:2504.01282) to evaluate Prompt-Reverse Inconsistency across LLMs.

name: CONDAQA
format: Contrastive reading comprehension dataset requiring reasoning about negation. Question-answer pairs with diverse negation cues, including paraphrasing, changing negation scope, and reversing negation.
notes: CONtrastive reading Comprehension dataset for reasoning about negation. Used in PRIN paper (arXiv:2504.01282) to investigate correlation between PRIN and negation-handling difficulty (Pearson r=0.67).

name: SamSum
format: Dialogue transcripts with abstractive human-written summaries

name: MedQUAD
format: Medical question-answer pairs from NLM Consumer Health Wikipedia, covering diseases, drugs, etc.

name: WMT19 German-English
format: Parallel German-English sentences (news domain)

name: AlignScore
format: Unsupervised metric for evaluating factual consistency between source and target text; computes semantic alignment score based on entailment

name: Pascal Context
format: scene images with per-pixel semantic labels (60 classes including background)

name: YouTube-VIS 2021
num_samples: 3,059 train / 421 val / 507 test video clips (longer sequences than 2019)
format: Short YouTube video segments with per-frame masks, categories, and track IDs; same format as 2019 but updated videos

name: YouTube-VIS 2022
num_samples: 3,141 train / 421 val / 507 test video clips (challenging long videos)
format: Short YouTube video segments with per-frame masks, categories, and track IDs; emphasized as having challenging long videos

name: OVIS (Occlusion Video Instance Segmentation)
num_samples: ~2,900 train / ~500 val video clips with frequent occlusions
format: Video clips with frequent occlusions, per-frame instance masks, categories, and track IDs

name: AmbigQA
format: Open-domain QA with ambiguous questions that may have multiple correct answers; requires disambiguation and comprehensive answer coverage
notes: From Min et al., EMNLP 2020. Addresses ambiguous factoid questions where multiple answer entities can be correct. Paper uses AmbigQA as an out-of-domain test set.
